text: Cognitive radio (CR) systems have to be able to detect the presence of a primary user (PU) signal by sensing the spectrum area of interest. Due to radiowave propagation effects like fading and shadowing, spectrum sensing is often complicated, because the PU signal can be attenuated in a particular area. In this paper, we explore a distributed spectrum sensing approach that exploits the largest eigenvalue of correlation matrices (CMs) that are adaptively estimated, based on the combine and adapt least (CTA) type of diffusion method with no fusion center (FC). More specifically, CR nodes exchange also observations with a subset of neighbouring nodes and combine the neighbouring observations based on the locally estimated signal to noise ratio (SNR) values. We analyse the resulting detection performance and verify the theoretical findings through simulations.

Parkinsonian gait is a defining feature of shaking palsy (SP) and it has one of the worse impacts on human healthy life than other SP symptoms. The objective of this work is to propose a Parkinsonian gait detection system based on an S-band perception technique to classify abnormal gait and normal walking. Due to the differences in the Gaits of Parkinson's patients compared with healthy persons, the wireless signals reflect and generates different variations at the receiver that could be used for SP diagnosis and classification. To detect a Parkinsonian gait, we first implement data preprocessing of the original data to obtain clear amplitude and phase information. Then, the feature extraction is carried out by principal component analysis (PCA). Finally, a support vector machine (SVM) classification algorithm is applied on collected data to classify the abnormal gait of SP patients compared with a normal gait. We evaluate the proposed system with different people, and the experimental outcomes show that the Parkinsonian gait detection of this training-based system achieves a high accuracy of above 90%. Moreover, the early warning of SP is achieved in a non-contact manner.

With the proliferation of data acquisition systems, multi-source remote sensing imagery has become increasingly accessible. In this paper, we present a solution to the challenging problem of building semantic segmentation using multi-source remote sensing imagery with varying spatial resolutions. Unlike previous approaches focused only on optimizing the segmentation model, our proposal incorporates super-resolution (SR) techniques to improve segmentation performance by addressing the effects of unaligned resolution between training and testing data. We assessed the feasibility of our method using high-resolution (HR) aerial and low-resolution (LR) panchromatic satellite imagery as representative materials for training and testing, respectively. Rather than directly segmenting buildings from LR imagery using an HR-trained model, we used a deep learning-based SR model to super-resolve the LR imagery into SR space. Experimental results from Tokyo, Japan attest to the effectiveness of our proposed SR-integrated method, which outperformed non-SR segmentation methods by approximately 19.01% and 19.10% as measured by the Jaccard index and kappa, respectively. These results confirm that our method offers a valuable solution for building semantic segmentation, particularly when resolution is not aligned.

Winning in multiplayer online games, specifically Dota 2 for teams, is influenced by numerous factors. One of the most critical factors is selecting the right heroes for the team. By examining the chosen heroes, it's possible to predict the outcome of a match. To tackle this classification problem, this paper explores various machine learning approaches for predicting match results. The comparison of predictive classification models was conducted, and their hyperparameters were optimized. The findings indicated that the most effective classification models are linear regression, linear support vector machine, and neural network with Softplus and Sigmoid activation functions. The linear regression model is the fastest and best suited for practical use.

Due to absorption and scattering effects the under-water scenes are characterized by poor contrast, color shifting, additional noise and hazy appearance. In this paper we introduce a novel solution that estimates locally the backscattered light. While in general the existing solutions estimate a global backscattered light value over the entire scene, our local strategy is able to deal effectively to the more challenging non-uniform illumination generated by multiple light-sources. Our solution computes two complementary estimates of the local backscattered light, covering a large and a small patch size. The optimal local backscattered light is computed as the mean of the outputs processed with the small and the large patches while the transmission map, is estimated based on the dark-channel prior (DCP) [1]. Finally, our restored results are computed by simply inverting the optical model using the transmission and the local backscattered light estimates. The qualitative evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach compared with the recent underwater enhancing techniques.

In this paper, a new algorithm is proposed for estimating parameters of multiple frequency-hopping (FH) signals. The algorithm is based on maximum energy difference and involves several steps. First, a time-frequency (TF) matrix is obtained using short-time Fourier transform (STFT) or smoothed pseudo wigner-ville distribution (SPWVD). The carrier frequency and the TF data with valid frequency are then determined based on the energy distribution. The number of signal segments and window length in each nonzero row of the TF data are obtained next. Finally, hopping time and hop cycle are estimated using the maximum energy difference.

Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the TF pattern modification method and the STFT-SPWVD method in terms of anti-noise performance. Moreover, the new method is suitable for both asynchronous and synchronous networks. Overall, the algorithm provides an effective approach for parameter estimation of multiple FH signals.

In this study, we propose the use of single channel Color Co-occurrence Matrices for texture description of Barrett's Esophagus (BE) and adenocarcinoma images. Supervised learning techniques, such as Optimum-Path Forest (OPF), Support Vector Machines with Radial Basis Function (SVM-RBF) and Bayesian classifier were used for further classification purposes to support the automatic BE and adenocarcinoma diagnosis. We validated three approaches of classification based on patches, patients, and images in two datasets (MICCAI 2015 and Augsburg) using color-and-texture descriptors and machine learning techniques. The best results for the MICCAI 2015 dataset were obtained using the blue channel for the descriptors and the supervised OPF for classification purposes in the patch-based approach, with sensitivity nearly at 73% for positive adenocarcinoma identification and specificity close to 77% for BE (non-cancerous) patch classification. For the Augsburg dataset, the most accurate results were observed using both OPF classifier and blue channel descriptor for the feature extraction, with sensitivity close to 67% and specificity around to 76%. This work showcases new advances in the related research area and provides a promising technique that combines color and texture information, allied to three different approaches of dataset pre-processing, aiming to create robust scenarios for the classification step.

Individual recognition of communication emitter can obtain the working mechanism, system parameters, and the usage model of the emitters based on the separation and interception of the specific emitter signals. In order to realize the individual recognition of communication emitter, a method of communication emitter recognition based on wavelet packet feature extraction and attribute reduction of granular computing is proposed. The method uses hierarchical and granularity to represent the subtle feature information of different emitter signals contained in the original data after the decomposition of wavelet packet, so that the feature attributes of different emitters are efficiently mapped to different levels of granular structure which can be used to search for an optimal reduced attributes operation for signal recognition. And then, the reduced attributes are used to distinguish the emitter signals correctly by label propagation method. The experimental results show that the proposed method based on wavelet packet feature extraction and granular computing attribute reduction has good classification performance in individual recognition of communication emitters.

The Middle Size League, or MSL, is a division within the Robocup competition, a global research organization focusing on developing soccer robots. The ultimate goal of this organization is to create a team of soccer robots that will compete against the human champions at the World Cup in 2050. However, in order to achieve this, mobile soccer robots must first master the basic skill of kicking. Therefore, extensive research is being conducted to improve accuracy and control in power shooting.

The research in question seeks to improve the flat and lob shoot abilities of soccer robots, with control over varying levels of kick power achieved through the use of a Fuzzy Logic Controller. This approach helps to enhance the accuracy of the kick, enabling the robot to land the ball in a predetermined location. Inputs such as the distance to the goalpost and the distance between the robot and the opponent are used to generate power kicks and angles, with power levels ranging from very fast to very slow. 

For instance, a voltage of 500V, combined with a 40 degree angle, can result in a very fast kick capable of reaching a distance of 8.5 meters, with a height of 2.2 meters. On the other hand, a slower kick, using a voltage between 150V-250V can result in a very slow kick, allowing for greater precision.

In summary, MSL is striving to develop advanced soccer robots that can perform basic skills such as kicking with accuracy and control. By using a Fuzzy Logic Controller, varying levels of kick power can be achieved, enabling the robot to make decisions during the kicking process. This research is an essential step towards achieving the ultimate goal of Robocup - creating robots that can beat the human champions at the World Cup.

Vector parabolic equation (VPE) methods have become a popular choice for modeling wave propagation in guiding structures due to their high accuracy and computational efficiency. However, accurately modeling the environment being studied can be challenging, as there may be significant uncertainties in the description of the environment. To address this issue, a non-intrusive formulation of the polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) method has been developed to quantify the uncertainties in VPE-based channel models for tunnel environments. 

In this paper, the proposed PCE method is validated against Monte Carlo simulations and measurements. Results show that the PCE method is capable of accurately quantifying uncertainties in the VPE-based channel models, and provides an efficient means to assess the impact of uncertainties on the model predictions. 

In summary, the PCE method offers a valuable tool for assessing uncertainties in VPE-based channel models, and provides a means to improve the accuracy of predictions for wave propagation in guiding structures.

This paper is concerned with theoretical and practices approach for overall quality-related fault detection and identification in process industries. Fault detection and fault tracing can help engineers to take corrective actions and recover the process operations. A novel diagnostic method is proposed based on stacked automatic encoder-canonical correlation analysis (SAE-CCA) and least absolute shrinkage selection operator (Lasso). First, a quality monitoring scheme based on SAE-CCA is proposed, which establishes a relationship model among quality and characteristic variables to detect faults. Then, Lasso is used for locating the root causes, according to the process state and fault information. Finally, the experiments are conducted with typical industry process data, i.e., a hot strip mill process (HSMP), in order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the whole diagnosis method.

Radiomics and state-of-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated their usefulness for predicting genotype in gliomas from brain MRI images. However, these techniques rely heavily on accurate tumor segmentation and do not facilitate any insights into the working of CNN to understand what areas distinguish these classes. To mitigate this, we employ a novel technique called Convolutional Neural Nets with discriminative localization (DL-CNN) on a clinical T2 weighted MRI dataset of IDH1 mutant and wild-type tumor patients. The technique not only is free of tumor segmentation with high classification accuracy of 86.7% but also locates the most discriminative regions. We demonstrate that in majority IDH1 mutants only the tumoral area is significant while in majority IDH1 wildtype the peri-tumoral edema is also involved. Overall, our method besides prediction provides information that is particularly important for clinical interpretability and can be used in targeted therapy.

In our investigation of establishing an immediate defense mechanism against DDoS attacks on Web applications via hacker botnets, we aim to develop a approach that does not require significant preparation time, such as training data, as is often the case with existing proposals. To this end, we offer a new mechanism that includes innovative data structures and algorithms specifically designed for detecting and filtering large numbers of attack packets, or Web requests. 

Our approach involves monitoring and capturing suspect groups of source IPs that exhibit similar patterns, such as high and comparable frequencies of packet sending. Our algorithm prioritizes reducing storage space and processing time, making it well-suited for applications that require real-time attack response. 

Overall, we believe our mechanism will be an effective solution to the ongoing challenge of defending against DDoS attacks on Web applications.

In this paper, firstly we model the channel impulse characteristic by combining the Monte Carlo method with Fournier-Forand (FF) phase function. Then we analyze the effects of various field of views (FOVs) and transmission distances on the channel impulse response and found that temporal dispersion has rigorous bandwidth limitations on the undersea wireless optical communication (UWOC) system in the harbor water. Furthermore, we propose to adopt the maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) method at the receiver to mitigate the bandwidth limitations and demonstrate that MLSE has great potential to improve system performance.

The Institute of National Colleges of Technology (NICT) was established to oversee the management of 55 national KOSEN institutions across Japan. The National Institute of Technology (NIT) serves as the centerpiece of the KOSEN system, with its Core curriculum serving as the foundation of KOSEN education. The Model curriculum is built on top of this core curriculum, which combines the unique characteristics of each college to create a Model Core Curriculum (MCC) that is largely comprised of ten fields. 

Each field in the MCC has defined learning goals and reach targets, as well as generic skills that are necessary for students to function in society. However, the assessment of generic skills is different from traditional knowledge retention assessments, making it challenging to evaluate through paper and confirmation tests. Currently, there is no evaluation method proposed for the integration of fields in MCC.

At NIT Sendai college, we have been conducting objective evaluations of generic skills for four years, providing us with the data necessary to propose a new evaluation method for MCC. This method would assess the ability to cross fields and highlight the potential of KOSEN education to prepare students for success in society.

A rapid growth in the smart-wearable industry is making it increasingly important to cater to the quality of experience (QoE) requirements of the end users. In this paper, we try to model the relationship between human experience and quality perception in relation to the smart-wearable segment. For this, the concepts of quality of data (QoD) and quality of information (QoI) are used. While QoD is concerned with the accuracy and precision of the data collected by the smart-wearables, QoI relates to the useful information that is obtained from the raw data captured by the devices via the companion applications of each wearable installed on a smartphone. A subjective experiment comprising of 40 participants and 5 wearable devices is performed in a free-living condition in order to create the QoE model. Four different approaches for weight determination are presented in this paper: balanced weight distribution, correlation-based distribution, hybrid distribution, and priority-based distribution while proposing the QoE model. Our results show that the priority-based distribution approach performs slightly better than the rest of the techniques and has the best correlation to the subjective QoE when compared against others. Based on the results, the appropriate recommendations are provided to the different smart-wearable vendors for improving their products, thereby ensuring greater user adoption.

In this paper, we consider the simultaneous connectivity of primary and secondary networks forming a cognitive model. It is assumed that the cognitive model includes guard zones that prevent the nodes of the secondary network from being active in the vicinity of primary nodes to limit interference. Under these assumptions, we characterize the region of densities, the transmission radii of the nodes in each of the networks, and the guard zones for which the two networks have a unique unbounded connected component. We prove that this model is feasible, that is, there exists simultaneous connectivity with the unique unbounded connected component in each of the networks. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the simultaneous connectivity of this cognitive model.

This paper presents a novel robust adaptive tracking control method for a hypersonic vehicle in a cruise flight stage based on interval type-2 fuzzy-logic system (IT2-FLS) and small-gain approach. After the input-output linearization, the vehicle model can be decomposed into two uncertain subsystems by considering matching disturbances and parametric uncertainties. For each subsystem, an interval type-2 Takagi-Sugeno-Kang fuzzy logic system (IT2-TSK-FLS) is then employed to approximate the unavailable model information. Following the idea of a small-gain approach, a composite feedback form for each subsystem is constructed, based on which the final robust adaptive tracking control law is developed. Rigorous stability analysis shows that all signals in the derived closed-loop system are kept uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB). The main contribution of this paper is that the proposed control law for the hypersonic vehicle is with only two adaptive parameters in total which can greatly alleviate the computation and storage burden in practice; meanwhile its superiority over the conventional minimal-learning-parameter (MLP)-based one is specifically illustrated. Comparative numerical simulations of three cases demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed control method with respect to complicated uncertainties.

Convolutional Neural Network is the base of all deep learning models. Therefore a Convolutional Neural Network model is created and developed to perform plant disease detection and classification using apple and tomato leaf images of healthy and diseased plants. The model consists of four convolutional layers each followed by pooling layers. Two fully connected dense layers and sigmoid function is used to detect the probability of presence of disease or not. Training of the model was done on apple and tomato leaf image dataset containing 3663 images achieving an accuracy of 87%. The overfitting problem is identified and removed setting the dropout value to 0.2. As the model allows parallel processing, it is also run on GPU Tesla to evaluate its speed of performance and accuracy. Hence the paper provides an insight of creativeness to the researchers to develop an integrated plant disease identification system that gives successful results in realtime.

This paper presents a comparative study between the response time of on-premises databases and cloud databases, emphasizing the benefits of storing data and applications in the cloud compared to local physical machines. To manage the cloud database, a Microsoft Azure account was created, and a Universal Windows Platform app was used to test it on multiple physical machines. The local tests were carried out on a locally stored server, with and without replication, while the cloud tests were performed on a server in Central US. The paper offers a practical approach that can be used to examine the performance of basic database operations when dealing with different numbers of user situations. Based on the tests conducted, the paper highlights the advantages of cloud data storage, including data accessibility, speed, security, automation, and disaster recovery. Additionally, the paper aims to answer the most common and important question: “Why cloud?”.

The data of the multi-objective job shop production process in intelligent manufacturing has the characteristics of diversity, ambiguity, heterogeneity and stochastic dynamics. Combined with the complex network theory, the network modeling algorithm is used to build a multi-objective job based on data information to dynamically weigh the complex network model. Taking the data information as a node, taking the relationship between data as the edge, and taking the intensity between relationships as the weight of the edge, the model introduces dynamic changes in time. In consideration of the dynamic evolution of internal nodes, edges and weights at different times, the process optimization model for the multi-objective job shop problem is transformed into the data optimization model. After the analysis of the characteristics parameters of the model, the simulation experiments verify that the model has the characteristics of network without scale, which proves that the model can perfectly describe the actual workshop production.

With the rapid expansion of the cloud-native computing paradigm, an increasing number of applications are adopting container-based microservices architecture (MSA). However, the resulting container-based MSA functions require tight stitching interconnections that necessitate persistent monitor/control coordination. To address this maintenance problem in a transparent and efficient manner, recent service mesh approaches have been developed. Unfortunately, the popular Istio-based service mesh realization exposes the monitor/control traffic for coordination to application tenants, which can be a potential security concern.

Since containers are limited to a single network interface, it is difficult to isolate control/monitor traffic from application data traffic. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a protected coordination scheme for service mesh as a work-around solution. Under this protected coordination scheme, the monitor/control traffic for coordination is separated and encrypted while data traffic is treated in the same way as the existing service mesh approach. This proposed scheme is expected to enhance the security and privacy of the service mesh-based microservices architecture, making it more robust and reliable for use in critical applications.

It is common the use of the sonar technology in order acquire and posteriorly control the distance of an underwater vehicle towards an obstacle. Although this solution simplifies the problem and is effective in most cases, it might carry some disadvantages in certain underwater vehicles or conditions. In this work it is presented a system capable of controlling the altitude of an underwater vehicle using computer vision. The sensor capable of computing the distance is composed of a CCD camera and 2 green pointer lasers. Regarding the control of the vehicle, the solution used was based on the switching of two controllers, a velocity controller (based on a PI controller), and a position controller (based on a PD controller). The vehicle chosen to test the developed system was a profiler, which main task is the vertical navigation. The mathematical model was obtained and used in order to validate the controllers designed using the Simulink toolbox from Matlab. It was used a Kalman filter in order to have a better estimation of the state variables (altitude, depth, and velocity). The tests relative to the sensor developed responsible for the acquisition of the altitude showed an average relative error equal to 1 % in the range from 0 to 2.5 m. The UWsim underwater simulation environment was used in order to validate the integration of the system and its performance.

The surge of demand of the Internet of Things (IoTs) poses more requirements for cellular communication systems, such as higher levels of reliability, latency and supported number of devices. A common scenario of IoT is massive machinetype communications (mMTC). The characteristics of mMTC, i.e. the massive number of sensors, small packets and sporadic transmission, require novel methods to detect the active devices, estimate their channel state information and recovery their data with high accuracy and low latency. In this paper, we propose a new compressive sensing based method to jointly conduct active device detection, channel estimation and data recovery. As a high level description of the proposed method, we improve the performance of active device detection and channel estimation by using side information brought from the data recovery, and improve the performance of data recovery in successive interference cancellation by using the side information brought from the active device detection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method has improved data recovery performance.

A problem of achieving consensus in state of multiagent system consisting of N identical agents is considered. The agents are modeled as discrete time linear time invariant (LTI) systems with bounded inputs (|u| ≤ 1) and complete communication among all agents is assumed. The goal of these agents is to achieve consensus in minimum number of time steps. An algorithm to compute the minimum number of time steps in which the consensus can be achieved is devised by computing the attainable set. Key idea of the proposed algorithm is to compute attainable sets by incrementally varying the time steps and checking for intersection of attainable sets corresponding to all N agents. Since, the attainable set is a convex polytope, intersection of attainable sets translates to checking feasibility of multiple linear inequalities. It is shown that for systems with eigenvalues inside the closed unit circle in complex plane, the proposed algorithm terminates in finite number of steps. The number of time steps counted by the proposed algorithm till the intersection of attainable sets becomes feasible is the minimum time steps required to achieve consensus. Lastly, it is shown using Helly's theorem that the computation of intersection of attainable sets in the proposed algorithm can be performed in distributed manner. The proposed algorithm is demonstrated with the help of an example.

Peripheral nerve decoding algorithms form an important component of closed-loop bioelectronic medicines devices. For any decoding method, meaningful properties need to be extracted from the peripheral nerve signal as the first step. Simple measures such as signal amplitude and features of the Fourier power spectrum are most typically used, leaving open whether important information is encoded in more subtle properties of the dynamics. We here propose a feature-based analysis method that identifies changes in firing characteristics across recording sections by unsupervised dimensionality reduction in a high-dimensional feature-space and selects single efficiently implementable estimators for each characteristic to be used as the basis for a better decoding in future bioelectronic medicines devices.

Radiomics is a fast-growing field that involves modeling the textural information that is present in different tissues of interest for clinical decision support. However, generating radiomic images can be computationally expensive and time-consuming, particularly for higher-order features like grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM). To overcome this challenge, we have developed RadSynth, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model that can efficiently generate radiomic images.

To test the efficiency of RadSynth, we used it on a cohort of twenty-four breast cancer patients, including ten benign, ten malignant, and four normal patients. Specifically, we computed GLCM entropy images from post-contrast DCE-MRI images. RadSynth successfully produced synthetic entropy images that were comparable to traditional GLCM entropy images. The average difference and correlation between the two techniques were 0.07 ± 0.06 and 0.97, respectively.

Overall, RadSynth represents a powerful new tool for quick computation and visualization of the textural information in radiological images.

A pair of blood vessels inside of the human neck that serves to deliver blood to the brain is called carotid artery. Cholesterol in human body can form plaque, causes blockage to carotid artery that evoke atherosclerosis, stroke and heart disease which is a dangerous disease that can lead to death. If in certain long time it is not discovered, carotid artery will rupture. In clinical practice, the availability of ultrasound is wide also it is a low cost method to observe plaque in carotid artery. Unfortunately, ultrasound plaque images in carotid artery is diverse, noisy and not easy to be identified. It is also hard to develop computational techniques for recognizing plaque from ultrasound images. Therefore, it is a challenge to develop an optimal method that can be implemented in computer system to recognize plaque from ultrasound images. One method from many techniques available in pattern recognition is a feature extraction which can be obtained from various ways. In this work, A Gabor wavelet which is one of the powerful method in feature extraction is applied to recognize plaque characteristics. However a Gabor wavelet feature extraction will result a huge data, therefore to reduce the data dimension, the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to reduce such huge data. The result of this method for recognize plaque in carotid artery is satisfied with 100% recognition rate by using 8 orientations and 3 scales bank of Gabor with 100% eigenvectors configuration. In this research we used 24 carotid artery training images.

In this position paper, we claim that immersive technologies, such as Augmented and Virtual Reality, are well-suited interfaces for the usage of crowd simulation software in different contexts. We introduce three use cases; planning, awareness creation, and education. Based on an overview of different Augmented and Virtual Reality approaches, we identify the ones most suitable for each of the three scenarios and illustrate related implementations. Initial observations with their usage confirm our statements, but also highlight areas to explore with future research.

Robots face numerous challenges in operating in a home environment due to its unstructured nature, unlike industrial or commercial environments. This scholarly paper examines the problem of path planning and the dynamic tuning of PID controllers in this context. The research proposes the use of Learning Automata, specifically Finite Action Learning Automata to predict the presence of people and Continuous Action Learning Automata for deriving PID controllers. The study shows that this approach leads to the efficient generation of better controllers for path planning in comparison to classical methods. In addition, the study demonstrates that the proposed method can accurately identify waypoints and approximates the location of people in home-care applications.

The computational model of cloud computing is based on large computer networks such as the internet. These networks present a new way for providing, consuming, and delivering Information Technology (including hardware, software, information, and other computational resources) by leveraging the internet. Cloud computing offers guidelines for providing IT services in a similar fashion as public utilities such as water, electricity, and telephone systems. This means that users can access IT resources in a flexible and scalable way based on their demand level.

However, optimal resource allocation in cloud computing systems is a complex challenge. Due to the large search space involved, random search methods are often used for solving this problem. Various algorithms have been proposed to address this issue. In this paper, we propose a meta-heuristic algorithm called GSA-RACloud for solving the resource assignment problem in cloud computing.

The proposed algorithm's performance is evaluated and compared with the ant colony algorithm (ACO). Empirical results reveal that the proposed algorithm performs better than the comparative ACO algorithm.

In summary, cloud computing offers a new paradigm for providing IT services using large computer networks like the internet. Resource allocation is a significant challenge in cloud computing systems, and the proposed GSA-RACloud algorithm presents an effective solution to this problem.

This paper examines the potential of handwriting patterns as biomarkers for modeling Parkinson's disease (PD). While PD research has garnered interest from researchers worldwide, databases for evaluating handwriting patterns are limited and knowledge about patterns associated with PD is scarce and biased to existing datasets. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a database featuring 935 handwriting tasks, collected from 55 PD patients and 94 healthy controls (45 young and 49 old). Three feature sets derived from the signals are evaluated: neuromotor, kinematic, and nonlinear dynamic. Different classifiers are employed to differentiate between PD and healthy subjects, including support vector machines, k-nearest neighbors, and a multilayer perceptron. Results show that the proposed features and classifiers can detect PD with accuracies ranging from 81% to 97%. Furthermore, this study offers insights into the potential usefulness of these features for monitoring and detecting PD.

We have leveraged machine learning to automate root cause analysis in agile software testing environments. Our approach involves extracting relevant features from raw log data by interviewing testing engineers, who are experts in the field. Initially, we try to cluster the unlabeled data, but we observe weak correlations between a few clusters and failure root causes. Thus, we consider labeling and conduct follow-up interviews with the testing engineers. This leads to the definition of five ground-truth categories.

We then use manually labeled data to train artificial neural networks, which are capable of either classifying the data or pre-processing it for clustering. The resulting method delivers an accuracy of 88.9%. This paper proposes a prototype or baseline approach for extracting expert knowledge and adapting it to machine learning techniques for root cause analysis in agile environments.

JCLedger is a BlockChain-based distributed ledger designed for JointCloud, with the objective of enhancing the reliability and convenience of cloud resource exchanges by encouraging collaboration among multiple clouds. However, implementing JCLedger has posed significant challenges, with the primary issue being the consensus approach. The existing consensus algorithms for public BlockChain, such as proof of work (PoW) or proof of stake (PoS), are not applicable to JointCloud as they demand massive computing power with low throughput, leading to monopoly risks. 

In this article, we introduce a practical Byzantine-fault-tolerance (PBFT)-based consensus algorithm, named proof of previous transactions (PoPT). PoPT selects accountants through a specific hash function from a pool of candidates. These candidates are selected based on their JointCloud participation. Only those candidates who join the PBFT-based consensus process are chosen, rather than all users. Additionally, we propose a new BlockChain structure for parallel accounting to boost the scalability of JCLedger, where a consistent hashing algorithm assigns transactions to different accountants. 

Simulation experiments reveal that the PoPT algorithm can neutralize unequal computing power among users, providing them with equal accounting opportunities. The parallel accounting approach can handle massive and high-frequency transactions in JointCloud more efficiently, significantly improving its scalability.

The security of inertial navigation system (INS) is the key factor to determine the safety of air vehicle. Due to the INS contains some components of dynamic logic gate, which makes its work process presenting a series of dynamic characteristics. When using dynamic fault tree to analyze the security of INS, most of the traditional approaches are based on Markov chain and Monte-Carlo simulation. However, those methods have curse of dimensionality problem and/or require long computation time particularly when results with a high degree of accuracy are desired. In this paper, an analytical method is proposed based on sequential binary decision diagrams (SBDD) for combinatorial reliability analysis of dynamic systems. Firstly, the dynamic fault tree (DFT) model of collapse of inertial platform is built based on safety analysis used DFT. Secondly, the DFT model is modularized into independent static sub-trees and dynamic sub-trees, and then the exact expression of the occurrence probability for each minimal cut-set is determined by the static fault tree analysis method or SBDD method. Finally, the possibility of collapse of inertial platform in all its life is obtained after comprehensive analysis, and the result is compared with that based on Markov chain and Monte-Carlo simulation. The result shows that the proposed approach can generate exact possibility of collapse of inertial platform. In addition, the system model of sequential binary decision diagrams and possibility evaluation expression are reusable for the reliability analysis with different component failure parameters, the method is more applicable and more effective, and the method of calculating occurrence probability of top event for a dynamic fault tree is expanded.

In recent times, the term "Internet of Things" (IoT) has been used to describe the interconnectivity of smart objects. The IoT aims to equip tangible entities with communication and computing power, enabling them to interact with one another. This technology has prompted the development of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), replacing the traditional Vehicle Ad-hoc Networks (VANET) to establish a sustainable global service. The IoV has garnered commercial interest and research value, attracting corporations and scholars across the globe. An evaluation of recently proposed IoV architectures and their features is recommended in this paper. An abstract network model of the IoV is presented, along with various services based on prevailing technologies. The paper also outlines the challenges faced by IoV and provides recommendations for upcoming research in the field.

To safeguard the overwhelming amount of diverse information available on network-connected computers, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential. In this paper, a new intrusion detection method is introduced, which analyses the heterogeneity of clusters formed by reducing the dimensions of data points. The class dominance in each cluster forms the basis of initial classification, followed by evaluating cluster confidence and spread. Detection is refined based on the parameters formulated by these criteria. Experiments conducted on the well-known KDD Cup '99 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in terms of high accuracy and low false alarm rates. The system's robustness and effectiveness are also parameterised by a run-time analysis.

Filter bank multi-carrier based on offset quadrature amplitude modulation (FBMC/OQAM) suffers from inter-symbol interference and inter-subchannel interference in multi-path fading channels. By exploiting the special structures of the FBMC/OQAM signal and the resulting correlation matrix and assuming perfect estimation of channel and noise power, we study the properties of the decision feedback equalizer (DFE) designed by the minimum mean square error criterion. The study leads to efficient and mathematically equivalent computation of DFE coefficients. Consequently, the DFE requires a smaller complexity in computing the equalizer coefficients than the linear equalizer, while achieving a significant performance gain in highly frequency-selective channels. Building upon the proposed efficient computation of DFE, we develop DFE-based detectors-namely, two-stage DFE and multi-band DFE-so that a better detection performance can be obtained more efficiently. Complexity analysis and simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed computation method and the DFE-based detectors.

The adoption of cache has the potential to reduce redundant traffic and decrease latency in wireless access networks, especially in the context of wireless video broadcasting. However, the impact of cache on video broadcasting with scalable video coding (SVC) remains an unsolved problem. In this study, we investigate the optimization of random caching in a large-scale Internet of Things networks enabled with cache. Specifically, we propose an optimization strategy for random caching aimed at maximizing successful transmission probability (STP) for video content at base stations (BSs) located at the edge of the network. Using stochastic geometry theory, we derive an analytical expression of STP while considering different levels of quality of service requirements based on SVC. We develop a gradient-based iterative algorithm to search for the optimal solution for the general random caching strategy optimization problem. The asymptotically optimal caching strategy is achieved with lower complexity, and we also derive closed-form STP in high signal-to-noise ratio and specific cache size. Based on these closed-form STP expressions, we further optimize the caching probability of various video contents to enhance STP performance. Compared to other reference schemes, the proposed caching strategy improves STP by up to 18% and 21.6% in low-density and high-density BSs, respectively.

This paper adresses one of the problems in voice conversion system design: the choice of the number of Gaussian components used to determine the conversion function. The adopted strategy integrates three steps that use i) common criteria of Gaussian mixture model order determination, ii) speech quality criteria for converted speech and iii) a statistical analysis based on ANOVA and Bonferroni test to decide on speech quality difference for several values of the number of Gaussian components. The proposed solution is validated for phonemes conversion, namely healthy /A/ phoneme conversion to healthy /I/ phoneme conversion and pathological /A/ phoneme conversion to healthy /A/ phoneme conversion.

Fruit grading is a crucial aspect of the olive industry, particularly when producing high-quality table olives. This research introduces an innovative method for accurate automatic olive-fruit grading that employs computer vision and feature modeling. The development involved photographing a total of 3600 olive fruits from nine varieties, which were stochastically distributed in an imaging chamber specially designed for this purpose. The image analysis algorithm relied on mathematical morphology to segment and extract descriptive features, including the major and minor axes and mass of each fruit. The algorithm was proven accurate, generating only six faulty fruit-segmentation out of 117 captures containing 11,606 fruits. Models for estimating the three features were computed by linearly correlating the data obtained by image analysis and corresponding reference measurements. These models were tested on 2700 external validation samples, producing errors that were never above 1.16% for estimating olive-fruit mass. The developed algorithm's ability to segment olives stochastically positioned, coupled with low error rates, makes it a promising alternative for integration into a new generation of non-invasive olive classification machines. Consequently, this new system has been registered with the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office under the number P201930297.

In partial label learning, an instance's label is represented by a set of labels, of which only one is the true label. However, existing algorithms for partial label learning only utilize the features of instances to measure their similarity, neglecting the information hidden in the label set. To address this issue, this paper proposes a candidate label-aware similarity graph constructing method for partial label data. 

Our proposed method effectively combines candidate label information using Jaccard distance and linear reconstruction to measure the similarity between instances. First, we calculate the similarity between instances and candidate label-sets. Then, we construct a similarity graph by combining the instance similarity and the label-set similarity. 

Extensive experiments were conducted on artificial and real-world PL datasets, demonstrating that our method can measure the similarity of partial-label data better and significantly improve the performance of graph-based partial label learning algorithms.

Acetabular fractures are a condition that primarily affects individuals between the ages of 21 and 30, with an increase in incidence due to accidents that have both immediate and late implications. The first step in evaluating this condition and determining treatment options is to analyze an X-ray image. Identifying whether the traumatic injury is located in the pelvis and is an acetabular fracture or not, provides crucial support for orthopedic surgeons dealing with this type of injury.

To improve the accuracy of classifying acetabular fractures, a method utilizing the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) feature extractor and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification method has been proposed. Additionally, the use of pre-processing methods for enhancing image quality has also been identified as a key contribution. Results show that the CLAHE pre-processing method can lead to an 80% accuracy rate in classification.

Overall, the proposed method can significantly aid in the accurate identification and treatment of acetabular fractures, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

The diagnostic accuracy of cervical dysplasia can be improved by fusing multi-modal information from a patient's screening tests. In this study, we introduce a novel multi-modal deep learning fusion network, MultiFuseNet, for cervical dysplasia diagnosis by utilizing multi-modal data from cervical screening results. To capture and fuse the relationships among different image modalities, we propose an Attention Mutual-Enhance (AME) module that integrates features of each modality during the feature extraction stage. Our approach involves the use of the Fused Faster R-CNN with AME modules to detect the cervix region automatically, fuse image features, and integrate non-image information to learn non-linear correlations among all modalities. We employ an alternating training scheme for effective training of the Fused Faster R-CNN. Experimental results demonstrate that our method is highly effective, achieving an average accuracy of 87.4% (88.6% sensitivity and 86.1% specificity) on a large dataset. Importantly, our method outperforms methods utilizing any single modality alone, as well as known multi-modal methods.

The coastal erosion is becoming of paramount importance for many countries. Many studies demonstrated that in some cases the beach overcrowding is the primary cause of coastal erosion. The goal of this work was to design, implement and test a system (BRB-Be Right Beach) that foster beach overcrowding avoidance and allows anyone to choose the right beach to go for having the best experience. The major requirement of our system was to have maximum accuracy (no errors, that is real-time data only are used) in the information provided to the users. The system exploits the Social Internet of Things paradigm to implement a classifier trained by a community of smartphones brought by the owners to the beaches. The BRB sensor network consists of control units equipped with a UV sensor, a thermometer, a humidity sensor and a camera for crowdedness estimation. Data are collected by a cloud platform that provide any user with information about beaches and suggestions where to go, based on users preferences like weather, crowdedness, time of travel, and so on.

Robotic systems are intrinsically complex, non-linear, and coupled. Thus, designing an effective controller that efficiently navigates the system while adhering to complex desired trajectories remains a challenging task. In this study, a fuzzy-logic based intelligent controller was developed to track a quintic trajectory for a 3-DOF robotic leg, which is subjected to ambient friction. The Lyapunov stability theory was used to ensure that the robotic leg's closed-loop stability is maintained.

In contrast, the conventional PID controller applied to Computed Torque Control (CTC) method revealed limitations in scenarios where environmental disturbances such as friction occurred, rendering the modular robotic leg unstable. Conversely, the combined adaptive fuzzy compensator counterbalances the effects of external disturbances by stabilizing the system and ensuring smooth trajectory tracking. Overall, this study demonstrates the effectiveness of the fuzzy-logic based intelligent controller in managing the navigation of complex robotic systems, serving as a significant contribution to the field of robotics.

Multi-level clustering is a promising technique for enhancing the energy efficiency of data gathering and scalability in large-scale wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Although some multi-level frameworks have been developed for static clustering and manually deployed WSNs, there is a lack of structured framework for evolutionary optimization based multilevel clustering protocols. Moreover, no work has been done for randomly deployed WSN performing dynamic clustering. The design of multi-level clustering depends on two critical parameters, the optimal position of layers, and the number of sensor nodes at each layer. To address these issues, this paper proposes a concentric layered architecture (CLA) for multi-level clustering in randomly deployed WSNs. CLA divides the network into layers based on node density and the number of sensor nodes at each layer. The proposed approach is evaluated on an evolutionary optimization technique-based clustering approach, namely PSO-C. The simulation results demonstrate that the CLA significantly enhances the network lifetime and energy efficiency.

This study aimed to develop a monitoring system for indoor spaces. The researchers investigated the use of the bioelectric potential of living plants as a human sensor system in the indoor environment. The system was designed to estimate a resident's location in a room by utilizing a change in the bioelectric potential. To build an estimation model, the researchers collected a lot of bioelectric potential data, which was then processed using a machine learning method. Initially, they attempted to build the estimation model using a convolutional neural network (CNN). However, they found that the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) method was also being used in many successful applications to analyze time sequential data. Therefore, the researchers applied the LSTM method to the bioelectric potential data to investigate its availability alongside CNN, in estimating the location of the resident. The result of the classification experiments with the model trained with collected bioelectric data showed that CNN was better than LSTM for this problem. However, the researchers acknowledged that the accuracy could be improved by further parameter adjustments in the future.

When the target is partially occluded or undergoes drastic appearance change, drift is prone to occur in traditional correlation filter-based trackers and ultimately leads to tracking failure. This paper proposes a robust tracking algorithm, which can be applied to practical engineering. The proposed algorithm divides all training samples into different training sets based on their similarities. An independent filter is trained for every training set. In each frame of the tracking process, the similarity between the candidate region and any training set's training samples is calculated to select the most matched filter for target location. As a newly introduced training sample, a feature map within the current frame's estimated target bounding box is assigned to the most similar training set to update the most matched filter. The updating of each filter is relatively independent. Each filter corresponds to one kind of target's typical appearance, and thus, the proposed tracking algorithm can memorize a variety of typical target appearances that appeared in the past and adapt to target's discontinuous appearance change. The detector improves tracking accuracy and assists occlusion judgment. After occlusion, the target may reappear with a different posture. As long as similar postures have been captured in the previous tracking process, the target can be retrieved accurately while not being confused with other objects of the target's category. We evaluated our method on massive videos shot in actual engineering sites, and the result demonstrates that the proposed tracking algorithm can handle occlusion and target's posture changes very well and significantly outperforms other tracking algorithms.

Poor efficiency and long running time of existent optimization algorithms in dealing with multi-objective multi-variable community microgrid optimization have always been a concern. To address this issue, a novel layered optimization algorithm based on NSGA-II is proposed. The proposed algorithm integrates the structural feature of community microgrid and the concept of multi-agent system into the optimization process and decomposes the complex microgrid optimization into several household optimizations of smaller scale and one central microgrid optimization. The household operation is optimized first and the central microgrid optimization is solved subsequently based on the Pareto solution set of household operation problems to obtain the optimal operation mode. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy is effective in improving optimization efficiency.

The purpose of this study was to determine the characteristics that make a professor more likely to succeed in achieving student engagement when moving from a face-to-face teaching environment to synchronous online `. This study presents a comparison of student outcomes between the traditional face-to-face model and the synchronous online model. The experimental group consisted of 118 courses with 2563 students, who received their classes online in the fall of 2017. The control group had a similar size; they received traditional face-to-face classroom instruction in the fall of 2016. The teachers were the same in the two periods. The statistical results showed differences between the two groups and allowed us to list the characteristics of the teachers who achieved student engagement in the synchronous online model. We conclude that the teachers who succeed in engaging students in the online courses are characteristically young, excellent in technology management, good with interpersonal interactions and maintain a robust social presence; or they are experienced teachers proficient in the use of technology, very well trained in didactic techniques, and who competently manage transactional distances.

Sea urchins can easily navigate a wide range of challenging environments through the coordinated action of thousands of individually addressable rigid protective spines and flexible, reversibly adhesive tube feet. To investigate the potential implementation of these unusual locomotory appendages in a robotic context, we describe here the design, fabrication, and characterization of an untethered sea urchin-inspired robot driven by fluidic soft actuators. Due to the intrinsic design and fabrication difficulties in attempting to replicate the complexity of an adult sea urchin, we instead focused our attention on the development of a design that closely mimicked the body plan of an anatomically much simpler post-larval juvenile urchin. Consistent with its biological counterpart, our robotic prototype contained five flexible tube feet and ten rigid spines that could be independently driven by soft tripod actuators. Through the incorporation of permanent magnets into the distal ends of the flexible tube feet, our sea urchin-inspired robot could easily navigate across ferrous surfaces while adopting gaits and defensive postures that were surprisingly similar to its biological analog.

It is widely accepted that Serious Games (SG) are efficient and effective tools that offer solutions for the medical field, particularly in the therapeutic area, and offer numerous benefits. To support rehabilitation doctors in adopting a particular therapeutic game from the available options, it is necessary to provide them with an easy-to-use model based on user-friendly, ergonomic graphical schemes that enable them to create and design therapeutic games efficiently. This approach enhances the intrinsic motivation of the patients and helps the doctors recover enough data for interpretation, allowing them to measure their patients' progress.

The primary focus of this research is to design specific serious games that are tailored towards doctors, rather than regular games. This is done to help them set up their games in a way that recovers enough data that is useful for interpreting their patients' progress. Our technique involves using production games design that allows rehabilitation doctors to participate in designing therapeutic games via KINECT sensor based on the patients' states and motivation. These games help with the medical re-education of cognitive disorders such as upper and lower limb movement disorders.

In summary, our work aims to develop a specialized model that enables rehabilitation doctors to create tailored therapeutic games that meet the needs of their patients. This approach not only accelerates the patients' progress, but it also makes it easier for doctors to evaluate the data and interpret it effectively. Ultimately, our goal is to improve the effectiveness of physical therapy by creating a personalized gaming experience for patients that offer significant benefits for rehabilitation doctors.

Low-rank tensor recovery in the presence of sparse but arbitrary errors is an important problem with many practical applications. In this work, we propose a general framework that recovers low-rank tensors, in which the data can be deformed by some unknown transformations and corrupted by arbitrary sparse errors. We give a unified presentation of the surrogate-based formulations that incorporate the features of rectification and alignment simultaneously, and establish worst-case error bounds of the recovered tensor. In this context, the state-of-the-art methods `RASL' and `TILT' can be viewed as two special cases of our work, and yet each only performs part of the function of our method. Subsequently, we study the optimization aspects of the problem in detail by deriving two algorithms, one based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and the other based on proximal gradient. We provide convergence guarantees for the latter algorithm, and demonstrate the performance of the former through in-depth simulations. Finally, we present extensive experimental results on public datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework and algorithms.

This paper presents a preliminary study investigating the potential of introducing robot technologies to therapists' work environments, including therapy preparation, management, and sessions. To begin this exploration, we conducted expert interviews, ideation, and prototyping as part of a design thinking workshop. The results showed that therapists desire technological support, in particular, systematic data collection, easy-to-use teaching aids, and effective communication with parents. With these needs in mind, robotics and therapy professionals joined together to develop technological solutions. During the prototyping phase, the professionals from each group created a robot-assisted therapy scenario-based design. The workshop concluded with therapy professionals advising that the ideal robot technologies incorporate expressive robotic platforms with autonomous modules that attract children's attention and motivate them. In addition, auxiliary sensors should gather the children's data installed in the environment, there should be a customizable software environment to program the robot, and a data server for managing and sharing children's data with therapists, doctors, teachers, and parents for consistent treatment. This conclusion provides a clear path for the development of robots for children with developmental disorders.

The problem of improving the processes of professional training of operators (by the example of operators of the portal crane) during training using computer simulators is considered. Computer technologies, in particular, simulators of technological installations and automated training systems, are widely used in the training of professional personnel. This contributes to the reduction of the human factor in the control of complex processes, as a result, the reduction of industrial injuries and emergency situations. However, the problem of automating the learning process in order to shape the future operator with the required level of sensorimotor skills is not well understood. The paper presents models and algorithms of the control system for the formation of operator sensomotor skills. Models and algorithms allow you to control the dynamics of the formation of skills as a multi-step process based on iterative learning. The practical implementation of the proposed scientific results on the training complex provides the necessary level of information support for the student and increases the efficiency of acquiring the ability to self-monitor the quality of technological operations.

While lexical and syntactic theories for phrase analyses have been extensively studied in linguistic theories and computational linguistics, semantic synthesis theories for cognitive computing remain a challenge in machine learning and brain-inspired systems. To address this, this paper examines theories and mathematical models of machine knowledge learning and semantic comprehension, and proposes the Algorithm of Unsupervised Phrase Learning (AUPL). The AUPL allows cognitive machines to autonomously learn phrase semantics in the sixth category of machine knowledge learning, and a set of experimental results is presented to demonstrate its efficacy. This work is essential for sentence learning, where the semantics of natural languages are reduced to those of phrases and terminal words represented by formal concepts in cognitive systems.

Drug behavior within the human body is complex and is typically described using pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) models. These models attempt to establish a relationship between drug behavior and elapsed time; however, as the relationship is highly intricate, even nonlinear regression algorithms tend to face challenges when identifying this relationship. 

To streamline this process, this paper proposes the simplification of the PK/PD model, which is based on the 3-compartment model, by applying the perturbation method. Specifically, a logistic model and a Gompertz growth model are analytically derived, which are easier to identify than the original PK/PD model. 

To validate the effectiveness of these simplified models, they are applied to clinical data, and it was found that their errors were less than 5% when compared with the PK/PD model. The simplified models, being simpler and easier to identify, hold immense potential in predicting the transition of drug effects and enabling the automatic correction of affected biosignals.

Internet of Things (IoT) security becomes of great importance, as IoT is the foundation for many emerging services. To safeguard IoT security, cryptosystems at upper layer relying on sophisticated key management alone can face many challenges due to the massive deployment of resource constrained machine-type communication (MTC) devices. Physical layer (PHY) security can complement and enhance IoT security, by exploiting the characteristics of the bottom layer. In PHY security, channel state information (CSI) estimated through reverse pilot training is essential for the sender to select appropriate beamforming/precoder, which however is also vulnerable to adversaries. An adversary can actively launch pilot contamination attacks to affect the channel estimation and improve its signal reception quality. In this paper, we propose a relay-aided vectorized (RAV) secure transmission scheme, to safeguard the downlink communication in IoT networks under potential pilot contamination attacks. The proposed scheme does not distinguish the pilot sequences sent from an adversary and the receiver; and the sender utilizes what it receives to estimate the CSI for beamforming/precoder design. Then, a set of data symbols are presuperposed using a random complex matrix to form signal vectors to send. Through cooperation with a relay, the signal vectors can be recovered by the intended receiver whereas the adversary or the relay cannot, as proved through security analysis. The simulation results also demonstrate that the bit error rate (BER) of the adversary is 0.5 regardless of its channel quality, indicating perfect secrecy is achieved.

Low-rank tensor recovery is a significant issue with a wide range of practical applications. It is mainly concerned with deformed data due to unknown transformations and affected by arbitrary sparse errors. In this research, we propose a comprehensive mechanism that restores low-rank tensors while integrating rectification and alignment. We also establish worst-case error bounds of the recovered tensor. Our innovative approach can be viewed as an all-in-one solution compared to the state-of-the-art methods, which can only handle parts of the issue. Moreover, we derived two algorithms, ADMM, and proximal gradient, to address the optimization aspects of the problem. We provide convergence guarantees for the latter algorithm and conduct extensive simulations for the former algorithm. Finally, we showcase the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework and algorithms through comprehensive experimental results on public datasets.

Cyanobacterial blooms have become an increasingly significant problem, adversely affecting ecosystems and human health. The objective of this study is to recommend pre-control plans that can systematically manage the risks associated with cyanobacteria by exploring the complex causal relationship involving multiple variables. The research is challenging due to three main reasons. Firstly, the time-series trajectories of cyanobacteria are characterized by deep uncertainties and nonlinear dynamics. Secondly, there are often hidden latent variables that provide additional information in such intricate aquatic systems. Thirdly, identifying an effective pre-control mechanism that takes into account the preferential regulation of variables is difficult. Therefore, we propose a latent variable structured Bayesian network model alongside an associated parameter learning algorithm. We test the model using real-time spatio-temporal data, the computational results of which reveal that the model performs better in terms of inference accuracy and providing a comprehensive understanding of the system. Sensitivity and combination-effect analyses are used to propose a systematic risk pre-control scheme that can be implemented by decision-makers to avoid cyanobacterial blooms in the context of global warming.

Massive machine-type communication (mMTC) is a key component of the internet of things (IoT) and concerns the access of massive machine-type communication devices to the base station. To support massive connectivity, grant-free access and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) have been recently introduced. In grant-free transmission, each device transmits information without the granting process, so the base station needs to identify the active devices among all potential devices. This process, called active user detection (AUD), is a challenging problem in NOMA-based systems as it is difficult to find out the active devices from the superimposed received signal.

This paper proposes a new type of AUD scheme suitable for highly overloaded mMTC, referred to as Dimension Spreading Deep Neural Network-based AUD (DSDNN-AUD). The key feature of DSDNN-AUD is to set the dimension of hidden layers larger than the size of a transmit vector to improve the representation quality of the support. In doing so, the proposed scheme can better discriminate the supports generated from a correlated structured environment. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms conventional approaches in both AUD success probability and throughput performance.

For solving the problem of sequence failure diagnosis of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) water management subsystem, this paper proposes a PEMFC failure diagnosis method of time series based on the bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE). This approach adopts the normalization strategy to eliminate the influence caused by dimensional differences of different parameters. The t-SNE is presented to decrease the dimensionality of normalized data to the estimate of intrinsic dimensionality to extract key characteristic variables. The width of the diagnostic window is set to transform the original single moment diagnosis problem into the fault diagnosis problem of multi-variable time series, which is more consistent with the time scale and physical evolution law of the PEMFC water management fault generation. The 672 sets of training sets and 448 sets of test sets are learned and tested by the BiLSTM. The experimental results show that the BiLSTM-tSNE method can realize the sequence fault diagnosis of the PEMFC water management subsystem with 96.88% diagnostic accuracy and 24 s of operation time. Compared with the conventional approach of multi-class support vector machine algorithm, the training accuracy and the testing accuracy of the proposed method are improved by 15% and 16.88%, respectively. The operation time of the presented approach is only about 1/28 of the multi-class support vector machine algorithm.

In this paper we propose a deep learning framework for classification of malware. There has been an enormous increase in the volume of malware generated lately which represents a genuine security danger to organizations and people. So as to battle the expansion of malwares, new strategies are needed to quickly identify and classify malware. Malimg dataset, a publicly available benchmark data set was used for the experimentation. The architecture used in this work is a hybrid cost-sensitive network of one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network which obtained an accuracy of 94.4%, an increase in performance compared to work done by [1] which got 84.9%. Hyper parameter tuning is done on deep learning architecture to set the parameters. A learning rate of 0.01 was taken for all experiments. Train-test split of 70-30% was done during experimentation. This facilitates to find how well the models perform on imbalanced data sets. Usual methods like disassembly, decompiling, de-obfuscation or execution of the binary need not be done in this proposed method. The source code and the trained models are made publicly available for further research.

To ensure successful operation of power systems in the present era where there is increased variability in climate and more penetration of Renewable Energy (RE), it is necessary to have accurate and efficient forecasting of RE power generation. Therefore, this paper utilizes a multi-layer Feed Forward Artificial Neural Network (FF-ANN) model to train datasets for short term wind power forecasting. The process involves two key steps, training and forecasting. To optimize the parameters for FF-ANN, the Levenberg Marquadrt (LM) learning algorithm is utilized during the training stage. For wind power forecasting, a new technique is proposed, known as the Weighted Least Square Error Correlation method (WLSEC), which was implemented using the C++ platform. The model's performance was tested with practical wind power data for one year, specifically in one of the southern states in India, with hourly resolution. The results show that the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for forecasting wind power hourly is 7.32% with the proposed WLSEC method, while it is 9% with the Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). This comparison demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model for short term wind power forecasting.

Research and development of dialog robots for the purpose of conversation has been actively conducted in recent years. Many of these robot technologies are specialized in language information such as speech recognition and sentence comprehension. However, the majority of the information that human beings emphasize during dialog is nonverbal information. Even in the same words, the meaning of words changes as voice tones, expressions and gesture change. In order for a robot to realize a smooth dialog like a human being, it is important to combine language information and nonverbal information. Therefore, this paper focus on speech information and head motion to estimate the confidence of the user. The confidence conditions were defined as five-level status according to the questionnaire answer: most confident, comparative certainty, neutral, relative uncertain, most unconfident. Two experiments were conducted in this paper. The first experiment was conducted machine learning by summarizing all data of participants. The second experiment was conducted machine learning for each participant with increasing the number of data per participant. The best results could be classified as the most confident/unconfident with an accuracy of 91.3% analyzed by multilayer perceptron (MLP) via Weka. Accuracy increased by about 31% over the first experiment. This is considered to be the reason that the characteristics of individuals were manifested by doing machine learning with data of each participant.

With the widespread use of smartphones, location information has become increasingly important. Our objective is to accurately estimate smartphone positions within a few centimeters of error. Additionally, we aim to identify patterns in people's behaviors and their areas of interest. These data will enable the development of new services, such as providing information about exhibits at event venues based on their positions.

One promising method for estimating a position with few centimeters error is dynamic magnetism. This approach relies on the frequency of dynamic magnetism to determine position, allowing it to function even in strong environmental magnetism. However, applying this method to smartphones presents a challenge, as the sampling frequency of the magnetic sensor mounted on a smartphone is much lower than the frequency required for dynamic magnetism.

To address this issue, we developed the Spinning Magnetic Marker (SMM), which generates dynamic magnetism through the motion of a strong magnet. Using this device, we proposed a positioning method based on dynamic magnetism that can be applied to smartphones. Our new method involves estimating the short-range path of a smartphone through the use of the hyperbolic function and curve fitting with the magnetism equation.

In conclusion, our proposed approach represents a significant advancement in the estimation of smartphone positions and the recognition of behavior patterns. It has major implications for the development of new services that depend on accurate location information, particularly in event venues and other large spaces.

The human visual system has the ability to recognize complex objects in cluttered natural scenes with ease. In order to develop machine vision systems that can mimic this ability, numerous computational models have been developed. HMAX is considered one of the best computational models and is inspired by the hierarchical structure of the human visual cortex. However, during the learning stage of HMAX, a large number of patches are extracted at random which degrades performance and increases computational complexity.

To address this drawback, we propose a new method based on information theory to select relevant patches and remove redundant ones. Our method is developed for a face categorization task, where the goal is to detect the presence or absence of faces in real-world images. We evaluated the performance of our method on the CalTech101 face image database and observed that our method outperformed the original HMAX by more than 5%.

Integrating low-power profile networks such as LPWAN (Low Power Wide Area Network) and WPAN (Wireless Personal Area Networks) can enable new IoT (Internet of Things) applications for Smart Cities in a cost-effective manner. The combination of LPWAN LoRA and WPAN BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) technologies found in low-cost devices, utilizing unlicensed frequencies, can lead to the development of applications that can transmit long-range data up to 45 kilometers while consuming low energy, and requiring minimal cost and easy implementation. This eliminates the need for mobile operators and simplifies the process further. In this study, we aim to integrate LPWAN and WPAN with LoRa and BLE using Fog/Edge Computing. This approach will enable procedures to be performed at the network edges, and allow only consolidated data to transmit to the cloud.
