Smart grid is the advancement of conventional grid with the help of computational intelligence and networking abilities of various communication networks to develop sustainable, robust, efficient and resilient power grid. Smart grid considered to be the next generation power grid, using bidirectional stream of electricity. For effective operation of smart grid, it is necessary to have secure interoperable and efficient communication network among the electronic gadgets used in smart grid as well as in consumers' premises. Efficient communication and optimization schemes is required for the data exchange among the communication modules to optimize the power system. In this paper, We present a survey of communication technologies for smart grid.

Person Re-Identification (Re-ID) refers to the process of tracking a person's movements as they traverse through camera-equipped zones. It involves matching the identities of humans captured in non-overlapping surveillance cameras. To reduce multi-camera matching errors, we propose a new low-dimensional metric space learning approach. Our method involves handcrafting the features of training and test samples and performing a two-step ranking using elementary distance metrics, followed by an ensemble of weighted binary classifiers. We evaluated our approach on the CUHK01 and PRID450s datasets and achieved impressive CMC Rank-1 results of up to 61.1 and 75.4, respectively, with only one sample per class for the probe and one sample for the gallery (single-shot). Our results follow the leading literature protocols and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

This work proposes a new method to accurately complete sparse LiDAR maps guided by RGB images. For autonomous vehicles and robotics the use of LiDAR is indispensable in order to achieve precise depth predictions. A multitude of applications depend on the awareness of their surroundings, and use depth cues to reason and react accordingly. On the one hand, monocular depth prediction methods fail to generate absolute and precise depth maps. On the other hand, stereoscopic approaches are still significantly outperformed by LiDAR based approaches. The goal of the depth completion task is to generate dense depth predictions from sparse and irregular point clouds which are mapped to a 2D plane. We propose a new framework which extracts both global and local information in order to produce proper depth maps. We argue that simple depth completion does not require a deep network. However, we additionally propose a fusion method with RGB guidance from a monocular camera in order to leverage object information and to correct mistakes in the sparse input. This improves the accuracy significantly. Moreover, confidence masks are exploited in order to take into account the uncertainty in the depth predictions from each modality. This fusion method outperforms the state-of-the-art and ranks first on the KITTI depth completion benchmark [21]. Our code with visualizations is available at https://github.com/wvangansbeke/Sparse-Depth-Completion.

The mobility load balancing (MLB) in self-organizing networks (SONs) is designed to efficiently allocate network resources to match network traffic demand. To tackle this challenge, we propose an off-policy deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based MLB framework that automates the load distribution for all cells. Our framework has three main contributions. Firstly, we suggest using off-policy RL with multiple behavior policies to learn the optimal MLB policy autonomously without prior knowledge of the underlying wireless environments. Secondly, we present a corresponding DRL-based MLB model that employs deep neural networks to boost generalization capabilities over complex system states. Finally, we propose an asynchronous parallel learning framework for MLB, which enhances training efficiency through a collaborative approach. Our experimental results indicate that our proposed DRL-based MLB model significantly outperforms current methods.

Relational databases have become ubiquitous in both the sciences and other fields. One of the main challenges is identifying hot spots of user interests, which can be done by clustering queries in the query log. However, meaningful query similarity is required for effective clustering. Previous query representations and similarity functions all had limitations, which led us to propose new similarity functions for SQL queries based on the access area, specifically the overlap and closeness of the access areas. Through systematic experiments, we showed that our new measures of similarity produced good indicators of user interests, as evidenced by the quality of clustering and comparison to a ground truth, as well as hand interpretation of clusters in the SkyServer database by a domain expert.

Camera pose estimation is an important problem in many applications that need localization of cameras, devices, or instruments in robotics, surgical operations, and augmented-reality. It is important to provide a cost-effective, real-time, accurate, and easy to use system for pose estimation. There are two kinds of optical tracking methods employed by camera pose estimation algorithms, model-based versus feature based methods. Here, we developed a feature-based camera pose estimationmethodutilizing justonesingle camera and a large marker. The keypoint features from the scene image and the marker are detected by Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF) detector. Then, their descriptors are extracted by Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) and they are matched using Brute Force matching (BF). A perspective transform is supposed to map the coordinates of the image keypoints to the coordinates of the corresponding 3D points in the marker.This problem is solved by OpenCV functionsand the final camera pose matrix is obtained. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a 3D printed calibrator with known placeholder positions. The proposed system can be realized usinga smartphone camera (in webcam mode) and a large marker on the wall. As results show, the proposed method achieves acceptable accuracy namely an average error of approximately 1.4 cm for position and 0.02 radianfor orientation.

On the basis of summarizing and analyzing the core technical architecture of WebRTC, the function and construction process of Room Server, Signaling Server and STUN/TURN/ICE Server are emphasized. Finally, using the Java programming language, the mobile video/audio system is developed based on WebRTC on the Android Studio platform. It realizes the point-to-point real-time audio/video communication between two mobile phones, and has good effect, and it is used for reference to the rapid development of the similar audio/video services.

The paper presents a new methodological approach to the automated construction of software for solving the design problems of heating systems. The methodological approach is based on the Model-Driven Engineering paradigm. The essence of this paradigm is that the software is generated on the basis of formal description represented by models. The knowledge about heating systems, applied problems, and the applied software is formalized in the form of ontologies. The automated construction of the software system is performed on the basis of a computer model of a heating system, the ontologies and modern metaprogramming technologies. The proposed approach allows us to successfully solve the problem of separation of methods for solving applied problems and models of heating system elements. To this end, the methods are implemented in the form of software components that are not related to properties and models of specific equipment. And the models of heating system elements are automatically compiled into software components. In the process of software system construction, software components that implement models and methods are integrated dynamically. As a result, the software system oriented to solving a specific applied problem is created in an automated mode. The developed approach has been used for the implementation of the SOSNA software. The software is applied to design urban heating systems.

This paper introduces a mathematical framework for state estimation of dynamic systems when a simplified and rough model is available. The approach considers estimation variation as a possible source of uncertainty, and focuses on the discrete-time case and filtering problem. To solve this problem, the Regularized Least Squares (RLS) algorithm is modified and nonsmooth analysis tools are utilized. The algorithm identifies an optimal region in the innovation space where no variation of estimation is best. Real-time applications are also discussed, and a numeric example is provided to demonstrate the advantages of this approach.

Modelling information flows is essential for understanding organisational communication and managing business functions effectively. The LINQ technique offers a new approach to modelling organisational information flows, and previous research has proven its effectiveness in capturing the dynamics of information flows. However, to enhance LINQ's utility, it is necessary to incorporate business rules in its framework.

To address this issue, the current study proposes extending LINQ with the norm analysis method. The norm analysis method defines business rules, conditions and constraints for controlling information flows within the organisation. By integrating the norm analysis method, the extended LINQ can accommodate conditional business rules and facilitate better modelling of information flows in businesses.

To demonstrate the effectiveness of the extended LINQ technique, it was applied to a real case study. The findings of the study indicate that the technique enabled analysts to model information flows and incorporate conditional business rules, thereby improving the overall effectiveness of the business processes.

Overall, the extended LINQ technique offers significant potential for organisations to model and manage their information flows more effectively. By incorporating business rules and constraints, businesses can gain a better understanding of their internal communication dynamics and improve their overall efficiency.

Efficient analysis of the health status of core router systems is crucial for maintaining high reliability and timely error recovery. Unfortunately, due to high computational complexity and expensive labor costs, only a small portion of the large amount of operational data collected from core routers is labeled by experts, making it difficult to adopt supervised learning.

To address this challenge, we propose an iterative self-learning procedure for evaluating the health status of a core router. First, we compute a representative feature matrix that captures various characteristics of time-series data, including statistical-modeling-based features from three general categories and recurrent neural network-based autoencoder to identify a wider range of hidden patterns. Additionally, we apply the minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance (mRMR) method and fully connected feedforward autoencoder to further reduce the dimensionality of the extracted feature matrix.

We employ hierarchical clustering to infer labels for the remaining unlabeled dataset, and finally, we build a classifier that iteratively updates using both labeled and unlabeled dataset. We experimentally validate the proposed health-status analyzer using field data collected from a set of commercial core routers.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed feature-based self-learning health analyzer achieves higher precision and recall than the traditional supervised health analyzer as well as the currently deployed rule-based health analyzer. Moreover, it performs better than the three anomaly detection baseline methods under the transformed binary classification scenario.

This paper represents an optimization method as well as energy management strategy of grid connected renewable energy sources for multi house. Optimization method has been accomplished using HOMER software to bring out optimal size of renewable sources and other components for management strategy. The main purpose of this paper is to design an energy management strategy to optimize the cost and minimize the power loss of extracted power from renewable energy sources based on Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). The system consists of PV array, AC wind generator, Battery, Converter and grid. FLC monitors load profile and delivers a signal to sources. Then FLC changes the switch for appropriate energy supply according to fuzzy rules. The management strategy is controlled by FLC in a way that extra power after meeting the energy demand of the house can be sold to the national grid which is more useful and cost feasible than any other conventional systems. The proposed management strategy is more effective than any other traditional systems which must minimize power loss.

Navigating through the vast and uncertain web of data has become increasingly challenging with the classical methods used in the past proving inadequate for handling uncertain web data and resources. Web data, publications and resources can often be heterogeneous, inconsistent, contain conflicting information or be in incompatible formats. Addressing the inherent uncertainty in web data is key to providing a positive user experience and delivering relevant answers. In this paper, we propose a probabilistic approach for modelling and interpreting uncertain web resources. As part of our approach, we present several operators that can be used to compute the uncertainty of the response. Additionally, we propose specific algorithms aimed at validating resources and facilitating uncertain navigation.

The issue of integrating the large population of deaf-mute individuals in China into mainstream society has become a significant concern. One promising solution involves the use of efficient sign language processing technologies to facilitate communication. Sign language processing involves the systematic recognition and translation of sign language images or videos to text or speech.

This survey provides an overview of the most important research on Chinese sign language recognition and translation, including its classification and the various features explored in sign language recognition. Additionally, it explores the available datasets and provides insights into future trends in this area of research.

Overall, sign language processing technologies offer tremendous potential for empowering deaf-mute individuals and promoting greater inclusion in mainstream society. As such, continued research in this field will undoubtedly play a crucial role in improving the lives of people with hearing disabilities in China and beyond.

We focus on the computation methods for analyzing the bumblebee behavior. In this paper, we recover the smooth 3D trajectory for flying bumblebee by stereo vision by employing EKF. We also tackle the matching problem when more than one targets appeared in the views. A variable length sliding window method is proposed to segment the 3D trajectory into three basic types. In our experiment, we show our method has more accuracy result than the state art of work.

Cooperative human–agent–robot teamwork (HART) provides enormous opportunities for present-day human users to orchestrate their real-time tasks in a coordinated fashion. However, given human users’ different preferences for real-time HART task execution, e.g., lower delay and monetary cost, the selection of proper task coordination services has emerged as an important research problem by taking dynamically changing cloud agent/robot resources, network bandwidth utilization, as well as delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant HART task properties into account. To cope with these challenges, in this paper, we explore the synergy between caching, computation, and communications for achieving cost-effective HART task execution. To exploit the locality of different HART-centric tasks and local/non-local cloud agent/robot resources for different HART-centric task execution, we consider integrated fiber-wireless (FiWi) enhanced networks with computation task offloading as well as fiber backhaul sharing and WiFi offloading capabilities. More precisely, to minimize task execution delay and monetary cost, we propose a user preference aware HART task coordination framework that selects the appropriate dedicated or non-dedicated robot and cloud agent for given caching and computing HART task execution requirements. Further, to cope with varying bandwidth resources, we propose a proactive bandwidth allocation policy for the execution of both delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant HART tasks execution across FiWi enhanced network infrastructures. We evaluate the performance of our proposed preference aware task offloading scheme and compare it to various baseline schemes in terms of different key performance indicators, including the task execution time and monetary cost saving ratio, communication to computation ratio, and offloading gain overhead ratio. Our findings indicate that the proposed delay cost saving policy exhibits a 27% higher task execution time saving ratio and a 48% lower monetary cost saving ratio than the proposed monetary cost saving policy in a typical scenario.

In today's social media, especially twitter is very important for the success and destruction of one's image due to the many sentences of opinion that can compete the users. Examples of phrases that mean evil refer to hate speech to others. Evil perspectives can be categorized in hate speech, which hate speech is regulated in Article 28 of the ITE Law. Not a few people who intentionally and unintentionally oppose a social media that contains hate speech. Unfortunately, social media do not have the ability to aggregate information about an existing conversation into a conclusion. One way to draw conclusions from aggregation results is to use text mining. In this Final Project to classify whether the text in the sentence contains elements of hate speech or not. The author hopes in this final project can make how to classify element of hate speech in text by computer, which later speech of hate can be recognized. By using an Artificial Neural Network method optimized with Backpropagation algorithm. The author hopes after this application the computer can know and classify the existence of hate speech on a text from social media twitter. From the results of tests that have been done the average precision of 80.664%, recall 90.07%, and Accuracy of 89.47%.

Making decisions during a disaster can be challenging when human lives and infrastructures are exposed. An important factor to consider when allocating resources, in these situations, is the critical infrastructures' interdependencies. i2Sim, the Infrastructures' Interdependencies Simulator, is a tool build for that purpose. As a layered architecture, i2Sim includes a dedicated decision-making layer. The use of Reinforcement Learning (RL), a machine learning approach based on an agent learning from experience, has been successfully tested with some dimensionality constraints. This paper introduces two improvements to our previous tests aiming at increasing speed and allowing larger dimensionality problems. The first addition is an improved reward scheme for speeding up convergence while guaranteeing it. The correct application of shaping rewards requires a deep understanding of the problem and extensive convergence tests. The second improvement added is the implementation of a scheduler programmed to trigger multiple instances of the same model using different parameters. This scheduler partitions the state space, enabling the agent's training to be done in parallel via a distributed RL algorithm. With this idea, the state/action matrix representing knowledge is partitioned for training, assigned to computing nodes, populated with knowledge (trained) and collected/reconstructed for use. This work has tested on an IBM cluster with 24 computing nodes. The test model is an aggregated model of the City of Vancouver configured for a disaster with numerous consequences over the different critical infrastructures. Based on the model's configuration, 24 scenarios were identified, created and solved simultaneously. The scheduler automates the training by setting up model and learning parameters, looping execution of instances and gathering results from all nodes. The results verify a proof of concept and enable applicability to new models with highly increased dimensionalities.

Deep learning shows great potential in the field of medical diagnosis. However, the success of training a disease discrimination model heavily relies on a large number of training samples. Unfortunately, in many scenarios, it is challenging to obtain enough high-quality training images, making it challenging to achieve good results. 

To tackle this issue, a new method called small sample expansion (SSE) has been proposed. SSE leverages user feedback to label a tiny number of training images and performs feature transformation in key areas to automatically expand the training set. Using the example of trichocryptosis diagnosis, the experimental results showed an improvement in accuracy rate and conviction rate with the implementation of SSE. 

Overall, SSE shows significant potential in generating more training data with minimal human input, which can enhance the efficacy of deep learning in medical diagnosis.

Global growth in participation in higher education has helped to increase diversity of students, and traditionally underrepresented minorities on gender, income and math skills have expanded their presence in engineering education. Nevertheless, late dropout has increased and the number of engineering graduates remains low in western world. The analysis of educational trajectories using process mining techniques can help to explain the relationship between a sequence of academic results and late dropout. This case study seeks to answer how gender, income and entry math skills may explain differences on educational trajectories of engineering students in high-failure rate courses that lead to late dropout. Academic records for 794 engineering students at Universidad Austral de Chile that belongs to cohorts 2007 to 2009, were extracted and analyzed using process mining discovery techniques. Models of educational trajectories on high-failure rate courses were created and then analyzed using the Investment Model as a reference framework. Findings reveal the following: late dropout is related to the number of consecutive semesters that a student maintain pending failed courses; low-income students and those with low entry math skills tend to be more persistent, even if they have unsatisfactory trajectories; female students tend to be more risk-averse when they have unsatisfactory results. Understanding the educational trajectories of students who end in late dropout can help managers and policy makers to improve the curriculum, entry conditions and programs that support disadvantaged students.

Authorship attribution is the task of identifying the author of an anonymous text from a set of potential candidates. In order to address this problem, we propose a novel method that utilizes an N-grams model. Our approach uses multiple measures to match an anonymous text with an author, and we have implemented and tested various versions of the method on PAN benchmarks.

The results of our experiments are highly promising, demonstrating the efficacy of our proposed approach. By leveraging the capabilities of N-grams and other measures, we are able to achieve accurate and reliable authorship attribution in a wide range of scenarios. This represents a significant advancement in the field, and has important implications for areas such as forensics, intelligence analysis, and more.

The computer aided diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) using multi-modality imaging data has become a challenging and compelling topic in recent years. Feature representation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis process. Previous studies have shown that deep learning (DL) methods have been successful in the field of feature representation learning, however, these methods still need to address the issues of overfitting and data insufficiency. In this study, we propose a stacked sparse auto-encoder (SSAE) based feature encoding algorithm. Our proposed SSAE effectively trains on a small-scale dataset and computes significant feature representation for PD diagnosis. 

We use longitudinal multi-modal neuroimaging data to learn the feature representation for PD diagnosis. Firstly, we train and test the baseline data using the 10-fold cross-validation method. Then we exploit the baseline data to train a classification model that can be used for the classification task in future time points. We conducted a series of experiments to verify the efficiency of our proposed method on the publicly available Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) dataset. Our experimental results showed that our algorithm works effectively on a small dataset and achieves remarkable classification results compared to existing DL methods.

The purpose of this research is to address the sustainability issue of a balancing robot, which is controlled by an artificial neural network acting as a regulator. The network calculates and outputs the control action of the robot, but any changes to its parameters or mode of functioning can affect the quality of the control, hence requiring online training of the network.

However, the rate at which the network learns needs to be limited to ensure the sustainability and stability of the control system. To this end, the researchers propose a method based on the second Lyapunov approach that calculates the allowable upper limit of the online learning rate under different conditions during the network's operation. Notably, this method doesn't require any mathematical model of the robot's plant.

Experiments conducted on a balancing robot using the EV3 platform have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach. By adopting this method, the sustainability of the control system can be maintained, thereby ensuring the smooth functioning of the balancing robot.

This paper addresses the output feedback sliding-mode control (SMC) problem for discrete-time uncertain nonlinear systems through Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy dynamic models. Combining with the sliding surface, a descriptor system is constructed to characterize the sliding motion dynamics. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability analysis of the sliding motion are attained by the piecewise quadratic Lyapunov functions within a convex optimization setup. Two SMC design approaches are proposed to ensure the finite-time convergence of the sliding surface. Two simulation examples are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

Lightweight cryptography has become more and more important in recent years because of the rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) and usage of smart mobile devices. In this paper, we propose a novel secure lightweight entity authentication hardware primitive called SLATE, where its area is about 50% to more than 3X smaller than existing lightweight ciphers and strong physical unclonable functions (PUFs), respectively. Even though the authentication of SLATE is done through challenge response pair (CRP) verification similar to strong PUFs, the source of the key for SLATE must be coming from any existing secret key storage used for any ciphers. A main advantage of SLATE over most existing strong PUFs being an entity authentication primitive is that SLATE is resistant to known attacks to strong PUFs or logic obfuscations, such as model building attacks and Boolean satisfiability (SAT) attacks. Furthermore, we show that the implementation cost of SLATE with a 176-bit key and 244 CRPs is only 663 gate equivalents (GEs). Compared with lightweight ciphers and existing secure strong PUFs, we show that SLATE is a practical security primitive for resource constrained systems for its extremely small footprint and security. Finally, we show that SLATE is information theoretically secure when valid CRPs are communicated through insecure channels.

This paper investigates the framework and characteristics of positive approximation sets and proposes a novel attribute reduction algorithm to accelerate existing approaches for incomplete decision tables. The proposed tolerance relation based algorithm (IFSPA) improves the performance of heuristic reduction algorithms, which is verified through a series of experiments using real-life data sets. The simulation results demonstrate that the improved algorithms output the same reducts as the original ones but in a shorter time and more stable manner.

In this brief, we analyze a class of second-order memristive neural networks (SMNNs) that have mixed time-varying delays. Our investigation utilizes nonsmooth analysis, Lyapunov stability theory, and adaptive control theory to derive several novel insights that guarantee the global stabilization of SMNNs. Unlike the prior approach of using a reduced-order method, we directly consider the SMNNs’ inherent properties for ensuring global stabilization. To demonstrate the efficacy of our results, we present numerical simulations.

In this paper, we delve into the implementation of a pilot-based space-time transmission scheme (STTS) for a large multiple input multiple output (MIMO) communication system. Our aim is to accurately estimate the channel state information (CSI) with the aid of orthogonal pilot sequences and null space concept incorporated in the design of the STTS. We employ the maximum-likelihood decoding method for signal detection. To measure the performance of the proposed system, we derive an approximate expression for the symbol error rate (SER) using the moment generating function of the instantaneous received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

We are focused on dynamic crosstalk-aware lightpath provisioning in translucent space-division multiplexing (SDM) elastic optical networks. These networks use spectral super-channels carried over multi-core fibers (MCFs) with distance-adaptive transmission and back-to-back (B2B) signal regeneration. Our goal is to establish lightpaths for connection requests in a way that meets allowable threshold levels for inter-core crosstalk (XT) impairment, which affects the quality of lightpaths on the network. To this end, we propose and analyze a method based on per-core static/worst-case XT estimation. This method is implemented in a dynamic XT-aware routing, spatial mode, and spectrum allocation (RSSA) algorithm which efficiently solves the lightpath provisioning problem and minimizes bandwidth blocking probability. Our extensive simulation experiments in realistic network scenarios show the significant impact of this method on network performance and motivate its application instead of commonly used per-fiber worst-case XT estimation.

Objectives: Administrative HIS (Hospital Information System) and EHR (Electronic Health Record) data are characterized by lower privacy sensitivity, thus easier portability and handling, as well as higher information quality. In this paper we test the hypothesis that the application of machine learning techniques on data of this nature can be used to address prediction/forecasting problems in the Health IT domain. The novelty of this approach consists in that medical data (test results, diagnoses, doctors' notes etc.) are not included in the predictors' dataset. Moreover, there is limited need for separation of patient cohorts based on specific health conditions. Methods: We experiment with the prediction of the probability of early readmission at the time of a patient's discharge. We extract real HIS data and perform data processing techniques. We then apply a series of machine learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors and Deep Multilayer Neural Network) and measure the performance of the emergent models. Results: All applied methods performed well above random guessing, even with minimal hyper-parameter tuning. Conclusions: Given that the experiments provide evidence in favor of the underlying hypothesis, future experimentation on more fine-tuned (thus more robust) models could result in applications suited for productive environments.

In article describes an intellectual-information system that will be used to make managerial decisions on the operation of technical personnel of power plants and similar process facilities. In particular, the results of its work will help to make a decision on the appropriateness of upgrading the skills of technical personnel. The methods of intellectualization used to determine the level of knowledge based on odd logic allow not only to assess the level of knowledge, but also to automate the process of its consolidation and enhancement. The use of this method allows the training of technical personnel on the job. The method of intellectualization of an estimation of a level of knowledge of the basic theory of calculation of optimum feeding parameters of regulating devices of automatic control systems is described. Solving this problem in the example of automation evaluation on the parametric synthesis of one-loop, cascade and combined control systems. Control of the level of knowledge for parametric synthesis determined by the correct choice of a point on a graph of the amplitude-phase characteristics and D-partition graphs. The adequacy of established fuzzy output system tested in a program FuzzyTECH.

The number of available applications (apps) for smart devices and Android-based IoT (Internet of Things) has significantly increased in the past few years. However, along with this increase is a corresponding growth in ill-designed and malicious apps (malapps). Numerous approaches have been proposed to separate malapps from legitimate ones to make the app markets safer. Machine learning algorithms are often used in the classification process, and the accuracy of detecting malapps is directly influenced by the characterization of the apps' behaviors or features. Extracting effective and representative features from Android apps is an ongoing challenge due to the complexity of their behaviors and the ever-increasing size of their codes. Although several feature types have been extracted in previous studies, there is no comprehensive survey yet that systematically examines the features constructed for detecting Android malapps. In this paper, we provide a detailed and comprehensive survey of the current state-of-the-art works that detect malapps by exhibiting app behaviors with various feature types. We extracted 1947 papers based on our strict selection criteria, and 236 papers were used to conduct the survey using four dimensions: the features extracted, the method of feature selection applied (if any), the detection techniques used, and the extent of evaluation conducted. Our extensive survey highlights the challenges of extracting effective features from apps, provides a taxonomy of these features, and points to future research directions.

Software reliability is achieved through modeling and estimation, with existing models being nonlinear and difficult for parameter estimation. Optimization methods such as Artificial Bee Colony algorithm (ABC) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) can be used to solve these nonlinear function problems. ABC has the advantage of fewer control parameters, strong exploration, and high accuracy of solutions, while PSO algorithm has relatively small computation and fast search speed. However, PSO may lead to premature convergence and poor local search ability. To address this, a new fitness function based on maximum likelihood estimation is proposed, and a hybrid PSO-ABC method is used for parameter estimation, which removes wrong solutions, and adds knowledge to improve solution accuracy. Five classic software failure data sets are used to estimate GO model parameters, and the results are compared with other algorithms. The new fitness function and hybrid PSO-ABC method provide more accurate parameter estimation, and the hybrid PSO-ABC has an advantage in generality, especially with limited data.

The emergence of modern web frameworks, microservices, and cloud architectures requires testers to generate and maintain test cases, scripts, and data in short agile sprints, sometimes in as little as a few hours. It is impossible to produce these assets in a comprehensive manner using legacy DevOps approaches that largely depend on the subjective judgement of test engineers. In this paper, we demonstrate the implementation of ATARI, an autonomous testing framework that uses a combination of search algorithms, page-rank heuristics, and reinforcement learning techniques to radically improve the completeness and velocity of testing to meet the needs of modern software engineering practices.

In recent years, there has been a growing trend of multi-core processors being implemented in control-oriented embedded systems, such as those found in-vehicle systems. The use of multi-cores allows for improved performance when controlling objects. To facilitate the testing of program behavior and the evaluation of control performance for such systems, we have developed a simulation environment for multi-core processors.

Our simulator consists of two functions: a target CPU instruction simulator and a target OS simulator. It provides simulated functions corresponding to CPU instructions and OS functions, as well as predicted execution times in the target system. We developed a target CPU instruction simulator that offers assembler level translation and a synthesis of measured instruction execution times. To simulate the multi-core related APIs of an embedded OS, we utilized the multi-threaded functions of the host OS.

Our target CPU and embedded OS of choice were an RH850 by Renesas and an Autosar OS, respectively. These are both widely used in the automotive field. With our simulation environment, we can accurately test the performance of multi-core processors in control-oriented embedded systems and improve their efficiency.

In this paper, we propose a new Perceptually Optimized Embedded ZeroTree Image Coder EVIC and Quality Assessor WVDP. The coder introduces a perceptual weighting to wavelet coefficients prior to control SPIHT encoding algorithm in order to reach a targeted bit rate with a perceptual quality improvement with respect to the coding quality of the SPIHT algorithm only. The paper also, introduces a new objective quality metric based on Daly visual model known as Visible Difference Predictor that integrates the properties of the HVS and plays an important role in our EVIC quality assessment. Our EVIC coder is based on a vision model that incorporates various masking effects of human visual system HVS perception. Thus, our coder weights the wavelet coefficients based on that model and enhances the perceptual quality for a given bit rate and observation distance. The model weights within all wavelet sub bands are computed with respect to 1) luminance masking and Contrast masking deployed to ensure threshold elevation, 2) the contrast sensitivity function CSF to filter invisible frequencies, 3) the Just Noticeable Differences JND used to take into account only wavelet coefficients with respect to that perceptual thresholds. The EVIC coder has the same computational algorithm complexity as the standard SPIHT. However, the experimental results show that it demonstrates very good performances in terms of image coding and quality measurement.

In non-contact heart rate (HR) monitoring via Doppler radar, the disturbance from respiration and/or body motion is treated as a key problem on the estimation of HR. This paper proposes a blind source separation (BSS) approach to mitigate the noise effect in the received radar signal, and incorporates the sparse spectrum reconstruction to achieve a high-resolution of heartbeat spectrum. The proposed BSS decomposes the spectrogram of mixture signal into original sources, including heartbeat, using non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) algorithms, through learning the complete basis spectra (BS) by a hierarchical clustering. In particular, to exploit the temporal sparsity of heartbeat component, two variants of NMF algorithms with sparseness constraints are applied as well, namely sparse NMF and weighted sparse NMF. Compared with usual BSS, our proposed BSS has three advantages: 1) clustering-induced unsupervised manner; 2) compact demixing architecture; and 3) merely requiring single-channel input data. In addition, the HR estimation method using our proposal delivers more satisfactory precision and robustness over other existing methods, which is demonstrated through the measurements of distinguishing people's activities, gaining both smallest absolute errors of HR estimation for sitting still and typewriting.

In wireless sensor networks, sensor data collected by a wireless sensor node is transmitted to a stationary wireless sink node via a wireless multi-hop transmission route. On this route, intermediate wireless sensor nodes forward the data messages to their next-hop intermediate nodes, while broadcasting this data in their wireless transmission range. Unfortunately, this also means that eavesdropper wireless nodes within this range can easily overhear the data messages. To prevent illegal eavesdropping, wireless sensor nodes that have overlapping wireless transmission ranges avoid passing data messages to next-hop intermediate wireless sensor nodes within these overlapping regions, and deliberately cause collisions at possible eavesdropper wireless nodes. This paper proposes an algorithm that assigns specific time slots for transmitting data messages, which maximizes the opportunities for interfering with eavesdroppers and enhances the regions where concurrently forwarded data messages collide, thereby preventing their overhearing.

A learning-gain-adaptive iterative learning control (LGAILC) mechanism is utilized for a class of repetitive linear discrete-time-invariant systems with unit relative degree. The objective is to minimize the tracking-error energies at consecutive iterations using the iteration-time-variable learning-gain vector as the argument. Control input and system parameters are not considered in the performance index. The method involves rows/columns exchanging transformations and matrix theory to solve an explicit learning-gain vector that incorporates system Markov parameters and iteration-time-wise tracking errors. The orthogonality of the transformation leads to non-conditionally strict monotonic convergence of the LGAILC scheme. A pseudo-LGAILC strategy is developed to enhance system robustness to uncertainties in the Markov parameters. The strategy involves a system Markov parameter-based learning-gain vector that accounts for parameter uncertainties. Analysis shows that the pseudo strategy is also strictly monotonically convergent, indicating robustness to a wider range of parameter uncertainties. Numerical simulations support the validity and effectiveness of the method.

We are investigating stochastic team problems with a static information structure, where controllers have linear information and quadratic cost, but the noise can come from a non-Gaussian class. In the case of Gaussian noise, it is well-established that these problems have linear optimal controllers. However, we find that for linear-quadratic static teams with log-concave noise, linear strategies can approach optimality for "most" problems if the length of the noise or data vector is large in comparison to the team's size and observations. As the length of the noise vector increases, the approximation quality improves. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if the optimal strategies for log-concave noise problems pointwise converge, they converge to the (linear) optimal strategy for problems with Gaussian noise. We also derive an asymptotically tight error bound on the difference between the optimal cost for the non-Gaussian problem and the best cost obtained under linear strategies.

The transformation process of a smart city requires a robust technological and connectivity platform that promotes the development of a more efficient, flexible, and cost-effective city. A crucial ally in promoting the sustainability of smart cities is GPON technology. This fiber optic access technology utilizes a multipoint architecture, offering a scalable frame structure of 622 Mbps up to 2.5 Gbps.

The goal of a smart city is to enhance the quality of life for its citizens, while also contributing to financial, social, and political progress. This is accomplished by creating new and more advanced services, as well as promoting the sustainability of the city. Achieving this objective is possible through the establishment of networks that can support a high volume of information traffic, coupled with an architecture and platforms that can integrate the various components of the city and ensure effective interaction.

In this article, GPON Technology is presented as an essential contribution to achieving the fundamental objective of smart cities: interconnectivity and access to information. Through its deployment, smart cities can experience improved efficiency, cost savings, and enhanced service delivery, thus positively impacting the quality of life for its inhabitants.

In recent years., overseas financial system crises (e.g., Lehman shock and European debt crisis) exerted major influence on the Japanese interest rates market through global financial transactions., such as interest rates derivative contracts and many types of interest rates arbitrage strategies. In this research., we examined the effect of overseas interest rates movements to the Japanese rates market. Then., we developed a forecasting model of Japanese yield curve based on a variety of machine learning methods., by considering the information obtained from overseas markets. Finally., we confirmed that the prediction accuracy of Japanese long-term interest rate improved by using the US interest rates data in addition to the Japanese interest rates data for machine learning. Furthermore., we confirmed that the prediction accuracy increased by using US and Japanese rates markets data in recent years., particularly after 2006. This result suggests that information of overseas interest rates can be used to forecast Japanese rates market nowadays.

Cloud computing is a widely adopted platform that provides online computing services to its users. However, with the increasing number of applications being migrated to the cloud, availability has become a major concern. Availability refers to the percentage of time that the application service is accessible to its users, and there are numerous factors that can impact it, particularly in the cloud environment. 

This paper focuses on the impact of scheduling or placing an application's components within a data center in the cloud. We propose an optimized availability-aware strategy to schedule the components of an application with the goal to maximize availability while satisfying various constraints. We have mapped the scheduling problem to an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) optimization model. 

To compare the proposed strategy with other scheduling strategies, we conducted tests and found that the availability-aware strategy outperformed the other strategies in terms of achieving higher application availability. Our test results clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed strategy in optimizing application availability in the cloud environment.

Internet of things can be defined as things which are belonging to the internet. IOT is actually merging of internet with RFID's, various sensors (like ambient, wearable) and smart objects (things) around us. Day by day billions of devices are expected to join the internet and acquire the state of `being connected', which will process the data collected from different sensors and hence transmit the information collected so as to make meaningful decisions from them. In the upcoming years, IOT is expected to become main hub between technologies. IoT is the now a days has become a blessing but still is lacking due to many challenges. This paper presents an introduction on internet of things and discusses on the architecture, various application areas of it.

In this paper we develop a methodology for state estimation of partially contracting systems inspired by the particle filter (PF). If a system is partially contracting, in the sense that once some state variables are assumed known and viewed as inputs, the remaining reduced system is contracting, then only those variables need to be estimated. Indeed, once those variables are known, the remaining variables are asymptotically recovered owing to the contraction properties. To estimate the state of such a system, we thus suggest to use a PF approach to estimate only the non-contracting part, whereas the other part is naturally recovered. The methodology is applied to a nontrivial tracking problem. The trajectories of objects one seeks to track, such as aircraft and marine vehicles, typically consist of smooth sections with large, but infrequent, unpredictable changes. As a result, their motion is well modeled by nonlinear deterministic ordinary differential equations driven by piecewise constant random control inputs. Following our methodology, we combine a type of PF called the variable rate particle filter (VRPF) with a bank of observers assumed to have convergence properties. Using the notion of virtual system, we devise a hybrid variable rate particle observer, that uses the particles to detect changes, and the observers for state estimation in between changes.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) has attracted significant attention from both industry and academia as an important paradigm change in network service provisioning. Most existing studies on admissions of NFV-enabled requests focused on deploying dedicated Virtualized Network Function (VNF) instances to serve each individual request without exploring the sharing of VNF instances among multiple user requests. However, with ever-growing demands of user services, exclusive usages of VNF instances in most networks drastically degrade the network performance and largely under-utilize the VNF instance resources. In this paper, we jointly explore two different VNF instance scaling techniques, horizontal scaling and vertical scaling techniques, to improve the network throughput while minimizing the operational cost of the network, where horizontal scaling that migrates some existing VNF instances from their current locations to new locations to allow the VNF instances to be shared by multiple requests to reduce the resource consumption and operational cost of the network, and vertical scaling that instantiates new VNF instances to meet the demands of new request admissions if existing VNF instances sharing becomes more expensive or the end-to-end delay requirements of currently executing requests will be violated. We first propose a unified framework of maximizing the network throughput, by admitting as many as NFV-enabled requests while meeting the end-to-end delay requirements of the admitted requests. We then provide an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) solution for the problem when the problem size is small. Otherwise, we devise an efficient algorithm through a non-trivial reduction that reduces the problem to the minimum-weight feedback arc set problem and the generalized assignment problem (GAP). We finally conduct experiments to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms a baseline algorithm and achieves a performance on a par with its optimal ILP solution.

Real-time electricity prices and volatile workload patterns have a major impact on the operational costs of distributed data centers. A smart grid enables large consumers to regulate their usage patterns with the knowledge of real-time prices at different locations, and their energy consumption through the demand response (DR) program. However, the price inclined workload assignment may lead to an increase in peak demand, and decrease the benefits of workload offloading. Moreover, energy-efficient service management is challenged by unpredictable network conditions that can cause service performance degradation. Using an actor-critic approach, we developed a system that distributes a service's load among distributed sites to take advantage of the spatial variations in energy pricing. Our experimental results on the CloudLab testbed have proved with 45% reduction in running costs without impacting the response time using the Wikipedia request traces considering peak-based pricing.

Face morphing attack is proved to be a serious threat to the existing face recognition systems. Although a few face morphing detection methods have been put forward, the face morphing accomplice's facial restoration remains a challenging problem. In this paper, a face de-morphing generative adversarial network (FD-GAN) is proposed to restore the accomplice's facial image. It utilizes the symmetric dual network architecture and two levels of restoration losses to separate the identity feature of the morphing accomplice. By exploiting the captured facial image (containing the criminal's identity) from the face recognition system and the morphed image stored in the e-passport system (containing both criminal and accomplice's identities), the FD-GAN can effectively restore the accomplice's facial image. The experimental results and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. It has great potential to be applied for tracing the identity of face morphing attack's accomplice in criminal investigation and judicial forensics.

We propose a robust state estimation approach for a linear reaction-convection-diffusion equation under bounded unknown disturbances. Inspired by sliding mode theory, an adequate discontinuous input function is designed to compensate for the effect of the unknown disturbances. Based on Filippov's solutions theorem, we report the existence of generalized solutions to the estimation error system subject to the discontinuous input. Based on a Lyapunov stability analysis, we show the asymptotic convergence of the estimation error. The observer is then designed under more relaxed and realistic assumptions by replacing the discontinuous input by a continuous approximation and by using adaptive techniques to compensate for the upper bound on the bounded disturbances which are rather assumed to be unknown. Numerical simulations are performed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed robust estimation approach.

Intelligent transportation is an emerging technology that integrates advanced sensors, network communication, data processing, and automatic control technologies to provide great convenience for our daily lives. With the increasing popularity of intelligent transportation, its security issues have also attracted much attention. SQL injection attack is one of the most common attacks in the intelligent transportation system. It has characteristics of various types, fast mutations, hidden attacks, etc., and leads to great harm. Most of the current SQL detection methods are based on manually defined features. The detection results are heavily dependent on the accuracy of feature extraction, so it cannot cope with the increasingly complex SQL injection attacks in the intelligent transportation system. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a long short-term memory based SQL injection attack detection method, which can automatically learn the effective representation of data, and has a strong advantage to confront with complex high-dimensional massive data. In addition, this paper proposes an injection sample generation method based on data transmission channel from the perspective of penetration. This method can formally model SQL injection attack and generate valid positive samples. It can effectively solve the over-fitting problem caused by insufficient positive samples. The experimental results show that the proposed method improves the accuracy of the SQL injection attack detection and reduces the false positive rate, which is better than several related classical machine learning algorithms and commonly used deep learning algorithms.

For multi-satellite combined orbit determination (COD) network system based on GEO-IGSO-MEO satellite constellation and LEOs, the to-be-estimated satellites trajectory parameters results are not very precise because of satellites orbit perturbation indefinable physical models, observation models without adequately considering model error or measure mixed error, imprecise parameters estimation algorithm or linear least squares (LS) estimation algorithm, which cannot meet high precision application requirements of LEOs. Firstly, the high precision sparse parameters representation model of GEO-IGSO-MEO and LEOs orbit dynamics model is proposed. Above on this, the extended integrative COD models which combine parametric modeling and semi-parametric component representation based on measurement systematic errors and model errors are proposed. Secondly, the paper proposed weighting iterative wavelet estimation method of dynamics sparse parameters representation model, and LS approximation estimation method of non linear semi-parametric model is designed based on above models. Lastly, combined optimal weighting parameters estimation algorithm of extended integrative COD models which combines parametric estimation and non-parametric estimation are designed. Theoretic analysis and simulated computation results show that if only the physical model is used for COD, there is relatively big dynamical modeling error between dynamical model implied and the actual, which LEO precision cannot meet application requirements. When the high precision representation method of sparse parameters model and the optimized modeling method of observation model considering model errors can improve modeling and parameters estimation precision, and parameterized system error, model error and model parameters are estimated by extended integrative COD synchronously, so the orbit determination precision of LEOs can be improved evidently.

In this study, we propose a novel method using convolutional neural networks (CNN) to estimate the 6 degrees of freedom (DOF) object pose, which includes both 3D orientation and position. Specifically, our proposed approach, called RotationCNN, predicts the 3D orientation of the object, while the object's position is estimated using an object detection CNN that predicts the object's class and bounding box. 

Unlike the traditional method of training CNNs with a large-scale database, our proposed system is trained with a minimum dataset obtained in a local environment similar to where the robot is used. To create the dataset, we use a semi-automated technique based on a web camera and AR markers, making it easier and quicker for users in different environments to train the network suited for their own environment.

We believe that our approach is suitable for practical robotic applications, as the results of our experiments show that the average error of 3D orientation prediction using RotationCNN was 18.9 degrees, which is low enough as an initial solution to successfully run the iterative closest point (ICP) algorithm that uses depth data to refine the pose obtained with CNNs.

Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method by applying it to object grasping by a robot manipulator. Overall, we believe that our method can overcome some of the limitations of traditional CNN-based approaches and can be a useful tool for a wide range of robotic applications.

To extract maximum power from wind turbines, control strategies are necessary. These strategies must be able to adapt to changes in wind speed in order to optimize aerodynamic torque. One such strategy is the use of fuzzy logic controllers.

In this study, a comparative analysis between conventional PI strategies and fuzzy logic controllers was conducted for both Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and Pitch angle control. While conventional strategies require a well-known mathematical model, fuzzy logic controllers do not, making them better suited for nonlinear systems that may be affected by wind disturbances.

Simulation results showed that the fuzzy logic controller outperformed the conventional control strategy in several areas. Specifically, it was able to achieve better reference tracking, high sensitivity to high wind speed variation, and improved performance in dealing with nonlinearities. The results of this study demonstrate that fuzzy logic controllers are a robust option for controlling wind turbines and extracting the maximum amount of power from them.

The Internet of Things is expected to generate an unprecedented number of unbounded data streams that will produce a paradigm shift when it comes to data analytics. We are moving away from performing analytics in a public or private cloud to performing analytics locally at the fog and edge resources. In this paper, we propose a network of tasks utilizing edge, fog, and cloud computing that are designed to support an Analytics Everywhere framework. The aim is to integrate a variety of computational resources and analytical capabilities according to a data life-cycle. We demonstrate the proposed framework using an application in smart transit.

In this paper, we focus on the distributed convex optimization problem associated with time-varying networks. To address this challenge, we introduce a dual method that converges R-linearly to the optimal point, under the assumption that the agents' objective functions exhibit strong convexity and Lipschitz continuous gradients. 

The proposed dual method requires only half the amount of variable exchanges per iteration compared to methods that are based on DIGing. Furthermore, we empirically demonstrate that it yields improved practical performance.

Few-shot semantic segmentation techniques endeavor to predict the areas of different object categories with only a scant number of labeled samples. However, generating segmentation results with high precision when a new category emerges is rather challenging. To address this problem, we introduce a Multi-scale Discriminative Location-aware (MDL) network that deals with few-shot semantic segmentation. Initially, we retain the last three convolutional layers of FCN to exploit information from various levels. Subsequently, we leverage the VGG-16 network to extract features from the support image-label pair, which adjusts the weight of the query image segmentation branch. To enhance the efficiency of few-shot segmentation, we add a discriminative location-aware architecture, which incorporates a global average pooling layer to generate location feature information. Finally, we assess the MDL model on the Pascal VOC 2012 challenge, and demonstrate that it attains a competitive mIoU score compared to recent techniques.

Domain adaptation is a technique used to overcome the problem of differences in the distribution between labeled training and unlabeled testing data. The Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) is a popular measure used to minimize the distribution distance and eliminate domain divergence in various domain adaptation algorithms. However, we discovered that the compactness within each domain and class is simultaneously reduced when the empirical MMD is minimized. This leads to overlap between points from different classes, resulting in unsatisfactory classification results. To address this issue, we present a graph embedding framework with intrinsic and penalty graphs for MMD-based domain adaptation algorithms. We revise the intrinsic graph of MMD-based algorithms to minimize the within-class scatter and produce discriminative new features. Two strategies are proposed to this end, and we instantiate the framework using four models. Each model has a penalty graph that characterizes a particular similarity property to be avoided. Comprehensive experiments on visual cross-domain benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed models significantly enhance classification performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We have studied HEMS (Home Energy Management System). In that system we use sensor network node for the way of wireless communication. Now we are trying to establish the wireless power supplying method for the sensor network HEMS nodes. Basically we use the node beside the floor. Then the power source coil is desired to be mounted in the floor. And receiving coil is set into the node near the floor. Now we consider the way for transmitting power to the specified scope distance under the condition of cheaper and easy installation. As the result we have derived the effective coil arrangement.

Quantitative analysis of spine parameters using X-rays is crucial in the field of routine diagnosis and treatment planning. However, current tools often rely on manual intervention, and attempts at automating the process have mostly focused on vertebral bodies, ignoring important regions such as the posterior arch. In this study, we present a novel approach using contextual visual features and a multi-class Random Forest classifier to perform pixel-wise segmentation and identification of all cervical spine spinous processes on sagittal radiographs. Our method was evaluated on 62 radiographs and compared to manual tracing. We found that our method could correctly identify all subjects with a mean dice coefficient of 88 ± 8%, a Hausdorff distance of 2.1 ± 1.4 mm, and a mean surface distance of 0.6 ± 0.4 mm. These results demonstrate the potential of our method to reduce the amount of manual intervention required for spine modeling and clinical measurements.

Cloud computing has been a significant breakthrough technology in large scale data storage and computation over a decade. However, due to advancement in mobile devices along with other technologies such as Internet of Things (IOT), Augmented Reality (AR), there is a need for real-time responses and reduce delays generated over WAN. Thus concepts of Edge computing such as Fog computing and Mobile Edge computing has evolved in order to bridge a gap between cloud and the consumer devices. This paper gives an overview of MEC in 5G, a brief comparison with Fog Computing and about various aspects and deployment scenarios.

Deep neural networks often need large labeled datasets to build accurate models, but labeling data can be a time-consuming and costly task. Semi-supervised methods try to overcome this issue by using a small labeled dataset and a larger set of unlabeled data. In this paper, we propose a flexible framework for semi-supervised learning that combines the power of deep convolutional neural networks with the deeply embedded clustering algorithm to assign data points to clusters based on their probability distributions and feature representations. Our proposed algorithm, named SSLDEC, alternates between using labeled and unlabeled data points to learn feature representations via iterations and compute target distributions from predictions. The SSLDEC requires only a few hyper-parameters and can be used with various state-of-the-art deep neural network configurations for image classification and segmentation tasks. We tested our approach on benchmark image classification tasks as well as a challenging medical image segmentation scenario, and our results showed that SSLDEC outperformed several state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods. The algorithm can effectively reduce the need for costly expert annotations and enhance applications such as automatic medical image segmentation.

We explore the utilization of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) for high-rate communication on an acoustic channel that is mobile. The mobile channel's time-variability and frequency offset are addressed using a specialized method that involves synchronization and partial FFT (P-FFT) demodulation. We incorporate this process within multichannel diversity combining. The traditional approach for receivers demodulates the signal utilizing one FFT that operates over the entire OFDM block interval. However, the P-FFT approach uses several FFT operations to demodulate the signal over several partial intervals. The partial demodulator outputs are then combined and fed into a 2nd stage, where data detection and refined channel estimation occur. Coherent and differentially coherent detection methods are examined, and least squares (LS) and matching pursuit (MP) algorithms are tested with refined channel estimation. The partial interval demodulation offers a higher degree of freedom through the opportunity to nullify time-variation before inter-carrier interference can form during demodulation. The data detection quality is enhanced as a result, which we prove with actual data from the 2010 Mobile Acoustic Communications Experiment MACE'10. Experimental data processing exhibits excellent performance with up to 2048 QPSK-modulated carriers functioning within the 10.5 kHz -15.5 kHz acoustic band across various distances (3-7 km) and speeds up to 1.5 m/s.

Nowadays, the success of the different institutions depends on the security of their information against possible attacks. Because much of this information is related to persons' activities, so safeguarding their identities is essential for these successes. For this purpose, persons' identity recognition can be categorized as an effective method to enhance the security of information systems. To do this, most of these systems use biometric methods, which are very efficient compared to traditional methods. In this context, the present paper attempts to design an effective multimodal biometric system using hand biometrics. In this work, Finger- Knuckle-Print (FKP) and PaLMprint (PLM) biometrics are used. In addition, for high accuracy, two simple and effective deep learning based feature extraction techniques, PCANet and DCTNet, are integrated. The security analysis presented in this paper can help simplify the understanding of biometric systems and thus finding a robust solution to protect information systems. Our experimental results, using a synthetic multibiometric dataset of 165 persons, show that our proposed system has a high identification rate and a very low classification error compared to several existing methods.

In orthopedic surgery, the restoration of comminuted fractures has traditionally relied on manual work by the surgeon, which can be intricate and prone to errors. Poorly reassembled fractured bones can lead to longer recovery times and increased exposure to radiation, while surgical errors can cause joint dysfunction or infection. To address these challenges, orthopedic surgeons need an intelligent assistance solution to improve the accuracy and reliability of fractured bone reassembly.

This paper presents an automatic pipeline for virtual reassembly of fractured bones using an intact bone as a template. The 3D fractured bone is reconstructed from CT data using MIMICS, and the shape structure of the bone model is analyzed by extracting key feature points and comparing descriptors. The correspondence between the fragments and template is then searched to ensure proper alignment, allowing the fragments to join together seamlessly.

Compared with semi-automatic reassembly methods used for archaeological artifacts and forensic evidence, our technique is fully automatic and specialized for medical purposes, helping orthopedic surgeons make the correct decisions in fractured bone reassembly. By removing the need for human interaction, this technique offers a reliable and efficient solution for restoring comminuted fractures with increased accuracy and precision.

Diabetes is a condition that gradually affects the body's natural defense mechanisms and vital organs, making it a silent and slow killer. It occurs when the body fails to utilize the energy provided by food due to excessive blood sugar levels. Diabetes is a potential cause of kidney diseases, heart attacks, blindness, and lower limb amputations. The World Health Organization estimates that more than 500 million people worldwide are affected by diabetes, and the disease is responsible for over 2.5 million casualties worldwide, with a higher incidence in medium and low-income nations.

This paper presents a procedural approach for estimating Gestational Diabetes using Microsoft Azure AI services. Microsoft Azure AI is a Machine Learning Studio that provides all major functions and algorithms through drag-and-drop. The classification model built predicts the occurrence of Gestational diabetes based on early pregnancy factors. The Pima Indian dataset from UCI was used to build and cross-validate the predictive model. The algorithm was tested on a dataset of 768 samples and achieved an accuracy of 77.8%.

In scenarios such as video surveillance, face images often exhibit combined variations such as occlusion and low-resolution. Existing approaches for face enhancement focus on handling one type of variation per model. However, in this paper we present a deep generative adversarial network (FCSR-GAN) that can jointly tackle face completion and super-resolution for combined variations in a single model. The generator of FCSR-GAN attempts to render a high-resolution face image without occlusion by using an input low-resolution face image with partial occlusions. In the FCSR-GAN discriminator, two adversarial losses, a perceptual loss, and a face parsing loss combine to ensure the recovered face images are of high quality. The experimental results from several public-domain databases (CelebA and Helen) demonstrate that our approach has outperformed the state-of-the-art methods for jointly doing face super-resolution (up to 4×) and face completion from low-resolution face images with occlusions.

This paper considers utility optimal power control for energy-harvesting wireless devices with a finite capacity battery. The distribution information of the underlying wireless environment and harvestable energy is unknown, and only outdated system state information is known at the device controller. This scenario shares similarity with Lyapunov opportunistic optimization and online learning but is different from both. By a novel combination of Zinkevich's online gradient learning technique and the drift-plus-penalty technique from Lyapunov opportunistic optimization, this paper proposes a learning-aided algorithm that achieves utility within O(ϵ) of the optimal, for any desired ϵ > 0, by using a battery with an O(1/ϵ) capacity. The proposed algorithm has low complexity and makes power investment decisions based on system history, without requiring knowledge of the system state or its probability distribution.

The Internet-of-Things (IoT) is focused on linking numerous smart devices and objects in a seamless manner by processing unprecedented amounts of data obtained from diverse IoT devices. Despite its quick evolution toward IoT-based infrastructures, this rapid growth has also led to security threats through IoT-based botnet attacks. In this paper, we propose an IoT botnet attack detection method using a sparsity representation framework that relies on a reconstruction error thresholding rule to identify malicious network traffic originating from compromised IoT devices at the IoT edge. Botnet attack detection is performed using small benign IoT network traffic data, and therefore, we have no prior knowledge about malicious IoT traffic data. Our method's efficacy is tested using a real IoT-based network dataset, and the results demonstrate that our technique is more effective than the reconstruction error-based autoencoder approach.

This study presents an innovative approach to energy harvesting for sensor nodes via a piezoelectric energy-harvesting module (PEHM) utilizing motor vibration signals. The authors developed a prototype PEHM, which was integrated into an environmental monitoring system alongside a front-end sensing platform, back-end server, and cloud database. The monitoring data collected by the sensor nodes are transmitted to the server through a layered multi-hop scheme where they are analyzed for motor faults. The results are displayed on a website in real-time while all data and analysis results are uploaded to the cloud database for remote monitoring.

Field testing of the proposed PEHM was conducted on continuously operating motors. The sensor nodes transmitted heavy-load packets for ten minutes before entering a sleep mode. The PEHM operated at the rated motor speed required charging for 24.3 hours to achieve node power self-sufficiency. Through this testing, it was demonstrated that the PEHM is capable of supplying energy stably to sensor nodes and building up a cloud factory monitoring system through the use of a wireless sensor network with a PEHM. 

Overall, this study provides an innovative and practical solution to energy harvesting for sensor nodes, ultimately improving environmental monitoring systems and aiding in the detection and prevention of motor faults.

The era of fake news, media manipulation and information wars has been beneficent to the lasting fame and continuous acclaim of George Orwell's 1984. The novel, published in 1949, influences to the present day the terminology of various political and social analysts through the use of its fictional language called “Newspeak”. The question arises - can the inner connections of the concepts present in Orwell's 1984, when analysing the text on a semantic level of the words in their contextual environment, be used to further the understanding of the inner-workings of the novel's language itself? More specifically, the aim of this paper is to examine whether a reader without knowledge of the subject of a fictional work of art, exemplified by Orwell's 1984, could gain deeper comprehension of the text just from analysing word vector representations, without the use of external resources and only through an overview of the established similarities on the semantic level of words in a given text. In fact, word vector representations, as a form of word embeddings in a vector space model, are a machine learning technique sometimes applied in natural language processing, which attempts to identify semantically similar words.

Drones have become increasingly prevalent in various civilian applications, including delivering package shipments to consumers, offering internet access and aiding in emergency situations. In emergency scenarios, drones can be used to locate victims in hard-to-reach areas and support emergency centers in managing reported emergencies. However, limited battery life poses a significant challenge to their operational capacity. To address this, a reliable strategy that minimizes energy consumption and fosters collaborative working is necessary to increase drones' ability to operate for longer periods in emergencies.
