Particularly, we first use deep neural networks pre-trained for classification of natural images to extract high-level image features from ultrasound images, then these feature maps are used as input to learn kidney boundary distance maps using a boundary distance regression network, and finally the predicted boundary distance maps are classified as kidney pixels or non-kidney pixels using a pixel classification network in an end-to-end learning fashion. Experimental results have demonstrated that our method could effectively improve the performance of automatic kidney segmentation, significantly better than deep learning based pixel classification networks.

With the advancement of digitization in industrial society, it has become commonplace to outsource large amounts of production data to cloud servers in order to reduce data management costs. However, ensuring the integrity, validity, and availability of outsourced data remains a challenging research topic. Recently, Zhang et al. (IEEE Trans. Industrial Informatic, doi:10.1109/TII.2019.2894108) presented an efficient and robust certificateless signature scheme to achieve data authenticity for industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Despite their efforts, their scheme has been found to be insecure due to the ability of an attacker to impersonate legitimate users and upload false messages by forging valid signatures. As a result, their certificateless signature scheme has not solved the IIoT data authenticity issue. Furthermore, their security proof has been deemed unsound as the difficulty of the problem they aim to solve cannot be solved by an adversary's ability.

In this study, we investigate the scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by two inverted PEC half-planes that are loaded with a dielectric layer. We employ the Wiener-Hopf technique in the spectral domain to obtain the solution. Our approach involves reducing the factorization problem to Fredholm integral equations of second kind.

The structure we examine is of significant interest in a range of applications, including antenna technologies, electromagnetic compatibility, and electromagnetic shielding. By studying structural singularities, we can estimate surface waves and leaky waves that are relevant to practical engineering applications.

Our results provide important insights into the behavior of electromagnetic waves in complex structures. They highlight the importance of considering the effects of dielectric layers and structural singularities when designing and optimizing electromagnetic devices. Overall, this study offers valuable contributions to the field of electromagnetics and has the potential to inform future developments in antenna technologies.

This paper investigates the controller design problem of networked control systems subject to cyber attacks. A hybrid-triggering communication strategy is employed to save the limited communication resources. State measurements are transmitted over a communication network and may be corrupted by cyber attacks. The aim of this paper is to design a controller for a new closed-loop system model with consideration of randomly occurring cyber attacks and the hybrid-triggering scheme. A stability criterion is obtained for the system stabilization by employing Lyapunov stability theory and stochastic analysis techniques. Moreover, the desired controller gain is derived by resorting to some matrix inequalities. Finally, a numerical example is exploited to demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed scheme.

In real-time embedded systems, it is common to use a data-flow chain consisting of a set of communicating tasks to implement system functionality. An essential non-functional requirement for such systems is to limit the amount of time taken for input to have an impact on its corresponding output, known as cause-effect latency. Previously, the problem of estimating the worst-case cause-effect latency has been well-studied in the context of blocking inter-task communication. However, recent research indicates that non-blocking communication, which preserves functional semantics, is crucial for model-based designs of dynamically updatable systems. To this end, we present a computationally efficient algorithm that accurately and tightly estimates the worst-case cause-effect reaction latency in non-blocking data-flow chains.

Credit card fraud detection is an active field of research due to increasing fraud risk, particularly with the introduction of new credit card payment methods such as nearfield communication (NFC) enabled cards and online payments. Machine learning has shown positive results in recent years when used in credit card fraud detection; nevertheless, certain complexities exist when using machine learning in credit card fraud detection. These include the lack of fraudulent transaction data and the skewed nature of training data used in credit card fraud detection models, as well as selection of an adequate metric to measure a model's performance. This paper introduces a new unsupervised learning model based on the combination of an auto-encoder and one-class support vectors machine (OSVM), where an input is fed to an auto-encoder and a the input reconstruction error is produced and passed on to an OSVM to determine whether a transaction is fraudulent. The introduced model is compared with other models such as the individual use of OSVM, auto-encoders, and a third model based on the combination of OSVM and Auto encoder using an approach different than the one proposed in this paper. When the performance is measured using the geometric mean (GMean) and F1 score the newly proposed model shows comparable results with OSVM and improved results over the other two models.

Convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithms are utilized to build a machine learning block to assist the optimizations of voltage noise, temperature distribution, and security of multi-phase on-chip switched-capacitor (SC) voltage converters. All the random sequences generated by the pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) are fed into the designed machine learning block in an SC converter sequentially to filter the unsatisfactory sequences. The results show that the maximum amplitude of the voltage noise and the highest temperature of the SC converter are reduced by 68.98% and 12.07%, respectively, while a negligible security degradation is achieved under the assistance of machine learning.

One of the most significant current issues in Emergency Medical Services (EMS) is the need for improved response times and accuracy in locating victims in emergency situations, such as acute cardiac arrests. One major challenge faced by EMS teams is identifying the exact location of the victim, which can result in wasted time and an unsuccessful rescue attempt. Additionally, the lack of availability of Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) can be a major issue when attempting to save a patient's life.

To address these issues, this study aims to develop an integrated emergency platform that monitors the location of AEDs and controls the opening/closing of AED cabinets through an app. This platform provides users with the ability to check the real-time status of the AED and track its location, ensuring that EMS teams can access the AED more easily and quickly.

Using a GPS system, this platform can also pinpoint and identify the exact location of the accident or emergency, providing EMS teams with accurate and timely information. Results from statistical tests show that the platform has a 95% accuracy rate in locating AEDs and can control the opening/closing of the cabinet with 96% accuracy. Additionally, the average response time through the app is just 658 ms, indicating that this platform can support EMS services more effectively.

Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of an integrated emergency platform as a tool to enhance EMS operations, improve response times, and ultimately save lives.

The article suggests a neural network-based method for implementing adaptive control in automatic control systems for trajectorial displacements of technological objects. The analysis of the structures of automatic control systems with complementary correction allows to propose two schemes for the inclusion of a neural network controller in the automatic control loop: (1) synthesis of the autonomous additional component by the neural network controller, implementation of the component in the control signal and organization of its channel; (2) software control correction implemented in the control signal generating device. These structures presuppose the online learning of the neural network. As an error signal used to adjust the weighting coefficients of the neural network, we propose to use a difference signal between the output coordinate of the reference model and the control object. In this research the corrections to the control law, synthesized in the system correction loop, are assumed to be unknown, i.e. we con-sider the reference value for the neural network output signal to be absent. The work outlines approaches to choosing the number of layers, neurons in them, activation functions and the delay time of input signals of the network. We also offer a modification of the gradient training method for the neural network. The re-search results of the correction loop are presented on the example of the robotic device actuator.

Cloud Technology is a most challenging modern area in the field of modern technologies in which assets (e.g., CPU and capacity) can be rented and discharged by the clients through internet on-demand basis. The cloud computing has been giving virtual computing services to a little, medium and extensive industries, and services, for example, infrastructure as a service (IaaS), platform as a service (PaaS), and software as a service (SaaS). Cloud computing has a great combination with the agile software development as a research area. Many researchers worked in Agile Cloud field. The software industries are using the agile methodology for efficient software development need some platform to get quick feedback from the client. Therefore, the agile-cloud is a great combination for it but due to security reasons that directly influence the less adoption of cloud in software industries. This paper reports the survey results of software industries. The total of seven IT industries and many professionals was involved in this paper. However, this paper also contributes and reveals how existing issues can affect agile-cloud adoption for efficient software development. Furthermore, we do not find any type of survey conducted in Pakistan's software industries-related to cloud-agile adoption.

IEEE 802.11ac for high throughput wireless access supports the use of wide channel bandwidth for improving the capacity of data transmission. To properly balance the needs of individual wireless stations (STAs) and the available network capacity, the standard proposes dynamic bandwidth channel access (DBCA) where the wide channel is divided into primary and secondary channel components; and a station needs to contend for the primary channel while it can use the secondary channel without any contention, when it is sensed free. This leads to the unfairness in channel access. Further, the network gets severely affected when STAs demand for specific Quality of Service (QoS) for various applications belonging to different access categories (ACs) running over it. Different ACs with different QoS types require separate treatment in terms of channel bandwidth allocation, which the standard IEEE 802.11ac DBCA fails to provide. In this paper, we develop a packet scheduling mechanism, High Throughput Multi-Level Scheduler (HT-MLS), to support dynamic bandwidth allocation over QoS associated traffic classes, while ensuring the fairness among the contending STAs. HT-MLS utilizes an adaptive learning over the channel sensing environment; and a testbed implementation (with 30 wireless stations) and thorough evaluation of HT-MLS indicate that it can improve QoS performance significantly, while ensuring the channel access fairness for the STAs.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIB) have found a wide range of applications in many consumer products in the last 25 years. The United States Navy and Marine Corps have various applications using LIB, and safe battery technologies are critically needed. While many consumer applications typically utilize smaller, high volume cells, military applications can utilize specialty large-format cells in their LIB packs. One of the most important safety considerations for LIB cells is their thermal stability under various abuses such as exposure to heat, nail penetration, external short circuit, crushing, and so on. Several exothermic reactions can occur as the inner cell temperature increases, and if the heat generation is larger than the dissipated heat to the surroundings, this leads to heat accumulation in the cell and acceleration of the chemical reactions, which can then lead to a thermal runaway. Since the behavior of batteries is strongly affected by the interaction of physics on varying length and time scales: a multi-physics and multi-scale model is needed to simulate this process. While many approaches have been reported in literature, they are not directly applicable in large-format LIB cells and the development of multi-scale and multi-physics models are relatively limited and still computationally expensive. For example, in large formatted battery cells, the uniformity of the electrical potential along the current collectors in the cell composites is no longer given. Additionally, due to the inhomogeneity of the distribution of the temperature field with respect to the cell geometry, thermal dynamics must also be taken into account. This study reports the recently developed multi-scale and multi-physics models for simulating the thermal runway inside a lithium-ion battery using COMSOL software. For the electrochemical processes, the porous electrode theory with contributions coming from exothermic side reactions is used to model abuse mechanisms, which could lead to a thermal runaway. For the thermal-mechanical processes, models of thermal abuse reactions that occur at specific elevated temperatures have been simulated. Prior experimental data on a large-scale lithium-ion battery tested at NSWCCD has been used to construct and validate the model with good agreement.

This study aims to realize a tactile display which can represent 2D haptic information on the display surface. The tactile display typically consists of a lot of compact linear actuators. In order to represent the haptic information on the display, the motion of the actuator should be controlled. The position sensor is usually attached to the actuator to derive the position information. However, the sensor makes the system large and expensive. Therefore, the sensorless control technique is effective to reduce the size and cost. In our previous works, a position estimation method for a compact dual solenoid actuator was proposed. In this paper, the position control with the estimated position feedback is proposed. Additionally, a disturbance observer is applied to achieve robust position control. The frequency characteristics of the sensorless position control was experimentally investigated. The results indicated that the sensorless position control was accurately achieved when a sinusoidal position command whose frequency was less than 2.0 Hz was applied. This proposal is useful since the compact actuation system is realized.

Lately, there has been a lot of interest in how to ensure secure communication in Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBSN). To accomplish this finish, applied researchers have become increasingly identified their own detection techniques. However, WBSN still vulnerable for many attacks, for instance: Jamming, Sybil attacks, Sinkhole, Denial of service (DOS), etc. Therefore, intrusion detection is officially compulsory process that helps physicians to get accurate medical decisions. The present work proposes an intrusion cancellation to add efficiency to medical anomaly detection based on Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Electromyogram (EMG) analysis. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed approach are evaluated using the Matlab tool. Hence, our scheme may be considered as a promising accurate detection of false alert rates.

The paper provides a comprehensive literature research regarding the field of data analysis in engineering change management. The focus is on a posteriori analysis methods of engineering change data. After an introduction to the topic, identified a posteriori data analysis procedures in the engineering change management are listed and supplemented by further a priori analysis procedures. Furthermore, the a posteriori data analysis methods presented are compared on the basis of a catalogue of requirements.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to a non-task-oriented dialogue system that controls the length of system utterances. Dialogue systems can be categorized into task-oriented or non-task-oriented systems, with the latter becoming increasingly popular. One important aspect of a dialogue system is the utterance length, which can vary based on the speaker and the listener as well as the nature of the conversation. However, the impact of utterance length on dialogue systems has not been thoroughly investigated in previous systems that use the Encoder-Decoder model. To address this issue, we propose an utterance length estimator (ULE) and an index of the utterance length, which consider the user's personality, for determining the length of system utterances. The ULE is a neural network that learns the length of the utterance through training data of dialogue, and the index of the utterance length is calculated during the conversation. Our system then employs a neural encoder-decoder to control the output length and generate the appropriate responses. The experimental results show that our proposed method improved user satisfaction compared to conventional methods.

Both wrapper and hybrid methods in feature selection need the intervention of learning algorithm to train parameters. The preset parameters and dataset are used to construct several sub-optimal models, from which the final model is selected. The question is how to evaluate the performance of these sub-optimal models? What are the effects of different evaluation methods of sub-optimal model on the result of feature selection? Aiming at the evaluation problem of predictive models in feature selection, we chose a hybrid feature selection algorithm, FDHSFFS, and conducted comparative experiments on four UCI datasets with large differences in feature dimension and sample size by using five different cross-validation (CV) methods. The experimental results show that in the process of feature selection, twofold CV and leave-one-out-CV are more suitable for the model evaluation of low-dimensional and small sample datasets, tenfold nested CV and tenfold CV are more suitable for the model evaluation of high-dimensional datasets; tenfold nested CV is close to the unbiased estimation, and different optimal models may choose the same approximate optimal feature subset.

The purpose of this study was to investigate the utilization and acceptance of e-books by students at a Namibian university. This research employed a mixed methods approach by administering a survey questionnaire to 35 undergraduate students, followed by telephonic interviews with 12 purposively-selected students based on their responses to the questionnaire. The findings indicate that the use and acceptance of e-books in Namibia is still in its early stages. Although students are aware of e-books, most prefer print books; one of the reasons for the low usage of e-books is the lack of training on how to access them. The researchers recommend that faculty officers work with librarians to ensure that prescribed e-books are available and that adequate Information Literacy training is provided to students. Future studies with a larger sample size, including multiple faculties and universities, will provide further insight into e-book adoption in Africa and worldwide. Additionally, further research is needed to determine why approximately 14% of students do not read books (print or electronic) at all while in school.

Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have proven to be valuable for camera pose regression, and are highly effective against challenging scenarios such as lighting changes, motion blur, and textureless surfaces. PoseNet further demonstrates CNN's ability to interpolate camera pose in space between training images. In this study, we investigate how different dataset processing strategies affect pose regression and propose a multi-scene dataset method for training CNNs. Our results demonstrate that multiple scenes can be remembered using only one CNN, and that combining scenes does not significantly decrease the accuracy of neural network position errors as camera distance increases. We also investigate factors that impact the accuracy of multi-scene camera pose regression models and suggest methods to improve data merging. This research provides an open code and dataset resource for other researchers to advance the field.

To overcome the limitations of traditional static measurement methods that include low efficiency, inconvenient data storage, and higher requirements for testers, a dynamic measurement method has been proposed for real-time online measurement of the amplitude frequency response of the broadcasting transmitter. The proposed model and test principles of the measurement system are explained in detail.

The dynamic method involves real-time collection of input and output signals from the broadcast transmitter. The generalized cross-correlation algorithm is used initially to find the system delay, followed by the FFT algorithm of time delay data interception to calculate the system's amplitude-frequency response.

Experiments on the proposed method have demonstrated accuracy and reliability, and as such, it is deemed practical and generalizable.

The conventional MapReduce algorithm can be time-consuming, especially with large data sets or big data. However, by defining data with fuzziness, retrieval time can be reduced, and actual data sets need not be disclosed. In this paper, we discuss fuzzy data mining methods, which enable data analysis without disclosing the original data sets.

We study two fuzzy functional dependencies (FFD) and fuzzy multivalve dependencies (FMVD) for data mining. Our fuzzy MapReduce algorithm using FFD and MVFD is useful for reducing the time of online analytical processing (OLAP) while ensuring the original data is not disclosed. Additionally, we make it easy to combine data sets and use them for association, providing several examples of fuzzy MapReduce applications.

In conclusion, fuzzy data mining is an effective solution for reducing the time complexity of conventional MapReduce algorithms while maintaining data privacy. With FFD and FMVD, we can achieve efficient OLAP without disclosing original data sets, making it easier to carry out large-scale data analysis.

The tongue image is a crucial source of physical information for clinical medicine, as it can aid in diagnosis and treatment. In China, herbal prescriptions are commonly used due to their simplicity, non-invasiveness, and low side effects. Therefore, studies on the automatic construction of herbal prescriptions based on tongue images can provide valuable insights for healthcare services in mobile medical systems by utilizing deep learning to explore the connection between tongue images and herbal prescriptions.

To develop an effective framework that can construct herbal prescriptions from tongue images captured in various photographic environments, this study proposes a neural network framework that comprises of single/double convolution channels and fully connected layers. Additionally, it introduces the auxiliary therapy topic loss mechanism to simulate the therapeutic practices of Chinese doctors and reduce the impact of sparse output labels on the diversity of results.

The experiment utilizes real-world tongue images and corresponding prescriptions to generate prescriptions that are comparable to the original samples. This outcome strengthens the viability of the proposed technique for automatic herbal prescription construction from tongue images. Additionally, it sets a benchmark for constructing herbal prescriptions based on other physical information.

Overall, the proposed approach provides a promising direction for constructing herbal prescriptions assisted by tongue images. The utilization of neural network frameworks and auxiliary therapy topic loss mechanisms can enhance the precision and efficacy of automated herbal prescription construction.

To address the issue of sentiment lexicons being constructed without considering the variability of sentiment polarities of words in different topics or domains, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical supervision topic model called TaSL. By jointly considering topics and sentiments of words, TaSL represents documents with multiple pairs of topics and sentiments characterized by a multinomial distribution over words, supervised under hierarchical information of documents and words. This approach allows for the sentiment polarity of each word in different topics to be adequately captured. Results from experiments on four publicly available datasets demonstrate that TaSL outperforms existing manual sentiment lexicons, topic model-based domain-specific lexicons, expanded lexicons, and deep neural network-based lexicons. Therefore TaSL is found to be beneficial for constructing a domain-specific sentiment lexicon and improving sentiment classification performance.

Islanding is a recent issue for power system engineers. In every normal or faulty case, the power system undergoes a sequence of states. These states are not directly observable but have a particular pattern. The patterns can be reflected in the measurements. The nonobserving states are referred to as hidden states. This paper has developed a novel hidden Markov model (HMM) based algorithm to engender a probability related to the event of islanding, depending upon the phasor measurements obtained from the smart grid. After processing the phasor data, an artificial neural network is methodically trained to provide emission probability of the hidden states. This emission probability is useful for the evaluation of the HMM. An IEEE 9 bus system is selected to test the algorithm. Several case studies are performed to generate a statistical analysis for the parameters of the HMM. The posterior probability is responsible for final pronouncement of the occurrence of islanding. The accuracy of the algorithm is estimated on the basis of finishing result. Nondetection zone is also estimated for the HMM-based islanding detection method. It is observed that this method HMM can detect islanding with less nondetection zone proficiently in a short time.

The work herein demonstrates how hybrid mesh network reliability can be improved by leveraging the channel diversity enabled by a compact, tripolar antenna. Specifically, through simulation, we show that a tripolar antenna can reduce packet drops to a third of that of when a single element antenna is used. These results were achieved assuming a slowly-varying, but highly-multipath, propagation environment such as those that may he exnected in industrial IoT settings.

Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks pose a serious threat as they are a highly organized effort to disable network-based computer systems. Attackers use a large number of agents to overwhelm victims with fake requests, which prevent legitimate users from accessing their services. Such attacks can target web services or even critical cyberphysical systems like power stations and water distribution networks.

Recently, there has been a surge in Distributed Reflective Denial of Service (DRDoS) attacks. These attacks reflect and amplify UDP traffic, redirecting a massive volume of traffic towards the victim. The store and flood DRDoS attacks, under this category, have utilized P2P networks to store attack data before the actual attack phase.

Unlike traditional DoS attacks, store and flood DRDoS attacks have shown to be highly efficient and more harmful. In this paper, we aim to combat the store and flood DRDoS problem. By investigating the attack elements and mechanism, we have developed strategies to reduce the impact of these attacks and filter out undesired traffic.

If the eye movement of a driver who makes a long drive during the day and at night can be measured with less stress to the driver in order to estimate the following items for a long time with high accuracy, it is expected that the information will make a great contribution to safe driving: 1) What the driver is looking at or paying attention to (i.e. gaze), 2) A feeling or sign of unwellness such as dizziness, car sickness, and discomfort (i.e. rotational eye movement). In this study, the authors propose an approach in which an area of high intensity gradients in the white part of the eye, i.e. an area that includes a blood vessel with a distinctive shape, is automatically selected to estimate the gaze and calculate the angle of eye rotation, so that the target ocular blood vessel can be tracked with high accuracy even if blood vessels in the white part of the eye differ considerably between individuals in terms of shape, length, and thickness. An evaluation experiment yielded excellent results under various lighting conditions. Especially, extremely positive results were obtained for the estimation accuracy of rotational eye movement, with an estimation error of -0.69° ± 1.02° (mean and standard deviation).

Linear Sensor Networks (LSNs) have recently garnered considerable attention due to the burgeoning demand for monitoring structures or areas with a linear topology. LSNs employ sensor nodes that are often battery-powered which necessitates duty-cycling techniques to enhance energy efficiency. However, the application of duty-cycling techniques leads to a significant issue known as sleep latency. To mitigate this issue, pipelined forwarding has been proposed as a potential solution. This paper focuses on analyzing interference in data collection services for a multi-hop LSN running a duty-cycling and pipelined-forwarding protocol. In scenarios involving multiple concurrent transmissions along a data collection path, the simultaneous transmissions can severely interfere with one another. We derived nodal distance distributions of all concurrent transmissions and analyzed the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and link capacity distributions based on the obtained distance distributions and the path-loss model in an interference-limited environment. The SINR distribution highlights the link outage probability at a given SINR threshold. By analyzing the transmission receiving the strongest cumulative interference, our model can provide valuable guidelines for duty cycle configurations to attain a desired network performance.

With the rapid growth of technology, the prevalence of malware has become a significant challenge to the security of computer systems. To address this concern, we have developed a malware detection system that utilizes deep learning on API calls. Through the use of cuckoo sandbox, we were able to extract the API calls sequence of malicious programs. By filtering and ordering redundant API calls, we were able to extract valid API sequences. The performance of BLSTM was then compared with GRU, BGRU, LSTM and SimpleRNN on large datasets, which included 21,378 samples. Our experimental results indicate that BLSTM is the most effective method for detecting malware, with an impressive accuracy rate of 97.85%.

Cloud Computing is a popular platform for providing online computing services to the tenants. With migrating large number of the applications to the cloud, application availability is raised as a concern issue. Availability is a non-functional requirement that refers to the percentage of time the application service is available for the use. Many factors can impact the application availability especially in the cloud environment. In this paper, we show the impact of scheduling (placement) of the application's components inside the Data Center of the cloud on the application availability. We propose an optimized Availability- Aware strategy to schedule the components with the goal to maximize the availability of the application while satisfying several constraints. We map the scheduling problem to Integer Linear Programming (ILP) optimization model. We compare the Availability-Aware strategy with other scheduling strategies. The results show that the Availability-Aware strategy achieves higher application availability compared to the other strategies.

A new normalized least mean square (NLMS) adaptive filter is first derived from a cost function, which incorporates the conventional one of the NLMS with a minimum-disturbance (MD) constraint. A variable regularization factor (RF) is then employed to control the contribution made by the MD constraint in the cost function. Analysis results show that the RF can be taken as a combination of the step size and regularization parameter in the conventional NLMS. This implies that these parameters can be jointly controlled by simply tuning the RF as the proposed algorithm does. It also demonstrates that the RF can accelerate the convergence rate of the proposed algorithm and its optimal value can be obtained by minimizing the squared noise-free posteriori error. A method for automatically determining the value of the RF is also presented, which is free of any prior knowledge of the noise. While simulation results verify the analytical ones, it is also illustrated that the performance of the proposed algorithm is superior to the state-of-art ones in both the steady-state misalignment and the convergence rate. A novel algorithm is proposed to solve some problems. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Sidelobes, which refer to the unwanted signals that occur in MIMO radars with antennas spread out over a wide area, have a significant impact on the shape of the detection ambiguity function. The antenna geometry and signal bandwidth also have a significant effect on sidelobe suppression. 

This paper focuses on naval surveillance radar design requirements and proposes a suitable antenna geometry. A genetic algorithm is used in a MIMO scenario simulator to compute the fitness function to verify its effectiveness. Using this approach, an optimized MIMO antenna geometry is identified that provides excellent resolution capability and sidelobe suppression exceeding 13 dB compared to a non-optimized geometry.

Emphysema quantification and sub-typing is actively studied on cohorts of full-lung high-resolution CT (HRCT) scans, with promising results. Transfer of quantification and classification tools to cardiac CT scans, which involve 70% of the lungs, is challenging due to lower image resolution and degradation of textural patterns. In this study, we propose an original deep-learning domain-adaptation framework to use a pre-existing dictionary of lung texture patterns (LTP), learned on gold-standard full-lung HRCT scans, to label emphysema regions on cardiac CT scans. The method exploits convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained for: 1) supervised lung texture classification on synthetic cardiac images, and 2) adversarial learning to discriminate between real and synthetic cardiac images. Combination of the classification and adversarial tasks enables to label real cardiac CT scans, and is evaluated on the MESA cohort (N = 15,357 scans). Our results show that image features derived from the adversarial training preserve the labeling accuracy on synthetic scans. LTP histogram signatures generated on 4,315 longitudinal pairs of cardiac CT scans, show high level of consistency over time and scanner generations. The ability to robustly label emphysema texture patterns on cardiac CT scans will enable large-scale longitudinal studies over 10 years of follow-up, for better understanding of the disease progression.

With the rise in popularity of mobile devices and the convenience of cloud computing environments, more and more individuals have grown accustomed to storing their captured videos in the cloud. However, concerns about privacy continue to exist as there is no guarantee that the stored information is not accessible to the cloud computing server. One way to protect privacy is to encrypt all videos before uploading them to the cloud; however, this approach may significantly impact retrieval performance, as every encrypted video needs to be downloaded, decrypted, and compared with the query request. To address this challenge, we propose to perform video retrieval directly in the encrypted domain, meaning that desired videos will only be retrieved and decrypted in the cloud.

The decision-making process of health professionals involves a lot of subjective reasoning, which cannot always be accurately analyzed using traditional numerical methods. Fortunately, recent advancements in computer technology have allowed developers to create software that can assist doctors in making decisions without the need for direct expert consultation. By utilizing intelligent tools and procedures, as well as a vast knowledge base, early identification of symptoms can be achieved.

Artificial intelligence, despite being an old concept, has been recognized as a powerful new technology that has been applied in various fields like aviation, education, finance, hospitals, marketing, and medicine across the globe. The intelligent decision-making systems can handle the unpredictability, unreliability, and imprecision of medical diagnostics, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of hospitals and healthcare systems.

This paper aims to focus on the application of artificial intelligence in hospitals and medicine and how it can help improve healthcare systems in both urban and rural areas. The fuzzy expert system has been proposed to enhance the existing systems by adding new features and functions, thereby providing a better and more accurate diagnosis experience for patients in both rural and urban areas. By developing an application that can diagnose people in rural areas, we can help bridge the gap in healthcare access and deliver vital medical services to those in need.

So far, we have explored the panoply of qualitative representations and how they can be used in reasoning and communication in a wide variety of tasks, providing evidence for their utility and for their psychological plausibility. We have already seen some examples of how such representations tie into other forms of conceptual structure, as in the discussion of how qualitative representations play a role in natural-language semantics in chapter 13 and the discussion of how qualitative representations play a role in high-level vision in chapters 14 and 16. Here we go further in explicating the roles for qualitative representations in human conceptual structure by looking three important topics:

Cognitive radio technology has emerged as a promising solution for achieving real-time spectrum situational awareness (SSA) and signals intelligence (SIGNIT) over a wide spectrum range. The technology employs a cognitive engine that leverages machine learning-based hierarchical radio frequency (RF) signal identification to classify and associate signals using as few features as possible. The classification algorithms can be based on any machine learning algorithm such as artificial neural networks (ANNs) or deep learning.

The proposed design of the cognitive engine allows operators to define and modify SSA parameters during field operations. The design is based on two levels of signal classification, including a broad type of signals such as communications or radar, and specific signals within each of these classes. It is worth noting that the cognitive engine can handle more than two levels of signal classification, making it easy to generalize the design to suit different use cases.

The study shows that the hierarchical approach outperforms dedicated classifiers with similar computational complexity. Furthermore, the proposed design can realize a large number of SSA definitions using permutations of the same two-stage classifiers. This design feature makes the cognitive engine versatile, enabling operators to tailor the parameters to specific tasks as needed.

In conclusion, cognitive radio technology, powered by a machine learning-based cognitive engine, presents a viable solution for achieving real-time spectrum situational awareness and signals intelligence over a wide spectrum range. The proposed design allows for customization of SSA parameters during field operations, making the technology adaptable to different application scenarios. Additionally, the study shows that the hierarchical approach outperforms dedicated classifiers and, thus, makes the cognitive engine design more efficient.

In the age of industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing, a large volume of sensor data is produced from cyber-physical systems (CPS) and prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) of a machine or system becomes crucial for prognostics and health management (PHM). Several linear regression and deep learning models have been studied to extract features from segmented time windows and learn the degradation patterns. However, distributions of features are varying between source learning domain and target test domains, due to different working conditions and environments. Thus, the generalization of traditional methods will be influenced, which leads to performance degradation. This paper develops a domain adaptive CNN-LSTM (DACL) model to predict the RUL of a system based on the multi-dimensional sensor data. The DACL model combines the CNN and LSTM with domain adaptive transfer mechanism and takes the operating conditions into consideration. The features extracted by CNN of both source and target data are transformed to a higher dimensional space by reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and the loss function is compensated by using maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to reduce the distributions discrepancy. The model is evaluated on C-MAPSS dataset and demonstrate its performance improvement by comparing with previous methods.

This work presents a new perspective on how Zadeh's ideas related to fuzzy logic and computing with words have influenced the crucial issue of information aggregation and have led to what may be called a human-centric aggregation. We indicate a need to develop tools and techniques to reflect some fine shades of meaning regarding what can be considered the very purpose of human-centric aggregation, notably stated by various modalities in natural language specifications, in particular the usuality. We advocate the use of the ordered weighted average (OWA) operator, which is a formidable tool that can easily be tailored to a user?s intention as to the purpose and method of aggregation, generalizing many simple and natural aggregation types, such as the arithmetic mean, maximum and minimum, and probability. We show some of the most representative extensions and generalizations, including the induced OWA, the generalized OWA, the probabilistic OWA, and the OWA distance. We show their use in the basic case of the aggregation of numerical values and in social choice (voting) results. Then, we claim that linguistic data summaries in Yager?s sense can be considered an "ultimately human consistent" form of human-centric aggregation and show how the OWA operators can be used therein.

Can we predict the words a child is going to learn next given information about the words that a child knows now? Do different representations of a child's vocabulary knowledge affect our ability to predict the acquisition of lexical items for individual children? Past research has often focused on population statistics of vocabulary growth rather than prediction of words an individual child is likely to learn next. We consider a neural network approach to predict vocabulary acquisition. Specifically, we investigate how best to represent the child's current vocabulary in order to accurately predict future learning. The models we consider are based on qualitatively different sources of information: descriptive information about the child, the specific words a child knows, and representations that aim to capture the child's aggregate lexical knowledge. Using longitudinal vocabulary data from children aged 15-36 months, we construct neural network models to predict which words are likely to be learned by a particular child in the coming month. Many models based on child-specific vocabulary information outperform models with child information only, suggesting that the words a child knows influence prediction of future language learning. These models provide an understanding of the role of current vocabulary knowledge on future lexical growth.

In today's digital age, electronic data is being created in massive amounts. As a result, organizations that provide data recovery services are becoming increasingly important. These organizations may encounter various types of disasters, be it natural or man-made, which can lead to significant data loss. Recovery technology provides a way to retrieve information from backup servers in the event of the main data server being lost due to a disaster. However, there are difficulties associated with implementing such techniques, such as the complexity of cost and time. By utilizing disaster conditions as a service, organizations can address these difficulties and enable data recovery at a lower cost and faster speed. 

This paper aims to compare and discuss various techniques for creating a robust backup and recovery system. All of these techniques have three core aspects in common: cost control, data replication, and security. By focusing on these three aspects, organizations can ensure that their backup and recovery system is designed to operate seamlessly and provide maximum data protection.

Utilizing Blockchain in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) can provide a potential solution to solving forensic challenges. The blockchain can be utilized in SDN-based Internet of Things (IoT) environments to enhance security provisioning and tackle digital forensics challenges such as data integrity and evidence deletion or alteration. However, previous works encountered problems such as poor attack detection and slow processing.

To overcome these issues, an effective forensics architecture is proposed in SDN-IoT to establish the Chain of Custody (CoC) using blockchain technology. The proposed SDN-based IoT architecture initiates flow table rules on switches for three types of traffic (Voice over Internet Protocol, File Transfer Protocol, and Hyper Text Transfer Protocol). In this work, overloaded switches migrate packets to nearby switches to balance the packet flow, while packets disobeying flow rules are discarded by the switches. 

The blockchain-based distributed controller in this forensic architecture uses the Linear Homomorphic Signature (LHS) algorithm to validate users. Each controller is fed with a classifier that uses Neuro Multi-fuzzy to classify malicious packets based on packet features. The event logs are used and stored on the blockchain in the proposed SDN-IoT architecture.

The performance of our forensic architecture was evaluated and compared to the existing model using various performance measures. Our evaluation results demonstrate performance improvement by reducing delay, response time, and processing time while increasing throughput, accuracy, and security parameters. Thus, utilizing blockchain in SDN-IoT environments can offer an efficient solution for enhancing forensic capabilities.

As multimedia data continues to grow rapidly on the Web, learning-based hashing techniques have proven to be successful for large-scale multimedia search. However, previous methods have limitations such as repetitive and highly correlated information in learned hash codes. In response, we propose a novel learning-based hashing method called deep attention-guided hashing (DAgH) that uses two stream frameworks. The first hashing network generates attention-guided hash codes with an attention network and hashing network, while the second hashing network is guided by these codes as supervised labels. Our loss function contains semantic and attention loss components, with the latter punishing the attention network to obtain salient regions. Results from our experiments demonstrate that DAgH generates high-quality hash codes and outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets.

In this paper, we propose a new power allocation scheme for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems in space information networks (SINs). With limited communication resources, such as power and storage on satellites, we focus on an optimization policy for long-term resource allocation that meets practical constraints. To solve this problem, we utilize the Lyapunov optimization framework to transform the long-term optimization problem into a series of online power allocation and rate control problems. By implementing the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, we can derive a globally optimal solution to this joint optimization problem with a linear computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that our joint optimization allocation NOMA scheme for SIN outperforms other schemes such as OMA and multiple sub-optimal NOMA benchmark schemes in terms of long-term network utility, average arriving rate, and queuing delay.

For an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM), parameter mismatching can have a significant impact on its performance and output efficiency. In this paper, we propose a variable parameter Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) control method based on online parameters identification.

We utilize an adaptive linear neural network algorithm to accurately identify the motor parameters, following which the MTPA control is modified by combining the identified parameters. Our approach demonstrates excellent adaptability to parameters mismatching, leading to improved output efficiency that is particularly advantageous for magnetic recording motor applications.

Overall, the results of this study suggest that our proposed strategy presents a promising solution for increasing the performance and output efficiency of interior permanent magnet synchronous machines, even in the presence of parameters mismatching.

In this study, a neural network pattern recognition tool was used to determine its effectiveness in identifying the gender of participants based on their ground reaction force patterns. The study involved 33 individuals, both male and female, and 132 recorded trials. The parameters of peak and trough were established for each pattern and used as inputs for the algorithm. These data clusters served to train, test, and validate the neural network through pattern recognition.

The findings of this study revealed that the neural network demonstrated considerable capability in identifying the gender of participants based on the peak parameters of ground reaction force. This innovative approach could potentially open avenues for using pattern recognition and machine learning in tasks related to biomechanics and physical performance.

A movable cable-driven lower-limb rehabilitation robot has been designed to aid patients with lower-limb dysfunction in restoring their motor function and enhancing their quality of life. The robot can control the position, posture and force of the lower limb, thus facilitating the comprehensive training of the lower limbs. The robot has various modes (passive, assistant and active) to assist patients in different rehabilitation stages with their rehabilitation training. Kinematics modeling, statics modeling and workspace analysis were conducted, and the robot configurations were analyzed and optimized based on these. Continuous cable tension was calculated using the 2-norm of the cable tension optimization algorithm. This work has laid the foundation for the subsequent research on parallel cable-driven lower-limb rehabilitation robot, and it serves as a reference for the development of flexible medical rehabilitation equipment.

This paper proposes a fast algorithm for the training of adaptive hinging hyperplanes (AHH), which is a popular and effective continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) model consisting of a linear combination of basis functions. The original AHH incrementally generates new basis functions by simply traversing all the existing basis functions in each dimension with the pre-given knots. Meanwhile, it also incorporates a backward procedure to delete redundant basis functions, which avoids over-fitting. In this paper, we accelerate the procedure of AHH in generating new basis functions, and the backward deletion is replaced with Lasso regularization, which is robust, requires less computation, and manages to prevent over-fitting. Besides, the selection of the splitting knots based on training data is also discussed. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the efficiency of the existing AHH algorithm even with higher accuracy and it also enhances robustness in the given benchmark problems.

My research during my PhD [1] focused on better understanding how individuals interact with the web. By analyzing the traces and logs of users' traffic, I developed two primary areas of study - data analytics and user modeling - that provide greater insight into how web services and users evolve over time.

Using machine learning techniques, I reconstructed users' online activity from passive measurements and developed models to identify the web pages and sites they intentionally visit. I also examined the evolution of device usage, the structure of navigation, and the interactions with social networks and search engines. By building users' profiles, I was able to create unique behavioral fingerprints that allowed me to re-identify users in the future, providing valuable insights for security applications.

In addition, I explored the dynamics of online advertising and its impact on revenue. By capturing the temporal dynamics of shown advertisements, I was able to improve revenues and enhance overall user experiences.

To ensure that my research is reproducible and fosters further analysis, I have made available all anonymized datasets and code to the community.

Overall, my research provides valuable insights into how people interact with the web and how ISPs and network managers can better serve their users based on their behavior and needs.

Many existing data is inconsistent due to various reasons, such as noise, missing data, or repeated errors. Previously, the CDP clustering algorithm has been shown as an effective method to detect data anomalies. Yet, single computational processor or sequential version of the CDP algorithm demands lengthy computational times and often not acceptable in practice when dealing with voluminous data. In this paper, we propose the PCDP algorithm on detecting data anomalies by parallelizing the CDP algorithm with the support of multiple machines. Through preliminary experiments, the PCDP algorithm has demonstrated its fast computation performance as well as retaining the anomaly detection accuracy for customer data of a commercial bank.

The selection of an appropriate reference model in data-driven control techniques is a crucial step as it has a significant impact on the closed-loop performance of the system. Moreover, the reference model should be achievable by the plant as well. In this letter, we present a methodology to construct a reference model that is not only achievable by the plant but also exhibits the desired behavior. The method is suitable for linear time-invariant (LTI) monovariable systems and involves the estimation of plant instabilities using an innovative data-driven stability analysis technique.

The proposed approach employs the Loewner data-driven control (L-DDC) algorithm to demonstrate the influence of the reference model on the design of the controller. Our choice of reference model specifications allows for the use of a controller validation technique based on the small-gain theorem. 

In summary, the approach presented in this letter provides a systematic method for determining a reference model for LTI monovariable systems. The proposed reference model is reproducible by the system and exhibits the desired behavior. The proposed controller validation technique based on the small-gain theorem ensures that the control system meets the desired specifications. Overall, the methodology proposed in this letter provides a robust and effective framework for data-driven control design.

Recently, there has been a significant increase in the number of accidents and incidents involving remotely piloted aircraft (RPA). As a result, researchers and engineers have turned their attention towards developing a complete software and hardware system based on antenna arrays and direction of arrival (DoA) estimation, to effectively locate intruding RPA. DoA estimation can be achieved through relative phase between antennas in an antenna array or received signal strength (RSS) estimation of an array of directional antennas. Prior works on DoA estimation through RSS utilized platonic solid geometry linked with the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. In this study, we propose a new DoA estimation algorithm, which focuses on exploiting incoming NTSC video signals to locate drones. We validated our algorithm by using an AD-FMCOMMS5-EBZ software-defined radio (SDR) platform with a Yagi-Uda antenna array in a measurement campaign. Results demonstrated that out of 19 different DoAs measured, ranging from -90° to 90° with steps of 10°, we obtained 14 accurate estimates, including the end-fire positions critical in traditional omnidirectional antenna array-based solutions.

With the rapid growth of the Industrial Internet of Things, industrial equipment is expected to increase in both categories and quantity. The intelligent manufacturing process demands centralized monitoring and management of numerous and multivariate equipment, which requires the identification of equipment categories. Manual labeling of electrical equipment is expensive, making it impractical. In order to accurately recognize industrial equipment in manufacturing systems, this study uses long short-term memory to analyze big data features and create a nonintrusive load monitoring system. The system employs edge computing to execute parallel computing, which improves the efficiency of equipment identification. To ensure practicality and affordability, a fairly priced low-frequency Smart Meter is used to collect the appliance data. The proposed optimal adjustment strategy of parameter model achieves an average random recognition rate of 88%. Furthermore, the average recognition rate of the continuous data of a single electrical equipment can achieve 83.6%.

After conducting a comparative analysis, we have confirmed that the dark channel pixels of the smoke image contain more detailed information than the non-smoke image pixels. This finding has led to the proposal of a dual convolution network named DarkC-DCN, which utilizes the dark channel prior for image smoke classification. The inception of DarkC-DCN is based on the AlexNet and incorporates continuous structural improvement and optimization to form a detailed CNN, which effectively extracts the features of dark channel images. Additionally, a residual network has been designed to extract general features in the image, forming the main framework of the entire network. To ensure the network's robustness, the two channels are trained separately for various inputs, and feature fusion is performed before the common fully connected layer. In the experiment, non-smoke data that is similar to smoke has been added to the public smoke data set for data expansion. The experimental results reveal that DarkC-DCN has performed well, with an accuracy value of 98.56%.

In named data networking (NDN), name lookup is a crucial technology for packet forwarding, similar to IP lookup in traditional networking. However, the hierarchical names used in NDN are of variable and unlimited length, in contrast to fixed-length IP addresses. This, combined with the large-scale name prefix database and high-frequency name update requirements, poses unprecedented challenges for high-performance packet forwarding.

Existing approaches have limitations that make it difficult to meet these requirements, such as complex structures, frequent memory access, and time-consuming encoding. To address these challenges, we propose CoDE, a conflict-driven encoding approach that achieves fast name lookup and updates. 

CoDE features a compact and scalable data structure that can be stored in the cache, and an efficient index for fast name and prefix location. The conflict-driven mechanism significantly reduces the number of name components that need to be encoded. 

Experimental results using real name prefix databases show that CoDE outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms. It achieves an order of magnitude faster name lookup and twenty times faster prefix updates compared to other algorithms on average. CoDE also reduces memory footprint by at least half compared to other algorithms. 

Overall, CoDE provides an effective solution for fast and efficient name lookup and updates in NDN, making it a promising option for high-performance packet forwarding.

Risk assessment is a central element for the development and validation of autonomous vehicles. It comprises a combination of occurrence probability and severity of future critical events. Time headway (TH) as well as time-to-contact (TTC) are commonly used risk metrics and have qualitative relations to occurrence probability. However, they lack theoretical derivations and additionally they are designed to only cover special types of traffic scenarios (e.g., longitudinal following between single car pairs). In this paper, we present a probabilistic situation risk model based on survival analysis considerations and extend it to naturally incorporate sensory, temporal, and behavioral uncertainties as they arise in real-world scenarios. The resulting risk spot detector (RSD) is applied and tested on naturalistic driving data of a multilane boulevard with several intersections, enabling the visualization of road criticality maps. Compared to TH and TTC, our approach is more selective and specific in predicting risk. RSD concentrates on driving sections of high vehicle density where large accelerations and decelerations or approaches with high velocity occur.

Spatial-temporal patterning is a critical process in synthetic and natural tissue development, as it determines the cell and tissue types that form. However, due to the complexity of biological systems, most approaches to engineering cell cultures have limited ability in controlling the timing of spatial patterning. To address this issue, this paper proposes a computational framework that can control spatial-temporal pattern formation in a network of locally interacting agents. 

The framework uses a parameterized model of patterning in stem cell colonies and combines supervised machine learning algorithm with temporal logics to quantitatively describe and characterize spatial-temporal patterns. An optimization procedure is utilized to achieve optimal parameters that maximize the occurrence of desired spatial patterns at a specified time interval. The results demonstrate that the algorithm can control transitioning in a sequence of patterns, thereby indicating the potential for future applications in biotechnological research.

Recently, Bluetooth low energy (BLE) is widely used for short-range communication among wireless devices. The challenge of utilizing BLE in indoor localization is the characteristic of the observation area where multipath fading, shadowing, interference, and reflection of signal would appear. This paper proposed a new approach of evaluating the performance of wireless device communication system using BLE module in an indoor environment in term of estimating the position of the device using localization technique. Linear Regression method is used to refine the modeling distance parameter which measured previously. The simulation result shows that combining Linear Regression and Lognormal shadowing method for distance modeling will enhance the accuracy up to 99%.

Taxi demand prediction has recently attracted increasing research interest due to its huge potential application in large-scale intelligent transportation systems. However, most of the previous methods only considered the taxi demand prediction in origin regions, but neglected the modeling of the specific situation of the destination passengers. We believe it is suboptimal to preallocate the taxi into each region-based solely on the taxi origin demand. In this paper, we present a challenging and worth-exploring task, called taxi origin-destination demand prediction, which aims at predicting the taxi demand between all-region pairs in a future time interval. Its main challenges come from how to effectively capture the diverse contextual information to learn the demand patterns. We address this problem with a novel contextualized spatial-temporal network (CSTN), which consists of three components for the modeling of local spatial context (LSC), temporal evolution context (TEC), and global correlation context (GCC), respectively. First, an LSC module utilizes two convolution neural networks to learn the local spatial dependencies of taxi, demand respectively, from the origin view and the destination view. Second, a TEC module incorporates the local spatial features of taxi demand and the meteorological information to a Convolutional Long Short-term Memory Network (ConvLSTM) for the analysis of taxi demand evolution. Finally, a GCC module is applied to model the correlation between all regions by computing a global correlation feature as a weighted sum of all regional features, with the weights being calculated as the similarity between the corresponding region pairs. The extensive experiments and evaluations on a large-scale dataset well demonstrate the superiority of our CSTN over other compared methods for the taxi origin-destination demand prediction.

Multiple robot systems (MRSs) are extensively utilized in a wide range of applications, including military and civil domains. To enhance their efficiency in scenarios such as path planning, situation awareness, and cooperative inference, machine learning approaches, particularly deep learning, have been widely adopted. However, individual robots often have insufficient resources to meet the high computational requirements of deep learning. A potential solution to this problem is cloud-augmented MRSs, where the central cloud performs computational tasks while the robots execute simple ones. Nonetheless, this approach can cause long transmission latency, which is unsuitable for critical applications that require a quick response. Recently, cooperative deep inference has emerged as an adaptive intelligence solution for cloud-augmented MRSs. Adaptive intelligence enables the system to determine which task parts to execute on the robot and which ones on the cloud for energy and time efficiency, maintaining some specific task requirements. In this paper, we survey recent advancements in cooperative deep inference and provide a framework for enabling adaptive intelligence in cloud-augmented MRSs. Finally, we illustrate that the proposed framework can efficiently reduce response latency using a target detection scenario.

Despite significant progress in emotion recognition, current methods are limited by the use of single modality or the lack of synchronous use of multiple modalities. In response to this challenge, we introduce a new crossmodal emotion embedding framework called EmoBed, which aims to enhance emotion recognition by leveraging knowledge from other modalities. The framework consists of two main components, joint multimodal training and crossmodal training, both of which aim to extract the underlying emotional semantics using a shared recognition network or a shared emotion embedding space, respectively. This approach allows the system to effectively use complementary information from multiple modalities, without the need for these modalities during inference. To evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of EmoBed, we conducted extensive experiments on two benchmark databases, RECOLA and OMG-Emotion, for the tasks of dimensional emotion regression and categorical emotion classification, respectively. The results demonstrate that EmoBed outperforms related baselines in monomodal inference and is competitive with or superior to recently reported systems, highlighting the significance of crossmodal learning for emotion recognition.

We present a comprehensive simulation platform for computational microwave imaging systems based on frequency-diverse metasurface antennas (FDMAs). FDMAs consist of a waveguide patterned with complementary metamaterial elements with resonant frequencies selected randomly from a band of operation, enabling the generation of distinct frequency-indexed radiation patterns. By accurately modeling the fields produced by the FDMA using a dipolar model, it is possible to predict the capabilities of the imaging system in a fast and reliable manner. In contrast to previous works, in this paper we include the mutual interaction between metamaterial elements, and it is demonstrated that these interactions are crucial to a better understanding of the FDMAs' capabilities e. g. effective aperture area and correlation of radiation patterns. The simplicity and accuracy of the proposed model permits the simulation of different metasurfaces for computational microwave imaging, where traditional antenna design- and metamaterial modeling-are prohibitively costly.

We systemically investigated the influence of sidewall morphology change based on TMAH etching on the optical performance of mini-LEDs. The dominant feature of prism structures on the sidewall of mini-LEDs with TMAH etching treatment varied from inhomogeneous to homogeneous as the TMAH etching time prolonged. Such prism structures only appeared on the sidewall along direction owing to the anisotropic TMAH etching. Experimental and simulation results demonstrated that these prism structures can effectively improve the light extraction from sidewall and homogenous prism structures on the sidewall function better in out-coupling light.

A cloud-based big data sharing system is a useful tool for sharing data with legitimate users. However, traditional solutions can present confidentiality issues due to the storage of shared data in data centers outside the data owner's trust domain. To address this problem, this paper proposes a secret sharing group key management protocol called SSGK. The protocol utilizes a group key to encrypt the shared data, and a secret sharing scheme to distribute the group key. This approach is different from prior works, and it highly minimizes security and privacy risks associated with sharing data in cloud storage. Additionally, SSGK saves about 12% of storage space. Our extensive security and performance analyses validate the effectiveness of the SSGK protocol.

The concept of utilizing a heterogeneous network is set to revolutionize the fifth generation mobile communication systems. The aim of this implementation is to enhance both network throughput and user throughput. Although many techniques have been investigated to achieve these goals, they are easily degraded by various factors. To combat this, the use of side information such as the terminal location and Doppler frequency could assist in avoiding performance degradation. By knowing the Doppler frequency before signal transmission, the reduction in throughput can be alleviated by selecting modulation schemes with lower cardinality.

This paper proposes a technique for Doppler frequency estimation using overlap frequency domain equalization and an optimum FDE weight derived for the proposed estimation technique. The proposed estimation technique with the optimum FDE weight achieves better estimation performance than the conventional MMSE weight.

In recent years, numerous measures of semantic relatedness have been proposed, but little is known about their effectiveness in real-world applications. This paper presents a unifying approach that classifies these measures into two categories: topic-based and ontology-based models. Despite the extensive research on ontology-based models, the significance of topic-based models has not been fully recognized. By presenting a comprehensive and cohesive approach to topic-based models, it aims to demonstrate the similarities and differences among them and to provide a theoretical link between topic-based and ontology-based models.

This unified approach has been tested using comprehensive experiments on geographic phrases, showing that topic-based models have significant advantages over ontology-based models. Their performance in computing sematic relatedness is superior and less restricted in real-world applications. These results suggest that topic-based models should be given more attention and consideration when developing semantic relatedness measures.

Mobile crowdsourcing in opportunist networks is a process that allows the outsourcing of location-based tasks to a crowd of workers. These tasks may include taking photos and surveying Wi-Fi signal characteristics at points of interest. Usually, the efficiency of task assignments is measured in terms of makespan. However, the quality of the performed tasks is equally important. This paper proposes two task assignment schemes, namely quality-aware task assignment (QA-TA) and minimum quality threshold task assignment (MQT-TA). 

The QA-TA scheme aims to maximize the quality of tasks within a given deadline, while the MQT-TA aims to minimize the makespan for a given minimum quality requirement. These schemes utilize the optimal stopping technique from mathematics for their algorithm designs. 

Simulation results using real mobility traces show that the proposed schemes achieve their design goals. Consequently, these schemes provide a more efficient solution for mobile crowdsourcing in opportunistic networks.

Skin cancer is a growing public health concern worldwide, and the initial diagnosis often relies on the appearance of skin lesions. Automated methods to assist in screening for malign lesions have been proposed as a potentially valuable tool. However, the efficacy of these methods depends on the quality of the generated feature space, which can vary depending on the image dataset and source used. In this study, we examined feature spaces obtained from deep convolutional networks (CNNs) using the PH2 dataset, testing three CNN architectures while investigating different layers, the impact of dimensionality reduction, and the use of color quantization and noise addition. Our findings reveal that the features have a comparable discriminative capability to other methods, with a balanced accuracy of 94%, and 95% with noise injection. Additionally, we performed a study of fine-tuning and generalization across image quantization and noise levels, contributing to the discussion of learning features from deep networks and offering a guideline for future research.

Preserving and protecting old books is crucial for future generations. However, preserving old antiques can present challenges, including errors, noises, and poor printing mechanisms. Moreover, correcting misspelled words in the complex Sinhala language can be difficult. To address these challenges, a new approach has been developed using machine vision and natural language processing to preserve text content in a searchable digital format. First, scanned images of old books are preprocessed to remove noise, and segmentation is used to aid character recognition. Optical character recognition (OCR) is then used to recognize text, and Sinhala spell correction is employed to correct errors. The system also provides summaries of the books and chapters, which is a challenge for the structured Sinhala language. Despite these challenges, the system achieves an average success rate of 84% for Text Line Segmentation and Layout Feature Identification, and 74% for OCR. Additionally, the system achieves an average success rate of 70% for OCR Correction, 75% for Keyword Extraction, and 52% for Summarization. Overall, this new approach offers a promising solution for preserving old books for future generations.

Cell-free massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) is considered, where distributed access points (APs) multiply the received signal by the conjugate of the estimated channel, and send back a quantized version of this weighted signal to a central processing unit (CPU). For the first time, we present a performance comparison between the case of perfect fronthaul links, the case when the quantized version of the estimated channel and the quantized signal are available at the CPU, and the case when only the quantized weighted signal is available at the CPU. The Bussgang decomposition is used to model the effect of quantization. The max-min problem is studied, where the minimum rate is maximized with the power and fronthaul capacity constraints. To deal with the non-convex problem, the original problem is decomposed into two sub-problems (referred to as receiver filter design and power allocation). Geometric programming (GP) is exploited to solve the power allocation problem whereas a generalized eigenvalue problem is solved to design the receiver filter. An iterative scheme is developed and the optimality of the proposed algorithm is proved through uplink-downlink duality. A user assignment algorithm is proposed which significantly improves the performance. The numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed schemes.

LoRaWAN is a rapidly developing technology that enables Low Power Wide Area Networks to connect billions of Internet of Things devices worldwide. It promises universal connectivity while keeping network structures and management simple. However, one major challenge is how to assign a spreading factor effectively, so that a single gateway can support a large number of end devices within a LoRaWAN cell. 

This research confirms that employing a more sophisticated spreading factor allocation strategy than the commonly used Adaptive Data Rate considerably improves network performance. The proposed heuristics are based on the fact that each subset of end devices assigned to a specific spreading factor establishes a spreading factor tier, which represents a pure Aloha network with a different packet length. Additionally, the data is used to control transmission parameters, which in turn control coverage sensitivities and system load in each spreading factor tier.
