The second strategy does not compare a generated offspring individual with its parent but the worst individual in the current population, which can accelerate the elimination of poor individuals and keep better individuals. We design a set of controlled experiments to evaluate these two strategies using CEC2013 benchmark functions with three different dimensions. The experimental results indicate that properly enhancing competition among individuals in DE can speed up its convergence and improve optimization performance.

As the number of mobile devices that natively support ad hoc communication protocols increase, large ad hoc networks can be created not only to facilitate communication among the mobile devices, but also to assist devices that are executing computationally intensive applications. Prior work has developed computation offloading systems for mobile devices, but this work has focused exclusively on offloading to single hop neighbors, due in part to the practical challenges of setting up multi-hop networks using existing ad hoc communication protocols. However, limiting the offloading of computation to one-hop neighbors inherently restricts the number of devices that can participate in the distributed computation. By presenting a heuristic, aimed at avoiding partitioning the network, as well as an iterative task assignment algorithm that can optimize the assignment of computational tasks to devices in a multi-hop cooperative network, we are able to evaluate the effect of computational offloading in multi-hop networks. Experimental results, obtained from an implementation on Android devices, are integrated with an analytical model that enables the evaluation of system performance under a variety of conditions. These experimental and analytic results demonstrate the benefit of enabling computation offloading to all devices in a multi-hop cooperative network.

Charge imbalance is a common problem in battery systems, which can lead to decreased performance and reliability. This can be caused by various factors such as manufacturing variations, inconsistent charging/discharging, and uneven thermal distribution. To address this issue, external circuit designs and internal battery cell/module/pack connections can be utilized for charge balancing. 

This paper focuses on reducing battery charge equalization (BCE) time by reconfiguring individual battery cells/modules. Reconfiguration algorithms are proposed for fast charge equalization under different levels of system reconfigurability. For systems allowing both module and intra-module cell reconfiguration, the proposed module-based bounded reconfiguration algorithm can achieve the minimum BCE times obtained by exhaustive search. When inter-module cell reconfiguration is allowed, the proposed module-based complete reconfiguration algorithm can achieve similar optimality to genetic algorithms with much less computational time. 

Circuit and numerical experiments demonstrate the optimality and computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms compared to other methods. By utilizing reconfigurable modules and intra/inter-cell reconfiguration, the proposed algorithms can effectively reduce BCE time and enhance the performance and reliability of battery systems.

Although 3D object recognition primarily focuses on small human manipulable objects, the challenge of recognizing large-scale objects remains a significant obstacle, particularly in the context of mobile robot manipulation and navigation tasks. This is especially true when dealing with objects that are only partially visible or far away from the camera and robot due to their size. In response, our research proposes a framework capable of recognizing and estimating the pose of large-scale objects. 

Our proposed framework utilizes semi-global descriptors for both scene segments and model views in combination with up-sampling and segment label merging techniques to achieve high accuracy. We refine the initially estimated pose and verify it to ensure reliability. We compared different model descriptors and determined that semi-global descriptors provided the most promising results. 

Through simultaneous reconstruction, segmentation, and recognition, our framework enables the recognition of large-scale objects and the estimation of their 6D poses.

While action video games have been shown to be effective for improving attention, there has been little research on how haptic interaction can be utilized for attention modulation and training in these games. To address this issue, we introduce a visuo-haptic game that combines fingertip force control with an immersive visual display. The game requires users to press a force sensor using either their index or middle finger from both hands, and respond quickly to visual cues by producing accurate fingertip force within a specific time frame. The difficulty of the task is dynamically adjusted using an adaptive model to maintain a constant success rate. We conducted validation tests on 12 participants and confirmed that the proposed model is capable of maintaining a success rate of 75% with fluctuations of ±5%. 

To examine the efficacy of the attention training, we administered pre- and post-tests to 12 trainees using the sustained-attention-to-response task (SART) and Stroop task. After five days of attention training with the proposed game, significant improvements were observed in both attention tests. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed visuo-haptic game for attention training.

A fast and efficient method for estimating the time-delay in a linear frequency modulation signal has been proposed, called the frFt-TELS estimator. This approach involves searching for the maximal bin of the fractional Fourier transform (frFt) as a rough estimation, followed by applying Taylor expansion to the theoretical frFt power spectrum around the coarse estimation. The fine estimation is then obtained by using least squares approximation between the theoretical frFt power spectrum and the frFt power spectrum of the given sample data. The simulations conducted have demonstrated that frFt-TELS achieves comparable performance to traditional estimators, while being computationally less complex.

For the problem of remaining useful lifetime (RUL) prediction of nonlinear system, the existing methods have not systematically carried out the studies on nonlinear degradation modeling with measurement error and random effect, priori parameter estimation and the corresponding RUL prediction. In this paper, a nonlinear Wiener process is used to establish a nonlinear degradation model with the consideration of measurement error and random effect to describe the implicitness, personality difference and nonlinearity of degradation process of a class of device. The expectation maximum (EM) algorithm is used to obtain the estimates of the fixed coefficient and the priori distributions of the random coefficients in the degradation model. Using the current monitoring data of the target device, the posteriori distribution of random coefficients is iteratively updated based on Bayesian inference. Using the full-probability formula, the remaining useful lifetime distribution of device is derived based on the first hitting time (FHT) distribution. A simulation example is analyzed to verify the correctness and advantage of this method.

The overwhelming commercial success of connected things and personal mobile devices is driving the dense and uncontrolled deployment of wireless networks using unlicensed frequency bands. This results in heavy congestion and interference, leading to considerable loss of network performance. The only sustainable solution is some form of collaboration between users. Not only does this require new technology to facilitate such collaboration, it also demands for new business models that accommodate new, collaboration facilitating roles. In this paper we propose a generic business model for sustainable spectrum sharing in unlicensed frequency band. It includes two new actors, the Spectrum Broker and the Wi-5 System Operator. The business model is tested against popular use cases, in dialogue with various European network operators. The results indicate that the model is applicable and viable.

In this study, external magnetic fields measured by the magnetometer sensors are considered. For low-Earth orbiting (LEO) satellites, there are variety of magnetometers available off-the-shelf commercially. Their noise levels differ based on the mission goals of the satellites and technological advances. Earth's geomagnetic field predicted by the geomagnetic field models is used for satellite attitude control. Any deviations from the model fields, caused by the external sources such as magnetic storms, are treated as magnetometer noise or bias. This may prevent the determination of the magnitude of the effects from the external sources correctly. This study aims to reveal the magnitude of the geomagnetic field variations due to the magnetospheric storms obscured by the magnetometer noise level used in the attitude control systems by implementing a range of magnetometer sensor noise levels on the simulation of the satellite's rotational motion for the selected geomagnetic storm events.

Today LEDs are continuously expanding in accordance with domestic and overseas energy policies, and related visible light communication technologies are attracting attention. This study constructs a sensing communication mode together with a unidirectional communication mode and a bidirectional communication mode of LEDs. In particular, the sensing communication mode proposes a design that dynamically configures the sensing module to optimize the communication performance and quality according to the external environmental variables of the optical wireless communication. The performance evaluation environment is a room where indoor fluorescent light and outdoor natural light illuminate. Therefore, we describe the sensitive design and future research directions of indoor LED based wireless visible light communication system.

Queue length is a critical measure of intersection performance, and the use of Probe vehicles (PVs) with advanced sensors to estimate queue length based on recorded vehicle trajectories has received considerable attention in the past decade. However, this technique typically requires high PV penetration rates of over 25% to ensure accuracy. While PVs are expected to increase, their penetration rate will likely remain relatively low in the near future. Moreover, most studies fail to account for the effect of the initial queue on cyclic queue length estimation, which is another important factor that directly impacts queue dynamics. 

To address these challenges, this paper proposes a cycle-based end of queue estimation method using sampled vehicle trajectory data under relatively low penetration rates. The method involves two major steps: modeling the vehicle arrival process as a certain distribution in line with traffic conditions and using an Expectation-Maximization (EM) procedure to estimate the arrival rate of each cycle; then estimating both ends of the queue and initial queue at each cycle based on shockwave theory. 

The performance of the proposed method is examined using the microscopic traffic simulator VISSIM, and the experimental results demonstrate that the cycle-based end of the queue can be estimated with desirable accuracy in different scenarios, including undersaturated, oversaturated, and queue spillback conditions. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods verify the advantage of the proposed method, especially under low-penetration-rate conditions.

The performance of hyperspectral image classification can be enhanced by incorporating texture information due to the spatial structural characteristic of surface materials. Predefined operators such as extended multiattribute profiles (EMAPs) and Gabor filters can be used for extracting spatial structure. However, superpixel segmentation, which reflects the homogeneous regularity of objects, has recently gained popularity. This paper proposes a collaborative representation-based multiscale superpixel fusion (CRMSF) approach for hyperspectral image classification. 

The EMAPs are first obtained from the raw hyperspectral image, and a group of predesigned 3-D Gabor wavelet filters is convolved with the EMAP features to achieve EMAP-Gabor features. Collaborative representation-based classification (CRC) then fully and efficiently makes use of the extracted EMAP-Gabor features. Multiscale superpixel maps are generated from the EMAP features and are used to regularize the classification map obtained by CRC. A heuristic strategy is employed to automatically decide the number of extracted superpixels in multiple scales, which can be perfectly compatible with hyperspectral images having various spatial sizes and resolutions. 

The classification task is accomplished by fusing the multiple regularized classification maps. The CRMSF approach is evaluated on four popular hyperspectral image datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate the advantages of CRMSF, particularly for hyperspectral images with high spatial resolution. The developed CRMSF approach's most important contribution is its heuristic strategy that can automatically decide the number of extracted superpixels in multiple scales, making it perfectly compatible with hyperspectral images of varying spatial sizes and resolutions.

Software Defined Networking (SDN) has been identified as the future of networking due to its ability to provide a central point of control over the entire network and the separation of software and hardware. SDN has the potential to deploy a range of network applications including load balancers, IPv4-IPv6 converters, virtual machines (VMs), intrusion detection systems (IDS) and intrusion prevention systems (IPS). However, the current deployments of these network applications have several shortcomings. To address these limitations, SDN solutions have been proposed.

In this survey, research papers were reviewed to understand the shortcomings of current deployments of network applications and to propose an SDN solution to overcome them. Three approaches to deploying SDN solutions were identified: the rip and replace model, the overlay model, and the hybrid model. The best approach for deploying an SDN solution for each of the discussed network applications was proposed.

The rip and replace model involves replacing the entire network infrastructure with an SDN solution. This approach is suitable for enterprises with outdated network infrastructure. The overlay model involves deploying an SDN solution on top of existing network infrastructure. This approach is suitable for enterprises with deployed network infrastructure that cannot be completely replaced. The hybrid model involves a combination of the rip and replace and overlay models. This approach is suitable for enterprises with partially outdated network infrastructure that requires upgrading.

Based on these deployment models, the proposed solution for load balancers is the overlay model. The proposed solution for IPv4-IPv6 converters is the hybrid model. The proposed solution for VMs is the rip and replace model. The proposed solution for IDS and IPS systems is the hybrid model.

In conclusion, the deployment of SDN solutions provides a better performance over traditional network infrastructure. By assessing the shortcomings of network applications in the current deployment, it is possible to choose the most appropriate deployment model for each network application. The proposed solutions and deployment models would help enterprises to realise the benefits of SDN in their networks.

This note investigates the output regulation problem of Boolean control networks (BCNs) under event-triggered control via semi-tensor product of matrices. Firstly, based on an algebraic state-space representation of BCNs, a necessary and sufficient condition is obtained for the solvability of the output regulation problem. Secondly, the feedback event-triggered control laws are obtained by using augmented system approach. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed results.

The revolution of deep neural networks (DNNs) has brought significant progress in the development of autonomous driving. However, achieving both timing predictability and energy efficiency in any DNN-based autonomous driving system is challenging due to their conflicting goals. In this paper, we introduce PredJoule, a novel framework for optimizing DNN workloads in a GPU-enabled automotive system that achieves both latency guarantees and energy efficiency.

PredJoule relies on a layer-aware design that explores the specific performance and energy characteristics of different layers within the neural network. We evaluated the system on the automotive-specific NVIDIA Jetson TX2 platform for five state-of-the-art DNN models with both high and low variance latency requirements. The results show that PredJoule rarely violates job deadlines and can improve energy efficiency by 65% on average compared to five existing approaches and 68% compared to an energy-oriented approach.

In summary, PredJoule is a promising solution for achieving both timing predictability and energy efficiency in DNN-based autonomous driving systems. By taking into account the specific performance and energy characteristics of different layers, PredJoule demonstrates improved energy efficiency while meeting job latency requirements.

The article discusses the end-to-end business concept of governance of information technology in the context of e-commerce enterprises as a sector of the digital economy that needs to improve the quality of management and training of targeted personnel. Processes for governance of enterprise IT were considered in accordance with the COBIT 5 methodology. Analysis and selection of IT enterprise management processes in e-commerce was carried out. An adapted CobiT model for ecommerce enterprises and a graphical model of the space of topics and competencies for learning in the digital economy are proposed.

Nowadays, based-on mobile devices and internet, social network services(SNS) are common trends to everyone. Thus, decision of social and public opinions, and polarity about social happenings, political issues, government policies and decision, or commercial products is very important to the government, company, and a person. But, SNS are basically making newly-coined words and emoticons. Especially, emoticons are made by a person or companies. Newly-coined words are mostly made by communities. The SNS big data mainly consists of his kinds of newly-coined words and emoticons so that newly-coined words and emoticons analysis are very important to understand the social and public opinions, and polarity about social happenings, political issues, government policies and decision, or commercial products. Social big data is unstructured data and contains many newly-coined words and various emoticons. Therefore, there is a limitation to guarantee the accuracy and analysis range of social data of emotional analysis. The newly-coined words contains the social phenomena and trends of modern society implicitly. And the emoticons are electronic quasi-languages made up of letters and symbols, and express the emotional state more implicitly. Although the newly-coined words and emoticons are an important part of the emotional analysis, they are excluded from the emotional dictionary and analysis. In this research, newly-coined words and emoticons extracted from the raw twit messages include polarity and weight with pre-built dictionary. The polarity and weight would be calculated for emotional classification. The proposed emotional classification equation adds up the weights among the same polarity(positive or negative) and sums the negative weight value with the positive weight values. The polarity summation result is recorded in the variable. If the polarity summation result is more than threshold value, the twit message is decided as positive. If it is less than threshold value, it is decided as negative and the other values are decided as neutral. The accuracy of social big data analysis is improved by quantifying and analyzing emoticons and new-coined words.

The objective of this research is to develop an automatic language classification system for Indian languages based on whether they are tonal or non-tonal. The proposed system uses a combination of cascade Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to model temporal dependencies in acoustic data. The system employs pitch chroma spectrogram coefficients in addition to the log-mel spectrogram coefficients to improve its performance. 

The proposed system was tested on the NIT Silchar language database (NITS-LD), which consists of All India radio broadcast news in 9 Indian languages. The study reports accuracies of 82.30% and 81.16% for 10s and 3s data, respectively. The performance of the system was also evaluated on the Oregon Graduate Institute Multi-Language Telephone-based Speech (OGI-MLTS) database, and it achieved accuracies of 77.2% and 74.95% for 10s and 3s data, respectively. 

Overall, the proposed cascade CNN-LSTM RNNs system with pitch chroma spectrogram coefficients has proven to be a successful method for tonal and non-tonal language classification, demonstrating high levels of accuracy on both datasets.

The traditional rechargeable battery has been the primary power source for mobile devices, but its limited capacity and constant need for recharging has prompted the search for alternative methods to deliver power. The emergence of novel wireless power supply methods such as energy harvesting and wireless power transfer has garnered significant attention in recent times. This article aims to provide an overview of the recent advances in wireless power supply and showcase several promising applications.

One of the wireless power supply methods is energy harvesting, which involves the conversion of ambient energy into electrical energy for mobile devices. This technology utilizes the energy available in the environment such as solar, thermal, or kinetic energy to power the devices. Another method is wireless power transfer, which delivers power from a source to a device without using cables. This method uses electromagnetic fields to transfer energy wirelessly, and it has shown great potential for charging phones, laptops, and other mobile devices.

In addition to presenting a summary of these methods, this article proposes an energy scheduling scheme for the EH-powered D2D relay network. The optimization problem is formulated, and a modified two-stage directional water filling algorithm is proposed to resolve it efficiently. By scheduling the harvested energy, we can ensure the mobile devices remain powered and avoid interruptions during use.

In conclusion, the emergence of wireless power supply methods has opened new avenues for the mobile device industry. Energy harvesting and wireless power transfer show great potential as alternatives to traditional battery sources. Additionally, the proposed energy scheduling scheme presents a new approach to efficiently manage harvested energy in the EH-powered D2D relay network. As research in this area continues, we can expect to see even more innovative and sustainable solutions for wireless power supply.

The economic progress of the Internet of Things (IoT) is phenomenal. Applications range from checking the alignment of some components during a manufacturing process, monitoring of transportation and pedestrian levels to enhance driving and walking path, remotely observing terminally ill patients by means of medical devices such as implanted devices and infusion pumps, and so on. To provide security, encrypting the data becomes an indispensable requirement, and symmetric encryptions algorithms are becoming a crucial implementation in the resource constrained environments. Typical symmetric encryption algorithms like Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) showcases an assumption that end points of communications are secured and that the encryption key being securely stored. However, devices might be physically unprotected, and attackers may have access to the memory while the data is still encrypted. It is essential to reserve the key in such a way that an attacker finds it hard to extract it. At present, techniques like White-Box cryptography has been utilized in these circumstances. But it has been reported that applying White-Box cryptography in IoT devices have resulted in other security issues like the adversary having access to the intermediate values, and the practical implementations leading to Code lifting attacks and differential attacks. In this paper, a solution is presented to overcome these problems by demonstrating the need of White-Box Cryptography to enhance the security by utilizing the cipher block chaining (CBC) mode.

This paper presents a deep learning based approach for small-signal stability of a single machine connected to infinite bus. The proposed approach is based on an optimal estimation of the synchronizing and damping torque coefficients of the synchronous generator by optimal measurement of the operating conditions including the voltage, real power and reactive power. The proposed approach in this paper is to train deep neural networks to estimate the synchronizing and damping torque coefficients for all examples that the power system may encounter. Hence, a large dataset of more than 310,000 examples is created to cover the full range of the possible operation conditions. The performance of deep neural networks based approach is compared with that of other neural networks reported in the literature. Simulations results show that the proposed approach is robust and training the neural network over a wide range of operating conditions yield fast, yet accurate estimation of the torque coefficients.

The problem of network function computation over a directed acyclic network is investigated in this paper. In such a network, a sink node desires to compute with zero error a target function, of which the inputs are generated at multiple source nodes. The edges in the network are assumed to be error-free and have limited capacity. The nodes in the network are assumed to have unbounded computing capability and be able to perform network coding. The computing rate of a network code that can compute the target function over the network is the average number of times that the target function is computed with zero error for one use of the network. In this paper, we obtain an improved upper bound on the computing capacity, which is applicable to arbitrary target functions and arbitrary network topologies. This improved upper bound not only is an enhancement of the previous upper bounds but also is the first tight upper bound on the computing capacity for computing an arithmetic sum over a certain non-tree network, which has been widely studied in the literature. We also introduce a multi-dimensional array approach that facilitates evaluation of the improved upper bound. Furthermore, we apply this bound to the problem of computing a vector-linear function over a network. With this bound, we are not only able to enhance a previous result on computing a vector-linear function over a network but also simplify the proof significantly. Finally, we prove that for computing the binary maximum function over the reverse butterfly network, our improved upper bound is not achievable. This result establishes that in general our improved upper bound is non-achievable, but whether it is asymptotically achievable or not remains open.

The number of applications (apps) available for smart devices or Android based IoT (Internet of Things) has surged dramatically over the past few years. Meanwhile, the volume of ill-designed or malicious apps (malapps) has been growing explosively. To ensure the quality and security of the apps in the markets, many approaches have been proposed in recent years to discriminate malapps from benign ones. Machine learning is usually utilized in classification process. Accurately characterizing apps' behaviors, or so-called features, directly affects the detection results with machine learning algorithms. Android apps evolve very fast. The size of current apps has become increasingly large and the behaviors of apps have become increasingly complicated. The extracting effective and representative features from apps is thus an ongoing challenge. Although many types of features have been extracted in existing work, to the best of our knowledge, no work has systematically surveyed the features constructed for detecting Android malapps. In this paper, we are motivated to provide a clear and comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art work that detects malapps by characterizing behaviors of apps with various types of features. Through the designed criteria, we collect a total of 1947 papers in which 236 papers are used for the survey with four dimensions: the features extracted, the feature selection methods employed if any, the detection methods used, and the scale of evaluation performed. Based on our in-depth survey, we highlight the issues of exploring effective features from apps, provide the taxonomy of these features and indicate the future directions.

A new algorithm has been proposed for the Block-matching and 3D filtering (BM3D) method for noising parameter selection. This algorithm automatically selects the optimal denoising parameter by analyzing the presence of retained structures in the ridge areas of initial noisy and filtered images, controlling the appearance of regular components on method noise with mutual information, and estimating image characteristic details through Hessian matrix eigenvalues analysis. Testing on images with added controlled Gaussian noise from general image TID2013 and BSDS500 databases showed that the proposed no-reference metric outperforms existing no-reference metrics in selecting the optimal denoising parameter. The algorithm's calculation time does not depend on the image noise level, making it promising to be used in image adaptive BM3D-based methods.

In recent years, deep reinforcement learning has shown impressive performance in various fields such as gaming, robotics, and dialogue systems. However, these methods require a massive amount of sampled data, which still poses a challenge. To address this issue, a hierarchical meta-learning method based on the actor-critic algorithm has been proposed in this paper. This approach provides transferable knowledge that can efficiently train an actor on a new task with minimal trials. 

In this proposed method, a global basic critic, meta critic, and task specified network are shared within a distribution of tasks. These networks can criticize any actor attempting to solve any specified task. Moreover, the hierarchical framework is applied to a critic network in the actor-critic algorithm to distill meta-knowledge above the task level and address distinct tasks. 

The performance of this proposed method was evaluated on multiple classic control tasks with reinforcement learning algorithms, including start-of-the-art meta-learning methods. The experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance and better results with more depth of the meta critic network. 

In conclusion, the hierarchical meta-learning method based on the actor-critic algorithm is a promising approach to address the limitations of deep reinforcement learning in terms of massive sampled data. The proposed method's performance shows significant potential for efficient learning in various fields.

Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of blindness in children worldwide. The grading and treatment guidelines for ROP rely heavily on identifying the zone, stage, and plus disease. In cases of severe ROP, accurate identification of zone is more critical than staging. However, the identification of zone I from RetCam fundus images remains subjective, which leads to inaccuracies by ophthalmologists. To address this issue, we have developed a new deep learning framework that automatically identifies zone I from RetCam images using a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) algorithm. The algorithm has been trained on RetCam images and accurately identifies the disc and macular center based on the intersection over union (IOU) threshold. The results are promising, with 91% accuracy achieved when the IOU threshold is set at 0.8. The successful identification of zone I from RetCam images indicates the potential for applications in ROP grading, monitoring, and prognosis for infants.

The Coach Ing model, applied to professionals in the engineering field, continues to be enriched through training experiments. After a careful evaluation of the results of the Coach-Ing path [1], this paper shows the results of a further experimentation performed in SAPIENZA - University of Rome. The experimentation was focused on the identification of a numerical evaluation technique of the skill level acquired by the students participating in the program. This was achieved through the guided validation of the set of 16 reference skills defined by the Coach-Ing model. During the training process a double level activity was carried out: on the one hand, the participants were taught about the possible working scenarios to which they could orientate themselves and, at the same time, assessed the personal strategies - observation and evaluation of the 16 parameters - more coherent to effectively propose itself in different working contexts. Further two steps (a unconventional final exam and a follow-up on the interview) integrated the students' training path and at the same time enriched the Coach-ing model with further reference indicators with communicative-relational indicators. The results of the complete experimentation confirm that the Coach-Ing model has excellent performances as a methodological lever within the training path. Moreover, the use of Mentor-Ing techniques allows to accompany the participants in the consolidation of the acquired skills.

Nowadays, Vehicular Information Network Technology has captured a lot of attention due to its practical and safety-related applications. In this technology, participating vehicles can communicate with each other on the road to obtain emergency information and other relevant data. Although the use of traditional host-centric approaches like TCP/IP is common, they are unable to provide robust communication between a large number of vehicles due to high vehicle speed. Therefore, the use of Named Data Network (NDN) in VANET (Vehicular Ad-Hoc Network) has led to the development of VNDN that exploits the content name rather than a vehicle address. This paper explores the main packet forwarding issues in VNDN and proposes a protocol called Control of Useless Interests Flooding (CUIF) in Vehicular Named Data Network to provide the best and efficient communication environment to users while driving on the highway. The CUIF scheme helps in reducing the Interest forwarding storm over the network and controls the flooding of useless packets against the direction of the Producer vehicle. The simulation results show that the CUIF scheme significantly reduces the number of outgoing Interest packets and data download time on the network, thus providing a more efficient and reliable communication medium for VANET.

Location estimation plays a crucial role in mobile and ubiquitous computing systems. However, measurement error caused by time difference of arrival (TDOA)/angle of arrival (AOA) hybrid location algorithm and non-linear optimization problems pose significant challenges in location estimation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm based on chaos theory for hybrid location of mobile location estimation. 

The proposed algorithm significantly enhances the location performance and accuracy by first obtaining the estimation function of the mobile station using the maximum likelihood method. The initial population of PSO is generated from the estimation function of the mobile station as a fitness function. The chaotic-optimized particle swarm optimization algorithm (CPSO) is used to obtain the optimal mobile location position estimation, thus improving the performance of the TDOA/AOA location algorithm.

Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method compared with the traditional Chan algorithm, the Taylor algorithm, and the TDOA/AOA hybrid location algorithm can reduce the impact of error on location accuracy, achieve a balance of global and local search capabilities, and have a faster convergence speed and more accurate positioning accuracy.

The article discusses contemporary trends that define the transformations in the corporate culture of multinational corporations. Moreover, the article explores the influence of corporate culture on a firm's growth. Several illustrations are provided to demonstrate how a corporate culture can be successfully cultivated, how human resources can be utilized effectively, and how the internal projects of a company's staff can be supported. As a result, the authors present diverse views on the development of corporate culture, as seen by both foreign and Russian corporate executives.

To determine an appropriate trading time for buying or selling stocks is always a difficult task. The common way to deal with it is using trading strategies formed by technical or fundamental indicators. Lots of approaches have been presented on how to form trading strategies and how to set suitable parameters for those strategies. Furthermore, some approaches were also designed to optimize a trading strategy portfolio, which is a set of strategies where the return and risk of the portfolio can be maximized and minimized, respectively. To provide a more useful trading strategy portfolio, we first define a group trading strategy portfolio (GTSP). Then, an algorithm that utilizes the grouping genetic algorithm is designed for solving the GTSP optimization problem. In the chromosome representation, the grouping, strategy, and weight parts are employed to encode a possible GTSP. The fitness value of a chromosome is calculated by the group balance, weight balance, portfolio return, and risk to assess the quality of every possible solution. Genetic operators, including crossover, mutation, and inversion, are applied on the population to form a new offspring. Evolution is continued until the stop conditions are reached. Lastly, experiments were conducted on two real datasets with different trends to show that the advantages and the effectiveness of the presented approach.

This article presents a prototype framework designed to enable formal and machine-checked validation of GPU pseudo-assembly code algorithms using the Coq proof assistant. Such a framework would offer reliable validation of high-assurance GPU computations without relying on any specific source-to-assembly compilation toolchain. 

The PTX pseudo-assembly language is used as an example in this article, with a formal operational semantics expressed via dependent Coq types. This allows for the easy development of proofs and proof tactics that refer directly to the compiled PTX object code. 

However, challenges arise when trying to model PTX's complex and highly parallelized computation model in Coq, and the article discusses how to overcome these difficulties while maintaining sufficient clarity and generality to establish useful properties of realistic GPU programs. Several examples demonstrate how the prototype can already be used to validate some realistic programs.

Internet of things (IoT) is revolutionizing this world with its evolving applications in various aspects of life such as sensing, healthcare, remote monitoring, and so on. Android devices and applications are working hand to hand to realize dreams of the IoT. Recently, there is a rapid increase in threats and malware attacks on Android-based devices. Moreover, due to extensive exploitation of the Android platform in the IoT devices creates a task challenging of securing such kind of malware activities. This paper presents a novel framework that combines the advantages of both machine learning techniques and blockchain technology to improve the malware detection for Android IoT devices. The proposed technique is implemented using a sequential approach, which includes clustering, classification, and blockchain. Machine learning automatically extracts the malware information using clustering and classification technique and store the information into the blockchain. Thereby, all malware information stored in the blockchain history can be communicated through the network, and therefore any latest malware can be detected effectively. The implementation of the clustering technique includes calculation of weights for each feature set, the development of parametric study for optimization and simultaneously iterative reduction of unnecessary features having small weights. The classification algorithm is implemented to extract the various features of Android malware using naive Bayes classifier. Moreover, the naive Bayes classifier is based on decision trees for extracting more important features to provide classification and regression for achieving high accuracy and robustness. Finally, our proposed framework uses the permissioned blockchain to store authentic information of extracted features in a distributed malware database blocks to increase the run-time detection of malware with more speed and accuracy, and further to announce malware information for all users.

Symbolic regression aims to find mathematical expressions of functions that can fit a finite set of given data. This problem is a typical problem for evaluating performance in the field of Genetic Programming (GP). Cartesian GP (CGP) is one of the extensions of GP, which generating the graph structure programs. By using the graph structure, the solutions can be represented by more compact programs. Therefore, CGP is widely applied to the various problems. In standard symbolic regression problem, the sample data is expressed by a simple function, which is continuous and smooth. On the other hand, In a complex system appearing in the real world, they can be produced by a discontinuous or non-smooth function. When conventional GP or CGP is applied to this complex system's modelling, it is difficult to obtain good performance. In this paper, we propose a new CGP framework for complex symbolic regression problem. The proposed CGP modularizes the output nodes, and module mutation is introduced to increase or decrease the number of modules during the search. Each module consists of a node corresponding to the output of the network and a node for selecting the output to be used. By switching the output node for each input, it is possible to output appropriate values for each section of the objective function. We have examined its effectiveness by applying it to symbolic regression problem where the objective function is divided into several different sub-function fields. Experimental results have shown that it outperforms conventional CGP.

The advancements in cloud and edge computing have paved the way for networked robots to gather supporting data from virtually anywhere, resulting in an abundance of information for users to access. However, this has also presented a challenge for wireless networks as the radio resources available are limited. In order to efficiently accommodate a large number of robots downloading map information from wireless LANs, it is imperative for a robotic wireless network (RWN) to optimize the utilization of wireless resources. The aim of this study is to explore how multiple wireless channels can be utilized more efficiently for a multi-layered RWN. Local data sharing among robots within clusters is proposed as a means of minimizing wireless resource consumption. The hierarchical structure of the multi-layered RWN forms the basis of the suggested multi-channel utilization scheme for local data delivery. By combining the sharing of local data through robot clustering with multi-channel utilization, the available wireless resources can be increased significantly, resulting in better accommodation of service robots. Quantitative analysis shows that the proposed channel separation-and-sharing system considerably improves the channel availability and capability for robot accommodation. Preliminary experiment results also provide evidence of the proposed system's effectiveness.

Use of electromagnetic modeling tools has significantly helped in analyzing human vital signs and gait. The paper will briefly discuss modeling efforts; radars used, and some recent simulated and measured results. This is a very important step in developing a practical 24/7 activity tracking system.

The Network Function Virtualization (NFV) paradigm is giving impetus to novel telecommunication infrastructures that readily benefit from virtualized environments. One of the most interesting implications consists in turning traditional network appliances (e,g, routers, switches, firewalls) into virtual applications also known as Virtual Network Functions (VNFs). Same virtualization concepts can be applied to complex network systems, such as IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS), where constitutive network elements can be recasted in a set of chained VNFs, thus resulting in a virtualized IMS infrastructure (or vIMS). Starting from this challenging environment, in this work we propose an availability assessment of a vIMS divided in two stages: i) a preparatory modeling phase by means of two formalisms: Reliability Block Diagram and Stochastic Reward Networks; ii) a numerical analysis aimed at characterizing both the optimal vIMS configuration satisfying an high availability condition (availability evaluation), and the robustness of the system as some parameters deviate from their nominal values (sensitivity analysis).

This article addresses the issue of discrete time sliding mode control with an external trajectory generator. The authors propose a new reference trajectory based sliding mode control strategy for a disturbed discrete time dynamical system. To design the control, they adopt the nonswitching type definition of the quasi-sliding mode and use the reaching law approach, which is a popular method in the field. 

In their proposed strategy, the desired trajectory of the system is generated externally using a new nonswitching type reaching law. The authors define a new desired trajectory following reaching law for the disturbed plant, which limits the impact of external disturbances and model uncertainties on the system to one step. In contrast, existing control methods are influenced by all disturbance values from the beginning of the control process, leading to a wider ultimate band and lower system robustness. 

The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is demonstrated through a simulation example. Overall, this research presents a promising approach for improving the performance and robustness of systems under external disturbances and model uncertainties in the context of discrete time sliding mode control.

The focusing ability of lens antennas can play a significant role in precise radio localization while keeping the complexity low in a massive antenna array (MAA). In this paper, we propose an approach for radio source localization using lens antennas and MAA, based on angle of arrival (AoA) estimation in a multipath propagation scenario. We present two simplified antenna selection techniques to choose and process the focused subsets of antennas. Additionally, we develop a low-complexity time of arrival estimation scheme to detect the first arrival path (FAP) that contains the actual AoA information. Ultimately, the FAP signal is analyzed efficiently to estimate the AoA using a subspace-based method. 

To reduce system complexity with only slight degradation in performance, we introduce a mixed analog–digital AoA estimation structure, which applies the sum–difference signal patterns technique. The proposed approach is capable of providing good AoA estimation results, while considerably reducing system complexity when compared to an MAA system without the lens. Simulated root mean squared error performance curves as a function of signal-to-noise-ratio demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

This paper discusses the potential utilization of new NVM devices, including Phase Change Memory (PCM), OxRAM (oxide-based), and magneto-resistive STT-MRAM memory, in System-on-Chip (SoC) for IoT-WSN (Wireless Sensor Node) applications. The proposed idea of a unified memory architecture utilizing all types of NVM implementations, specifically for IoT-WSN applications, is validated in this study. The results of simulation and analysis for the NVM-based unified memory architecture are presented using the MSP430 platform with Contiki, and benchmarked for the Sky-Collect application. Important performance parameters such as area, write hits, write hit rate/evolution, power, and latency are considered in this study.

Mangosteen is an export commodity with great potential in Thailand, and it is known as the queen of fruits due to its popularity. While it generates substantial revenue, it is not without defects, both internal and external, which can result in rejected shipments and a decrease in export reliability. To tackle this problem, this research aims to develop a method to detect and classify surface roughness of mangosteen. The proposed approach is based on texture image analysis, which employs Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) to extract textural features for roughness classification into three categories: Glossy Surface, Mid Rough Surface, and Extreme Rough Surface. This study represents a novel attempt to use GLCM for mangosteen surface roughness classification.

The Influence maximization (IM) problem seeks to identify a small number of users who can maximize the profit of viral marketing, while the Reverse Influence Maximization (RIM) problem focuses on minimizing the cost of viral marketing in social networks. The cost of viral marketing is measured by the minimum number of nodes required to activate seed nodes, while the profit is determined by the maximum number of nodes influenced by seed users upon activation. Unfortunately, most existing research has only focused on maximizing the profit without regard for the cost of viral marketing.

To address this limitation, we propose a Viral Marketing Cost (VMC) Minimization problem and an associated Heuristic Mixed (HM) approach under mixed Reverse Independent Cascade (RIC) and Reverse Linear Threshold (RLT) diffusion models. Our HM model utilizes a combination of greedy techniques and a heuristic approach to optimize the VM cost, while addressing the challenging issues of the RIM problem.

We further demonstrate the effectiveness of our model by simulating its performance on two real social networks. Our results show that our model outperforms both the baseline and existing models.

Machine learning (ML)-based traffic classification is becoming increasingly important as traditional port-based and payload-based approaches are losing their effectiveness. However, previous methods have relied mainly on packet-level analysis, which requires additional hardware and personnel resources. In this paper, we propose a more efficient method of traffic classification using NetFlow, a flow-level monitoring solution widely used by network operators.

We first analyzed the performance of per-application classification by using C4.5 decision trees with features derived from NetFlow records. Our results showed that the accuracy obtained was comparable to the packet-level method. To further improve classification accuracy and reduce computational complexity, we introduced an ensemble feature selection (FS) method.

To address the issues of concept drift and imbalanced datasets, we proposed a clustering-based under-sampling approach combined with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). In doing so, we extracted meaningful insights and practical recommendations.

In conjunction with the proposed methods, our experiment results demonstrated a high F-measure for two traffic traces comprising a wide range of applications with low computational complexity. Our findings demonstrate the potential of using a flow-level approach for traffic classification while reducing both cost and resource requirements.

In online learning, predicting student behaviors and performance is essential for implementing early warning systems. This study aims to predict such behaviors and academic performance using data mining strategies and a decision tree to construct a learning intervention model of an adaptive learning system. The data reveals that male students are more likely to perform poorly in academics and have reduced total learning duration. Additionally, master students have the highest probability of poor learning time span. Male science students also have the highest probability of reduced average length of staying per study session while art students have limited discussion participation probability. Furthermore, female art students are more likely to take poor notes while male students tend to provide limited feedback times. These findings suggest the need for targeted interventions for students based on individual learning characteristics and behaviors.

Watermarking is a technique of embedding an imperceptible signal known as watermark in the form of text, audio into digital media in such way a way so that intruder does not get any access to misuse the data to ensure copyright protection and ownership identification. The proposed work presents a hybrid watermarking technique that merges Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Discrete Wavelet Transformation (DWT), and Rail Fence methods applied on digital media in the form of images and videos. The proposed method will work on embedding of watermark in videos of various formats available now a day's thus ensuring quality of videos after insertion of watermark. The scheme will target high frequency sub bands formed from frames of the video. Different attacks have been imposed on the watermarked video to measure the robustness and efficiency of proposed scheme. The major challenge faced while insertion of watermark is that the quality of video gets lost after insertion of watermark. The proposed scheme is intended to solve the given problem.

Perception-controlled, intelligent robots are becoming increasingly important in the logistics industry due to the dynamics, flexibility, and diversity of its operations. These robots are being used to automate logistical handling steps to streamline the entire process. However, the industrial environment poses additional challenges such as labeling or damage, which make it difficult to accurately identify objects. This is where generalizing deep neural networks (DNN) come in. Over the years, DNN has shown to be highly effective in accurately classifying objects based on publicly available data sets.

However, when re-training DNNs on training data from the industrial environment, a lower performance is observed. This is because the industrial environment is highly complex and varied, and requires a more specialized approach. Furthermore, international locations of vehicle plants have shown that a drop in performance is observed in the implementation of a network trained in one location when used in another location. Therefore, it is important to take into account the unique characteristics of each location to ensure the best results possible.

To use robots in the logistic processes in the future, measures such as a revised composition of training data or their extension by data augmentation are proposed. By doing so, we can ensure that robots are highly efficient, flexible and adaptable to handle any challenges of industrial environments. Ultimately, the use of robots in logistics will lead to improved efficiency and reduced errors, saving valuable resources for businesses.

Beamspace channel estimation in millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive MIMO system is a very challenging task, especially when the number of radio-frequency chains is limited. To address this problem, we present a novel approximate message passing (AMP)-based network with deep residual learning, referred to as LampResNet. It mainly consists of two components: 1) a learned AMP (LAMP) network and 2) a deep residual learning network (ResNet). The former utilizes the sparsity property of beamspace channel matrix and is employed to obtain a preliminary estimation result, while the latter is designed to reduce the impact of channel noise and further refine the coarse estimation obtained by the LAMP network. Simulation results validate the efficiency of the proposed network.

Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has obtained growing attention during the past years. For this purpose, various methods have been proposed. Feature extraction is the major part of SER methods and aims to attain effective emotional features from speech signal. One of the most important features in speech processing task is Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). The vocal production mechanisms of speakers at different emotional states can improve the discrimination abilities of the aforementioned features for SER task. This work aims to propose a novel feature extraction scheme for SER task that integrates this particular information through the decomposition of emotional speech spectra and providing an improved spectral representation of various emotions. By employing this scheme, two novel procedures are represented. In the first procedures, cepstral-like features are obtained by a filter bank which is computed by Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) technique on emotional speech spectra. In the second procedures, the activation coefficients of NMF technique which are achieved by decomposition of speech spectrums, are considered as the new features. Finally, to increase the discrimination abilities of features among emotion classes, each of the feature vectors is normalized to its mean value. According to experiments on Emo-DB database, fusion of the proposed features with MFCCs outperforms the performance of an SER system compared with conventional MFCC as the baseline or the simple unsupervised NMF-based features derived from the speech spectra.

In this paper, we investigate the implementation of deep learning algorithms in low resource computational environments in real-time. Specifically, we aim to compare the accuracy and speed of neural networks for smile detection using different architectures and their system level implementation on the NVidia Jetson embedded platform. In addition, we propose an asynchronous multithreading scheme for parallelizing the pipeline to enhance the system's efficiency. 

In this study, we experimentally compare thirteen widely used network topologies within this framework. Our findings demonstrate that low complexity architectures can achieve comparable performance to larger ones with a fraction of the computation required. Our results suggest that implementing deep learning algorithms in real-time on low resource systems with optimized network configurations and multithreading strategies could produce substantial gains in computational efficiency without sacrificing performance.

This article presents a medical simulation solution. This solution allows a physician to train a clinical scenario by interacting with a graphical interface. The aim is to instigate the learning and internalization of clinical procedures. Currently these resources have been intensifying in the most diverse areas, being our focus, Medicine. Within this area, the focus is on medical simulation. There are numerous biomedical simulation centers, whose main objective is to create realistic simulations to aid health professionals. Thus, it is intended to optimize its performance, to meet the needs detected and to anticipate unexpected situations (critical or complex events). However, current simulation systems face some limitations, since they have enough difficulties in the development of new scenarios, since they are restricted to the level of modularity and the number of simulated situations. The training of these professionals is limited to simulation centers. The goal is to create a platform to simulate real scenarios and develop serious games that simulate various clinical situations, in order to facilitate access to this type of training and training.

Based on the analysis of the local monotonicity of the modularity function, this paper presents a fast and effective mutation operator and an improved Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA) to solve the community detection problem. The proposed algorithm was tested on both basic and large-scale complex networks. The experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm can achieve an average Q function of 0.419 8 after 100 runs, surpassing Girvan-Newman (GN) algorithm, Fast Newman (FN) algorithm, and Tasgin Genetic Algorithm (TGA) in performance.

Augmented reality technologies have become mainstream, with Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) being integral to driving them. However, enabling SLAM on mobile devices still poses challenges due to computation and power limitations. To overcome these limitations, this paper explores the microarchitecture design space of visual SLAM. Firstly, a characterization was conducted to make the image signal processing stage in the front-end image acquisition stage configurable, and to explore SLAM's sensitivity to individual stages. The characterization showed that only demosaicing, gamma compression, and denoising in the image signal processing process have significant influences on SLAM's accuracy. Therefore, the image signal processor in SoC in traditional mobile devices can be substituted by an approximation logic to save hardware overhead and energy. Secondly, a new CGRA architecture, called SL-CGRA, was proposed and tailored specifically to SLAM's workload characteristics. It features a two-level memory design, which includes data-redirection layer support for on-chip memory, and an efficient CGRA memory controller stacked through Through-Via Silicon (TSV) for highly efficient off-chip memory access. Furthermore, PEs in SL-CGRA support different execution modes to exploit the data-level parallelism and task-level parallelism of SLAM. Evaluation results show that SL-CGRA achieves excellent performance and energy efficiency.

To increase noise immunity of the MFCC (mel-frequency cepstral coefficients) widely used for voice signal parametrisation it is suggested to use a psychoacoustic model of frequency masking. Additionally, taking into account the formation mechanism of the formant regions in the voice signal spectrum it is suggested to influence the spectral samples corresponding to multiple harmonics of the fundamental tone. The modified algorithm is investigated on the basis of the single word recognition system adapted for MFCC voice signal parametrisation only. The positive effect of using proposed additional voice signal transformation in the parametrisation algorithm is shown.

Environmental conditions have a significant impact on health and all human activities. On the one hand, laboratories are spaces characterized by various sources of pollution that can lead to unhealthy indoor environments. On the other hand, laboratory activities, especially in the case of experiments using thermography, require the supervision of several parameters. The proliferation of the Internet of Things paradigm (IoT) shows great potential for the creation of automatic solutions for monitoring indoor environments. In general, people spend about 90% of their time inside buildings so it is significant to use realtime monitoring systems in order to identify bad ambient conditions. The timely detection of poor ambient conditions allows you to plan interventions in the building for enhanced living environments and occupational health. This paper aims to present a laboratory environment conditions supervision solution based on IoT architecture called iLabM+. The solution is composed of prototype hardware for the collection of the data environment and a Web portal for data consulting and analysis. This system allows monitoring of temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and air quality. The results obtained are promising and represent a significant contribution to IoT-based environmental quality monitoring systems.

Modern-day robots are highly efficient at completing a variety of tasks, but their usefulness is limited due to their non-social nature. To improve the sociability of robots, it is important to study human behavior in different conditions. Object and people tracking is a promising field of computer vision that can help make robots more social. 

In this study, we focused on detecting and tracking multiple vehicles and people in both outdoor traffic environments and indoor office environments. A background subtraction algorithm was used for vehicle detection, and a Kalman filter was used to predict the position of each vehicle in the next frame. Some vehicles were also detected in cluttered scenes, and every moving vehicle was counted in video frames.

In addition, we developed a different methodology to track people's faces, as their behavior and indoor scenarios differ greatly from those of vehicles. We detected and tracked the faces of multiple people on two different datasets with varying camera heights. Point features were extracted and compared sequentially to track the faces of multiple individuals. Each face was then bounded by a rectangular shape with a unique identity, and the total number of faces was counted in the sequence of frames.

The results from both the vehicle and face datasets showed promising results, accurately tracking the trajectories of the objects being studied. This research provides a useful dataset for assessing human behavior, which can be used in social robotic applications in the future.

This paper describes the implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for recognizing different hand gestures based on electromyographic signals. The proposed architecture is versatile and capable of recognizing six different commands. To build the database, 2880 multi-channel feature maps were created by processing signals from the 8 sensors of a Myo Armband. Power spectral density maps were utilized to extract relevant features from the signals. The database was split into three sets of equal size for training, validation, and testing. The implemented CNN achieved 98.4% accuracy in the validation and 99% in the tests. The processing time of the network was verified as 4 ms, demonstrating the potential of a shallow CNN to support multiple channels from different sensors, achieve high accuracy, and execute in real-time applications.

In the current cloud market tradition, multi-cloud broker environments have an important role to support multi-tier cloud applications where a set of interconnected virtual machines (VMs) are required for the deployment and execution of the application. There are several cloud service providers (SP) who provide services in the form of different VM instances. For different SPs, pricing of different configurations is different based on various technical, service level as well as economic factors. Also, these SPs have multiple data centers located at different geographical locations with diverse resources and pricing schemes due to differences in electricity costs, maintenance costs etc. in different regions. Considering these facts, in this paper, we propose a multi-cloud broker environment to select an optimal VM coalition for multi-tier applications from an SP with minimum coalition pricing and better quality of service. We model the problem as a bi-objective optimization problem and solve it using ant-colony optimization based technique. The entire interaction of SPs is modeled using game theory and results from simulation show promising behavior in achieving the trade-off between the aggregate cost and the QoS.

The traffic models typically proposed in literature are heuristic in nature, as they only account for the random nature of the generated traffic. In contrast, our paper introduces a model for M2M communications that generates the traffic itself, resulting in a more comprehensive view of the subject matter. Our model specifically showcases the behavior of M2M uplink communication within a network featuring limited information capacity shared channels. We conducted an analysis of the number of transmitted packets using the traffic model derived from our model, comparing it to the state-of-the-art traffic models through simulations. The findings indicate that our proposed model offers greater accuracy in estimating the number of transmitted packets than existing models in this field.

High speed vehicles or driving by consuming alcohol is one of the main reasons of accidents. So, the number of accidents can be decreased by controlling the vehicles moving at higher speed. In this paper, we proposed a Position Based High Speed Vehicle Detection Algorithm (PHVA) for detecting the higher speed vehicles in a Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) by using a vehicular cloud server, where the cloud server is used as computing as a service. The proposed algorithm calculates the speed of a vehicle based on the data directly received from the Road Side Units (RSUs). When a vehicle comes under the coverage of an RSU, RSU receives the time, position and other information about the vehicle. RSU then sends the received information to the Cloud Server (CS). Based on the information received from the nearby RSUs, the CS calculates the average speed for that vehicle in a particular lane. The calculated speed is then compared with that of the permitted speed on that lane. If it is greater than the permitted limit, then the CS increments the speed violation counter for that vehicle. Depending upon the frequency of violation and with the help of Certification Authority (CA), appropriate action will be taken on that high speed vehicle. To check the efficiency of our PHVA algorithm, we simulated our work in Vehicles in Network Simulation (Veins) hybrid simulation framework. Veins uses Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) as the road traffic simulator and OMNeT++ as the network simulator. Both simulators are connected via a TCP socket which has been standardized in Traffic Control Interface (TraCI). The results show that our algorithm has better detection accuracy over ReVISE scheme in this environment.

One of the significant problems in Social Net-works (SN) analysis is how to find the best influential members. This problem was proved to be non-deterministic polynomial (NP-hard). The influence maximization (IM) problem in SNs aims to maximize the spread of influence in the network. It represents an optimization problem. IM is a fundamental research problem in social networks. Influence maximization problem is the problem of assigning a subset of k users as (seed nodes) in a graph that could maximize the spread of influence by maximizing the expected number of influenced users. It represents a key algorithmic problem in social influence analysis. In this study, centrality-based methods are utilized to select top k nodes of high centrality values. The degree centrality is used to select the opinion leaders, while the between-ness and Eigenvector centrality is used to select the early adopters. The degree discount (as a heuristic approach) is proposed to replace the Greedy algorithms applied in other studies to avoid the time complexity. A mixed diffusion model (replacing the linear threshold and independent cascade) is utilized to be main diffusion model in this study.

Robotic-assisted rehabilitation of the upper limb following neurological injury can achieve best possible functional recovery when patients are engaged in the therapy. However, implementation of active training is still difficult as it's challenging to detect human motion intention online and impose corresponding robot control. This paper introduces a novel upper-limb rehabilitation robot, and proposes a sEMG-driven (sEMG: surface Electromyography) torque estimation model based on artificial neural networks (ANN). The robot has three DOFs, of which the first two DOFs adopt a planar parallel structure, and the wrist module has an exoskeleton form. In this study, we design an impedance controller and an admittance controller for the first two DOFs and the wrist module, respectively. Specifically, for the first two DOFs, the assistance/resistance force at the end-effector was controlled according to its motions and desired interaction impedance; for the wrist module, an sEMG armband was used to collect 8 channels of sEMG signals from the forearm muscles, and a time-delay ANN model was developed to estimate the wrist pronation/supination torque, based on which the wrist rotation was controlled according to the human motion intention. To overcome the overfitting problem, besides the experimental samples of wrist rotation, both resting and co-contraction samples were collected for training. Finally, combining with the design of a virtual reality game and force fields, the proposed methods were implemented and tested experimentally on the upper-limb rehabilitation robot.

Passwords form part of our daily routine and even though there are alternative authentication mechanisms, such as biometrics, passwords stubbornly persist. Passwords have been around for the last few decades, but also the various problems associated with users trying to create passwords that are strong and secure. Users are faced with a cognitive burden in managing passwords which often leads to poor password practices or users recycling passwords across various accounts. While there is no anticipated end to the use of passwords, scholars have identified that passwords need to be better supported - one such method is using a password manager. There is a wealth of technical research relating to password managers, which has led to drastic improvements and the maturing of the technology. However, there is a little research on why people would choose to adopt password managers. To explore these factors, this research uses an adapted version of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT2) that includes trust as an additional construct. Using empirical data, the results of the study show that performance expectancy, habit, and trust are key factors in the intention to adopt a password manager.

Multi-agent motion planning is a critical area of study, finding applications in search and rescue missions as well as transportation missions. The primary concerns of motion planning are path planning and inter-agent collision avoidance. While Lyapunov-based models offer great solutions to these problems, it is often challenging to set reasonable parameters for the models. Additionally, agents controlled by these models tend to converge to destinations slowly. Heuristic planning algorithms are also useful in guiding agents without consideration of kinetics.

To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel approach using a decentralized velocity-aware planning algorithm and a collision avoidance algorithm to facilitate motion planning for multiple agents. The velocity-aware algorithm generates acceleration vectors that converge towards predefined destinations to create paths for the agents to follow. The collision avoidance algorithm is triggered in case agents come too close to one another, helping to prevent collisions.

Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared with the prioritized A* algorithm paired with Lyapunov-based low-level control laws, our approach allows agents to take much shorter paths and less time to move to their destinations safely. Overall, our algorithm provides a more efficient and effective solution for multi-agent motion planning, with potential applications in search and rescue missions and transportation missions.

Discussions surrounding Computer Architecture are becoming more prevalent, as various new areas are being explored. These include Domain Specific Architecture, Deep Learning chips, Approximate Computing, Security Aware Architecture, and even Quantum Computers. Meanwhile, users' expectations regarding ICT and A.I. are also evolving, with a desire to see these technologies utilized for solving social problems and improving quality of life. There is also a pressing need for low power consumption in technology.

Given these significant changes, it is essential for architects and engineers to consider how they can effectively promote R&D over the long term, to meet the evolving societal needs and expectations. This panel discussion aims to explore what immediate steps should be taken, as well as how to implement human resource development and project management systems that align with these goals. Ultimately, the goal is to ensure that technology continues to be developed in a way that benefits society at large.

This paper presents the mechanical design of YAFT, a custom-built two-wheeled inverted pendulum, along with its intelligent control system. YAFT is equipped with various sensors and processing units, making it suitable for telepresence, cognitive robotic, and human-machine applications. Despite the use of low-cost components, we show that YAFT has a rigid body frame through deflection analysis and derive its dynamical model. To handle real-world uncertainties, we propose an intelligent control structure that combines control theory, fuzzy logic, and sensor fusion for stabilization and position control. Comparative experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control structures on YAFT in real-time.

Although feature extraction methods can improve the speed of hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, achieving effective classification with high dimensional spectral data remains a big challenge. Classical feature extraction methods have been found to sacrifice accuracy for increased classification speed. In this regard, a new hyperspectral classification method, RILDA-NRS, has been proposed in this paper to address this challenge. RILDA-NRS is based on rotational invariant linear discriminant analysis theory (RILDA) and nearest regularized subspace (NRS) theory. RILDA is used to extract useful spectral features from hyperspectral images, which not only reduces the dimensionality of HSI but also enhances the discriminability between samples. The extracted features are then embedded into the NRS classification model to classify HSI. The experiments conducted show that the proposed method has significant advantages in terms of classification accuracy and speed when compared to the existing methods.

The language study and automatic processing require the availability of large raw and annotated corpora. Collecting data and constructing such language resources are non-trivial tasks in the NLP field, especially when it comes to deal with low-resource languages.
