This letter studies an energy-efficient unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-aided cellular network, where the UAV is dispatched to serve cell edge users in cellular network and helps offload data from the base station by flying with circle path. The goal of this letter is to maximize the energy efficiency of UAV by jointly optimizing resource allocation, user partitioning and UAV trajectory. The formulated problem is shown in a complicated and non-convex form, which is hard to tackle. To this end, the original problem is first decomposed into two sub-problems and then a block coordinate descent method is leveraged, which leads to an efficient iterative algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the benchmarks in terms of the energy efficiency of UAV.

In reliability engineering, the accelerated life test has become increasingly popular and necessary. This test quickly provides information on the lifetime distribution of a particularly reliable product by conducting the life test at more extreme stress levels than normal operating conditions. By extrapolating, the lifetime distribution at the usage stress can then be estimated with an appropriate regression model. 

This paper revisits the problem of design optimization for a general k-level step-stress accelerated life test under progressive Type-I censoring with an equispaced step duration Δ for design simplicity. Intermediate censoring is allowed to take place at each stress change time point (iΔ, i = 1, 2, . . . , k), and the existence of the optimal stress duration is demonstrated under various design criteria, including A- and E-optimality, as well as D-, T-, and C-optimalities.

The existence of these optimal designs is investigated in detail for exponential lifetimes with a single stress variable, and the effect of the intermediate censoring proportion on the design efficiency is numerically studied. Overall, the findings suggest that accelerated life testing with optimal design can provide a useful tool for reliably estimating the lifetime distribution of products in a short period of time.

This paper addresses the resource allocation (RA) problem in a cellular network that enables full-duplex (FD) device-to-device (D2D) communication. The scenario involves multiple FD-D2D pairs sharing uplink channels with regular cellular users (CUs), causing interference between the two communication types. The objective is to properly allocate resources, such as transmit power and channels, to maximize network-centric metrics such as weighted-sum rate (WSR) and global energy efficiency (GEE). However, the complex coupling between links and the flexibility in channel assignment results in a non-convex optimization problem. 

This paper proposes an innovative approach to globally solve the RA problem of an FD-D2D-based cellular network. The problem is decoupled into two sub-problems: power allocation (PA) and channel assignment (CA). The PA sub-problem is solved using monotonic optimization theory with the proposed polyblock-based algorithm, MARIO, which efficiently converges to the global solution. Based on the optimal PA solution, the CA problem is reduced to an assignment problem solvable with Khun-Munkers algorithm. 

Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms and provide insights into solution design parameters such as proximity distance and self-interference cancellation capability. Overall, this paper provides a first and innovative solution to a challenging resource allocation problem in an FD-D2D-based cellular network.

The aim of this paper is to develop an intelligent lifelong learning cancer care framework that will be adapted by the King Hussein Cancer Center in Jordan. Cancer care is defined as comprehensive care for cancer patients, addressing not just their medical and physical needs, but also their psychological, social, and emotional needs. Lifelong learning is the process of continuous personal and professional development throughout one's life. 

As humans, our lives span multiple decades, during which the environment we live in is constantly changing. Thus, we need to be empowered to face emerging challenges and thrive in a continuously changing environment. There are multiple interactions that take place between an individual and their environment. The Oxford dictionary defines interaction as communication or direct involvement with someone or something. 

Communication through interactions occurs for valuable causes and purposes. On one hand, these interactions are didactic, with complex interactions between an individual and their environment. On the other hand, they involve interactions between an individual and other members of the community, who are continuously changing. Ultimately, the aim of this framework is to improve cancer care by promoting a culture of lifelong learning and empowering cancer patients and their families to deal with the challenges of cancer, using the services of many professionals working together.

The unpredictable behaviors of the Tumor-Immune system can be attributed to the inherent uncertainty inherent in it. Randomness in cell-cell interactions, incomplete and vague data, and the dynamic properties of the tumor are some of the factors that contribute to the uncertainty of the system. Fuzzy Stochastic Petri Net (FSPN) is a modeling approach that combines Stochastic Petri Net (SPN) with fuzzy sets to capture this uncertainty. The FSPN model associates fuzzy numbers instead of crisp numbers with the kinetic parameter of the SPN to consider fuzziness. In this study, the tumor-immune system was modeled by considering the interactions between Tumor cells, Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL), and Myeloid-derived suppressor cell as the major components. The model simulates the dynamics of the cells in tumor escape and tumor elimination phases, taking into account the uncertainty of the kinetic parameters. The results show that with increasing uncertainty of model parameters, the uncertainty of cell dynamics also increases. This method can be applied to model and simulate any biological network with uncertain information.

In the realm of identifying power quality disturbances (PQD), signal processing efficiency has been identified as an inefficiency that cannot meet the demands of the practical applications. Additionally, due to a lack of effective feature analysis, the complexity of classifiers has been increased, and the classification efficiency has been decreased by redundant features. In this study, a PQD recognition method is proposed based on image enhancement techniques and feature importance analysis to overcome these limitations.

Initially, PQD signals are transformed into gray images, and three image enhancement techniques were adopted, including gamma correction, edge detection, and peak and valley detection. These enhancement techniques were used to amplify the disturbance features. The disturbance features were then extracted from the binary images, and the original feature set was constructed, where the classification ability of each feature was quantified using Gini importance. The sequence forward search (SFS) method was utilized for characteristic selection based on the order of importance by Gini to select the optimal feature subset. Lastly, the random forest (RF) classifier was utilized to identify the PQD signals based on the optimal feature subset.

The results of the simulation and contrast experiments revealed that the new method can effectively identify PQD signals in different noise environments by determining the optimal classification subset. In addition, the new method demonstrates higher signal processing efficiency compared with the EMD and ST methods.

Overall, the proposed method is efficient in identifying PQD signals through the use of image enhancement techniques and feature importance analysis to select the optimal feature subset. By addressing the inefficiencies of existing methods, the proposed method can improve the quality of PQD recognition.

Edge computing (EC) has quickly ascended to be the de-facto standard for hosting emerging low-latency applications, as exemplified by intelligent video surveillance, Internet of Vehicles, and augmented reality. For EC, service function chaining is envisioned as a promising approach to configure various services in an agile, flexible, and cost-efficient manner. When running on top of geographically dispersed edge clouds, fully unleashing the benefits of service function chaining is, however, by no means trivial. In this paper, we propose an online orchestration framework for cross-edge service function chaining, which aims to maximize the holistic cost efficiency, via jointly optimizing the resource provisioning and traffic routing on-the-fly. This long-term cost minimization problem is difficult since it is NP-hard and involves future uncertain information. To simultaneously address these dual challenges, we carefully combine an online optimization technique with an approximate optimization method in a joint optimization framework, through: 1) decomposing the long-term problem into a series of one-shot fractional problem with a regularization technique and 2) rounding the fractional solution to a near-optimal integral solution with a randomized dependent scheme that preserves the solution feasibility. The resulting online algorithm achieves an outstanding performance guarantee, as verified by both rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive trace-driven simulations.

The paper involves an improved vector field clustering algorithm, which has achieved good performance when incorporated into the analysis of vector field. Additionally, a weighted K-means algorithm is presented, which is more appropriate for the analysis of scalar field clustering. The improved algorithm has better clustering results on the scalar field, which are more consistent with the physical laws by comparison. Ultimately, the algorithm is put in use for the CFD calculation. The number of iterations is decreased and the convergence speed is accelerated after the clustering algorithm is adopted for better initial condition.

There are different types of arc may occur depending on the arcing conditions and involved surfaces. The severity of the arc is determined by the involved arcing surface and the arcing current flowing path. In this study, arc in Sphere-Gap and Rod-Gap surfaces is considered for the time-frequency domain analysis. The voltage characteristics for both the arc events are recorded in different voltage levels and gap length. A Stockwell Transform (ST) based approach is applied on the arc signals for the harmonic decomposition. Further, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) machine learning algorithm is applied on the ST coefficients for the classification of real-time arc signals of different arcing conditions. The results obtained using ST and KNN algorithm successfully classifies different arc faults due to rod-gap and sphere-gap by their harmonic signature.

Keywords provide a short way of reflecting a main idea of the document, making it easier for the readers in reading. Extracting keyword is the main task in natural language processing. Since it is not only time consuming but also requires lots of efforts to extract the keywords manually, it arises the need for the automated approaches. This paper has proposed a solution for the automatic keyword extraction in Vietnamese language using hybrid deep learning approaches. Every existing deep learning approach has its own advantages; and the hybrid deep learning model we are introducing is the combination of the superior features of CNN and LSTM models. The proposed model shows enhanced accuracy and f1-score over another approach.

Gait rehabilitation is a crucial factor in enhancing the quality of life after trauma. The use of haptic biofeedback as a gait rehabilitation tool has immense potential, and therefore requires exhaustive investigation. Recently, we developed a wearable system that captures gait data through instrumented insoles and provides real-time vibrotactile cueing to augment gait symmetry training. In this study, we have updated our system to generate novel modes of vibrotactile feedback based on symmetry ratio. We have evaluated the effectiveness of these different modes of feedback in delivering cues for gait symmetry training.

The novel modes of gait symmetry related task are based on varying vibration on-time and intensity, and their relationship (proportional or inversely-proportional) with the error in symmetry ratio. Twelve young healthy adults participated in walking trials with the objective of achieving a target gait symmetry ratio while utilizing the vibrotactile biofeedback. Dependent t-tests revealed improved achievement of the target gait symmetry ratio while utilizing the proportionally varying on-time or intensity based biofeedback modes compared to no biofeedback mode (P-value <; 0.05). Furthermore, two-way repeated measures ANOVA revealed a statistically significant difference in symmetry ratio for relation type variations (proportional or inversely-proportional) in biofeedback (P-value <; 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.764).

The outcomes of this study provide a clear path towards the application of this system for training individuals with gait asymmetry, which may significantly contribute to their overall quality of life.

In this study, we present a comparison between two control approaches, namely PID and fuzzy, applied to platooning vehicles. Our experiment involved two vehicles, whereby the first one was driven by a human operator while the second was controlled longitudinally and laterally by two different controllers. Communication was established between the two vehicles, whereby information on speed and orientation angle was exchanged while maintaining a fixed safety distance between them. We developed a kinematic model of the vehicles and carried out 3D simulations using Matlab, Simulink, and V-REP software. To validate our approach, we utilized various reference trajectories and compared the results obtained from the simulation of the vehicles model in V-REP with the communication of speed and orientation angles from our model. The outcomes of the simulation confirmed the efficacy of our control approach and provided a prospect for future work.

This paper presents a comparative study that utilizes machine learning algorithms to forecast the shooting success of basketball players in the National Basketball Association (NBA). The primary objective is to analyze the dataset from the NBA regular season to enable teams to prepare game plans based on the performance of opposing players. This involves assessing the shooting proficiency of each player at different distances and the defensive strategies they typically employ. Random Forest and XGBoost models are implemented in this study to facilitate shooting prediction.

When a group of agents such as unmanned aerial vehicles are operating in 3-dimensional space, their coordinated action in pursuit of some group objective generally requires all agents to share a common coordinate frame or orientations of the coordinate axes of agents up to an unknown coordinate rotation common to all agents, which are simply referred to as having common coordinate axis orientations. Given coordinate axes that are initially unaligned, this paper considers the process of using direction measurements between agent pairs (obtained in their own coordinate frames) to achieve orientation localization, i.e. determination of common coordinate axis orientations, the calculations all being distributed. The process builds on the initial determination of relative orientations of agent pairs in a common coordinate basis. Distributed differential equations then allow determination of a common set of coordinate axis orientations, uniquely up to a common rotation transformation, which can itself be determined if and only if one or more agents have access to global coordinates.

When it comes to shared environments, where processes distributed in process nodes access critical shared resources in the mode of distributed mutual exclusion, it is important to know how they are managed and the order in which the demand for resources by the processes is resolved. In this work, through an aggregation operator, a consensus mechanism is proposed to establish the order in which resources are allocated to groups of processes. Consensus is understood as the agreement that must be reached for the allocation of all the resources requested by each group of processes. To model this consensus, it is necessary to take into account that the processes may form groups of processes or be independent, the state of the nodes where each of them is located, the computational load, the number of processes, the process priorities, the use of the CPU, the use of the main memory, virtual memory, etc. These characteristics make it possible to evaluate the conditions for agreeing on the order in which resource allocations will be made, ordered by process group.

A model for an ongoing interruption location master framework is described that is capable of identifying break-ins, entrances, and other forms of computer abuse. Based on the premise that security breaches can be detected by monitoring a system's audit logs for irregular patterns of system usage, the interruption detection program will be able to determine whether a website that requires a user ID and password is trustworthy or not. This model is not dependent on any particular system or application environment, making it versatile in identifying different types of system vulnerabilities or intrusions. As a result, it provides a framework for a comprehensive and general-purpose interruption detection master system.

Employee turnover and retrenchment have been on the rise in organizations in United Arab Emirates (UAE) and primarily one the reason for this high turnover and retrenchment is due to the lack of skilled manpower. Leaders and HR managers are constantly looking for effective strategies to create a positive work environment and as a result, change, adaptation and revival are a constant phenomenon that organizations undergo to continue being competitive. Of late due to the shift in labor market and education policy there has been a growing concern and pressure on educational institutions to relook at their employability skills offered as part of the curriculum in order to produce employable graduates. It has been argued that technical (academic skills) are vital to attract candidates, however, work place behavioral competencies (soft skills) are equally important. This exploratory research explores the employability and hiring trends particularly focusing on certain work and behavioral related competencies that are vital in Engineering graduates that makes them employable. Data is collected from 41 Engineering professionals based in UAE using an anonymously completed survey and the findings has helped researchers chalk out recommendations to educational institutions pertaining to the essential workplace competencies that are critical for Engineering graduates' employability.

In paper different standards for intelligent medical systems and multimodal architecture interfaces are under review. Application of Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resource (FHIR) standard for data model of intelligent multimodal interface are proposed. Intelligent multimodal interface for EEG and accelerometer bio-signals based on FHIR are shown. Use case diagrams, resource diagrams and class diagrams for production and research mode of this interface are described.

With increasing interest in e-commerce and online shopping recently, customer reviews are one of the most important elements that determine the satisfaction of customers about the products. Also, it gives a comprehensive picture of products to business owners. Hence, the aim of this paper is to conduct a sentimental analysis approach on a set of customer reviews collected from Amazon. As will, classify each review into one of these class: positive review or negative review by using ensemble machine learning method. The ensemble machine learning method used in this research is Voting which combined five classifiers: Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Random forest, Bagging and Boosting. All the Experiment in this paper done using Weka. We test six different scenarios to evaluate our proposed model against the five classifiers. The scenarios are using unigram (with/without) stop of word removal, using bigram (with/without) stop of word removal and using trigram (with/without) stop of word removal. The result shows the random forest technique give the highest accuracy which equals to 89.87% in the case of using unigram and with a stop of word removal but voting algorithm shows the best performance on the other scenarios.

This article presents the results obtained from the collaboration and participation of the Spanish University for Distance Education (UNED) and the renewable energy company INOMA, both based in Spain, in the Microelectronics Cloud Alliances Project (MECA project). As part of this project, three open courses were created, two of microelectronics and one of maintenance in renewable energies systems. These courses were integrated into a cloud architecture, which are accessible to everyone. After three years of project, which involved the development and design of cloud architecture; the contents and implementation of the three courses; and a small pilot test. This article presents the results and conclusions reached, as well as points to take into account in the future.

This article discusses the economic security of the production of onboard equipment as autonomous objects, taking into account the interrelation of factors that affect these objects and trigger processes that can lead to changes in their properties. To assess the economic security of economic operations and industry systems, a mathematical method and a criterion have been presented, with the possibility of implementing them in machine learning technologies.

Today, many of the aid systems deployed for visually impaired people are mostly made for a single purpose. Be it navigation, object detection, or distance perceiving. Also, most of the deployed aid systems use indoor navigation which requires a pre-knowledge of the environment. These aid systems often fail to help visually impaired people in the unfamiliar scenario. In this paper, we propose an aid system developed using object detection and depth perceivement to navigate a person without dashing into an object. The prototype developed detects 90 different types of objects and compute their distances from the user. We also, implemented a navigation feature to get input from the user about the target destination and hence, navigate the impaired person to his/her destination using Google Directions API. With this system, we built a multi-feature, high accuracy navigational aid system which can be deployed in the wild and help the visually impaired people in their daily life by navigating them effortlessly to their desired destination.

In video surveillance systems, infrared sensors have become a prevalent tool due to the robustness of their imaging procedure, which can operate under extreme conditions, such as low illumination or dim environment. However, to reduce human labor in video monitoring and enable intelligent infrared video understanding, locating the object of interest accurately in consecutive video frames is a crucial task. Therefore, a strong and robust object tracking algorithm in infrared videos is necessary.

Despite the benefits of infrared information, it may sometimes be unreliable, and appearance modeling with solely the infrared modality may not yield satisfactory results. To address such issues, this paper proposes an infrared tracking framework that exploits RGB-modality information to aid in infrared object tracking. Specifically, the framework incorporates an online non-negative feature template learning model to handle contaminated features caused by large appearance variations. The non-negative constraint enables the model to capture local part-based characteristics of the target appearance. Additionally, an adaptive modality importance weight learning scheme is incorporated to emphasize the contribution of more important modalities to appearance representation. 

To ensure model optimality, an iterative optimization algorithm is derived. Experimental results on various RGB-infrared videos confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Energy harvesting has emerged as an important research topic in recent years with the advent of autonomous systems and the Internet of Things (IoT). In this article, we provide an updated review of kinetic energy harvesting techniques, with a special focus on their applications in wearable technology.

Our discussion begins with an exploration of the fundamental limits of ambient kinetic energy sources. We then delve into the electrostatic mechanism and provide a comprehensive review of recently proposed electromechanical devices intended for energy conversion.

Ultimately, we discuss the design of a kinetic energy harvester at the system level. Our review provides valuable insights into the progress made in the field of energy harvesting, with significant potential for applications in the development of wearable technology.

Network traffic analytics has long been a pivotal area for both cybersecurity and network operations. The task of analyzing data streams (network traffic) can be performed in a real-time online mode for network operations or in an offline mode for forensic analyses. Our paper aims to explore the usefulness of machine learning models in network analytics, with a focus on traffic flows, for both network operations and forensic analyses. We aim to create systems that can facilitate human experts in analyzing traffic with "unknown background."

In order to fully comprehend the vast amount of new scientific knowledge being published daily, a new combinatorial approach is needed that can effectively supplement the process of reading scientific articles with artificial intelligence technologies. We present a novel method which we refer to as the “double funnel of artificial intelligence”. This approach involves an increase in the amount of data collected at the initial stage of the process, followed by the cleaning and enrichment of the data set to yield a much greater understanding of the new findings as compared to the traditional literature review method.

Our methodology involves the use of natural language processing and text visualization techniques to uncover new and important findings that may be missed by the human reader due to the sheer volume of available data. Through practical examples taken from various use cases, we illustrate the individual steps in the process and demonstrate the merits of our approach. Additionally, our method has proven to be successful in reproducing findings from regular review papers and uncovering additional and new findings in different fields, such as data science and medicine.

Despite the many advantages of our approach, we acknowledge its limitations and suggest ways in which it can be further developed. The increasing amount of data available demands a more efficient and effective approach to reviewing scientific literature. Our combinatorial approach presents a promising solution to this problem and has the power to uncover new and vital knowledge in a variety of fields.

Rehabilitation exercise with the use of functional electrical stimulation (FES) has become one of the effective technique of rehabilitation for hemiplegic and other neurological disorder conditions. Control is among the main issues in FES since muscle response is highly dynamic due to fatigue and other reasons. Different way of FES application may come with different structure of control technique. In this work, fuzzy logic controller (FLC) based cycle-to-cycle control with an energy storage element was designed and implemented for FES-assisted elliptical stepping exercise. The aim is to obtain appropriate control performance by combining the control action of FLC cycle-to-cycle control and effect of the energy storage element. The energy storage element makes use linear extension spring that provide resist and assist action to the exercise movement. Thus, instead of control action that totally rely on the FLC cycle-to-cycle control, the energy storage element could provide additional assistance in improving the exercise performance. Analysis was conducted to determine the appropriate spring length and constant. Comparison of performance with the FLC cycle-to-cycle control without the energy storage element was also conducted. The result showed a promising performance and hence supports the potential use of the proposed control technique for FES-assisted elliptical stepping exercise.

Poultry farms are an important contributor to the human food chain. Worldwide, humankind keeps an enormous number of domesticated birds (e.g. chickens) for their eggs and their meat, providing rich sources of low-fat protein. However, around the world, there have been growing concerns about the quality of life for the livestock in poultry farms; and increasingly vocal demands for improved standards of animal welfare. Recent advances in sensing technologies and machine learning allow the possibility of automatically assessing the health of some individual birds, and employing the lessons learned to improve the welfare for all birds. This task superficially appears to be easy, given the dramatic progress in recent years in classifying human behaviors, and given that human behaviors are presumably more complex. However, as we shall demonstrate, classifying chicken behaviors poses several unique challenges, chief among which is creating a generalizable "dictionary" of behaviors from sparse and noisy data. In this work we introduce a novel time series dictionary learning algorithm that can robustly learn from weakly labeled data sources.

Radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting is a promising technology for wireless networks. This paper focuses on wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs), where a hybrid access point (H-AP) coordinates RF energy/information transmissions to/from a set of nodes. In particular, we consider WPCNs where nodes have throughput requirements, and aim to minimize H-AP's energy provision (EP) by optimizing the time allocation of energy/information transmissions and H-AP's transmission power while satisfying node throughput requirements.

For half-duplex WPCNs, we prove that H-AP's energy transmission power must be at the maximum allowed value to achieve minimal EP. We also prove that the problem is convex under this condition, and design an algorithm that applies golden section search and bisection search to efficiently obtain the optimal time allocation. 

For full-duplex WPCNs, we prove that the EP minimization problem is convex but difficult to solve directly. Instead, we solve the feasibility problem (FP) for a given EP per unit time. We construct a convex optimization problem based on this FP and design a dual subgradient algorithm to find its optimal solution, which determines whether this FP is feasible. The minimal EP per unit time and its corresponding optimal solution are then found using the bisection search method.

Simulation results demonstrate that EP-minimized schemes significantly reduce H-AP's EP compared to baseline schemes.

Nowadays, the term "machine learning" has become a buzzword, but it encompasses a vast range of cutting-edge techniques that have disrupted the performance of numerous applications with the aid of increased amounts of data and novel approaches to data analysis. While some of these techniques, such as multivariate analysis, have been known for some time, they have been rediscovered and enhanced in light of this new application trend. This paper focuses on how multivariate analysis techniques can enhance the extraction of information in sensing. Specifically, we demonstrate the capabilities of a novel compact implementation of a soil moisture sensor that utilizes a contactless microwave impedance spectroscopy technique.

When researchers use Electroencephalograms (EEGs) to diagnose clinical outcomes, they face computational complexity problems. This is because the process of extracting complex, sometimes nonlinear, features from a large number of time series often requires significant processing time. In this study, we present a distributed system that harnesses cutting-edge cloud-based technologies and tools to successfully and efficiently undertake clinical research.

We compare the cost (both in time and money) of developing a distributed machine learning pipeline that predicts gestation time based on features obtained from EEGs using three different cluster types. Our findings demonstrate that the use of cloud-based technologies and tools allows for an effective and economical approach to clinical research involving EEG analysis.

We study a mobile wireless sensor network (MWSN) consisting of multiple mobile sensors or robots. Three key factors in MWSNs, such as sensing quality, energy consumption, and connectivity, have attracted plenty of attention, but the interaction of these factors is not well studied. To take all the three factors into consideration, we model the sensor deployment problem as a constrained optimization problem. Our goal is to find an optimal sensor deployment (or relocation) to optimize the sensing quality with a limited communication range and a specific network lifetime constraint. We derive necessary conditions for the optimal sensor deployment in both homogeneous and heterogeneous MWSNs. According to our derivation, some sensors are idle in the optimal deployment of heterogeneous MWSNs. Using these necessary conditions, we design both the centralized and distributed algorithms to provide a flexible and explicit tradeoff between sensing uncertainty and network lifetime. The proposed algorithms are successfully extended to more applications, such as area coverage and target coverage, via properly selected density functions. The simulation results show that our algorithms outperform the existing relocation algorithms.

Measurement processes which structural uncertainties are due to missing data, missed information in measurements, etc. are considered. A new algorithm for estimating the parameters of measurement processes is built on the basis of a structurally-adaptive model with dynamic properties which are due to the correspondence to the Hamilton-Ostrogradsky principle. The intellectual properties of the estimation appear in the adaptation of the dynamics of an evolutionary model to the dynamics of the occurring measurement processes. Mathematical modeling shows that their use makes it possible to reduce the errors in the estimation of dynamic processes compare to the “alpha-beta” filter under conditions of missing data by an average of 12%.

The inspection of printed circuit boards shifted from regular inspections based on two-dimensional images to sophisticated inspections using three-dimensional images. Light-based three-dimensional measurement systems tend to produce defects in the measured surface of the electrical components. A new method is proposed and tested to use deep neural network models to detect and repair such defects reliable. The neural network uses masked convolution to predict valid three-dimensional data based on damaged three-dimensional data and a set of two-dimensional images of the scene. The neural model is trained using an advanced online learning system, taking data from and feeding results to multiple inspection systems at the same time. The proposed method is tested with real data and different defects recorded on inline inspection systems. The benefits and drawbacks of this method are discussed and an outline for future work is given.

The integrated navigation system, consisting of barometric altimeter (Baro) and GPS, is presented. The integration is achieved by using a Kalman filtering type data fusion algorithm. The proposed data fusion algorithm utilizes the barometric altimeter and GPS measurements in the estimation procedure in order to increase the altitude estimation accuracy. The performance of the proposed Baro/GPS integrated system is evaluated by the simulations for altitude estimation of an aircraft.

Machine learning methods have achieved good performance and been widely applied in various real-world applications. They can learn the model adaptively and be better fit for special requirements of different tasks. Generally, a good machine learning system is composed of plentiful training data, a good model training process, and an accurate inference. Many factors can affect the performance of the machine learning process, among which the diversity of the machine learning process is an important one. The diversity can help each procedure to guarantee a totally good machine learning: diversity of the training data ensures that the training data can provide more discriminative information for the model, diversity of the learned model (diversity in parameters of each model or diversity among different base models) makes each parameter/model capture unique or complement information and the diversity in inference can provide multiple choices each of which corresponds to a specific plausible local optimal result. Even though diversity plays an important role in the machine learning process, there is no systematical analysis of the diversification in the machine learning system. In this paper, we systematically summarize the methods to make data diversification, model diversification, and inference diversification in the machine learning process. In addition, the typical applications where the diversity technology improved the machine learning performance have been surveyed including the remote sensing imaging tasks, machine translation, camera relocalization, image segmentation, object detection, topic modeling, and others. Finally, we discuss some challenges of the diversity technology in machine learning and point out some directions in future work. Our analysis provides a deeper understanding of the diversity technology in machine learning tasks and hence can help design and learn more effective models for real-world applications.

In this paper, based on the exponential synchronization of double-layered networks composed of multiple subnets, we bring forward a chaotic secure communication scheme, which is robust to different network sizes, time-varying delays, and stochastic noise. Cluster analysis is used to process the nodes with different dynamics, such that the subnets in the transmitter and receiver are one-to-one correspondence and constitute subnet pairs, while the node size of each subnet can be inconsistent. Each subnet pair is only accountable for encrypting/decrypting a part of information. There are many encryption/decryption units and they are operating in parallel, which can not only indicate the complex characteristic of different nodes but also speed up the information encryption/decryption. The proposed scheme applies the chaotic signals yielded by many chaotic systems as key sequences, such that the key space can grow with node sizes in the transmitter. This scheme is not subject to the constraint on the amplitude of the original message and chaotic signal, the influence of time-delay and stochastic noise, and it shows that only the nodes with large degrees need to apply controllers in restoring the original information. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulation manifest the feasibility and validity of the given scheme.

In this paper, we propose a scheme to classify different Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) lesion images for diagnosis. The main contribution is to quantify multi-scale pooled channel-wise information and merge multi-level features together by explicitly modeling interdependencies between all feature maps of different convolution layers. Firstly, feature maps are resized into multi-scale size with bicubic interpolation, and then down-sampling convolution method is adopted to obtain pooled feature maps of the same resolution, and finally one by one convolution kernels are utilized to fuse feature maps after quantization operation based on channel-wise attention mechanism in order to enhance feature extraction of the proposed architecture. Preliminary experimental result shows that our proposed scheme with less model parameters achieves competitive results compared to the state-of-the-art methods in WCE image classification task.

In this paper, the co-design of the clock and power delivery networks is proposed for ultra-low power IoT applications operating in sub-threshold. A distributed, multi-voltage domain and hierarchical power distribution network is proposed to deliver current to the clock buffers, registers, and combinational circuits in local clock distribution networks. The variation of the clock skew, setup time, hold time, and clock-to-q delay are analyzed under process and supply voltage variation. The effect on timing due to supply and process variation is analyzed for a target operating voltage and frequency of, respectively, 250 mV and 2 MHz in a 130 nm CMOS technology. The minimum clock period, skew, and insertion delay are reduced to, respectively, 0.74×, 0.52×, and 0.79× when optimized sub-threshold buffers are implemented, as compared and normalized to a clock network that includes non-optimized buffers. In addition, the co-designed clock and power networks were resilient to as much as 10% variation in the supply voltage when the proposed multi-voltage domain and distributed power distribution network is used with the optimized clock buffers.

Tracking technologies and location-acquisition have led to the increase of the availability of trajectory data. Many efforts are devoted to develop methods for mining and analysing trajectories due to its importance in lots of applications such as traffic control, urban planning etc. In this paper, we present a new trajectory analysis and visualisation framework for massive movement data. This framework leverages formal concepts, sequential patterns, emerging patterns, and analyses the evolution of mobility patterns through time. Tagged city maps are generated to display the resulting evolution analysis and directions at different spatio-temporal granularity values. Experiments on real-world dataset show the relevance of the proposition and the usefulness of the resulting tagged city maps.

Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery is vital to identify incipient failures and avoid unexpected downtime in industrial systems. This paper proposes a new rolling bearing fault diagnosis method by integrating the fine-to-coarse multiscale permutation entropy (F2CMPE), Laplacian score (LS) and support vector machine (SVM). A novel entropy measure, named F2CMPE, was proposed by calculating permutation entropy via multiple-scale fine-grained and coarse-grained signals based on the wavelet packet decomposition. The entropy measure estimates the complexity of time series from both low- and high-frequency components. Moreover, the F2CMPE mitigates the drawback of producing time series with sharply reduced data length via the coarse-grained procedure in the conventional composite multiscale permutation entropy (CMPE). The comparative performance of the F2CMPE and CMPE is investigated by analyzing the synthetic and experimental signals for entropy-based feature extraction. In the proposed bearing fault diagnosis method, the F2CMPE is first used to extract the entropy-based features from bearing vibration signals. Then, LS and SVM are used for selection of features and fault classification, respectively. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified for rolling bearing fault diagnosis using experimental vibration data sets, and the results have demonstrated the capability of the proposed method to recognize and identify the bearing fault patterns under different fault states and severity levels.

Online estimation of electromechanical oscillation parameters provides essential information to prevent system instability and blackout and helps to identify event categories and locations. We formulate the problem as a state space model and employ the extended Kalman filter to estimate oscillation frequencies and damping factors directly based on data from phasor measurement units. Due to considerations of communication burdens and privacy concerns, a fully distributed algorithm is proposed using diffusion extended Kalman filter. The effectiveness of proposed algorithms is confirmed by both simulated and real data collected during events in State Grid Jiangsu Electric Power Company.

Eye contact, also known as mutual gaze, is a fundamental component of human communication and socialization. As such, it has been extensively studied across a range of fields, including psychology, social science, and medicine. Our research group has focused on the development of wearable, camera-based technology to detect and evaluate gaze skills in the context of dementia care.

To achieve this, we have experimented with various deep learning-based techniques for accurately detecting eye contact from a relatively small number of labeled images. Specifically, we have implemented and tested both naïve deep-learning-based algorithms and GAN-based semi supervised learning (SSL) algorithms. These approaches were validated using the Columbia Gaze Dataset, Facescrub, and our own original datasets.

Our findings indicate that both deep-learning-based and GAN-based algorithms can be effective for detecting eye contact. However, we also observed some limitations and challenges associated with these approaches. Notably, we discovered that the accuracy of eye contact detection varied depending on the facial pose of the person being observed. It is possible that this variability is linked to differences in our learning datasets.

Overall, our investigation highlights the potential for advanced machine learning techniques to support the development of novel tools and technologies for facilitating communication and connection among individuals with dementia and their caregivers.

Fall represents a major health risk for the elderly people. If the situation is not alerted in time then this leads to loss of life or impairment in the elderly, which reduces the quality of life. In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a Fall Detection System based on Internet of Things (FallDS-IoT) by designing a wearable system to detect the falls of elderly people. We use Accelerometer and Gyroscope sensors to get accurate results of fall detection. We classify the daily activities of elderly people into sleeping, sitting, walking and falling. We use two well-known machine learning algorithms, namely K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) algorithm and decision tree to deal with the above work. The resultant accuracies for our generated dataset were 98.75% and 90.59%, respectively. Therefore, we were able to conclude that K-NN gives more accuracy in detecting falls and this method is used for classification. whenever a fall happens, a message informing about the fall will be sent to a registered phone number through a Python module.

This study proposes an enhanced heterogeneous ensemble model to facilitate real-time equipment condition assessment. The proposed model enables the planning of preventive maintenance activities before the occurrence of unexpected equipment failure. The study emphasizes the class-imbalanced problem, which has not been addressed in equipment condition assessment research. In reality, equipment exhibits multiple conditions, spending most of its operational time in the normal condition and rarely in the critical condition. Consequently, the distribution of samples is severely imbalanced among different conditions, making classification performance excessively challenging. To overcome this issue, a genetic algorithm-driven ensemble model is suggested. Numerical experiments, including comparative studies, have been conducted revealing the superior effectiveness of the proposed model compared to the existing models.

Palmprint, a biometric characteristic, is commonly used in civil and commercial security systems due to its high reliability and ease of capture using low-resolution devices. This study aims to develop a hand identification and geometry system utilizing hand features such as hand length, finger length and width, and palm size. The radius distance method is employed to determine the position of fingertip and finger concave from the hand contour, ensuring flexibility in detecting fingertip and finger curves accurately. By using these reference points, we can identify individual hand characteristics. The sample images were acquired via a simple and low-cost acquisition system, and the experimental results have shown the efficiency of the proposed method.

In recent times, the use of mobile devices and sensors has become increasingly widespread, accompanied by the emergence of new wireless and networking technologies such as wireless sensor network, device-to-device (D2D) communication, and vehicular ad hoc networks. These novel forms of networks are expected to achieve an increase in data rates, coverage, and the number of connected devices while significantly reducing latency and energy consumption. However, due to the constraints on energy resources in users' devices and sensors, the problem of wireless network resource allocation has become more challenging. To address this issue while ensuring an excellent user experience, advanced techniques are required to achieve a tradeoff between energy consumption and network performance. In this paper, we propose the use of reinforcement learning as an efficient simulation-based optimization framework for this purpose. Our primary contribution is to suggest a novel real-time approach based on deep reinforcement learning that will address the problem of energy-efficient power allocation while satisfying quality of service constraints in D2D communication.

Image segmentation is a critical process in numerous medical imaging applications, particularly in the Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) system for mammography. The quality of segmentation is vital to enhancing the performance and efficiency of the CAD system, which is essential for the radiologist to conduct a clear diagnostic analysis and make better decisions. Therefore, effective tools and techniques are necessary to achieve this goal. 

This paper presents a novel approach to extract the mass from the designated Region of Interest (ROI) using texture features and Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering with a setting of c=2. The user manually selects the ROI, and the clustering process is applied within a suitable range limited by the maximum intensity and a threshold determined by significant changes in the texture features levels. The proposed method is tested on the Mini-MIAS database and compared to other existing methods. The results show an overlap measure (AOM) of approximately 81%, indicating good performance.

This paper presents a Human Partner System (HPS) that is composed of three sub-systems: a hearing system, a speaking system, and a vision system. Coordinated with these systems, HPS can recognize people and dialog with them. To attract a human's attention for interaction, this paper combines the difference image method and the GrabCut algorithm for HPS. To assist humans in their daily lives and to enhance their interactive fun, HPS has a short-term memory function and can read out new email when a known person appears in her line of sight. To allow HPS to search for a target object in a complicated environment, this paper proposes the double peak continuously adaptive mean shift (DPCAMS) algorithm, which combines the contours and color information of target object. This algorithm is easy to implement and the experimental result demonstrates that this algorithm is faster than the speeded up robust features (SURF) algorithm.

This letter investigates the estimation of the slip distribution of a seismic event using the information provided by interferometric phase gradients. Even if the technique is expected to be suboptimal when compared with an estimation using the unwrapped interferometric phase, such an approach would permit to avoid the solution of phase ambiguities also including the parts of the interferogram that could not be reached by the phase unwrapping otherwise. This specifically addresses the cases where the motion gradients are so strong that particular areas have to be masked out due to unwrapping errors. Aim of this letter is to propose a possible way to include such areas modeling the motion with phase gradients. The rationale of this letter relies on the description of the coseismic motion given by the Okada model that provides both the 3-D surface displacement and the gradient tensor information. Based on the latter, this letter defines an inversion strategy that uses the information extracted by the phase gradients, hence avoiding phase unwrapping. This technique is tested on real test sites and compared with the results obtained using the absolute phase.

Small hydro power plants typically utilize fixed speed drives. However, with the advancement of power electronics converter, doubly fed induction generator (DFIG), an autonomous variable speed drive has become increasingly popular. Nowadays, small hydro power plants allied with DFIG as alternative sources of energy have played a crucial role in addressing energy crisis, environmental protection, and economic development in emerging countries.

This paper proposes a newly improved control strategy using artificial neural network (ANN) for grid-connected DFIG associated with small hydro power plants, with the aim of maintaining power factor at unity level in the grid side, reducing loss, and controlling reactive and real power flow in the rotor side. The SHPP system includes a back to back voltage source converter, which controls both sides of converter.

With the help of DFIG, optimum reactive and real power flow from the rotor side to grid side occurs at variable speeds. The ANN controller not only improves the transient response of DFIG but also makes the system more suitable for real-time applications. The stability of the system under different load conditions is investigated through model simulations. A 2 MW DFIG linked with a 2 MW SHPP model is simulated in SIMULINK for time domain applications.

This study examines a groundbreaking cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) network that utilizes a large number of multiple-antenna access points (APs) to simultaneously serve single-antenna uplink and downlink users in the same frequency band. In this system, the APs operate in full-duplex (FD) mode, while the users operate in half-duplex (HD) mode. The APs use a conjugate beamforming/matched filtering scheme with channel state information obtained via uplink training with orthogonal pilots transmitted from the users. 

However, the study found that residual self-interference (RI) is the primary limitation of cell-free massive MIMO systems with a large number of APs. To address this, the study proposed a simple power control method to mitigate RI. The study also derived the closed-form expressions of uplink and downlink achievable rates, taking into account a finite number of APs and channel estimation error. 

Numerical results showed that the FD mode could achieve a spectral efficiency gain of 140% over the HD mode when the RI was sufficiently low in the cell-free massive MIMO system. Additionally, the study confirmed that the FD cell-free massive MIMO systems outperform the FD collocated massive MIMO systems in terms of spectral efficiency.

In this article, we focus on the real-time detection of boats in high-resolution aerial images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This problem is similar to object detection in images taken from the ground or elevated surfaces, but it presents certain specific challenges such as the smaller size of objects to be detected and different camera orientations. Therefore, the general detection methods are not suitable for our problem. 

Several CNN-based methods have been adapted for object detection in remote sensing images by modifying the network models and parameters. In this article, we will review some of these techniques and architectures, and compare the improvements used in these methods. Moreover, we will present our strategy and techniques to provide practical advantages and a reliable solution to this problem. Finally, we will report the results obtained using our approach.

Since more and more vehicles are used, traffic speed prediction is of great importance to ensure public safety and improve traffic management. However, it is difficult to provide an accurate traffic speed prediction since the traffic is affected by many complex factors, in which the most challenges are internal sequential correlations, spatial dependencies and external factors such like weather and holidays. To solve the problem, we propose a broad learning based method, named spatio-temporal broad learning networks (ST-BLN) to forecast the traffic speed. First, to deal with temporal dependencies and spatial dependencies of traffic speed, spatio-temporal region of support (ST-ROS) is defined and identified using historical data. More specifically, for spatial dependencies, we propose a method of slide-window correlation coefficient to find related road segments with the current one. And for temporal dependencies, we obtain temporal region of support by analyzing the cumulative distribution of correlation coefficient. Second, we extract slow features of traffic speed as feature nodes of ST-BLN which can carry major information provided by raw speed. Further, the feature nodes are combined with external factors to generate enhancement nodes. In order to prevent overfitting and eliminate the influence of noncritical information, we simultaneously add L1 regularization and L2 regularization to the solution of final connecting weights. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method is illustrated using traffic data in Hangzhou and the superiorities are verified in comparison with five counterparts.

Since humans first gained cognitive capabilities, their desire to disseminate knowledge has been a constant companion. Various methods have been developed to effectively disperse one's knowledge or information to others, ranging from vocal and hand gestures to spoken and written languages. The ultimate objective of these methods is to create a replication of information from one's mind to the inner domain of others, a process known as communications. Over time, the meaning of the word communications has expanded to include machine-to-machine communications (M2M). 

Throughout history, we have only been able to use three modes of communications: strictly auditory, strictly visual, and a combination of both. However, ancient Hindu religious epic, Mahabharata, explicitly mentions the use of five primary senses - visual, auditory, olfactory, gustatory, and tactile - to describe a subject and transfer holistic information to someone at a distance. More recently, an idea for Human Bond Communications (HBC) was developed, which employs the use of all five senses to transmit and recreate holistic information using sensing and communication techniques. 

This article offers a technical framework to materialize the complex HBC environment, which makes it possible to achieve the idea of a holistic recreation of a subject. Incorporating the additional three senses - olfactory, gustatory, and tactile - alongside visual and auditory experiences, we hope to create a system that can bring the information closer to reality, imbuing it with greater significance.

The pervasive presence of IoT networks in our modern life grabbed the attention of the research community to investigate ways to enhance its reliability and stability. Many of these systems are considered as mission critical due to the criticality of the applications it handles. Health related IoT networks are among those. In IoT networks GateWays (GW) can be a major bottlenecks and single point of failure. GWs handle all the traffic flowing from the sensors to the backend cloud. In this paper we propose an optimized automated workload migration mechanism between closely ad-hoc mobile GWs to enhance the mission critical IoT network's reliability and efficiency. We exploit mobile devices to work as a temporarily GW for close by IoT networks. The proposed system comes with a multi objective GW selection mechanism to select the best GW to suit each IoT network. As a demonstration of the system effectiveness, simulation results showed the effectiveness of the proposed system in minimizing the IoT network power consumption expanding the network's lifetime.

A proposed scheme for advanced reservation path allocation has been refined. Constraints among optical switches over time are efficiently managed by introducing continuous variables to superpose switch states over reservation periods. The scheme has proved successful in path calculations over hierarchical, multi-granular, and heterogeneous networks.

Future power distribution networks will undergo uncertain changes due to the integration of distributed generators (DG) and prosumers. Meter deployment design will play an increasingly critical role in ensuring the safe and effective monitoring of these networks. To achieve more accurate and real-time data measurements, any available and newly-installed metering devices, such as smart meters (SMs) and micro phasor measurement units (μPMUs), can be utilized. This paper focuses on investigating a novel meter deployment technique for distribution network planning that aims to minimize the total amount of heterogeneous meters while ensuring the quality of state estimation (SE) in consideration of measurement uncertainty. In particular, the paper adopts the interval arithmetic (IA) theory to depict the measurement uncertainty in SE, which is shown to have advantages over existing probabilistic and fuzzy approaches. The paper presents case studies and comparative results based on actual distribution networks, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed IA-based SE algorithm and the meter deployment technique.

Based on the analysis of the fault characteristics of the inverter interfaced distributed generation under PQ control and the influence of the distributed generation access on the traditional protection technology, an active distribution network protection scheme considering the capability of regional measurement is proposed. The protection scheme based on the direction of zone current is proposed for the region with enough capability of measurement. The distribution network is divided into zones, and the fault zone is judged by collecting the fault component of current at breakers. As for the region with poor capability of measurement, an reclosing scheme coordinated with DG re-grid timing is proposed. The proposed scheme effectively solves the influence of distributed generation access on traditional protection and reclosing of distribution network. The simulation results of the examples in PSCAD/EMTDC prove the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

Solar energy is among the new sources of renewable energy. It is possible to convert solar energy into electrical energy using photovoltaic technology. To ensure that photovoltaic receives maximum intensity of sunlight, a two-axis solar tracker system is employed. The solar tracker system uses a DC motor to control the pitch and yaw angle. Fuzzy logic is utilized to optimize the error and delta error of the sun tracking system. The boundaries of the fuzzy system are optimized using the Bacterial Foraging Optimization (BFO) method. By using fuzzy control and BFO, the Mobile PV systems achieve better performance as compared to Fuzzy Logic Controller with an increase in efficiency of 0.4%.

Electrical modeling of vehicular antennas is required for design of modern vehicle-to-everything communication networks. However, full-wave modeling and the existing equivalent source methods still ask for long computation time. To address this issue, a fast simulation method is proposed in this paper: a sparse equivalent source model is developed based on Huygens’ principle where a vehicular antenna is made equivalent to magnetic current placed on a finite conducting plate. The image theory and the uniform theory of diffraction are then applied, a modified Green’s function is derived, and the sparse equivalent source model is constructed to replace the original vehicular antenna. Because of its simple geometry and material, in comparisons with the existing methods, the proposed model uses significantly less expenditures for simulation of vehicular antennas while has better accuracy due to the consideration of the finite conducting plate. Simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method, and a real-world experiment is designed and conducted to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method with real measurement data. It is shown that the proposed method can save simulation time by four times, with less than 1-dB error compared to measurement.

By sensing wirelessly the radio propagation environment and analyzing the channel state information (CSI), one can extend human senses beyond our traditional reach and enrich the insight into the surrounding environment and activities, with or without line-of-sight. On one hand, different indoor activities bring distinctive perturbations to wireless radio propagations. On the other hand, thanks to the nature of multipaths, indoor environmental information is contained and embedded in the wireless CSI. Since the occurrence of an indoor event lasts for a certain period of duration and repeats a similar transition pattern among different realizations, information is embedded not only in each instantaneous CSI sample, but also in how CSI changes along time, e.g., the CSI time series. Inspired by that, this paper proposes an indoor monitoring system that monitors the occurrence of different indoor events in real time with commercial WiFi devices, by exploiting the temporal information embedded in the CSI time series. Through extensive experiments, this paper studies the robustness of the proposed system to variabilities in event instances and human motion interference, and its long-term performance in a one-month test.

Giving effective feedback to students is known to be a challenging task, but with the widespread use of machine learning, it has become easier to provide valuable and timely feedback to students. In this panel session, attendees will be introduced to various machine learning algorithms and their implementation in aiding feedback for students.

The panel will focus on several applications of machine learning in this context, including determining the students’ conceptual understanding, personalizing their learning pathway, and providing feedback on programming components. These applications have proven to be effective in enhancing the quality of feedback provided to students, and attendees will have the opportunity to learn about their successful implementation.

Furthermore, the panel will explore how machine learning can develop in this area in the future. As students’ learning processes and feedback expectations continue to evolve, there is a need for more advanced and personalized systems to assist in providing feedback. The panel discussion will focus on the future developments in machine learning, including the integration of artificial intelligence and natural language processing to provide even more valuable feedback.

Overall, participants will leave this session with a deeper understanding of the potential of machine learning in aiding feedback provision for students and its future developments.

In this paper, we present a closed-form lower bound for the uplink rate achievable in a single-cell massive MIMO system utilizing a ZF receiver. The BS contains a large number of uniformly and linearly spaced antennas and serves single-antenna users, estimating CSI via uplink pilot symbols. We assume a finite channel model dimension and define the spectral efficiency as the sum of derived uplink rates. We optimize this expression of spectral efficiency via power allocation between data and pilot symbols, showing the superiority of our allocation scheme compared to equal power allocation. Simulation results are used to evaluate the approximation of spectral efficiency and highlight the pilot symbols' importance in low signal-to-noise ratios, mandating increased power allocation.

With the advances in hand-held devices (smart-phones and tablets, etc.) and high speed wireless networks, users have an explosive growth demand for live streaming service. Due to the diversity of user equipments (UEs), the live streaming has to be transcoded as different versions. However, transcoding is a computationally expensive and time consuming process. Since the shortage of computational resources and unstable of wireless networks, providing strict delay requirement and high quality live videos for wireless UEs is a big challenge. In this paper, we investigate user scheduling, transcoding decision, computational and wireless spectrum resources allocation problem in software-defined networking (SDN) based cloud-aided of heterogeneous networks (HetNets). Our research focuses on improving UEs' quality of experience (QoE) while guaranteeing time-delay requirement for live streaming services. Different from existing literature, to approach the real wireless environment, the available computational and wireless spectrum resources are modeled as random processes in our research. Considering dynamic characteristics of wireless networks and the available resources, the above problem is modeled as a Markov decision problem (MDP). Since the action space of the MDP is multi-dimensional continuous variables mixed with discrete variables, traditional learning algorithms are powerless. Therefore, an online actor critic algorithm is proposed to resolve the problem. Simulation results show the proposed algorithm has superior performances compared with the policy gradient algorithm and deep Q-learning network (DQN).

In this paper, a purely measurement-based method is proposed to estimate the dynamic system state matrix by applying the regression theorem of the multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. The proposed method employs a recursive algorithm to minimize the required computational effort, making it applicable to the real-time environment. One main advantage of the proposed method is model independence, i.e., it is independent of the network model and the dynamic model of generators. Among various applications of the estimated matrix, detecting and locating unexpected network topology change is illustrated in details. Simulation studies have shown that the proposed measurement-based method can provide an accurate and efficient estimation of the dynamic system state matrix under the occurrence of unexpected topology change. Besides, various implementation conditions are tested to show that the proposed method can provide accurate approximation despite measurement noise, missing phasor measurement units (PMUs), and the implementation of higher-order generator models with control devices.

Examples of instructional videos - both good and bad - have prompted me to consider how often we actively choose the communication medium we use. With computers giving us an abundance of options, it is important to consider how we can take advantage of them. Surprisingly, thinking about videos and other media has made me appreciate the strengths of the written word. Writing allows us to convey profound ideas and lighthearted musings alike, and this column has made an effort to do just that.

In this paper, our focus is on the issue of cross-domain aerial scene classification. The main assumption behind our proposed cross-domain distance metric learning (CDDML) framework is that while training data is sufficient in the source domain, it's limited in the target domain. Data distribution bias is a significant challenge in cross-domain scene classification due to differences in dates, sensor positions, lighting conditions, and sensor types. To address this, the CDDML framework replaces the existing color space with hybrid color features derived from all candidate color components, reducing the spectral shift between domains. Hybrid color features and bag of convolution features (BOCFs) are combined into a discriminating DML (DDML) method to reduce data distribution bias in the feature space. Lastly, we propose an image-to-subcategory distance measure that fuses hybrid color features and BOCF in the distance space to reduce the impact of intraclass variability on the nearest neighbor classifier. Our experiments on three aerial target images and data sets show that the CDDML framework outperforms most previous methods in cases of inadequate samples. The results also demonstrate that DDML, hybrid color features, and the image-to-subcategory distance measure all contribute to higher classification accuracy.

Multiple kernel clustering (MKC) has been intensively studied during the last few decades. Even though they demonstrate promising clustering performance in various applications, existing MKC algorithms do not sufficiently consider the intrinsic neighborhood structure among base kernels, which could adversely affect the clustering performance. In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective neighbor-kernel-based MKC algorithm to address this issue. Specifically, we first define a neighbor kernel, which can be utilized to preserve the block diagonal structure and strengthen the robustness against noise and outliers among base kernels. After that, we linearly combine these base neighbor kernels to extract a consensus affinity matrix through an exact-rank-constrained subspace segmentation. The naturally possessed block diagonal structure of neighbor kernels better serves the subsequent subspace segmentation, and in turn, the extracted shared structure is further refined through subspace segmentation based on the combined neighbor kernels. In this manner, the above two learning processes can be seamlessly coupled and negotiate with each other to achieve better clustering. Furthermore, we carefully design an efficient iterative optimization algorithm with proven convergence to address the resultant optimization problem. As a by-product, we reveal an interesting insight into the exact-rank constraint in ridge regression by careful theoretical analysis: it back-projects the solution of the unconstrained counterpart to its principal components. Comprehensive experiments have been conducted on several benchmark data sets, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

In recent years, many algorithms have been developed to tackle the challenge of multi-label learning where each instance is associated with multiple labels. Some methods have been proposed to select label-specific features to take advantage of discriminative features for multi-label classification. However, little attention has been paid to the critical correlation among instances. In this paper, we introduce a new approach called multi-label learning with label-specific features using correlation information (LSF-CI). LSF-CI considers both correlation information in label space and correlation information in feature space. 

The instance correlation in feature space is computed by a probabilistic neighborhood graph model, while label correlation in label space is computed by cosine similarity. LSF-CI can select label-specific features for each label and classify an unseen instance into a set of relevant labels. To evaluate LSF-CI, we conducted experiments using eight multi-label datasets.

The results show that LSF-CI is capable of selecting compact label-specific features and achieves competitive performance compared to existing multi-label learning approaches. In conclusion, LSF-CI is an effective method for multi-label learning that considers the correlation information among both instances and labels.

Traditional distant supervision for relation extraction is faced with the problem of introducing noises. In this paper, we present a shared representation generator to de-emphasize the noisy expressions by extracting common features in relation. Different from computing weighted sum in widespread attention mechanism, we directly generate bag representation in multi-instance learning by feature transformation, which only remains the semantics related to predict relation. We introduce the generator loss into objective function to improve the performance of shared representation. Also, the structure of our proposed generator is flexible and scalable. To capture more structural information, piecewise convolutional neural network (PCNN) is widely used to divide the output of convolutional layer into three segments, but this approach breaks the consistence and inner relationship of the sentence. We encode the sentence with piecewise-LSTM convolutional neural network (PLSTM-CNN) to alleviate this issue, which adopts BiLSTM after the pooling layer of PCNN. The experimental results show that we achieve significant improvement on relation extraction as compared with the baselines.

The integration of smart home platforms and third-party apps has revolutionized the way users interact with their homes. With the help of innovative developers, smart home systems have become more efficient, user-friendly, and convenient. However, this increased functionality comes at a cost: the potential for privacy breaches.

Third-party apps that monitor a user's activities can quickly learn their behavior patterns, which is a major concern for users. In this study, we investigated how IFTTT, a popular smart home platform, monitors user data without drawing attention to itself. Our proposed solution, called "Specific-fuzzification," provides two layers of protection for users. First, we filter out irrelevant events that might reveal sensitive information. Then, we obfuscate the remaining data before it is uploaded.

Our evaluation of "Specific-fuzzification" on a sample of seven users showed promising results. Compared to the traditional IFTTT platform, our modified version with the "Specific-fuzzification" patch was able to mask rare events that could reveal user behavior patterns. As a result, we were able to protect user privacy without compromising performance.

Our study highlights the importance of privacy protection in third-party smart home apps, and we hope that our proposed solution can help mitigate the potential risks associated with them.

Polynomials and rational functions of total degree l that are defined on an n-dimensional box can be represented in the Bernstein form. The range of these functions can be bounded by the smallest and largest Bernstein coefficients. This paper aims to extend the bounding properties of the range of monomials to the multivariate rational Bernstein case.
