The generated data packets may be voluminous and the data need to be delivered at the destination with minimal delay for applications like intrusion detection in the battle-field, monitoring chemical plants, nuclear plants, health of bridges and issuing tsunami alerts. Wireless sensor networks are limited in resources, such as energy, storage, processing power and bandwidth. A huge amount of data and limited bandwidth may result in packet collisions, which leads to packet drops. To achieve the data transmission reliability, retransmission of the lost packets need to be done. However, retransmissions increase packet delivery delay and energy consumption. In this paper, a data forwarding (routing) mechanism has been proposed to control the congestion for voluminous data collection in Wireless Sensor Networks. Further, a M/M/1/B queueing model has been adopted to determine the probability of occurrence of buffer overflow at a node. In the proposed mechanism, every node chooses the best node to route the data based on the level of congestion and available buffer space at upstream neighbour nodes. Simulation has been performed and results are compared with AODV (ad hoc on-demand distance vector) routing algorithm to show the virtue of the proposed mechanism in terms of packet drop, average packet delay and packet delivery ratio.

The concept of Security Aware Routing has not been widely implemented in current networks. However, the emergence of new IoT-centric core networks presents an opportunity to re-examine research in this area. We believe that routing can be an effective addition to traditional network security measures, particularly in the context of IoT. Security-aware routing integrates security and safety metrics into existing metrics such as bandwidth, network delay, hop count, path cost, and load. 

This paper introduces a new approach to security-aware routing using Software Defined Networks (SDN). We establish trust relationships between nodes and flows and utilize them to create SDN paths that adhere to the Cognitive Packet Network (CPN) principle. The proposed solution involves the use of Random Neural Networks (RNN) and cognitive packets to make routing decisions. We are currently implementing this solution in the SerIoT project to showcase the potential of secure networks for the Internet of Things (IoT).

Multimodal image registration is a crucial technique for analyzing scenes with remote sensing images obtained through different spectral regions. Due to the highly nonlinear radiometric relationship, finding common features between images of different modal types can be challenging. In this paper, a deep neural network is used to learn descriptors for multimodal image patch matching, which is key to image registration. A Siamese fully convolutional network is set up and trained using a novel loss function that maximizes the feature distance between positive and hard negative samples. The two branches of the Siamese network are connected by convolutional operation, resulting in a similarity score between the two input image patches. This score is used not only for correspondence point location but also for outlier identification. A generalized workflow for deep feature-based multimodal RS image registration is proposed, including the curation of training data, candidate feature point generation, and outlier removal. The proposed network is tested on a variety of optical, near infrared, thermal infrared, SAR, and map images. Experiment results verify its superiority over other state-of-the-art techniques.

Overweight and obesity are both associated with in-meal eating parameters such as eating speed. Recently, the plethora of available wearable devices in the market ignited the interest of both the scientific community and the industry toward unobtrusive solutions for eating behavior monitoring. In this paper, we present an algorithm for automatically detecting the in-meal food intake cycles using the inertial signals (acceleration and orientation velocity) from an off-the-shelf smartwatch. We use five specific wrist micromovements to model the series of actions leading to and following an intake event (i.e., bite). Food intake detection is performed in two steps. In the first step, we process windows of raw sensor streams and estimate their micromovement probability distributions by means of a convolutional neural network. In the second step, we use a long short-term memory network to capture the temporal evolution and classify sequences of windows as food intake cycles. Evaluation is performed using a challenging dataset of 21 meals from 12 subjects. In our experiments, we compare the performance of our algorithm against three state-of-theart approaches, where our approach achieves the highest F1 detection score (0.913 in the leave-one-subject-out experiment). The dataset used in the experiments is available at https://mug.ee.auth.gr/intake-cycle-detection/.

Vehicle-to-vehicle networks have gained significant interest in recent times from researchers all around the world. V2V/V2I are emerging as an efficient solution for achieving road safety and securely transmitting data from one vehicle to other. However, in such opportunistic environments such as a sparse vehicular network where disruption, dynamic network topology, fast vehicle movement, and environmental conditions are the major concerns, data forwarding is extremely challenging. Traditional ad-hoc routing protocols like Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) and Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) fail to deliver in such laborious conditions. Routing protocols of Delay/Disruption Tolerant Networks(DTN) exploit the Store-Carry-Forward Mechanism (SCF) strategy in these cases. Taking advantage of temporary connections to disseminate information is the focus of DTN. DTN helps to increase information propagation coverage in sparse areas where there are very few devices. In this paper, we first compare the performance of AllJoyn framework and Direct Delivery protocol in a single-hop scenario and then draw the attention towards a multi-hop scenario by comparing other three routing protocols that use DTN as the underlying paradigm. These protocols are Flooding, Epidemic, and PRoPHET. The performances are evaluated by transmitting the files of size 1, 4, and 10 MB from a static sender to a mobile receiver in the multi-hop scenario. We also develop an Android application that contains the implementation of these routing protocols along with file sharing functionality. From the outcomes of this experiment, it can be said that Epidemic routing protocol performs the best in our considered multi-hop scenario in terms of transfer delay, coverage, and throughput whereas, Direct Delivery routing protocol performs better than AllJoyn in single-hop communication.

The goal of this project is to create a wireless sensor network using event-driven nodes to monitor plant health and larva population in a remote field. Rather than the traditional approach of clock-driven nodes, our event-driven sensing nodes are developed with a STM32F407VG board that only acquires and transmits data when a significant change is detected. This approach reduces power consumption and increases efficiency. Data collected from the sensors is transmitted via wireless ZigBee interface to a base station where it is collected and analyzed by a MATLAB application. Findings are displayed on a CPU to allow for timely interaction and care of the crop field. The system parameters have been adjusted to achieve effective module integration and performance. Validation with an experimental setup has shown promising results for the system's realization.

The edge detection is yet a critical problem in many computer vision and image processing tasks. The manuscript presents an Holistically-Nested Edge Detection based approach to study the inclusion of Near-Infrared in the Visible spectrum images. To do so, a Single Sensor based dataset has been acquired in the range of 400nm to 1100nm wavelength spectral band. Prominent results have been obtained even when the ground truth (annotated edge-map) is based in the visible wavelength spectrum.

The study of the structure of Arabic texts is a relatively new focus, but one with great significance. By identifying the semantic and rhetorical meaning of the discourse through a coherent structural graph consisting of text units and rhetorical relations linking them, this approach has a broad range of applications in the natural language processing field. For example, it can be used in question/answer systems, automated translation and text summary systems, and the acquisition of Arabic terminology.

The study of rhetorical analysis involves three pillars. The first is dividing the text into units, the second is finding structural links between different text units, and the third involves linking these units to each other through rhetorical relations and semantic meanings. Our task, the automatic construction of discourse structure, focuses on the third pillar of rhetorical analysis, specifically the case of attachments.

Our approach to rhetorical analysis is based on segmented discourse representation theory (SDRT) and utilizes the classifier RandomForest. We tested our method on a test corpus and achieved an F-measure of 73%.

Sequential convex programming (SCP) is a popular method used for various trajectory planning problems, including entry flight, planetary landing, and aircraft formation. The method involves solving convex programming subproblems sequentially to obtain the optimum of original nonconvex problems. To improve the efficiency of solving search directions in convex programming for SCP-based quadrotor trajectory planning, this paper proposes a matrix-structure-driven interior point method (MSD-IPM). 

MSD-IPM uses primal-dual systems derived from the Karush-Kuhn-Tucher (KKT) conditions of quadrotor trajectory planning subproblems to solve search directions. Furthermore, successive elimination is used to solve the inverse of large-scale coefficient matrices of primal-dual systems using more efficient operations on small-scale matrices. The numerical stability of computing search directions is achieved by exploiting the positive definiteness of several small-scale matrices, and the specific diagonal structures of small-scale matrices are used for efficient computation of search directions. 

The complexity analysis indicates that the proposed method's efficiency is about one order of magnitude higher than the standard IPM. Furthermore, simulation experiments show that the MSD-IPM outperforms well-known optimizers like MOSEK, SDPT3, and SeDuMi in terms of efficiency and robustness. Finally, indoor trajectory tracking experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can generate smooth trajectories for real-world applications.

Basic ideas and formal concepts from fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic have been used successfully in various branches of science and engineering. This paper elaborates on the use of fuzzy sets in the broad field of data analysis and statistical sciences, including modern manifestations such as data mining and machine learning. In the fuzzy logic community, this branch of research has recently gained in importance, especially due to the emergence of data science as a new scientific discipline, and the increasing relevance of machine learning as a key methodology of modern artificial intelligence. This development has been accompanied by an internal shift from largely knowledge-based to strongly data-driven fuzzy modeling and systems design. Reflecting on the historical dimension and evolution of the area, we discuss the role of fuzzy logic in data analysis and related fields, highlight existing contributions of fuzzy sets in these fields, and outline interesting directions for future work.

This paper proposes the use of long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks for mass spectral substance detection. The method employs differential operation as the pre-processing method to determine the start time points of detections and the Relief feature selection algorithm to select the most significant channels for the mass spectrometer. The LSTM network has excellent understanding ability for historical information and classification capability for time series data, enabling high detection rates for datasets collected by time-of-flight proton-transfer mass spectrometer. Results show that the accuracy performance is improved by 123%, network size is reduced by 28%, and training speed is improved by 35%. The use of these pre-processing methods enables the LSTM-based substance detection system to achieve a tradeoff between high detection rate and low computing resource consumption, which is beneficial for devices with constraint computing resources such as low-cost embedded hardware systems.

It is a challenging task to deploy lightweight security protocols in resource-constrained IoT applications. A hardware-oriented lightweight authentication protocol based on device signature generated during voltage over-scaling (VOS) was recently proposed to address this issue. VOS-based authentication employs the computation unit such as adders to generate the process variation dependent error which is combined with secret keys to create a two-factor authentication protocol. In this paper, machine learning (ML)-based modeling attacks to break such authentication is presented. Experimental results show that ANN, RNN and CMA-ES can clone the challenge-response behavior of VOS-based authentication with up to 99.65% prediction accuracy.

We propose a novel method to enhance the comprehension of the reasons behind the uncertainties in liquid water content (LWC) retrievals, which are caused by the combination of instruments with various beam widths and horizontal displacement. In addition, we provide the first quantitative uncertainty estimates. Our research is based on a case study of a single-layer, warm, stratiform cloud observed at the Jülich Observatory for Cloud Evolution. We forward-simulated the LWC profiles of this cloud using the passive and active radiative transfer model and obtained radar and microwave radiometer (MWR) observables for all cloud columns. We converted these observables back into LWC profiles, combining MWR and radar observables from different columns, thus representing horizontal displacement. We analyzed the impact of the horizontal distance between a radar and an MWR on a widely-used retrieval for LWC, which scales radar reflectivity profiles with the MWR-estimated liquid water path. Our results revealed that even a displacement of only 10 m introduces an additional relative uncertainty of 10%, while a displacement of 100 m leads to a 30% increase in the relative error. The use of instruments with different beam widths slightly decreases the retrieval accuracy by a few percent, yet radiometers with larger beam widths marginally lower retrieval error induced by the displacement at large distances. Lastly, we demonstrated that cloud edge studies demand optimally matched beams between the radar and the radiometer, and that a displacement of only 10 m yields unreliable outcomes.

Automatic speech verification (ASV) involves using automatic algorithms to assess biometric parameters in humans. However, there are serious concerns regarding security, particularly relating to spoofing attacks. This paper proposes investigating the potential of using voice textures to identify spoofing attacks. Voice texture refers to the overall sound homogeneity of a voice. Spoofing attacks often involve text-to-speech (TTS), voice conversion (VC), and replay techniques, which produce distinct voice textures that are different from genuine speech. 

The concept of texture is well-established in image processing, with Local Binary Patterns (LBP) being a famous visual descriptor. We adapt LBP to be used as a speech texture descriptor. LBP coding is applied to both genuine and spoofed speech signals, and the resulting histograms of LBP descriptors are used as features. Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifiers are used to classify the features as genuine or spoofed. 

Experimental results show that the proposed method increases the difference between genuine and spoofed speech, making it an effective way to detect spoofing attacks in ASV systems.

Aiming at the issue how users in Windows domain cross-realm access cloud computing resources, a cross-realm authentication scheme based on federated identity was proposed. Based on the idea of the declaration, the scheme uses the federated identity provider to replace the gateway in the traditional gateway-based cross-realm authentication model, so as to realize the users in Windows domain access the cloud resources without re-authentication. The scheme uses SAML protocol to exchange user identity information between different domains, which ensures versatility and security of the system and realizes seamlessly secure communication between different security domains. Finally, based on claim provider, federated identity provider and application service provider, we give the design of the key components of the three modules, then the feasibility of the scheme is verified with the popular cloud platform OpenStack.

Simulating the response to radiotherapy (RT) in cancer patients can aid in the development of new therapeutic strategies. Computational models provide a means to address the multi-scale biological mechanisms that characterize these diseases. In this study, we present an in silico model of tumor growth and radiation response, capable of simulating an entire RT protocol for prostate cancer. The model includes oxygen diffusion, tumor cell proliferation, angiogenesis based on VEGF diffusion, an oxygen-dependent response to irradiation, and resorption of dead cells. A multi-scale framework was implemented to account for these processes. 

A sensitivity analysis was conducted using the Morris screening method on 21 computational tissues, which were initialized from prostate histopathological specimens presenting varying tumor and vascular densities. The dose per fraction and the duration of the cycle of tumor cells were identified as the most important parameters of the model. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of computational models in simulating RT response in cancer patients, and highlights key parameters that warrant further investigation.

The security of logic locking has been widely studied where it's assumed that there's an activated IC available. However, structural attacks such as redundancy analysis have shown that logic locking is not always foolproof. To address this challenge, we present a new technique for logic locking that's based on gate selection. Our technique identifies the best gate insertion points where the redundancy level is minimized under all possible key assignments. We evaluated our technique on benchmark circuits and found that it offers strong protection against redundancy analysis attacks.

This paper proposes a novel regular-shaped geometry based stochastic channel model (RSGBSM) for outdoor vehicle-to-vehicle visible light communication (VVLC). Traditional channel models fail to account for the mobility of vehicles and the inherent characteristics of light propagation, making the RSGBSM an innovative solution. By utilizing an ellipse shape to represent the line of sight (LOS) and reflection components of the VVLC, this approach provides a level of flexibility to realistically model numerous factors including vehicle locations, speed, direction, and stationary and non-stationary reflectors that are in a constant state of flux. The simulation results revealed that the LOS channel component is more significantly impacted by the direction of motion, whereas the reflection component is more sensitive to the relative speed between the vehicles. The proposed model provides valuable insight for VVLC research and development, and may ultimately facilitate the widespread adoption of VVLC technology for outdoor use cases.

Low power and lossy networks (LLNs) require specific routing protocols to meet application requirements such as latency and reliability. The IETF ROLL working group designed RPL for such challenging networks, defining an objective function (OF) that can use a set of metrics and constraints to allow nodes to select the best parents and construct paths. However, the use of metrics and constraints is an open issue for implementation due to the various applications of RPL.

To address this issue, we propose an opportunistic fuzzy logic-based OF (OPP-FL), which incorporates a new routing metric that measures neighbor load in addition to the traditional IETF ROLL specified metrics. Our proposed approach combines the traditional expected transmission count (ETX) and Hop Count (HC) metrics to propose a Children Number (CN) metric, using a fuzzy logic process.

Simulation results indicate that our proposed approach outperforms the based ETX OF, namely MRHOF and the OF-EC, in terms of packet delivery ratio (PDR) and acceptable results in terms of delay when the network size expands without inducing high traffic overhead. Therefore, the OPP-FL can effectively support routing in LLNs with varying application requirements.

The scalability of Internet of Things (IoT) systems is a significant concern due to the large amounts of data generated. Centralized data exchange leads to a single performance bottleneck, while a distributed data exchange faces network performance issues. A decentralized approach is the only solution that fully enables efficient IoT systems as there is no single performance bottleneck and network overhead is minimized. This paper presents an approach that leverages the semantics of DX-MAN for realizing decentralized data flows in IoT systems. The algebraic semantics of such a model allows for a well-defined data flow structure that is easily analyzed by an algorithm. The algorithm forms a direct relationship between data consumers and producers, preventing data from being passed alongside control among multiple coordinators. Data is only read and written on a decentralized data space. The approach is validated using smart contracts on the Blockchain, and experiments show that it scales well with the size of IoT systems.

This paper introduces a new approach to feature selection in high-dimensional data, called the class-specific guided local feature selection (CSGLFS) model. Traditional methods use a global feature subset to represent all classes in the input data, whereas the proposed algorithm derives a unique discriminant feature subset for each area of the data. This approach takes into account local changes, optimizing the feature subsets to suit the specific region of high-dimensional space.

The algorithm also includes a linked scheme that measures the similarity between query data and each of the specific classes. The CSGLFS method is expressed as a linear programming problem, providing an effective and efficient means of feature selection.

Experimental results demonstrate that the CSGLFS algorithm outperforms existing feature selection methods in terms of classification accuracy. These results were obtained through analysis of six public datasets, and confirm the efficacy of the proposed approach.

Small cells (SCs) mounted on top of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are a promising solution to boost the capacity in hotspot areas. However, the adoption of UAV-SCs involves the planning of their missions over time, which includes the scheduling of recharging actions of each UAV-SC at ground sites. Typically, the energy needed to recharge UAV-SCs is derived from the grid, which can be coupled with microgeneration exploiting renewable energy sources (e.g., solar panels). In this architecture, the energy that is locally produced can be either sold to the grid or used to recharge the UAV-SCs. On the other hand, when the energy from microgeneration is insufficient for recharging the UAV-SCs, additional energy can be bought from the grid. In this paper, we investigate the trade-off between maximizing the throughput provided by the UAV-SCs over a set of areas, maximizing energy sold to the grid, and maximizing energy bought from the grid. The proposed model, MaxUAVProfit, is designed to (i) plan the UAV-SCs missions as a sequence of positions and actions in 3D space vs. time, (ii) manage the grid-connected microgeneration, and (iii) control the amount of throughput received by each hotspot. We then evaluate the MaxUAVProfit in a realistic scenario, which is based on the measurement of real cellular metrics and a realistic UAV-SC energy consumption model. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of the MaxUAVProfit with respect to other competing solutions, which include either optimization of microgeneration or maximization of the area throughput.

A serial ensemble classifier based on feature selection using support vector machine (SVM) is proposed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of unbalanced data classification while fully harnessing the potential of the features. Traditional SVM model "one-versus-others" performance measurement indicators are defined. The primary objective is to achieve higher classification precision with a smaller feature set scale, hence implementing the serial ensemble classifier that employs "one-versus-others" binary SVM classifier as a base. Ant colony optimization (ACO) is used to determine the recognizable category and input feature subset of each level.

Several experiments are conducted on real engine vibration signals to compare the proposed approach, the traditional "one-versus-one" and "one-versus-others" parallel SVM classifiers. The results demonstrate the superiority of the serial SVM ensemble classifier based on feature selection in precision and efficiency in unbalanced data classification.

Photovoltaic monitoring is crucial for efficient and optimal functioning of various systems. Despite modern protective devices, many faults can remain undetected. This study proposes a monitoring and detection algorithm for identifying different operating conditions and faults in single-phase photovoltaic systems. The algorithm leverages machine learning techniques for pattern recognition and classification, as well as wavelet transform for feature extraction. The pre-processing stage involves using discrete wavelet transform to extract signal features, while a multi-layer perceptron neural network is employed to classify faults. The required data for algorithm development comes from simulation of PV systems with varying operating conditions in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. Results show that the developed algorithm achieves a training accuracy of 99.3% and a testing accuracy of 100%, based on a randomly divided data set.

Driver fatigue is a major cause of road accidents all over the world, accounting for 20% of total accidents. To address this issue, a system for detecting driver fatigue is of the utmost importance. EEG-based systems have proven to be the most reliable and accurate in estimating a driver's cognitive state. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms have shown promise in analyzing EEG data, and a highly accurate EEG-based driver fatigue classification system has been proposed in this work.

The study found that the relative power of theta, alpha, beta, and delta waves in the EEG showed a significant correlation to driver fatigue. Using 20 well-established classifiers in the field of driver fatigue, the selected EEG features were trained and evaluated. Fine Tree, Subspace KNN, Fine Gaussian SVM, and Weighted KNN were the most accurate classifiers among all those tested.

Different performance metrics were used, and the study identified Deep Autoencoder and KNN as the best suitable deep learning and machine learning algorithms for driver fatigue prediction, with an accuracy of 99.7% and 99.6%, respectively. Overall, the proposed system has the potential to significantly reduce the rate of fatigue-related road accidents.

In 2015, Google's Deepmind made headlines when it announced that it had created an autonomous agent using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) that could beat a professional player in a series of 49 Atari games. However, DRL still has significant drawbacks, particularly when it comes to exploration during the training process for high-dimensional problems. 

To address this issue, our paper proposes a mixed strategy approach that mimics human behavior when interacting with the environment. This approach creates an agent that is capable of efficient exploration during the DRL training process, ultimately leading to better performance. Specifically, our simulation results using the Breakout game show that our approach has a higher probability of achieving a maximum score than the baseline DRL algorithm - the asynchronous advantage actor-critic method. 

Our proposed scheme therefore has significant potential for real-world applications, particularly when it comes to solving complex tasks. By creating a "thinking" agent that is better equipped to explore a problem space, we can improve the performance of autonomous agents and unlock new possibilities for AI-powered solutions.

The Conceive-Design-Implement-Operate (CDIO) mode as a brand-new mode of engineering education has received a wide attention and many applications in recent years. Its features have inspired the capstone project and project-based learning method. This article starts with a survey and clarifies the two major issues of the current capstone project. Afterwards, the systematic design of the capstone project based on the CDIO model is proposed, and some suggestions are made on the equipment and learning space. Finally, we analyze current issues of project-based learning method in universities and make some inspiring suggestions.

The Internet of Things (IoT) generates immense amounts of data, making it challenging to manage the distributed Things that orchestrate it. To simplify this process, data-centric middleware can be employed. However, given the heterogeneity and resource limitations of IoT applications, they can suffer from performance, scalability, or resilience issues. One effective solution is to use caching techniques.

We are currently undertaking research to establish data caching within IoT middleware. Our paper explores the fundamentals of caching, key challenges, state-of-the-art techniques, and a description of our current methods. We propose using machine learning to improve caching in the IoT.

Overall, caching is a powerful tool that can be used to overcome the limitations of IoT applications. By employing caching techniques, we can boost performance, enhance scalability, and improve system resilience, setting the stage for more efficient and effective IoT operations.

Radical orchifunicolectomy has traditionally been the primary clinical treatment for small testicular masses (STMs). However, as STMs become increasingly common and are often found incidentally, a more conservative testis-sparing surgery has been proposed. This approach requires distinguishing between benign and malignant masses, which is challenging. Although perfusion patterns may provide useful information about the type of mass, there is currently no consensus on how to differentiate STMs. To address this issue, we propose building a dictionary of relevant perfusion patterns extracted through non-negative matrix factorization on contrast-enhanced ultrasound data. By reconstructing the data using this dictionary, we can create a tissue signature vector, which can be used by support vector machine classifier. In pilot testing, the accuracy of the classifier reached 100% in cross validation. This approach has the potential to significantly improve the diagnosis and treatment of STMs.

The swinging posture of floating objects plays an important role in improving the simulation degree of oceanic scenes. In this paper, we study the influence factors of swinging posture of floating objects in oceanic scenes, including the environment and its own influences. For the problem that the traditional floating model only applies to regular objects, such as boxes, we propose a floating model with multi-center force, including the confirmation of the center of the corner block, the distribution of weights, the vector synthesis of forces, and the determination of resistance problems. This model analyzes the shape of floating objects and allocates a branch center of gravity for the more prominent corner blocks, which makes the corner block contribute to the swing posture. In this way, the swing posture of irregular floating objects is more in line with reality. Through experimental comparison, a floating model based on multi-center force shows swinging posture which is more consistent with practical mechanics than the traditional single-center floating model on the irregular floating objects with more corner blocks.

In this paper, we address the issue of low-rank tensor decomposition of incomplete tensors, which has numerous real-world applications, such as recommender systems, machine learning, signal processing, and image inpainting. Our primary focus is on nonnegative tensor completion using low-rank Tucker decomposition. Notably, our model's unique feature is that the ranks of nonnegative Tucker decomposition are not constant, but rather they are a part of the decision-making process for optimization.

To solve this problem, we adopt a penalty method and blocks coordinate descent method with prox-linear updates for regularized multiconvex optimization. We also establish the convergence of our algorithm. Finally, we conduct numerical experiments on three image datasets, which illustrate that our proposed algorithm performs competitively against other existing algorithms, even when the data is significantly sparse.

This paper proposes a novel image feature set based on a principled information theoretic analysis of the convolutional neural network (CNN). The output of convolutional filters is modeled as a random variable conditioned on the object class and network filter bank. The conditional entropy (CENT) of filter outputs is shown in theory and experiments to be a highly compact and class-informative feature that can be computed from the CNN feature maps and used to obtain higher classification accuracy than the original CNN itself. Experiments involve three binary classification tasks using the 3D brain MRI data: Alzheimer's disease (AD) versus healthy controls (HC), young versus old age, and male versus female, where the area under the curve (AUC) values for the CENT feature classification (93.9%, 96.7%, and 71.9%) are significantly higher than the softmax output of the original CNN classifier trained for the task (81.6%, 79.4%, and 63.1%). A statistical analysis based on the Wilcoxon test identifies CENT features with significant links to brain labels, which could potentially serve as diagnostic biomarkers.

In recent years, IT security has become a major economic issue. Intrusion detection systems are an effective way to detect malicious connections in computer networks. However, the network traffic data used to build these systems is often large and includes a lot of ineffective information, which can decrease their efficiency. To address this issue, we need to keep only the relevant information from the original high dimensional data by using a feature extraction technique. One of the most commonly used techniques is Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). However, this method often uses between-class scatter against within-class scatter, which are almost always singular. 

In this paper, we suggest using the optimal mean PCA as a pre-step before LDA. Our proposed approach has been tested on KDDcup99 and NSL-KDD, and the results indicate its superiority over other techniques. By using this method, we are able to extract the most informative features from the network traffic data, which results in more effective intrusion detection systems.

Network devices are using growing number of 10 Gbit/s links. Such throughput upgrade imposes new challenges on creating high speed packet generators that can provide real network conditions. Traffic generators implemented as software solutions have challenges in achieving required performance, as they are commonly using kernel network stack for packet I/O. We describe different techniques for implementing Poisson traffic model in software-based traffic generator that is using netmap API as fast packet I/O.

Collaborative filtering (CF) is susceptible to shilling attacks, which can manipulate CF recommendations by injecting well-crafted profiles. Although there are various supervised learning-based shilling attack detection methods, they mainly measure rating values and items of a profile individually, disregarding the relation between items. This study aims to strengthen the resilience of CF against shilling attacks by considering the correlation between rated items. Real users rate items based on their preferences, whereas malicious users randomly select items for their profiles, leading to different rated item correlation between real and malicious profiles. To capture the information from different intervals of the rated item correlation distribution in terms of Cosine Association (CA), three features are proposed. The proposed features are evaluated on a benchmark dataset, MovieLens 100K, and their discrimination ability is illustrated. The experimental results suggest that these features significantly contribute to shilling attack detection in CF.

Millimeter Wave (mmWave) technology coupled with full duplex (FD) communication has the potential of increasing the spectral efficiency. However, the self-interference (SI) encountered in the FD mode and the ubiquitous multi-user interference (MI) contaminates the signal. Furthermore, the system performance may also be limited by channel aging that arises because of the time-varying nature of the channel. Therefore, in this paper, we conceive FD hybrid beamforming (HBF) for K-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-aided orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) using learning-aided channel prediction. We first derive a joint precoder and combiner design for full duplex K-user MIMO-OFDM interference channels, where we aim for minimizing both the residual SI and the MI, followed by an iterative hybrid decomposition technique developed for OFDM systems. Then, we propose a learning-aided channel prediction technique for systems suffering from channel aging relying on a radial basis neural network, where we show by simulation that upon using sufficient training, learning-assisted channel prediction can faithfully estimate the current channel. Furthermore, we demonstrate by simulations that our proposed joint hybrid precoder and combiner design outperforms the popular Eigen beamforming (EBF) technique by about 5 dB for a 128 × 32-element MIMO aided OFDM system having 32 sub-carriers.

The efficiency and safety of communication among vehicles are highly dependent on the accuracy of the data transmitted between them. This paper discusses the detection and classification of location spoofing misbehavior using the VeReMi dataset. We propose a framework where plausibility checks become feature vectors for machine learning models, which can detect and categorize this misbehavior. Our findings indicate that we can enhance plausibility check detection precision by more than 20% using KNN and SVM, while still retaining a recall rate of 5%. We have also demonstrated that misbehavior types can be classified, resulting in improved accuracy and specific action steps to prevent such attacks, thus boosting the security and safety of the system.

The fifth generation (5G) wireless system plays a crucial role in realizing future network applications that have diverse service requirements. To meet these requirements, the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) has proposed 5G New Radio (NR) specifications that offer significant flexibility in configurations and procedures. This facilitates a more efficient and agile radio access network (RAN). However, the increasing complexity of resource management demands the exploration of new approaches, such as machine learning techniques.

In this article, we explore the issue of radio resource scheduling in the 5G RAN. Using a modularized deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) architecture, we have developed a method that uses a combination of scheduling algorithms to perform more efficiently and effectively. Our proposed architecture has been shown to be efficient in training and performing well compared to conventional scheduling algorithms. Furthermore, this approach can be applied to other radio resource management problems that have similar characteristics.

Overall, our study emphasizes the importance of machine learning techniques to help manage the complexity of resource management in the 5G RAN. By utilizing a combination of scheduling algorithms and an efficient DDPG architecture, we can improve the performance of radio resource scheduling. Further research on this topic may lead to even more efficient and effective solutions for managing radio resources in the 5G RAN.

Strong correlation of link gains over multiple wavelengths has been demonstrated in non-line-of-sight optical wireless scattering communication. In this paper, we further demonstrate that the channel impulse responses for different wavelengths are also strongly correlated. Thus, a novel channel estimation method based on such correlation over multiple wavelengths is proposed, where only certain reference wavelengths are assigned pilot signal. On each channel with assigned pilot signal, we adopt an improved least-squares channel estimation method to estimate the tap parameters and the tap length (or the number of taps). The channel tap coefficients on other wavelengths can be estimated based on the correlation. Under the proposed channel estimation, the channel estimation accuracy can be improved as shown by the simulations. Moreover, under the same total channel estimation overhead, the accuracy of the proposed channel estimation first increases and then decreases with the number of reference wavelengths.

In this paper, the authors present a solution to the risk estimation problem for robots operating in the presence of bounded uncertainties with arbitrary probability distributions. Specifically, they address the challenge of estimating the probability of a robot violating safety constraints as a result of probabilistic parameters of the unsafe set and probabilistic states of the robot. To achieve this, the authors use a moment-based representation of probability distributions and describe upper and lower bounds of the risk as a linear weighted sum of the moments. The weights are obtained by solving a sum-of-squares optimization problem in the offline step, and given a finite number of moments of probability distributions, the risk can be estimated in real-time. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach by solving probabilistic collision checking problems for a non-convex obstacle in the presence of probabilistic uncertainties in the robot’s location, as well as the size, location, and geometry of the obstacle.

With cloud storage becoming increasingly popular, many data owners opt to outsource their private data to cloud servers. However, ensuring the security and privacy of this data is crucial. To achieve this, data owners may choose to store their data in multiple cloud servers as ciphertext. Although previous studies have utilized keywords to retrieve encrypted target data, this method overlooks the conceptual relationship between keywords, leading to imprecise query results. 

To address this issue, a Dynamic Multi-server Searchable Encryption Scheme Based on Concept Hierarchy has been proposed. This scheme uses a concept hierarchy tree to design the respective index of sub-servers and documents. This ensures that the most relevant cloud servers are located, thereby improving the retrieval efficiency. Additionally, the scheme utilizes the TF*IDF method to enhance the accuracy of retrieval even further. 

Simulations have demonstrated the superiority of this scheme as compared to other typical schemes. Overall, this solution presents a viable solution to the security and privacy issues involved in cloud storage, particularly where multiple servers are involved.

The incidence of skin melanoma is rapidly increasing, along with the number of fatalities attributed to it. Automatic image segmentation tools have become essential in providing standardized computer-assisted analysis for skin melanoma patients. Current segmentation methods are based on fully convolutional neural networks that use an encoder-decoder approach. However, it has been noted that these methods produce coarse segmentation masks due to the loss of location information during the encoding layers. 

Taking cues from the Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSP-Net), we propose a novel encoder-decoder model that incorporates pyramid pooling modules in the deep skip connections for aggregating global context and compensating for lost spatial information. Our approach was trained and validated using the ISIC 2018: Skin Lesion Analysis Towards Melanoma Detection grand challenge dataset. Our approach showed a Jaccard index of 0.837 on validation, outperforming U-Net. 

Based on our reliable results, we suggest that this segmentation method can be introduced for clinical practice.

Our approach utilizes both automatic features generated by convolutional neural networks (CNN) and handcrafted features computed by the bag-of-visual-words (BOVW) model to achieve the latest results in facial expression recognition (FER). Various CNN architectures, pre-trained models, and training procedures, including Dense-Sparse-Dense, are experimented with in order to obtain automatic features. The two types of features are fused, and a local learning framework is utilized to predict the class label for each test image. 

The local learning framework comprises three steps, with a k-nearest neighbors model applied first to select the nearest training samples for a given input test image. Next, a one-versus-all support vector machines (SVM) classifier is trained on the selected training samples. Finally, the SVM classifier makes a prediction only for the test image it was trained for. While local learning has been used with handcrafted features previously, this is the first known application in conjunction with deep features.

 Experiments on the 2013 FER Challenge data set, the FER+ data set, and the AffectNet data set show our approach surpasses the state-of-the-art methods by over 1% on all data sets. Our top accuracy is 75.42% on the FER 2013, 87.76% on the FER+, 59.58% on the AffectNet eight-way classification, and 63.31% on the AffectNet seven-way classification.

The diversity of personal interest and preference of mobile users results in a wide spectrum of mobile app usage, and it is important to predict such app preference in order to provide personalized services. However, currently available individual app usage data is very limited, which does not cover a large user base. In this paper, we demonstrate that it is possible to make personalized app usage estimation by learning user's app preference from the social media, i.e., public accessible tweets, which can also reflect user's interest and make up for the sparsity of app usage data. By proposing a novel generative model named IMCF+ to transfer user interest from rich tweet information to sparse app usage, we achieve personalized app recommendations via learning the interest's correlation between apps and tweets. Based on a real-world app usage and tweet dataset over a large population, we evaluate the performance of IMCF+ with a variety of scenarios and parameters. With only 10 percent training data, our IMCF+ approach achieves 82.5 percent hitrate in predicting the top ten apps. Moreover, IMCF+ outperforms the other six state-of-the-art algorithms by 4.7 percent and 10 percent in high sparsity case and user cold-start scenario, indicating the effectiveness of our method. All these results demonstrate that our technique can reliably learn user's interest from tweets to help solve the personalized app recommendation problem. Our study is the first step forward for transferring user's interest learned from social media to app preference, which paves the way for providing higher-quality personalized app recommendation and services for mobile users.

Computational cost is an important consideration for memory encoding prediction models that use data from dozens of implanted electrodes. We propose a method to reduce computational expense by selecting a subset of all the electrodes to build the prediction model. The electrodes were selected based on their likelihood of measuring brain activity useful for predicting memory encoding better than chance (in terms of AUC). A logistic regression prediction model was built using spectral features of intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) from the selected electrodes. We demonstrate our method on iEEG data from 37 human subjects performing free recall verbal short-term memory tasks. The method achieves a 36.3% reduction in the number of electrodes used for prediction, resulting in a 64.9% reduction in inference computation time with just a 0.3% loss in prediction performance compared to the case when all electrodes were used. The electrodes selected using our method provided improved prediction performance compared to those electrodes that were not selected in 31 out of 37 patients. Building upon this observation, we also developed a method to identify the subjects for whom the proposed electrode selection method would be beneficial.

As part of their daily work, radiologists often review medical images such as CT scans to identify significant lesions and write reports describing them. In this study, the authors investigate the annotation of lesions as a critical step in computer-aided diagnosis. The aim is to predict multiple relevant labels for a given lesion, such as body part, type, and attributes. To achieve this, 145 labels based on RadLex are defined to describe a wide variety of lesions in the DeepLesion dataset. Training labels are directly mined from the corresponding radiology reports, which requires minimal manual input and can be applied to large data and label sets. A multi-label convolutional neural network is designed to accommodate images with multi-scale structure and a noise-robust loss. The framework is validated through both quantitative and qualitative experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness. The average area under the ROC curve on 1,872 test lesions is 0.9083.

Constructing a model for online sentiment classification of film and television commentary can help filmmakers understand their audience's opinions and improve their productions. However, traditional methods based on sentiment lexicon and machine learning have various limitations, including ignoring contextual semantics and sparse features. To address these issues, this paper has optimized the internal structure of the existing convolutional neural network model and proposed a new model called NCNM (New Convolutional Neural Network model) that utilizes a multi-sliding window and new pooling method. Additionally, the model clusters feature words using feature vectors. The classification accuracy of NCNM was evaluated on the Stanford SST and Cornell MRD datasets, with promising results. Overall, NCNM showed improvements over existing mainstream methods when it came to accurately classifying emotional sentiments in short text video reviews.

Whole-slide imaging (WSI) allows digitization of conventional glass slides and enables digital pathology. However, current computational algorithms for WSI use only local information within image patches and neglect important context information from neighboring patches. To address this, we propose a multi-scale convolutional network (ConvNet) to utilize the image pyramids present in WSI. By incorporating low-resolution images in addition to high-resolution ones, our model considers context information and enhances prediction accuracy. Our experiments on a benchmark breast cancer WSI dataset show that multi-scale networks with WSI image pyramids achieve higher accuracy than traditional models. The late fusion method that averages feature vectors provides the highest accuracy of 81.50%. This approach shows promise for multi-scale analysis of WSI and can aid computer-aided diagnosis in digital pathology.

Real-time embedded systems are increasingly prevalent in modern society, as automated systems become more and more relied upon for both critical and non-critical functions. However, the complexity of these systems and their importance demands a monitoring tool that can reliably detect anomalies in their behavior. While standard error detection mechanisms exist, they often rely on a priori knowledge of the application behavior and are focused on detecting errors in a single application without considering the broader system.

To address these issues, we propose a hierarchical attention-based anomaly detection (HAbAD) model based on stacked Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Networks with Attention. This model takes a closed-world prediction-classification approach, using reconstruction error from a non-parametric kernel density estimator to detect anomalies.

Our results show that this approach is effective in detecting anomalies in real-time embedded systems, even in cases where the anomaly occurs across multiple layers of the system. By leveraging the bespoke nature of embedded real-time system design, our model can detect deviations in kernel traces, which reflect the behavior of the hardware components and application at every point in time. 

In conclusion, our HAbAD model offers a robust means of detecting anomalies in real-time embedded systems, and has the potential to be a valuable tool for ensuring the safety and reliability of these systems.

Lipreading is a challenging task when it comes to classifying gestures. One of the main problems with computer lipreading is achieving speaker-independence. Simply put, speaker-independence refers to how accurately a system can recognize the test speaker, who was not included in the training set, as compared to a speaker who was included in the training set. Unfortunately, the literature on speaker-independent lipreading is limited, and the few accuracy scores that do exist are usually aggregated within dependent test speaker accuracies, thereby making independent results unclear. 

In this study, we conducted a systematic survey of experiments with the TCD-TIMIT dataset using both conventional approaches and deep learning methods. We provided a series of wholly speaker-independent benchmarks and discovered that the best speaker-independent machine, using CNN features and an SVM classifier, scored 69.58% accuracy. While this accuracy score is less than state-of-the-art speaker-dependent lipreading machines, it is greater than previously reported in independence experiments.

State of charge (SOC) estimation is a critical technology for battery management systems (BMS) and is vital for the safe, reliable, and economical operation of electric vehicles (EVs). In this paper, we present a new approach to improve the accuracy of SOC estimation based on the Spherical Simplex-Radial Cubature Kalman Filter (SSRCKF) algorithm. Our results show that this approach outperforms the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) and Cubature Kalman Filter (CKF) in estimating SOC.

To validate our approach, we conducted experiments using the Worldwide harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, which was introduced in the European Union last year. To test the anti-interference ability of the SSRCKF algorithm, we added noise to the measured data of current and voltage. The results showed that our approach estimated SOC more accurately than the UKF and CKF.

In conclusion, our new approach based on the SSRCKF algorithm is a promising method for improving the accuracy of SOC estimation in BMS for EVs. We believe that this will contribute to the broader adoption of EVs by enhancing their safety, reliability, and economic efficiency.

Slewing bearings play a critical role in the functioning of large machinery. Therefore, it is important to study their life prediction and health management. While many studies use data-driven approaches, some “black-box” models lack physical meaning due to their opaque structures, making it difficult to choose optimal parameters. Few studies focus on explicit model relationships for slewing bearings' life models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach based on symbolic regression. The aim of this approach is to explore slewing bearings' explicit life models to predict residual useful life (RUL). The proposed method combines multiple signals to provide a comprehensive response to slewing bearings' health and uses various genetic programming (GP) algorithms to model life expressions. Additionally, the approach introduces independent, hybrid, and piecewise strategies to establish explicit model relationships with respect to degradation indicators (DIs) via GPs. To verify the proposed method, three run-to-failure experiments under discrepant operating conditions of slewing bearings are carried out. The results show that models generated by epigenetic linear genetic programming (ELGP) under hybrid and piecewise modeling strategy with similarity-based combination strategy performed the best. These models had succinct and intelligible life expressions compared to other situations.

With the advent of network densification and the development of other radio interface technologies, the major bottleneck of future cellular networks is shifting from the radio access network to the backhaul. The future networks are expected to handle a wide range of applications and users with different requirements. In order to tackle the problem of downlink user-cell association, and allocate users to the best cell, an intelligent solution based on reinforcement learning is proposed. A distributed solution based on Q-Learning is developed in order to determine the best cell range extension offsets (CREOs) for each small cell (SC) and the best weights of each user requirement to efficiently allocate users to the most appropriate SC, based on both backhaul constraints and user demands. By optimizing both CREOs and user weights, a user-specific allocation can be achieved, resulting in a better overall quality of service. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms current solutions by achieving better user satisfaction, mitigating the total number of users in outage, and minimizing user dissatisfaction when satisfaction is not possible.

While New Product Development has been widely researched and implemented, there has been less focus on New Service Development in various industries. This research aims to investigate the concept of New Service Development in the hotel industry through a real hotel case study. To evaluate the required services, Axiomatic Design Theory is utilized. The customer domain is analyzed using a business model Canvas, which involves functional requirements analysis for a hotel and mapping them to general services available in the market. The system complexity is optimized while ensuring its feasibility. The required data is obtained through a knowledge-based structure, which allows business owners to manage data around the market. The research findings indicate that the focus has been limited to the customer segment, and there is no systematic approach for knowledge creation from business data. The proposed framework aims to address these limitations and enhance the New Service Development paradigm in the hotel industry.

Artificial neural networks, which are widely used in artificial intelligence applications such as object recognition and speech recognition, have come a long way since their inception. To expand the applications of neural networks, high-performance customized hardware is crucial, as the traditional CPU and GPU are not efficient enough. Over the past four years, numerous architectures have been proposed to boost the energy efficiency of deep learning inference processing, including the works of Tsinghua and Deephi. 

In this talk, we will discuss various architectures based on CMOS technologies, including FPGA accelerators that can achieve 200GOPS/W, chips with DDR subsystems that can achieve 1-5TOPS/W, and chips with everything on the chip that can achieve over 50TOPs/W. We will also explore the potentials and trends of emerging NVM technology, such as in-memory computing, which promises to improve the energy efficiency of learning systems.

In conclusion, the evolution of artificial neural networks has brought about tremendous progress in artificial intelligence, but the need for efficient customized hardware is still a vital issue. We hope that our discussion and exploration of various architectures and emerging technologies will further advance the development of energy-efficient neural networks.

Wireless sensor networks are composed of various sensors that are deployed to monitor the physical world. While traditional cryptography theory is used to protect message content and contextual information, the location security of nodes is a growing concern. To tackle this issue, the anonymous routing strategy for preserving location privacy (ARPLP) has been proposed. ARPLP sets a proxy source node to conceal the location of the real source node. The real source node selects several neighbors as receivers until the packets are transmitted to the proxy source, which is randomly selected to make it challenging for adversaries to obtain location information. Additionally, the scheme sets a branch area around the sink, which increases the routing branch and confuses attackers. Analysis and simulation experiments demonstrate that ARPLP can reduce traffic consumption and communication delay while improving the security of source nodes and base stations.

An intelligent tutoring system (ITS) is designed to simulate the behavior of the traditional educational process while providing a more interactive and engaging learning environment. To achieve this goal, ITS employs various tools, ranging from simple to complex ones, to provide mindful feedback to students. The impact of ITS is measured by learners' academic performance and their subsequent learning outcomes.

To understand the effect of intelligent tutoring in the form of "informed feedback" on learners' satisfaction with an interactive learning environment, this study examines contemporary research on instructional designing, feedback strategies, and intelligent tutoring systems. Primary data collected for this study includes the intervention of ITS, which simulates human tutors, acting as intelligent tutors, and providing informed feedback based on the Interactive Tutoring Feedback Model's factors.

The Interactive Tutoring Feedback Model factors include Requirement Engineering, Characterization of learners based on meta-cognition and motivation, and Characterization of informed feedback for mindful acceptance. Despite the contextual interpretation difficulties, this study concludes that intelligent tutoring can bring about a positive change in learners' satisfaction scores in an interactive learning environment.

In summary, the results of this study show that an intelligent tutoring system, by providing informed feedback through simulation, can enhance students' engagement and satisfaction in an interactive learning environment. Moreover, the study reinforces the importance of feedback strategies in improving the learning outcomes of students in intelligent tutoring systems.

In multi‐path transmission control protocol (MPTCP)‐based aggregation solutions, aggregation occurs at the TCP layer. The target of MPTCP aggregation is to transmit data using multiple paths without causing modifications to existing infrastructures, such as the 4G mobile network, Wi‐Fi access. The MPTCP connection consists of a combination of several TCP connections, with each TCP connection transmitted on a path to appear as a normal connection for the different devices crossed. For a normal TCP connection, congestion control introduces another limitation provided by the congestion window (cwnd). If during an MPTCP connection, a previously advertised address becomes invalid, then the affected host must advertise it in the REMOVE_ADDR option so that the other end can delete the TCP connections bound to that address. At the beginning of an MPTCP connection, it is important to ensure that the path is fully compatible with the MPTCP options.

Autonomous driving systems have become a widely discussed topic in recent years, and the use of Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in industrial settings is no exception. These AGVs are controlled by their autonomous driving systems which utilize sensors such as vision sensors, laser sensors, and ultrasonic sensors to detect the driving environment. Vision sensors, in particular, are able to gather a multitude of information on the environment through the use of color and shape recognition in captured images.

In order to control the AGV using visual cues, such as those found in traffic light signage, it is necessary to detect and analyze these signals. The Faster Regions with Convolutional Neural Network features (Faster R-CNN) is a commonly used method for detecting signs, while RGB color space can be utilized to analyze color symbolism. However, using only RGB color space can be insufficient. Thus, the proposed method combines RGB and CIE L*a*b* color space to improve the effectiveness of the analysis. 

Using the proposed method, the color of the extracted region is determined by the fuzzy inference system, which is based on RGB, CIE L*a*b* and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR). Experimental results confirm that this method successfully detects and analyzes color signs found in the driving environment. With the rise of autonomous technology, such developments are vital in ensuring the safe and efficient use of autonomous systems in various industries.

A self-driving system for an electric wheelchair needs to effectively estimate its location, identify the travelable area and determine the route. While indoor self-location can be estimated using wireless LAN or beacons, more accurate position estimation is needed for self-driving. Earlier research on self-driving electric wheelchairs has used LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) and laser range scanner methods; however, such research configurations are complex and lead to increased power consumption. In this study, we propose using smartphone images for deep learning-based position estimation, resulting in cost-effective self-driving solutions. We also integrated augmented reality (AR) markers and Bluetooth low-energy beacons to estimate position when challenges are encountered. The travel route is calculated with map information available within the system. Our experiments confirmed the success of the proposed system for self-driving an electric wheelchair from initial position to a destination. While our prototype boarded a GPU, we are working to incorporate the AI chip in smartphones for future smart system development.

Caching popular content on mobile devices is a promising technique for reducing backhaul data rate demand. However, both file placement and data exchange among devices can consume energy and impact caching utility. Therefore, this study focuses on optimizing caching in a cellular network served by one base station. Considering that devices can collect file segments from local storage, D2D links, and cellular links, this study aims to minimize the percentage of file segments collected from the BS by optimizing the file placement scheme at devices. To this end, a residual energy-aware file placement algorithm based on popularity distribution and causality of energy arrival is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the percentage of file segments collected from the BS in comparison to conventional caching methods.

The Internet of Things (IoT) provides users with access to a vast amount of data from a multitude of devices. This information is critical for understanding, managing, and improving processes. However, the volume of data generated by these devices requires resources for processing and transportation, which presents new challenges to the IoT. Two key factors, latency and energy consumption, must be considered when completing a task. When attempting to perform all processing at the device level, both metrics may be exceeded.

To mitigate these issues, cloud and fog computing concepts can be used. However, utilizing these concepts adds complexity and overhead to the system. This paper examines latency and communication tasks in a distributed IoT system and investigates the impact of cloud and fog offloading. We develop cost functions for the tasks examined and provide insights into tradeoffs and constraints in the scenario studied. Our methodology is applicable to a wide range of IoT systems, offering a more general analysis.

VM placement is widely used in various areas of resource management in cloud computing environments. However, previous work has failed to ensure sufficient efficiency to meet user requirements, including energy efficiency and cost efficiency. Moreover, most previous approaches did not consider multi-metrics based on the objective. To maximize energy efficiency, a decision method combining Fuzzy and AHP must be employed. Our simulations show that a hierarchical VM placement scheme is needed to meet user requirements. 

In this paper, we propose a VM energy-efficient placement (VMP) scheme based on the Fuzzy-AHP system for sustainable cloud computing. We demonstrate the efficiency of our proposed scheme by using static VMP schemes. By combining fuzzy logic and AHP, our approach can accurately and efficiently select the most energy-efficient VM placement plan. The simulations show that our proposed scheme greatly improves energy efficiency and meets user requirements. 

In conclusion, the proposed VMP scheme can provide sustainable cloud computing by achieving energy efficiency and cost efficiency simultaneously. This is achieved by combining the Fuzzy-AHP system with a hierarchical VM placement scheme. Our proposed scheme can be used in a practical cloud computing environment and can serve as a reference for future research in the field.

Bitcoin (BTC) is an internet-based world's top-ranking cryptocurrency. Among widespread cryptocurrencies available in the market, Bitcoin is most experienced by the people due to anonymity and transparency in the system. Daily trends in the Bitcoin market has gained popularity among the spectators, investors, consumers and many more. Bitcoin price data exhibit desirable properties where some classical time series prediction methods exploit the behavior, producing poor predictions and also lack a probabilistic interpretation. This paper conducts an in-depth study on evolution of Bitcoin and also a systematic review is done on various machine learning algorithms used for predicting the prices. Comparative analysis envisions to select optimal technique to forecast prices more precisely.

Content Delivery Networks (CDN) are regarded as important internet infrastructure that supports business on the Internet. Network latency has been identified as an important metric to improve the quality of service (QoS) of CDNs. Given the limitations to response times because of the geographic distance between servers and end-users, CDN providers have developed architectures such as Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB) and IP Anycast to realize fast responses. This study investigates how GSLB and IP Anycast contribute towards improving QoS from the users' perspective. User traffic in the campus network was analyzed and it was found that: 1) 88% of the traffic reaps the benefits of well operated internet services, i.e., they have a Round-Trip Time (RTT) of less than 100 milliseconds. 2) Although GSLB is still the primary architecture for realizing fast responses, IP Anycast supports 5.8% of the traffic.

The article describes a unique method of processing scanned point cloud on a moving object with variable speed. Point clouds represent a set of trucks loaded by a scanning gate made up of four 2D laser scanners. Three scanners record the surface of the truck from three sides, the fourth scanner records the longitudinal change of the profile of one of a truck's side. From this profile, the method evaluates the motion movement function by which all other point clouds are recalculated. The result is a modified point clouds representing the surface of the standing set. The article also provides a way of point segmentation that separates the points representing the timber load from the truck.

Computer aided diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) by using the multi-modality imaging data is a challenging task and a topic of keen interest in the recent years. Feature representation plays a vital role in diagnosis. In previous studies, deep learning (DL) has been a great success in the field of feature representation learning. However, DL methods still need to overcome the issues of overfitting and data insufficiency. In the current study, we propose a stacked sparse auto-encoder (SSAE) based feature encoding algorithm. The proposed SSAE effectively trains on a small-scale data and computes the significant feature representation for PD diagnosis. The feature representation is learned via longitudinal multi-modal neuroimaging data for PD diagnosis. We first train and test the baseline data with the 10-fold cross-validation method, then we exploit the baseline data to train a classification model to complete the classification task in future time points. A number of experiments are carried out to verify the effectiveness of our method on the publicly available Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed method works efficiently on a small dataset and achieves significant classification results as compared to existing common DL methods.

This paper proposes a linearization technique for third-order input intercept point (IIP3) improvement in subthreshold low noise amplifiers (LNAs). The proposed LNA is designed for 2.4 GHz radio-frequency wireless receiver front-ends for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. A novel modified derivative superposition technique is presented for the linearization of subthreshold LNAs. In this technique, the main transistors are biased in the weak inversion region, while the auxiliary transistor in the feed-forward path is biased in the strong inversion region, for third-order non-linearity cancellation. With a DC power consumption of 503 μW from a supply voltage of 0.9 V, the LNA delivers an IIP3 of -0.77 dBm, a noise figure of 2.42 dB, and 12.36 dB of power gain. The LNA was designed using UMC 90 nm RF CMOS technology.

The incidence of arc faults in aircrafts is a common problem which requires prompt diagnosis and exclusion. One of the main causes of this issue is the poor working environment of the cable. At present, research on detecting and studying AC fault characteristics and detection algorithms relies heavily on experimental data. However, AC arc fault experimental data is random, and this necessitates a study on AC arc modeling.

This paper aims to research AC arc modeling based on the simplified Schavemaker model. As values of model parameters vary depending on working conditions, and calculation methods tend to be complex, inaccurate, and require dependence on experimental data, this paper first proposes a calculation method based on easy-to-operate experimental data with high accuracy. The second calculation method, based on a neural network, uses the first method to obtain training samples. A neural network between the model parameters and the working conditions is constructed. Finally, by comparing the experimental data and simulation results, the accuracy of the proposed calculating method for the model's parameters as well as the AC arc model are verified.

In sum, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the ongoing development of reliable detection and exclusion methods for arc faults in aircrafts. By focusing on AC arc modeling, this paper offers an innovative and practical solution for optimizing the performance and safety of aircrafts.

This paper presents a loop antenna for deep implant powering in an intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring application. This work is continuation of our on-going development of a wirelessly powered implantable system for ICP monitoring. Experimental results indicate that the implant can be activated until the depth of 19 mm from the skin. This is 8 mm more than our previous work where we were able to activate the implant until 11 mm depth from the skin. Moreover, we have also presented pressure readout experimental results with the proposed antenna.

Pose estimation of 3D objects in six degrees of freedom has been a topic of interest in the research community for quite some time now. The integration of cameras and robots in a system enables the estimation of an object's pose through the camera, enabling it to be accurately manipulated by the robot. Traditional object pose estimation methods include template matching-based and invariant feature-based methods. While the method based on invariant features performs well on images with rich texture, it is not suitable for texture-less parts, which are commonplace in industrial applications. On the other hand, the template-matching method based on edge and contour information is better suited for industrial part detection and pose estimation. LINEMOD, proposed by Hinterstoisser, is a well-known and successful template-matching method that utilizes a specially designed storage structure to accelerate the template matching process. However, the template-based matching method is generally computationally intensive and therefore impractical for robotic applications. 

This paper presents a new method that combines Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) with LINEMOD algorithm. With this method, the detection and location of the object in the image can be quickly achieved, and the local image is used for LINEMOD template matching, instead of the entire image. Experimental results indicate that this approach results in increased pose estimation speed and consistent matching results when compared to the standard LINEMOD method.

Multi-view hashing is an effective method for large-scale near-duplicate video retrieval due to its low storage cost, fast retrieval speed, and the mutual reinforcement of multiple features. However, there are still limitations that hinder its performance. Existing methods only consider local structures within the features, and ignore the global structures that are important for near-duplicate video retrieval. Additionally, current works learn hashing functions bit by bit, which increases the time complexity of the function learning process.

To address these issues, this paper proposes a supervised hashing scheme called joint multi-view hashing (JMVH).
