In this paper, it is verified experimentally for the decoupled vector control of GSC, where, the positive and negative sequence voltages are decoupled through DDSRF while currents are decoupled through enhanced DDSRF methods in the respective dq-axes. It is implemented experimentally using TI-2407A DSP controller.

The technological development of the energy sector also produced complex data. In this study, the relationship between smart grid and big data approaches have been investigated. After analyzing which areas of the smart grid system use big data technologies and technologies, big data technologies for detecting smart grid attacks have received attention. Big data analytics can produce efficient solutions and it is especially important to choose which algorithms and metrics to use. For this reason, an application prototype has been proposed that uses a big data method to detect attacks on the smart grid. The algorithm with high accuracy was determined to be 92% for random forests and 87% for decision trees.

This paper presents an investigation of the electrothermomechanical (ETM) phenomena in a multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB) under heat cycle aggression using an original multiphysics KB modeling approach. The study analyzes the coupled thermal and intrinsic mechanical interactions, as well as the PCB electrical response. The via-interconnect line (IL) junction fatigue caused by mechanical tensions is explained using tensorial equations. The ETM effects transduced between the PCB components are modeled using equivalent graphs, and the problem's general tensorial relation is formulated. To validate the Kron-Branin model, the study introduces a numerical application of a three-layer PCB proof-of-concept under thermal cycle aggression with a varying temperature range of 0-to-70 °C. The tensile stresses induced by the thermal effect on the vias and ILs are calculated, and the via cracking fatigue model is approximated. The paper also discusses the PCB voltage transfer function and input impedance in the function of the thermal aggression.

In recent years, the electric load power forecasting (ELPF) has become an essential activity in power systems. As per ELPF literatures, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique based models are more accurate than any other. Hence this technique with new framework for day-ahead ELPF which includes features of calendar, weather and lagged load of previous day in time domain is chosen. This research paper is mainly focused to deal with the selection of best suitable weather feature from many weather variables with calendar and lagged load features as constants. The real time data used for this research work were collected from Tata Power Delhi Distribution Utility (TPDDL). The correlation analysis of ELP with respect to each selected feature is performed and presented. Then, suitable framework for development of models is created. The performance criteria for ELPF are chosen and for better understanding, the experimental results are presented with the help of histogram and bar charts. The proposed models produce an average forecast error of 2.6% to 3.3% per hourly samples throughout the year irrespective of seasonal and weather variations. The proposed models are proven for their simplicity, less measurement requirement and easiness in implementation with higher accuracy.

Data security and privacy are of great concern for users of cloud computing. In order to provide such guarantees in public clouds, hardware manufacturers have designed trusted execution environments such as Intel’s Software Guard eXtensions (SGX). Intel SGX supports privacy-preserving, tamper-proof containments called enclaves. Regrettably, an SGX enclave has to rely on the untrusted operating system or hypervisor for underlying services, which contradicts the threat model of Intel SGX. Whereas much of the previous work concentrates on protecting trusted applications by means of modifying a hypervisor, we tackle the problem by reusing existing drivers and leveraging processor-enforced protection. We propose a novel approach, named SMK, to provide trusted system services for SGX enclaves. SMK leverages existing Intel architecture features, i.e., System Management Mode (SMM) and Uniform Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI). Specifically, we retrofit UEFI firmware and design an isolated micro-kernel inside SMM to securely provision critical system services for enclaves. To highlight the effectiveness and extensibility of SMK, we implement two system services: trusted clock and trusted network. Furthermore, we harden two real-world security-sensitive applications, OpenSSL and OpenVPN, with SMK’s system services. Our evaluation indicates that SMK can supply trusted system services for enclaves with modest runtime overheads.

The depletion of fossil fuels and concern for environmental issues such as air pollution and global warming have led to increased research in developing innovative alternatives in engineering systems. This study aims to minimize the life cycle cost (as an economic criterion) of an air conditioning system using vapor compression technology, as well as maximizing the useful heat (as a thermodynamic criterion). 

The mathematical model utilized in this study includes four decision variables: the evaporation and condensation temperatures of the refrigerant, and the volumetric flow rate of air in both the condenser and evaporator. This global optimization problem is solved using a genetic algorithm. A thermodynamic model was utilized that included the design of the exchanger. 

The methodology used in this study focuses on R-1234yf, a low GWP refrigerant that is intended to substitute R-134a refrigerant. This approach aims to offer a more sustainable solution to air conditioning systems while simultaneously reducing costs through efficient design.

A procedure based on compressed sensing (CS) is proposed for speech enhancement. The latter is Prior-noise-estimation free. This approach is motivated by the fact that CS allows the recovery of only the sparse signal in the presence of non-sparse signal (noise). An application to an Arabic speech signal corrupted with white Gaussian noise is studied. Comparison of CS-based enhancement with three state-of-the-art methods is performed in terms of segmental SNR, root mean square error, and perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ); and proved promising performances.

We propose a battery-less location tracking system that enables 3-D positioning of an Internet of Things (IoT) device powered by the radio frequency (RF) wireless power transfer (WPT). In the proposed system, a power beacon is equipped with a phased antenna array that has the dual purposes of high-efficiency WPT and phase-based accurate positioning. In order to enhance the efficiency of the RF WPT, we propose a beam focusing algorithm that dynamically controls the respective phases of antenna elements to place the focal point of the electro-magnetic (EM) wave onto the target IoT device. We also propose a phase-based positioning algorithm that requires only one multi-antenna anchor point for determining the distance as well as the direction from the anchor point. We analyze the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) of the phase-based positioning with a single multi-antenna anchor point, and show that the distance from the anchor point can be estimated as long as the IoT device lies within the radiative near-field region. We propose a joint location tracking and WPT algorithm that performs 3-D positioning and beam-focused WPT in a unified way. We have built a real-life testbed with a large-scale antenna array with 64 antenna elements for testing the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in a real environment.

In many neural applications such as brain-machine-interfaces and long-term brain stimulation, neural dynamics can be non-stationary. Adaptive modeling is a useful approach for tracking these non-stationarities. Prior work has tracked time-variant linear state-space models to describe human electrocorticogram dynamics. However, the forgetting factor, a key design parameter in adaptive identification, has not been systematically studied. 

In this study, comprehensive numerical simulations were used to investigate the effect of the forgetting factor on identifying time-variant linear state-space models. Non-stationary neural activity was simulated using time-variant linear state-space models, and different forgetting factors were used to track and predict the activity. The results showed that the prediction accuracy strongly varied with the choice of the forgetting factor. Additionally, the optimal forgetting factor that led to the highest prediction accuracy varied as a function of various properties of the simulated time-variant linear state-space models.

These findings have important implications for building more accurate adaptive models to track non-stationary neural network dynamics. They also facilitate the investigation of neural non-stationarity using adaptive models.

In this paper, we propose a sequence-to-sequence NMT model on Farsi-Spanish bilingually low-resource language pair. We apply effective preprocessing steps specific for Farsi language and optimize the model for both translation and transliteration. We also propose a loss function that enhances the word alignment and consequently improves translation quality.

Electricity demand is a vital factor in the development of economies today. To meet the needs of customers and support daily electrical demand, companies and electricity operators rely on powerful and precise forecasting tools. PREVEOS-DZ is one such solution that was designed and implemented to predict short and mid-term electrical energy and power demand. This forecast system enables operators to plan their day-to-day production planning and yearly electrical development established by the Algerian Operator System. PREVEOS-DZ utilizes the multiple regression approach, as well as Artificial Neural Networks, especially for power forecasting, and provides models for both paradigms. Moreover, this software is implemented not only for global national forecasts but also for regional demands, even if the electrical grid is fully connected. Developed using C #, PREVEOS-DZ is fully compatible with Excel tabular, which is the preferred choice of the system operator. The results obtained from the PREVEOS-DZ proof-of-concept exercise were validated on data from 2018, which is presented in this paper.

This paper attempts to investigate novel Text-to-Speech algorithm based on Deep voice which is an attention based, fully convolutional mechanism. The procedure of producing speech synthesis involves with learning statistical model of the human vocal production mechanism which is eligible of taking some text and vocalize that as speech. This paper would reveal the route of the attempt where there is the destination of accuracy and realism. Serenity and fluency are the most important qualities which expect from a TTS. The idea is to give an outline of discourse amalgamation in the Sinhala language, compresses and replicates about the characteristics of different blend procedures utilized. The proposed TTS synthesizing with the neural network based approach to perform phonetic-to-acoustic mapping has described by the purpose of applying for multilingual synthesizers.

Matrix completion is a fundamental problem in image processing, where the aim is to recover an incomplete matrix from its observed entries. One popular approach to this problem is to treat it as a low-rank matrix approximation problem. In a recent paper, a new regularization method called truncated Frobenius norm (TFN) was proposed, which was used in combination with a hybrid truncated norm (HTN) model for solving matrix completion problems. 

To address this model, a two-step iteration algorithm was designed, along with an adaptive way to adjust the penalty parameter to reduce computational costs. The convergence of the proposed method was also discussed and mathematically proven. 

The proposed approach not only improves the recovery performance but also promotes the stability of the model. It eliminates large variations that exist when estimating complex models and achieves competitive success in matrix completion. 

Experimental results on synthetic data, real-world images, and recommendation systems confirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. The statistical analysis strategy used in the experiments showed that the proposed method is more stable and effective than other state-of-the-art approaches.

Tactile Internet can be seen as the next wave of innovation, which has the characteristics of low latency, high reliability, availability, and security. Tactile Internet promises its application in various fields ranging from industry automation and transport systems to healthcare, education, and gaming. Therefore, in this paper, we present the application of tactile Internet in healthcare by considering the diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) as a use case, which is a potentially life-threatening complication of diabetes mellitus. Severe DKA causes Kussmaul breathing, which is a life-threatening condition that usually requires hospitalization. However, to date, no real-time monitoring system exists for DKA. In this paper, we propose a nonintrusive breathing monitoring system using the C-Band sensing technique. The system exploits a microwave sensing platform to capture breathing-induced chest movements in diabetic patients. A peak detection algorithm is used to acquire the respiratory rate and extent, identified as normal breathing or Kussmaul breathing. The real-time respiratory rate and extent could be used to diagnose DKA in diabetic patients. The accuracy for all the subjects are 99.76%, 98.69%, 97.82%, 99.06%, and 98.42%, respectively; therefore, the reliability of the system is demonstrated.

Early detection of seismic events is fundamental to mitigate the damages produced by these natural phenomena, and mainly, save lives. In this paper, logistic regression models were applied to distinguish between seismic and non-seismic local events considering data segments from four seismological stations (epicenter in the Santander department, Colombia) of the National Seismological Network of Colombia. The classification outputs obtained by each individual classifier were then combined using voting functions. For each station, Degree of Polarization, Ratio of Vertical power to Total power, Skewness and Kurtosis of the three-component seismic data were extracted. Results showed that the best individual classifier achieved an accuracy of 95% and reaches an accuracy of 98% using voting functions. This classifier is the first step in the development of alert mechanisms for the early detection of seismic events in Colombia.

Segmentation of breast tumors is a crucial step in the diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer. However, this task can be challenging and time-consuming for radiologists, leading to a need for automated approaches. To address this, we propose a deep learning-based method for automatic segmentation of breast tumors in DCE-MRI data.

Our approach is based on a U-net fully convolutional neural network architecture, which can handle both detection and segmentation on each single breast slice. We trained and validated the model on a dataset of 86 DCE-MRI scans, consisting of 5452 slices acquired before and after chemotherapy from 43 patients with local breast cancer. The dataset was manually annotated by an experienced radiologist.

Our trained model achieved a mean Intersection-over-Union (IoU) of 76.14%, demonstrating its effectiveness in segmenting breast tumors. Overall, our study suggests that deep learning-based approaches can help automate the segmentation of breast tumors, reducing the workload for radiologists and potentially improving the accuracy of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment.

The classification algorithms were developed to label the objects with the same characteristics into similar groups. In Arabic poetry, poems belong to different eras based on the time they were written in. Changes in time resulted in changes in the style of writing Arabic poetry. Hence, this study is testing the use of different classification algorithms to discover their ability to classify poems in their correct era. This process can be automated by studying the linguistic changes that happened to the Arabic poetry in terms of the words used in the hemistichs structure (part of poem line) without considering poems rhyme. In this paper, we studied applying different classification algorithms to discover poems written in the Abbasid and Andalusian eras. Data have been collected and classifiers have been trained on an overall dataset that contains 30,058 words from 10,895 poetic hemistich collected from both eras. The experiments obtained 70.50% accuracy rate using the support vector machine classifier when tested with a sample of random poem lines. The study showed that it is possible to distinguish, with decent accuracy, poems from different eras based on identifying discriminant features that can be used in the classification.

Cloud simulation has long been an important research field in computer graphics, serving essential roles in applications ranging from weather forecasting and flight simulation to big game scenes. However, creating large-scale cloud simulations, especially realistic and interactive clouds, poses a significant challenge. 

To address this challenge, a new method for efficiently simulating interactive large-scale clouds in games has been proposed. This method involves combining 2D clouds with 3D volume clouds to create a more realistic effect. 

Overall, this innovative approach holds great promise for improving cloud simulation in computer graphics and has the potential to significantly enhance weather forecasting accuracy, flight simulation realism, and gameplay experiences in big game scenes.

This paper presents a new method for combining compact descriptors to improve recognition performance. Using multiple kernel learning (MKL), the method optimally learns which features to use for prediction. However, traditional MKL models are limited in scalability due to high memory and computational requirements. To address this, the authors propose SVRG-MKL, a new approach that combines MKL with a stochastic variance reduced gradient method. This method allows for the combination of millions of samples, performs optimization with a linear complexity algorithm, and avoids unnecessary memory allocation. Experimental results demonstrate improved accuracy and faster convergence compared to other methods. The proposed technique shows promise for other MKL applications, including visual search and transfer learning.

The Telecommunications Engineering program at Macquarie University is currently undergoing a renewal. The School of Engineering is transforming its pedagogy while Macquarie University is restructuring its curriculum. This study aims to examine the impact of the changes in Telecommunications Engineering education at the university.

The changes include an update in technical content using a project-based learning (PBL) approach, project ownership, the replacement of traditional lectures, virtual laboratories, and an emphasis on software tools and programming skills. This means students will learn by working on real-world problems, taking ownership of projects, and developing the skills they need to succeed in the industry.

The transformation of the pedagogy is expected to bring a positive impact on students' learning experience. The PBL approach will enable students to gain hands-on experience in addressing complex problems. Students will become actively engaged in learning as they work to solve practical problems, promoting the development of analytical and problem-solving skills.

Moreover, the use of virtual laboratories and software tools should enhance the students' learning experience. Instead of learning through simulations, students will have the opportunity to work with real-world problems, use real tools, and gain industry experience. The focus on programming skills will also give students a valuable set of skills in the job market.

In conclusion, the renewal of Telecommunications Engineering education at Macquarie University is a positive move. The changes in pedagogy and curriculum structure will provide students with a more meaningful learning experience, preparing them for success in the industry. The use of project-based learning, virtual laboratories, and software tools will enhance the students' ability to solve problems, while also improving their programming skills.

It is very important to strengthen the management of medical insurance and guarantee the steady operation of medical insurance fund. Data mining technology can provide an effective solution for medical aggregation behavior mining. It is helpful to find out the people who have the gathering behavior of medical treatment. In view of the aggregation behavior of medical insurance funds during operation, this study proposes the consistent behavior mining algorithm based on frequent pattern mining. Experiments show that this algorithm has better performance than Apriori and Eclat, can effectively detect the aggregation behavior of medical insurance, and has achieved remarkable results in the management and supervision of medical insurance.

The development of the human brain is a complex process that begins during early pregnancy and continues until the end of adolescence. Alongside changes in brain size and gyrification, various microstructural changes occur in the cortex, including dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis and pruning, and fiber myelination. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides indirect markers of these changes through the mapping of quantitative parameters. To explore this further, we utilized a robust methodological framework to conduct reliable voxel-wise analyses over the infant cortex. In doing so, we were able to investigate hemispheric asymmetries in microstructure while simultaneously accounting for morphological asymmetries through a 2-step matching process. Specifically, the DISCO approach aligned sulci, while the DARTEL approach registered cortical ribbons. We focused on longitudinal diffusivity, as measured by Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI), in infants between the ages of 1 and 5 months. This allowed us to identify distinct microstructural evolution patterns in specific sensorimotor and language regions within the left and right hemispheres.

Human action recognition for automated video surveillance applications is an interesting but a daunting task especially if the videos are captured in unfavourable lighting conditions. These situations encourage the use of multi-sensor video streams. However, simultaneous activity recognition from multiple video streams is a difficult problem due to their complementary and noisy nature. This paper proposes simultaneous action recognition from multiple video streams using deep multi-view representation learning. Furthermore, it introduces a spatio-temporal feature based correlation filter, for simultaneous detection and recognition of multiple human actions in low-light conditions. We evaluated the performance of our proposed filter with extensive experimentation on nighttime action datasets. Experimental results indicate the effectiveness of deep fusion scheme for robust action recognition in extremely low-light conditions.

Autonomous robot manipulation involves estimating the translation and orientation of the object to be manipulated as a 6-degree-of-freedom (6D) pose. Methods using RGB-D data have shown great success in solving this problem. However, there are situations where cost constraints or the working environment may limit the use of RGB-D sensors. When limited to monocular camera data only, the problem of object pose estimation is very challenging. In this letter, we introduce a novel method called SilhoNet that predicts 6D object pose from monocular images. We use a convolutional neural network pipeline that takes in region of interest proposals to simultaneously predict an intermediate silhouette representation for objects with an associated occlusion mask and a 3D translation vector. The 3D orientation is then regressed from the predicted silhouettes. We show that our method achieves better overall performance on the YCB-Video dataset than two networks for 6D pose estimation from monocular image input.

To achieve high computational throughput, heterogeneous architectures utilize many special-purpose cores as floating point computing coprocessors. Typically, programming models offload computing intensive operations to coprocessors and then aggregate results, resulting in the need to transfer a large amount of data via the peripheral component interconnect express (PCIe). To overcome this limitation, a reverse offload (rOffload) model has been developed. In this model, the autonomous Intel Many Integrated Core (MIC) coprocessor is treated as the host processor, while the CPU is treated as the coprocessor. The MICs orchestrate the computation and offload work, which cannot be accelerated on MIC, to the CPUs. This reduces overhead introduced by moving data among distinct memory regions. This paper provides an overview of rOffload, including the basic programming interface and its implementation on a CPU-MIC system. Results from benchmarking and application experiments on the Tianhe-2 supercomputer demonstrate the efficiency of our rOffload model in terms of programmability, portability, and performance.

Shadows bring great challenges but also play essential roles in image understanding. Most recent shadow detection methods are based on patches, then further reasoning method is required for the obtaining of a completed shadow detection result for an image. In this paper, an injection network is proposed to detect shadow regions for the whole image directly. In order to maintain as many as details, the skip structure is applied to directly inject the details from convolutional layers to de-convolutional layers. Meanwhile, a weighted loss function is proposed for the network training. With this adapted loss function, the network becomes more sensitive to errors of shadow regions. Thus the proposed network can focus on the learning of robust shadow features. Furthermore, a shadow refinement method is proposed to optimize the boundary region of shadows. In the experiments, the proposed methods are extensively evaluated on two popular datasets and shown better performance on shadow detection compared with current methods.

This paper is focused on addressing the time synchronization problem in a large database business network. The communication times can be a hindrance to functioning optimally, therefore, to minimize communication intervals, an event-triggered control protocol is proposed based on the second-order multi-agent system. For every agent, a distributed triggering condition is used to decide the appropriate communication timing. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated through simulation results presented in this paper.

Service migration is crucial in leveraging cloud resources for efficient execution of mobile applications in pervasive cloud computing. To optimize service executions and achieve accurate prediction of cloud resources, this paper proposes a service migration approach called LSTM4PCC, which is based on the long and short-term memory model (LSTM). LSTM4PCC employs a LSTM network to predict cloud resource availability and establish a service migration mechanism. 

To evaluate the performance of LSTM4PCC, we compared it with the AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) approach in terms of prediction accuracy. The results indicated that LSTM4PCC outperformed ARIMA. 

Overall, our LSTM4PCC approach can effectively predict cloud resource availability and optimize service migration for pervasive cloud computing, leading to better execution of mobile applications.

The synchronization control problem for a class of nonlinear complex dynamical networks with network attacks and actuator faults is addressed in this paper. The main contributions are as follows: (1) The developed controller is capable of compensating for nonlinearity and actuator faults simultaneously; (2) Compared with existing network attacks results, the input matrix considered in this paper is more general. To be more specific, by approximating the nonlinear uncertainty by a fuzzy logical system (FLS), a new FLS-based distributed adaptive controller is developed. By virtue of estimating the norm of weight vector in the FLS, the developed controller can compensate for the effect of nonlinearity under actuator faults. By using matrix factorization technique and sliding mode control method, the developed method is shown to be resilient to network attacks. Moreover, it is proven that the developed controller can guarantee asymptotic convergent of synchronisation errors. Finally, an illustrative example is used to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

This work describes the implementation of a machine learning (ML) strategy based on the neural network for real-time range-adaptive automatic impedance matching of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) applications. This approach for the effective prediction of the optimal parameters of the tunable matching network and classification range-adaptive transmitter coils (Tx) is introduced in this paper aiming to achieve an effective automatic impedance matching over a wide range of relative distances. We propose a WPT system consisting of a tunable matching circuit and 3 Tx coils which have different radius controlled by trained neural network models. The feedforward neural network algorithm was trained using 220 data and classifier's in pattern recognition accuracy were characterized. The proposed approach achieves a Power transfer efficiency (PTE) around 90% for ranges within 10 to 25cm, is reported.

This paper presents a study on the acoustic modeling of child speech for large vocabulary speech recognition of Cantonese. This research was conducted with the aid of a new speech corpus, CUChild127, which was collected for developing acoustic assessment systems for speech sound disorders in Cantonese-speaking children. The corpus comprises 127 Chinese words spoken by 1,500 preschoolers in Hong Kong. To train the system, a small amount of manually transcribed child speech was utilized to initiate a GMM-HMM based speech recognition system that was later used to transcribe a large amount of training data. The researchers adopted a multi-task learning approach to train a conventional DNN model and a time-delay neural network (TDNN) model. The primary task was context-dependent phone modelling for child speech, while the secondary task was context-dependent phone modelling for adult speech. The training data for adult speech were obtained from an existing phonetically rich speech corpus. The experimental results proved that the TDNN-based acoustic model significantly outperforms DNN and GMM-HMM systems. Moreover, multi-task learning improved the performance of the TDNN model even further. With the weights of primary and secondary tasks at 0.8 and 0.2, respectively, the best syllable error rate achieved in the experiments was 8.96%.

Leveraging high-performance software-defined networks (SDNs) to manage industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices has become a promising trend; the SDN is expected to be the next generation as a unified and virtualized network platform that provides unprecedented automation, flexibility, and efficiency. As the core of business applications and sensitive data storage, the SDN is vulnerable to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks in IIoT environment that numerous requests are sent to the SDN to interrupt its services. In the traditional defense systems, honeypots have shown great promises in resisting DDoS attacks. In this paper, we reveal a new attack that can identify honeypots to invalidate their protection. In addition, we analyze the optimal strategies of attackers, so that they can find the best time to carry on attacks. To protect SDN from such a kind of anti-honeypot attacks, we propose a pseudo-honeypot game (PHG) strategy with theoretical performance guarantee. We prove several groups of Bayesian-Nash Equilibrium in the PHG strategy. Moreover, we show that these strategies can achieve the optimal equilibrium between legitimate users and attackers. The proposed honeypot strategies can provide dynamic protection for SDN. Hence, malicious attacks under our strategies can be effectively controlled. Finally, we evaluate our proposals on a testbed, and experimental results show that our proposals can effectively resist DDoS attacks with lower energy consumption compared with the existing methods.

More than 50 percent of building energy consumption in Thailand comes from air conditioning (AC), which highlights the significance of managing AC energy consumption in buildings. In this study, a three-level AC energy consumption concept for Building Energy Management System (BEMS) using a data mining framework is presented. The method combines unsupervised and supervised learning techniques, where K-means is utilized to determine levels of energy consumption, and decision trees are utilized to map the relationship between energy consumption level and key variables. A case study is presented by using data from Chulalongkorn University's Building Energy Management System (CU-BEMS). Finally, the results of the method are used to develop an algorithm for automatic AC control to enhance energy saving.

Global surrogate models are presented for antenna elements in large phased arrays, to cheaply and accurately model scan-dependent impedance and radiation responses for systems with wide-angle scanning requirements. Adaptive sampling combined with rational and Kriging interpolation is found to produce accurate, convergent models within 50 full-wave EM simulations of a patch element within a planar PBC unit cell.

We consider the distributed secondary voltage control problem for microgrids subject to delays in a connected communication topology. For each distributed generator (DG), a distributed event-triggered control law, which uses its own voltage and those of its neighbors, along with a strategy for its triggering, are designed. Under these distributed event-triggered control laws, the magnitudes of the output voltages of all DGs can be synchronized to their reference value subject to a bounded time-varying delay that can be arbitrarily large, and no Zeno behavior will occur. The simulation results illustrate the theoretical conclusions.

Over the past few decades, there has been a significant rise in the computer processing power that has been supporting the increased sophistication of sensors. This growth in technology has resulted in more accurate data points for control, leading to the impression that expert systems would be more effective and in greater demand. Despite such advancements, many companies and plants have found it challenging to capitalize on the benefits of expert control systems. Expert control has been identified as a means to enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and lower emission levels. However, achieving these targets can prove to be difficult if the expert system is not well understood or if the prerequisites for success are not followed.

This paper aims to explore the issues that may hinder the operation of expert control systems. Additionally, the paper provides guidelines on how to optimize existing expert control systems and outlines the prerequisites for companies planning to install expert control systems.

In conclusion, while expert control systems have the potential to enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and lessen emission levels, their implementation requires a thorough understanding of the system itself and the prerequisites necessary to achieve success. By following the guidelines provided in this paper, companies can maximize the benefits they receive from their expert control systems and use them to gain a competitive edge in their industry.

This document presents a learning system architecture for the practice of the cannulation procedure for medical students in cardiovascular specialization. The architecture is composed of three modules that support the practice and learning of this surgical procedure; surgical instrumentation, hygiene and simulation of the cannulation. The architecture rests on different multimedia technologies that allow an autonomous practice but that may be supervised by the teacher. In the document are discussed the context, the need for tools for this medical practice, an architectural design of the proposed system and a comparison with the current practices in medicine programs.

In this paper, we study the separability of the commonly used features to monitor the performance of optical signal in coherent optical systems. Specifically, our study focuses on the histogram-based features; the asynchronous amplitude histogram (AAH) and the two-dimensional extension of AAH, which we call IQ histogram (IQH). We investigate the conditions under which the optical channel impairments can be monitored. This study utilizes a dimensionality reduction technique, known as the t-distribution stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE). Using t-SNE, we show that under certain conditions the histogram-based features cannot be used to distinguish between the high and low impairment effects, rendering these features useless for certain cases, regardless of the type or complexity of the implemented impairments' estimator/classifier. Extensive simulations results have been conducted to investigate single and multiple impairments conditions and the performance of histogram-based features in each case. The results show that both AAH and IQH can be used for monitoring all types of single Impairment except phase noise in case of AAH. Moreover, under multiple impairments conditions, polarization mode dispersion values can be monitored to some extent, while it is difficult to monitor optical signal-to-noise ratio and chromatic dispersion values especially in the case of concurrent presence of more than two impairments. The results of these investigations are validated by providing a quantitative measure that ties their usefulness to the actual monitoring performance through the estimation of channel impairments under different conditions using linear support vector machine (SVM) regression. It has been found that there is a match to a great extent between the separability investigation using t-SNE and estimation results obtained using SVM.

Computational thinking is a necessary skill for human life. However, promoting this competency in primary school students sometimes is hard and difficult for instructors. This article proposes a learning approach based on the use of a platform as part of a strategy of computational thinking to enhance learning of geometry. A case study was performed with primary school children from fourth grade at the Comfacor School (Montería-Colombia). The aim of the study was to analyze the effects of the approach in the children's motivation and performance.

In this study, we propose a technique for classifying ghost moving detections in automotive radar sensors as part of advanced driver assistance systems. To achieve this, we adopted a fully connected network to differentiate between genuine and false moving detections in the occupancy gridmaps. Using this network, we integrate the local Doppler information with the spatial context of the surrounding environment to accurately classify the moving detections. 

The proof of concept experiment yielded very promising results when tested in an urban scenario. Therefore, we believe that our proposed approach can effectively enhance the performance of automotive radar sensors in detecting real-time moving objects.

Edge clouds pose significant challenges to resource allocation and load balancing due to the unpredictability of user mobility, server load, and network state. To address these issues, dynamic resource migration techniques are essential for achieving fault tolerance, load balance, and system maintenance objectives. Container migration is emerging as a promising solution that enables dynamic resource migration in virtualized networks and mobile edge cloud (MEC) systems.

This paper proposes a traffic aware container migration approach and validates it with an end-to-end system implementation using a pure container hypervisor called LXD. The container migration model is evaluated for real-time applications such as license plate recognition, which is run in a mobile edge cloud scenario based on city-scale mobility traces from taxicabs in San Francisco. The evaluation considers key metrics associated with application quality-of-experience (QoE) and network efficiency, such as the average system response time and the migration cost for different combinations of load, compute resources, inter-edge cloud bandwidth, network, and user latency.

To optimize resource allocation and network efficiency, a specific compute resource and network-aware distributed resource migration algorithm called “ShareOn” is proposed and compared with alternative techniques using the San Francisco MEC model. Overall, the proposed approach demonstrates significant improvements in QoE and network efficiency, making it a promising solution for edge cloud resource allocation and load balancing challenges.

This paper presents a model for gesture recognition that utilizes the latest open-source Tensorflow framework by Google. The authors introduce the platform characteristics of Tensorflow and propose a convolution network model that is based on this framework. To evaluate the performance of the model, the authors conduct experiments using both recognized and self-collected datasets. The results indicate that the model achieves high recognition accuracy, strong robustness, and high computational efficiency. In addition, the Tensorflow framework allows for easy adjustment of the network structure, enabling quick identification of the optimal model and better accomplishment of the task of gesture recognition.

Lung volume segmentation is a crucial step in developing computer-aided diagnosis systems for automatic lung pathology analysis. However, it can be challenging to isolate the lungs from CT scans due to significant deformations and the potential presence of pathologies. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective tools for modeling the spatial relationship between lung voxels. However, training a CNN requires a large quantity of annotated data, and manually delineating the lungs from volumetric CT scans is a cumbersome process. To solve this task, we propose training a 3D CNN based on semi-automatically generated annotations. To achieve this, we introduce an extension to the well-known V-Net architecture that can handle higher-dimensional input data. Even with noisy and erroneous training set labels, we demonstrate through experimentation that it is possible to learn to accurately segment the lungs. Numerical comparisons on an external test set, containing lung segmentations provided by a medical expert, demonstrate that the proposed model can generalize well to new data – reaching an average Dice coefficient of 98.7%. The proposed approach results in superior performance compared to the standard V-Net model, particularly on the lung boundary.

Due to the diversity of redundant configuration schemes, the existing calibration algorithm for the redundant inertial measurement unit (RIMU) cannot be universally applied. In addition, the linearized calibration model used in traditional methods results in low calibration accuracy. This paper proposes a high-precision calibration scheme for the RIMU that is universally applicable.

The proposed scheme first establishes a general calibration model for the RIMU. To improve system observability, a zero-space amplification algorithm is then employed. Finally, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) based on the second-order Taylor series expansion is proposed for simultaneous estimation of biases, scale factor errors, and installation errors.

Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed calibration algorithm calibrates the system accurately and effectively improves the performance of the RIMU. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm's versatility allows it to be applied universally in all types of RIMU.

Various standards for intelligent medical systems and multimodal architecture interfaces are currently being reviewed. The proposal is to utilize the Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resource (FHIR) standard for the data model of intelligent multimodal interfaces. As an example, an intelligent multimodal interface for EEG and accelerometer bio-signals based on FHIR has been presented.

To further illustrate the development of this interface, use case diagrams, resource diagrams, and class diagrams for both the production and research modes have been described. By incorporating the FHIR standard, this intelligent multimodal interface can facilitate efficient and secure data exchange between healthcare providers and researchers. This could greatly enhance the diagnosis and treatment of various medical conditions.

Automatic gesture recognition is a crucial technology that can enhance the functionality of surgical robotic systems (SRSs) by enabling advanced assistance features. These features could include user-specific feedback, detection of safety-critical situations, and autonomous execution of procedure sub-steps. Video data are commonly available for minimally invasive surgical procedures, but SRS could also leverage kinematic data to provide accurate movement measurements. Kinematic data can be used to identify low-dimensional features for gesture recognition, enabling on-line processing during data acquisition. To introduce temporal modeling in gesture recognition, we propose the use of a Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN) applied to kinematic data. We assessed the precision and accuracy of this method on a public benchmark dataset for surgical gesture recognition (JIGSAWS) and introduced a new dataset that provides a different training exercise executed in a virtual environment to evaluate the method’s generalization capability. The dataset is publicly available for future testing of other methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is comparable to other methods currently available in literature and can be used for on-line processing during surgical procedures, making it a valuable tool for the automation of SRSs with advanced situation awareness capabilities.

To promote efficient and flexible learning, a conceptual learning model can be developed using the differences between the stable features of various concepts, thereby allowing scalable and continuous learning concepts to be obtained from a small number of labeled samples. By using a stable feature expressed as a vector to represent each concept, the conceptual learning model can distinguish the representative feature of each concept, thus increasing the interpretability of the model. In addition to adjusting the mapping relationship between concept instances and concept stability features, constraints on the differences between stable features of different concepts are also introduced into the model. Because this constraint can improve the sensitivity of the instance features to the stable features of each concept, the proposed model has the ability to learn from a small number of samples. In this paper, sub-networks of the same structure were applied to learn each concept, and unified learning methods were used to achieve scalability and the ability to easily manage new concepts. By training the proposed model using the MNIST dataset, the model demonstrates that prediction accuracy of 96% can be achieved as a result of using 100 labeled training samples for each concept. Furthermore, the proposed model not only demonstrated an improved learning ability for small samples, but it was also found to considerably reduce the training time, with each concept requiring only 18 s on average. Thus, the small-sample and continuous learning capabilities of the proposed model enable the construction of a conceptual space that promotes improved knowledge representation and complex scene understanding.

Synchrophasor technology is an up-and-coming technology used for monitoring and controlling wide area measurement systems (WAMS). In a typical WAMS, phasors measured at different locations have phase angle differences because their reference waveforms are not synchronized with each other. One solution for this issue is to use phasor measurement units (PMUs), which measure input phasors with respect to a common reference wave based on the atomic clock pulses received from GPS satellites. This technology has various applications, such as fast fault detection, accurate measurement of current, voltage, frequency and phase angle, and fault location analysis.

However, commercially available PMUs can be costly for research and development as well as grid integration projects. This is where this research article proposes an economic PMU model that optimizes for steady-state performance based on recursive discrete Fourier transform (DFT). The results show that the developed PMU model is accurate up to 13 digits after the decimal point for both nominal and off-nominal frequency inputs in steady state, which meets the compliance specifications of IEEE standard C37.118.1. 

In summary, this research presents an economic PMU model that provides accurate steady-state performance for WAMS control and monitoring. This development has the potential to reduce the overall cost for research and development and grid integration projects while still providing reliable and accurate data for analysis.

Robot task programming often leads to inefficient plans, as opportunities for parallelization and precomputation are usually not exploited by the programmer. This inefficiency is often especially obvious in mobile manipulation, where path planning and pose estimation algorithms are time-consuming operations. In this letter, we introduce the concept of resource-aware task nodes (RATNs), a powerful descriptive action model for robots. Next, we propose an algorithm that executes so-called concurrent dataflow task networks (CDTNs), robot plans consisting of RATNs. It optimizes programmed plans based on two sources of information: 1) The control flow represented in the original task plan, whose constraints are relaxed to generate opportunities for parallelization and precomputation. 2) Dependencies between actions pertaining to resources, data flows, and world model changes, the latter being equivalent to preconditions and effects. CDTNs have been integrated in our open-source task programming framework RAFCON, and we show that it leads to 11%-29% improvement in terms of execution time in two simulated mobile manipulation scenarios.

Four-legged walkers are frequently used by elderly individuals and patients recovering from leg injuries to maintain mobility and aid in rehabilitation. However, correct use of these walkers can be challenging, often leading to injuries. To address this issue, an IoT sensor-augmented walker has been developed that continuously monitors the weight distribution on the legs of the walker. This data stream can be processed by a deep neural network-based classifier, which learns to detect dangerous use patterns that can increase the risk of falls and injury. This classifier is trained using examples of unsafe use, thus eliminating the need for costly engineering to customize the algorithm to the specific user and walker. Alerting the user in real-time about unsafe use patterns allows for the correct and safe use of the walker to be learned.

It is well known that backstepping method suffer from the problem of "explosion of terms", which is solved by dynamic surface control (DSC) method. This paper presents an improved dynamic surface control (IDSC) method, which constructs the state errors by directly using virtual control signals, rather than using the signals produced by first-order filters in DSC method. The signals produced by first-order filters will only be used to construct the virtual control laws and actual control law. This modification makes the state errors to be more free from the influence of first-order filters. The stability of systems controlled by the proposed IDSC method is proved based on Lyapunov theorem. Finally, the advantage of IDSC method has been shown by simulation results, and it can be seen in the simulation results that IDSC method has better tracking performance and is more stable than DSC method.

This paper presents a novel flow estimation approach that assimilates distributed pressure measurements of autonomous underwater robots through coalescing recursive Bayesian estimation and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based flow model reduction. The proposed flow estimation approach does not rely on any analytical flow models and is thus applicable to many and various complicated flow fields for arbitrarily shaped underwater robots while most of the existing flow estimation methods apply only to those with simple and well-defined shapes. Neural network is further used to establish the relationship between the POD flow model and the flow parameters of interest, e.g., the angle of attack and flow-relative velocity. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed distributed flow estimation approach, two simulation studies, one with a circular-shaped robot and one with a Joukowski-foil-shaped robot, are presented.

For road networks that have multiple intersections and links, accurately forecasting traffic flow is a complex problem that involves time series forecasting on graphs. This challenge arises due to the intricate spatiotemporal dependence among traffic flows in the entire road network as well as the sharp non-linearity and dynamic nature of traffic flows under different conditions. To address these challenges, our paper proposes extending the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm to have graph attention structures in both the input-to-state and state-to-state transitions. We name this extension the Graph Attention LSTM Network (GAT-LSTM), which we use to build an end-to-end trainable encoder-forecaster model that solves the multi-link traffic flow forecasting problem. Our experiment results demonstrate that our GAT-LSTM network successfully captures spatiotemporal correlations better and outperforms state-of-the-art prediction models by 15% - 16%.

To enhance the precision of surface electromyography (sEMG) based gesture recognition, we propose a new hybrid method that merges actual sEMG signals with corresponding virtual hand poses. The virtual hand poses are produced using a newly developed cross-modal association model based on adversarial learning to capture the intrinsic correlation between the sEMG signals and the hand poses. Our approach is thoroughly evaluated for frame- and window-based sEMG gesture recognition for seven-sparse-multichannel and four-high-density-benchmark databases. The experimental results indicate that our method outperforms existing approaches, achieving significant improvements in sEMG-based gesture recognition. Compared to existing methods, our framework achieves an average accuracy enhancement of +5.2% on the sparse multichannel sEMG databases and +6.7% on the high-density sEMG databases for frame-based sEMG gesture recognition. For window-based sEMG gesture recognition, we observe a +0.2% improvement in recognition accuracy for three of the high-density sEMG databases, where the state-of-the-art recognition accuracies are already higher than 99%. For the remaining eight sEMG databases, the improvement in recognition accuracy with our proposed framework for the window-based approach is an average of +2.5%.

Through the internet and local networks, IoT devices exchange data. Most of the IoT devices are low-power devices, meaning that they are designed to use less electric power. To secure data transmission, it is required to encrypt the messages. Encryption and decryption of messages are computationally expensive activities, thus require considerable amount of processing and memory power which is not affordable to low-power IoT devices. Therefore, not all secure transmission protocols are low-power IoT devices friendly. This study proposes a secure data transmission protocol for low-power IoT devices. The design inherits some features in Kerberos and onetime password concepts. The protocol is designed for devices which are connected to each other, as in a fully connected network topology. The protocol uses symmetric key cryptography under the assumption of that the device specific keys are never being transmitted over the network. It resists DoS, message replay and Man-of-the-middle attacks while facilitating the key security concepts such as Authenticity, Confidentiality and Integrity. The designed protocol uses less number of encryption/decryption cycles and maintain session based strong authentication to facilitate secure data transmission among nodes.

This paper introduces an innovative state estimation approach for linear dynamic systems with outlier-corrupted measurements. The typical methods for handling outliers in state estimation incorporate the NP test and KF; however, this paper proposes a new method that optimizes the subset of measurements to minimize the risk of having outlier-affected measurements while still meeting performance specifications. The application of this approach is connected and autonomous vehicles operating in sensor-rich environments, where not all sensor data may be necessary to meet the system's accuracy specification. By using an optimized measurement subset, the state estimate is exposed to less needless risk of outlier inclusion. The main contributions of this paper are (1) a more efficient algorithm for selecting the optimal measurement set and (2) a comparison between the proposed approach and the traditional NP-KF method using real-world GPS Doppler and differential pseudorange data acquired on a moving platform.

Developers constantly make various assumptions regarding requirements, environment, design decisions, etc. during software development. However, these assumptions are usually implicit and undocumented and there is a lack of understanding regarding what assumptions have been made and discussed in software development. Open Source Software (OSS) is recently becoming an important part of software industry. To this end, we conducted an exploratory study on assumptions in OSS development. We extracted and analyzed 9006 posts from the developer mailing list of Hibernate (a popular OSS project), in order to explore (1) assumption expression and (2) classification, (3) the trend of assumptions over time, and (4) related software artifacts of assumptions in OSS development. We identified 832 assumptions from the Hibernate developer mailing list. The findings are: (1) most of the assumptions are expressed as "Feature Request" and "Solution Proposal"; (2) more than half of the identified assumptions are design assumptions and are made for software design; (3) assumptions exist in the whole OSS development lifecycle; and (4) the major category of related artifacts of assumptions is "Design Document".

Electrooculography (EOG) is a highly stable physiological signal which is essential in the development of Human-Computer Interface (HCI) systems for detecting eye-movement variations. Recently, EOG signal classification has become more important in overcoming physical inconveniences in paralyzed patients. In this paper, a robust classification technique, which involves eight directional movements, has been investigated. This technique incorporates the use of a buffer along with a variation of the slope to prevent misclassification effects in EOG signals. Blinking detection can be complicated when the magnitude of the signals is taken into consideration. To overcome this challenge, a correction technique has been introduced to avoid misclassification for oblique eye movements. Moreover, a case study has been conducted to demonstrate how these correction techniques can be applied to an HCI baseball game in order to learn eye-movements.

This paper proposes an adaptive network fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) based decision support system that can provide European policy makers with systematic guidance in allocating and prioritizing scant public resources, whilst accomplishing the best growth performance at a regional level. We do so by taking the stance of the Smart Specialization Strategies, which aim at consolidating the regional strengths and make effective and efficient use of public investment in R&D. By applying the ANFIS method, we were able to understand how - and to what extent - the competitiveness drivers promoted technological development and how the latter contributes to the economic growth of European regions. We used socio-economic, spatial, and patent-based data to train, test, and validate the models. What emerges is that an increase of R&D investments enhances the regional employment rate and the number of patents per capita; in turn, by taking into account the several combinations of specialization and diversification indicators, this leads to an increase of the regional gross domestic product (GDP).

Direct monocular simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) methods, for which the image intensity is used for tracking and mapping instead of sparse feature points, have gained in popularity in recent years. However, feature-based methods usually have more accurate camera localization results than most direct methods, though direct methods can work better in a textureless environment. To tackle the localization issue, we develop a novel real-time large-scale direct SLAM model, namely, GCP-SLAM, by integrating the learning-based confidence estimation into the depth fusion and motion tracking optimization. In GCP-SLAM, a random regression forest is trained off-line with pre-defined confidence measures for learning confidence and detecting the ground control points (GCPs). Then, the confidence value along with the selected GCPs is utilized for depth refinement and camera localization. Our proposed method is shown experimentally more reliable in tracking and relocalization than the previous state-of-the-art direct method when compared with feature-based and RGBD SLAMs.

Recognizing human actions from the video streams has become one of the very popular research areas in computer vision and deep learning in the recent years. Action recognition is wildly used in different scenarios in real life, such as surveillance, robotics, healthcare, video indexing and human-computer interaction. The challenges and complexity involved in developing a video-based human action recognition system are manifold. In particular, recognizing actions with similar gestures and describing complex actions is a very challenging problem. To address these issues, we study the problem of classifying human actions using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and develop a hierarchical 3DCNN architecture for similar gesture recognition. The proposed model firstly combines similar gesture pairs into one class, and classify them along with all other class, as a stage-1 classification. In stage-2, similar gesture pairs are classified individually, which reduces the problem to binary classification. We apply and evaluate the developed models to recognize the similar human actions on the HMDB51 dataset. The result shows that the proposed model can achieve high performance in comparison to the state-of-the-art methods.

We present a novel automated target recognition (ATR) tool for pulse-Doppler radars used in coastal surveillance. The uniqueness of this tool lies in the inclusion of new classification features and an innovative classification algorithm which integrates predictive models with M/N logic rules. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive explanation of the ATR tool's design. To demonstrate its efficacy, we tested it using real-time data for the recognition of fishing vessels. Our independent tests confirmed that the proposed ATR tool outperformed those discussed in recent publications in terms of classification performance.

When classifying brain signals in practical applications, the data used for training and prediction often come from different distributions. Additionally, datasets collected from different subjects or tasks may have unique feature spaces. As these classified data are usually limited in quantity, it is important to use techniques that can generalize learned information. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) significantly benefit from the increased availability of data. In this study, we applied transfer learning to a deep convolutional neural network (Deep ConvNet)-based framework to demonstrate the transferability of error-related brain signal patterns across different tasks. Results from the experiments suggest that our transfer learning technique improved performance when only a limited amount of data was available for differentiating erroneous and correct completion of tasks. It was found that this improvement could not solely be attributed to the transfer of general brain signal characteristics, but instead indicates the transfer of error-specific information as well. Furthermore, we identified similar patterns in time-frequency analyses from identical channels, resulting in selective high signal correlations between two different paradigms. The intracranial data classification demonstrated median accuracies of (81.50 ± 9.49)%. With pre-training, decoding using only 10% of the data yielded performances of (64.95 ± 0.79)%, whereas without pre-training, performances were (54.76 ± 3.56)%.

Ahstract- The current network infrastructure needs to adjust to meet the rapidly growing data demand generated by new emerging applications. Planning this infrastructure should be thought by operators so that the high number of applications that are emerging, with different types of requirements, can be efficiently met. In this work, a model of resource provisioning for hierarchically distributed data centers is proposed using Linear Programming (LP). The goal is to increase efficiency in the use of computational resources and decrease the overhead of network links. The results shows that the model is able to efficiently accommodate 48 % more applications when compared to First-Fit.

Given a nonlinear dynamical system, this letter considers the problem of selecting a subset of the total set of sensors that has provable guarantees on standard metrics related to the nonlinear observability Gramian. The key contribution is a simple randomized algorithm that samples the sensors uniformly without replacement, and yields probabilistic guarantees on the minimum eigenvalue or the inverse of the condition number of the nonlinear observability Gramian relative to that of the complete set of sensors. Numerical studies reveal that the utility of the theoretical results lies in the regime of large total number of sensors wherein the combinatorial nature of the problem presents a significant computational challenge. The results are demonstrated numerically on a problem of moving target localization using an extended Kalman filter in two scenarios: one using range sensors and another with time-difference-of-arrival measurements. A graceful degradation of performance with a decreased number of sensors is observed when compared to the use of all of the sensors for localization. It is also observed that for certain metrics, the proposed approach provides an improvement over a heuristic that selects the sensors in a greedy manner based on the contribution of an additional sensor toward the observability Gramian metric.

In this work, we present three models of noise level at thoroughfare. These models were built using equivalent sound level data recorded by a monitoring station, and we utilized both Random Forest and regression trees to construct them. We then applied the obtained models to reconstruct equivalent sound levels for more than 60 days, during which the monitoring station did not record any sound levels. The noise level values were reconstructed separately for three 24-hour sub-intervals: day (6-18), evening (18-22), and night (22-6).

We also conducted statistical analysis of the sound levels throughout the year, both before and after reconstruction. Through this analysis, we were able to observe the changes in noise levels over time and assess the effectiveness of our reconstruction methods.

Overall, our work provides valuable insights into the modeling and reconstruction of noise levels in busy thoroughfares. By utilizing advanced statistical methods and machine learning techniques, we hope to better understand the impact of noise pollution on urban environments and develop effective strategies for managing and reducing noise levels in the future.

Human respiration state is an important indicator to reflect health conditions. Recent advances in wireless human sensing have enabled device-free respiration monitoring using narrow-band wireless signals, which, however, fail to map the estimated respiration states to multiple persons. In this paper, we present Multi-Breath, a UWB-based system to achieve separate respiration monitoring for multiple persons. The UWB radar can accurately measure the travelling distance of the signals, which helps to separate the signals affected by different persons and map the detected respiration patterns to the corresponding persons with the location information. However, the radar signal time series of each person are quite noisy due to the multi-path effects caused by the respiration movements of other persons, making it difficult to accurately estimate the respiration state. To overcome this challenge, we propose to transform the UWB radar signal matrices of different persons as separate RGB images to reveal the respiration pattern of each individual. Then, the image processing operations, including image smoothing, edge detection, dilation and erosion, are applied to identify the breathing cycles. Finally, the respiration state, including the respiration rate and the presence of apnea, is estimated via blob detection and calibration. Extensive experiments show that the mean absolute error on respiration rate estimation is 0.3 - 0.6 bpm, and the percentage of missed and false detected apnea is 3% - 7%.

The forecasting of electricity load is a crucial tool, particularly in countries with a restructured electricity market. Mid-term prediction, covering a period of 1 month to 1 or 2 years, is essential for mid-term planning, including repair planning and economic exploitation of power systems, which have a direct impact on system reliability. The focus of this paper is on monthly and daily basis (peak load) forecast horizons. To predict the load, a combined method utilizing neural network and particle optimization algorithm was deployed, followed by calculating the maximum amount of environmental pollution resulting from electricity production required to meet the predicted load. This method was tested on data from a North American electric company for four months (four seasons), and in contrast with prior research, the accuracy was deemed acceptable.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the use of structure from motion (SFM) for 3D reconstruction in computer vision and graphics. The quality and speed of SFM systems heavily depend on feature tracking techniques. When dealing with large volumes of image data, the speed of the SFM system can become slow, especially for large-scale scenes which require capturing several thousand images to create a point-cloud model of the scene. Existing methods, such as brute force matching and hashing matching, have limitations in dealing with fast feature tracking for large-scale scenes.

To address this problem, we propose a new feature tracking method based on a parallel method of keypoint detection, descriptor computing, descriptor matching using parallel k-nearest neighbor (Parallel-KNN) search, and outlier rejecting. This method can quickly match a large volume of keypoints and reduce computation time, producing a set of correct correspondences. We compare our method to existing state-of-the-art methods on several challenging benchmark datasets, including those with highly repeated features. The experimental results demonstrate that our method is both more efficient and effective than other methods.

Overall, our proposed method offers a solution to the problem of fast feature tracking in SFM systems for large-scale scenes. It is expected that this method will have broad applications in various fields, where fast and accurate feature tracking is required.

Conventionally, automatic assessment of pathological speech involves two main steps: (1) extraction of pathology-specific features; (2) classification or regression of extracted features. Given the great variety of speech and language disorders, feature design is never a straightforward task, and yet it is most critical to the performance of assessment. This paper presents an end-to-end approach to automatic speech assessment for Cantonese-speaking people with aphasia (PWA). The assessment is formulated as a binary classification problem to differentiate PWA with high scores of subjective assessment from those with low scores. The sequence-to-one GRU-RNN and CNN models are applied to realize the end-to-end mapping from speech signals to the classification result. The speech features used for assessment are learned implicitly by the neural network model. Preliminary experimental results show that the end-to-end approach could reach a performance level comparable to conventional two-step approach. The experimental results also suggest that CNN performs better than sequence-toone GRU-RNN in this specific task.

We offer a multi-agent approach based on microservices to solve complex computational problems that arise in scientific and applied research in various fields. The specific nature of these problems is due to the exponential increase in runtime caused by the multidimensional calculations of input data, the variability of mathematical models, and the algorithms used to solve the problem. Using microservices in our approach allows for reusability, ease of update, and cross-platform functionality, which makes it modular and adaptable for distributed computing conditions with message passing mechanisms as the only means of communication between modules. Our platform automates the development of a distributed microservice application based on an applied program package and the management of microservices composition in a decentralized manner. With new mechanisms for deploying and updating microservices, cloud knowledge bases and installed user computers can synchronize, offering additional opportunities through the Dew computing paradigm that combines cloud computing with the capabilities of the user's local computers. Scientific computational experiments using our approach have proven its effectiveness and convenience.

This paper describes and evaluates the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for path planning in support of smart mobility applications such as indoor and outdoor navigation applications, individualized wayfinding for people with disabilities (e.g., vision impairments, physical disabilities, etc.), path planning for evacuations, robotic navigations, and path planning for autonomous vehicles. We propose an architecture based on GANs to recommend accurate and reliable paths for navigation applications. The proposed system can use crowd-sourced data to learn the trajectories and infer new ones. The system provides users with generated paths that help them navigate from their local environment to reach a desired location. As a use case, we experimented with the proposed method in support of a wayfinding application in an indoor environment. Our experiments assert that the generated paths are correct and reliable. The accuracy of the classification task for the generated paths is up to 99% and the quality of the generated paths has a mean opinion score of 89%.

This paper compares two approaches to the development of a voltage source converter. The first approach involves implementing only off-line simulation, while the second approach also involves on-line simulation using the hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) system. The HiL simulation system plays a crucial role in testing the control algorithm and control electronics. The paper describes the hardware structure and software support required for real-time implementation of HiL simulation and details the necessary adjustments to fully utilize the functionality of the system.

The development of a fan drive converter is used as an example, with an off-line simulation model developed in the PLECS software package and a model adapted for execution in the corresponding RT Box simulation device. Results obtained by experimental testing of the developed converter are compared with the simulation results. The paper shows that the implementation of HiL simulation can predict errors in converter design, particularly errors in the control algorithm that cannot be detected by off-line simulations.

Overall, the paper highlights the importance of using HiL simulation in the development of voltage source converters. The inclusion of on-line simulation provides a more comprehensive testing of the control algorithm and control electronics and can accurately predict errors in converter design.

Nonlinear optimization problems with dynamical parameters are widely arising in many practical scientific and engineering applications, and various computational models are presented for solving them under the hypothesis of short-time invariance. To eliminate the large lagging error in the solution of the inherently dynamic nonlinear optimization problem, the only way is to estimate the future unknown information by using the present and previous data during the solving process, which is termed the future dynamic nonlinear optimization (FDNO) problem. In this paper, to suppress noises and improve the accuracy in solving FDNO problems, a novel noise-tolerant neural (NTN) algorithm based on zeroing neural dynamics is proposed and investigated. In addition, for reducing algorithm complexity, the quasi-Newton Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) method is employed to eliminate the intensively computational burden for matrix inversion, termed NTN-BFGS algorithm. Moreover, theoretical analyses are conducted, which show that the proposed algorithms are able to globally converge to a tiny error bound with or without the pollution of noises. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the superiority of the proposed NTN and NTN-BFGS algorithms for the online solution of FDNO problems.

Video based vehicle detection is an active research area in Intelligent Transportation System.
