In conclusion, this paper provides a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of chronic disease research driven by emerging technologies. This approach provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners involved in the development of digital health solutions to mitigate the burden of chronic diseases globally.

Unmanned aerial vehicle-based base stations can provide wireless cellular service to ground users in various scenarios, and deploying these UAV-BSs while optimizing coverage area is a key challenge. This study focuses on the 3D placement of UAV-BSs to maximize the number of users covered while using minimal power and accommodating their Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements. We model the placement problem as a multiple concentric circles placement problem to achieve our objective of maximizing the number of covered users. The UAV-BS deployment problem is decoupled in the horizontal and vertical dimensions without any loss of optimality. After some mathematical manipulations, we formulated a Mixed Integer Second Order Cone Problem (MISOCP) and proposed an improved Multi-Population Genetic Algorithm (MPGA) for horizontal dimensions placement problem. Our numerical simulations show that improved MPGA outperforms the Standard Genetic Algorithm (SGA) in solving this problem.

High-precision motion control is essential in process and industrial automation, encompassing a wide range of domains such as machine tools, ultra-precision spindles, micro-manufacturing, biotechnology, disk drive read/write mechanisms, air-bearing positioning stages, to name a few. However, the nonlinear factors in the actuators limit their performances, leading to issues such as friction, creep, force ripples, and hysteresis. This paper focuses on friction compensation schemes and reviews literature focusing on intelligent designs of friction compensation in motion control systems. The review covers different types of friction models, ranging from simple to complex structures, followed by detailed discussions on various friction compensation schemes. Finally, the advantages and disadvantages of the methods in these two categories are highlighted, and recommendations for potential research directions are offered.

The traditional approach to analyzing satellite scene images typically involves classifying them into a specific land use category, which can limit the ability to identify and interpret sub-regions of the image. However, a new approach has been proposed which utilizes a deep rule-based image classification method to automatically analyze the semantic content of sub-regions of satellite images.

This approach involves a self-organizing set of transparent zero order fuzzy IF-THEN rules with human-interpretable prototypes identified from the training images and a pre-trained deep convolutional neural network as the feature descriptor. The training process is highly parallelizable and requires very little parameter tuning, making it an efficient and effective method for analyzing the semantic features of local areas of the image.

The proposed approach has been tested on benchmark datasets and has demonstrated its validity and effectiveness in analyzing sub-regions of satellite images. With the ability to accurately identify and interpret multiple land use categories within a single image, this approach has the potential to be a valuable tool for a range of applications, from environmental monitoring to urban planning.

For a long time, previous studies focused on convolutional neural network depth and width to improve accuracy in image super-resolution tasks. Although overall performance has grown as going deeper and going wider over time, until recently, these two elements start to show saturating accuracy and we meet a marginal utility. To address this problem, model efficiency is improved successfully by introducing two effective strategies, multi-cardinality, and spatial attention, to image super-resolution from high-level vision tasks. We propose a novel and efficient architecture aggregated residual attention network (ARAN) and set a new state-of-the-art model efficiency. According to the multi-cardinality strategy, we use group convolutions in each basic module. Moreover, we apply spatial attention blocks as gate units to capture detailed information in input images, which can be the counterparts of their basic modules. Extra representation ability is demonstrated compared with both the same sized enhanced deep super-resolution network (EDSR) baseline model and currently the-state-of-the-art cascading residual network (CARN). The experiments suggest the effectiveness of these two missing strategies previously. Especially, in the aspect of model efficiency, ARAN exceeds almost all the medium sized models currently. Code and pre-trained models are publicly available on the github: https://github.com/Xingrun-Xing/ARAN.

Achieving reliable and robust object segmentations is crucial, and one way to accomplish this is by discarding outliers during the segmentation process. Ideally, a one-to-one mapping from model points to valid observations would be used for an object model such as an active shape model (ASM). However, a one-to-many mapping is often required to ensure that valid observations are detected for a reliable and robust fitting process. This work compares three observation detectors: two based on handcrafted texture features and one based on a deep CNN classifier. To reduce from many detections to one valid observation, the Generalized Expectation-Maximization (GEM) algorithm is incorporated into the ASM framework, which assigns low weights to outliers to neglect them. The proposed methodology achieves remarkable accuracy with all the detectors in the segmentation of the left ventricle in two publicly available MRI datasets, and is competitive with other state-of-the-art methods.

Constructing strong AI systems for video games is difficult due to enormous state and action spaces and the lack of good state evaluation functions and high-level action abstractions. In spite of recent research progress in popular video game genres such as Atari 2600 console games and multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) games, to this day strong human players can still defeat the best AI systems in adversarial video games. In this paper, we propose to use a deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to select among a limited set of abstract action choices in Real-Time Strategy (RTS) games, and to utilize the remaining computation time for game tree search to improve low-level tactics. The CNN is trained by supervised learning on game states labeled by Puppet Search, a strategic search algorithm that uses action abstractions. Replacing Puppet Search by a CNN frees up time that can be used for improving units' tactical behavior while executing the strategic plan. Experiments in the μRTS game show that the combined algorithm results in higher win-rates than either of its two independent components and other state-of-the-art μRTS agents. We then present a case-study that investigates how deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) can be used in modern video games, such as Total War: Warhammer, to improve tactical multi-agent AI modules. We use popular RL algorithms such as Deep-Q Networks (DQN) and Asynchronous AdvantageActor Critic (A3C), basic network architectures and minimal hyper-parameter tuning to learn complex cooperative behaviors that defeat the highest difficulty built-in AI in mediumscale scenarios.

The objective of this paper is to enhance an outdated airport system into a sophisticated, improved, and real-time system using IoT technology. The escalating demand for flights and airport traffic underscores the necessity of improving the traveler's experience, a need that many airports struggle to meet. Through the integration of IoT technology, smart airports can vastly enhance the traveler and employee experience by simplifying the processes and enhancing the overall concept. Implementing IoT-based smart airports will notably improve the operational efficiencies, passenger services, and security capabilities. This paper proposes an IoT-based smart airport solution that includes a mobile application interface and sensor network systems integrated with cloud technology. The proposed system has undergone rigorous testing and has been deemed secure, reliable, and more robust than conventional airport infrastructure.

Fog computing offers the ability to process data on the network edge, reducing network bandwidth and latency. However, it comes with security challenges as the existing protocols do not wholly cater to the mobility and heterogeneity of the fog. This results in an increased latency and overhead on resource-constrained fog nodes, which has a ripple effect on the overall fog network.

To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an OTP-based encryption protocol that addresses the shortcomings of existing protocols. The protocol has no packet loss, and its time and energy overheads are significantly lower than the ones proposed by prior research. The protocol generates the OTPs using a random number generator within the nodes and will be tested on wireless sensor nodes to assess its viability. 

The outcomes of the testing are positive, showing that the proposed protocol can be implemented on resource-constrained fog nodes. With this protocol, the fog network can become more secure and efficient, and latency and overhead can be reduced, allowing data to be processed faster and more effectively.

As the Internet continues to get stronger, so does the potential risk of malicious users trying to harm others. An intrusion detection system (IDS) can be used to alert the appropriate entities when potentially dangerous operations are happening within a host of set of hosts. Nowadays, we need a system that can accurately process large amount of network data quickly. Most of the state-of-the art IDSs apply the traditional machine learning algorithms to classify whether a packet is a part of an attack. However, these algorithms typically aren't implemented with a big data platform. In this research, we will use Apache Spark, a big data processing tool known for handling tasks at fast speeds, to process network packet data. This paper utilizes the Spark libraries to implement Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, and Gradient Boosted Trees. We also implement a Deep Multilayer Perceptron, which is a Spark implementation of a deep learning algorithm. We compare the results of the traditional machine learning algorithms to the deep learning method. Our results show that the deep learning algorithm produces favorable accuracy, precision, and recall, but takes longer to analyze the data than classical machine learning algorithms.

This work considers the simulation of an array consisting of identical, interconnected elements using dynamically constructed macro basis functions. The dynamic construction of the macro basis functions is based on the iterative Jacobi technique and, for the examples presented here, improves the convergence of this method.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a contemporary concept that aims to connect various objects in our environment to the Internet. This allows these objects to transmit information that can be accessed anywhere and at any time, making our lives more convenient and modern. The IoT has rapidly developed in recent years, gaining widespread adoption across various industries such as buildings, healthcare, transportation, education, and agriculture.

However, the increasing use of IoT devices means that there is a greater volume of data being collected and transmitted. This data needs to be secured to ensure that it is not accessed by malicious attackers. This paper discusses the different types of attacks that can be carried out on IoT devices, as well as the security weaknesses present in the IoT environment. It also highlights the challenges that IoT faces in terms of hardware, network and software.

Furthermore, this paper provides an overview of the attacks that have been carried out on various IoT applications, such as smart cars, smart homes, smart campuses, smart farms, and healthcare. By providing a comprehensive review of these attacks and security weaknesses, this paper aims to raise awareness and provide insights for developing robust security measures that can ensure the safety and integrity of IoT devices and systems.

One issue with computer based histopathology image analysis is that the size of the raw image is usually very large. Taking the raw image as input to the deep learning model would be computationally expensive while resizing the raw image to low resolution would incur information loss. In this paper, we present a novel deep hybrid attention approach to breast cancer classification. It first adaptively selects a sequence of coarse regions from the raw image by a hard visual attention algorithm, and then for each such region it is able to investigate the abnormal parts based on a soft-attention mechanism. A recurrent network is then built to make decisions to classify the image region and also to predict the location of the image region to be investigated at the next time step. As the region selection process is non-differentiable, we optimize the whole network through a reinforcement approach to learn an optimal policy to classify the regions. Based on this novel Look, Investigate and Classify approach, we only need to process a fraction of the pixels in the raw image resulting in significant saving in computational resources without sacrificing performances. Our approach is evaluated on a public breast cancer histopathology database, where it demonstrates superior performance to the state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, achieving around 96% classification accuracy while only 15% of original image pixels are required for computation.

Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) technology emerged in Release 13 as one of the solutions to provide cellular IoT connectivity. NB-IoT is designed to achieve better indoor coverage, support of a massive number of low-throughput devices, with relaxed delay requirements, and lower energy consumption. Particularly, the extensive coverage of NB-IoT poses a great challenge. The goal is to cover devices in areas previously inaccessible by cellular networks due to penetration losses or remote locations. To solve this, NB-IoT utilizes bandwidth reduction and repetitions. However, for the targeted low range of signal to noise ratio (SNR), the coverage gain due to repetitions can be significantly limited by the performance of the channel estimator. In this paper, we provide an analytical evaluation framework to study the performance of NB-IoT. Our analysis includes the limitations due to realistic channel estimation (CE) and delves into the estimation of the SNR. Additionally, the conducted evaluation shows the impact of the coverage extension in the final performance of the NB-IoT user equipment (UE) in terms of uplink packet transmission latency and battery lifetime. Specifically, regarding UE's battery lifetime, for a maximum coupling loss (MCL) of 164 dB, realistic CE evaluations obtain a battery lifetime reduction of approximately 90% compared to ideal CE.

A growing number of user applications rely on the computing resources of edge cloud data centers (ECDCs). The efficient management of ECDC resources has a positive impact on the cloud service providers' profitability and on the stringent quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of user applications. This paper proposes a resource allocation framework of interconnected ECDCs using software-defined networking (SDN). SDN technology is used to ensure QoS and to efficiently embed user applications into the ECDCs. The proposed framework, called infrastructure as a service provisioning using SDN (IaaSP-SDN), includes the two-phase coordinated IaaS requests. Provisioning approach and a set of SDN management modules to set up accepted IaaS. The performance of IaaSP-SDN is evaluated in two steps: 1) a prototype is compared with generalized multi-protocol label switching (GMPLS) and 2) the impact of SDN controller physical location on the performance of the IaaSP-SDN framework is evaluated. The results illustrate that the SDN framework is more stable and scalable than GMPLS. We also show that SDN controller location attributes have a significant effect on the acceptance ratio of IaaS requests.

Over the last decade, several industrial wireless technologies have emerged, offering to replace the need for wires in various use cases. However, most wireless communication options have reliability and latency issues when it comes to industrial applications. Closed loop communication requires high reliability (over 99%) and limited jitter and latency, which can be challenging over a wide area. 

Sub-GHz technologies, including IEEE 802.11ah, promise extended coverage, but only IEEE 802.11ah offers sufficient data rate for frequent bidirectional communication. Therefore, we assessed IEEE 802.11ah for low-latency time-critical control loops and proposed a network set-up that adjusts the network dynamics to control loops, enabling limited jitter and high reliability.

We also tested the scalability of IEEE 802.11ah networks that host both control loops and monitoring sensors transmitting periodic measurements. We assigned end-nodes for the control loop to a dedicated restricted access window (RAW) slot, resulting in over 99.99% successful deliveries. We observed that interpacket delay concentrated around the cycle-time in the following or preceding beacon interval if the beacon interval was at least half the value of the shortest cycle-time.

We adjusted the beacon interval to the fastest control loop in the network to achieve latency requirements at the expense of maximum achievable throughput and energy consumption.

We consider the problem of channel aging in massive multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems using the Kalman filters without knowledge of channel correlation statistics. Although Wiener filtering can be used to estimate the channel state information to construct accurate precoders and decoders, their use is limited in the case where regular adaptation to channel changes is needed. In addition, since different users exhibit different mobility conditions, use of an adaptive Kalman filter is advantageous when compared to conventional estimation approaches. We build a general model that allows a wide range of user mobilities in each cell. Simulations using the model reveal that the Kalman filter is effective in predicting channel coefficients to build an effective precoder. In addition, we perform both uplink and downlink analysis and show that with poorer channel tracking, the achievable rates in massive MIMO diminish unless more accurate channel estimates are present.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) are increasingly being adopted for sensing and control functions in safety-critical systems such as self-driving cars, medical diagnostics, and industrial robotics. As failures can result in fatal consequences, it is important to verify and validate these systems to ensure their reliability. Although formal verification methods are being explored, testing remains the primary technique for evaluating the dependability of DNNs. However, the cost of obtaining labeled test oracle data is high, which affects the amount and quality of testing that can be performed. Thus, prioritizing input data for testing DNNs is critical to reduce labeling costs and increase testing efficacy.

This paper proposes using gauges of the DNN's sentiment, calculated by the model, as a means to identify inputs that are likely to expose weaknesses. We investigated the efficacy of three sentiment measures-confidence, uncertainty and surprise-for prioritization and compared their fault-revealing capability and retraining effectiveness. Our empirical assessments showed that sentiment measures can effectively flag inputs that reveal unacceptable DNN behavior. For MNIST models, the average percentage of correctly flagged inputs ranged from 88% to 94.8%. In conclusion, our proposed approach can help identify inputs for testing that are likely to be more informative, reducing the costs and increasing the effectiveness of testing DNNs in safety-critical applications.

In this study, we assess network utilization and connectivity challenges in WiFi deployments by analyzing data collected from hundreds of access points. We examine AP-client session data, including the start and end times of association, as well as the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the duration of the session. Our analysis is based on four enterprise WiFi deployments in India, over a period of 45 days. By examining the session data, we were able to determine patterns in the spatio-temporal use of the WiFi network, as well as any anomalies in connectivity and coverage. These insights have numerous applications in cell planning, radio resource management, and network management.

The Internet of Things (IoT) encompasses devices that capture data from the physical world and present it to users in a comprehensible manner. As such, selecting the correct technology to store data collected from these devices is crucial. In this article, we examine the ideal database management system for cultural heritage applications, with a focus on lighting monitoring at the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua, Italy, where Giotto's frescoes are displayed. We compare SQL and NoSQL solutions and use the results to determine the most suitable option for this use case. These findings serve as a practical reference for selecting the appropriate database for real-world applications.

Numerous cloud encryption techniques have been proposed to encrypt and decrypt users' data stored on public cloud databases. Although some heterogeneous database connection access methods have been studied, none of them can offer transparent access to encrypted databases on public clouds, crossing various languages and platforms. In response to these issues, we built a middleware system in a private cloud using Mysql protocol and technology for heterogeneous database data integration. This system has been applied in a hybrid cloud environment to achieve transparent access to heterogeneous encrypted databases for users. Our report includes a preliminary assessment of system security and experimental evaluations of system performance. These evaluations separately test the time costs for users to execute transparent access to individual and heterogeneous encrypted databases.

The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is a term applied to the industrial application of M2M devices. The security of IIoT devices is a difficult problem and where the automation of critical infrastructure is intended, risks may be unacceptable. Remote attacks are a significant threat and solutions are sought which are secure by default. The problem space may be analyzed using threat modelling methods. Software Defined Networks (SDN) provide mitigation for remote attacks which exploit local area networks. Similar concepts applied to the WAN may improve availability and performance and provide granular data on link characteristics. Schemes such as the Software Defined Perimeter allow IIoT devices to communicate on the Internet, mitigating avenues of remote attack. Finally, separation of duties at the IIoT device may prevent attacks on the integrity of the device or the confidentiality and integrity of its communications. Work remains to be done on the mitigation of DDoS.

The mining time complexity is more with the conventional MapReduce algorithm particularly with large data sets or big data. The existing MapReduce algorithms will take time and data sets have to be disclosed for analysis. Defining data inherently with fuzziness will reduce the retrieval time and actual data sets need not be disclosed. In this paper, Fuzzy data mining methods are discussed. With these methods the original data sets need not be disclosed for analysis. The fuzzy functional dependency (FFD) and fuzzy multivalve dependency (FMVD) are studied for data mining. The fuzzy MapReduce algorithm of FFD and MVFD are useful to reduce time of OLAP and the original data need not be disclosed, The FFD and FMVD are made easy for combining the data sets and used for association, some examples are given for fuzzy MapReduce.

With modern communication technology, the distribution of intelligence over vast distances can be achieved by pushing apart sensors, estimators, and controllers. This eliminates the need for periodic data transmissions, as smart sensors can decide on their own whether data are worth transmitting. This letter focuses on event-based transmissions from the sensor to the estimator. The sensor-side event trigger conveys useful information, even if transmission is not initiated, resulting in implicit information that can still be used by the remote Kalman filter. 

To utilize this implicit data, an easy-to-implement trigger mechanism is proposed based on finite impulse response prediction, contrasted against a stochastic decision variable. The stochastic event trigger allows implicit data to be processed efficiently by the Kalman filter, which transmits Gaussian representation. The parameters for the stochastic trigger are retrieved from the finite impulse response filter, and this leads to significant communication rate reduction as demonstrated in simulations.

With the development of aviation, the air traffic density in the terminal area is high and the traffic situation is relatively complex, which brings challenges to the flight deployment. In order to fully understand the air flight situation and provide decision-making basis for controllers, this paper proposes a key conflict aircraft identification method based on complex network theory and node deletion method. First, an aircraft state network is constructed with an aircraft as nodes and airborne collision avoidance system (ACAS) communication relations as edges. Network efficiency, network robustness, connection density, and largest component were used as the indexes of network performance. The weight of each index is determined by using AHP-entropy weight method. A multi-attribute decision-making method was introduced to quantify network performance. Then we used a node deletion method to determine key conflict aircrafts. The simulation and experiment are respectively carried out on the artificial network and the aircraft state network of a certain day in the terminal area of Kunming Changshui Airport. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can identify the key conflict points in the aircraft state network. The deployment of selected nodes can not only effectively reduce the complexity of the flight state network, but also provide a reference for air traffic control services and reduce the control difficulty of the controller.

In this paper, a dynamic integrated energy efficiency model is presented as part of the efforts in implementing high energy efficiency manufacturing, which also aims to provide model support for energy fine-grain management as well as comprehensive energy efficiency performance analysis and evaluation of computer numerical control machine tools (CNCMT). An integrated energy efficiency index system is proposed for measurement of energy utilization performance of machine tools. And the dynamic energy efficiency model is established based on Discrete Event System Specification (DEVS), which can dynamically acquire the important machining information and the attribute information such as energy consumption and energy efficiency of CNCMT. And a case study of machining a tailstock spindle on CNC grinding machine tools is simulated by using Eclipse to validate the proposed model.

The phase wire breakage of an overhead line is the common damage in electric networks with 6-10 kV voltage. To set a protection in case of a phase wire breakage, the negative and zero sequence voltages are used as an information parameter. The protection device itself is installed either at the end of the 6-10 kV overhead line or at the side of a low voltage step-down transformer with 6-10/0.38 kV voltage. To select the information parameter, to obtain its quantitative characteristics and to determine the protection installation location, the investigations using a MATLAB/Simulink computer model, a physical model in the laboratory and experimental electric network are carried out. The article provides the results of the negative and zero sequence voltages research and shows the expedience of using the negative sequence voltage as an information parameter and justifies the installation of a protection device at the side of a low voltage step-down transformer with 6-10/ 0.4 kV voltage. The article shows that the negative sequence voltage more fully characterizes the phase wire breakage of 6-10 kV overhead line than the zero sequence voltage and information on the negative sequence voltage can be obtained on both the side of a high and the side of a low voltage of the 6-10 /0.4 kV step-down transformer.

Accurately describing and classifying driving style is crucial for driving safety intervention strategies in the design of advanced driver assistance systems (ADASs). This paper presents a novel driving style classification method based on constructed driving operational pictures (DOPs) which map sequential data from naturalistic driving into 2-D pictures. By using the nested time window method, 798/1683/1153 DOPs sized 42 (features) × 60 (seconds) were generated for three different driving styles (low-risk, moderate-risk, and high-risk), respectively. The three kinds of neural network algorithms, i.e., convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and pretrain-LSTM were applied to recognize driving styles based on DOPs. The results showed that CNN performed the best with an accuracy of 98.5%, better than the traditional support vector machine (SVM) method. This study provides a new perspective to classify driving style which may help design ADASs operating characteristics to improve driving comfort and safety.

We investigate Bayesian shrinkage methods for constructing predictive distributions. We consider the multivariate normal model with a known covariance matrix and show that the Bayesian predictive density with respect to Stein's harmonic prior dominates the best invariant Bayesian predictive density when the dimension is greater than or equal to 3. Alpha divergence from the true distribution to a predictive distribution is adopted as a loss function.

In this paper, character recognition system for documents written in Kannada language is proposed. Paper provides the technical details of design and implementation of proposed. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is used for the implementation and Chars74K dataset is used for training the model. System has achieved accuracy of 98% for the document containing non-overlapping lines of characters.

This paper presents the design of a hybrid Kalman filter for a specific class of nonlinear systems where the state equation is nonlinear and the measurement equation is linear. The system model accounts for stochastic nonlinearities, which are characterized by statistical means to account for multiplicative stochastic disturbances. The presence of multiple missing measurements is represented by a set of Bernoulli distributed random variables that have known conditional probabilities and different missing rates for each sensor. In order to mitigate the effects of stochastic nonlinearities and multiple missing measurements, the filter parameters are computed. 

A new hybrid Kalman filtering algorithm is proposed based on the recursive projection formula and the unscented transformation approach. This algorithm is designed to minimize the filtering error for the stochastic nonlinearities and multiple missing measurements. By solving the recursive matrix equation, we can obtain the filter gain matrices and error covariance matrices. The proposed results can be verified using standard numerical software. 

To demonstrate the performance of the proposed approach, a numerical example is provided. The results show that the proposed hybrid Kalman filter outperforms the extended Kalman filter and unscented Kalman filter in terms of filtering accuracy.

In this work, a novel data-driven approach to anomalous event detection in CPPS has been developed. The approach utilizes the non-convex hull's geometric structure to establish a decision boundary for classification of novel observations. To construct n-dimensional non-convex hulls, a new algorithm based on a Mixture-of-Experts model has been introduced. Additionally, a new technique for resolving the point in non-convex hull issue has been proposed. By combining these methods, a unique algorithm has been developed that allows for anomaly detection. Compared to anomaly detection approaches based on convex hulls, this technique can handle datasets of varying shapes. The presented geometric approach avoids assumptions about either the probability density or the structure of the data, making it compatible with various machine learning algorithms. Real-world data obtained from wind turbines has been used to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

Voice biometrics has been applied to enhance the security of spoken language proficiency tests and ensure valid test scores by detecting fraudulent activity. These methods can, however, be triggered by certain distortions, including background noise and adjacent test-takers, resulting in false positive alarms. In this paper, a two-layer bi-directional LSTM RNN model is employed to detect these distorted (unusable) responses and a sub-sampling method is applied to reduce the difficulties of model training caused by very long input sequence and imbalanced training data. The system is evaluated on a corpus that was collected from an assessment of English language proficiency around the world. Results show that our approach significantly outperforms two baselines: a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) classifying frame-level features and an AdaBoost classifier operating on i-vectors. Our system's F-score in unusable response detection is 0.60 compared to 0.43 and 0.49 for the two baseline systems.

The classification falls into the essential tasks of supervised learning. The prediction of highly disperse nature of data, such as clinical medical data, is an open challenge. This study performs experimental analysis of machine learning algorithm to develop an effective prediction model for the clinical dataset. A real time clinical dataset has been considered for the model development. The machine learning algorithms: Decision Tree (J48), Naïve Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) have been applied. The validation of prediction model has been evaluated using both cross validation and split percentage methods. It has been evident that classification algorithms in combination of ensemble methods perform better. Thus, an effective prediction model performs better in presence of ensemble methods. The bagging, voting and stacking - ensemble methods have been used in this study. The experimental outcomes revealed that Naïve Bayes produced better predictive results using 10-fold cross validation method. Whilst, MLP outperformed using split percentage method for evaluation.

Document semantic similarity is a rapidly growing field of study, particularly when it comes to the automatic extraction of entity-based characterizations from content. This is especially important for building effective recommender systems and for document retrieval and ranking. In this study, we set out to develop an expert system for job placement that is based on skills, capabilities, areas of expertise present in a person's curriculum vitae, and personal preferences. The primary challenge in this project is to consider all the personal, educational experiences of the individual, formal, informal, and on-the-job, as well as their work-related knowledge, in order to create a concept-based profile. This profile would allow for a reasoned matching process with existing job positions, as well as additional educational experiences for profile improvement.

To achieve this goal, we developed a domain-specific approach to semantically characterize documents and compare their similarity, taking inspiration from the explicit semantic analysis (ESA). We enriched and filtered the general purpose German Wikipedia dump to create a domain-specific model tailored to our task. The domain was further defined through a German knowledge base of descriptions for educational experiences and job offers. Initial testing with a small set of documents indicated that our approach meets the main requirements. There are still open issues to tackle in the next project steps, including considering information granulation theories, optimizing algorithm tuning parameters, and extending our solution to multi-lingual contexts.

This paper focuses on the event-triggered tracking of uncertain nonlinear systems. Unlike previous related works, this paper considers systems with serious uncertainties and limited a priori information on the reference signal. As a result, event-triggered control becomes more challenging due to the difficulty in precisely bounding sampling errors. The main contribution of this paper is the proposal of new adaptive event-triggered tracking schemes for two event-triggering architectures that have different roles in information transmitting and control computing/updating. The dynamic gain is incorporated in both schemes to counteract serious uncertainties and overcome the negative impact of sampling errors. Two adaptive event-triggered controllers are designed based on the dynamic gain with distinct event-triggering mechanisms. To ensure application flexibility, one of the triggering mechanisms is rendered relatively independent of the controller signal. The proposed event-triggered controllers can achieve practical tracking for the systems, ensuring prespecified arbitrary tracking accuracy while avoiding infinitely fast sampling/execution.

In this paper, we propose a distributed event-triggered algorithm for separable optimization problems with smooth and strongly convex cost functions. We consider a multiagent system where each agent has a state and an auxiliary variable for the estimates of the optimal solution and the average gradient of the entire cost function. Agents exchange their states and auxiliary variables when the differences at the current time and the last trigger time exceed a threshold. We show that the proposed event-triggered algorithm with an exponentially decaying trigger condition linearly converges to the optimal solution.

The analysis of multi-dimensional signals becomes more challenging with the availability of 5G. To be able to estimate the important features of such signals, minor component analysis (MCA) is a beneficial data analysis approach. MCA neural network approaches are capable of adaptively extracting minor components from real-time data streams online, and their rapid convergence is valuable in practical applications. Our proposal is a deterministic discrete time-based method to analyze the convergence performance of MCA neural network algorithms. We have revealed that the norm of initial weight vectors in MCA algorithms has an effect on convergence speed. Based on our convergence analysis, we have devised a new MCA algorithm that achieves faster convergence than the current approaches. The theoretical analysis and simulation results have proven the effectiveness of our proposed MCA algorithm.

Location information is generally considered to be indispensable information in wireless sensor networks, but existing algorithms have notable limitations in their positioning accuracy in 3-dimensional (3D) spaces. To improve the positioning accuracy of nodes in a 3D scenario, this paper proposes a new method called N2-3DDV-Hop (non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II with 3D distance-vector hop) that builds on the 3D-DV-Hop algorithm by adding multi-objective model and NSGA-II. In this paper, it is analyzed that the limitations of the traditional single-objective positioning model and showed the relationship among the average hop distance, the number of sensor nodes, and the theoretical average distance. In addition then, the multi-objective positioning model incorporating the NSGA-II algorithm is presented. To evaluate its performance relative to other current methods, we compared our method by testing all of the methods with three different complex network topologies. Simulation results demonstrate that the N2-3DDV-Hop offered the best overall positioning performance compared with other algorithms and better robustness than the 3DDV-Hop algorithm.

To reduce network traffic and service delays in next-generation networks, there is a proposal to temporarily store popular contents, such as videos and music, in the cache located at edge nodes like base stations. However, accurately predicting the contents to store is a challenging issue since the more popular the contents, the more reduction in network traffic and service delays. Moreover, network virtualization aims to split a cellular network into InPs and MVNOs to reduce capital and operational costs. In this approach, MVNOs lease physical resources like network capacity and cache storage from InPs to provide services to their users. Ensuring that an MVNO leases enough resources to store popular contents without wasting resources is essential. Thus, we propose a deep learning-based prediction scheme to intelligently manage the resource leasing and caching process, thereby improving MVNO's profit. The main challenge in utilizing deep learning is searching for the most suitable prediction model. Hence, we also propose a reinforcement learning-based model searching scheme to find the optimal deep learning model. The prediction models are implemented using Keras and Tensorflow libraries, and the cache leasing and caching scheme's performance is tested using a Python-based simulator. Our simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms randomized caching with an optimal cache leasing scheme by 46%.

We propose the use of a wireless body area network for remote patient health monitoring applications. Our network consists of a controller and multiple sensors that gather vital information on a patient's health state. We model this patient-sensor network as a partially observable Markov decision process, allowing for accurate monitoring of a patient's health state while minimizing operational and misclassification costs. 

The sensor outputs are used by the controller to update the patient's health-state belief probabilities and select a subset of sensors to be activated at the next decision epoch. We have developed two operational algorithms to achieve these objectives: a greedy algorithm for a one-step look-ahead approach, and a dynamic programming-based algorithm which yields the optimal policy. 

To test the proposed methods, we provide a numerical example which demonstrates their applicability and provides insights. The algorithms function together seamlessly, and the wireless network allows for instant analysis of the patient's health state from a remote location. 

Our proposed wireless body area network for remote patient health monitoring applications provides a cost-effective, reliable and sustainable solution for monitoring patients' health states in real-time. It has the potential to revolutionize patient care, providing healthcare professionals with vital information that can help with early diagnosis and intervention, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

Gait recognition is an emerging computer vision problem that complements other identification methods such as face or iris recognition. The gait identification method is unique in that it is based on the motion of body points, which can be accurately captured by using the Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS). In this study, we have examined the potential of gait recognition through visualization of the event stream and application of existing methods that have shown state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks. We have also explored several auxiliary problems that are associated with this method, such as moving object detection and human pose estimation. 

Our research has evaluated and compared different algorithm settings to determine the most effective means of capturing and analyzing gait data from the event-based stream. We have achieved high-quality results in all the related problems, which is on par with the quality of that achieved in conventional colored videos. These findings conclude that the gait recognition process can be successfully carried out using event-based data, and this method has the potential to further improve identification techniques in the future.

Deep learning models, such as deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), are highly sought-after in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification due to their exceptional feature extraction ability. Ensemble-based learning systems have also shown great potential in supervised classification. To further enhance the performance of deep learning-based HSI classification, a deep learning ensemble framework is proposed in this study. This framework integrates deep learning models and random subspace-based ensemble learning. Two ensemble-based methods are proposed, namely CNN ensemble and deep residual network ensemble. These methods use CNNs or deep residual networks as individual classifiers and random subspaces are utilized to diversify the ensemble system in a simple yet effective manner. Transfer learning is also investigated to improve the classification accuracy. This mechanism transfers the learnt weights from one individual classifier to another (i.e., CNNs) to speed up the learning stage. The experimental results using widely-used hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed deep learning ensemble system provides competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy. The combination of deep learning and ensemble learning shows significant potential for reliable HSI classification.

As the number of people using social networks continues to rise, users demand access to data across multiple domains. However, ensuring privacy and security in this scenario is a significant challenge. To address this issue, we propose a cross-domain access control scheme based on multi-authority attribute-based encryption for big data from social networks. Our hybrid encryption algorithm, which combines symmetric encryption and CP-ABE, not only achieves cross-domain access control but also improves system efficiency. Trusted proxy users help ensure proper storage of symmetric keys, enhancing system security. Additionally, formulating access control policy through an inter-domain trusted proxy user instead of an intra-domain data owner reduces computational overhead associated with ciphertext re-encryption technology, greatly improving overall efficiency. Security and performance analyses demonstrate the proposed scheme's trustworthiness and effectiveness.

Learning a performance model for a cloud service is challenging since its operational environment changes during execution, which requires re-training of the model in order to maintain prediction accuracy. Training a new model from scratch generally involves extensive new measurements and often generates a data-collection overhead that negatively affects the service performance.In this paper, we investigate an approach for re-training neural-network models, which is based on transfer learning. Under this approach, a limited number of neural-network layers are re-trained while others remain unchanged. We study the accuracy of the re-trained model and the efficiency of the method with respect to the number of re-trained layers and the number of new measurements. The evaluation is performed using traces collected from a testbed that runs a Video-on-Demand service and a Key-Value Store under various load conditions. We study model re-training after changes in load pattern, infrastructure configuration, service configuration, and target metric. We find that our method significantly reduces the number of new measurements required to compute a new model after a change. The reduction exceeds an order of magnitude in most cases.

An innovative method for quantifying 18O labeled LC-MS data has been proposed based on I-Ching divination evolutionary algorithm (IDEA). Traditional methods that employ genetic algorithms or other optimized algorithms are computationally complex due to the poor label efficiency when calculating the least squares regression function. The proposed algorithm makes use of highly flexible I-Ching operators such as the intrication operator, turnover operator, and mutual operator. Its objective is to determine the coefficients comprising the 18O/16O ratio r, label efficiency f, and abundance a of 16O. Compared to the GA, the proposed algorithm significantly improves the accuracy and precision of peptide ratio measurements, and performs better in the evolution procedure in determining the function. The experiment was conducted using mixed peptide raw data of predefined ratio, and the findings revealed that the proposal algorithm is superior to the conventional GA in exploring the optimal solution for better quantification accuracy.

The single shot multi-box detector (SSD) is a real-time detector that uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to achieve state-of-the-art detection performance. However, there is still room for improvement due to the semantic gap between CNN feature layers. To address this issue, we propose a new training scheme for the SSD. In object detection, a ground truth (GT) box is a bounding box that encloses an object boundary. To enhance the semantic level of the feature map, we generate additional GT boxes by zooming in and out from the original GT boxes. Our experiments show that the SSD trained using our scheme significantly outperforms the original one on a public dataset.

In this letter, we utilize deep neural networks to perform unsupervised clustering of seismic data. Our approach involves optimizing the feature space simultaneously with the clustering assignment, resulting in highly effective learned feature representations for a specific clustering task. To demonstrate the applicability of our method in seismic signal processing, we develop two neural networks primarily consisting of full convolutional and pooling layers. We then use these networks to 1) differentiate between waveforms recorded at different hypocentral distances and 2) differentiate between waveforms with different first-motion polarities. Our method achieves precision levels comparable to those of supervised methods, but without the need for labeled data, manual feature engineering, and large training sets. By using this approach, we can reduce false alerts on an individual station level in standard single-site earthquake early warning systems. Furthermore, the presented technique can be generalized for various applications, including quality control of labeling and classification results from other supervised methods.

With the development of cloud server, reversible data hiding in encrypted domain has received widespread attention for management of encrypted media. Most of existing reversible data hiding methods are based on stream ciphers, which are mainly concerned with data storage security. While homomorphic ciphers focus on data processing security, which is popular in cloud and other third-party platforms. Reversible data hiding with homomorphic cryptography has been an active topic in the research filed. In this paper, we propose a new lossless data hiding method based on homomorphic cryptosystem. After a content owner generates encrypted media with homomorphic ciphers, a data hider embeds secret data by establishing a mapping between secret bits and losslessly modifying encrypted media. At the receiver side, the embedded data is extracted from encrypted domain with a little auxiliary message. And original media is recovered by directly decrypting marked encrypted media. During the embedding process, the modification of encrypted media does not change the corresponding original media owing to homomorphic and probabilistic properties. Thus, no distortion is introduced in the whole procedures of data embedding. And directly decrypted media containing embedded data is the same as the original media. Meanwhile, the proposed method achieves a high embedding rate through efficient mapping and skillful use of expanded pixel values. The experimental results show that compared with state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method has higher embedding rate without distortion.

In this study, researchers have developed an educational intelligent question answering bot known as Xiao-Shih, which can assist learners in solving their queries as instructors and teaching assistants on MOOCs. The researchers conducted experiments with Xiao-Shih on ShareCourse, a well-known MOOC platform in Taiwan, in a paid course titled "Python for Data Science." The bot was trained using over a thousand discussion threads posted in both English and Chinese languages to improve natural language processing and machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest.

The researchers initially developed Xiao-Shih through NLP techniques and text similarity approaches. However, the bot's precision was only up to 0.413, with different thresholds for question similarity. Hence, the researchers collected features and labels concerning answer correctness for the next version of Xiao-Shih. Random forest was used to train the bot using 70% of the entire dataset, leading to Xiao-Shih achieving a precision of 0.833 with test data.

The educational intelligent question answering bot enables learners to solve their questions and problems immediately in seconds, rather than waiting for hours or even days for human responses. Additionally, it can also ease the burden of instructors and teaching assistants responding to numerous queries from students. In conclusion, Xiao-Shih provides an effective solution to the difficulties that learners and instructors face while using MOOCs.

Network traffic analytics has always been an important field for cybersecurity and network operations. The analysis could be done on the stream of data (network traffic) in an on-line mode for real-time network operations or on the captured traffic data in an off-line mode for forensic analysis. In this paper, we aim to shed light into using machine learning based network analytics on traffic flows both for network operations and forensic analysis purposes. In doing so, our goal is to design and develop systems that could assist the human expert in analyzing "unknown background" traffic.

This letter provides a brand new way of feature extraction, which can be applied in the supervised classification of hyperspectral image. The convolutional neural network (CNN) has been proven to be an effective method of image classification. However, due to its long training time, it requires a large amount of the labeled data to achieve the expected outcome. To decrease the training time and reduce the dependence on large labeled data set, we propose using the method of transfer learning by taking the advantage of Bayesian framework to integrate with spectrum and spatial information, making use of the Markov property of images to distinguish and separate the ones with class tags, and employing the CNN trained by band samples randomly selected from the data sets. The method of classification mentioned in our letter makes use of the real hyperspectral data sets to perform the experimental evaluation. The result demonstrates that our method is superior to the previous methods.

Keyword extraction is an indispensable step for many natural language processing and information retrieval applications such as; text summarization and search engine optimization. Keywords hold the most important information describing the content of a document. With the increasing volume and variety of unlabeled documents on the Internet, the need for automatic keyword extraction methods increases. Even though keyword extraction can be used in many applications, Arabic research in the field still lacking. In this paper, a supervised learning technique that uses statistical features and Support Vector Machine classifier was implemented and applied to extract the keywords from Arabic news documents. The proposed supervised learning approach achieved a precision of 0.77 and a recall of 0.58.

In this contribution, an innovative approach to estimate the electrical properties of biological tissues in vivo is presented. This estimation is a crucial step in hyperthermia treatment planning, where magnetic resonance or computerized tomography images are used to convert the electric parameters based on ex-vivo measured properties to predict the treatment's effects. Since parameters vary from patient to patient, and ex-vivo measurements can be distinct, the proposed approach solves the inverse scattering problem by processing backscattered data from the patient and conveniently uses morphological information on the tissues available from medical images to overcome the issues arising in inverse problems.

This work proposes a new Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation for traffic grooming, routing and spectrum allocation to be used in the design of Elastic Optical Networks (EON). In order to compare our method with classic Routing and Spectrum Allocation (RSA) formulation without grooming, the evaluation of the benefits of exact traffic grooming and RSA formulation are presented over three small networks. For each network, the objective function is set as minimizing the maximum slot index among all fibers. Then, the collected results show the benefits of traffic grooming in EON networks. Due to the NP characteristic of the MILP proposed, we propose a heuristic algorithm for large networks, and the benefits of the grooming using this algorithm are investigated.

Network motifs bring a great interest to many fields, because they are a perfect candidate to speed up the applied research in the understanding of complex networks dynamics. One of the biggest problems raised in the process of finding these motifs is the performance. Starting from splitting the initial network into subgraphs to the subgraphs clusterization, each algorithm used addresses an NP problem. Hence there are many algorithms that are trying to solve network motifs discovery, however there is no perfect approach talking from a time performance perspective, but only solutions that are faster than others. This paper presents a redesign of one of the most competitive algorithms for subgraphs enumeration found in the literature called ESU. In the proposed approach a given network can be processed by using parallel programming, either with a process-driven model, or a hybrid one (process-driven and thread-driven). Finally, the existing and proposed models are compared using benchmark graphs, revealing competitive results.

The physical characteristics of wireless channels, in particular the channel impulse response (CIR), have become an attractive source of shared secrecy between two communicating parties for many wireless applications. However, ensuring high-entropy secret bits from the CIR may not be always feasible, including in IoT and/or indoor environments, where the coherence time may not be easy to obtain, or mobility is limited. Many techniques have been developed to resolve the above problems, including privacy amplification for higher entropy output, and pre-processing for data distillation. In this paper, we develop a framework for extracting entropy from sequentially arriving channel impulse response observation samples, and propose algorithms for both online and offline versions of the problem. We fully characterize the optimal solutions to these problems through a series of analytic results, and establish the optimality of our proposed online and offline algorithms, namely A_EMSON and A_EMSOFF to solve the problem. We also verify the performance of the algorithms through comparisons with the existing related techniques, and evaluate their capability to ensure high-entropy under different channel models using MATLAB simulations.

To overcome the slacking effect and motivate the patients to actively participate into the training therapy, it is crucial to achieve online assessment of patients’ neural engagement and functional performance in robot-assisted rehabilitation. In this work, a fine motor control task has been designed for functional training of the upper limbs. The subject needs to control the hand position and gripping force, with visual and haptic feedback. Then subjects’ neural engagement and functional performance were assessed online based on the measured EEG and motion information. Experiments with healthy subjects have been conducted, and the relationship between subjects’ neural engagement and functional performance with the task configuration parameters was studied through statistical analysis.

Cost volumes are essential in attaining accurate stereo matching in Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) based stereo matching methods. In this study, we present a fully trainable end-to-end CNN that maximizes the usefulness of the cost volumes for stereo matching. The CNN comprises three sub-modules: shared feature extraction, initial disparity estimation, and disparity refinement. Multiple cost volumes are computed at different levels using shared features and are used for both initial disparity estimation and disparity refinement. To enhance the efficiency of disparity refinement, the sub-module introduces multi-scale feature constancy for measuring the accuracy of the initial disparity in the feature space. Our approach tightly couples these sub-modules, making it easier to train and compact. Additionally, we tackle the challenge of developing a robust model that performs well across varied datasets with distinct features. To achieve this, we propose a two-stage fine-tuning approach to smoothly transition the model to target datasets. In the first step, we use a large synthetic dataset and target datasets to fine-tune the model with a sizable learning rate, while in the second phase, we use only the target datasets with a small learning rate. The proposed method is tested on several benchmarks, including the Middlebury 2014, KITTI 2015, ETH3D 2017, and SceneFlow datasets, with the experimental results showing that it outperforms the state-of-the-art performance on all datasets. Furthermore, our approach won the first prize in the Stereo task of Robust Vision Challenge 2018.

Geo-Social Networks (GSN) play a crucial role in offering location-based services by leveraging the large volumes of data generated in the GSN. However, existing studies on user location prediction based on user-generated data in GSN have some limitations. Specifically, predicting the user's next check-in location or predicting their future check-in location at a given time with coarse granularity has been widely studied. However, a unified model that can predict both scenarios with fine granularity is rare. Additionally, the integration of multiple factors, including temporal-spatial context, semantic information, and sequential relations, remains a challenging task.

In this paper, we propose a novel embedding model, Venue2Vec, inspired by word embedding in natural language processing. Venue2Vec automatically integrates multiple factors associated with user location prediction and uses a unique approach, which situates locations of the same type, geographically close or often visited successively by users closer within the embedding space. The Venue2Vec model enables predicting a user's next check-in location as well as their future check-in location at a given time with fine granularity. Our model outperforms several state-of-the-art models on various evaluation metrics, as validated by experiments conducted on three real-world GSN datasets.

Furthermore, we show that the Venue2Vec model is more time-efficient due to being parallelizable, making it a promising approach to predicting user location in real-time. In conclusion, our Venue2Vec model provides an effective and efficient solution for user location prediction and enhances the location-aware capability of GSN-based services.

The Fiber-Wireless (FiWi) access network is a promising network architecture for providing constantly available connections for the collaboration of objects in the Internet of Things (IoT). Network virtualization is dominating the evolution of FiWi, specifically the virtualized FiWi access network, which allows for customized transmission of different types of IoT services in a common substrate network. However, the differences between optical and wireless subnetworks pose a severe obstacle to their interoperability. 

This paper focuses on the survivable virtual network embedding (SVNE) in the FiWi access network to provide robust IoT service provisioning in the event of network component failure. Each type of IoT service is carried on one virtual network (VN), which is characterized by computing resource and bandwidth resource demands and connection availability requirements. We propose a connection availability model as an indicator of network survivability and IoT service robustness. Our goal is to allocate resources for each VN with minimized resource cost. 

We formulate the optimization problem of resource allocation in the integer linear programming (ILP) model and solve it for the optimal solution in a small-scale network. Additionally, we propose a heuristic algorithm to facilitate the use of the SVNE mechanism in a large-scale network. The simulation results confirm that the proposed SVNE mechanism has significant advantages in lower resource redundancy and a higher acceptance ratio of VNs.

Bidikmisi is a government scholarship that provides access to higher education for the poor. Although thousands of Bidikmisi enthusiasts spread awareness about the program, only 10% of the quota is accommodated. To improve the selection process for the scholarship recipients, a Decision Support System (DSS) can be utilized. While many DSS studies address similar issues, few discuss methods that incorporate an intuitive aspect approach. This study solves the problem by utilizing the FIS type-1 method and dividing the ten criteria into two phases with fuzzy reasoning. Two decision experiments were conducted, and the second experiment resulted in a better outcome by tuning the parameter's range intuitively.

The article delves into the process of automating the monitoring of computer system states through intellectual analysis of unstructured system log data. The objective is to detect and diagnose abnormal system states to aid technical support in resolving issues accurately. As log sizes continue to grow, data mining models are utilized to extract pertinent system information. 
The process of automating this monitoring involves four stages. Firstly, system logs are collected and recorded with information pertaining to process execution and system states. In the second stage, a log parser is utilized to yield a set of event templates, thereby structuring raw logs. Thirdly, parsed logs are presented in form of numerical attribute vectors, which are compiled as a set forming a matrix of signs. Lastly, the feature matrix is used for machine learning methods to detect anomalies that signify abnormal system states. 
A decision tree algorithm was implemented as a classification method for machine learning. The article demonstrates the effectiveness of this automated monitoring process in detecting anomalous system states using the example of a distributed HDFS dataset.

Vehicles can augment their perceptual range regarding road traffic through the collective perception technique, which enables the sharing of sensor data among neighbors using Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication. However, during high vehicle density, the problem of packet collisions and hidden terminals makes it challenging to deliver messages containing sensor data. To combat this, we have proposed a method for controlling the transmission frequency of sensor data based on vehicle positioning and road structure to improve the awareness of the vehicle's surroundings.

In this paper, we present the details of our proposed strategy, which includes an automated system for selecting vehicles that have a high probability of broadcasting sensor data. We also evaluate the effectiveness of this method through simulations and compare it with similar previous studies. Our results indicate that our method is highly effective in avoiding collision accidents because it allows vehicles to perceive the presence of other vehicles while reducing radio traffic. 

Overall, our proposed method offers a viable solution to improve the awareness of the vehicle's surroundings amidst high traffic density, thereby enabling a safer and more efficient transportation system.

Java-Bali grid is the largest electricity grid in Indonesia. The most recent recorded peak load of 26.834 MW occurred on October 2, 2018. Several loss of generation events have been recorded by Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) which placed in several locations in Java-Bali system. The recently installed Wide Area Monitoring System (WAMS) can collect PMU data within the Java-Bali grid so the data can be compared with high accuracy. This paper shows monitoring of frequency response in Java-Bali system during loss of generation event in 2018. The analysis includes rate of change of frequency, grid frequency control evaluation, and simplified estimation of system inertia constant.

Object depth estimation is a crucial aspect of visual analytics systems. While significant progress has been made in recent years, accurately estimating depth in real-world videos remains a challenge. In this presented paper, the approach used involves estimating the distance of surrounding vehicles using a mono camera. YOLO (You Only Look Once) is utilized in the detection process by generating a boundary box around the object. By determining an inverse proportional correlation between the distance and the boundary box's dimensions (height and width), an exact equation is obtained. The distance is considered the dependent variable, while the height and width of the YOLO boundary box are treated as independent variables. Multiple regression techniques are employed in the regression models to avoid heteroskedasticity and multi-collinearity issues. The result is real-time detection with 23 FPS and an accuracy of 80.4% for depth estimation.

This article presents an innovative model aimed at safeguarding the Cloud by providing a hybrid solution based on the distribution of intrusion detectors and the centralization of alerts for management purposes. The objective of this approach is to protect the most critical layers of the Cloud through the use of intrusion detection systems, customized for each layer. Each layer has distinct properties, which require specific intrusion detectors for efficient protection.

To achieve this objective, the proposed detection model is divided into two segments. The first segment is equipped with signature-based detectors to identify known attacks, while the second segment comprises anomaly-based detectors to detect previously unknown malicious events on the application layer. By using both signature and anomaly-based detection methods, it is possible to fully protect the Cloud using open-source software.

This article provides the Cloud service provider with a comprehensive model to protect, monitor, and manage the Cloud effectively. The model involves visualizing and correlating logs and alerts to enhance the identification of potential threats. The proposed model underscores the possibility of achieving a high-level of protection for the Cloud by distributing intrusion detectors, enabling prompt response to potential threats, and centralizing alerts for effective management.

This paper analyzes the common text clustering algorithm and text representation model for the hot topics found in the campus. Through the use of the word segmentation system, the text word segmentation and keyword extraction are proposed, and a knowledge representation model of the message text is proposed. The study of vector space model uses the word frequency of statistical messages to determine k initial clustering centers and improve the optimization algorithm k-Means. The detailed process and concrete steps of the hot topic discovery algorithm are given, and the topic discovery module is verified. The experimental results show that the intelligent topic clustering process can be processed faster and better, and the clustering accuracy can be kept high when the number of reported messages is large.

The Curriculum for the Enhancement of Digital Competences for School Employees, developed as part of the Croatian e-Schools project, is presented in its updated and improved form. This curriculum has been designed with an open, flexible approach that enables creativity and encourages change throughout its implementation. It is intended for adult learners, with tailored content related to adult education.

Considering the speed at which society, work, and education are turning digital, there is a pressing need to enhance digital competence. Schools have an essential role to play in leading the way with digital technologies, by demonstrating their use in learning environments, fostering vital skills and competencies, and highlighting the importance of this field for future education and employment.

We believe that this Curriculum will enable schools to more effectively address the key challenges that they face in light of the digital age. By promoting a framework of open and flexible learning, we hope to encourage lifelong digital learning and to prepare school employees for the technological shifts of the future.

Phoneme lattices have been shown to be a good choice to encode in a compact way alternative decoding hypotheses from a speech recognition system. However the optimal phoneme sequence is produced by tracing all the phoneme identities in the lattice. This not only makes the search space of the decoder huge but also the final phoneme sequence may be prone to have false substitutions or insertion errors. In this paper, we introduce the split lattice structures that is generated by splitting the speech frames based on the manner of articulation. Spectral flatness measure (SFM) is exploited to detect the two broad manner of articulation sonorants and non-sonorants. The manner of sonorants includes broadly the vowels, the semivowels and the nasals whereas the fricatives, stop consonants and closures belong to non-sonorants. The conventional way of speech decoder produces one lattice for one test utterance. In our work, we split the speech frames into sonorants and non-sonorants based on SFM knowledge and generate split lattices. The split lattice generated are modified according to the manner of articulation in each split so as to remove the irrelevant phoneme identities in the lattice. For instance, the sonorant lattice is forced to exclude the non-sonorant phoneme identities and hence minimizing false substitutions or insertion errors. The proposed split lattice structure based on sonority detection decreased the phone error rates by nearly 0.9 % when evaluated on core TIMIT test corpus as compared to the conventional decoding involved in the state-of-the-art Deep Neural Networks (DNN).

This paper presents a new design scheme for a carrier runway simulation system that can be used for aircraft carrier landing training. The proposed system replicates an environment similar to an actual landing, providing pilots with crucial movement information. The carrier runway simulation system comprises two main components: the runway motion simulation system and the ideal landing point simulation system.

The simulation system of ideal landing point simulates the height variation of the ideal landing point using the horizontal variation of optical virtual arresting cable. This system provides pilots with critical movement information necessary for carrier aircraft landing. The runway motion simulation system employs a programmable multi-axis controller to control linear motion guides that move with the infrared cooperative targets, simulating carrier runway movement. The high-precision magnetic grid measurement sensor collects motion information and transfers it to the computer.

The paper details an 8:1 scale experiment that was conducted to test the feasibility of the runway motion simulation system. The results showed that the maximum height error of the targets between actual and setting motion was 0.02m, which fulfills the requirement of the simulation system. The research team anticipates that the simulation system will support further research in carrier-based aircraft landing ground simulation. Overall, the proposed design scheme enhances training and supports realistic carrier landing simulations.

The development of the vocational education system is closely tied to the demand for professional services in the economy and labor market. The regions, society, and institutions of higher education hold the responsibility of improving the quality of vocational training, qualifications, and motivation for personal and professional growth in the citizens of the Russian Federation. In the Republic of North Ossetia-Alania, the labor market is plagued by an imbalance in both the quantity and quality of employees, with new professions and specialties appearing annually.

To eliminate the disproportion in the development of the labor market and educational services, the vocational education system's primary objective is to produce highly qualified specialists for the Republic's economy. To achieve this objective and address the challenges faced in education development, information and communication technologies, including distance education, must be used efficiently.

To address the Republic's education development problems comprehensively, an integrated program of joint actions of responsible and interested individuals and organizations is necessary. This cooperation will provide a foundation of organizational sustainability, leading to the growth of educational services and the development of the vocational education system in the Republic.

Objective: Deep learning has recently been applied to electrical impedance tomography (EIT) imaging. Nevertheless, there are still many challenges that this approach has to face, e.g., targets with sharp corners or edges cannot be well recovered when using circular inclusion training data. This paper proposes an iterative-based inversion method and a convolutional neural network (CNN) based inversion method to recover some challenging inclusions such as triangular, rectangular, or lung shapes, where the CNN-based method uses only random circle or ellipse training data.
