However, this paper introduces a vision-based framework that uses only frontal eye images to aid in an initial IOP screening. 

This novel framework utilizes a fully convolutional neural (FCN) network on frontal eye images for sclera and iris segmentation. Six features are then computed, including mean redness level of the sclera, red area percentage, Pupil/Iris diameter ratio, and three sclera contour features (distance, area, and angle), which are used to determine the status of the patients in terms of IOP (normal or high). 

This work utilized a database of 400 facial images from the Princess Basma Hospital, including 200 cases with normal IOP and 200 cases with high IOP. The two classifiers used in this work, support vector machine and decision tree, achieved an overall accuracy of over 97.75%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework. 

The contribution of this work lies in the introduction of a fully convolutional network architecture for eye sclera segmentation, as well as the correlation of frontal eye view (image) with IOP through the introduction of new sclera contour features. These features have not been previously discussed in the literature regarding frontal eye images for IOP status determination.

In this study, we examined the effectiveness of Bayesian shrinkage methods in developing predictive distributions. Specifically, we focused on the multivariate normal model with a known covariance matrix and found that the Bayesian predictive density, utilizing Stein's harmonic prior, outperforms the best invariant Bayesian predictive density when the dimension is three or greater. Our analysis was based on the alpha divergence, which measures the difference between the true distribution and predictive distribution, and served as our loss function. These findings highlight the usefulness of Bayesian shrinkage methods in developing predictive models that are both accurate and reliable.

Recently, a new approach to region-based 3D video coding has been proposed, but existing methods to estimate view synthesis distortion (VSDE) are performed at the frame level. To address this issue and guide the optimization process, we propose the first pixel-level VSDE (PL-VSDE) method. We define pixel-level view synthesis distortion and develop a backward prediction approach that starts from pixels of interest (POIs) in the virtual view to find their corresponding pixels in the reference view via a coarse-to-fine backward prediction (CFBP) method. The CFBP considers 3D warping, rounding operations, and warping competition in view synthesis to improve prediction accuracy. We also introduce a table-lookup method and a warping property to speed up the CFBP, making it ideal for parallel processing. With the integration of CFBP into PL-VSDE, we can estimate view synthesis distortion at the pixel level. Our method is independent pixel-by-pixel, making it efficient and accurate. Experimental results show that our proposed method is more accurate and efficient than existing frame-level VSDE methods.

In this paper, we study the physical layer security and transmission reliability problem where there is an active eavesdropper (AE) in the D2D underlaying cellular networks. We formulate the cooperation between the cellular user equipment (CUE) and the D2D user equipment (DUE), the completion between legitimate users and the AE to be a secrecy anti-jamming game. In the proposed game framework, DUE launches the cooperative relaying or the friendly jamming mode to help CUE to improve its anti-eavesdropping and anti-jamming performance. CUE gives different-level rewards for the assistance of the DUE. And AE shifts its attacking modes between actively jamming and passively eavesdropping to maximize the destruction for the D2D underlaying cellular networks. Under the perfect information, we prove the existence of the pure-strategy equilibrium of the proposed game. Under the imperfect information, we analyze the existence of the mixed-strategy equilibrium of the proposed game and propose a distributed Q-Iearning-based algorithm to converge to a mixed-strategy equilibrium. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is convergent and verify that average utilities of legitimate users are improved by the cooperation between CUE and DUE.

Now in current days the method to monitor the patients in hospitals is such that it keeps the patients tied to their beds, and monitoring by this method is uncomfortable for patients. Building a wireless Heart rate monitoring system that will allow patients to be mobile in the surrounding environment is the aim of this system. The heart attack causes death in first attempt or may be in third attempt. It is because blood flow reduces to the heart muscles. In india it is major problem within our research. So for safety and comfort point of view of patient in this paper designing of the wireless patient monitoring system. In this paper design of the wireless belt that continuously monitoring human pulse rate and temperature is proposed. It receive signal from body and send SMS to the doctor and their family member so at the time of heart attack treatment can be provide within time. Life is precious many people among us loss their life to heart attack. By using this system and checking our health on daily basis it is possible to reduce the chance of heart attack.

Safe and affordable surgery is not accessible for five billion people when they need it. Multiple surgical capacity studies have shown that hospitals in low-and-middle income countries do not have complete coverage of basic surgical equipment such as, theatre lights, anesthesia machines and electro surgical units. Currently, almost all equipment is designed and manufactured with a main focus on the context in high income countries. The context in low-and-middle income countries in which surgical equipment is used, differs from high income countries, especially in terms of financial resources and access to maintenance, spare parts and consumables. The aim of this study is to present a roadmap for design of surgical equipment for worldwide use. The roadmap consists of four phases: before the start of a design project a clear need for certain surgical equipment should be identified (Phase 0). During Phase 1 the context should be researched thoroughly by determining the barriers encountered by patients to surgical care, the structure of the health care system and if the aspects required for safe surgery are in place. In Phase 2 the implementation strategy and design requirements should be determined and in phase 3 prototyping starts in close interaction with local end-users. We believe that designers should strive for design that is of the same quality and complies with the same safety regulations as equipment designed for HICs. In this way user and patient safety can be assured in any setting worldwide. And we advocate for surgical equipment that fits the context optimally and that will be applicable in comparable settings globally.

We present an improved unsupervised anomalous trajectory detection algorithm for crowded scenes, based on clustering. The proposed algorithm consists of four main steps. Firstly, trajectories of all moving objects in a crowd are extracted using a multi-feature video object tracker. Secondly, several features are extracted from these trajectories, which are then transformed into feature matrices. Thirdly, a mean-shift clustering algorithm is applied to these feature matrices to obtain distinct clusters, while an anomaly detector based on Shannon Entropy identifies corresponding anomalies. Finally, a voting mechanism identifies the trajectories that exhibit anomalous characteristics. 

The algorithm is tested on crowd scene videos from datasets representing various crowd scenes with different motion patterns. The results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately detects anomalous trajectories, achieving a high level of performance.

The automotive industry is moving toward a more cleaner energy source and the usage of Electric Vehicles is increasing. One of the major problems of the electricvehicle is the driving range covered with a fully charged battery. The main reason for this is the power consumption by different electronic components in the vehicle. The major source of power consumption is an electric motor, and apart from this, there are many other electric units in the vehicle which consumes power.To achieve optimal power delivered to the different power consuming components and delivering the optimal required power to the electric motor and thereby the increasing the driving range of the electric vehicle is a major challenge. In the proposed method, a deep learning algorithm based on MRNN (Modular Recurrent Neural network) is used to predict the power requirements of the electric vehicle from different data inside the vehicle. The proposed method uses different data and parameter from the electric vehicle like power requirement to the electric motor under different driving conditions, power requirements of other devices in the vehicle are used to model the system and with the MRNN deep learning algorithm to train the network to predictthepowerrequirementsandprovidingoptimalpowerand thereby enhancing the driving range. By predicting the power demand of the vehicle, the battery power distribution to the motor can be more optimized as instead of delivering the power as such it can be controlled based on the classification of the powerdemand.

This paper introduces a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) conjugate prior, which is specifically designed for multiple extended object filtering. The PMBM prior utilizes a Poisson point process to represent the existence of targets that have yet to be detected, combined with a multi-Bernoulli mixture that describes the distribution of the targets that have been detected. The standard transition density and measurement likelihood are used to derive the prediction and update equations. Both prediction and update operations maintain the PMBM structure of the density, making it a conjugate prior. However, data associations lead to a large number of terms in the PMBM density, which makes it challenging to compute. Hence, approximations are necessary to make it tractable. A gamma Gaussian inverse Wishart algorithm is presented, along with strategies for handling the data association problem. A simulation study shows that the extended target PMBM filter performs well in comparison to the extended target δ-generalized labelled multi-Bernoulli and LMB filters. Additionally, a Lidar data experiment illustrates the benefit of tracking both detected and undetected targets.

We have developed an algorithm called iterative refinement for lossy image compression systems that significantly improves the decoder's reconstruction compared to standard decoding techniques. Our approach utilizes a recurrent neural network to iteratively decode compressed images, resulting in a nonlinear reconstruction process. Our decoder, which can be used with any encoder, employs self-connected memory units that utilize both causal and non-causal spatial context information to iteratively reduce reconstruction error over a fixed number of steps. Through testing, we have found that our iterative refinement approach consistently produces images with lower distortion and higher perceptual quality compared to other methods. Specifically, on the Kodak Lossless True Color Image Suite, our approach provides a 0.871 decibel (dB) improvement over JPEG, a 1.095 dB improvement over JPEG 2000, and a 0.971 dB improvement over a competitive neural network model.

To effectively enhance the supporting and regulation capacity of battery energy storage systems on the power grid, accurate load forecasting is crucial. Traditional mathematical models for load forecasting often lack self-learning and self-adaptation abilities, resulting in weak forecasting system robustness. This paper proposes a new method for load forecasting using a feedback neural network with input delay characteristics to improve accuracy. The Elman neural network model is studied, and an experimental model is established and trained using real power system data. Results indicate that load forecasting based on this model has high accuracy and strong adaptability and learning abilities for power grid load.

Doctors need to have a complete understanding of how drugs interact with each other, especially when patients are on multiple medications at the same time during treatment. Extracting information regarding drug-drug interactions (DDIs) from biomedical literature is essential to ensure successful treatment. Currently, the latest approaches for DDI extraction rely on artificial intelligence and natural language processing techniques. The existing methods utilize external resources, such as biomedical databases or ontologies, to enhance their performance. However, updating these external resources has proven to be challenging. User-generated content (UGC) offers an alternative form of external medical resources that can be quickly updated. Our study proposes a DDI extraction method that employs UGC resources to provide more available information for deep learning. Our approach utilizes a new attention mechanism, full-attention, which combines UGC information with contextual information. We evaluated our method by conducting a series of experiments on the DDI 2013 Evaluation dataset. The results showed that our method outperformed the state-of-the-art DDI extraction methods, achieving a competitive F-score of 0.712.

This paper focuses on solving the problem of joint sparse signals recovery from incomplete measurements at the data fusion center. Previous approaches to this problem assumed that all measurements were fully observed, but in reality, this is often not the case due to limited sampling rates, noise, and transmission errors. Therefore, the proposed method uses Regularized M-FOCUSS algorithm to reconstruct the sparse signals efficiently. Unlike matrix completion-based methods, this approach obtains the solution directly from the received measurements. Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms other recovery methods including matrix completion, independent vector recovery, and block-sparse recovery methods.

This research paper introduces a novel compensation method for estimating temperature using a voltage disturbance observer. One of the key challenges in motor driving systems is to monitor the temperature of motors to avoid demagnetization and dielectric breakdown. Typically, thermal sensors are used to obtain temperature information, but this approach increases costs and motor size. As an alternative, researchers have proposed a method to estimate the temperature based on the motor model without using thermal sensors. However, voltage disturbances can cause issues with this approach. To overcome these issues, the paper suggests a new method for compensating voltage disturbances and verifies its effectiveness through experiments.

This paper investigates the synthesis of edit functions for opacity enforcement using abstraction methods to reduce computational complexity. Edit functions are used to alter system outputs by erasing or inserting events in order to prevent violations of opacity. We introduce two abstraction methods, called opaque observation equivalence and opaque bisimulation, that are used to abstract the original system and its observer before calculating edit functions. We present a set of results on abstraction for opacity and its enforcement by edit functions that prove that edit functions synthesized from abstracted models are “equivalent” to ones synthesized from original ones. Our approach leverages the technique of edit function synthesis using the All Edit Structure from prior works.

The blooming of the Internet of Things has led to the creation of increasingly smart buildings, where tasks such as adjusting lighting to ambient sunlight are automated through the use of intelligent LED lighting systems. However, this has brought about blurring effects that may significantly impact the effectiveness of visible light localization. To combat this, we propose the use of the DIMLOC system in smart buildings, which is a high-precision visible light localization system designed to function under dimmable LEDs.

Our proposed system focuses on a novel imaging processing framework utilizing second-order polynomial fitting, histogram equalization, and Sobel filter techniques to address the blurring effects. We then build upon this framework and develop a new algorithm based on vision analysis and scaling factor that utilizes only two LEDs for positioning. We have successfully created a DIMLOC prototype out of off-the-shelf components, and extensive experiments conducted to validate our system demonstrate its ability to achieve centimeter precision, up to 4.5 cm.

The implementation of our proposed system in smart buildings will undoubtedly broaden the application scenarios of visible light localization in this era of the Internet of Things.

The author introduces the top picks selection of papers in computer architecture that were published in 2018. This is the 16th year of publication of what has now become a tradition in the computer architecture community. Each year, the MICRO Top Picks selection committee, which I chaired for this year, selects 12 papers for this special issue, to highlight for the IEEE Micro readership, a sample of the papers published in 2018 that have architectural contributions of potentially high impact and significance. After a short review of the selection process the papers are briefly summarized.

To address the reliability and latency challenges of future mixed sub-6GHz/millimeter wave (mmWave) fifth generation (5G) cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks, a semi-blind UL/DL decoupling concept is introduced. This concept involves gathering measurements of the Rician K-factor and DL reference signal receive power (RSRP) for both 2.6GHz and 28GHz frequency bands, and training a non-linear support vector machine (SVM) algorithm. The trained SVM algorithm is then used to predict the target frequencies and access points (APs) that can be independently used for the UL and DL. The proposed classifier has an accuracy score of 95% for few training samples. This approach allows for fast radio resource management in both uplink and downlink while also dealing with blockage situations.

The System-by-Design (SbD) paradigm provides an efficient solution to complex electromagnetic (EM) design problems. By decomposing the synthesis into several interconnected functional blocks, while considering the overall system functionality as the design target, significant time savings can be achieved in comparison to standard approaches. This is made possible by using a fast surrogate model to explore the solution space, rather than relying on fullwave simulations. 

To further improve the accuracy of the predictor and guide the optimization algorithm, an adaptive sampling strategy is proposed. By adapting the sampling to the behavior of the predictor, the accuracy of the model is enhanced, leading to better results. 

To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SbD strategy, a numerical example is shown for the design of large-scale airborne radomes. The results demonstrate the superiority of the SbD approach in terms of both design efficiency and accuracy. By leveraging the benefits of fast surrogate models and adaptive sampling, the SbD paradigm offers a powerful tool for solving complex EM design problems.

Software-Defined Systems provide ample opportunities for deploying programmable networks and large-scale services distributed across clouds. By utilizing both Software-Defined Networking and Network Function Virtualization principles, these systems make use of various enabling technologies, such as containers and container orchestrators, that simplify the integration and management of virtual components while offering a high level of flexibility, isolation, and performance. As major tech companies are investing heavily in these technologies, smaller businesses are struggling to select the most suitable platforms and tools to implement them. 

To address this, this paper offers a three-fold contribution. It begins by exploring the state of the art in container engines and container orchestrators. It then analyzes the main supporting tools that offer advanced and additional features to enhance container networking. Finally, the study defines a set of qualitative Key Performance Indicators to conduct a preliminary comparison of the reviewed technologies. The aim of the study is to provide high-level guidelines and constructive comments to assist in the wider adoption of Software-Defined Systems.

This paper deals with the problem of discrete time sliding mode control with an external trajectory generator. We consider a disturbed discrete time dynamical system and present a new reference trajectory based sliding mode control strategy. We adopt the nonswitching type definition of the quasi-sliding mode and, following the main stream of research on the topic, we use the reaching law approach to design the control. We propose generating the desired trajectory of the system externally, using a new nonswitching type reaching law. Then, we define a new desired trajectory following reaching law for the disturbed plant. We demonstrate that the trajectory following reaching law limits the impact of external disturbances and model uncertainties on the system to one step, whereas in the existing control methods the performance of the system is influenced by all disturbance values from the beginning of the control process. Therefore, our control strategy guarantees a reduction of the width of the ultimate band and increases the system's robustness. The results of our study are verified with a simulation example.

In this paper, we introduce a new approach for achieving global stabilization of linear systems that experience actuator saturation, using a model-free algorithm. Our technique involves the application of gain-scheduled low gain feedback control laws that prevent saturation and promote global stabilization. To develop these control laws, we use parameterized algebraic Riccati equations (AREs) as the framework. However, we avoid the need for knowledge of the system dynamics by using reinforcement learning techniques to find the solution of the parameterized ARE. We present an iterative Q-learning algorithm that searches for an optimal value of the low gain parameter and solves the parameterized ARE an appropriate number of times. Our proposed algorithm is shown to achieve model-free global stabilization under bounded controls, while also converging to the solution of the ARE. Additionally, the approach requires neither an initially stabilizing policy nor is affected by any excitation noise bias. Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

This work is devoted to the study of issues of improving information systems efficiency by utilization of certain procedures for managing of information resources distribution. The problem of distribution of applications for information provision in information subsystems of automated control systems in various functioning conditions are considered. This paper reveals the main provisions of the method of adaptive information resources control in the automated control system with loss of performance in network infrastructure nodes.

The performance of an antenna array is determined by the maximum value of its sidelobe beampattern, or radiation pattern in the power domain. In this study, we use extreme value theory (EVT) to approximate the maximum sidelobe value, or peak sidelobe level, for array antenna elements with random phase centers. An expression for the beampattern distribution at each angle in the array field of view is first found before utilizing the exponential distribution approximation to apply EVT with samples of the beampattern. We also obtain the pointwise convergence of the difference between the beampattern and exponential distributions in the limit of a large number of antennas. We provide a bound for the difference between the maximum sample of the beampattern and its true maximum in the sidelobe region. Overall, this study highlights the importance of understanding the maximum value of an antenna array's sidelobe beampattern in determining its performance.

This brief deals with finding the necessary conditions which should be met by the polynomials appeared in the admittance functions passively realizable by using RLC components and two fractional elements. These conditions include structurally necessary equalities/specifications and positive-realness-based inequalities which should be satisfied by the involved polynomials. In the realizable cases, the acceptable region for choosing the pseudo inductances/capacitances of fractional elements is found from the obtained conditions.

Intelligent networks are regarded as existing networks incorporating some intelligent mechanisms such as cognitive and cooperative approaches to improve network performance. Security is highly essential in intelligent networks but has received less attention so far. In this article, we propose a framework that enables a secure intelligent network with the assistance of cloud-assisted privacy-preserving machine learning. In the framework, the cloud server can first generate a model using outsourced machine learning algorithms and then process testing data from the network with the generated model in real time, which reflects to the network and makes it more intelligent. At the same time, the proposal guarantees the security and privacy of both the training data and the testing data in the sense that the proposed framework takes advantage of differential privacy to perform privacy-preserving data analysis and homomorphic encryption to conduct valid operations over encrypted data. The performance evaluations of the core primitives employed in the framework including differential privacy and homomorphic encryption algorithms demonstrate the practicability of our proposal.

Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) are widely acknowledged as an important strategy for corporate growth. However, the process of M&A involves a lot of effort and the success rate is not high. Therefore, scientific research is urgently needed to aid M&A decision-making. The present study focuses on M&A categorization as a fundamental research strategy for accurate prediction and recommendation of M&A deals. The study utilizes M&A data, financial data, and corporate data for comprehensive analysis. In particular, we designed 13 features comprising acquirer features, target features, and their relationship features. We employed the K-means clustering technique to separate M&A cases and identified five distinct clusters of M&A deals. Each cluster exhibited unique characteristics according to the 13 features. Our results showed that these features could be effectively used for future M&A prediction and recommendation. Overall, the findings of this study shed light on the crucial role of M&A categorization in enhancing the success rate of M&A deals.

In this paper we aim to solve a problem which many home-cooks encounter when searching for recipes online. Namely, finding recipes which best fit a handy set of ingredients while at the same time follow healthy eating guidelines. This task is especially difficult since the lion's share of online recipes have been shown to be unhealthy. In this paper we propose a novel algorithm which utilizes machine-learning techniques such as neural networks and matrix factorization in order to model the interactions between ingredients and their proportions within recipes for the purpose of offering suitable recommendations. The empirical results support the method's intuition and showcase its ability to retrieve healthier recipes.

This paper deals with the problem of adaptive estimation, i.e. the simultaneous estimation of the state and parameters, for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems. A nonlinear adaptive sliding-mode observer is proposed based on a nonlinear parameter estimation algorithm. The nonlinear parameter estimation algorithm provides a rate of convergence faster than exponential while the sliding-mode observer ensures ultimate boundness for the state estimation error attenuating the effects of the external disturbances. Linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are provided for the synthesis of the adaptive observer and some simulation results show the feasibility of the proposed approach.

In a wireless sensor network (WSN), multiple battery-operated sensors gather information and transmit it to a central controller. However, this poses a challenge in terms of minimizing re-transmissions and increasing sensor sleep time while still maintaining timely information. Recently, the concept of the age of information (AoI) has been introduced as a measure of information freshness at the controller. This problem becomes even more complex under the threat of in-band full duplex jammers that can detect transmissions and inject interference in real-time. 

To combat these jammers, a decision-making policy has been developed for the central controller that aims to minimize re-transmissions while maintaining AoI. Three modes for sensors have been introduced - sleep, silent, and transmit – to enhance the anti-jamming capability of the WSN. The operating mode of each sensor and the decision to switch to a new channel are optimized using the Markov Decision Process. The proposed strategy has been validated through extensive simulations, considering various parameters such as switching cost, transmission cost, failure to meet AoI cost, and channel quality. The results demonstrate the superiority of this strategy in efficiently managing WSNs in the presence of in-band full duplex jammers.

The potential of using social networks to solve searching-for-a-target (SFT) problems, such as finding missing individuals, is widely recognized. Incentives can play a key role in encouraging individuals to participate actively and promote efficient search strategies. However, previous research into incentives for information propagation in social networks has not focused specifically on the importance of a clear propagation direction based on a specific goal.

To address this gap, we propose an effective contribution-driven information propagation incentive mechanism (IPIM) that harnesses the power of ego networks to solve SFT problems. Our approach uses an all-pay auction-inspired model to determine the propagation of alters within each ego network. We then introduce a novel algorithm, known as the node propagation utility, which focuses the propagation towards the target in a cost-effective and resource-efficient way.

Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that IPIM is truthful, individually rational, and feasible within budget constraints. We conducted simulations using real and public social datasets, which demonstrate significant improvements in efficiency compared with existing incentive mechanisms. Specifically, the IPIM achieved a success rate increase of 951.18%, a reduction of 215.65% in propagation hops, and a scale increase of 514.41% in participation.

In conclusion, our research demonstrates the potential of IPIM to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of SFT problem solving by leveraging the power of social networks and incorporating clear and focused propagation strategies.

This paper proposes a solution to the challenge of industrial robotic system control using visual information obtained from stereo camera monitoring robots' workcells. A comprehensive method of extracting an object's positional information is described, along with supplementary functions that enhance the detection process when multiple objects are present in the workcell. Additionally, the paper presents a description of a camera-robot system incorporating the extraction process outlined above.

A class of nonlinear equation solvers known as the holomorphically embedding method, when applied to the power-flow problem is theoretically guaranteed to find an operable solution to the power-flow problem, if one exists, provided rather mild conditions are satisfied. To date, all of the published approaches use a Gauss-Seidel-based fixed-point form as the starting point for the embedding. We show that a fixed-point form based on a Newton-Raphson scheme may also be use and has some advantageous properties when attempting to find the saddle-node bifurcation point (SNBP).

Assessing Mental Workload (MW) plays a critical role in many mentally demanding occupations such as first responders, air traffic control, among others. It is used to quantify an operator's cognitive abilities. Recently, there has been a growing demand for wearable-based MW monitoring for real-time feedback and human performance augmentation. However, most previous studies have focused on stationary users, while realistic applications require ambulant users under varying types and levels of physical activities. The presence of movement artifacts can interfere with the quality of signals measured, which raises doubts about their efficacy in situ.

To overcome this issue, we conducted a study to compare the performance of several automated artifact removal algorithms for electroencephalograms (EEG), as well as the robustness of two classical feature sets for MW assessment. We evaluated the effectiveness of these algorithms for MW assessment under varying physical activity levels. The results showed that the performance of the artifact removal algorithms varied based on the type and level of physical activity levels. While some algorithms outperformed others under low physical activity, different algorithms performed better under high physical activity.

In conclusion, our study examined the performance of several automated artifact removal algorithms for EEG in MW assessment. The results indicate that the choice of algorithm depends on the type and level of physical activity. Therefore, the technology used for MW assessment needs to be robust and adaptable to the user's movement during operation. Furthermore, the development of further future studies is essential to determine the compatibility and reliability of wearables under different physical activity scenarios.

In this paper, we examine the challenge of state reconstruction in large-scale traffic networks through the use of heterogeneous sensor data. To start, we address the constraints regarding the number and location of fixed sensors required for the unique reconstruction of all flows in the network. With partial information on turning ratios, we calculate the minimum number of sensors necessary to solve the problem, followed by the presentation of a linear time algorithm for their allocation in a network. Utilizing these outcomes along with floating car data, we present a technique for reconstructing all traffic density and flow. Finally, we test these algorithms in a simulated Manhattan-like network.

Energy efficiency is a vital factor that is contributing in the implementing of IOT, since IOT devices are powered by batteries or energy harvesting sources, thus it's very important to extend the lifetime of the overall network. This can be achieved using energy efficient techniques which have sorted into five types regarding the ISO model. One of them is the sleep/wakeup schemes which are considered in this paper. Duty-cycling, wake-up radios, and topology control were discussed and some of the newest works have been reviewed. However, every technique has its own limitations and advantages. This paper also determines some of the open research areas that companies between energy efficiency and some new technologies, standards or network and application types.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is changing the way information is processed and stored. With latency-sensitive applications and vast amounts of data produced on the edge of the network, data is increasingly being processed where it is generated, resulting in emerging network topologies that include both large data centers and micro data centers on the edge.

However, managing multiple data centers needed to execute large-scale applications like those in smart cities, self-driving vehicles, and telemedicine is becoming increasingly complex. The challenge is to deploy applications that meet user requirements such as Quality of Service parameters (e.g., latency) while minimizing energy consumption required to process the application.

This talk will explore the research challenges related to deploying real-time analytics on the edge of the network.

Situation Awareness is the capability of understanding what is happening in order to make informed and correct decisions. The process for gaining good levels of Situation Awareness is defined as situation assessment. One of the main tasks of situation assessment is the identification of the situation. Expert-based and learning-based techniques can be used to automatically identify a situation by processing the available information. In this paper, we propose an approach for supporting situation assessment using Dominance-based Rough Set analysis to learn decision rules from a set of example decisions made by experts, hybridizing both expert-based and learning-based techniques. A case study for Maritime Situation Awareness demonstrates the capability of the approach to support the situation assessment.

The constrained command tracking problem for the cloud robotic system with unknown bounded time-varying delays is considered. Based on a novel predictor-observer approach, a command governor is proposed to modify the received command in order to guarantee the constraint enforcement of remote robot. We firstly use a prediction algorithm in the forward channel to generate a virtual command, which is close to the original one as much as possible when the danger of constraint violation exists. Then, to deal with the measurement delay and disturbance in the backward channel, interval estimations of the system states are applied instead of delayed measurements in the prediction algorithm of the command governor. The constraints can be rigorously enforced with the upper and lower estimations. The efficiency of the proposed approach is demonstrated by simulations in the case of a single-degree-of-freedom manipulator.

The adoption of complex and technologically advanced integrated circuits (ICs) in safety-critical applications, such as the automotive industry, has resulted in the need for new solutions to guarantee the required reliability targets. One such solution involves performing in-field tests to detect faults that may arise during the electronic circuit's lifespan. Software test libraries (STLs) have become increasingly popular in this scenario. These libraries provide suitable code that can run on the system's CPU to detect permanent faults in both the CPU and the system.

To assess the effectiveness of STLs, fault simulation is performed. This allows for the computation of fault coverage, such as stuck-at faults. However, fault simulation of STLs is a different problem compared to the classical fault simulation of test stimuli. Effective algorithms and tools are available for classical fault simulation, but this is not the case for STLs. Fault simulation of STLs can be highly computationally expensive, which necessitates the need for solutions to reduce the computational cost.

This paper explains why fault simulation of STLs is distinct from classical fault simulation, explores the computational expense involved, and provides an overview of potential solutions to reduce computational costs while considering accuracy as well.

To effectively address the issue of noise pollution caused by traffic, it is essential to have a reliable method of predicting the levels of noise that will be produced. Over the years, different mathematical models have been proposed based on experimental data obtained through regression analysis. However, more advanced techniques such as soft computing can potentially improve the accuracy of these models.

This study focuses on the application of soft computing techniques in predicting road traffic noise levels. Two models were developed using neural networks and optimization methods based on swarm intelligence and evolutionary algorithms. The predictions made by these models were compared to experimental data collected through traffic noise monitoring in an urban environment, as well as to predictions made by commonly used traffic noise models.

The statistical analysis of differences between the measured and calculated noise levels shows that the soft computing techniques employed in this study are effective in improving the accuracy of traffic noise prediction models. This suggests that these methods can be utilized in the development of more reliable models for controlling noise pollution caused by traffic.

In this work, we propose a deep neural network to forecast single-trial event-related electroencephalographic (EEG) activity using observed pre-event EEG data. Forecasting event-related potentials (ERPs) have a number of potential benefits for brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. Accurate predictions of neural responses can reduce the latencies of neural signal classification algorithms and closed-loop feedback systems. Various models of ERPs propose that there exists a causal dependency between post-event neural responses and ongoing pre-event neural dynamics. Accordingly, we implement a deep neural network that extracts features from pre-event data in order to predict a single-trial ERP. To capture the variability of a single trial, the network constructs the post-event waveform in two parts: 1) generating ongoing neural activity and 2) generating event-related components comprising the ERP. We evaluate our model by forecasting 500 milliseconds of single channel post-event data from a Rapid Series Visual Presentation (RSVP) task. Our results indicate a significant increase in forecasting performance compared to baseline methods, suggesting that deep neural networks can extract informative features from pre-event EEG data in order to generate a prediction of the post-event waveform.

Natural scenic images often contain valuable textual information that can provide insight into the scene. However, processing this text can be challenging due to variations in font, size, skewness, and noise within the captured image. The task of text extraction is essential in further processing, and has been the focus of much research in recent years. This article highlights the various extraction methods used for text in both Indian and non-Indian scripts, providing a comprehensive overview of the state of the art and future directions in this field. It will be of great use to academicians and practitioners alike, seeking to further develop and refine text extraction techniques in scenic image processing.

Mobile devices usually access the internet through a wireless station such as a Wi-Fi access point. However, when multiple devices connect to the same station, their bandwidth is shared, resulting in a decrease in throughput. To address this issue, a traffic distribution mechanism is necessary. This paper proposes a dynamic traffic distribution system for multiple mobile devices using MultiPath TCP (MPTCP) to connect to the internet via a VPN server. The VPN server monitors the conditions of all stations and switches some paths between the server and devices accordingly. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively distributes traffic among multiple devices.

When deploying body sensor networks (BSNs), it is important to dynamically tune the sampling rates to meet application requirements and conserve energy. However, this can result in variable data rates and an efficient resource allocation is needed to maintain reliable transmission for all traffic loads. We propose a BSN system that addresses this joint problem by autonomously detecting user behaviors and triggering dynamic sampling and resource scheduling via an adaptive MAC scheduling scheme. Our cross-layer scheme uses time-slotted channel hopping in IEEE 802.15.4 to determine the best slotframe length and allocate timeslots. We implemented our approach on a BSN testbed and evaluated its effectiveness in terms of throughput, packet delivery ratio, and energy per bit, which demonstrated that our approach ensures reliable data transmission and energy efficiency compared to existing techniques.

This paper presents a novel hybrid variable selection method, named F-Score with proposed threshold, aimed at improving the recognition accuracy of radiated magnetic field signals generated by electrical discharges in insulation systems, particularly in insulators of high-voltage lines and power transformers. The proposed method reduces the duration of both training and testing phases, while maintaining high accuracy. The support vector machine (SVM) classifier was employed to test the proposed method on a dataset of 161 signals, with 106 signals used for training and 55 signals for testing. The experimental results demonstrate a significant reduction in the number of variables, combined with a substantial improvement in recognition rate, compared with the pre-selection rate. The proposed F-Score with proposed threshold method integrated with SVM is a promising approach for electric discharge signal recognition, and can enhance the reliability and efficiency of electrical insulation systems.

With abundant spectrum resources, the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band has emerged as a leading candidate for fulfilling the requirements of faster data rates and lower latency for future automotive networks. However, the usage of mmWave directional transmission and the diverse mobility of vehicles prompt frequent beam realignment, which in turn increases the beamforming overhead and diminishes the time available for data transmission. This paper explores an energy-angle domain access and transmission frame structure for mmWave vehicle-to-everything communications, which comprises two phases: initial access and data transmission.

In view of the transmission interruption dilemma caused by blockage, an energy-angle domain initial access scheme is proposed, in which signals are classified using various directions with multi-power levels. Several performance measures are subsequently computed to assess the proposed scheme. Subsequently, the access time-throughput tradeoff problem is mathematically formulated, and it is demonstrated that optimal access time exists, yielding the highest throughput for data transmission. Furthermore, a binary-decision beam tracking scheme is developed to ensure sustained directional link connection in the data transmission phase. To verify our stance's accuracy and our proposed strategies' superiority, numerical evaluations and simulations were conducted.

Evolutionary circuit design is a process that requires a lot of time, especially for circuits that are large in scale. In order to address this issue, a distributed computation framework for evolutionary circuit design via parallel genetic algorithm has been designed in this study. The framework enables tasks to be distributed and collected by utilizing a communication network structure using client-server mode. Results from a series of experiments have shown that this framework has a better performance in seeking circuits that satisfy designer specified performance goals with a high efficiency, great flexibility, and strong fault tolerance.

Research on data confidentiality, integrity and availability is gaining momentum in the ICT community, due to the intrinsically insecure nature of the Internet. While many distributed systems and services are now based on secure communication protocols to avoid eavesdropping and protect confidentiality' the techniques usually employed in distributed simulations do not consider these issues at all. This is probably due to the fact that many real-world simulators rely on monolithic, offline approaches and therefore the issues above do not apply. However, the complexity of the systems to be simulated, and the rise of distributed and cloud based simulation, now impose the adoption of secure simulation architectures. This paper presents a solution to ensure both anonymity and confidentiality in distributed simulations. A performance evaluation based on an anonymized distributed simulator is used for quantifying the performance penalty for being anonymous. The obtained results show that this is a viable solution.

Identification of a person based on their handwriting has been a challenging problem for a long time, but the application of this method is invaluable in various fields such as forensics and historical documents. Deep-learning-based approaches have shown immense potential as feature extractors for massive amounts of data when compared to traditional approaches. In this study, a deep transfer convolutional neural network has been employed to identify writers using handwriting text line images written in both English and Arabic languages. Several layers of the CNN have been evaluated to determine their impact on writer identification rates. The study focused on transfer learning using ImageNet as the base dataset and QUWI dataset as the target dataset. The sliding window approach has been used to generate patches as the input unit to the CNN model, while AlexNet architecture has been employed to extract discriminating visual features from multiple patch representations resulting from enhanced pre-processing techniques. Support vector machine classifiers have been used to analyze extracted features. Data augmentation techniques like contours, negatives, and sharpness have been employed to enhance the target dataset and limit the chances of over-fitting. The results revealed that the highest accuracy was attained using a freeze Conv5 layer, achieving 92.78% on English, 92.20% on Arabic and 88.11% on the combination of Arabic and English, respectively.

Nowadays, social media is an inseparable part of people's lives, with platforms like Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, and many others. Almost everyone has multiple social media accounts on their smartphone, which makes social media an excellent source of data for collecting public opinion instantly. This paper discusses sentiment analysis focusing on the user's satisfaction with telecommunication operators' data services in Indonesia, using official accounts or relevant keywords. To improve the accuracy of classification, the author used Support Vector Machine with TF-IDF weighting, POS Tagging, and Negative Handling. This study presents a system of sentiment analysis classification regarding the operator's data service user's satisfaction level using the support vector machine method. The SVM used in this analysis utilized an RBF kernel (Radial Basis Function) following preprocessing, POS Tagging, and TF-IDF weighting. The results of the study showed an average f1-score rate of 95.43%, precision of 92.45%, recall of 93.90%, and accuracy of 99.01%.

As the volume of data available for analysis grows, feature selection is becoming a vital part of ensuring accurate classification results. In classification problems, selecting a small number of features reduces computational complexity, but selecting the right features is important to maintain a high level of accuracy. In this paper, we present a feature selection method based on hybrid improved quantum-behavior particle swarm optimization, called HI-BQPSO. The HI-BQPSO combines a filtering method with an improved quantum-behavior particle swarm optimization algorithm to greatly reduce the dimensionality of the data so as to overcome some of the shortcomings of BQPSO. Tests were conducted on nine gene expression datasets and 36 UCI datasets to evaluate and compare the classification accuracy of the HI-BQPSO’s selected feature subsets against four other algorithms. The results, using a variety of different classifiers, show that the HI-BQPSO significantly reduces the number of features required for classification while maintaining higher levels of accuracy in many cases.

The Multi-Processors System-on-Chip (MPSoCs) has emerged as a vital technology for new computational paradigms such as Internet-of-Things (IoT) and Machine Learning. However, the continuous deployment of MPSoC devices in critical and sensitive applications poses a significant threat to data confidentiality and privacy. Malware infections and code injection during booting and operation time can compromise the security of MPSoCs. A persistent threat to MPSoCs security is the configuration of critical MPSoC infrastructures such as security frameworks. 

To address this issue, we propose a secure infrastructure that ensures secure booting and dynamic operation of MPSoCs. Our approach integrates lightweight security infrastructure based on firewalls and lightweight authentication. We explored the design space of the security infrastructure to evaluate its impact on the overall performance and cost of the system. In contrast to previous works, we explored fine and coarse-grained reconfiguration and showed the impact of the security manager's location on the overall system performance. 

Our proposed infrastructure provides enhanced security features for MPSoCs, ensuring data confidentiality and privacy of critical and sensitive applications. It offers flexibility and high parallelism for new computational paradigms such as IoT and Machine Learning. With this infrastructure, MPSoCs can operate securely, ensuring the integrity and authenticity of the data being processed.

In industrial wireless sensor networks (IWSNs), it is crucial to transmit monitoring data generated by field devices (FDs) to the gateway in a timely and reliable manner. Previous research has focused on the convergecast problem with a global channel set, where unreliable channels are blacklisted. However, in practical industrial environment, wireless channels have different local available channel sets (LACSs) due to the location-dependent characteristics. In this paper, we address the LACS-based convergecast scheduling problem in IWSNs with tree topologies. 

We first formulate the convergecast scheduling problem using integer programming. We then propose a novel method to calculate priorities for each FD, and design two heuristic rules for allocating channels to FDs. These rules maximize the number of concurrent transmissions in each time slot while considering the priority of each FD and the constraints in the integer programming formulation. Finally, we propose an LACS-based convergecast scheduling (LCS) algorithm to generate efficient schedules for IWSNs in polynomial time. 

The simulation results show that our proposed algorithm performs better than existing works in terms of latency for different scenarios. Our LCS algorithm shows promising results for practical usage in industrial wireless sensor networks.

The recent growth in the maritime industry stemming to increase in global commerce as well as searching for hydrocarbons at offshore locations, the high data rate and cost affordable maritime communication is acquired. A mesh network is envisaged for maritime communications because of its expanded coverage, self-healing, and high-capacity. With the development of multi-radio technology, the frequency interference can be decreased sharply with proper channel assignment. The static channel assignment optimization is often applied to decrease the wireless frequency interference which is known as an NP-hard problem. In this paper, we focus on the static channel assignment issue and propose a heuristic algorithm to solve the optimization problem. The problem is addressed by assigning channels to communication links to minimize the interference from overall network. A modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed to optimize the problem, and a new merging solution is adopted to reassign channels for nodes, which violate the radio constraints. Multi-radio simulation is performed in NS-3 to validate the effectiveness of the proposed channel assignment algorithm. The results show that the algorithm is able to find an optimized assignment with fewer iterations than the previous work and improve network performance.

In this paper, a new wideband/narrowband fusion-based motion estimation method is proposed for maneuvering target. In the fusion scheme, a fast motion parameters estimation method based on cross-correlation of adjacent echoes (CCAE) is adopted as the wideband estimation method. The narrowband estimation method is the maximum likelihood estimation with Newton's method (MN method). The proposed method mainly includes three steps. First, the velocity and acceleration of the target are estimated by CCAE. Second, the velocity and acceleration estimated by CCAE are adopted as the initial velocity and final acceleration of MN method, respectively. Finally, the high precision velocity and distance of the target are estimated by MN method. The proposed fusion method has two advantages. First, due to the large scope of the unambiguous velocity of CCAE, the velocity ambiguity problem of MN method is solved. Second, the three dimensional (3D) search in MN method is reduced to two dimensional (2D) search. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed fusion method achieves similar estimation performances on distance and velocity with much lower computational cost, compared with the MN method.

The purpose of this paper is to introduce the concept and outcomes of Blended Learning in the training process for directly productive employees. Blended Learning is a modern teaching method commonly used by universities, and we applied it in an automotive factory setting. In this day and age, technology and IT have become vital components of the learning infrastructure to educate employees scattered over wide areas. Therefore, we chose to use the Blended Learning concept in an automotive production environment to prepare individuals for the Industry 4.0 approach. 

The implementation of Blended Learning in an automotive factory led to an increase in knowledge about Lean methods and the active participation of employees in the continuous improvement process. This involvement significantly improved production performance and productivity, and quality and waste reduced, which are crucial elements of Industry 4.0.

Frequency channel allocation is a vital technique used to improve the performance of cellular networks. In this study, we focus on the channel allocation problem in a 5G multi-cell system. Our network is heterogeneous and accommodates cellular users, micro-cell users, and device-to-device communications coexisting within the macro cell's radio range. Our approach aims to maximize the aggregate transmission rate by utilizing channel diversity and managing both inter-cell, typical of cellular networks, and intra-cell interference generated by nonorthogonal transmissions of small-cell and D2D users.

We model the allocation problem as a potential game, and we propose a novel decentralized solution. The Nash equilibria of the potential game correspond to local optima of the objective function, which helps us in developing a better response dynamic based on a message passing approach, ensuring that our scheme's convergence is enforced. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of our approach in terms of convergence time and achievable rate under various configurations.

Distributed energy resources (DER) systems introduce uncertainties in the electrical grid that cannot be addressed by classical deterministic methods. Power system analytic tools, such as Load Flow (LF), should be revisited to address such uncertainties and dependencies. Probabilistic Load Flow (PLF) provides a solution to this problem by handling these uncertainties as random variables, which addresses the rising need for fast and accurate sampling methods. Among the existing methods, the Unscented Transform (UT) has provided reliable and fast estimations. In this paper, three variants of PLF based on the UT method, with the effects of their weighting and scaling parameters are described, analyzed and compared in the IEEE 30 test case.

In many cases, pattern-based classifiers are highly accurate and provide an explanation of the result in terms of the patterns used for classification. However, they struggle with class imbalance problems as there are significantly fewer objects belonging to one class. This can bias the classification towards the majority class. To address this issue, we propose an algorithm that discovers cost-sensitive patterns in class imbalance problems and a pattern-based classifier uses these patterns for classification. Our approach combines pattern discovery with the cost-sensitive method for class imbalance problems. Our experiments show that our proposal obtains cost-sensitive patterns that lead to significantly lower misclassification costs than using patterns mined by other state-of-the-art pattern miners. Additionally, our proposed pattern-based classifier is suitable for working with cost-sensitive patterns.

Traditional analog circuit fault diagnosis usually consists of feature extraction, feature selection and fault classifier. However, fault feature extraction and selection take much manual effort, which make the design of the fault diagnosis system complicated and not universal. This paper proposes an analog circuit fault diagnosis method based on Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). The proposed method uses the single pulse as the stimulus signal to circuit-under-test (CUT), and then the raw time domain response of CUT is directly sampled to construct fault samples, which are inputted into the ELM network to obtain fault diagnosis results. The experimental results show that the average diagnostic accuracies reach 100% and 99.5% on the Sallen-key band-pass filter circuit and the four opamp biquad high-pass filter circuit, respectively. The algorithm achieves good diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in the absence of feature extraction and selection.

Context-Aware (CA) systems have a wide range of applications, but they require Context Recognition (CR) that is accurate and based on real data. Currently, machine learning and deep learning approaches are used to collect "in-the-wild" datasets with ground truth labels. However, users sometimes assign the wrong or incomplete context labels, which reduces the quality of the dataset and lowers classification accuracy. To solve this problem, we present COMEX, an interactive visual analytics tool that helps analysts identify instances of mislabeled context data to improve the quality of CA datasets. We provide a categorization of mislabeling error types and develop linked visualizations with anomaly scores to provide insights into the dataset. Our approach was validated on an open source dataset and showed improvements in classification accuracy after excluding mislabeled data, identified using COMEX.

Plug-and-play priors (PnP) is a powerful framework for regularizing imaging inverse problems by using advanced denoisers within an iterative algorithm. Recent experimental evidence suggests that PnP algorithms achieve the state-of-the-art performance in a range of imaging applications. In this paper, we introduce a new online PnP algorithm based on the proximal gradient method (PGM). The proposed algorithm uses only a subset of measurements at every iteration, which makes it scalable to very large datasets. We present a new theoretical convergence analysis, for both batch and online variants of PnP-PGM, for denoisers that do not necessarily correspond to proximal operators. We also present simulations illustrating the applicability of the algorithm to image reconstruction in diffraction tomography. The results in this paper have the potential to expand the applicability of the PnP framework to very large datasets.

This demo showcases a hardware system for continuous speech recognition that utilizes the DeltaRNN accelerator for low latency RNN computation. The RNN network is trained on a dataset of augmented audio samples from TIDIGITS and achieves a remarkable label error rate of just 2.31%. The system is implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7100 FPGA with a clock rate of 1 MHz, and has an incremental RNN power consumption of only 30 mW. Visitors can test the system by speaking digits into a microphone connected to the FPGA, and the system continuously displays the classification outputs on a laptop screen in real time.

In this paper, we consider the uplink channel parameter estimation problem in the presence of pilot contamination for massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems. We propose a parallel factor (PARAFAC)-based estimation scheme, which exploits the low-rank property of massive MIMO channels caused by the finite scattering in a physical environment. Specifically, we first parameterize the channel in terms of three parameters, i.e., fading coefficients, directions of arrival (DOAs), and delays; thereby, the channel is characterized via three equivalent PARAFAC models. Then, the proposed PARAFAC-based scheme is developed, which jointly estimates these three channel parameters using an alternating least squares (ALS) algorithm. Therein, we certify the identifiability of the three channel parameters of the PARAFAC models to mitigate the pilot contamination and state the convergence of the ALS algorithm, which guarantees that the three channel parameters can be uniquely determined with the proposed scheme. Moreover, to further reduce the computational complexity, two advanced schemes are proposed by antenna selection and reducing the estimation frequency of DOAs and delays, respectively. Simulation results show that the proposed schemes can achieve both low computational complexities and close to optimal Cramer-Rao Bound performance.

Flatfoot is a common disease in children and juveniles. If the disease is not controlled and treated in time, it may last into adulthood, which can bring a great deal of inconvenience and even pain to daily life. In addition to the diagnosis of the disease simply by doctors and medical equipment, artificial intelligence has become a very promising auxiliary diagnostic tool. In this paper, a neural network with a simple structure is used to classify the foot data to achieve the function of diagnosing flatfoot. The presented neural network is termed as modified weights-and-structure-determination neural network (MWASDNN), of which the input weights are analytically determined by the pseudo-inverse method, while the output weights are randomly generated within a specified interval, and the number of hidden-layer neurons is determined by an incremental method. In addition, the stratified cross-validation method is introduced to choose the model structure that best fits the features of the data set, thereby improving the generalization performance and robustness of the MWASDNN. Utilizing the MWASDNN models to classify the foot data we collected, we finally get the accuracy of 84.31% and 85.29% on the left and right foot data, respectively. Besides, MWASDNN achieves the highest classification accuracy on our foot data set compared to some traditional neural networks, pattern classification methods, and two improved neural networks. These excellent results indicate that the MWASDNN is expected to be designed as a practical flatfoot diagnostic tool.

Surgeons normally need surgical scissors and tissue grippers to cut through a deformable surgical tissue. The cutting accuracy depends on the skills to manipulate these two tools. Such skills are part of basic surgical skills training as in the Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery. The gripper is used to pinch a point on the surgical sheet and pull the tissue to a certain direction to maintain the tension while the scissors cut through a trajectory. As the surgical materials are deformable, it requires a comprehensive tensioning policy to yield appropriate tensioning direction at each step of the cutting process. Automating a tensioning policy for a given cutting trajectory will support not only the human surgeons but also the surgical robots to improve the cutting accuracy and reliability. This paper presents a multiple pinch point approach to modelling an autonomous tensioning planner based on a deep reinforcement learning algorithm. Experiments on a simulator show that the proposed method is superior to existing methods in terms of both performance and robustness.

In addition to the ambient noise, the effective signal to noise ratio (ESNR) considers the impact of intercarrier interference (ICI) and channel estimation error, and it is shown to be more consistent than input SNR (ISNR) and pilot SNR (PSNR) in system performance indication. In this paper, the performance of ESNR of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system with orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) channel estimation is analyzed by building the relationship between the ESNR and the ISNR, ICI and so on. It is shown that for OMP with high delay grid resolution, ESNR indeed functions similarly as PSNR. Simulation results have demonstrated the correctness of our derivations.

Human motion measurement plays a critical role in the fields of motion analysis, virtual reality, and ergonomics design. With the advent of inertial measurement units (IMUs), it is now possible to measure human motion accurately. However, conventional IMU-based motion-capture systems only consider ground contact constraints, failing to consider the constraints between the user and the product. This study aims to develop a full-body motion estimation system that reflects the contact conditions between the user and the product based on user-specified contact constraints using IMUs.

We conducted experiments on walking and chair-sitting motions to validate the proposed system. The walking experiment showed that the estimated joint angles' average error ranged from 2.79±2.00 degrees for the right ankle to 9.55±6.04 degrees for the right hip. Furthermore, the chair-sitting experiment showed that our system could provide an accurate estimation of the sitting motion by reflecting the contact condition between the subject and the chair surfaces.

In conclusion, our findings indicate that the proposed system has the potential to accurately measure a wide variety of human motions while addressing the challenges posed by contact constraints. By doing so, the proposed system could contribute to enhancing the design of products, promoting ergonomics, and improving the development of virtual reality systems.

IoT is leading a digital revolution in both academia and industry. It brings convenience to people's daily lives; however, the issues of security and privacy of IoT become challenges. Blockchain, a decentralized database based on cryptographic techniques, is promising for IoT security, which may influence a variety of areas including manufacture, finance, and trading. The blockchain framework in an IoT system is an intriguing alternative to the traditional centralized model, which is struggling to meet some specified demands in IoT. In this article, we investigate typical security and privacy issues in IoT and develop a framework to integrate blockchain with IoT, which can provide great assurance for IoT data and various functionalities and desirable scalability including authentication, decentralized payment, and so on. We also suggest some possible solutions to these security and privacy issues in IoT based on blockchain and Ethereum to show how blockchain contributes to IoT.

Fault detection plays an important role in supervising the operation of robotic swarm systems. If faults are not detected, they can considerably affect the performance of the robot swarm. In this paper, we present a robust fault detection mechanism against noise and uncertainties in data, by merging the multiresolution representation of data using wavelets with the sensitivity to small changes of an exponentially weighted moving average scheme. Specifically, to monitor swarm robotics systems performing a virtual viscoelastic control model for circle formation task, the proposed mechanism is applied to the uncorrelated residuals form principal component analysis model. Monitoring results using a simulation data from ARGoS simulator demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved fault detection performances compared with the conventional approach.

Over the years, the analysis of big data in healthcare has played a vital role in providing cost-effective health care data and improving health services. However, with the enormous amount of data being generated constantly over a long period of time, the write performance and capability have been significantly affected. Retrieving data belonging to multiple clusters also remains a challenging issue as focusing only on a chosen cluster may result in data loss. To overcome this difficulty, this paper proposes a solution using the clustering of healthcare big data with the fuzzy c means algorithm. This algorithm works by allocating memberships for each data point equivalent to each and every cluster midpoint based on the distance between the midpoint and its data point. This fuzzy implementation helps to reduce data loss while clustering vast amounts of data.

Conventional robots have shown good positioning accuracy and reliability in multiple environments. However, the robots' lack of flexibility makes them unsuitable for application in certain areas. Thus, a soft robotic system should be considered due to its adaptivity and flexibility. This paper proposes a novel shape memory alloy (SMA)-actuated multiple degrees of freedom (DOF) soft robot, which theoretically supports a maximum of nine-DOF movement and good positioning accuracy. A motion test and positioning evaluation are conducted for the proposed multi-DOF soft robot. The structural design, control method, and analysis of the kinematics and the coordinate system are also given.

We propose a geometric reinforcement learning algorithm for real-time path planning for mobile sensor networks (MSNs) in the problem of reconstructing a spatial-temporal varying field described by the advection-diffusion partial differential equation. A Luenberger state estimator is provided to reconstruct the concentration field, which uses the collected measurements from a MSN along its trajectory. Since the path of the MSN is critical in reconstructing the field, a novel geometric reinforcement learning (GRL) algorithm is developed for the real-time path planning. The basic idea of GRL is to divide the whole area into a series of lattice to employ a specific time-varying reward matrix, which contains the information of the length of path and the mapping error. Thus, the proposed GRL can balance the performance of the field reconstruction and the efficiency of the path. By updating the reward matrix, the real-time path planning problem can be converted to the shortest path problem in a weighted graph, which can be solved efficiently using dynamic programming. The convergence of calculating the reward matrix is theoretically proven. Simulation results serve to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed GRL for a MSN.

In this paper we evaluate the suitability of handwriting patterns as potential biomarkers to model Parkinson's disease (PD). Although the study of PD is attracting the interest of many researchers around the world, databases to evaluate handwriting patterns are scarce and knowledge about patterns associated to PD is limited and biased to the existing datasets. This paper introduces a database with a total of 935 handwriting tasks collected from 55 PD patients and 94 healthy controls (45 young and 49 old). Three feature sets are extracted from the signals: neuromotor, kinematic, and nonlinear dynamic. Different classifiers are used to discriminate between PD and healthy subjects: support vector machines, k-nearest neighbors, and a multilayer perceptron. The proposed features and classifiers enable to detect PD with accuracies between 81% and 97%. Additionally, new insights are presented on the utility of the studied features for monitoring and detecting PD.

Aiming at the problems of the complex modeling, large amount and variety of data in the 3D modeling of viaducts and underpass tunnels in digital city, a novel approach is proposed for the rapid construction of 3D urban road network based on the two-dimensional raster map. Extract the centerlines of roads from the two dimensional raster map of different layers, then the rapid three-dimensional solid modeling of the viaducts and underpass tunnels could be realized through the parametric modeling and texture mapping. The experimental results show that the proposed parametric modeling approach of the urban road network could greatly reduce the modeling time, and improve the design efficiency with better flexibility and interactivity.

Petroleum exploration relies on various sources of information, including logging and drilling data, to identify underground strata. Real-time measurement parameters obtained from mud logging can facilitate the early discovery of oil and gas resources and prevent safety accidents during drilling. To address the challenge of formation misjudgment due to the fuzzy and random characteristics of big data from drilling element parameters, we propose a new method called the grey wolf optimization-support vector machine (GWO-SVM). By analyzing the relationship between logging data and formation, we use element content and Gamma-ray value to mine real-time data from the drilling site and establish a comprehensive estimation and prediction model for strata. The GWO-SVM model is applied to three actual wells, and the error analysis shows that the error range of the algorithm is within 10%. Compared to other models such as SVM and Particle Swarm Optimization-Support Vector Machine (PSO-SVM), GWO-SVM has higher accuracy and achieves faster convergence speed, stronger generalization effect and improves the identification accuracy of elements for the formation. The average accuracy of the GWO-SVM in stratum dynamic identification is 93.5%. Our model can support the logging system and improve its application strength.

Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and autonomous communicating smart devices, when combined with blockchain technologies, become the foundation for the implementation of a Machine-to-Machine (M2M) economy. This paper presents a M2M learning environment that creates an electric context where various energy providers and electric autonomous vehicles can interact with each other. Economic operations can be efficiently carried out through the IOTA cryptocurrency, which allows deep understanding of the transaction and blockchain technology underlying the M2M scenario.

Aquatic exercises have been demonstrated to benefit the facilitation of motor recovery and the enhancement of well-being in middle-aged adults and the elderly. Personalization, immersiveness, and biofeedback are key for amplifying and accelerating any rehabilitation process in neurological and orthopedic patients.
