However, a therapist can neither properly visualize nor monitor rehabilitation exercises executed under water, nor can he/she measure them. Therefore, this paper aims to provide adaptive biofeedback during aquatic exercises in order to enhance the training's effectiveness. A wearable biofeedback suit equipped with wearable underwater-resistant sensor nodes has been designed, produced, and tested. A dedicated algorithm for quantitatively extracting joint angles has been developed and validated against the optical tracking system. Multiple biofeedback modalities are proposed based on visual feedback: amplitude control with set target angles; velocity-amplitude control with set target angles and angular velocity; and velocity tutor with set target angles, a frequency value, and a rest period. Joint angles estimated using the sensor network are compared to those estimated using an optical tracking system with the root-mean-squared angle error between the two systems ranging from 4.0° to 6.3° and a significant correlation coefficient that is always greater than 0.99. Pilot tests during aquatic exercises executed in a thermal environment demonstrate the feasibility and usability of the complete system in the final working environment. The relevant angles are correctly calculated and monitored online during the exercises, and the tested subjects understand the implemented biofeedback modalities easily and follow them well as the SUS evaluation indicates.

We consider the problem of low-rank tensor decomposition of incomplete tensors that has applications in many data analysis problems, such as recommender systems, signal processing, machine learning, and image inpainting. In this paper, we focus on nonnegative tensor completion via low-rank Tucker decomposition for dealing with it. The specialty of our model is that the ranks of nonnegative Tucker decomposition are no longer constants, while they all become a part of the decisions to be optimized. Our solving approach is based on the penalty method and blocks coordinate descent method with prox-linear updates for regularized multiconvex optimization. We demonstrate the convergence of our algorithm. The numerical results on the three image datasets show that the proposed algorithm offers competitive performance compared with other existing algorithms even though the data is highly sparse.

Achieving consistency in a network is a crucial step towards ensuring resiliency, and is just as important as ensuring security. Attackers are now targeting small and crucial parts of a network such as network configurations and flow tables, which makes consistency verification even more critical. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is playing a significant role in providing fast responses to evolving threats. Software Defined Networking (SDN) offers a global overview of the network, and is adaptable and robust. Integrating AI and SDN leads to the creation of an Artificial Intelligence Resiliency System (ARS), the goal of which is to achieve consistency in the network. This paper suggests a new AI-based consistency verification system that will be part of ARS in the future. After testing different deep learning architectures, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) proved to be the best with an accuracy rate of 99.39% on the dataset and 96% in the consistency test scenario.

Text detection in natural scene image is challenging due to text variation in size, orientation, color and complex background, contrast, and resolution. In this paper, we focus on the long text detection in complex background. In order to deal with multi-scale text variation and exploit the recognition result to enhance the detection performance, we propose a detection and verification model based on SSD and encoder-decoder network for scene text detection. First, we present a text localization neural network based on SSD, which incorporates a text detection layer into the standard SSD model and can detect horizontal texts, especially long and dense Chinese texts in natural scenes more effectively. Second, a text verification model based on the encoder-decoder network is designed to recognize and verify the initial detection results, in order to eliminate non-text areas that are falsely detected as text areas. A series of experiments have been conducted on our constructed horizontal text detection dataset, which is composed of the horizontal text images in ICDAR 2017 Competition on Reading Chinese Text in the Wild (RCTW 2017) and some scene images taken by cameras. Compared with previous approaches, experimental results show that our method has achieved the highest recall rate of 0.784 and competitive precision rate in text detection, indicating the effectiveness of our proposed method.

Unit commitment (UC) problems are the most fundamental problems that system operators solve every day in both day-ahead and real-time markets to guarantee secure and economic operation. UC problems are usually formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) or a mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) model with binary variables representing ON/OFF statuses of generators, and is solved via Branch and bound (B&B) type algorithms. With the prosperity of applying semidefinite programing (SDP) in the power system field, researchers attempt to solve UC under the SDP framework by relaxing integrality requirements, seeking an optimal solution or a better lower bound than the traditional linear programming (LP) relaxation. This paper uses 2-order moment relaxation technique to reformulate UC problems as an SDP model, which can be solved by an interior point method. Considering significant computational burden by 2-order moment relaxation, a variable reduction strategy and two refined moment relaxation based UC models are further applied. The relationship among the proposed models in terms of their tightness is studied. In addition, a sufficient condition under which a solution is exact is stated. Numerical studies illustrate effect of the proposed models and potential applicability of the proposed models is also discussed.

The estimation of the direction of arrival for sources impinging on an antenna array has received large attention in mobile communications. In this article we explain how to acquire DOA information using Matrix Pencil (MP) with Uniform Circular Arrays (UCA) and Uniform Linear Array (ULA) based on the analysis of receiving signals. The role of Least Mean Square algorithm (LMS) is to focus the power in the required direction and nullify the interferer for the Uniform Linear Array (ULA). Simulation results show clearly that the matrix Pencil is very performant and stable compared to the published one.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of the latest advancements in pedestrian and evacuation dynamics, with the aim of gaining a better understanding of pedestrian motion behaviors from observation to simulation. Various data collection methods, comprising of field survey, controlled experiment, and animal experiment, are classified, and their interconnections and differences are explored. After data collection, pedestrians' complex behaviors marked by self-organization and movement data characterized by fundamental diagrams are studied. These findings can be employed in calibrating and validating pedestrian models.

The mathematical models for pedestrian dynamics at both tactical and operational levels are also highlighted. The simulation data produced by these models are able to reproduce pedestrian behaviors during observations, contributing to improved evacuation efficiency. The paper also discusses the applications of pedestrian models for behavior analysis, evacuation simulation, and layout design. Furthermore, future directions and challenges in the pedestrian and evacuation dynamics research are also presented.

Overall, this paper is a useful resource for researchers seeking to understand pedestrian and evacuation dynamics and to undertake further research in this field.

Time series forecasting is a crucial research problem in a variety of fields, including financial forecasting, traffic flow forecasting, medical monitoring, intrusion detection, anomaly detection, and air quality forecasting. In this paper, we present a deep learning framework for multivariate time series forecasting using a sequence-to-sequence approach that addresses the dynamic, spatial-temporal, and nonlinear characteristics of the data with an LSTM-based encoder-decoder architecture. Our experiments with air quality multivariate time series forecasting demonstrate that our model outperforms classic shallow learning and baseline deep learning models. Furthermore, the predicted PM2.5 value matches well with the ground truth value for both single timestep and multi-timestep forward forecasting conditions. Our results indicate that the proposed model is capable of achieving high accuracy when dealing with multivariate time series forecasting.

CoMP transmission and reception have been considered in cellular networks for enabling larger coverage, improved rates, and interference mitigation. To harness the gains of coordinated beamforming, fast information exchange over a backhaul connecting the cooperating BSs is required. In practice, the bandwidth and delay limitations of the backhaul may not be able to meet such stringent demands. These impairments motivate the study of cooperative approaches based only on local CSI that require minimal or no information exchange between the BSs. To this end, several distributed approaches are introduced for CB-CoMP. The proposed methods rely on the channel reciprocity and iterative spatially precoded over-the-air pilot signaling. We elaborate how F-B training facilitates distributed CB by allowing BSs and UEs to iteratively optimize their respective transmitters/receivers based on only locally measured CSI. The trade-off due to the overhead from the F-B iterations is discussed. We also consider the challenge of dynamic TDD where the UE-UE channel knowledge cannot be acquired at the BSs by exploiting channel reciprocity. Finally, standardization activities and practical requirements for enabling the proposed F-B training schemes in 5G radio access are discussed.

This paper presents a simulation analysis of data dissemination algorithms using existing Tendermint blockchain client-server system as an example. Algorithm analysis is connected with the Mempool component of the aforementioned system, which is responsible for disseminating data through the network. It is currently implemented in a way that it guarantees a certain outcome, yet it produces a large overhead. Simulation will show that one of the proposed solutions reduces the redundancy by 56.53% (or 3.62 times) on average, which is a significant improvement.

In the present-day setting of smart-grids, the concept of virtual power plants (VPPs) plays a pivotal role in enabling the seamless integration of renewable energy sources into the existing energy systems with a high level of penetration. A VPP is essentially an aggregation of decentralized, medium-scale power sources which include photovoltaic and wind power plants, combined heat and power units, demand-responsive loads, and storage systems, with a twofold objective. Firstly, it alleviates the dispatchability and stability issues on the external smart grid by operating as a single unit. Secondly, it enhances the flexibility of the entire networked units and helps traders to improve their forecasting and trading of renewable energy sources. 

This paper proposes a novel, distributed, decentralized prediction method for managing VPPs. The proposed approach effectively combines the concepts of neural networks and machine learning with a distributed architecture that is suitable for aggregation purposes of VPPs. The novelty of this approach lies in its ability to overcome the limitations of existing centralized approaches by re-distributing the computational workload among the constituent elements of the VPP. The proposed technique thereby enables a more efficient and accurate prediction of the energy demand and supply, leading to better resource allocation and utilization. 

In summary, our proposed approach presents a promising solution for the efficient and effective management of VPPs. With the expected increase in the integration of renewable energy sources into the energy systems, this distributed and decentralized approach can play a crucial role in fostering the smooth transition towards a more sustainable and resilient energy future.

Taxi services are an essential means of transportation for the public, and it is crucial to categorize payment types accurately. In New York City, the Yellow Taxi Trip Open Data contains significant amounts of unlabelled data, which poses a classification challenge. To address this issue, we utilized the Learning from Unlabelled Data (lfun) framework and a deep learning neural network as a classifier. Our experiments aimed to compare the performance of using the lfun framework versus traditional classification methods. 

Our findings demonstrated the superior performance of the lfun framework, achieving an f-measure average value of 0.725. These results underscore the potential of utilizing deep learning techniques in processing big data and addressing classification challenges. By improving the accuracy of categorizing payment types, taxi services can enhance their reliability and better serve their passengers.

The initialization process in Visual-Inertial SLAM (VI-SLAM) and Odometry (VI-O) is known to be less reliable compared to other parts of the pipeline. The first data readings are used to estimate the initial state which includes camera poses, IMU states and landmark positions. However, the accuracy and robustness of these estimated values are not always dependable resulting in high failure rates and/or initialization delays of up to tens of seconds. Such unreliable initialization can be a significant problem for AR systems, as it can lead to sub-optimal user experience or require impractical guided calibration.

To address this issue, our paper proposes a solution that utilizes a monocular-inertial sensor setup, which is commonly used in AR platforms. Our contributions include a general linear formulation to obtain an initialization seed, and a non-linear optimization scheme that incorporates gravity to refine the seed. Our experimental results, based on a public dataset, demonstrate that our approach greatly improves the accuracy and robustness of current VI state initialization schemes.

Owing to the ever increasing demand of privacy protection and security concerns, hand geometry based biometric system aimed at addressing these concerns is developed. In this study we have developed an authentication system which is based on finger shapes. The shapes of fingers are considered as patterns for extracting features using Eigen vector method and discrete wavelet transform. There are four feature types that include (i) Frequency and power content using Eigen vector method, (ii) Pisaranko's method (iii) Wavelet entropy of individual fingers, and (iv) Specific area of finger.

Pulmonary emphysema, overlapping with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder (COPD), contributes to a significant amount of morbidity and mortality annually. Computed tomography is used for in vivo quantification of emphysema and labeling into three standard subtypes at a macroscopic level. Unsupervised learning of texture patterns has great potential to discover more radiological emphysema subtypes. In this work, we improve a probabilistic Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model to discover spatially-informed lung macroscopic patterns (sLMPs) from previously learned spatially-informed lung texture patterns (sLTPs). We exploit a specific reproducibility metric to empirically tune the number of sLMPs and the size of patches. Experimental results on the MESA COPD cohort show that our algorithm can discover highly reproducible sLMPs, which are able to capture relationships between sLTPs and preferred localizations within the lung. The discovered sLMPs also achieve higher prediction accuracy of three standard emphysema subtypes than in our previous implementation.

This paper presents a design for an intelligent self-configuring control scheme for robot manipulators. The proposed scheme consists of two control structures - one centralized and the other decentralized - both utilizing Integral Sliding Mode (ISM) control to compensate for matched disturbances, uncertain terms, and unmodeled dynamics or couplings. In addition to its control capabilities, ISM also serves as a "perturbation estimator," enabling the development of a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based decision-making mechanism. This mechanism switches between the two control structures based on an appropriate reward function, accommodating a range of velocity and acceleration requirements. The proposed scheme has been evaluated using a COMAU SMART3-S2 industrial robot manipulator model, identified with real data and realistic sensor noise.

The response of patient blood pressure to the drug infusion of phenylephrine (PHP) is modeled as an intra-and-inter-variability model with time delay. In this paper, we introduce a novel Bayesian-filtering-based approach for estimating the model parameters' variability and drug transport delay (time delay) in real-time. 

The proposed approach takes a data-driven perspective, and it employs cross-correlation (XCF) of mean arterial pressure (MAP) measurement with drug infusion to provide prior knowledge of time delay estimation. Additionally, cubature Kalman filter (CKF) is used to provide nonlinearity estimation of model parameters and posterior knowledge of time delay. 

Our proposed Bayesian-filtering-based approach was validated with animal experimental data in a sequential mechanism. The experimental results demonstrated the superiority of the proposed approach over multiple-model EKF (MMEKF) in terms of MAP and drug transport delay estimation accuracy and sensitivity analysis of model parameters and drug transportation delay estimation.

Overall, the proposed approach offers a practical and reliable solution for real-time estimation of model parameters and drug transport delay in PHP drug infusions.

The advent of digitization and its modern day Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) triggered a paradigm shift in product and product-service-system design across many sectors. Many related developments in the context of Industry 4.0 rely on the use of vast amounts of data. When it comes to managing and handling this data, one of the prime technology approaches is that of Cloud Computing. However, Cloud Computing has a number of shortcomings, such as data security and latency challenges. Recently, Fog Computing has emerged as a new approach to complement Cloud Computing. It operates on cloud layers connected to data sources and minimizes issues related to data transmission latency, reduced bandwidth, and cyber security aspects. In this paper, the authors discuss Fog Computing and the way in which it complements Cloud Computing. They also elaborate on the benefits of utilizing Cloud and Fog Computing in concert.

This paper presents a novel hybrid fuzzy dynamic surface control (DSC) approach that combines the supertwisting control (STC) method with a supertwisting nonlinear disturbance observer (STO) to address multi-input multi-output nonlinear strict-feedback systems. In addition, a new partial tracking error constraining method is proposed. The design of the stabilizing controls of the DSC utilizes the virtual tracking errors in recursive procedures, which are transformed into the design variables of the STC. The uncertainties are estimated using the STO, which includes the approximation error between the unknown plant dynamics and fuzzy optimization function, along with external disturbances. The proposed DSC combined with the STC scheme can prevent the complex analysis problem of the filtered output error in conventional DSC schemes. A novel convenient tracking error constraining method is also presented. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms control systems with a conventional nonlinear disturbance observer and several other DSC schemes in terms of improved tracking error performance and robustness to uncertainty.

The advanced switching techniques enable the topology reconfiguration of microgrids (MGs) in active distribution network. In this paper, we enhance and generalize the traditional reconfiguration strategy resorting to the concept of “dynamic MGs” (i.e., the reorganization of MGs boundaries), to achieve a higher operational feasibility against the emergency islandings. Also, a risk-averse two-stage mixed integer conic program model is presented to support the networked MGs planning with generalized reconfiguration decisions. The MGs capacity expansion and seasonal reconfiguration decisions are made in the first stage, and validated under stochastic islanding scenarios in the second stage, where the network operations are captured by a second-order conic program (SOCP). Furthermore, a conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) measure is involved to quantitatively control the islanding risks. By theoretically proving the strong duality of the SOCP subproblem, we develop and customize Benders decomposition method with the guaranteed finite convergence to the optimal value. Finally, numerical results on 33- and 56-bus networked MGs validate the effectiveness of proposed reconfiguration strategy as well as planning approach. Our method demonstrates a cost-saving up to 22.56% when comparing to the traditional scheme with fixed MGs boundaries.

In order to realize the transient and accident analysis of reactor system and verification of system control scheme, the latest computer technology is used to develop advanced graphical modeling tool for TRANTH code, the human-machine interaction interface, and integration research between software and digital reactor design and verification platform, so as to the design and simulation system of digital reactor fluid instruction control system is built up. The nuclear power plant (ACP1000) is chosen as a research object some typical operating conditions are selected and executed. Results show that the design and simulation system can implement the modeling, calculation, interactive manipulation and display of reactor fluid instruction control system, which brings a multi-professional joint simulation of reactor fluid instruction control system to fruition, and provides technology support for rapid generation, evaluation, verification and optimization of design scheme about reactor fluid instruction control system.

Memristive devices have the potential to revolutionize memory and logic operations, paving the way for non von-Neumann Computation-In-Memory architectures. To accurately evaluate the performance of such architectures, it is necessary to have accurate and compact models for memristive devices due to the unavailability of standard devices. In this paper, a flexible model for bipolar, filamentary switching, redox-based memristive devices is proposed. The model is able to capture both the device resistance ratio and nonlinearity of switching kinetics. This model is used to perform design exploration for three memristive-based circuit designs (IMPLY, MAGIC, and CRS) for computation-in-memory architectures.

In this paper, we present a novel Personal Identity Verification (PIV) technique utilizing a 2-D convolutional neural network (CNN) mechanism with electrocardiosignal (ECG singles). With the emergence of CNNs in the field of image recognition that is demonstrating amazing performance, we leverage this advantage by innovatively converting electrocardiosignal into 2-D grayscale images to be analyzed in our PIV approach. This augmentation still ensures that the full cardiac cycle is represented in the images and allows the network to learn both the electrocardiosignal period's characteristics and the connections between each electrocardiosignal period. A set of deep learning techniques like batch normalization, data augmentation, Xavier initialization, and dropout was used in optimizing the proposed CNN classifier. Our results indicate that our trained classifier achieves a 99.90% average accuracy, and 10-fold cross-validation was performed to evaluate its accuracy with each ECG recording as a proving ground. Collectively, we believe that our experimental results demonstrate the potential of utilizing our proposed CNN classifier with the transformed ECG images and showcase an excellent identification accuracy rate.

This study focuses on the problem of model parameter estimation for in-pipe walking robots. It examines three different estimators: a regressor function-based method and two different least squares-based methods (with and without damping). The study investigates the influence of sensor resolution on the accuracy of the estimation and discusses the impact of the initial estimation's accuracy on the performance of these methods. Additionally, two performance functions are proposed to simplify the analysis process.

Results reveal that the least squares method has a significant advantage when the robot's exact state information is known; however, its performance changes significantly when sensors have finite resolution. In contrast, the regressor-based method is much less affected by sensor resolution. Overall, the use of these performance functions provides insight into the optimal estimation method choice for in-pipe walking robots.

Dispersed computing is promising paradigm to supplement the conventional cloud computing. Performing computation on the edge leads to significant reduction in communication with the remote cloud. However, challenges exist to fully exploit the advantages of dispersed computing systems: The edge devices are heterogeneous in computation and communication capacity; Tasks decomposed from the target applications can have complex precedence requirements captured by a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). With these challenges in mind, we propose a throughput optimized task scheduler, targeting at applications (such as computer vision and video processing) where input data are continuously and steadily fed into the execution pipeline. The scheduler incorporates two innovative techniques: task duplication and task splitting. To circumvent low bandwidth data links in the highly heterogeneous environment, we duplicate critical tasks to reroute communication paths. To load-balance the various tasks in complicated target applications, we split heavy-loaded tasks to allow cooperation of multiple nearby edge devices. Through simulation, we thoroughly evaluate the performance of the scheduler under various configuration of tasks and dispersed systems. Task duplication improves throughput of the baseline schedule significantly (> 1.2×), for systems with large variance in data link bandwidth and tasks with large communication-to-computation ratio. Task splitting leads to significant throughput improvement (> 1.25×) for systems with heterogeneous processing power and tasks with large variance in workload. On average, our scheduler improves throughput of the baseline schedule by > 1.6×.

Electrical embarked network can be described as strongly coupled multi-sources, multi-loads systems. This system can be affected by a long overload or frequency variations. However, if these disturbances cannot be controlled or isolated in a short time, they will be responsible for a lots of energy crisis. So, in this paper, we describe a prototype of smart electrical protection device that can be used to control and monitoring a typical electrical embarked system by Ethernet network at anytime and anywhere. This embarked system will be controlled by programmable logic controller Zelio Schneider and embedded system Raspberry Pi. Moreover, the communication between these two parties will done by sending data from the website to our electrical system by Json-file and store data in cloud database server. For any fault or change of data estimation in our system, the smart electrical protector sends a message and musical alert to website which can be changed automatically without refresh.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has seen a rapid increase in the number of services available due to the widespread use of smart devices and cyber-physical systems. However, a major challenge for exploring the potential of these services is to ensure interoperability in a decentralized environment. One solution with promising results is blockchain technology (BCT), which can establish trust in data and process execution. BCT works by verifying data or processes and recording them in a distributed ledger. However, BCT still faces obstacles to interoperability, including consensus protocols and block sizes. Proof-of-work (PoW) protocols can lead to excessive delays, while trust may become an issue if validators are chosen improperly. A potential solution is Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance, which offers fast finality settlement and uses hyperledger to support scalability. However, trust remains a concern. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an architecture solution that integrates BCT, service-oriented architecture (SoA), and enablers of key performance indicators (KPIs) and service selections. The proposed architecture aims to solve both interoperability and trust issues for IoT services. The paper provides examples of smart contract implementations to validate the method's feasibility.

The recent growth in the maritime industry has led to an increase in global commerce as well as the search for hydrocarbons in offshore locations. As a result, high data rate and cost-effective maritime communication is needed. To address this issue, a mesh network is envisaged for maritime communications due to its expanded coverage, self-healing capabilities, and high capacity.

To decrease frequency interference, multi-radio technology has been developed which allows for proper channel assignment. Despite this, the static channel assignment optimization remains a challenging problem. In this paper, we propose a heuristic algorithm to address the static channel assignment issue. The algorithm assigns channels to communication links in order to minimize overall network interference. 

A modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed to optimize the problem. Additionally, a new merging solution is adopted to reassign channels for nodes that violate radio constraints. Simulation in NS-3 is performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed channel assignment algorithm. The results show that the algorithm can find an optimized assignment with fewer iterations than previous work, therefore improving network performance.

Several pathologies are linked to abnormal asymmetries in brain images, and automated detection can significantly improve diagnosis, segmentation, and analysis of abnormal brain tissues, such as lesions. This paper proposes a fully unsupervised supervoxel-based method for detecting abnormal asymmetries in brain MRI images. Additionally, we introduce SymmISF, a new method for extracting symmetrical supervoxels. Our experiments on a large set of MR-TI images demonstrate improved detection rates and fewer false positives compared to a deep learning auto-encoder approach.

Paraseptal emphysema (PSE) is a subtype of emphysema that is often asymptomatic but has recently been associated with interstitial lung abnormalities that can lead to poor clinical outcomes, including mortality. Existing methods for quantifying emphysema subtypes have not adequately characterized PSE, as they often fail to capture the global nature of the disease. Path-based approaches are not well-suited to identify PSE, and segmentation is a better paradigm. In this study, a new convolutional network architecture called the Slice-Recovery network (SR-Net) is presented. This network uses 3D contextual information for 2D segmentation of PSE lesions in CT images. The results show that the proposed approach is effective in identifying and segmenting PSE lesions of different sizes, even in the presence of other emphysema subtypes in an advanced stage. The dataset used for training and testing the method was comprised of 664 images from 111 CT scans. Overall, the study highlights the benefits of incorporating 3D context information in the network for improving the identification and segmentation of PSE lesions.

Crowd simulation becomes one of the active research over the last three decade. Crowd simulation research is part of research about human behavior. One of research focus on crowd simulation was simulation at disaster evacuation. People who trapped in disaster usually has different behavior and abilities when evacuating. So the simulation looks more real, there are several simulations scenario used when disaster simulation like invariant speed and relation between virtual agents scenario. In this research will be used agent-based reciprocal velocity obstacle method. The agent-based method used because applying a microscopic approach. With agent-based method then each virtual agents can have different behavior and abilities. Optimal reciprocal collision avoidance(ORCA) which is the best version of Reciprocal velocity obstacle(RVO) used as virtual agents collision avoidance in crowds simulation. Experiment result demonstrates the simulation of hundreds of agents in a three evacuation scenario. Leader-follower relations on heterogeneous agents result in the possibility of collisions between agents getting bigger with the number of collisions is 7781 collisions. The longest simulation time is 151 seconds with the smallest FPS number is 33 FPS.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) consists of hundreds of continuous narrow bands with high redundancy, resulting in the curse of dimensionality and an increased computation complexity in HSI classification. Many clustering-based band selection approaches have been proposed to deal with such a problem. However, a few of them consider the spectral and spatial relationship simultaneously. In this letter, we proposed a novel clustering-based band selection approach using deep subspace clustering (DSC). The proposed approach combines the subspace clustering task into a convolutional autoencoder by treating it as a self-expressive layer, enabling it to be trained end to end. The resulting network can fully extract the interaction of spectral bands based on using spatial information and nonlinear feature transformation. We compared the results of the proposed method with existing band selection methods for three widely used HSI data sets, showing that the proposed method is able to accurately select an informative band subset with remarkable classification accuracy.

A novel distributed algorithm designed for weighted average consensus is presented. This algorithm is developed based on the well-known Belief Propagation (BP) algorithm for statistical learning. For a connected network without loops, the algorithm will converge in finite number of iteration and produces a correct average consensus value for every node in the network. For a network with loops, we convert the weighted average problem into an optimization problem with a relaxation factor whose solution approaches to the weighted average with appropriate relaxation factor. A modified algorithm is also proposed for loopy networks and consensus will be reached asymptotically with low computation complexity and fast convergence rate.

As an alternative of the Lyapunov function-based design of adaptive controllers the Fixed Point Transformation based Adaptive controller was introduced that in the first step transforms the control task into a Fixed Point Problem then so solves it via iteration that during one digital control step one step of iteration happens. In the actual step this scheme takes into consideration the controlled system's response obtained for the control action in the previous step, therefore it applies delayed feedback that makes it very flexible in the adaptive control of time-delayed systems. In transforming the control problem into a fixed point problem countless mathematical possibilities exist. Till now only a few versions were in use. On the basis of certain old antecedents in this paper a novel version is suggested that creates abstract rotations in the n dimensional space on the basis of the generalization of the Rodrigues formula. Its main advantage is its simplicity, easy geometric interpretation, lucidity, and better fitting to the features of the particular control task. Its applicability is exemplified by simulations for the adaptive control of two mass-points coupled by nonlinear springs.

This paper presents the problem of block simplex constrained signal recovery, which has been demonstrated to be a suitable formulation for estimation problems in networks such as route flow estimation in traffic. There are several natural approaches to this problem: compressed sensing, Bayesian inference, and convex optimization. This paper presents new methods within each framework and assesses their respective abilities to reconstruct signals, with the particular emphasis on sparse recovery, ability to incorporate prior information, and scalability. We then apply these methods to route flow estimation in traffic networks of various sizes and network topologies. We find that both compressed sensing and Bayesian inference approaches are appropriate for structured recovery but have scalability limitations. The convex optimization approach does not directly incorporate prior information, but scales well and has been shown to achieve 90% route flow accuracy on a full-scale network of over 10 000 links and 280 000 routes on a synthetic benchmark based on the I-210 corridor near Los Angeles, CA, USA.

The management and configuration of optical networks, as well as implementing new policies to keep up with the ever-changing network, can be tedious tasks. However, software-defined networking (SDN) has revolutionized the way network solutions are developed for electrical networks. The application of SDN for optical networks offers new opportunities to simplify and expedite these tasks. To achieve this objective, an optical network description language (ONDL) has been developed as a first step. ONDL is utilized to describe various network components, their configuration, and run-time states including modulation schemes, wavelength, and spectral width of a transponder, switching matrix of an optical switch, etc. The language is based on resource description framework (RDF). Moreover, a controller that understands and sends instructions in ONDL has been developed to different network devices to provide or change their states. The applicability of ONDL is demonstrated through the simulation of a network, where its nodes are controlled and managed using ONDL and the developed controller.

This paper presents a simplified modeling and simulation approach to investigate the behavior of vehicle handling and stability, utilizing the single-track model of an automobile. Two different control technologies, namely traditional PID control and Fuzzy PID control, were employed in this study. To achieve the desired results, a complete control system, including linear and nonlinear single-track vehicle models, along with the control method, was developed. A steering input driving condition was used in this work, which involved step steering angle and a lane change maneuver. Results from the simulations showed that the control systems constructed for the vehicle models were effective in improving the handling and stability of the vehicle.

Blockchain and AI are two technological advancements that have seen considerable growth in recent years, with the potential to revolutionize the next-generation wireless networks. Blockchain technology plays a crucial role in establishing a secure and decentralized resource sharing environment that facilitates data transmission in a reliable and trustworthy manner. In contrast, AI can prove invaluable in solving problems with uncertain, time-variant and complex features. By integrating these two technologies into wireless networks, we can enhance their performance significantly.

To this end, we propose a secure and intelligent architecture for the next-generation wireless networks that integrate AI and blockchain. This architecture enables flexible and secure resource sharing and provides a robust foundation for future wireless networks. We then propose a novel approach, blockchain-empowered content caching, aimed at maximizing system utility, and develop a new caching scheme using deep reinforcement learning. Our approach provides a reliable and efficient solution that minimizes delays, reduces congestion, and ensures seamless connectivity of wireless networks.

Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, which outperforms existing content caching methods in terms of transmission delay and overall system performance. Our results indicate that the combination of AI and blockchain technologies can significantly improve wireless networks' reliability, security and efficiency, making them indispensable in the ever-evolving technology landscape. In conclusion, we believe that this approach is a promising avenue for future research in the wireless networking domain.

A plethora of decision-making methods have been applied to tackle the issue of network selection in Heterogeneous Wireless Environment (HWE). Network selection refers to the process of identifying a network that offers reliable and satisfactory service to the end-user. Due to conflicting and dynamic operating conditions, network selection is performed by implementing appropriate decision-making methods. However, each decision-making method has its unique procedure with pros and cons, making the identification of an appropriate method for network selection a challenging task. This article aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Multiple Attribute Decision Making (MADM) and Cost Function (CT) methods in the context of network selection. The performance of both methods has been evaluated based on Selection Accuracy and Processing Time.

In this paper, we have focused on the development of a Two-Wheel Inverted Pendulum (TWIP), which is a highly non-linear, unstable, and strongly coupled system. This concept forms the basis for two-wheel self-balancing robots. During simulations, transfer functions were displayed using MATLAB-2016 software. Our study involved analyzing various controllers for the Two Wheel Self Balancing Robot (TWSBR). We designed a model using state-space and developed mathematical models for controllers such as LQG & MPC. We compared these two controllers for their effectiveness, with the fundamental objective of generating an efficient controller for real-time operation of the robot. We found that the designed LQG controller had better performance while the MPC had the best results.

When it comes to describing robots, many roboticists choose to focus on the size, types of actuators, or other physical capabilities. As most areas of robotics deploy robots with large memory and processing power, the question “how computational resources limit what a robot can do” is often overlooked. However, the capabilities of many miniature robots are limited by significantly less memory and processing power. At present, there is no systematic approach to comparing and quantifying the computational resources as a whole and their implications. This letter proposes computational indices that systematically quantify computational resources-individually and as a whole. Then, by comparing 31 state-of-the-art miniature robots, a computational classification ranging from non-computing to minimally-constrained robots is introduced. Finally, the implications of computational constraints on robotic software are discussed.

This paper proposes a novel real-time collaboration scheme for industrial wireless sensor networks (IWSNs) using multiple-input-multiple-output ultrawideband (MIMO-UWB). The proposed scheme, called request-to-send/clear-to-send (RTS/CTS) collaboration with scalable rate-prediction (RCC-RP), selects the transmission rate based on the prediction of the consequent signal-to-noise (SNR) of data frames to transmit in the event of poor channel conditions. The simulation results demonstrate that RCC-RP minimizes the overhead of the RTS/CTS collaboration and mitigates the issues of frame collision compared to other rate prediction schemes by implementing an optimal RTS/CTS frame collaboration with respect to contending station numbers and current data frame transmission rates.

Pulmonary and respiratory diseases are a significant global health burden, particularly in developing countries where resources for diagnosis are limited, leading to misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. To address this issue, we have developed a mobile toolkit that consists of a low-cost peak flow meter and a mobile phone app called Pulmonary Screener. This toolkit can screen and diagnose three of the most common pulmonary and respiratory diseases, including Asthma, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), and Allergic Rhinitis (AR).

The Pulmonary Screener app uses machine vision software to capture the reading from the peak flow meter automatically, without requiring any electronics or Bluetooth radio. The app then uses an integrated clinical questionnaire and a machine learning model to calculate individual probabilities of a patient having a specific pulmonary disease or comorbidity. The model was trained using diagnostic data from 325 patients collected over the past three years and achieves accuracy values above 0.90 for all diseases and combinations, except for Asthma with AUC = 0.84. Sensitivity and specificity values for all diseases are also greater than 0.90.

Overall, this is the first clinically validated mobile tool capable of diagnosing multiple pulmonary diseases using a single app. Future versions of the Pulmonary Screener will expand support for infectious diseases such as pneumonia and tuberculosis and include features extracted from auscultation and cough sounds. With the Pulmonary Screener, health workers and general practitioners in developing countries can now diagnose pulmonary diseases more accurately, leading to improved outcomes for patients.

This paper studies some challenges in Internet of Things-based remote healthcare and smart environment sensing domains. A cloudlet architecture with virtual sensors is proposed and its advantages are discussed in the context of resolving certain issues. The issues are handled by applying sensor virtualization techniques in cloudlet and developing a PaaS platform to support relatively expensive computation at the edge. The utility of our design has been summarized with a number of use case implementations, test results, and performance metrics, based on the challenges we initially faced.

We suggest the utilization and assessment of multi-core Erbium-Ytterbium-doped fiber amplifiers in conventional multi-fiber-based optical transport networks. Our study reveals that the design strategies such as launched power adaptation and core-to-span connection optimization guarantee excellent performance for various practical links, confirming the feasibility of the system.

This paper proposes an active learning strategy for robots, which leverages the Koopman operator representation to enable fast learning and control synthesis while considering task information. The paper motivates the use of this approach by demonstrating improved control performance in an actuated Van der Pol system. Utilizing information-theoretic methods, the Koopman operator formulation is applied to dynamical systems to derive an active learning controller for robot dynamics. The results show that the active learning controller increases the rate of information about the Koopman operator and allows for policies built on the Koopman dynamics to be easily incorporated for improved control. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated in a quadcopter experiment where it showed single-execution active learning and stabilization capabilities during free fall. The paper further extends the active learning approach to automate Koopman observables and is implemented on real robotic systems.

In this paper we introduce an adaptation to the "driver intent inference algorithm for urban intersections". This algorithm has been proven to detect potential right turns of vehicles by estimating the probability of a driver to turn right, and we propose to use it for reducing the number of cycling deaths at an intersection. We extend this algorithm following the IoT design principles and thus, with this approach, cyclists' safety no longer depends only on actions taken inside the vehicles, but also can use additional safety solutions based on standards and available information shared about the vehicles and drivers in vehicular networks. Our approach proposes to process the inference algorithm outside the vehicle, considering cloud and edge computing. We use predicting models for identifying driver's intention of turning right at intersections and the use of edge connected devices running our algorithm for alerting cyclists of possible collisions, thus preventing as many collisions as possible in intersections.

A novel approach to resource allocation in cache-aided mobile-edge computing (MEC) is proposed in this paper, aimed at providing efficient communication, storage, and computing services for intensive computation and latency-sensitive tasks. To address the resource allocation problem, a mixed integer non-linear program (MINLP) is formulated, which requires joint optimization of cache allocation, computation allocation, task offloading decision, and dynamic power distribution. In order to tackle this challenging problem, a Markov decision process (MDP) is used to enable mobile users and access points (AP) to learn optimal allocation policies based on historical experience, thereby improving the efficiency of resource allocation. To overcome the large state space dimensionality inherent in MDP, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed, which provides an optimized solution with low complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is capable of achieving a quasi-optimal performance under various system configurations, and outperforms other benchmark methods considered. Finally, comparison with the results of the optimal solution confirms the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Visual servoing is a popular technique used in robotics to control the motion of a robot based on visual feedback from one or more cameras. One of the key challenges in this area is uncalibrated visual servoing, which requires accurate estimation of the image Jacobian matrix.

To address this issue, this paper proposes an online estimation method for the total Jacobian matrix using the unscented particle filter. The total Jacobian matrix is defined and the problem is formulated in a Bayesian filtering framework. The unscented particle filter is then used to estimate the total Jacobian matrix, with each particle propagated and updated using the unscented Kalman filter equations. This approach makes full use of image feature measurements, resulting in more accurate estimation.

The proposed method is evaluated on a 2DOF robot visual servoing platform and achieves accurate and reliable performance in object tracking tasks. Overall, this study highlights the potential of the unscented particle filter for effective online estimation of the total Jacobian matrix in visual servoing applications.

The human vision system is a subjective perception that varies among individuals. When it comes to securing data within an image, the complexity of the image plays a significant role. In this paper, a novel steganography approach is introduced using a combined 3D Color Texture Feature (CTF) to identify complex regions of the image for data hiding. This makes it challenging for visual attacks to detect the hidden message. The frequency domain is utilized to hide data in these selected complex regions through Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). These areas are intrinsically noisy, making it difficult to extract any additional information. The steganography system is adaptive since each image has different complexity levels and spatial regions. The data hiding is directly dependent on these factors. The proposed adaptive method provides secure message hiding while maintaining high embedding capacity and imperceptibility quality. The final cover images maintain a PSNR value of above 50. In comparison to a similar algorithm that uses Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrices (GLCM) feature to identify complex regions of images for data hiding, the embedding capacity is approximately twice as high.

Recently, imbalanced traffic classification has attracted more attention due to the fact that most internet traffic exhibits imbalance behavior. However, few works only have considered real-time imbalanced traffic classification. In this project, we propose a comparative study comprising several machine learning algorithms for nine different scenarios. We vary dataset and flow sizes following an under-sampling approach, in order to establish an objective evaluation of the best parameters for classification. The results showed that: 1) Combined with packet length, inter-arrival time and maximum segment size, features related to TCP session signalization enhance imbalanced traffic classification performances; 2) Ensemble approaches, especially Bagged Random Forest, achieve the best results for real-time imbalanced traffic classification; 3) Increasing flow sizes while reducing (to a certain level) training set sizes, enhances classification performances as we learn more about each individual instance. The best classification scenario includes 500 samples in each class with 8 packets flows.

An optical motion capture system utilizes retroreflective markers to determine the position and orientation of an object. However, occlusion of some markers often results in inaccurate localization. Previous research has applied moving horizon estimation (MHE) to improve estimation accuracy. MHE determines states in a way that minimizes the sum of error magnitudes under constraints. Marker association plays a significant role in accurate estimation. A proposed method for MHE marker association leverages a potential function and optimization to improve robustness against occlusion and false marker images. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method improved estimation accuracy in scenarios where previous methods failed due to missing or misrecognized markers.

A Low-latency Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (L-CRNN) is proposed to reduce the complexity of a Keyword Spotting (KWS) system with high accuracy. The L-CRNN reduces a number of parameters between RNN layer and Full-Connected (FC) layer, which saves at least 1/2 memory for on-hands device compared with Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) depending on the number of FC units. Furthermore, it learns valid deep audio features to classify the keywords and garbage words with high accuracy. Results of experiments on the Google's Speech Commands Datasets show that the L-CRNN achieves 96.17% accuracy with less than 1/4 number of parameters and fewer float operations compared with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and CRNN.

We study support for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications through a cell-free massive MIMO architecture. Under the general assumption that the propagation channel between the mobile stations, either UAVs or ground users, and the access points follows a Ricean distribution, we derive closed form spectral efficiency lower bounds for uplink and downlink with linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) channel estimation. We also propose power allocation and user scheduling strategies for such a system. Our numerical results reveal that a cell-free massive MIMO architecture may provide better performance than a traditional multicell massive MIMO network deployment.

As we are all aware, the number of internet-connected devices is rapidly increasing. According to estimations, there will be an average of seven active internet connections per human by the year 2020. These smart devices are able to communicate with each other seamlessly, creating a thriving internet of things (IoT) environment. The integration of these smart devices, however, is not an effortless task. While IoT presents a plethora of great applications, it also poses various challenges and issues. To overcome these challenges and issues, researchers have proposed numerous solutions. One of the most significant concerns in an IoT environment is security. Hence, various frameworks and solutions have been proposed to tackle this issue. In this research paper, we aim to perform a systematic review of various security frameworks. Our main focus, however, will be on trust-based security frameworks.

Real-time remote estimation is crucial in applications such as industrial automation, smart grid, and the tactile internet. To improve estimation quality, we propose a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)-based framework for linear time-invariant (LTI) dynamic systems. However, there is a tradeoff between the reliability and freshness of sensor measurement transmission. Our approach optimizes the sensor's decision policy, whether to retransmit or not, based on the current estimation quality of the remote estimator and number of retransmissions, to minimize the long-term remote estimation mean-squared error (MSE). We provide a sufficient condition for a stationary and deterministic optimal policy that stabilizes the system and minimizes MSE, proving it has a switching structure and deriving a low-complexity suboptimal policy. Numerical results demonstrate improved performance over conventional non-HARQ policies.

In recent years, with the development and application of distributed generation, multi-microgrid structure has gradually become a future development form. However, new challenges have been brought to optimal operation due to its structural dispersion, complex composition, and information barrier. This paper proposes a distributed optimal operation model and solution method based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. The original problem is decoupled into several independent sub-problems including distribution network and microgrids. Based on the second-order cone relaxed power flow model and the chance-constrained method, the model is optimized to realize the optimal operation of a distribution network with multi-microgrid. Finally, a case study is presented based on the modified IEEE33 node system, and the result illustrates the feasibility of the ADMM algorithm and it is applicable to optimize the operation of distribution networks with multi-microgrid.

We explore the possibility of using multiple input artificial neural networks for the solution of Poisson Equation. Results are shown for 1D case considering a boundary value problem with Dirichlet boundary conditions. As opposed to previous work, we consider the cases where input to the ANN is provided at multiple input nodes. A typical variation is considered containing sinc and cosine type functions and output validation is shown for different discretization steps. Time and error performances of the algorithm are presented.

This paper proposes adaptive sideband selection for periodic interference cancellation using digital signal processing. The proposed selection enables the periodic interference cancellation to attain better performance by providing sideband signals having higher ICNR(interference to carrier and noise power ratio). An algorithm that selects such sideband signals is shown in this paper. The proposed selection achieves 18dB better SINR(output signal to interference and noise power ratio) performance than random selection in the channel with CIR(carrier to interference power ratio) of 10dB and CNR(carrier to noise power ratio) of 30dB.

Transfer learning can train a neural network for a target task's small dataset using a source task's pre-trained network; however, catastrophic forgetting, where the knowledge of the pre-trained network disappears during transfer learning, is problematic in this setting. PathNet was proposed to address this problem. However, PathNet can only be applied to modular neural network cases:thus, a non-modular pre-trained neural network is unavailable. Consequently, PathNet cannot be used to improve network structure versatility. Therefore, we propose Stepwise PathNet to improve versatility by considering the layers of a non-modular pre-trained neural network as modules. The performances of the proposed Stepwise and original PathNet methods were compared using the CIFAR-10 dataset (10 classes, and 60,000 images), and the results confirm the proposed method's potential to stabilize learning curves and accelerate learning to 45%.

This paper introduces two innovative deep learning models for the classification of objects in extremely low-resolution time-of-flight imagery in 2D and 3D. These models are designed to suit the latest range imaging hardware which employs the recently fabricated Single Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) camera with a resolution of 64 x 64 pixels. However, the small size of the data set illustrates great challenges in terms of training the models. To overcome these challenges, transfer learning is used in conjunction with the widely used VGG-16 convolutional neural network (CNN), with additional layers being added specifically to handle the SPAD data. 
Moreover, this paper presents a shot noise removal algorithm that can effectively mitigate camera sensitivity in excessive lighting situations. 
The proposed models were evaluated in both low-light indoor and outdoor daytime settings, including eight objects with small physical dimensions, low reflectivity, and featureless structures located at ranges from 25m to 700m. Despite the challenges, the 2D model achieved an average precision and recall of 95%, with even higher accuracy for the 3D model. As a result, these models offer benchmark models for comparison to a newly created 3D CNN operating on time-of-flight data acquired by the SPAD sensor.

Based on statistical mechanics of information due to the mean-field theory (MFT), we predict environmental variables and electric power consumed by air conditioner in small-scale systems by making use of Bayesian inference using the expected a posterior (EAP) estimation. Here, we clarify that the present method succeeds in providing an optimal thermal index due to the temperature-humidity index (THI) at each sampling point and power used due to air conditioner, if we set parameters under optimal conditions and that this fact is confirmed by exact proof via equality. Also, we find that the provided THI is further improved, if we introduce correlations of environmental quantities between sampling points into the conventional model.

The understanding of the Broken Rotor Bar (BRB) features frequencies and amplitudes has a great importance for all diagnostic methods. These characteristics frequencies shows a drawbacks under varying load condition. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) has been widely used to achieve these requirements, because of its efficiency. However, this paper present an enhancing of the fault detection based on a Machine Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) method. Indeed, the use of Sparse Autoencoder (AE) with the combination of Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) shown a good accuracy. Furthermore, the extraction of the new features to use in multi-class classification for the healthy and faulty Induction Motor (IM) is presented.

Breast cancer is the first female cancer responsible for high mortality worldwide. Despite the progress that has made it possible to better understand the mechanisms of cancer development, the causes of breast cancer are currently unknown. Nevertheless, studies have identified some risk factors that promote breast cancer and a healthy lifestyle can reduce risk. In Morocco, breast cancer is the first cancer in women. It represents 34.3% of all female cancers. In this work, the Fast Correlation-Based Feature selection (FCBF) method is used to filter irrelevant and redundant characteristics in order to improve the quality of cancer classification, and we will provide an overview of the evolution of key data in the health system and apply five learning algorithms to a breast cancer data set. The purpose of this research work is to predict breast cancer, using several machine-learning algorithms that are Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines SVM, K-Nearest Neighbors K-NN, and Multilayer Perception MLP, in order to select the most effective algorithm with and without FCBF. The experimental results show that SVM gives the highest accuracy of 97.9% without FCBF but if we apply this method we find that the SVM and MLP show the best results in comparison with other algorithms. The results will help to choose the best learning algorithm machine classification for breast cancer prediction.

In this paper, a framework for collaborative localization of heterogenous systems is presented. Making advantage of the original MSCKF framework, we design a collaborative MSCKF filter that operates in two levels and allows a decentralized 3D collaborative localization without use of external computation systems. To achieve that, based on MSCKF localization, we first propose a range based collaboration that we optimize using the extracted environment constraints, an operation allowed by the use of a truncated unscented kalman filtering updates. The collaborative filtering is managed to not impact the original MSCKF odometry properties. The framework is applied to collaborative localization of aerial and ground robots; experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Traffic flow prediction is important in modern traffic control and induction. Short-term traffic flow prediction plays an important role in urban traffic navigation planning and traffic optimization control. Due to the advantage in processing of time series data, LSTM is very suitable for predicting short-term traffic flow. This paper builds a deep learning model based on LSTM to predict the traffic flow volume. In experiment, we build models with different hyper parameters, compared and analyzed the performance of different models.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have demonstrated impressive performance in many edge computer vision tasks, causing the increasing demand for DNN accelerator on mobile and internet of things (IoT) devices. However, the massive power consumption and storage requirement make the hardware design challenging. In this paper, we introduce a DNN accelerator based on a model compression technique vector quantization (VQ), which can reduce the network model size and computation cost simultaneously. Moreover, a specialized processing element (PE) is designed with various SRAM bank configurations as well as dataflows such that it can support different codebook/kernel sizes, and keep high utilization under small input or output channel numbers. Compared to the state-of-the-art, the proposed accelerator architecture achieves 4.2 times reduction in memory access and 2.05 times throughput per cycle for batch-one inference.

Recently, facial image de-occlusion and in-painting tasks have garnered attention in the field of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Auto-Encoders (AEs). In this paper, we propose an unsupervised technique to remove occlusions from facial images and simultaneously complete the occluded parts using optimized Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs) in an iterative manner. GANs, as generative models, utilize a generator and a discriminator to estimate the distribution of images. DCGANs, a variant with proposed improvements to its instability during training. Traditional facial image in-painting methods define a block of pixels as the missing part, then generate potential content using generative models such as GANs or AEs. Our method infers a mask from an occluded facial image via a novel loss function, which is then used to in-paint the occlusions automatically using pre-trained DCGANs. We evaluated the efficacy of our method on facial images with various occlusions such as sunglasses and scarves, and our experiments demonstrated that our method can efficiently detect certain kinds of occlusions and in-paint the occluded parts in an unsupervised manner.

The use of distributed generators and non-linear loads can have a negative impact on power quality at the point where the microgrid connects with the low voltage distribution network. To ensure safe and stable operation of the microgrid, it is crucial to track and compensate for power quality issues caused by converters. However, the current research on power quality problems only focuses on pre-emptive and post-processing strategies, which are not enough to ensure continuous and stable operation.

This paper proposes an advanced converter with situation awareness and orientation functions, which can be implemented in three main aspects: awareness, decision-making, and execution. Firstly, situation awareness is achieved by establishing an information management system and optimizing the prediction algorithm to manage power quality-related elements. Secondly, the decision model of the grid-connected converter and optimal control are used to actively make decisions to solve power quality problems. Finally, the situation orientation of power quality problems is accomplished by establishing a smooth switching model of an adaptive control strategy.

By considering these three aspects, the proposed advanced converter provides a more effective approach to manage power quality problems in microgrid. With its comprehensive functionalities, it can ensure the continuous and stable operation of the microgrid, thereby contributing to a more sustainable and reliable power supply network.

Daily human activity recognition using sensor data is a crucial task for many real-world applications, including home monitoring and assisted living. However, one of the challenges in human activity recognition is distinguishing between activities with infrequent occurrences and less distinctive patterns. In order to address this challenge, we propose a dissimilarity representation-based hierarchical classifier to perform two-phase learning. 

In the first phase, our classifier learns general features to recognize majority classes, while the second phase focuses on identifying subtle differences between minority classes. We compared our approach with state-of-the-art classification techniques on a real-world third-party dataset that was collected in a two-user home setting. Our results show that the hierarchical classifier approach performs better than existing techniques in differentiating between users performing the same type of activities.

The key novelty of our approach is the exploration of dissimilarity representations and hierarchical classifiers, which enable the identification of discriminating features between activities with subtle differences. As such, our approach offers a promising solution to improve accuracy in human activity recognition.

Over the past decades, humans have redesign themselves with the intent to evolve beyond their current physical and mental limitations. This phenomenon has been known as transhumanism, wherein robotics and biomimetics have been exploiting the unique designs of the human body with the intent to develop disruptive anthropomorphic artificial appendages. Nevertheless, while lower extremity prosthetics have evolved to the point at which lower leg amputees may be competitive with professional runners in the world, there is still a gap between upper extremity prosthetics and real hands. This work intends to be a pioneer into developing a low-cost multipurpose robotic hand for research and academia. This paper describes the robotic hand, including its electromechanical development and full ROS integration. Moreover, the paper also presents a MatLab framework designed to introduce sequence data classification, namely providing the ability to control the robotic hand using electromyography (EMG) signals from the forearm. This paper expects to contribute to an ever-increasing human-robot symbiosis by motivating students to engage in transhumanism studies using more sophisticated technologies and methods.

The articles featured in this special section delve deeply into the realm of edge computing. The concept of an ecosystem is key to understanding the Internet of Things, as it involves active participation and contribution from a diverse array of entities such as humans, animals, devices, and software. Similar to the transition from mainframe computers to personal computers, and the adoption of simple networks and smart terminals that underpin the protocols of the internet, edge computing is driven by ever-increasing computational capabilities of terminal devices. As a result, the power of edge devices to store and process data is constantly growing, ushering in a new era of computing that is defined by the term - Edge.

Mobile cloud computing is a cutting-edge technology that enables businesses to extend their IT capabilities beyond their current infrastructure. By accessing shareable remote computing resources, organizations can greatly enhance their operational efficiency and productivity. While many providers offer mobile cloud services, there is currently no formal definition of quality criteria for assessing these services. This has led to the development of several quality models for cloud service evaluation; however, these models often lack sufficient metrics for evaluating mobile cloud services, and fail to consider the unique characteristics of mobile technology.

To address these shortcomings, we have developed a cloud service integration model. This model incorporates additional metrics to capture the specific features of mobile technology, and includes an extended SLA model for handling complex service-dependencies in mobile cloud services. Additionally, we have developed a method for discovering the relationships between various metrics associated with mobile cloud services, and have used these relationships to establish new SLAs.

With this new model, organizations will be able to better evaluate the quality of their mobile cloud services and ensure that they are meeting their business needs. By incorporating metrics that reflect the specific characteristics of mobile technology, the model provides more accurate insights into the performance of mobile cloud services. Additionally, the extended SLA model enables businesses to better manage complex service-dependencies inherent in mobile environments. Ultimately, the cloud service integration model offers a more comprehensive approach to evaluating and managing mobile cloud services.

This paper outlines a two-stage ensemble-based approach to localize anatomical structures in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. Specifically, the proposed method focuses on localizing the hippocampus, which is a region associated with memory loss and significant structural changes in Alzheimer's disease. Accurate localization of the hippocampus is crucial for analyzing these structural changes, as well as for segmentation and registration of anatomical structures.

To achieve this goal, the proposed models combine a Hough voting method with a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to estimate the target position. The CNN is utilized to calculate displacement vectors by exploiting the Hough voting strategy from multiple 3-viewpoint patch samples. The displacement vectors are then used to estimate the target position. To efficiently learn from samples, the proposed models employ a local and global strategy. Multiple global models are trained using randomly selected 3-viewpoint patches from the whole MRI scan, and their results are aggregated to obtain global predictions. Similarly, multiple local models are trained using patches from the vicinity of the hippocampus location and assembled to obtain a local prediction.

The proposed models were tested using the Alzheimer's disease neuroimaging initiative (ADNI) MRI dataset and the Gwangju Alzheimer's and related dementia (GARD) cohort MRI dataset for training, validating and testing. The results indicate that the average prediction error using the proposed two-stage ensemble Hough CNN models are 2.32 and 2.25 mm for the left and right hippocampi, respectively, for 65 test MRIs from the GARD cohort dataset. Similarly, for the ADNI MRI dataset, the average prediction error for the left and right hippocampi are 2.31 and 2.04 mm, respectively, for 56 MRI scans.

Overall, the proposed two-stage ensemble Hough convolutional neural network (Hough-CNN) models show promising results for accurately localizing anatomical structures in MRI scans, especially the hippocampus in Alzheimer's disease.

Utilizing pre-trained DCNN for image classification has shown great potential in achieving remarkable results in some image recognition tasks. However, employing a single convolutional feature as a representation for vein recognition is not very effective due to the sparse distribution of vein information. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach, which involves concatenating multi-layer convolutional features with a semantic feature selector to obtain more distinctive and representative convolutional features. 

In this proposed method, different convolutional layers encode different levels of feature information. The high-level convolutional features contain vein information and cover more semantic information, while the low-level convolutional features contain vein information and cover more detailed information but also background information. To remove the background information of low-level convolutional features, a semantic feature selector is introduced. 

The proposed semantic feature selector involves applying local max-pooling of preserving spatial position (LMP-PSP) information on the activation map, which is obtained by adding up all feature maps of the high-level convolutional layer to generate the semantic weighting map. The semantic weighting map reflects the essential vein information of high-level convolutional features and is used as a feature selector to discard the background information of the low-level convolutional features and preserve the detailed information of low-level convolutional features. 

Finally, the low-level convolutional features with vein information are selectively linked to high-level convolutional features with vein information based on the proposed semantic feature selector. The effectiveness of this approach is verified through a series of experiments conducted using two lab-made vein databases (CUMT-Hand-Dorsa Vein database and CUMT-Palm Vein database), as well as additional experiments with PUT Palm Vein database and the subset of PolyU database, which demonstrate the model's generalization ability and robustness.
