Missions in extreme environments such as exploration and mapping of chemical leakage, radiation and high temperature are hazardous for human workers. Therefore, robotic solutions can be utilised in these applications. Swarm robotics is an alternative approach to traditional robotics, with potential to increase the efficiency of robotic solutions in an extreme environment. Swarm robotic systems are low-cost, robust and scalable. In this paper, we focused on an exploration scenario for use in an extreme environment application. The scenario for this study was to explore the different levels of radioactive or chemical leakage from drums in a nuclear storage facility. The environment and mobile robot used for this work, Mona, were modelled in the V-REP simulation software. The effects of experimental parameters, i.e. the number of robots and complexity of the storage facility, on the efficiency of the exploration system were evaluated. The results revealed that, an increase in population size increased the performance of the exploration significantly. Moreover, the complexity of the environment did not have significant impact on the performance of the system.

The pursuit-evasion differential game is a classic decision-making process in the continuous domain, which has recently seen significant advancement in research through the use of reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. In this paper, the dynamic model of the game is described, and the optimization problem of the pursuer is addressed. To enable self-learning of the control strategy, the actor-critic based, model-free, end-to-end approach of the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is applied to train the pursuer. 

The training is conducted in two phases; in the first phase, the pursuer is trained only with a given evader's control strategy. In the second training phase, both the pursuer and evader are trained simultaneously without any prior expert knowledge. The results reveal that both the pursuer and evader can learn the control strategy during the training phase. Overall, the application of the DDPG algorithm in the pursuit-evasion differential game proves to be effective in ensuring the efficient and rapid learning of the control strategy.

Pedestrian detection has made significant progress with the use of current benchmark datasets. However, there is still a disparity between real-world requirements and current pedestrian detection benchmarks. Existing datasets are mostly taken from a regular traffic scenario, resulting in a lack of diversity. Additionally, there is an underrepresentation of crowd scenarios with highly occluded pedestrians, leading to low density. To address this gap, we introduce WiderPerson, a diverse dataset for dense pedestrian detection in the wild. This dataset includes annotations in various scenarios and contains 13,382 images with 399,786 annotations, resulting in 29.87 annotations per image. The dataset includes dense pedestrians with various occlusions, making it challenging to evaluate pedestrian detectors in the wild. To serve as a baseline, we introduce an improved Faster R-CNN and the vanilla RetinaNet. We conduct experiments on previous datasets to analyze the generalization capabilities of WiderPerson and achieved state-of-the-art performances. However, we found that detecting false alarms and mismatches require improvements in the classification ability of pedestrian detectors. WiderPerson can be accessed at http://www.cbsr.ia.ac.cn/users/sfzhang/WiderPerson.

Facial expression recognition is crucial for effective human-computer interaction, and the key to achieving accurate recognition lies in feature extraction. Although single feature extraction techniques are commonly used, fusion of multiple features can offer several advantages. However, traditional serial feature fusion methods are plagued by the issue of high dimensionality. To overcome this problem, a novel fusion technique has been introduced. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method yields higher recognition rates and better real-time performance.

EMG-force models are widely utilized across several domains such as prosthesis control, clinical biomechanics, and ergonomics analysis. These models enable the control of movement direction and speed, assess healthy muscle performance, and evaluate injury risks. Advanced EMG-force models incorporate subject-specific and task-specific dynamics and are calibrated for durations exceeding 1-2 minutes. In our study, we examined several models' EMG-force estimation error based on calibration duration for two degree-of-freedom (2-DoF) hand-wrist contractions. Additionally, we analyzed the influence of electrode count on the EMG-force estimation error. By reducing the calibration duration and/or the number of electrodes, we make EMG-force modeling more accessible for wider applications, providing cost-effectiveness and time-saving benefits.

This paper combines the so-called congelation of variables method with adaptive immersion and invariance (I&I) to adaptively control systems with varying parameters. A dynamic scaling estimator without overparameterization is proposed. This does not require solving partial differential equations and removes other restrictive assumptions in the classical I&I estimator design. A controller that guarantees input-to-state stability of the closed-loop system is then used. The joint estimator-controller design guarantees global stability of the adaptive closed-loop system, convergence of the plant state and global boundedness of the estimator state. A design example for the position/force control of a series elastic actuator is discussed. This exploits the idea that bounded nonlinearities in the system dynamics can be viewed as time-varying parameters. Simulation results show a well-damped transient response and illustrate the theoretical results.

In the Internet of Things and smart environments data, collected from distributed sensors, is typically stored and processed by a central middleware. This allows applications to query the data they need for providing further services. However, centralization of data causes several privacy threats: The middleware becomes a third party which has to be trusted, linkage and correlation of data from different context becomes possible and data subject lose control over their data.Hence, other approaches than centralized processing should be considered. Here, Secure Multiparty Computation is a promising candidate for secure and privacy-preserving computation happening close to the sources of the data.In order to make SMC fit for application in these contexts, we extend SMC to act as a service: We provide elements which allow third parties to query computed data from a group of peers performing SMC. Furthermore, we establish fine-granular access control on the level of individual data queries, yielding data protection of the computed results. By adding measures to inform data sources about requests and the usage of their data, we show how a fully privacy-preserving service can be built on the foundation of SMC.

The aim of this paper is to control a photovoltaic (PV) generation system under partial shading conditions connected to the grid. The PV generator is connected to the grid through a Grid Side Converter (GSC). In fact, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is achieved by using the intelligent algorithm for finding the Global Maximum Power Point (GMPP). This algorithm combines a traditional MPPT technique based on Perturb and Observe (P& O) with the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique. A hybrid MPPT algorithm is based on the ANN and used to predict the global maximum power point region. Consequently, the (perturb and observe) technique searches for the Maximum Power Point (MPP) in the predicted region. The GSC is controlled in system a way to guarantee a smooth DC voltage with a unity power factor at the grid side. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the control strategies applied to the studied system.

This paper proposes a novel approach for distributed modeling of a 4-port transistor. The approach is based on the concept of a multi-finger transistor being considered as an association of an elementary active linked to extrinsic passive networks. An electromagnetic analysis is used to determine the electrical equivalent scheme of the passive networks. On the other hand, the internal active device is defined by an equivalent model. The intrinsic device (based on 2 fingers) and the values of the distributed parasitic network elements can be accurately extracted and modeled with standard measurements. In the Ku-band, a GaAs HEMT transistor was used to validate the approach by comparing measured and simulated results.

Hypertension is a medical condition that is well-established as a risk factor for many major diseases. For example, it can cause alterations in the cardiac structure and function over time that can lead to heart related morbidity and mortality. However, at the subclinical stage, these changes are subtle and cannot be easily captured using conventional cardiovascular indices calculated from clinical cardiac imaging. In this paper, we describe a radiomics approach for identifying intermediate imaging phenotypes associated with hypertension. The method combines feature selection and machine learning techniques to identify the most subtle as well as complex structural and tissue changes in hypertensive subgroups as compared to healthy individuals. Validation based on a sample of asymptomatic hearts that include both hypertensive and non-hypertensive cases demonstrate that the proposed radiomics model is capable of detecting intensity and textural changes well beyond the capabilities of conventional imaging phenotypes, indicating its potential for improved understanding of the longitudinal effects of hypertension on cardiovascular health and disease.

From positions of the principles of training selection decomposition and collective estimation the synthesis technique of multilevel nonparametric systems of pattern recognition for the multialternate classification problem is offered. Their application provides high computing performance of information processing of big dimension. Two approaches are considered. Poorly dependent feature sets of the classified objects are in case of the former used. Considering the assumption of independence of feature sets the generalized decisive rule of maximum likelihood is under construction. The basis of the second method is made by a dichotomy method. At each its stage we form the family of the private decision functions corresponding to various feature sets of the classified objects with the subsequent their integration in the non-linear decisive rule by means of methods of nonparametric statistics. At the same time formation of the generalized decision on situation belonging to this or that class is carried out in space of values of private decision functions. The offered technique allows to use technology of parallel calculations.

People desire to be connected, no matter where they are. Recently, providing Internet access to on-board passengers has received a lot of attention from both industry and academia. However, in order to guarantee an acceptable Quality of Service (QoS) for the passenger services with low incurred cost, the path to route the services, as well as the datacenter (DC) to deploy the services should be carefully determined. This problem is challenging, due to different types of Air-to-Ground (A2G) connections, i.e., satellites and Direct Air-To-Ground (DA2G) links. These A2G connection types differ in terms of cost, bandwidth, and latency. Furthermore, due to the flights' movements, it is important to consider adapting the service location accordingly. In this work, we formulate two Mixed Integer Linear Programs (MILPs) for the problem of Joint Service Placement and Routing (JSPR): i) Static (S-JSPR), and ii) Mobility-Aware (MA-JSPR) in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGIN), with the objective of minimizing the total cost. We compare S-JSPR and MA-JSPR using comprehensive evaluations in a realistic European-based SAGIN. The obtained results show that the MA-JSPR model, by considering the future flight positions and using a service migration control, reduces the long-term total cost notably. Also, we show S-JSPR benefits from a low time-complexity and it achieves lower end-to-end delays comparing to MA-JSPR model.

In this paper, we present a side-channel resilient moving target defence mechanism against power-/electromagnetic-based side-channel attacks. Recent countermeasures use fresh re-keying after every encryption/decryption process; this causes major overhead in synchronizing the communicating parties. In contrast to prior work, our mechanism integrates fresh re-keying and masking techniques at an interval, where these techniques are driven by the maximum number of side-channel leakage traces required towards a successful embedded attack. Hence, the mechanism tracks the effect of attacks on the number of traces, and consequently applies re-keying at suitable intervals to reduce the computational/communication overhead, while increasing the attack cost. The mechanism scalability was evaluated against an advanced attack model based on machine learning methods that reduces significantly the number of traces required for a successful attack under masking implementation.

We have introduced a novel method for automatic image annotation (AIA) that employs salient object detection. To obtain salient objects for AIA, we used the Minimum Barrier Salient Object Detection (MB) method. To enhance the AIA quality, we combined features from salient objects and the entire image by performing a weighted average. We utilized these combined features to build a random forest (RF) classifier, which produced labels for testing images. Our study used Corel 5K as the dataset, which consists of 50 categories of images. However, we only tested 25 groups of images (2500 images) with clear objects in the image since the saliency approach seeks the dominant object in an image. Our experiments showed that the feature was most accurate when averaged using a weight of 2/17 for the salient-object feature and 15/17 for the overall-image feature. The image labeling accuracy reached 79.89%, with a 95%-CI ranging between 76 and 83%. These results demonstrate that our proposed approach, which uses the RF generated with training data through a combined feature, can achieve better classification than the RF that uses either whole image features or only the features of the salient object.

Traffic congestion and occlusions are major problems nowadays in metropolitan cities which leads to an ever growing traffic accidents. Therefore, the need of traffic flux management in order to avoid these congestions, unnecessary time wastage and tragic accidents is very important. Traffic regulation by optimizing timing of traffic control signals is one of the solutions for this purpose. This paper presents a low cost camera based algorithm in order to control traffic flow on a road. The algorithm is based on mainly three steps: vehicle detection, counting and tracking. Background subtraction is used to isolate vehicles from their background, Kalman filter is used to track the vehicles and Hungarian algorithm is exploited for association of labels to the tracked vehicles. This algorithm is implemented on both daytime and night time videos acquiered from CCTV camera and IR camera. Experimental results show the efficacy of the algorithm.

Recently, end-to-end (E2E) neural text-to-speech systems have started to surpass traditional multi-stage hand-engineered systems, such as Tacotron2, due to their simplified system building pipelines and high-quality speech. The unique encoder-decoder neural structure of the Tacotron2 system eliminates the need for separately learned text analysis front-end, duration model, acoustic model, and audio synthesis module. The attention mechanism is the key to its success, learning an alignment between the encoder and the decoder that serves as an implicit duration model bridging the text sequence and the acoustic sequence. However, attention learning faces challenges such as low training efficiency and model instability, which restrict the E2E approaches from wide deployment.

To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel pre-alignment guided attention learning approach that addresses the problems faced by attention learning. This approach injects handy prior knowledge-accurate phoneme durations-in the neural network loss function to bias the attention learning more accurately. The explicit time alignment between an audio recording and its corresponding phoneme sequence can be achieved using forced-alignment from an automatic speech recognizer (ASR). In experiments, we show that the proposed pre-alignment guided (PAG) attention approach significantly improves training efficiency and model stability. Specifically, the PAG updated version of Tacotron2 can quickly obtain the attention alignment using only 500 (text, audio) pairs, which is not possible for the original Tacotron2. A series of subjective experiments also demonstrate that the PAG-Tacotron2 approach can synthesize more stable and natural speech.

Video saliency detection is a challenging task as it requires considering both spatial and temporal constraints jointly. In this paper, a new method based on sparse reconstruction and propagation is proposed to detect salient objects in videos. The approach utilizes static and motion priors to design a single-frame saliency model that represents spatial saliency in each frame through sparsity-based reconstruction. Then, a sparsity-based propagation is applied to capture sequential correspondence in the temporal space to produce inter-frame saliency maps. Finally, these maps are combined into a global optimization model to achieve spatio-temporal smoothness and global consistency of the salient object in the entire video. Experimental results on three large-scale video saliency datasets indicate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms both qualitatively and quantitatively.

Indoor localization has become an increasingly important aspect in our daily lives, catering to the need for high accuracy indoor localization. The utilization of WiFi systems in indoor environments has led to the emergence of traditional model-based localization schemes, which achieve sub-meter accuracy through the fusion of multiple CSI observations. However, the computational overhead of these traditional schemes is considerable. In response to this issue, model-free localization techniques using deep learning frameworks have been proposed, with classification-based techniques being the norm. In this paper, we propose a logistic regression-based scheme as an alternative to classification-based techniques. Our proposed scheme can achieve sub-meter level accuracy (97.2cm medium distance error) in standard laboratory environments, while maintaining reasonable online prediction overhead under a single WiFi AP setting. We believe that our logistic regression-based scheme will pave the way for practical deep learning-based WiFi localization systems and contribute to the development of model-free localization techniques.

Since many books and papers on voice quality improvement are circulating around the world, we think that there are at least those who want to change their own voice. However, there is an image that voice quality improvement is difficult. The reason is that it is difficult to objectively evaluate user's oneself with voice training by user's oneself, and user cannot improve voice quality user's oneself easily. Therefore, in this research, we propose and verify the method of creating user's ideal voice, which is the goal when improving voice quality based on user's voice by using software UTAU and Interactive Genetic Algorithm (IGA). As results of experiment, in a search experiment using IGA, the average and the maximum evaluation values increased significantly. Furthermore, using the best individuals found in this search by comparing significant increase was also observed (p<;0.05). Therefore, it turns out that the proposed method has the possibility of making the ideal voice of the user.

Liquid level control in a tank can be done using various controllers. Conventionally there are many controllers that give a response which is sometimes not desirable. Industries want to improve the control strategy for making the controller work more efficiently. This can be achieved by optimizing the mechanism of controller using some heuristic optimization technique. In this paper optimization techniques like genetic algorithm, ant colony, fuzzy logic control and ANN are discussed. Fuzzy logic controller and ANN are more preferable over other optimization techniques because of their fast response and ability to reduce the error with a considerable amount. ANN can be used to train the fuzzy logic controller to make it more robust.

Optimal transport has emerged as a promising and useful tool for supporting modern image processing applications such as medical imaging and scientific visualization. Indeed, the optimal transport theory enables great flexibility in modeling problems related to image registration, as different optimization resources can be successfully used as well as the choice of suitable matching models to align the images. In this paper, we introduce an automated framework for fundus image registration which unifies optimal transport theory, image processing tools, and graph matching schemes into a functional and concise methodology. Given two ocular fundus images, we construct representative graphs which embed in their structures spatial and topological information from the eye's blood vessels. The graphs produced are then used as input by our optimal transport model in order to establish a correspondence between their sets of nodes. Finally, geometric transformations are performed between the images so as to accomplish the registration task properly. Our formulation relies on the solid mathematical foundation of optimal transport as a constrained optimization problem, being also robust when dealing with outliers created during the matching stage. We demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the present framework throughout a comprehensive set of qualitative and quantitative comparisons against several influential state-of-the-art methods on various fundus image databases.

In the field of automatic speech recognition, combining multiple models can improve performance, but it can also be computationally costly. One solution is to use teacher-student learning, where a single student model is trained to emulate the behavior of the ensemble of models. This paper explores teacher-student learning within a sequence-level framework, which allows for greater flexibility in the diversity of the ensemble. The paper proposes a novel training criterion based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence between context-dependent state sequence posteriors, which enables a diversity of state cluster sets to be present in the ensemble. The proposed criterion is shown to be an upper bound to a more general criterion based on KL-divergence between word sequence posteriors. The methods are evaluated on two speech transcription tasks, achieving improved performance compared to previous methods.

In this paper, we focus on addressing a convex-concave function problem in network applications. Our inspiration for this problem comes from saddle-point subgradient methods, and we tackle a saddle-point problem for multi-agent systems. Specifically, the objective function for this problem must be non-smooth but Lipschitz continuous. We introduce a distributed gradient-free algorithm that can effectively solve this issue, given the constraints of a convex constrain set and global convex inequality constraints. 

In order to evaluate the algorithm's performance, we examine the results of convergence rate and the impact of smoothing parameters on error bounds. We ultimately find that when Slater's condition is met, our approach is highly effective in solving multi-agent convex-concave optimization problems.

Fault detection is an essential aspect of supervising the operation of robotic swarm systems. Failure to detect faults can significantly impact the performance of the robot swarm. In this study, we propose a robust fault detection mechanism that can effectively detect faults despite noise and uncertainties in data. Our mechanism combines the multiresolution representation of data using wavelets with the sensitivity to small changes of an exponentially weighted moving average scheme.

To monitor swarm robotics systems performing a virtual viscoelastic control model for a circle formation task, our proposed mechanism is applied to the uncorrelated residuals from a principal component analysis model. Our simulation data from ARGoS simulator shows that our proposed method achieves improved fault detection performances compared to the conventional approach.

Therefore, the proposed mechanism can potentially help to enhance the performance of robotic swarm systems by detecting faults in a timely manner, despite the presence of noise and uncertainties in data.

In this paper, a method of determining examinations is proposed for ophthalmologic outpatients, using feedforward neural network (NN for short). The determination is based on the data classification. The proposed method defines four classes of ophthalmologic examinations. It prepares data for NN training and examination determination from handwriting sentences in outpatients' interview sheets. A set of the training data is prepared in the form of a matrix. The words extracted from the sentences are assigned to the matrix columns, while each sheet (or sentences in it) is assigned to a matrix rows. Entries in the matrix takes binary values meaning whether extracted words appear in the sentences in the sheet. The proposed method also the ages of outpatients as entries. NN training is conducted according to the normal backpropagation algorithm using a row as one of the training data. The trained NN has four output neurons each of which takes the value belonging to the range [0, 1]. The class of data to be examined is determined by searching the neuron at which the largest value appears in the output layer. Experimental results comprehensively establish that the proposed method can achieve higher percentages of concordance than other methods.

Polar codes are a crucial part of the 5G standards and are the only provable capacity-achieving channel code. Among the popular decoding methods for polar codes, belief propagation (BP) algorithm, known for its high parallelism, has taken the lead. However, compared to the successive cancellation list (SCL) algorithm, BP algorithm still falls short in terms of performance. 

To address this issue, this paper proposes an intelligent post-processing design for polar BP decoder to enhance error performance. The post-processing method identifies error bits and flips them as the messages of the initial frozen positions, and deep neural networks are used to enhance the accuracy of error bit detection. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach can achieve a performance improvement of approximately 0.3 dB with only a slight increase in complexity, compared to the original BP decoding.

Sign language is a means of communication that uses hand gestures to convey words to people with hearing impairments. However, its use is often not understood by those who do not suffer from hearing impairments, rendering it meaningless to them. The advancement of computer vision and recognition processes has provided a solution to this problem, allowing sign language to be learned and recognized by computer systems. This is especially useful in enabling ordinary people to understand and translate sign language. In this article, we present a study on the recognition of sign language using deep learning processes. The 3D-CNN algorithm is employed for the recognition process with images from the Kinect sensor. Our study found that the use of 3D-CNN for sign language recognition was highly effective, with the highest accuracy rate being 91.23%.

Low-rank tensor completion has become a focus of interest in various applications, such as image processing, data mining, and machine learning. A well-known approach for solving this problem is to minimize the sum of nuclear norms of unfolding matrices of a tensor. 

In this study, an accelerated alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is proposed for efficiently solving the objective function. The main idea is to incorporate a multistep acceleration scheme into the classical ADMM. To ensure computational efficiency, we provide an effective implementation of the algorithm and discuss its convergence properties. 

To verify the effectiveness of our approach, we test it using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Extensive numerical experiments show that our proposed algorithm outperforms the standard ADMM in terms of both convergence speed and solution accuracy.

A fault diagnosis method is proposed in this study, which employs a combination of wavelet packet reconstruction of energy entropy, particle swarm optimization (PSO), and least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) for non-stationary vibration signals of rolling bearings. The signal is preprocessed and subjected to 3-layer wavelet packet decomposition. The energy entropy percentage of the reconstruction coefficient is extracted as the feature vector, yielding an 8-dimensional fault feature vector that is then reduced to a 2-dimensional feature vector by principal component analysis (PCA). The 2-dimensional feature vector is taken as the input sample of PSO-LSSVM, and four LSSVM classifiers are established to diagnose the three fault states of the inner ring, the ball, and the outer ring of the rolling bearing. The diagnostic accuracy rate of the LSSVM multi-classifier group was found to be 100% after simulation analysis of the bearing vibration data, which clearly demonstrates the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

Modern deep learning approaches have shown that the amount of data used during training is directly proportional to the performance achieved. However, the process of annotating data is notoriously time-consuming and expensive, especially for tasks like semantic segmentation. One potential solution is to use synthetically generated images, but models trained on such data often fail to perform well on real images due to the domain shift problem. To overcome this issue, we propose using a domain-to-domain image translation GAN to bridge the gap between real and synthetic images. Our approach introduces semantic constraints into the generation process, which helps to prevent artifacts and guide synthesis. Through experiments with a semantic segmentation CNN trained on images from the synthetic GTA dataset, we demonstrate that our method can improve performance by more than 16% mIoU compared to the same model trained exclusively on synthetic images.

A coordinated bacterial nanonetwork could be applicable to large and diverse application areas including nanomedicine, nanobiotechnology, green-nanoproducts, and so on. For the construction of a bio-inspired coordinated bacterial molecular communication (MC) nanonetwork, synchronization technique is essential. This paper presents a stochastic analytical model of the nanonetwork synchronization using quorum sensing (QS). The QS mechanism that controls bacterial behavior in a collective manner is often observed in bacterial community. Bacteria use secreted chemical signaling molecules called autoinducers (AI) to communicate with each other. For more practical analysis, the presented bacterial network model employs a birth death-based statistical approach with a logistic growth curve (S curve) instead existing deterministic approach with an exponential growth curve (J curve). Assume that the internal or external AI concentration is Gaussian-distributed with corresponding mean and variance. Via simulation, we analyze the global synchronization behavior of the presented bio-inspired nanonetwork in terms of synchronization time, bacterial density and AI concentration.

Accurate load forecasting can create both economic and reliability benefits for power system operators. However, the cyberattack on load forecasting may mislead operators to make unsuitable operational decisions for the electricity delivery. To effectively and accurately detect these cyberattacks, this paper develops a machine learning-based anomaly detection (MLAD) methodology. First, load forecasts provided by neural networks are used to reconstruct the benchmark and scaling data by using the k-means clustering. Second, the cyberattack template is estimated by the naive Bayes classification based on the cumulative distribution function and statistical features of the scaling data. Finally, the dynamic programming is utilized to calculate both the occurrence and parameter of one cyberattack on load forecasting data. A widely used symbolic aggregation approximation method is compared with the developed MLAD method. Numerical simulations on the publicly load data show that the MLAD method can effectively detect cyberattacks for load forecasting data with relatively high accuracy. Also, the robustness of MLAD is verified by thousands of attack scenarios based on Monte Carlo simulation.

Acoustic word embeddings (AWEs) have been widely used for low-resource query-by-example speech search. These embeddings leverage vector distances to locate the spoken query in search content, which requires much lower computation compared to conventional DTW-based approaches. However, there is a mismatch between the learning of AWEs, which is usually done using variable-length isolated spoken words, and their application on search content, which is fixed-length speech segments obtained by shifting an analysis window.

To address this mismatch, we propose a method for learning recurrent neural AWEs by including temporal context information on spoken word pairs. In this method, we represent spoken word pairs with multilingual bottleneck features (BNFs) and pad them with the neighboring frames of the target spoken words to form fixed-length speech segment pairs. Then, we train a deep bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM) network with a triplet loss using the speech segment pairs. Finally, we obtain recurrent neural AWEs by concatenating the BLSTM backward and forward outputs.

During QbE speech search stage, both the spoken query and search content are converted into recurrent neural AWEs, and cosine distances are measured between them to find the spoken query. Our experiments show that the inclusion of temporal context information is crucial to alleviate the mismatch. The proposed recurrent neural AWEs, trained with temporal context, outperform previous state-of-the-art features, achieving a relative mean average precision (MAP) improvement of 12.5% on QbE speech search.

Nowadays, people of all ages experience high levels of stress, which can adversely affect their physical and mental health. Traditionally, the Perceived Stress Score (PSS-14) questionnaire is used to calculate stress levels, requiring manual intervention. However, in this study, we propose the use of Electroencephalography (EEG) to predict stress levels without manual intervention using a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) instrument. EEG measures and records the electrical signals in brains using sensors exhibited over the scalp. In this study, we designed a brain mapping based stress identification system using a single electrode EEG device, NeuroSky Mindwave Mobile. We recorded EEG readings from 63 students and extracted a novel feature combination of bandpower ratios (alpha, beta, delta, and theta). These features were then used to train Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbour machine learning algorithms to identify the stress level of subjects. The stress scores calculated from the PSS-14 questionnaire were used as the target class for the training set. Our results showed that the highest average classification accuracy of 74.43% was achieved using K-NN algorithm. We also observed a correlation between the bandpower ratios of different bands obtained from recorded EEG signals from the frontal portion of the brain and the stress level of subjects.

The diversification of wireless network traffic attack characteristics has led to the problems what traditional intrusion detection technology with high false positive rate, low detection efficiency, and poor generalization ability. In order to enhance the security and improve the detection ability of malicious intrusion behavior in a wireless network, this paper proposes a wireless network intrusion detection method based on improved convolutional neural network (ICNN). First, the network traffic data is characterized and preprocessed, then modeled the network intrusion traffic data by ICNN. The low-level intrusion traffic data is abstractly represented as advanced features by CNN, which extracted autonomously the sample features, and optimizing network parameters by stochastic gradient descent algorithm to converge the model. Finally, we conducted a sample test to detect the intrusion behavior of the network. The simulation results show that the method proposed in our paper has higher detection accuracy and true positive rate together with a lower false positive rate. The test results on the test set KDDTest + in our paper show that compared with the traditional models, the detection accuracy is 8.82% and 0.51% higher than that of LeNet-5 and DBN, respectively, and the recall rate is 4.24% and 1.16% higher than that of LeNet-5 and RNN, respectively, while the false positive rate is lower than the other three types of models. It also has a big advantage compared to the IDABCNN and NIDMBCNN methods.

A proposed numerical method for determining the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in electrocardiograms (ECG) that may be distorted by different types of additive noise is described. This method calculates the compression ratio (CRn) of a 10-second duration ECG fragment. The corresponding functional relationships between SNR and CRn for ECG fragments that have been distorted by muscle artifacts, electrode motion, and mixed noise were derived, and found to be exponential. The root mean square errors (RMSE) based on these dependencies for SNR within the range of -10 dB to 45 dB were determined to be 4.24 dB, 3.57 dB, and 3.33 dB, respectively. Furthermore, the inclusion of heart rate (HR) in the model reduced the error by 0.6-0.8 dB. This approach uses the standard library zlib and is recommended for use in portable mobile systems.

Welcome to the first "Tech Travel" column, which will appear as a regular contribution in future issues of IEEE Potentials. As a bioengineering Ph.D. student, my main base is Instituto Superior T?cnico in Lisbon, Portugal, but the second half of my four-year journey took me to Boston, Massachusetts. Boston is a city that loves its sports. You can see this in how residents proudly wear their favorite team gear everywhere.

We adopted actual intelligent production requirements and proposed a tiny part defect detection method to obtain a stable and accurate real-time tiny part defect detection system and solve the problems of manually setting conveyor speed and industrial camera parameters in defect detection for factory products. First, we considered the important influences of the properties of tiny parts and the environmental parameters of a defect detection system on its stability. Second, we established a correlation model between the detection capability coefficient of the part system and the moving speed of the conveyor. Third, we proposed a defect detection algorithm for tiny parts that are based on a single short detector network (SSD) and deep learning. Finally, we combined an industrial real-time detection platform with the missed detection algorithm for mechanical parts based on intermediate variables to address the problem of missed detections. We used a 0.8 cm darning needle as the experimental object. The system defect detection accuracy was the highest when the speed of the conveyor belt was 7.67 m/min.

Data aggregation is one of the most important functions provided by wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Among a variety of data aggregation schemes, the coding-based approaches (such as Compressive sensing (CS) and other similar programs) can significantly reduce traffic quantity by encoding the raw sensed data using weight vectors. The critical feature to design a coding-based data aggregation protocol is to construct a weight/measurement matrix for the application scenario. After that, the sink node assigns the column of the matrix, which is treated as the weight vector during the encoding process, to each sensor node respectively. However, for a dynamic scenario where the number of sensor nodes changes frequently, the existing approaches have to reconfigure the network by regenerating the measurement matrix and allocating the new weight vectors for all the existing nodes, which causes a considerable energy consumption and affects the regular monitoring tasks. To solve this problem, we propose a Vandermonde matrix-based scalable data aggregation protocol (VSDA), which preserves the advantages of coding-based schemes and addresses the issues mentioned above. In VSDA, as new nodes join into the scaled-up network, the original weight vectors owned by the original nodes do not need to regenerate the weight vectors entirely but add some new entries by itself at all. It outperforms the existing schemes by saving the energy in network scaling-up. Besides, we propose a concise hardware framework to quantify the data encoding process of VSDA, which provides a performance analysis process that is closer to practical application. The numeric tests validate the performance of VSDA compared with the existing schemes in several aspects, such as, the number of transmissions, energy consumption, and storage space showing the outperformance of VSDA scheme.

Making decisions in everyday life is a crucial activity that has a significant impact on shaping the course of one’s life, the quality of life, and the efficiency of completing daily tasks. The use of recommendation systems is widespread and serves to reduce the cognitive load associated with decision-making. Personal process management (PPM) involves managing the flow of activities in one’s personal life, which may involve simple tasks such as planning a party or complicated ones such as buying a house. In this study, we propose a reference model for context-aware mobile decision support systems that take into account the human factor involved in managing personal processes.

The growing popularity of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has led to the search for efficient computational platforms to enable these algorithms. Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based architectures offer a promising alternative to commonly used GPU-based platforms for CNN training. However, backpropagation in CNNs is susceptible to the limited precision of ReRAMs. As a result, training CNNs on ReRAMs affects the final accuracy of learned model. In this work, we propose REGENT, a heterogeneous architecture that combines ReRAM arrays with GPU cores, and exploits the benefits provided by 3D integration along with a high-throughput yet energy efficient Network-on-Chip (NoC) for training CNNs. We also propose a bin-packing based framework that maps CNN layers and then optimize the placement of computing elements to meet the targeted design objectives. Experimental evaluations indicate that REGENT improves full-system EDP by 55.7% on average compared to conventional GPU-only platforms for training CNNs.

Cloud computing has become the new home for virtualized and dynamically scaling computing loads. However, the pay-as-you-go business model dominant in the Cloud can prove to be financially detrimental when a high percentage of requests include low-value data. Internet of Things (IoT) offerings have expanded the list of data sources for cloud-based services. Consequently, the pre-processing required to filter data and get to the core requests that offer the most value has become even more complex. The availability of Fog nodes presents an opportunity to distribute the load and minimize network congestion. However, designing Cloud services that optimize the data management process is complex. 
Cloud service designers need to make decisions about where each step in the data management process should occur to mitigate risks of pushing high loads to Cloud servers and the network, which increases costs, and localizing the entire process, resulting in the loss of Cloud service benefits. This process is made even more complicated by Fog node capacity and available bandwidth constraints, as well as realistic factors such as Fog node ownership and device priority. To address this challenge, we propose a novel optimization model for a data-intensive, highly distributed Cloud service; it has three alternate objectives- request computational delay, service provider cost, and a weighted multi-objective version. 
We present initial experimental results using four heuristic algorithms, which highlight the contradictory factors at play such as cost, network capacity, node capacity, and Cloud capacity. These results offer valuable insight into the optimization of Cloud services in the IoT era.

Since the debut of iOS and Android smartphones 10 years ago, the world has seen a mobile era wherein our phones have become a mobile computing platform deeply integrated into our lives [1]-[4]. Due to the advancement of computing, it is believed that the world is shifting to a new era where artificial intelligence (AI) is unlocking capabilities that were previously unthinkable [5]-[13]. Because computing is becoming more universally available, interaction with computing devices needs to be much more natural, intuitive, and, above all, intelligent [14].

Satellite attitude control system is an important subsystem that ensures the normal operation of the satellite. Aiming at the problem that the model-based fault detection method relies on modeling accuracy, an actuator fault detection method based on neural network observer is proposed. The neural network is trained with the error back propagation algorithm including a correction term to ensure the accuracy and weight bounded. The neural network is used to identify and estimate actuator failure. The stability of the observer is proved by Lyapunov method. Simulation results show that this method can effectively detect and estimate actuator failure.

Noncontact penetrating detection and classification of human activities based on micro-Doppler signatures (MDs) using ultrawideband (UWB) bio-radars are valuable tasks in various practical applications such as post-disaster search-and-rescue operations and urban military operations. However, for all classifiers, MD features of different-magnitude activities at different positions are likely to result in classification errors due to MD attenuation and confusions. This letter proposes a classifier improving method called position-information-indexed classifier (PIIC). It aims at enhancing the performance of various classifiers in terms of recognition and classification. This method fully exploits the position information acquired by UWB bio-radar to create a position-labeled modularized database of MD features. It also guides searching adaptively for optimal predict submodel of PIICs for activity classification at a random position. We report through-wall detection and classification experimental results related to five activities within a range of 6 m. These results, based on four typical classifiers, demonstrate that PIIC-based classifiers can avoid those classification errors in an effective manner. Moreover, all PIIC-based classifiers present a better classification performance with an average accuracy rise of 8.16% compared with those of overall-model-based classifiers. These performance evaluation experiments suggest that this method is strongly robust and stable, presenting wide applicability to various classifiers.

With von-Neumann computing struggling to match the energy-efficiency of biological systems, there is a pressing need to explore alternative computing models. Recent experimental studies have revealed that resistive random-access memory (RRAM) is a promising alternative for DRAM. Resistive crossbar arrays possess many promising features that can not only enable high-density and low-power storage but also non von-Neumann compute models. However, most recent works focus on dot product operation with RRAM crossbar arrays and are, therefore, not flexible to implement various logical functions. 

To address this limitation, we propose a low-power dynamic computing-in-memory system that can implement various functions in Sum-of-Product (SOP) form in RRAM crossbar array architecture. To evaluate our proposed technique, we conducted simulations over a wide range of MCNC benchmarks. The simulation results showed a 1.42X and 20X latency improvement, as well as 2.6X and 12.6X power saving, compared to static and MAGIC computing-in-memory methods. 

In conclusion, our proposed low-power dynamic computing-in-memory system using RRAM crossbar arrays shows promising results for implementing a variety of logical functions in an energy-efficient manner. This could potentially pave the way for future computing models that utilize RRAM technology to address the energy-efficiency challenges faced by traditional von-Neumann computing models.

In this paper, the prospect and challenges of employing advanced memory technologies in neuro-inspired computing are discussed. In today's tech-dominated world, moving beyond the traditional Von-Neumann architecture has become critical, which has led to an increased interest in emulating biological systems. The article examines the necessary characteristics of a synaptic device required for constructing neural networks to highlight the functionalities that can be emulated with new non-volatile memory (NVM) devices. 

Moreover, the basic requirements necessary to create artificial inorganic neurons and synapses are also discussed in detail. The authors also delve into the material and device structures and how they can be used to achieve this goal. In conclusion, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the potential and obstacles that exist in utilizing state-of-the-art memory technologies in neuro-inspired computing.

In this paper, we present first-ever optimized hardware implementation of a state-of-the-art neuromorphic approach Histogram of Averaged Time Surfaces (HATS) algorithm to event-based object classification in FPGA for asynchronous time-based image sensors (ATIS). Our Implementation achieves latency of 3.3 ms for the N-CARS dataset samples and is capable of processing 2.94 Mevts/s. Speed-up is achieved by using parallelism in the design and multiple Processing Elements can be added. As development platform, Zynq-7000 SoC from Xilinx is used. The tradeoff between Average Absolute Error and Resource Utilization for fixed precision implementation is analyzed and presented. The proposed FPGA implementation is ~ 32 × power efficient compared to software implementation.

Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of blindness globally. To aid in its diagnosis based on visual fields (VF), which provide an indication of the optic nerve's functional damages, we developed a convolutional neural network. Nevertheless, the medical imaging domain presents two major challenges. Firstly, labelling a large amount of data is expensive and challenging, yet most modern deep learning methods require it. Secondly, severe data imbalance makes the classifier vulnerable to over-fitting. To overcome these challenges, we employed an AutoEncoder to train with both labelled and unlabelled data to acquire optimal features. Furthermore, we used an active learning (AL) scheme to choose a small number of the most valuable samples from the unlabelled set for model training. Augmenting negative samples generated through a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) was another approach we used to deal with the second challenge. Experiments conducted using our dataset comprising 738 samples reveal the effectiveness of this proposed approach.

With the emergence of the Internet of Medical Things in the field of medicine, the volume and variety of medical data are expanding rapidly, making clustering an important procedure for mining the vast data. Several swarm intelligence clustering algorithms, including particle swarm optimization (PSO), firefly, cuckoo, and bat, have been designed, which can be parallelized for the benefit of mass data computation. However, there are few studies focusing on the systematic analysis of the time complexities, the effect of instances (data size), attributes (dimensionality), number of clusters, and agents of these algorithms. 

This paper presents a comparative research for the PSO, firefly, cuckoo, and bat algorithms based on both synthetic and real medical data sets. The aim of the study is to identify which algorithms are effective for medical data mining and to recommend the most suitable algorithms developed for different medical data to achieve optimal clustering. 

The research findings indicate that the PSO algorithm outperforms firefly, cuckoo, and bat algorithms in terms of time complexity, while the firefly algorithm is better in terms of accuracy. The number of instances (data size) and attributes (dimensionality) have a considerable effect on the performance of clustering algorithms. Additionally, the number of clusters has an impact on the effectiveness of the clustering algorithms, and the optimal number of clusters varies depending on the studied dataset. 

This study provides valuable insights into the performance of swarm intelligence clustering algorithms for medical data mining. Furthermore, by recommending the most suitable algorithms for different medical datasets, this study can assist medical researchers in making informed decisions to achieve optimal clustering results.

Currently, there is a lack of tools available for validating 5G scenarios. Due to the increasing traffic demand on 5G networks, network operators are in search of cost-effective solutions. One such solution being adopted is the multi-tenancy approach, which requires changes to the network architecture to accommodate user mobility. This shift towards more dynamic services necessitates the development of new tools that can provide these capabilities to facilitate the validation of all new developments. To meet this need, this work presents a novel experimentation framework for the emulation of 5G scenarios with real-time user mobility and multi-tenancy support. This framework has been validated through a series of experiments, establishing its functional viability.

Agile automation of virtual network functions (VNFs) deployment is crucial for the growth of softwarized networks in the future. This automation is achieved through Virtual Network Function Descriptors (VNFDs), which are descriptor files associated with the VNFs that define resource requirements, operational behavior, and policies needed for the deployment. In this experience paper, we propose a framework for the mining of VNFDs based on Word Embeddings and Deep Neural Networks. The objective of the framework is to automatically recommend VNF descriptors that are appropriate for a given description or complete the descriptors with suitable data. The proposed framework incorporates Long short term memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), two complementary neural network methods that can be combined to enhance the performance of the framework. The experiments conducted with the proposed framework show promising results.

Unsupervised manifold learning is a vital tool for dimensionality reduction of datasets, as it finds the meaningful low-dimensional representation located on a nonlinear subspace. However, most existing manifold learning methods lack an explicit mapping function for novel out-of-sample data, limiting their effectiveness for classification tasks, especially for iterative methods like active learning.

To address this issue, out-of-sample extension methods have been introduced to generalize an existing embedding of new samples. In this paper, we propose a novel method that utilizes high-dimensional model representation (HDMR) as a nonlinear multivariate regression with the Tikhonov regularizer for unsupervised manifold learning algorithms. We conducted extensive analysis on the proposed method using illustrative and 3D synthetic datasets, as well as face recognition datasets, and compared its performance to several well-known out-of-sample methods, including locally linear embedding, Laplacian Eigenmaps, and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding.

Our results show that the proposed method achieves competitive or even better performance than the other out-of-sample methods. We conclude that HDMR can effectively provide an explicit mapping function for novel out-of-sample data, improving the effectiveness of unsupervised manifold learning for classification tasks.

Health and safety management has been an important issue in construction industry. National regulations impose the using of hard hats in construction sites. However, there are often cases in which the construction workers neglect the regulations. It is desired to monitor the correct wearing of hard hat in real time and explore monitoring techniques facilitated by deep-learning algorithms. In this paper, a convolutional neural network based hard-hat detection algorithm is proposed. In this algorithm, the detection of construction workers and the hard hats are assisted by computer vision technique where deep learning model are trained to identify the proper wearing of hard hats. The optimization of the proposed neural networks can reduce the computational complexity while maintaining a relatively high recognition precision. Experiments have been performed using five different algorithms for comparison and results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm excels in the mAP and FPS performance metrics. The experimental results collected on an embedded platform reveal that the proposed algorithm presents a good candidate for similar applications where real-time deep-learning application is desired.

some hearing-impaired people face a communication problem. Even though they can communicate with others by using sign language, but a lot of people cannot understand the sign language. As a consequence, they can only communicate with limited people. Therefore, we need a Sign Language Recognition System (SLRs) which catch the sign language and translate them into text. Some research about SLRs have been done in some countries. But only a few people conducted research on Indonesian sign language. Further, the research were limited to static features for recognizing static sign language. Other researcher conducted a research on dynamic features, but the dynamic features were good only for dynamic sign language. Thus, in this study we proposed the integration between the static features and dynamic features to recognise both static sign language and dynamic sign language. In this study we conducted two integration scenario. Based on our experiment, recognising whether a gesture was static or dynamic before doing classification produced a good result. The accuracy of this proposed study reach 89% to recognise 20 words.

The structure of the microtubule cytoskeleton provides valuable information related to morphogenesis of cells. The cytoskeleton organizes into diverse patterns that vary in cells of different types and tissues, but also within a single tissue. To assess differences in cytoskeleton organization methods are needed that quantify cytoskeleton patterns within a complete cell and which are suitable for large data sets. A major bottleneck in most approaches, however, is a lack of techniques for automatic extraction of cell contours. Here, we present a semi-automatic pipeline for cell segmentation and quantification of microtubule organization. Automatic methods are applied to extract major parts of the contours and a handy image editor is provided to manually add missing information efficiently. Experimental results prove that our approach yields high-quality contour data with minimal user intervention and serves a suitable basis for subsequent quantitative studies.

Epilepsy is one of the most prevalent neurological issues faced by a large population around the globe. Epilepsy is marked by intermittent seizures, the detection of which can be a challenging problem. Therefore, reliably detecting the onset of seizures has evoked the interest of researchers over the last few years. Major leaps in the domain of machine learning, signal processing methods, and computational capabilities have made it a tractable task. In this paper, we apply multi-resolution dynamic mode decomposition (MRDMD), which is a data-driven dimensionality reduction technique, on the problem of epileptic seizure detection. This method can effectively separate a complex non-linear system into a collection of time-scale components at different resolutions. We have applied this algorithm on two different scalp EEG datasets, i.e., CHB-MIT and KU Leaven datasets. We have applied necessary post-processing steps to reduce the false alarm rate and boost the sensitivity and specificity. A detailed analysis of the results has been presented for the proposed method applied to both the datasets. The algorithm achieves a sensitivity of 0.937 and 0.96, a specificity of 0.99 and 0.99, a false alarm rate of 0.587 and 0.413 per hour, and a latency of 3.12 and 2.75 s for CHB-MIT and KU Leuven, respectively. The results indicate that the multi-resolution analysis yields a significant improvement in sensitivity compared with the basic dynamic mode decomposition.

This paper presents a fuzzy supervisor for a neural emulator of nonlinear MIMO processes. Its goal is to ensure optimal performance of the neural emulator, in terms of rapid convergence and accurate representation. Unlike classical cases that require initialization of parameters and online adaptation, this proposed system does not require either. Numerical simulations were conducted to demonstrate the improved performance of the proposed fuzzy supervisor, compared to the classical case that relies on starting terms.

The consumer Internet of Things (IoT) platforms are gaining high popularity. However, due to the open nature of wireless communications, smart home platforms are facing many new challenges, especially in the aspect of security and privacy. In this article, we first introduce the architecture of current popular smart home platforms and elaborate the functions of each component. Then we discuss the security and privacy challenges arising from these platforms and review the state of the art of the proposed countermeasures. We give a comprehensive survey on several new attacks on the voice interface of smart home platforms, which aim to gain unauthorized access and execute over-privileged behaviors to compromise the user's privacy. To thwart these attacks, we propose a novel voice liveness detection system, which analyzes the wireless signals generated by IoT devices and the received voice samples to perform user authentication. We implement a real-world testbed on Samsung's SmartThings platform to evaluate the performance of the proposed system, and demonstrate its effectiveness.

In this work, we combined the model based reinforcement learning (MBRL) and model free reinforcement learning (MFRL) to stabilize a biped robot (NAO robot) on a rotating platform, where the angular velocity of the platform is unknown for the proposed learning algorithm and treated as the external disturbance. Nonparametric Gaussian processes normally require a large number of training data points to deal with the discontinuity of the estimated model. Although some improved method such as probabilistic inference for learning control (PILCO) does not require an explicit global model as the actions are obtained by directly searching the policy space, the overfitting and lack of model complexity may still result in a large deviation between the prediction and the real system. Besides, none of these approaches consider the data error and measurement noise during the training process and test process, respectively. We propose a hierarchical Gaussian processes (GP) models, containing two layers of independent GPs, where the physically continuous probability transition model of the robot is obtained. Due to the physically continuous estimation, the algorithm overcomes the overfitting problem with a guaranteed model complexity, and the number of training data is also reduced. The policy for any given initial state is generated automatically by minimizing the expected cost according to the predefined cost function and the obtained probability distribution of the state. Furthermore, a novel Q(λ) based MFRL method scheme is employed to improve the policy. Simulation results show that the proposed RL algorithm is able to balance NAO robot on a rotating platform, and it is capable of adapting to the platform with varying angular velocity.

This paper proposes an innovative edge computing system for IoT-based smart grids to overcome the limitations of the current cloud computing paradigm in power systems. The challenges faced by cloud-based power systems such as high bandwidth with low latency requirements can be addressed by the new system by introducing edge computing into the traditional cloud-based power system and establishing a new hardware and software architecture. Large amounts of data generated in the electrical grid will be analyzed, processed and stored at the edge of the network, ensuring that the IoT-based smart grids have the ability to connect and manage numerous terminals, perform real-time analysis and processing of massive data, and facilitate the digitalization of smart grids. 

Furthermore, this paper proposes a privacy protection strategy through edge computing, data prediction strategy, and preprocessing strategy for hierarchical decision-making based on task grading (HDTG) in IoT-based smart grids. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approaches. Thus, the implementation of such an innovative edge computing system can lead to a more efficient and effective power system, improved data management, and a better overall user experience.

Reliability is nowadays considered a key requirement in wireless sensor networks for their increasing diffusion in various Internet of Things applications. However, radio interference from various sources may heavily affect the performance of wirelessly connected embedded devices, resulting into increased packet collisions and congestions. There is therefore a widely recognized need of both theoretical and practical investigations capable of shedding light on the factors affecting the operativeness of sensor networks subject to interference. In this paper, we investigate the role of packet length into the reliability and energy efficiency of low-power medium access protocols. Specifically, we propose a mathematical model to explore the functional dependence of the reliability of a pair of sensor nodes under interference from packet length. We also present a wide range of experimental evaluations aimed at validating the model and at providing novel insights on dependability issues. In particular, we assess the performance of Contiki's default medium access control layer (together with that of an always listening receiver, as a baseline) in terms of packet loss rate and energy efficiency for varying payload lengths. Experimental results highlight the interplay between packet size and interference and in particular the tradeoff between the robustness against interference and the overhead imposed to communication as a function of the length of data packets. The Pareto curve describing the energy efficiency as a function of the packet loss rate, demonstrates the existence of intermediate packet size representing an optimal choice for balancing energy consumption and communication reliability, enabling adequate system dimensioning at design-level.

In this paper, we introduce a new multiple access scheme for wireless sensor networks (WSNs) based on Network MIMO technology. Our proposed approach uses a slotted ALOHA type protocol with successive interference cancellation (SIC) to efficiently meet the IoT society's evolving requirements.

To achieve effective results, we rely on the capture effect. However, in the past, the typical sensor node (SN) arrangements did not always ensure adequate power for packets resulting in uneven distribution at the fusion center (FC). Even with SIC, which utilizes temporal and spatial diversity, these arrangements can still pose a challenge.

Our approach overcomes this issue by making use of the signal separation method present in network MIMO systems. This allows FCs to decode such packets, boosting the number of SNs that transmit data while preventing any loss of service quality. 

To prove our methodology's effectiveness, we conducted computer simulations, which have demonstrated that our proposed approach is efficient and results in a significant increase in the number of SNs that can send data without compromising the quality of service, thus providing an optimal solution for WSNs.

In vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs), the protection of user privacy is essential, particularly due to the disclosure of the vehicle movement trajectory. Location-based services offer numerous advantages, but they must be refined to address privacy concerns. This study proposes an innovative differential privacy mechanism that is RL-based to randomize the released vehicle locations to safeguard the semantic trajectory of the vehicle while employing RL to select the obfuscation policy. By considering the semantic location of the vehicle and attack history, this scheme allows for the vehicle to optimize the obfuscation policy in terms of privacy gain and quality of service loss. This method outperforms benchmark schemes by increasing privacy gain, decreasing the quality of service loss, and ultimately enhancing the utility of the vehicle. The scheme operates effectively as a dynamic privacy protection game that adapts to varying attack models without the vehicle being aware of the current situation. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this innovative scheme.

Customized Two Photon Dose Computation Engines for Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT) Plans

To ensure high conformity and fast computation for Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT) plans, two photon dose computation engines have been customized based on pencil beam models. These engines are designed specifically for prostate cancer radiation treatment but can be adapted for other radiation treatment plans.

The first model is designed to run through the initial VMAT iteration steps, allowing for swift execution but limited accuracy. The second model is more precise but requires a longer computation time, as it is designed to run over VMAT while it converges. 

Both models have been optimized to meet the requirements of high precision and fast delivery times while maintaining adherence to the constraints applicable to VMAT plans. The customized photon dose computation engines serve as a valuable tool for accurate and efficient radiation treatment planning.

Objective: The objective of this study is to develop a reliable method for monitoring cerebral embolic load from high-intensity transient signals (HITS) recorded with a single-channel transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasound.

Methods: The proposed method involves HITS detection and characterization using a weighted-frequency Fourier linear combiner to estimate baseline Doppler signal power. An adaptive threshold is then determined by examining the Doppler signal power variance about the baseline estimate, and HITS are extracted if their Doppler power exceeds this threshold. The detected HITS are analyzed in the time-frequency domain to segment the signals into individual emboli since signatures from multiple emboli may be superimposed. A logistic regression classification approach is employed to classify HITS into emboli or artifacts. Data from 12 children undergoing mechanical circulatory support or cardiac catheterization were collected using a commercial TCD device with emboli-detection capabilities. A subset of 696 HITS were reviewed, annotated, and split into training and testing sets for developing and evaluating the HITS classification algorithm.

Results: The classifier yielded 98% and 96% sensitivity for 100% specificity on training and testing data, respectively. The TF approach decomposed 38% of candidate embolic signals into two or more embolic events that accounted for 69% of the overall embolic counts. The processing pipeline produced highly accurate emboli identification, and the emboli counts were lower (by a median of 64%) compared to the commercial ultrasound system's estimates.

Significance: The proposed method enables sensitive detection and segmentation of embolic signatures using only single-channel, single-frequency Doppler ultrasound. This approach paves the way toward accurate real-time cerebral emboli monitoring.

In the area of multimedia indexing and processing, a big challenge is to classify the mood of the listener through music. It is also a prodigious challenge to separate the noisy signals into speech, music or silence. Mood of a person may depend upon music. According to the music psychologists, behavior of a person is defined by his mood. Thus, this research evaluates the features of audio that have substantial impact on mood of a person and focuses that how to distinguish the speech signals and music from audio file at the same time. Many audio extraction algorithms have been hashed out in this paper and proposes one MMCAD (music mood classification & Audio discrimination) which is the integration of mood detector and speech / music discriminator with improved efficiency and accuracy.

The call centers could be broadly categorized in two types: Inbound and Outbound. In an Inbound call center, the focus is always on multiple factors, such as customer satisfaction and customer retention. However, in outbound call centers, the only focus is on revenue generation by making sales and conducting successful surveys. The main challenge in all outbound call centers is to increase the revenue without increasing the expenses. The management of the call centers has used various techniques to make their Customer Service Representatives (CSRs) perfect sellers. For outbound call centers, we do not find the same level of research and systems, like the ones available for inbound call centers. Several intelligent systems have been developed for inbound call centers, which operate based on the history of their customers, maintained in their data repository. It has been observed that such systems lack a thorough analysis of the dialing data. In this paper, we use the dialing data intelligently (besides CRS's performance), after analyzing it statistically and by using different data mining techniques. We implemented the concept of 3R (Right Data to the Right CSR at the Right Time). Our work helped us to increase the number of sales (revenue) besides decreasing the expenses, by smart utilization of data and the workforce.

A novel domain decomposition method (DDM) for analyzing electromagnetic fields in composite very thin dielectric/complex finite array objects has been proposed. This DDM, based on simplified volume-surface integral equation (S-VSIE), is both non-overlapping and non-conforming. The composite objects are decomposed into subdomains to improve modeling efficiency. To model very thin dielectrics efficiently, the S-VSIE is applied using simplified prism vector (SPV) basis functions. To discretize volumes conformally and non-conformally, a discontinuous Galerkin volume integral equation method (DG-S-VIE) based on the SPV basis functions is proposed. Additionally, an additive non-overlapping DD preconditioner is designed for fast iterative solutions.

With the rapid development of cloud manufacturing (CMfg), a large number of functionally equivalent cloud services are available on the Internet, thus quality of service (QoS) prediction has become a hot issue. Since the QoS of service varies widely among users, many Collaborative Filtering (CF) approaches are recently proposed to predict the unknown QoS by extending the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) similarity. However, most existing approaches either enhance the similarity computation inadequately or ignore the data sparsity problem, and are thus vulnerable to the unreliable result. To address this problem, we propose a hybrid approach HAP for QoS prediction. First, to achieve high prediction accuracy, we employ a similarity-enhanced CF (L-CF) for local QoS prediction, in which the personalized influence of similar users and services are considered when computing PCC similarity. Second, to overcome the data sparsity problem, we propose a global QoS prediction approach based on the case-based reasoning (G-CBR) which could make full use of both user and service information. Finally, we establish an ensemble model to combine the results of two approaches. Comprehensive real-world experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared with other state-of-the-arts approaches, particularly when the QoS data is very sparse.

Modern tactical wireless network (TWN) communication technologies are not only capable of transmitting voice but also capable of transmitting data. Due to such capabilities, TWN have high security requirements as any security breach can lead to detrimental effects. Hence, securing such an environment is not only a requirement but also a virtual prerequisite to the network centric warfare operational (NCW) theory. One key to securing this environment is to promptly and accurately recognize information warfare attacks directed to the network and respond to them. This is achieved using intrusion detection systems (IDS). However, false detection of nodes in hostile environment remains a major problem that need to be addressed. Recently, machine learning methods and algorithms have shown applicability and are growing research area for cyber security and intrusion detection. Conversely, several decades of research in the field of machine learning have resulted in a multitude of different algorithms for solving a broad range of problems. The question then becomes, which one amongst these machine learning algorithms have the potential to enhance or address IDS issues in TWN. In this paper, seven machine learning classifiers are analyzed; Multi-Layer Perceptron, Bayesian Network, Support Vector Machine (SMO), Adaboost, Random Forest, Bootstrap Aggregation, and Decision Tree (J48). WEKA tool was used to implement and evaluate the classifiers.
