The results obtained indicate that ensemble-based learning methods outperformed single learning methods when we consider the detection accuracy metrics; AUC, TPR, and FPR. However, ensemble classifiers tend to be slower in in terms of build time and model test time.

With CMOS feature size heading towards atomic dimensions, unjustifiable static power, reliability, and economic implications are exacerbating, prompting for research on new materials, devices, and/or computation paradigms. Within this context, Graphene Nanorib-bons (GNRs), owing to graphene's excellent electronic properties, may serve as basic blocks for carbon-based nanoelectronics. In this paper we build upon the fact that GNR behaviour can be controlled according to some desired functionality via top/back gate contacts and propose to combine GNRs with complementary functionalities to construct Boolean gates. To this end, we introduce a generic GNR-based Boolean gate structure, composed of two GNRs, i.e., a pull-up GNR performing the gate Boolean function and a pull-down GNR performing the inverted Boolean function. Subsequently, by properly adjusting GNRs' dimensions and topology, we design 2-input AND, NAND, and XOR graphene-based Boolean gates, as well as 1-input gates, i.e., inverter and buffer. Our SPICE simulations indicate that the proposed gates exhibit a smaller propagation delay, from 23% for the XOR gate to 6× for the AND gate, and 2 orders of magnitude smaller power consumption, when compared with 7 nm CMOS based counterparts, while requiring a 1 to 2 orders of magnitude smaller active area footprint. These results clearly indicate that GNR-based gates have great potential as basic building blocks for future beyond CMOS energy effective nanoscale circuits.

This paper investigates the problem of coarse timing synchronization for low signal-to-noise radio wireless orthogonal frequency-division-multiplexing (OFDM) systems in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT). OFDM is widely used in IoT scenarios, where the system often needs to work at a low SNR to achieve greater coverage. To address this challenge, the proposed coarse synchronization method employs a noise-eliminated timing metric that efficiently responds to the low SNR environment. Simulation results demonstrate a significant improvement in detection failure probability at different SNRs and number of processed frames, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

In recent times, the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become widespread due to their low cost and high flexibility. However, the rational deployment of UAV aerial base stations (ABSs) is crucial when dealing with sudden emergency events and uncertain user service requests. Deploying multiple UAVs with varying properties such as power and service radius presents a challenge. To solve this problem, researchers have turned to mean-field-type game (MFTG) to obtain optimal strategies for UAV deployment that can be applied in practical applications. MFTG considers the arbitrariness of the number of UAVs, the distinguishability of agents, and their non-negligible effect on the system. However, the homogeneity of multiple UAVs cannot be guaranteed in the practical communication model. To address this, the deployment of multiple UAV ABSs with varying properties has been formulated as a MFTG problem. Each UAV analyzes the communication requests of ground users and decides on the best flight strategy to minimize its own cost function. Furthermore, the study proves the existence of the Nash equilibrium of the MFTG problem and utilizes the direct square complement method to minimize the cost function of each UAV. Simulation results indicate the proposed method's correctness and the rationality of the deployment.

This paper presents an autonomous intersection management scheme using reservation-based scheduling. The scheme coordinates the access of the autonomous vehicles to an intersection without a traffic light such that all vehicles can travel across the intersection without collision. In this paper, we make our model applicable to real-world system by allowing the vehicles to move within a predefined speed range while in the intersection. Simulation shows the effect of the speed range size to the efficiency of the system.

Medical devices measure vital parameters such as pulse, respiration rate, and blood oxygenation, over periods of days or weeks in a continuous manner. Traditional systems only support such requirements in stationary applications where a constant power supply is available. Trends toward remote healthcare and telemedicine require wearable devices, able to provide similar functionalities in wireless mode. Miniaturized and thin form factors, desirable in wearable applications, set stringent constraints on the available power, and consequently on the accuracy and lifetime. Energy harvesting combined with low-power design and energy efficient processing can significantly extend the lifetime of wearable devices. This paper presents a wearable pulse oximeter assembled in a 3D ring-like geometry that achieves self-sustainability by exploiting efficient power management, solar energy harvesting, and ultra-low power processing in a multi-core microcontroller. The design strategy of combining onboard processing to monitor blood oxygenation and the transmission of only relevant information via a Bluetooth low-energy (BLE) interface, significantly reduces the overall energy consumption. Experimental results on the designed and developed prototype demonstrate that measuring the blood oxygenation once every minute with a sampling rate of 100 samples/s achieve accurate results at the daily energy consumption of 28 J including hourly BLE transmissions. The low-power design allows the system to be self-sustainable with just 64 min of sunlight per day or 12 hrs. of indoor home light.

We have expanded a recently introduced data-driven control method for reference tracking to a broader category of Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) systems that feature weak coupling between various states in terms of the induced norm. We have extended the analysis using results from former research and integrating it with small-gain arguments for the coupling terms to accommodate MIMO systems. Additionally, we have proposed a comprehensive approach for fine-tuning and estimating the controller parameters. The efficacy of the data-driven controller has been demonstrated through simulations and experiments conducted on a Control Moment Gyroscope (CMG) test bed. We have compared the tracking performance of our technique with that of an LPV controller and shown that our approach is highly effective.

Current indoor semantic recognition systems rely on smartphones to sense patterns. However, there is a need for a device-free system, which is where WiFiMap+ comes in. WiFiMap+ is an inference system that utilizes WiFi signals to recognize high-level indoor semantics from human activities and environments. The system consists of a two-stream architecture that characterizes static indoor environments and dynamic human activities separately to generate spatial and movement streams. The CSI-environment model reduces the effect of human activities on environment detection. The environment-based testing sample representation method utilizes environment knowledge to overcome CSI diversity caused by environment changes. WiFiMap+ was implemented using commercial WiFi devices and evaluated for seven common semantic detection cases in six-room scenarios. The results showed that WiFiMap+ is robust to multi-room scenarios and achieved an average accuracy of 92.8% and a minimum accuracy of about 82%.

The rapid growth of vehicular networks has led to a significant increase in the amount of sensing data generated. Sharing this data between vehicles has enabled the development of numerous vehicular applications, aimed at enhancing driving safety and improving vehicular services. However, to ensure that this data sharing is secure and traceable, a Delegated Proof-of-Stake (DPoS) consensus algorithm has been utilized to establish Blockchain-Enabled VEhicular Networks (BEVENs).

Within DPoS, miners are divided into active miners and standby miners. Active miners are responsible for block generation and verification, while standby miners conduct further verification and auditing of newly generated blocks. However, the limited number of active miners in DPoS increases the risk of internal collusion, which may result in a malicious manipulation of block verification results.

To prevent collusion among active miners and incentivize participation in block verification, a contract theory-based model has been adopted. This model considers both block verification security and delay, enabling efficient interaction between active and standby miners. Numerical results have shown that this approach enhances the security and efficiency of data sharing in BEVENs.

In summary, the utilization of DPoS consensus algorithm and contract theory-based modeling ensures the security, traceability, and efficiency of data sharing within vehicular networks, allowing for the development of innovative vehicular applications aimed at enhancing driving safety and improving vehicular services.

This paper presents 2nd order adaptive controller for a linear delta robot based on the backstepping design. For different inputs, including step and continuity signals, such as sine waves, 1st order and 2nd order controller design the compensation and achieve the tracking error can converge to zero. We used the parameters of linear delta robot and input the step function, sine wave to compare the performance which linear delta robot system is in the external disturbance. The design of the controller is mainly for the reference input order to reduce the system steady-state error, effectively improve the tracking performance of the input signal and achieve zero steady-state error.

Artificial intelligence (AI) was formally introduced in 1956, and since then, the world has witnessed a significant change from manual labor to digital systems. This transformation is an ongoing process, driven by the immense research aimed at developing intelligence in machines with relatively limited guidance. The ultimate goal of AI is to create intelligent machines that can perceive and apply knowledge similarly to humans.

This study seeks to comprehend the dynamics and impacts of AI and explore the link between Human Cognition and Artificial intelligence in the contemporary world. To achieve this, the research methodology involved a focus group interview with 15 experts from Dubai with a subsequent thematic analysis of the data. The findings indicate that AI and psychological science continuously influence one another. Perception is also a crucial aspect of the cognitive process and forms the basis for AI in action.

Classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is crucial for identifying heart arrhythmias. However, automatic classification is challenging due to the diverse waveform and characteristic variations in ECG signals among patients. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes i-vector adapted patient-specific deep neural networks (iAP-DNNs), which adapt a patient-independent DNN using both patient-specific identity vectors (i-vectors) and raw ECG data. The i-vector is obtained by compressing the patient's ECG data using a factor analysis model, and is then incorporated into the middle hidden layer of the patient-independent DNN. The whole network is fine-tuned using stochastic gradient descent to create a patient-specific classifier. The analysis reveals that the iAP-DNNs, which leverage the information in the i-vectors, are more effective at discriminating normal and arrhythmic heartbeats than networks that only use patient-specific ECG data for adaptation. The experimental results based on the MIT-BIH database demonstrate that the iAP-DNNs outperform existing patient-specific classifiers in terms of sensitivity and specificity, with ROC curves that exceed those of existing methods.

A problem deeply investigated by multimedia forensics researchers is that of detecting which device has been used to capture a video. This enables us to trace down the owner of a video sequence, which proves extremely helpful to solve copyright infringement cases as well as to fight distribution of illicit material (e.g., child exploitation clips and terroristic threats). Currently, the most promising methods to tackle this task exploit unique noise traces left by camera sensors on acquired images. However, given the recent advancements in motion stabilization of video content, robustness of sensor pattern noise-based techniques is strongly hindered. Indeed, video stabilization introduces geometric transformations to video frames, thus making camera fingerprint estimation problematic with classical approaches. In this paper, we deal with the challenging problem of attributing stabilized videos to their recording device. Specifically, we propose: 1) a strategy to extract the characteristic fingerprint of a device, starting from either a set of images or stabilized video sequences and 2) a strategy to match a stabilized video sequence with a given fingerprint. The proposed methodology is tested on videos coming from a set of different smartphones, taken from the modern publicly available Vision Dataset. The conducted experiments also provide an interesting insight on the effect of modern smartphones video stabilization algorithms on specific video frames.

With the feature size of CMOS technology approaching atomic dimensions, concerns over static power consumption, reliability, and economic implications are becoming more significant. Thus, research into new materials, devices, and computation paradigms is needed to address these issues. Graphene Nanoribbons (GNRs) are a potential solution, as their exceptional electronic properties make them useful for constructing carbon-based nanoelectronics. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to combine GNRs with complementary functionalities to create Boolean gates. By adjusting the dimensions and topology of the GNRs, we design 2-input AND, NAND, and XOR gates, as well as 1-input gates. Our SPICE simulations show that these GNR-based gates have 2 orders of magnitude lower power consumption and require a 1 to 2 orders of magnitude smaller active area footprint than traditional 7 nm CMOS-based counterparts. This highlights the great potential of GNR-based gates as basic building blocks for energy-efficient nanoscale circuits beyond CMOS technology.

In the modern scenario of smart-grids, the concept of virtual power plant (VPP) is undoubtedly a cornerstone for the smooth integration of renewable energy sources into existing energy systems with a high penetration level. A VPP is the aggregation of decentralized medium-scale power sources, including photovoltaic and wind power plants, combined heat and power units, as well as demand-responsive loads and storage systems, with a twofold objective. On one hand, VPP relieves the stability and dispatchability problems on the external smart grid since it can be operated on an individual basis, appearing as a single system on the whole. On the other hand, VPP improves flexibility coming from all the networked units and enable traders to enhance forecasting and trading programs of renewable energies. This paper proposes a novel distributed decentralized prediction method for the management of VPPs. The novelty of the proposed technique is to effectively combine the concepts of neural networks and machine learning with a distributed architecture that is suitable for the aggregation purposes of the VPP.

In this paper, we propose a data-driven visual rhythm prediction method, which overcomes the previous works' deficiency that predictions are made primarily by human-crafted hard rules. In our approach, we first extract features including original frames and their residuals, optical flow, scene change, and body pose. These visual features will be next taken into an end-to-end neural network as inputs. Here we observe that there are some slight misaligning between features over the timeline and assume that this is due to the distinctions between how different features are computed. To solve this problem, the extracted features are aligned by an elaborately designed layer, which can also be applied to other models suffering from mismatched features, and boost performance. Then these aligned features are fed into sequence labeling layers implemented with BiLSTM [9] and CRF [10] to predict the onsets. Due to the lack of existing public training and evaluation set, we experiment on a dataset constructed by ourselves based on professionally edited Music Videos (MVs), and the F1 score of our approach reaches 79.6.

Cloud computing has emerged as one of the most important technological revolutions globally. However, the rapid growth of cloud computing has imposed a massive financial burden and resulted in environmental side effects due to excessive energy consumption. The high power consumption is not only attributed to the size of data centers but also to the ineptitude of resource usage. Most of the extant research has focused on reducing power consumption by an aggressive VM consolidation, which leads to the violation of the service level agreement (SLA). Furthermore, the unbalanced resource consumption exacerbates the unavailable wasted resources that are referred to as unavailable resource fragmentation. In this paper, we propose the use of a balanced resources consumption algorithm called BRC-IBMMT in order to enhance the efficiency of resource consumption while achieving an acceptable balance between conflicting correlation objectives of power consumption as well as SLA violation. The extensive simulation results of different types of workload validate and lend credence to the significance of the proposed method in reducing power consumption and SLA violation of the cloud data center.

A brain is comprised of numerous structured regions that are responsible for various functions. However, obtaining detailed regional annotations on stereotaxic coordinates is a rare occurrence, necessitating the use of one or few available annotated results of a specific brain section to label images of broadly accessible brain section samples. In this study, we present a one-shot learning approach for segmenting regions of mouse brains. We utilize the highly organized geometry of brains and introduce a reference mask that incorporates both the anatomical structure (visual information) and the brain atlas to achieve improved brain segmentation. Using the UNet model in conjunction with this reference mask, we successfully predict the region of hippocampus with a high degree of accuracy. Moreover, we implement this methodology to segment brain images into 95 detailed regions, which are augmented from the annotation on only one image from Allen Brain Atlas. Our one-shot learning approach provides neuroscientists with an efficient method for brain segmentation that will facilitate future region-specific functional studies of brains.

In LTE systems, the size of the cyclic-prefix (CP) can be extended to improve resilience against multipath distortions, but this complicates downlink synchronization. This paper proposes a maximum likelihood (ML) approach to detecting CP length in the presence of timing uncertainty and frequency offset. The proposed ML approach accounts for the irregular LTE symbol and computes a different metric for each possible position of the irregular symbol within the observation window. This flexible approach can be applied to any future multicarrier standard for CP length detection, with or without irregular symbols.

Texture classification is a crucial task in machine vision for various applications, which can be achieved by learning texture features using a convolutional mask. However, the conventional convolutional mask has limited learning ability, as it has a single orientation. Moreover, the optimization process can get trapped at local optima, and the discrimination capacity of the learned mask is often unsatisfactory. To overcome these challenges, a novel moving convolutional mask is introduced in this approach. It enhances the discrimination of specific texture features and improves the optimization process. 

The process of achieving a suitable convolutional mask is considered as a combinatorial optimization problem, which is solved by maximizing texture energy using ant lion optimizer (ALO). The proposed approach is tested on publicly available images and compared with other state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that ALO has strong optimization ability and the proposed method is robust, adaptive, and outperforms improved grey level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM), directional statistical Gabor filter, and Tuned convolutional mask in terms of fitness value and classification accuracy. The proposed method has achieved a fitness value of 27 and classification accuracy of 91% for all images.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been highly successful in computer vision and speech processing applications, but deploying large-scale models on embedded systems is constrained by computation and memory. To address these, we propose an optimized block-floating-point (BFP) arithmetic in our accelerator for efficient deep neural network inference. We represent feature maps and model parameters in 16-bit and 8-bit formats, respectively, in off-chip memory, reducing memory and off-chip bandwidth requirements by 50% and 75% compared to the 32-bit FP counterpart. Our proposed 8-bit BFP arithmetic with optimized rounding and shifting-operation-based quantization schemes improves energy and hardware efficiency threefold. A CNN model can be deployed without retraining with no more than a 0.12% accuracy loss. The reconfigurable accelerator, implemented on the Xilinx VC709 evaluation board, has three parallelism dimensions, ping-pong off-chip DDR3 memory access, and an optimized on-chip buffer group. It achieves a performance of 760.83 GOP/s and 82.88 GOP/s/W at a 200-MHz working frequency, significantly outperforming previous accelerators.

Creative problem solving involves experimentation, evaluation, and iteration. However, evaluating design concepts can be difficult as they are often ill-defined. To address this issue, we propose a computational theory of evaluation in creative design. Our technique utilizes analogical comparison to evaluate a design concept by comparing it with alternative articulations of the concept.

We apply this theory to biologically inspired design, which involves using biological analogies for conceptual design of technological systems. Our analogical comparison technique supports evaluation of prior technological designs, biological source cases, and candidate conceptual designs by mapping between alternative functional models of these design concepts. Using a hierarchically organized analogical mapping technique, we can align two models and identify differences between them.

To implement this technique, we have developed an operational artificial intelligence agent called Design Evaluation through Simulation and Comparison (DESC). We have evaluated DESC through computational experimentation across several models to demonstrate its strengths and limitations and to identify areas for future research.

Overall, our computational theory of evaluation provides a valuable tool for creative problem solving and design evaluation, particularly in biologically inspired design.

Traditional web security assessments are evaluated using a single data source, and the results of the calculations from different data sources are different. Based on multi-source data, this paper uses Analytic Hierarchy Process to construct an evaluation model, calculates the weight of each level of indicators in the web security evaluation model, analyzes and processes the data, calculates the host security threat assessment values at various levels, and visualizes the evaluation results through ECharts+WebGL technology.

We present a higher order quadrilateral surface remeshing approach for application to the method of moments. We briefly introduce the motivation for high-quality quadrilateral meshes for accurate and efficient application of cutting edge integration and singularity extraction approaches. Results are demonstrated for simple surfaces and compared with a common quadrilateral remeshing algorithm.

This paper defines flexibility reserve trajectory as a single reserve product that not only supplies the energy imbalance in real-time operation but also the resulting ramping requirements by embedding the flexible ramping trajectories as time derivative of the reserve trajectories. Further, a stochastic optimization model is proposed for multi-fidelity co-optimization of energy and flexibility reserve in day-ahead power systems operation. The proposed model integrates operation decisions with different levels of modeling fidelity in a single stochastic optimization problem. More specifically, day-ahead energy trajectories, day-ahead flexibility reserve capacity trajectories, and real-time flexibility reserve deployment trajectories are modeled by Bernstein polynomials with different degrees as required to match the load and renewable generation with different levels of variability in day-ahead and real-time operations. The proposed model is implemented on the IEEE reliability test system using load and solar generation data of California ISO, where the numerical results demonstrate that the proposed model schedules a reserve capacity that more accurately matches the real-time energy imbalance and ramping requirements of net-load, while reducing the total operation cost of the system.

Inspired by the thought of TOPSIS, a new multi-attribute decision making (MADM) method is proposed under the interval normal type-2 fuzzy set (INT2FS) environment. Firstly, the Expected value of INT2FS is defined to obtain the ideal solutions. Secondly, the Euclidean distance of INT2FS is given to depict the similarity between each alternative and ideal solutions. Finally, a supplier selection problem is used to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the the proposed approach.

A metasurface-based thermophotovoitaics system directly converts thermal radiation to electricity through the photovoitaic effect. The efficiency of such a system significantly depends on the thermal stability and efficiency of the spectral reshaping of the metasurface. We couple the generative adversarial network technique with the topology optimization to design a new class of high-efficiency metasurface thermal emitters. Numerical simulations confirm that due to non-trivial metasurface topologies the proposed method generates the close-to-ultimate high-efficiency emitters. Comparison with a conventional global optimization technique shows that our topology-optimized designs demonstrate superior spectral control of thermal blackbody radiation than the regular-shape emitters optimized with conventional optimization.

The use of human biometrics is becoming increasingly prevalent, with the main objective being the recognition of individuals to control unauthorized access to both digital services and physical locations. However, implementation of human biometrics for recognition purposes presents several challenges including template storage capacity, computational requirements, and privacy of biometric data. These issues need to be considered in addition to performance accuracy, particularly for authentication systems with limited resources.

To address these challenges, we propose a palm-vein recognition scheme based on the wave atom transform (WAT). This scheme allows for efficient computation, maintenance, and matching of palm-vein templates while providing a secure and privacy-preserving environment. The WAT domain is used to extract palm-vein traits, which offers sparser expansion and better texture feature extraction capabilities. Randomization and quantization are applied to the extracted features to generate compact, privacy-preserving palm-vein templates.

Our analysis of the proposed scheme shows that it offers comparable matching accuracy with a minimum template size and computational time of 280 bytes and 0.43 seconds, respectively. Equal error rates (EERs) of 1.98%, 0%, 3.05%, and 1.49% were obtained for PolyU, PUT, VERA, and our palm-vein datasets, respectively.

In conclusion, the proposed WAT-based palm-vein recognition scheme addresses the challenges faced by traditional recognition schemes, in terms of template storage space, computational complexity, and privacy preservation. It offers comparable accuracy with minimal resource use and provides a secure authentication system with potential to be used in various applications.

Trending is the era of artificial intelligence, which now a day plays very crucial roles for performing daily repetitive as well as decision making complex tasks. Sensing the dynamic scenario and making decision based on visual perception is blooming a bit. In this we propose an algorithm in which we divide the image in two categories frame of reference and the visual objects. Frame of reference gives a platform on which the object is placed that deals in making environment decision. We use faster RCNN algorithm for object and background detection. In co-relation of object, there motion and environmental condition, for making decisions Naives bayes algorithm is developed which is used to sense the surrounding and automatically make a decision based on visual perception and coordinate needs. At the end we analysis the experimental results such as training accuracy, total losses function which has pretty fine reliability and accuracy.

During aircraft, missile, and ship movements, rudders play a crucial role in controlling their direction. However, traditional methods of production and manufacturing of rudders involve manual measurement of individual parameters, leading to substantial loss of time and manpower. In this paper, we propose a new intelligent approach to the fault testing of rudders using machine learning technology. Our focus is primarily on the prediction-oriented issues of multi-dimensional performance parameter data mining and classification modeling, which includes data feature analysis, processing, and fault location based on classification models. Our algorithm is optimized with shuffled frog leaping algorithm (SFLA) to enhance the accuracy of the classification model, resulting in a more efficient and accurate decision-making process. Thus, our new method breaks through the technical bottleneck of low efficiency in parameter testing and the limitations of traditional rudder fault location by utilizing automatic testing and intelligent analysis.

From a single RGB image of an unknown face, taken under unknown conditions, we estimate a physically plausible lighting model. First, the 3D geometry and texture of the face are estimated by fitting a 3D Morphable Model to the 2D input. With this estimated 3D model and a Virtual Light Stage (VLS), we generate a gallery of images of the face with all the same conditions, but different lighting. We consider non-lambertian reflectance and non-convex geometry to handle more realistic illumination effects in complex lighting conditions. Our hierarchical Bayesian approach automatically suppresses inconsistencies between the model and the input. It estimates the RGB values for the light sources of a VLS to reconstruct the input face with the estimated 3D face model. We discuss the relevance of the hierarchical approach to this minimally constrained inverse rendering problem and show how the hyperparameters can be controlled to improve the results of the algorithm for complex effects, such as cast shadows. Our algorithm is a contribution to single image face modeling and analysis, provides information about the imaging condition and facilitates realistic reconstruction of the input image, relighting, lighting transfer and lighting design.

Recently, visible light communication (VLC) networks have emerged as a promising alternative for indoor data access, due to high data rate, low implementation cost, and immunity to radio frequency (RF) interference. However, the co-existence of VLC with the RF access points as well as the dependence of VLC to room illumination compel both technologies to work in parallel and thus, to form a hybrid heterogeneous VLC/RF network. This network offers the advantages of both technologies, namely increased capacity and ubiquitous coverage. Furthermore, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a very promising candidate technique for the next generation of wireless networks, mainly due to its increased spectrum efficiency compared to orthogonal access schemes. However, the optimal user grouping in NOMA is a combinatorial NP-complete problem, which calls for low complexity techniques. To this end, in this paper, we propose the use of coalitional game theory, where the users served by the same access point (VLC or RF) form a single coalition, while the users can switch through coalitions based on their payoff. A novel utility function is proposed that takes into account the peculiarities of the NOMA hybrid VLC/RF network. Finally, a coalition formation algorithm is presented as well as an efficient power allocation policy. Computer simulations validate the presented analysis and reveal the effectiveness of the proposed user grouping scheme compared to an opportunistic approach.

In this paper, we introduce Deep Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (DCFA) as a means to identify complex nonlinear transformations of two variables for information fusion. DCFA can represent the coupled patterns between two different sets of variables by minimizing the Frobenius norm distance in the transformed domain. Unlike previous kernel methods, DCFA achieves feature mapping through deep networks (DN) instead of the traditional kernel method, allowing for a representation that is not limited by a fixed kernel. DCFA can be considered as a nonlinear extension of the linear Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (CFA) and an alternative to nonparametric method Kernel Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (KCFA) and the recently proposed Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis (Deep CCA) method. The performance of DCFA was evaluated on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset and two audio emotion datasets. Experimental results showed that our proposed solution outperformed KCCA, KCFA, Deep CCA, and the deep learning-based method-Alexnet in terms of accuracy.

In order for robots to be effective in real-world applications, their plans must be flexible and adaptable to different environments, objects, task contexts, and hardware platforms. However, current general-purpose methods are not yet efficient enough for practical use. To address this issue, we propose a new approach that specializes general plans by using specific task data to learn appropriate adaptations from experience. Our system architecture collects data during plan execution to create supervised learning problems and utilizes learned models to continuously adapt the plan. 

To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted experiments with a PR2 robot tasked with fetch and place. By specializing the general plan, the robot was able to perform the task more accurately and efficiently. Our results show that the specialized plan significantly outperformed the original plan.

The sustainable development of ocean engineering has been marked by increased maritime activities in different waters. However, this has also led to a high-level accidental risk of maritime transportation, making it necessary to monitor the maritime traffic more efficiently. To accomplish this objective, a deep understanding of the massive vessel traffic data from different perspectives is essential in practical applications. Advanced data visualization techniques are one such tool that can help gain deep insights into maritime traffic behavior from vast amounts of vessel traffic data.

Data visualization has become a powerful and widely-used tool for the analysis and interpretation of complex big data. It performs well in generating visual presentations of information, making it easier to understand complex data sets. The primary objective of this paper is to provide a brief review for interested researchers regarding the maritime traffic data visualization techniques. Within this brief review, data visualization techniques in the fields of spatio-temporal vessel trajectories and vessel traffic density have been comprehensively surveyed.

Visualization techniques offer significant advantages, and there is a vast potential to utilize these techniques to enhance vessel traffic safety and service reliability in maritime activities. By analyzing vast amounts of vessel traffic data via advanced data visualization techniques, risk levels can be reduced, and efficient maritime traffic management can be established. In conclusion, it is essential to understand the latest visualization techniques and technologies to facilitate efficient and safe maritime operations.

This paper proposes a novel layered belief propagation (BP) detector with a concatenated structure of two different BP layers for low-complexity large multi-user multi-input multi-output (MU-MIMO) detection based on statistical beams. To reduce the computational burden and the circuit scale on the base station (BS) side, the two-stage signal processing consisting of slow varying outer beamformer (OBF) and group-specific MU detection (MUD) for fast channel variations is effective. However, the dimensionality reduction of the equivalent channel based on the OBF results in significant performance degradation in subsequent spatial filtering detection. To compensate for the drawback, the proposed layered BP detector, which is designed for improving the detection capability by suppressing the intra- and inter-group interference in stages, is introduced as the poststage processing of the OBF. Finally, we demonstrate the validity of our proposed method in terms of the bit error rate (BER) performance and the computational complexity.

Data converters are ubiquitous in data-abundant systems, where they are heterogeneously distributed across the analog-digital interface. Unfortunately, conventional data converters trade off speed, power, and accuracy. Furthermore, intrinsic real-time and post-silicon variations dramatically degrade their performance. In this paper, we employ novel neuro-inspired approaches to design smart data converters that could be trained in real-time for general purpose applications, using machine learning algorithms and artificial neural network architectures. Our approach integrates emerging memristor technology with CMOS. This concept will pave the way towards adaptive interfaces with the continuous varying conditions of data driven applications.

Human computer interaction is very wide-ranging and diverse field regarding research and design activity. This interaction between humans and computer systems can be done through various methods. Gesture recognition offers a natural and intuitive way for interaction. It is a natural and effective mean of communication and interaction for hearing-impaired people. Gestural cue is a category of non-verbal communication in which noticeable body actions transfer specific messages. This paper presents a gesture recognition system for the development of a Human Computer Interaction (HCI) using Leap Motion Sensor (LMS). LMS is a device proficient with tracking hand motions or gestures. The objective of this research is development of an HCI system that will convert sign language to text for hearing impaired people. Through hand or body gestures, the disabled can easily convey their message to the caregiver or robot. Sign language has been known for providing natural and intuitive way to interact with computers or machines and robots. We are employing three recognition techniques of Sign Language to Text Conversion (SLTC) to determine the performance of the model. Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Geometric Template Matching and Cross Correlation techniques were employed for static gesture recognition and the best results were acquired from geometric template matching.

During testing, highly compact test patterns are at risk of experiencing IR-drop, which could result in failures or breakdowns. However, due to the lengthy analysis run time, an accurate analysis of all test patterns is not possible. Past methods for predicting IR-drop based on switching activity were imprecise because they relied on an insufficient amount of data from the test set. To address this issue, we present a dynamic IR-drop prediction methodology that considers both resistive and capacitive parasitic elements of the circuit in conjunction with switching activity. Our proposed approach employs machine-learning based clustering and is more precise than the general switching-based method. Furthermore, our methodology is speedy enough to process the complete test set, allowing it to identify vulnerable patterns susceptible to IR-drop failure. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach for an approximate analysis of the complete test set.

In brain-computer interfaces that rely on motor imagery for rehabilitation, the occurrence of false positives can lead to undesired brain plasticity, resulting in incorrect reconstruction of damaged brain tracts. Additionally, clinical use of these interfaces can be hampered by practical difficulties arising from the large number of electroencephalogram (EEG) electrodes required. To mitigate these issues, a novel two-phase classifier based on detecting Mu band event-related desynchronization (ERD) has been proposed. Using only five channels to detect motor imagery and three channels to reject ERD-like noise or non-motor signals, this algorithm effectively reduces the rate of false positives with a small number of EEG channels. A two-day experiment conducted with four healthy subjects evaluated the performance of the proposed algorithm, with a total sensitivity of 60.83% and total selectivity of 78.49%. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method to improve the clinical utility of brain-computer interfaces for rehabilitation.

In this paper, we propose a simplified and efficient quantum neural network that employs only O(n log_2k) qubits and O(nk) quantum gates. The proposed network consists of N input parameters and k weights applied to these parameters. We describe the network in terms of a quantum circuit and illustrate its equivalent classical neural net which involves O(k^n) nodes in the hidden layer.

The network utilizes a periodic activation function of cosine values of the linear combinations of the inputs and weights. We describe the backpropagation through gradient descent and validate the performance of the proposed network using iris and breast cancer datasets in simulations.

Our numerical results suggest that the proposed network can be effectively used in machine learning problems and offers an exponential speedup over the same structured classical neural net. Overall, our work offers a promising alternative approach to quantum machine learning and opens up new avenues for quantum computing research.

Data explosion and higher service level agreements (SLA) are common terminologies in modern communication networks. Recent advancements toward 5G networks add to the complexity where billions of devices, both static and mobile, are connected generating trillions of megabits of data flooding the network and where service providers scuffle daily to deliver key performance indicators: Lower latency, longer battery life, higher data rates, ultra-high reliability, and more connected devices. The optical-fiber world simultaneously witnesses a denser, fiber-rich network infrastructure which is critically challenged in fast economically developing countries by heavy construction of roads and other infrastructures that inflict repeated and unpredictable cuts to the extent that traffic is simultaneously interrupted in up to 10% of the optical links. Thus, network resiliency to fiber failures is already and will continue to be a top priority for operators. Depending on the SLA, operators choose from various resiliency options, e.g., at single network layers or across multiple ones, with dedicated protection or shared restoration, depending on decisive factors like network availability and total cost of ownership (TCO). With traditional network architectures, high resiliency comes with significantly increased TCO involving optical transport network (OTN) switches, L1 protection switching, and L1 restoration. This translates into high CAPEX and excessive space and power consumption, hampering the desirable seamless scalability with the continuously increasing demand for more capacity. This paper explores an alternative hyperscale network architecture, which is adaptable and resilient to multiple fiber failures, thus delivering committed service levels to the end users and which, at the same time, significantly reduces network cost compared to a traditional all OTN-switched network. The hyperscale architecture exploits low footprint carrier grade, data center interconnect type high-density transponders and cost-effective optical protection switching and restoration via software defined networking control. The paper also describes a routing and grooming algorithm to dimension a shared resource pool for optical restoration and a statistical simulation method for time effective execution, simulating failures over a carefully selected sub-set of failure scenarios to guarantee a high degree of network availability. Via network simulation, the paper demonstrates that multiple failure resiliency and cost effectiveness do not necessarily represent a contradiction in transport networks as long as an appropriate network architecture is chosen and that efficient network planning and optimization are applied.

In recent years, oil spills have been frequent and marine pollution has become increasingly serious. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites can effectively track the oil slicks expansion caused by the oil spill. The mRMR_SVM algorithm is used to identify oil spills in SAR images and the recognition results provide important preconditions for oil spill accident decision support. First, the algorithm of minimum redundancy and maximum relevance (mRMR) is applied to select the optimal eigenvector set, and the input values are reduced. Then the SVM algorithm is used to solve the oil spill image classification problem, and RBF is selected as the kernel function. Train the model using training sets and adjust the model parameters. The trained model is used to identify oil spills with the test set eigenvector as an input. The experimental results show that mRMR_SVM model are effective for the identification of "oil slicks" and "look-alikes oil slicks" image, and the accuracy rate is 96.875%.

Telecommunications are a crucial element of smart grid technologies. Utility communication systems need to combine cost effectiveness with the need for high reliability. Due to its wide geographic coverage, satellite communication can be an appropriate alternative for power system automation in order to reach remote substations. This paper presents the experimental testing of Broadband Global Area Networks (BGAN) M2M technology between the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system running a primary front end processor (FEP) and the reclosers. Hardware test results for a number of different scenarios are discussed, compared and validated. The challenges for keeping the polls reliability at highest levels are also discussed.

This paper presents an innovative macromodeling technique that enables the efficient simulation of complex arrays of scatterers. The proposed approach uses a macromodel to represent each array element consisting of an equivalent electric current density applied on a fictitious surface surrounding the element, alongside a set of linear discrete operators. The use of this approach leads to a better conditioned linear system, lower memory consumption and faster computations when compared to the standard surface integral equation formulations.

The concept of mobile edge computing (MEC) and device-to-device (D2D) communications has been developed to enable high-performance mobile computing and data communications. In this paper, we have proposed the integration of both techniques to form the D2D-MEC technique, which aims to further enhance the computation capacity of cellular networks. Our objective is to maximize the number of supported devices by formulating a mixed integer non-linear problem. To solve this problem, we have decoupled it into two subproblems, and our analysis has shown that the optimal solutions to the subproblems combine to form the optimal solution to the original problem.

The first subproblem focuses on minimizing the required edge computation resource for a given D2D pair, while the second subproblem maximizes the number of supported devices via optimal D2D pairing. By solving the two subproblems, we have developed an optimal algorithm, and we have highlighted some insightful results. Our numerical results show that combining D2D communications with MEC can significantly improve the computation capacity of the system.

In summary, our proposed D2D-MEC technique provides a novel approach for enhancing the computation capacity of cellular networks. Through the integration of D2D communications and MEC, we aim to maximize the number of supported devices and develop an efficient algorithm for solving the mixed integer non-linear problem. Our results indicate that this technique can significantly improve the performance of the system, emphasizing the importance of the integration of advanced techniques for enhancing mobile communication and computing.

As the era of the Internet of Things (IoT) arrives, the colossal volume of data generated has far exceeded what conventional computer systems can handle and process. As a result, cloud computing has shown its promising future for storing and handling the enormous amount of data. The data availability is one of the most critical issues related to data management. Losing data, in particular for those important, could cause unrecoverable damage in many cases. Most cloud platforms maintain multiple copies of data to lower the risk of losing data from hardware failure or natural disasters. Hadoop is one of the most popular cloud platforms in the cloud community. Its default file system, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), keeps multiple copies for every file. Moreover, HDFS provides users a snapshot function to make point-in-time copies of files in the file system for system recovery in the future. Usually files in snapshots are considered crucial to users, otherwise users would not even bother to keep them in snapshots. Ideally, important data files should have more replicas to increase their availability during the occurrence of hardware failure or disasters. However, the current snapshot scheme only records the contents of files at various snapshot moments and it does not affect their numbers of replicas kept in HDFS. It would be desirable if files in snapshots could have more copies so their data availability can be enhanced accordingly. Unfortunately, HDFS cannot achieve this in an efficient way. We improved and modified HDFS to automatically increase the numbers of replicas for files in snapshots. Consequently, the data availability of important files involved in snapshots can be bettered. The experimental results show that our design and implementation noticeably outperforms what the current HDFS can do in the course of taking snapshots and increasing the number of replicas for files in snapshots.

In this paper, we study a class of nonautonomous recurrent neural networks (NRNNs) with time-varying delays on time scales. We consider both bounded and unbounded delays and present some stabilization results for these networks.

To accomplish this, we construct a new generalized Halanay inequality on time scales using time-scale theory and analytical techniques. This inequality serves as the foundation for our stabilization results for NRNNs with bounded delays. We also apply these results to a class of drive-response NRNNs to synchronize them.

Additionally, we investigate the stabilization of NRNNs with unbounded delays. We successfully obtain stabilization criteria for NRNNs with proportional delays without any variable transformation. Our generalized Halanay inequality on time scales extends the results in existing literature and covers continuous-time and discrete-time NRNNs as well as systems that involve time intervals.

Finally, we showcase the validity of our results using some examples and propose an application to image encryption and decryption.

This paper presents the control design for the two-phase Stefan problem using a single boundary heat input. The two-phase Stefan problem is a model for describing the liquid-solid phase transition, where the temperature profile evolves over time and is separated by domains of liquid and solid phases with a moving interface position. The mathematical formulation includes two diffusion partial differential equations and an ordinary differential equation driven by Neumann boundary values of both PDE states, resulting in a nonlinear coupled system. 

To extend our previous work on the one-phase Stefan problem, we propose a state feedback control law using the backstepping method to stabilize the interface position to a desired setpoint. We prove that the closed-loop system under the control law ensures conditions for model validity, and global exponential stability is estimated in L2 norm. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control law.

Sound source separation (SSS) using a microphone array is an effective method in various scenarios, particularly in recording target speech in noisy environments. We previously presented an SSS system using a differential-type array and time-delay neural network (NN), which prevented target speech distortion due to the nonlinear property of the NN. However, this system only worked for narrowband signals. To overcome this limitation, we propose a new SSS system that extends the previous model in two main areas. First, we utilize sound pressure distribution images as input to the NN, which are formed based on the microphone outputs. Second, we increase the number of layers in the NN. Our computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed system achieves higher SSS performance than conventional arrays, including our previous model.

Recently, end-to-end (E2E) neural text-to-speech systems, such as Tacotron2, have begun to surpass the traditional multi-stage hand-engineered systems, with both simplified system building pipelines and high-quality speech. With a unique encoder-decoder neural structure, the Tacotron2 system no longer needs separately learned text analysis front-end, duration model, acoustic model, and audio synthesis module. The key of such a system lies in the attention mechanism, which learns an alignment between the encoder and the decoder, serving as an implicit duration model bridging the text sequence and the acoustic sequence. However, attention learning suffers from low training efficiency and model instability problems, which hinder the E2E approaches from wide deployment. In this paper, we address the problems and propose a novel pre-alignment guided attention learning approach. Specifically, we inject handy prior knowledge-accurate phoneme durations-in the neural network loss function to bias the attention learning to the desired direction more accurately. The explicit time alignment between an audio recording and its corresponding phoneme sequence can be achieved by forced-alignment from an automatic speech recognizer (ASR). The experiments show that the proposed pre-alignment guided (PAG) attention approach can significantly improve training efficiency and model stability. More specifically, the PAG updated version of Tacotron2 can quickly obtain the attention alignment using only 500 (text, audio) pairs, which is apparently not possible for the original Tacotron2. A series of subjective experiments also show that the PAG-Tacotron2 approach can synthesize more stable and natural speech.

This paper focuses on addressing the issue of bipartite output consensus of heterogeneous multi-agent systems over signed graphs. To achieve this, the authors propose a dynamical neighbor-based consensus protocol that comprises of a solution pair of a regulation equation and a homogenous compensator. The controller parameters are derived using Lyapunov stability theory and matrix theory. 

To enable agents to reach bipartite output consensus without utilizing any global information, a fully distributed adaptive protocol is also designed. Overall, the proposed protocol offers an efficient approach to bipartite output consensus for heterogeneous multi-agent systems, making it a promising solution for various applications.

Continuous memory technology scaling causes memory cells to be vulnerable to wearout. To ensure reliable operations of circuits and systems in the presence of wearout, we require accurate estimation of the lifetime of circuits and systems degraded by wearout. Since the conventional method of estimating circuit and system reliability degradation based on device-level accelerated life test (ALT) does not account for the tolerance of a circuit and a system to a wearout failure of a device, accelerated lifetime testing at the circuit and system level is necessary. For accurate estimation of system reliability using system-level ALT, we propose a method that optimizes the design of experiments for ALT. From significant observations from failure data statistics of system-level ALT with various stress conditions applied to the memory system of the Leon3 as a case study, we define acceptability regions for memory testing of each wearout mechanism. In addition, by analyzing errors in estimating Weibull parameters from system-level ALT, we develop a methodology that optimizes experimental designs in acceptability regions of each wearout mechanism to minimize such estimation errors in system-level ALT.

The uncontrollable weather conditions can cause a serious problem to remote sensing imaginary. One of the weather conditions is a resulting from cloud contamination. As a result, this paper proposed the use of the convolutional autoencoder neural networks to remove clouds from cloud-contaminated images by training on a multi-temporal remote sensing dataset. Here, the observations from different spectral bands are assumed to be independent since their spectral responses are usually nonoverlapped. From this assumption, each convolutional autoencoder neural networks are trained with the observation from only one spectral band. In our method, we have three convolutional autoencoder neural networks for red, green and blue spectral bands. The experiments were conducted on both synthesis and real dataset derived from the actual LANDSAT 8 images from the central part of Thailand where our algorithm has shown to have a superb performance.

One of the main challenges of supporting massive machine-type-communications (MTCs) by future mobile networks, is the radio access network (RAN) congestion. A viable solution is a hierarchical architecture where cluster-grouped machines are indirectly connected to the mobile network through a cluster gateway. This paper considers such an architecture and focuses on radio resource allocation to machine-clusters where resources can be spatially reused for concurrent transmissions. In particular, resources can be accessed simultaneously by machines of different clusters and by different communication phases, thus resulting in an interference-limited system. Three different resource partitioning schemes are proposed and evaluated, mainly differing on how interference is taken into account. The aim is to minimize the packet loss probability, and thus maximizing the spectral efficiency. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed schemes in comparison to benchmark methods. In particular, by joining resource reuse and interference-mitigation, the efficiency improves significantly.

Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks (IWSNs) have become increasingly popular in various industrial applications due to their ability to boost efficiency while reducing costs. However, many of today's industrial fields require collaboration between both static and mobile nodes to optimize performance. Unfortunately, current industrial wireless standards typically only account for static nodes, meaning that their performance is noticeably lacking in environments involving mobile nodes. Specifically, mobile nodes' movement can cause changes in the network that often result in the disconnection of related paths, leading to substantial data and command loss. This critical problem can disrupt industrial environments that demand high-reliability and high-accuracy. 

To address this issue, we propose constructing routing graphs to minimize network changes caused by mobile nodes. The method involves constructing a skeleton graph consisting of static nodes, to which mobile nodes are grafted. This approach reduces the number of disconnected paths and minimizes the impact of network changes on mobile nodes. Additionally, the method can easily adapt to various standards that utilize graphs for routing. We applied this proposed method to the WirelessHART standard and confirmed its effectiveness through simulation results. Overall, we conclude that our approach significantly reduces the damage caused by network changes for mobile nodes when compared to the current WirelessHART standard.

Dynamic graph link prediction has attracted increasing attention in various fields such as social networks, paper citation networks and knowledge graphs. Many models have been developed to predict the future graph structure. In this paper, we propose a link prediction model with semantic evolution (LISE), to predict links in a sequence of graph over time. Our approach is based on the discovery of non-random initialization dynamic word embedding which is a kind of method to study semantic evolution. It can help us train node embedding in the same space and introduce temporal context into the embedding training of nodes. Based on node embedding in the same space, LISE can unify historical behavior, graph snapshots structure information and dynamic attributes into a frame. We evaluate our proposed method and various comparing methods on two real-world datasets. The experimental results prove the effectiveness of the link prediction made by LISE model.

Imitation learning has gained huge popularity due to its promises in different fields such as robotics and autonomous systems. A great deal of past research work in the field of imitation learning has been devoted to developing efficient and effective policies using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The performance of CNN-based control policies intimately depends on the network architecture. Determination of the optimal architecture for CNNs is still a hot research topic for the deep learning community. This study comprehensively investigates and quantifies the impact of CNN architecture on the performance of learned policy for an autonomous vehicle. CNN models with different architectures (number of layers and filters) are fed by visual information from multiple cameras obtained from multiple driving simulations. These networks are trained to precisely find the mapping between visual information and the steering angle. Two ensemble approaches are also introduced to further improve the overall accuracy of steering angle estimations. Obtained results indicate that deeper networks show a better performance than less deep networks during autonomous driving. Also it is observed that best results are achieved by ensemble approaches.

Identifying the research areas of academics is a challenging task that requires the use of supervised machine learning techniques. However, obtaining labeled data can be time-consuming and costly. Therefore, in this paper, we suggest using clique percolation, an algorithm that detects overlapping communities, to identify the research areas of academics.

To collect our data, we created a framework that gathers information from digital libraries and selected university websites in Pakistan. We then utilized clique percolation to identify researchers working in multiple research areas.

Our analyses of the results show that clique percolation is an effective method for identifying the research areas of academics. This technique can be used to find out relevant research areas, increase collaboration opportunities between researchers, and form research groups that work together to solve complex problems.

Overall, the proposed approach can eliminate the need for labeled data and provide a more efficient method for identifying the research areas of academics.

Diagnosis of lung pathologies from chest X-rays (CXRs) is a crucial task for modern image-based diagnosis. Recent developments in deep learning-based clinical decision making have significantly improved the automation of lung pathology diagnosis. These deep learning solutions have shown a tendency to enhance with the increasing number of training X-rays, which can be artificially augmented to improve the performance of the models. However, current augmentation approaches are commonly applied to the available training data without determining the actual value of individual augmentation. Our study aims to address this gap in computerized lung pathology diagnosis by evaluating the contribution of various data augmentation approaches using the publicly available ChestX-ray14 dataset.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the use of biological signals as a tool for human interface. One such signal, Electromyogram (EMG), has found a wide range of applications, particularly in the measurement of muscular volume in the arms and shoulders. However, the use of wet type sensors have proved to be expensive and inconvenient.

In contrast, the use of dry type sensors attached to the wrist has yielded good results in hand motion recognition and personal authentication. However, there has been no previous method to establish both at the same time. In this paper, we propose a method to carry out hand motion recognition and personal authentication simultaneously by measuring EMG with dry type sensors attached to the wrist.

Conventional methods for hand motion recognition have mainly used EMG from the movement Japanese Janken, with an average accuracy of 92.9%. On the other hand, personal authentication has relied solely on the "paper" of Japanese Janken, with an average accuracy of 96.7%. For learning and identification, we utilized a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN).

We then applied a multi-input and multi-output model of CNN, and our proposed method achieved an average accuracy of 94.5% for hand motion recognition and an average accuracy of 94.57% for personal authentication. Our results show the potential for using dry type sensors attached to the wrist for both hand motion recognition and personal authentication simultaneously.

This article proposes a new camera calibration method using the image of an absolute quadratic curve (IAC). Additionally, a new target is designed to facilitate this method. The process involves identifying characteristic points and lines on the target, finding the vanishing point and line, correcting the image distortion, and calculating the internal and external parameters of the camera. Nonlinear optimization using the reprojection method is used to obtain optimal results. The fundamental matrix is then employed to determine the relative position between different target images. The normalization method is used to improve the accuracy of data processing. This method has wide-ranging applications and does not require any prior knowledge of the camera.

Discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) methods using explicit time integration schemes often suffer from unreasonably small time-step size when applied to simulations involving electrically small structures. In this paper, an exponential time integration (ETI) scheme based on Krylov subspace is proposed for DGTD. The proposed scheme is unconditionally stable and exhibits good accuracy for large time-step sizes. When compared with classic ETI schemes, in the proposed scheme, the dense matrix exponentials are absorbed in matrix–vector products, hence the prohibitive memory costs are avoided. Moreover, a preconditioner combining the shift-and-invert technique and restricted additive Schwarz method is also developed to accelerate the proposed scheme.

Spell Checker is an important part of language specific text processing applications. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid approach for spell checker for Punjabi language. Available spell checkers use traditional method for error detection such as dictionary lookup technique and minimum edit distance for error correction. The proposed spell checker aims to improve performance as well accuracy. In this paper, we present the use of trie data structure to store Punjabi words dictionary and then use tree based algorithm along with n-gram analysis to detect misspelled words. To correct misspelled words, best possible suggestion is listed using Long-short term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network along with rule based approach and minimum edit distance. Error detection using trie-based dictionary improves the performance and Error correction using LSTM improves the accuracy of proposed spell checker. In addition to error detection techniques and error correction techniques, proposed spell checker uses handcrafted rules, language syntax rules and rules regarding tokenization.

Automated object identification in aerospace images is crucial for efficient decision-making in various industries. However, accuracy of image segmentation remains a primary challenge in object-oriented image analysis. To address this issue, this paper presents several techniques that aim to enhance color segmentation in images. This includes partitioning the image into frames and merging adjacent color areas, splitting relatively narrow areas, and adaptively approximating color area edges. Experimental results indicated that the proposed techniques significantly improved object identification efficiency based on shape features. This study utilized high-quality aerial images from a publicly available dataset to provide evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

The performance evaluation of primary frequency regulation (PFR) of generator is helpful to improve the frequency stability of power grids. Existing research cannot comprehensively and accurately evaluate the PFR performance of generators, and the research methods have the disadvantage of poor adaptability. Based on the simulation model of PFR of generator, this method takes vertiginous rate, regulation limit, dead zone and response delay time of the PFR as model key parameters. The improved genetic algorithm is used to find the model parameters which have the smallest error comparing with the generator actual output. Those parameters are used as the evaluation index of the PFR performance of the generator. Thus the method can more comprehensively and accurately evaluate the performance indexes of the generator primary frequency regulation. Finally, based on the measured data of the primary frequency regulation of the generator in Northwest Power Grid, the response output of the primary frequency regulation model and identified parameters are compared with the actual output, the validity and accuracy of the evaluation method are verified.

Multidisciplinary design optimization techniques become more and more applied in the field of aerodynamics due to the rapid development of computers high-performance, numerical methods and optimization algorithms. These techniques coupled with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), which aims to incorporate mathematical relations and algorithms to analyze and solve fluid flow problems, involve the use of those numerical methods and algorithms to improve the fluid flow solutions. CFD analysis of an airfoil determines its ability by producing results such as lift and drag forces, and the application of an optimization algorithm involves improving the shape of this airfoil in order to manipulate the lift and drag coefficients according to the requirements. In this work, a numerical investigation, using ANSYS/Fluent, of two-dimensional transonic flow over a NACA 0012 airfoil was conducted at various Mach numbers and compared with the provided experimental data. The flow to be considered is compressible and turbulent and the solver used is the density based implicit solver, which gives good results for high speed compressible flows. Then a shape optimization algorithm, based on a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm, was used in order to obtain an improved performance control of the aerodynamic coefficients of the optimized airfoil.

Li-ion batteries are a critical component in the consumer electronics, hybrid electric vehicle, and distributed energy storage industries. The reliability of battery-powered systems depends on accurate estimation of the state of charge (SOC) and remaining useful life (RUL) of the battery. However, most commercial battery applications currently available do not monitor the RUL, which can negatively impact system performance. 

To address this gap, this paper proposes a method to estimate the RUL of a Lithium cobalt oxide battery accurately. To validate the RUL estimation method, a mathematical model of a single cell Li-Ion battery was developed in the Matlab/Simulink platform. Aging parameters such as charge/discharge rate and operating temperature were incorporated into the model. 

Stress factors such as operating temperature and storage time were applied to the battery, and the proposed RUL estimation method was verified. Results indicate that the proposed method was effective in accurately estimating the RUL of the battery. This is a significant development in the field of battery-powered systems, as it will enable more efficient and effective performance of lithium cobalt oxide batteries in various applications, ultimately improving overall system performance and reliability.

In many fields, such as reinforcement learning, discounted costs are often considered when determining optimal inputs for finite horizons. However, the related literature tends to focus on optimality and lacks attention on stability. To address this, we examine the stability of general nonlinear discrete-time systems that are controlled by an optimal sequence of inputs that minimize a finite-horizon discounted cost. This is computed using a receding horizon strategy.

Assumptions are made regarding the stabilizability of the system and its detectability with respect to the stage cost. We then construct a Lyapunov function for the closed-loop system with the receding horizon controller. This ensures a uniform semiglobal stability property, where the discount factor and horizon length are adjustable parameters. By strengthening the initial assumptions, we guarantee uniform global exponential stability, and we provide explicit bounds for the discount factor and horizon length. 

We compare our results to related literature, specifically in the cases where there is no discount or the horizon is infinite. Our bounds improve upon existing ones in these cases.

In this paper, we present the design and implementation of our latest OpenVLC1.3 platform to perform research in Visible Light Communication Systems. We retain the advantages of the previous versions such as TCP/IP layers support, software programmability and low-cost front-end. We re-design the transceiver to support higher modulation rates and sensitivity. This allows us to reach a throughput of 400 kb/s (a factor of 4 with respect to the previous version) and increase the distance by a factor of 3.5. We further improve the software robustness of the system and reduce the form factor at similar hardware cost.

Having the right skill sets, knowledge, and a proactive attitude are all essential in contributing to society and succeeding in the labor market. However, this can be a significant challenge, especially when faced with gender disadvantages. This is particularly true for young women who have not completed compulsory education or entered the workforce, requiring special initiatives and guidance.

To address this issue, an engineering solution has been developed in the form of a multimodal profiling tool. This online, automated employability profiling tool aims to identify the user's existing skills, competences, attitudes, and experiences and match them against identified digital job profiles.

The tool combines the user's age, personal goals, and formal education to place them in an employment matrix. A digital employability pathway is then defined, outlining the individual training needs, experiences, and work requirements needed to achieve objectives.

With this tool, young women and other individuals facing gender disadvantages can access the necessary resources and guidance to successfully enter and progress in the labor market.

Fog computing extends Cloud Computing to the edge of the network, enabling computation, storage, applications, and network services between the Internet of Things and cloud servers. However, security must be a priority in Fog computing because of the huge number of nodes involved. Therefore, we propose a new cryptographic primitive called CCA2 secure publicly-verifiable revocable large-universe multi-authority attribute-based encryption (CCA2-PV-R-LU-MA-ABE) for fine-grained access control in Fog computing. 

In this primitive, end nodes generate private keys from multiple authorities differentiated by geographical locations or functions. These nodes' attributes can be denoted by any strings in the large universe, fulfilling diverse needs in practical Fog applications. Also, accessibility to nodes can be efficiently revoked even by resource-limited devices. The primitive's validity is ensured by supporting public verification, meaning that only valid ciphertext can be stored or transmitted. 

We construct a concrete CCA2-PV-R-LU-MA-ABE scheme based on the primitive and the feature of Fog computing. We also define the security model of this primitive, which is much more secure than the CPA-secure scheme. Finally, we compare the efficiency of the proposed concrete scheme with that of the existing CPA-secure scheme through theoretical and experimental analysis, and the results show that the extra efficiency consumption in improving CPA to CCA2 is low. The proposed scheme is secure, flexible, and efficient enough to be practical in Fog computing.

This paper presents a proposed hardware implementation of the Izhikevich model, one of the most widely-used spiking neuron models.
