The network consists of two major components: 1) a learned AMP (LAMP) network, which takes advantage of the sparsity of beamspace channel matrix to generate a preliminary estimation, and 2) a deep residual learning network (ResNet), which minimizes the impact of channel noise and enhances the coarse estimation derived from the LAMP network. We have carried out simulations that confirm the effectiveness of LampResNet.

In this note, we propose a novel event-triggered adaptive control scheme for a class of nonlinear systems that have unknown control direction and unknown sensor faults. We introduce auxiliary filters and a bound estimation approach to compress the effects of the network-induced error and sensor faults. This method helps us to address the challenges associated with unknown control direction and Zeno phenomenon.

Our proposed scheme employs differentiable auxiliary functions and high-order Lyapunov functions to avoid the Zeno phenomenon and ensure that all closed-loop signals are globally uniformly bounded. We also demonstrate that the tracking error converges to a residual set. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, we present simulation results that show its robustness and stability in the face of network-induced error and sensor faults.

In summary, the novel event-triggered adaptive control scheme that we propose in this paper is effective in addressing the challenges of unknown control direction and sensor faults. The proposed method is robust and stable, as demonstrated by the simulation results, and represents a significant contribution to the field of nonlinear control systems.

Wireless energy transfer can extend the lifetime of wireless sensor networks deployed in hard-to-reach and/or harsh environments. A number of works have proposed using dedicated mobile chargers (e.g., robots, drones, or vehicles) to transmit Radio Frequency (RF) energy to sensor nodes, which, despite optimal route selection, remains an expensive approach. In this article, we consider a scenario where sensor nodes could be recharged by passing vehicles. This could be the case of a wireless sensor network deployed to monitor the health of a bridge or a dam. We provide exact mathematical modeling of the harvested energy from a moving vehicle over T seconds and over a trip time. This model captures the effect of the vehicle's speed and location. Then, we extend the discussion to the case of multiple vehicles and propose a multi vehicle harvesting protocol. This protocol allows the sensor node to maximize its energy intake by proactively selecting the source vehicle. This work paves the ground for accurate designs of energy harvesting protocols that leverage surrounding sources of RF energy. The accuracy of the derived results is verified using computer simulations.

In the mobile edge computing (MEC) network, devices can offload their applications to a MEC server via a wireless link and process them using computation resources to meet computational and latency requirements. This creates a two-stage tandem queue in the MEC network consisting of a transmission queue and a computation processing queue. However, the fluctuating wireless channel environment leads to variability in the service in the transmission queue and random task arrivals in the computation processing queue, making it difficult to guarantee quality of service (QoS). 

This paper derives the effective capacity of MEC with the two-stage tandem queue and formulates a joint bandwidth and computation resource allocation problem that maximizes network revenue, while ensuring statistical QoS guarantees. The problem is shown to be NP-hard by reducing it to the two-dimensional knapsack problem. An efficient algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is proposed to reduce computation complexity, decomposing the problem into convex subproblems. 

Simulation results show the relationship between required bandwidth and computation resource in relation to supported arrival rate and end-to-end delay. The proposed scheme offers superior performance to other schemes.

Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) have emerged as a key area of research, standardization, and development, with the potential to provide more efficient and secure roads by enabling vehicles to communicate with one another, sharing information about traffic and road conditions.

To ensure urgent safety messages are delivered regardless of the buffer status, this paper proposes a set of Markovian chain models that control the rate of beacon messages in the control channel (CCH) according to 802.11 EDCA back off analysis. Specifically, we present three Markov methods. Firstly, we aim to minimize the drop and delay of urgent messages by controlling the beacon message rate according to the buffer state. The second method involves modifying the contention window size with respect to the buffer threshold, resulting in the ability to compute the transmission probability of Access Category (AC). The third method takes into account the probability of collision of AC.

Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed Markov models outperform the original IEEE 802.11p in terms of packet delivery ratio and throughput. Overall, this research provides an innovative and effective approach for ensuring the delivery of urgent safety messages in VANETs by utilizing Markovian chain models.

In recent years, wireless sensor networks have been extensively deployed to collect various data. Due to the effect of harsh environments and the limitation of the computing and communication capabilities of sensor nodes, the quality and reliability of sensor data are affected by outliers. Thus, an effective outlier detection method is essential. The existing outlier detection methods have some drawbacks, such as extra resource consumption introduced by the size growth of a local detector, poor performance of combination methods of local detectors, and the weak adaptability of the dynamic changes of the environment, etc. We propose an isolation-based distributed outlier detection framework using nearest-neighbor ensembles (iNNE) to effectively detect outliers in wireless sensor networks. In our proposed framework, local detectors are constructed in each node by the iNNE algorithm. A new combination method taking advantage of the spatial correlation among sensor nodes for local detectors is presented. The method is based on the weighted voting idea. In addition, we introduce a sliding window to update local detectors, which enables the adaption of dynamic changes in the environment. The extensive experiments are conducted on two classic real sensor datasets. The experimental results show our framework significantly improves the detection accuracy and reduces the false alarm rate compared with other outlier detection frameworks.

FPGAs have made their way into the cloud, allowing users to gain remote access to the state-of-the-art reconfigurable fabric and implement their custom accelerators. Since FPGAs are large enough to accommodate multiple independent designs, the multi-tenant user scenario may soon be prevalent in cloud computing environments. However, shared use of an FPGA raises security concerns. Recently discovered hardware Trojans for use in multi-tenant FPGA settings target denial-of-service attacks, power side-channel attacks, and crosstalk side-channel attacks. In this work, we present an attack method for causing timing-constraints violation in the multi-tenant FPGA setting. This type of attack is very dangerous as the consequences of timing faults are temporary errors, which are often impossible to notice. We demonstrate the attack on a set of self-timed true random number generators (STRNGs), frequently used in cryptographic applications. When the attack is launched, the STRNG outputs become biased and fail randomness tests. However, after the attack, STRNGs recover and continue generating random bits.

The exponential growth of data on the World Wide Web (WWW) has resulted in a significant challenge for data organization and data usability in real-life scenarios. The WWW has become an integral part of our daily life, utilized frequently through various web-based applications to connect with others. This study puts forward a new similarity measurement technique that enhances document retrieval from the repository and therefore, improves the effectiveness of the Web Information Retrieval (WIR) system. Using bio-inspired PSO methodology, top-ranked documents are retrieved in a shorter response time, thereby optimizing the WIR process and increasing the system's efficiency. Additionally, we present a comparative study of the proposed system against the existing method, with experiments conducted on CACM collections. By achieving better precision-recall rates than the existing system, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

To address the issues of rapid network energy exhaustion and unreliable links in the Internet of Things (IoT), this paper proposes the use of mobile intelligent computing based on compressive sensing data gathering (MIC-CSDG) algorithm. This technique enhances the accuracy of data reconstruction. The proposed research focuses on four main components. Firstly, using mobile intelligent computing, the method derives the multi-hop function among sensor nodes and determines a proportional relationship between them. Secondly, the observation matrix is designed based on sparse matrix which has low correlation to mitigate the effect of data packet loss on the entire IoT system to achieve higher data reconstruction accuracy for the sink node. Thirdly, data forwarding strategy that includes an acknowledgement mechanism is utilized to improve the reliability of the data transmission among clusters. Lastly, efficient data handover is achieved for the multi-path routing data among various nodes. 

The simulation results show that the MIC-CSDG algorithm exhibits a data reconstruction error of less than 5%, even if the packet loss rate is as high as 40%. In comparison with other existing algorithms, the proposed method reduces the average network energy consumption by 23.59% and decreases the data forwarding time by 16.36%. This affirms the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

This paper addresses the learning problem for data-adaptive transform that provides sparse representation in a space with dimensions larger than (or equal to)the dimensions of the original space. We present an iterative, alternating algorithm that has two steps: (i)transform update and (ii)sparse coding. In the transform update step, we focus on novel problem formulation based on a lower bound of the objective that addresses a trade-off between (a) how much are aligned the gradients of the approximative objective and the original objective, and (b)how much the lower bound is close to the original objective. This allows us not only to propose approximate closed form solution but also gives the possibility to find an update that can lead to accelerated local convergence and enables us to estimate an update that can lead to a satisfactory solution under a small amount of data. Since in the transform update, the approximate closed form solution preserves the gradient and in the sparse coding step, we use exact closed form solution, the resulting algorithm is convergent. On the practical side, we evaluate on image denoising application and demonstrate promising denoising performance together with advantages in training data requirements, accelerated local convergence and the resulting computational complexity.

Today's software complexity makes developing defect-free software almost impossible. Consequently, developing classifiers to classify software modules into defective and non-defective before software releases have attracted great interest in academia and software industry alike. Although many classifiers have been proposed, no one has been proven superior over others. The major reason is that while a research shows that classifier A is better than classifier B, we can find other research that shows the opposite. These conflicts are usually triggered when researchers report results using their preferable performance evaluation measures such as, recall and precision. Although this approach is valid, it does not examine all possible facets of classifiers performance characteristics. Thus, the performance evaluation might improve or deteriorate if researchers choose other performance measures. As a result, software developers usually struggle to select the most suitable classifier to use in their projects. The goal of this paper is to apply the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP) as a popular multicriteria decision-making technique to reliably evaluate classifiers' performance. This evaluation framework incorporates a wider spectrum of performance measures to evaluate classifiers performance rather than relying on selected preferable measures. The results show that this approach will increase software developers' confidence in research outcomes and help them in avoiding false conclusions and infer reasonable boundaries for them. We exploited 22 popular performance measures and 11 software defect classifiers. The analysis was carried out using KNIME data mining platform and 12 software defect data sets provided by the NASA metrics data program (MDP) repository.

This paper handles the problems of identification and equalization. To recognize the impulse response for frequency radio, we focus on positive kernel algorithm and we proceed to the equalization MC-CDMA systems. In this paper, we employ a broadband radio access network channels (BRAN A and BRAN E) standardized by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) and Proakis channels (channels A, B and C). Through theoretical analysis and the experimental simulation, it shows the appropriateness of the kernel algorithm using different SNR. To indicate the robustness of the algorithm, we have done a comparison with the RLS method. In the equalization part, we used the Zero Forcing algorithm (ZF) and Minimum Mean Square Error Algorithm (MMSE). Simulations results show that the proposed algorithm is efficient and effective for practical channels.

Water is a scarce resource, which needs to be managed optimally. A reservoir is a key water storage source in water management, where they are utilized by various sectors for different purposes. Therefore, there is an essential need in taking the best decision in releasing water from reservoirs not only to manage water as a resource, but also to mitigate floods, which has been one of the most expensive natural disasters causing an increased impact on human causalities and property damage. Research on predicting the future water height of reservoirs, when the reservoir receives a significant amount of rainfall and the water inflow is uncertain due to human intervention, are very limited. Hence, this research proposes a prediction model to forecast the future water height of a reservoir, when the reservoir receives a significant amount of rainfall and the water inflow is uncertain. It presents the effectiveness of applying K-Medoids clustering on top of regression model in predicting the future water height on next three days, while identifying the most effective set of features of the model.

Word sense disambiguation (WSD) is a problem that has been heavily researched in the field of computational linguistics. Different approaches have been used to tackle this problem, with supervised models often achieving high accuracy. However, knowledge-based solutions that use human annotators and engineered features remain more flexible and effective. This work aims to bridge this gap by using neural sequence models with an attention mechanism. 

The main focus of this work is to combine multiple attentions on different linguistic features, providing a unified framework. The weighted attention enables the model to easily disambiguate an ambiguous word by attending to a suitable portion of a sentence. Our experiments show that this weighted multiple attention approach leads to a more versatile encoder-decoder model, resulting in state-of-the-art results.

Skin lesions are a type of illness that are often detected and diagnosed through dermoscopy imaging. Accurate segmentation of lesion regions is a critical step in skin lesion analysis. However, the varying viewpoints and scales of lesion regions can make segmentation a challenging task. To address this issue, we propose an effective skin lesion segmentation architecture based on a modified generative adversarial network. Our network can learn great feature representation of dermoscopic images in an unsupervised way, and supervised learning can make it even more promising. Our encoder-decoder network concatenates residual blocks and atrous convolution as the generator to generate segmentation masks. This generator can obtain deep representation and preserve fine-grained information. We also apply two discriminators to enhance reliability of the discrimination and distinguish generated masks from ground truth jointly. We train and evaluate our model using the ISIC skin lesion challenge datasets from 2017. Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed network achieves favorable segmentation performance when compared with other CNN-based supervised methods.

This paper proposes an alternative method for evaluating pathological gait and estimating the vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) using insoles, instead of costly force plates. However, machine learning techniques for estimation still require force plates, which can induce fall risks and physical strain on patients. Thus, this paper presents an accessible and efficient learning scheme for insole-based vGRF estimation using a low-cost scale and Gaussian process regression (GPR). This approach can estimate vGRF without overfitting of small-sized data sets that are corrupted by measurement errors and noise. Additionally, the authors propose a "one-step learning" scheme based on probabilistic data augmentation that augments actual measurements of a single walking step to create a virtual data set for multiple steps. The GPR models learned from two walking steps estimated vGRF with mean errors of 8% or under for entire/local magnitudes, and the learning from one step with probabilistic augmentation improved the estimation accuracy. Overall, this method provides a cost-effective and accurate alternative to force plates for evaluating pathological gait.

Terrain classification plays a crucial role in all types of robotic systems, particularly in unknown environments. Over the past few years, researchers have proposed a range of algorithms aimed at improving the efficiency and accuracy of terrain classification. However, there are still limitations in terms of classification efficiency. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel approach - the double-tower convolutional neural network - to achieve end-to-end underwater terrain classification. 

The proposed method uses matched sonar and visual images, obtained simultaneously by the robot's sonar and visual sensors, as input. The images are paired and fed into the convolutional neural network, which outputs the classified terrain. Sonar and visual image features are applied simultaneously in the network to achieve accurate terrain classification. Therefore, this paper establishes an end-to-end convolutional neural network equipped with a classification function for underwater terrain classification.

A novel emotional speech synthesis method is proposed in this study, utilizing a Deep Neural Network (DNN) and the Pleasure-Arousal-Dominance (PAD) emotional state model. The PAD model is utilized initially to annotate the emotional state of the multi-speaker and multi-emotion speech corpus. This is done by calculating the distance between the marked emotional point in the speech corpus and the typical emotional point. The DNN-based method is used to generate acoustic features, followed by modification of the prosodic features of the synthesized emotion speech with the PAD model. Finally, the target emotional speech is synthesized using the vocoder. Results of subjective evaluations indicate that the proposed method outperforms both Hidden Markov Model (HMM)-based and DNN-based methods. Objective tests also demonstrate that the spectrum of emotional speech synthesized by the proposed method is much closer to the original speech.

The papers in this special section provide a series of high quality papers which significantly contribute to new theories, applications, and algorithms about uncertain multicriteria decision making. It not only reports recent significant developments but also highlights potential, growing research directions, and future trends, which will benefit researchers in studying theories, applications, and algorithms about uncertain multicriteria/ multiobjective/multiattribute decision making.

Flowers play an exceptionally significant role in our lives, offering high research and application value. Traditional flower classification methods have generally been based on features such as shape, color, and texture. However, this approach is associated with low classification accuracy since it requires the manual selection of features. This paper aims to propose an effective flower classification approach using convolutional neural networks and transfer learning. The study utilized various models to compare network initialization and transfer learning models, including VGG-16, VGG-19, Inception-v3, and ResNet50. The experimental results highlight that transfer learning can effectively reduce issues such as deep convolutional neural networks being prone to local optimal and over-fitting problems. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed approach significantly improves flower recognition accuracy using the Oxford flowers dataset, as well as exhibit impeccable robustness and generalizability.

We consider a class of nonlinear equations that are related to the numerical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for dynamic programming. Equations of this class can be solved with a simple fixed-point iteration, however this method may have slow convergence. We present two main contributions for increasing the efficiency of the solution: a simple preconditioning, inspired by the Jacobi method, and a selective node update procedure that reduces the number of required elementary operations.

In this paper, a new hybrid optimization approach for the pattern synthesis of linear antenna array is proposed. Hybrid approach (TAGAPSO) contains Taguchi Algorithm(TA), Genetic Algorithm(GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The aim of the optimization is to obtain desired side lobe level and half power beam width of the linear antenna array. Optimization results obtained by TA, GA, PSO and TAGAPSO are compared. The results show that TAGAPSO is much better than TA, GA and PSO. Optimization goals satisfied via TAGAPSO are much better than the other methods. Results of TAGAPSO are also compared with the results obtained by High Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS) in order to verify the results.

Deep learning, as a subfield of machine learning, is known for its ability to learn multi-level representations of raw data and improve the accuracy of tasks like classification and prediction. This approach presents a new idea for complex system fault diagnostics and prognostics. To take advantage of the benefits of deep learning and the characteristics of complex system test data, a fault diagnosis method utilizing a convolutional neural network has been proposed. This method involves preprocessing, model training, and optimization to create a complex system fault diagnostic algorithm platform based on deep learning. Simulation of an aero-engine gas path test demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach in characterizing the varied and complex nature of system data. The resulting platform provides technical support for the design, test, and management of complex systems, improving safety and significantly reducing life cycle costs.

This paper presents a novel approach for background and scene activity modelling using Spearman correlation analysis and a customized deep learning model. The system is capable of detecting and analyzing correlated regional activities in the same scene captured by multiple cameras. The experiment was conducted using four overlapping videos captured inside a hall by four cameras. Upon analysis by our model, it was found that only 17.32% of the correlated co-occurrences were actual correlations, while the remaining 82.68% were background footage showing similar and repetitive features. Our simulation results demonstrate that this approach can effectively detect high correlations among all activities during the frame rate with tied features ability.

Battery power detection is essential for the safe and efficient operation of electric vehicles. Accurate and fast estimation of the charged state of the battery is important for efficient battery management. The aim of this study was to estimate the lithium ion battery SOC of an electric car with an iron phosphate lithium-ion battery PNGV model using Matlab Simulink module and simulation of the model.

Experiments were conducted to prove that the PNGV model had higher precision. The system implemented the extended Kalman filter algorithm to estimate the charge state of the lithium battery. Concrete implementation steps were also given. The experimental simulation showed that using the extended Kalman filtering algorithm led to rapid estimation of the charged state of lithium-ion batteries, with a maximum error of about 4% and an average error of around 2%. This satisfies the accuracy requirements of the battery management system. 

In conclusion, the extended Kalman filter algorithm is a reliable and efficient method for estimating the SOC of lithium-ion batteries. The results of this study provide useful insights for the development of battery management systems for electric vehicles.

This paper focuses on real-time object recognition for indoor humanoid robots, specifically Nao robots. As improving the perceptive ability of service robots has been a research hotspot, the breakthrough of computer vision technology represented by object recognition provides a broader idea for this purpose.

In order to make the Nao robot detect objects faster, we presented an architecture for real-time object recognition on Nao robots, and offloaded the task of control and data collection from the robot to a PC. We deployed a micro-cloud layer that connects the robot with the computer vision, realizing the concept of RaaS (Robot as a Service).

Image data is transmitted over Ethernet to the workstation, running multiple parallel image processing services. These services are built with the current popular deep neural network by TensorFlow and running on a GPU GTX1080 Ti. In the micro-cloud layer, we designed a universal robotic visual task queue model, where a PC registers the task queue to the LAN. Within the LAN, multiple workers are independent service processors that process the task queue and put the results back to the manager. 

The experimental results of the Nao robot in both simulation and real-world scenarios showed that our model and method were effective, allowing the robot to recognize approximately 90 common objects with an image processing time of about 100 milliseconds per frame.

This paper presents an extension of the Terminal Sliding surface for nonlinear plants of arbitrary order. The proposed approach guarantees the finite-time robust stabilization of systems with matched uncertainties. The proposed surface possesses mathematical properties that allow for a fixed bound on the settling time of the state variable after reaching the surface. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a simulation study has been conducted using a magnetic levitation system. Overall, the results show promising potential for the application of Terminal Sliding surfaces in practical control systems.

Research into applying Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs) as a methodology for summative assessment has generated polarized opinions regarding the testing of higher levels of learning. For large classes, automatically marked MCQs which provide immediate feedback is attractive to both students and teachers. This paper is a case study into the use of MCQs in formal examinations alongside conventional questions. The study examined results of 3rd-year engineering undergraduate students studying a compulsory course in Professional Practice in a transnational education context. The results indicate that well-written MCQs can test basic factual knowledge, provide a good indication of student performance, and assess surface and deep learning. Essay questions did not correlate well with overall student performance when English was a second language. MCQs provide valuable and rapid insight into students' ability when used with other assessment methods. The paper concludes with recommendations to provide a more robust validation.

This paper proposed a Wasserstein metric-based distributionally robust approximate framework (WDRA), for unit commitment problem to manage the risk from uncertain wind power forecasted errors. The ambiguity set employed in the distributionally robust formulation is the Wasserstein ball centered at the empirical distribution. The proposed framework minimizes the generating cost, start-up cost, shut-down cost, reserve cost, and the expected thermal generation adjusting cost under the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set. The more historical available, the smaller the ambiguity set is and, hence, the less conservativeness the decision is. The size of the Wasserstein metric based robust counterpart (WDRC) model mainly depends on the size of sample set, which has a computation burden when more historical data are available. To overcome this drawback, this paper proposed an upper approximate of WDRC and verified the condition that makes the approximate model become exact. Comparisons with robust optimization and stochastic optimization illustrate that the proposed model can balance the economy and conservativeness effectively. Monte Carlo simulations on a modified IEEE-118 and a real 703-bus systems show that the proposed WDRA framework could reduce the computational time by several times when compared with WDRC.

LoRaWAN, a Low-Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) technology specifically designed for Internet of Things (IoT) deployments, has been successfully deployed in Southampton, UK. This citywide network supports an array of air quality sensors, and has helped to familiarize users with the LoRaWAN technology. To achieve successful deployment, the network utilizes both commercially available and custom gateways, with the custom gateways requiring the creation of a new printed circuit board interface, that is available for public use. Gateway locations were chosen based on availability and predicted areas of coverage, resulting in reasonable coverage across the city.

Device-to-device (D2D) communications-enabled dense heterogeneous networks (HetNets) with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are promising solutions to meet the high-throughput requirement and support massive connectivity. In this paper, we propose a novel framework on the D2D-enabled HetNets with NOMA, where small cells underlay the uplink spectrum of macrocells to make full use of spectrum resources, NOMA technique is invoked to serve more downlink users simultaneously, and D2D-enabled multi-hop transmission is established to enhance signal reception of the far users (FUs) on cell edge. We investigate joint power allocation and user scheduling to maximize the ergodic sum rate of the near users (NUs) in the small cells while guaranteeing the quality-of-service requirements of the FUs and the macro-cell users. The optimal solution to this problem is complexity-prohibitive especially with large numbers of users and small base stations (SBSs) because it requires an exhaustive search over all possible combinations of SBSs, NUs, and FUs. To simplify the solution, we develop a two-step approach by decomposing the original problem into a power allocation problem and a user scheduling problem. We derive the closed-form solution of the power allocation problem via analyzing the objective function and constraints. The user scheduling problem is a joint user pairing and access point assignment problem. To solve it, we propose an SBS-NU-FU matching algorithm to obtain a near-optimal one-to-one three-sided matching of SBSs, NUs, and FUs. The simulation results show that the two-step method gets around 95% of the system throughput of the optimal one and can significantly improve the spectral efficiency of the D2D-enabled HetNets.

In this paper, a lightweight security solution is proposed for the Internet of Things (IoT) systems. In fact, this proposed solution is called TrioSec, and can ensure the basic security requirements such as Authentication/Authorization, Intrusion Detection System (IDS), and System Monitoring with minimum computation and resources overhead. The proposed solution uses optimized open source software agents that can be implemented in the Gateway node of the IoT network layer. In fact, several recent interesting security solutions were being presented in the literature to tackle these security requirements. However, there is not yet any complete security solution for IoT systems that integrates multiple software agents. The advantage of the proposed solution is its ability to combine the best existing and customized security tools to reach a maximum level of security with a minimum overhead level in terms of computation and resources.

A non-invasive approach to monitor the human chest in real-time has been developed. The method employs an innovative learning by examples (LBE) technique to efficiently solve the inverse problem of electrical impedance tomography (EIT). The partial least squares (PLS) feature extraction technique is combined with output-space-filling (OSF) adaptive sampling to create a small yet informative training database. This database is then used to make accurate and real-time predictions of lung conductivity through support vector regression (SVR). The potential of LBE inversion technique has been assessed through preliminary numerical validation.

Artificial intelligence is seeing a tremendous revival, with predictive maintenance (PdM) using data-driven methods becoming the most effective solution for smart manufacturing and industrial big data. Health perception, such as fault diagnosis and remaining life assessment, is especially critical. However, current PdM research is still in primary experimental stages, and most works use open datasets. Specific applications, such as rotating machinery, are rarely combined. This paper focuses on data-driven PdM methods, providing a comprehensive survey of its applications and offering graduate students, companies, and institutions a preliminary understanding of recent publications. 

First, the PdM approach is briefly introduced, as well as the PdM scheme for automatic washing equipment. The challenges encountered in conducting PdM research are also demonstrated. Second, specific industrial applications are classified based on six algorithms of machine learning and deep learning (DL). Five performance metrics are compared for each classification, and the accuracy of these PdM applications is analyzed in detail. The summarized literature mainly uses data from public datasets, such as Case Western Reserve University (CWRU)/Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), and researchers seem to be focusing more on DL algorithms in recent years. 

Finally, the common features of surveyed PdM applications are summarized, and potential directions for research are discussed.

The purpose of Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) is to find the optimal routes to reach the destination for the customers. Effects of transports on the environment are dangerous nowadays. It is important to reduce the distance traversed by the vehicles. Over the past few years many algorithms have been proposed for vehicle routing problem. This paper outlines the basic concepts of few algorithms and these algorithms are compared based on the outcomes. In addition to finding the best route during travel, vehicle speed, carbon dioxide emission rates can also be examined. The study indicates that each algorithm has some specific features and is suitable for particular applications.

The papers in this special section focus on emerging non-volatile memory technologies (NVM). Emerging NVM technologies have attracted significant interest in recent years because of the fast-growing performance and capacity demands on memory and storage in the big data era. Well known examples include the 3D XPoint memory and various NVDIMM hybrid memory technologies. They have shown potential towards larger memory and storage capacities with nearly zero leakage power, while extending memory/ system architecture design approaches. The unique characteristics of NVM technologies not only introduce new opportunities, but simultaneously create challenges to the designs at multiple levels of abstraction in computer systems, including those of device management, CPU cache management, memory/storage architecture, and system design. Furthermore, emerging NVM technologies also drive the development of techniques which perform computing operations in memory, i.e., processing-in-memory (PIM), by taking advantage of crossbar-based accelerators using NVMs. Thus, for the emerging NVM technologies, there is an urgent need for technology innovation, modeling, analysis, design, and application, ranging from the device-level to the system-level.

Independent mobility of visually impaired people is key to making an inclusive society for them. Unstructured infrastructure in developing countries pose significant challenges in developing aids to address the mobility problem of visually impaired. Most of the assistive devices available internationally assume a structured and controlled environment severely restricting the applicability of such devices. In this paper, we assess the ability of state-of-the-art assistive devices for addressing the independent outdoor mobility needs of the visually impaired in an unstructured environment. We have created realistic datasets for various scenarios and evaluate deep neural networks for object detection on these datasets. We also present a portable prototype for the task. Further, we have also developed a cloud based solution to address the mobility requirements. We compare the local device based and cloud based solutions in terms of accuracy, latency, and energy. We present and discuss results from these two implementations that can provide insights for an effective solution. The results and insights open up novel research problems for embedded systems.

The increasing number of resource-constrained devices in machine-type communications (MTC) has led to a critical challenge in fulfilling communication needs in ultra-dense and dynamic wireless environments. Although 5G and beyond networks are expected to support multiple application scenarios, the massive machine type communications (mMTC) pose a technical challenge due to handling a vast number of devices in cellular networks. This paper aims to analyze technical issues, review recent advances, highlight potential solutions, and propose research directions. The challenges include providing quality of service (QoS), handling dynamic and sporadic MTC traffic, high signaling overheads, and RAN congestion. The paper discusses the key enablers for mMTC, the legacy random access procedure's inefficiency, and emerging cellular IoT standards like LTE-M and narrowband IoT (NB-IoT). A framework for performance analysis of transmission scheduling with QoS support is presented, and the challenges in short data packet transmission are highlighted. The paper provides a detailed overview of current solutions and emerging techniques like machine learning (ML) to tackle RAN congestion as well as identifying use cases and challenges. The low-complexity Q-learning approach for mMTC is discussed alongside its recent enhancements towards better learning performance and convergence. Finally, the paper highlights some open research challenges and promising future research directions.

To apply PRAM technology to IoT devices, it is important to reduce the energy consumption required for writing data to PRAM. A study was conducted using the Sentaurus TCAD simulator to optimize the heater material and structure of sub-20nm PRAM. The results showed that TiN was the most efficient material compared to Poly Si or W, and the wall structure had better write energy efficiency than the confined structure. Furthermore, a new method called Heat-Aware Write (HAW) was introduced. This technology controls the write current and voltage, taking into consideration the heat generated by the heater. With the use of HSPICE simulation, which employs an industry-compatible 0.25-μm model, the PRAM cell achieved an improvement in write energy by 22%, 19%, and 36% in the case of the wall structure with TiN, the proposed HAW, and both combined, respectively.

This chapter addresses the issue of fair distribution of resources in wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) for both types of energy storage strategies. To simplify the analysis, the chapter assumes only the additional power consumed by the circuitry and linear RF-to-direct power conversion. The proposed policies include optimal power allocation at the base station (BS) and optimal time sharing among the energy harvesting units (EHUs), ensuring proportional fairness in resource sharing. The proposed policies also adhere to the constraint of average power consumption at the BS. In poor channel conditions, the proposed policies impose silence at the BS, resulting in high energy efficiency of the WPCN. The chapter provides closed-form solutions for power and time allocation for fairness-aware WPCNs.

Human posture recognition is a critical component of human activity monitoring, especially for the elderly living alone, who need to monitor their health status and accidental falls. With the world's elderly population set to double by 2050, there is a high demand for activity monitoring systems. Researchers have developed various camera and wearable device-based human recognition systems, but they are often considered privacy-invasive or not practical for long-term monitoring.

To address these challenges, we propose a device-free unobtrusive indoor human posture recognition system. The proposed system leverages a low-resolution infrared sensor-based wireless sensor network and a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). The system integrates an AMG8833 sensor module with 8x8 thermal sensors to sense the human body temperature and a WiFi module for a wireless sensor network. We use three wireless sensor nodes to capture 3-axis human thermal images.

To validate our proposed system, we collected 15063 samples from four volunteers while they performed eight human postures. These samples served as the ground truth for the 10-fold cross-validation of our DCNN models. Experimental results indicate that the highest average F1-score for the eight postures was 0.9981. Thus, our proposed system boasts high potential for monitoring elderly daily activities, exercise, and falls in emergency cases.

We believe that our device-free unobtrusive sensing technology will be a milestone, enabling researchers to create more responsive and effective activity monitoring systems, which will enhance elder care and help to keep individuals safe.

Linear detectors, such as minimum mean square error (MMSE), present a computational burden for massive multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems due to large-scale matrix inversions. To overcome this problem, iterative detectors based on Jacobi and steepest descent (SD) algorithms have been introduced. However, these methods become less beneficial in scenarios where the number of users is close to that of the base station antennas and channel correlation is considered. In this paper, a new iterative detector called SDBB, based on SD and Barzilai-Borwein (BB) algorithms, is introduced. Additionally, an enhanced version of SDBB (ESDBB), which combines SDBB with SD, is proposed to improve performance in challenging scenarios. Both theoretical and numerical results are presented to demonstrate the advantages of ESDBB in balancing performance and complexity. ESDBB outperforms methods including adaptive Jacobi and successive over relaxation (SOR) and has a faster convergence rate and better bit error rate (BER) results. An efficient hardware architecture for ESDBB is also proposed and implementation results on a Xilinx Virtex-7 XC7VX690T FPGA show the advantages of the proposed ESDBB detector in terms of throughput (31.3 Mb/s) and efficiency when compared to the state of the art (SOA).

An electromechanical-electromagnetic hybrid simulation algorithm based on boundary nodes grouping and decoupling is proposed in this paper. The UHV $AC/DC$ backbone network is described as electromagnetic transient models and the others are described as electromechanical transient models and power grids at low voltage side are decoupled at their boundary. A new partitioning method of backbone network based on heuristic rules is proposed to support electromagnetic transient parallel computing and a hybrid parallel simulation algorithm based on subnet groups is designed. The theoretical analysis and derivation of the algorithm shows that the algorithm can improve the efficiency of hybrid simulation with a large number of boundary nodes.

The problem of loss-free burst transmission has been extensively researched within Burst Switching Networks (BSN). Despite numerous approaches proposed for performance improvement, these approaches often fall short of achieving optimal performance levels. In order to address this issue, a dynamic IO queue management scheme based on burst rate has been put forward. This method monitors incoming burst traffic from a greater number of nodes and adjusts the size of the input-output queue systems based on the rate of incoming bursts. The queued bursts are then routed through available paths as they are identified. The method is capable of dynamically triggering the IO queue systems to expand or contract in response to the varying levels of burst traffic. By implementing this method, the performance of burst switching networks can be significantly improved.

Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a condition where diabetes affects the eyes and is the leading cause of blindness. As individuals with diabetes grow older, they are at a higher risk of developing DR. During the early stages of the disease, microaneurysms, hemorrhages, and exudates may be present as significant indicators. However, patients do not typically experience vision problems until the late stages of DR when the disease becomes difficult to treat.

Early detection of DR is crucial in preventing its progression. Thanks to advanced technology such as intelligent diagnosis systems, image processing, and computer vision systems, doctors can detect DR at an early stage. This is achieved using a convolutional neural system, which precisely identifies and categorizes the disease through spatial examination, providing high accuracy results.

In summary, early diagnosis of Diabetic Retinopathy is imperative to prevent blindness. Technology plays a crucial role in detection, and advanced techniques such as convolutional neural systems can provide precise results that aid in the prevention of the disease's progression.

The rapid development of the Internet of Things has raised the bar for traffic volume and user connectivity density in 5G networks. In order to meet these demands, ultra-dense networks (UDN) are projected to be the future direction. However, as the number of mobile devices (MDs) and computationally intensive applications continue to increase, there exists a conflict between the limited computing and battery resources of MDs and the ever-increasing demands of mobile applications. In order to overcome this issue, mobile edge computing has emerged as a promising solution. Previously, research on computation offloading in UDN focused primarily on task offloading decision-making, without adequately considering important information about the MDs, such as remaining battery and computation frequency. This study proposes an energy-aware game theoretical offloading scheme that takes into account the remaining battery and computation frequency of MDs as part of the task offloading for ultra-dense edge computing. Our results indicate that our energy-aware task offloading scheme is efficient in saving MDs' energy and also produces a delay-optimal profile for task offloading decisions.

This paper investigates the effectiveness of supervised machine learning algorithms when it comes to forecasting the tensile strength of high density polyethylene film that is created by the extrusion-blown molding process. Three different algorithms were assessed in this research including Artificial Neural Networks, Decision Tree, and k-Nearest Neighbors, all of which took into account eleven input parameters. Specifically, these algorithms were modeled using five materials-related input parameters and six process-related input parameters. The results of this study demonstrate the potential of these algorithms' ability to accurately forecast the desired property of products created using the extrusion-blown process.

The recent success of neural networks has significantly advanced the performance of 3D human pose estimation from 2D input images. However, the diversity of capturing viewpoints and the flexibility of the human poses remain some significant challenges. In this paper, we propose a view-invariant 3D human pose estimation module to alleviate the effects of viewpoint diversity. The proposed framework consists of a base network, which provides an initial estimation of a 3D pose, a view-invariant hierarchical correction network (VI-HC) on top of that to learn the 3D pose refinement under consistent views, and a view-invariant discriminative network (VID) to enforce high-level constraints over body configurations. In VI-HC, the initial 3D pose inputs are automatically transformed to consistent views for further refinements at the global body and local body parts level, respectively. For the VID, under consistent viewpoints, we use adversarial learning to differentiate between estimated 3D poses and real 3D poses to avoid implausible results. The experimental results demonstrate that the constraint on viewpoint consistency can dramatically enhance the performance of 3D human pose estimation. Our module shows robustness for different 3D pose base networks and achieves a significant improvement (about 9%) over a powerful baseline on the public 3D pose estimation benchmark Human3.6M.

By incorporating powerful soft-decision error correction codes such as LDPC to replace legacy hard-decision codes like BCH, the reliability of flash memory can be increased beyond its current limits. However, this comes at the cost of additional reading latency to generate soft information, namely log-likelihood ratios (LLRs). Unfortunately, the memory channel is highly variable due to factors such as temperature, parasitic coupling and retention time, rendering the use of precomputed LLR lookup tables ineffective as the device ages. To avoid performance degradation, estimated LLRs need to be regularly updated. 
To address this challenge, we propose a dynamic, low-latency blind detection algorithm that adaptively adjusts hard/soft-decision boundaries and estimates the corresponding LLR codebook. Our demodulator offers near-optimal performance while keeping complexity overhead low.

High-frequency (HF) signal injection methods have proved to be good candidates for permanent magnet synchronous motor sensorless control at zero or low speed. However, conventional methods have some shortcomings, and several improved methods have been put forward by scholars. In order to analyze the essential relationships among these methods, a unified graphical model is proposed in this paper based on the analysis of mechanism of conventional HF signal injection methods. According to the unified graphical model, the signal modulation modes can be categorized into phase-modulated-based HF injection (PMHI) and amplitude-modulated-based HF injection (AMHI), meanwhile the demodulation modes can be classified into open-loop calculation and close-loop convergence. Besides, novel methods are easily deduced from the unified graphical model. Furthermore, the effects of adverse factors, including resistance, digital control delay, inverter nonlinearity, and cross saturation on PMHI and AMHI are analyzed, respectively. Finally, experimental results prove the validity of the theoretical analysis.

The article is devoted to the discussion of the problems of development of predictive neural network models based on the residual number system and the use of modular arithmetic to improve the quality of automatic control systems by adding to the control algorithms a prognostic component, which is especially important for astatic control objects. The possibility of implementing neural network training algorithms in the residual number system is shown, which allows to significantly accelerate the work of these algorithms, which is especially important when adding new functionality to automatic control systems in the form of prognostic neural network models.

While image matching has been studied in remote sensing community for decades, matching multimodal data [e.g., optical, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and map] remains a challenging problem because of significant nonlinear intensity differences between such data. To address this problem, we present a novel fast and robust template matching framework integrating local descriptors for multimodal images. First, a local descriptor [such as histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) and local self-similarity (LSS) or speeded-up robust feature (SURF)] is extracted at each pixel to form a pixelwise feature representation of an image. Then, we define a fast similarity measure based on the feature representation using the fast Fourier transform (FFT) in the frequency domain. A template matching strategy is employed to detect correspondences between images. In this procedure, we also propose a novel pixelwise feature representation using orientated gradients of images, which is named channel features of orientated gradients (CFOG). This novel feature is an extension of the pixelwise HOG descriptor with superior performance in image matching and computational efficiency. The major advantages of the proposed matching framework include: 1) structural similarity representation using the pixelwise feature description and 2) high computational efficiency due to the use of FFT. The proposed matching framework has been evaluated using many different types of multimodal images, and the results demonstrate its superior matching performance with respect to the state-of-the-art methods.

A novel antiresonant fiber with a hollow core has been investigated numerically, with a focus on enhancing its performance. The fiber cladding is designed with nested antiresonant tubes without any additional radial interconnection struts, thereby eliminating the presence of spurious loss peaks and dips within the antiresonant windows. This improvement significantly benefits the fiber's excellent bandwidth and minimal loss transmission properties, promoting its widespread application in the field.

Furthermore, the adoption of antiresonant membranes in this novel fiber design effectively reduces the leakage loss, while the bending loss is negligible. In comparison to the previously reported antiresonant fibers, the adoption of this fiber design in negative curvature fibers has led to enhanced performance in terms of losses. Overall, the results of this study indicate that the novel hollow core antiresonant fiber design has great potential for improving the performance of optical fibers in various applications.

A new Krylov subspace method has been developed to significantly reduce the computational complexity of a specific class of quadratic bilinear dynamical systems. The proposed method utilizes the first two generalized transfer functions of the system and implements a Petrov-Galerkin projection scheme. This projection involves interpolating the transfer functions at specific points, which is equivalent to constructing the corresponding Krylov subspace. 

In the case of single-input single-output systems, the relevant Krylov subspace can be conveniently constructed for the interpolation points. However, for multi-input multi-output systems, the method requires user-specified directional information to determine a tangential interpolation. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through numerical examples.

Melanoma skin cancer is one of the most deadly forms of cancer which are responsible for thousands of deaths. The manual process of melanoma diagnosis is a time taking and difficult task, therefore researchers introduced several computerized methods for recognition. Through computational methods, improves the accuracy of diagnostics process which is helpful for dermatologists. In this paper, we proposed an automated system for skin lesion classification through transfer learning based deep neural network (DCNN) features extraction and kurtosis controlled principle component (KcPCA) based optimal features selection. The pre-trained ResNet deep neural network such as RESNET-50 and RESNET-101 are utilized for features extraction. Then fused their information and selects the best features which later fed to supervised learning method such as SVM of radial basis function (RBF) for classification. Three datasets name HAM10000, ISBI 2017, and ISBI 2016 are utilized for experimental results and achieved an accuracy of 89.8%, 95.60%, and 90.20%, respectively. The overall results show that the performance of the proposed system is reliable as compared to existing techniques.

Improving image visibility in participating media, like mist or water, is a challenging task. Image dehazing is the process of generating a clear image from a hazy one, and prior approaches used physical models based on simplifications and priors. However, a new study demonstrates the effectiveness of an end-to-end convolutional neural network, which can learn the dehazing process without any parameters or priors. This generic method was trained on hazy indoor images but was able to restore outdoor images with real haze. The researchers also introduced Guided Layers in their architecture, which helped reduce spatial information loss while restoring the images. The proposed method outperformed other machine learning-based models, yielding better results both qualitatively and quantitatively.

Online verification of dynamic CPS systems has gained widespread recognition as a practical and effective method for handling the non-deterministic and unpredictable behavior of these systems. However, one major challenge is ensuring that the verification process completes quickly enough to allow sufficient time for the running system to respond if an error is detected. While the problems to be verified in each cycle are similar, there are differences caused by changing parameter values or reorganization of active components during runtime.

To address this challenge, this paper proposes an incremental verification technique for online verification of CPS systems. The method involves distinguishing the differences between the current problem under verification and the previously verified problem. Then, the problem space of the previous problem is used as a warm-start base, into which the modified parts are introduced and solved incrementally and efficiently.

To demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique, a set of case studies involving a real-case train control system is presented. The results show that the incremental online verification technique significantly reduces the verification time while maintaining a high level of accuracy. This technique has the potential to improve the safety and reliability of dynamic CPS systems in various fields, such as transportation, manufacturing, and healthcare.

This paper investigates creativity of students in the context of engineering education. The main goal is to get new insights on how to motivate engineering students to express more creativity in solving their assignments. The research included a crowdvoting contest on a sample of was 28 students in the area of information technologies at Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade. Results point out that a crowdvoting competition can be used to induce students' creativity in engineering education. Additionally, we discuss how students creativity styles relate to the design of creative-based educational tasks.

An existing physical layer security scheme cannot be applied to legacy devices operating on long coherence-time channels since it requires changes to the physical layer. Therefore, a new physical-layer security scheme has been developed to secure legacy clients. In this scheme, secret keys are generated by a client and transmitted to the access point (AP). To protect these keys, a special device called secrecy protector (SP) transmits jamming signals to prevent eavesdroppers from overhearing the keys. The SP is equipped with multiple antennas, each of which transmits an independent jamming stream with a pseudo-preamble.

Since the SP can share jamming signals with the AP secretly, the AP can use a certain analog network coding scheme to remove jamming signals and decode the keys, while eavesdroppers have no knowledge of jamming signals to decode the keys. To enhance the security of the system, frequency diversity is exploited. The design of jamming mechanisms also resists collusion among eavesdroppers, allowing for secret keys to be secretly shared between the AP and a client.

This scheme has been implemented on a software-defined radio platform and performance results demonstrate that it can effectively deliver secure communications without any changes to the physical layer of legacy clients, making it a highly efficient and practical solution.

Frequently executed methods have major impact in increasing the performance of CPU as well as in code optimization to address the best set of optimization. In this study it is proposed to develop a machine learning based predictive model using Support Vector Machine (SVM), classifier for identification and prediction of frequently executed methods in a program. Since kernel functions play an important role in performance of the SVM and choosing suitable kernel function is still an area of research, here the performance of various kernels of SVM classifier is evaluated and compared. It is found that when trained with ten static program features, the derived SVM model using Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel function predicts the best accuracy of 65% using SPEC CPU 2000 INT dataset. When the same data set was compared with Linear kernel, Polynomial and Sigmoid kernel the prediction accuracy is found to be 40%, 45% and 15% respectively.

Facial recognition technology has emerged as a promising solution to address the increasing need for identity verification in various industries. It has been widely applied and has demonstrated its effectiveness as an additional layer of security through native applications. However, there has been no attempt to integrate this solution into a web-based platform, supporting real-time classification.

In light of the frequent reports of websites being exploited and databases being leaked, there is a pressing need for an intelligent security mechanism that can enhance the traditional authentication methods, such as usernames and passwords. This paper explores the feasibility of unobtrusive, continuous authentication for web applications, based on facial data collected through WebAssembly driven detection algorithms. This innovative detection technique has shown the capability to perform real-time image processing on the web, achieving near-native speeds. Moreover, this is coupled with a competitive server-side facial recognition rate of 91.67% achieved on the Labeled Faces in the Wild dataset.

Overall, integrating facial recognition technology into web-based authentication mechanisms could be a game-changer in the field of cybersecurity. It has the potential to offer a more secure and reliable authentication method for web applications, without the need for intrusive, traditional methods of authentication. As such, it could prove a welcome solution in the fight against cybercrime.

In wireless sensor network (WSN), the appearance of coverage hole reduces the efficiency of data collection and has a serious impact on network quality of service. Detection of coverage holes is foundation of patching the sensor network to guarantee network quality of service. The paper proposes a distributed coverage hole detection algorithm based on hole boundary nodes (HPNs-CHD). The algorithm firstly uses sensing disk model to identify the HBN nodes in WSN and then exploits probabilistic message mechanism to detect coverage hole. The simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm outperforms other two algorithms in terms of average energy consumption and average time of coverage holes detection.

In this paper, we introduce a method to obtain necessary and sufficient stability conditions for systems governed by one-dimensional nonlinear hyperbolic partial-differential equations with closed-loop integral controllers, when the linear frequency analysis cannot be used anymore. We study the stability of a general nonlinear transport equation where the control input and the measured output are both located on the boundaries. The principle of the method is to extract the limiting part of the stability from the solution using a projector on a finite-dimensional space and then use a Lyapunov approach. This paper improves a result of Trinh, Andrieu, and Xu, and gives an optimal condition for the design of the controller. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations where the predicted stable and unstable regions can be clearly identified.

Template-matching-based approaches have been used for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR) for many years, but are strongly affected by background clutter and noise as well as data set size. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multilevel reconstruction-based multitask joint sparse representation method. Using the attributed scattering center (ASC) model, SAR images exhibit point-scatter-like behavior, which can be modeled by scattering centers on the target. ASC extraction and multilevel reconstruction based on energy ratio (ER) enhance the data set and reduce background clutter and noise. Subdictionaries are designed based on the label of training samples, and multiple test images are reconstructed and classified using random projection coefficients and a multitask joint sparse representation classification framework. The final decision is made based on accumulated reconstruction error. Experimental results on MSTAR data confirmed the method's effectiveness.

Spatial misalignment caused by variations in poses and viewpoints is one of the most critical issues that hinder the performance improvement in existing person re-identification (Re-ID) algorithms. Although it is straightforward to explore correspondence learning algorithms for alignment, online learning is intractable for negative pairs due to the intrinsic visual difference between negative pairs and efficiency concern. To address this problem, in this paper, we present a robust and efficient graph correspondence transfer (REGCT) approach for explicit spatial alignment in Re-ID. Specifically, we propose the off-line correspondence learning and on-line correspondence transfer framework. During training, patch-wise correspondences between positive training pairs are established via graph matching. By exploiting both spatial and visual contexts of human appearance in graph matching, meaningful semantic correspondences can be obtained. During testing, the off-line learned patch-wise correspondence templates are transferred to test pairs with similar pose-pair configurations for local feature distance calculation. To enhance the robustness of correspondence transfer, we design a novel pose context descriptor to accurately model human body configurations, and present an approach to measure the similarity between a pair of pose context descriptors. Meanwhile, to improve testing efficiency, we propose a correspondence template ensemble method using the voting mechanism, which significantly reduces the amount of patch-wise matchings involved in distance calculation. With the aforementioned strategies, the REGCT model can effectively and efficiently handle the spatial misalignment problem in Re-ID. Extensive experiments on five challenging benchmarks, including VIPeR, Road, PRID450S, 3DPES, and CUHK01, evidence the superior performance of REGCT over other state-of-the-art approaches.

A logic diagnosis procedure provides information about the defects that are present in a faulty unit as a set of candidate faults. To obtain smaller, and more accurate, sets of candidate faults, a diagnostic test generation procedure produces a test set that distinguishes fault pairs. This paper observes that large sets of candidate faults are obtained when multiple defects are present in a faulty unit, even if a diagnostic test set is used for logic diagnosis. This points to the possibility that fault pairs do not provide a complete set of targets for diagnostic test generation. This paper analyzes the conditions that cause a large set of candidate faults to be formed under a particular logic diagnosis procedure and suggests new targets for diagnostic test generation. The experimental results for benchmark circuits demonstrate that a diagnostic test set can be improved by adding diagnostic tests for the new targets.

In this brief, we explore coordinated path-following control for multiple nonlinear autonomous vehicles connected by digital networks, focusing on compensating for time delays in the network. We put forward a novel networked predictive control strategy that offers several benefits over existing methods, including high computational efficiency, robustness to disturbances and relaxed restrictions on communication topology. We provide theoretical analysis of our approach, including conditions necessary to achieve control objectives. Finally, we conducted experiments that demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

Biomedical image analysis is one of the most challenging and inevitable part of the computer aided diagnostic systems. Automated analysis of the image can detect various diseases automatically without human intervention. Computer vision and artificial intelligence can sometimes defeat human diagnostic power and can reveal some hidden information from the biomedical images. In the field of health care, accurate results are highly required within stipulated amount of time. But to increase accuracy, proper preprocessing with sophisticated algorithms is required. Low quality image can affect processing algorithm which can leads to the poor result. Therefore, sophisticated preprocessing methods are required to get reliable results. Contrast is one of the most important parameter for any image. Poor contrast may cause several problems for computer vision algorithms. Conventional algorithms for contrast adjustment may not be suitable for many purposes. Sometimes, these methods can generate some images that may lose some critical information. In this work, a contrast optimization method based on well-known metaheuristic technique called genetic algorithm with elitism is used that can enhance the biomedical images for better analysis. A new kernel has been proposed to detect the edges. Obtained results illustrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

This paper addresses a concept of a spherical autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) with vertically rotatable thruster units. Compared to torpedo-type AUVs, the spherical AUV would have precise path following and close inspection abilities with high degrees-of-freedom motions and slow speed. While various underwater missions are being automated through improvements in AUV motion control methods, the spherical shape would further enhance the performance due to its simple hydrodynamic models that are beneficial for computer simulations. The spherical AUV consists of a main cubic unit that contains main computers, batteries, and proprioceptive sensors, and six surrounding units that contain either a propeller, a sampling device, sensors, or extra computers. The attachment of the six surrounding units at each surface of the main unit completes the AUV's spherical shape. The surrounding units are modularized and, therefore, can be substituted by other units to carry out different underwater missions.

Today, a wide variety of applications with different requirements are rapidly developed in industrial wireless sensor networks, and providing the Quality of Service (QoS) for this kind of communication network is inevitable. It is difficult to solve the problems of poor adaptability and difficulty in the implementation of the QoS-based network configuration and management in traditional network architecture. We present a hierarchical software-defined network architecture for wireless sensor networks, which makes the complex network management possible and the system more adaptable. Furthermore, we propose a QoS-based routing protocol, called QSDN-WISE, which consists of a clustering algorithm, a routing algorithm, and local network maintenance. A double-cluster head-based uneven clustering algorithm, called DCHUC, avoids the energy hole phenomenon and reduces the workload of a single cluster head. The centralized QSDN-WISE routing algorithm constructs two heterogeneous forwarding paths for nodes, which meets the requirements for different data levels. Local network maintenance reduces the number of control messages in the network. The simulation results indicate that the QSDN-WISE can provide the QoS support for data with different requirements, balance the network energy consumption, and prolong the network's lifetime.

In this paper, we study the stabilization problem of quantum spin-1/2 systems under continuous-time measurements. In the case without feedback, we show exponential stabilization around the excited and ground state by providing a lower bound of the convergence rate. Based on stochastic Lyapunov techniques, we propose a parametrized feedback controller ensuring exponential convergence toward the target state. Moreover, we provide a lower bound of the convergence rate for this case. Then, we discuss the effect of each parameter appearing in the controller in the convergence rate. Finally, we illustrate the efficiency of such feedback controller through simulations.

Scheduling of smart appliances is an effective method to decrease peak demand, but it can result in underutilization of available power. This gap between desired and actual power consumption is mainly caused by constant power usage of some appliances. To address this issue, we have analyzed the distributed scheduling algorithm proposed by Chen et al. (2014) and developed a new approach to maximize available power during peak hours. By utilizing this approach, appliances may finish their operations earlier, thereby optimizing power consumption.

Software Defined Networks (SDNs) have proven to be effective in policy enforcement and intelligent routing. While SDNs can provide policy enforcement and routing, incorporating higher layer information can provide a greater advantage. With the help of Machine Learning (ML), modern networks can classify traffic by gathering data. In order to perform application aware policy enforcement and routing in SDNs, data features such as flow meta-data information and payload statistics should be used, especially when dealing with encrypted traffic.

However, there are several difficulties involved such as the scalability costs of sending packets to the controller and obtaining application layer labeled data to train and validate classifiers. To overcome these issues, this work proposes using a data collection mechanism to gather traffic data using the OpenFlow protocol and extending a hybrid SDN architecture with a distributed control plane. Additionally, a semi-supervised approach is used in classifiers, which improves traffic classifiers even with a small number of labeled data entries in the training data sets.

The proposed architecture extensions and the obtained data-set features include flow meta-data information and the sizes and inter-arrival times of initial packets. With just 20% of labeled data entries in the training data sets, valid traffic classification can be achieved. Therefore, incorporating higher layer information along with Machine Learning can provide a greater advantage in policy enforcement and routing in SDNs.

Recently, there has been significant interest in the development of face tracking technology. 3D face tracking typically relies on RGB and Depth Data to detect and track faces. However, changes in ambient lighting can adversely affect face tracking stability, making it difficult to achieve optimal results. To address this challenge, this study focuses on the effect of color components on real-time 3D face tracking using Kinect. Specifically, the experiment involved projecting 24 different colors onto the user's face and analyzing the impact of their R, G, B, H, S, and V components. Statistical analysis was performed using ANOVA and regression to identify the most significant component affecting face tracking stability with Kinect. The results showed a stability rate of above 80% for face tracking in the dark, with the HSV color model outperforming the RGB model. The brightness level (Value) was found to be the most significant component that affects the system's ability to detect faces in a dark environment. These findings can be used to guide the selection of animation design background colors for 3D face projection mapping in a nearly complete dark room.

This paper proposes a method for evaluating the reliability of complex software based on a weighted network model for large-scale complex software systems. The model is designed to address the limitations of existing software networks in depicting dependencies of real software systems. The complex software system is initially converted into a complex software network, which represents the internal topology structure in the form of the network. Subsequently, a weighted network model is created based on this topology between nodes to analyze the actual dependencies of each structure within the software system. Lastly, using the weighted network model, the reliability analysis of a real software system is conducted and compared with other technologies.
