The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Transmission lines are the most vulnerable and crucial part of the power system network, as they have the highest percentage of fault occurrence. In this paper, a transmission line model is created using PSCAD software, which can simulate all types of faults. To provide an alternative to conventional relays, an artificial neural network is proposed, which has a strong capability to learn complex relationships through the data presented to it. In this study, data generated by the PSCAD model is provided to the neural network, which consists of sets of three currents and voltages.

A neural network of 6-10-4 configuration was created based on the default setting, which resulted in a mean squared error of 0.051 and a correlation of 0.88. The influential parameters of the neural network, which includes hidden neurons, layers, and transfer functions, were varied, and a change in performance was observed. Finally, a model with a configuration of 6-17-6-4 was selected, which reduced the error to 0.017, and the overall correlation increased to approximately 0.97. The whole neural network process was carried out on the MATLAB® software, resulting in a useful alternative to conventional relays for the transmission lines in a power system network.

The demand-controlled ventilation is an innovative control approach that has been developed in recent years as part of smart building technologies. It aims to optimize energy consumption, air quality, and occupant comfort through the use of cost-effective, scalable, low-power wireless networks for monitoring and controlling building automation systems. However, devices and communication routes are susceptible to faults, which can compromise the system's performance. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel fault injection framework to enable scholars to monitor the behavior of the system in the presence of different faults. The authors also present a fault-error-failure propagation model at the component and system levels for testing fault detection and diagnosis methods. The wireless sensor and actuator networks used for this demand-controlled ventilation and heating system are validated by the previous cabled model and are found to be compatible with the prevalent ZigBee protocol for building automation. In the result section, the temperature signals in healthy-mode and faulty-mode and the comparison of energy consumption in healthy mode and different faulty modes are presented. Overall, this study highlights the importance of fault-tolerant design in smart building technologies and provides a useful tool for testing and improving fault detection and diagnosis methods.

Serious Game (SG) has been used in many area of education and training. It has been used to help teacher or educator to teach students so that they can increase their ability to understand the subject using a realistic simulations of real-life situations. On the other hand, music has become a big element in the world of entertainment. Thus, this paper propose a new framework for the software developer to create new Serious Game for learning musical instrument. This paper discusses the notion of a SG schema and how pre-existing SG for musical practice can be used to provide design guidelines by developing a framework. Thus, SG developer for musical instrument game can easily map the learning aspects, describe software design, and describe ways to control them with new interfaces for musical expression. The framework is developed from analysis of several previous researches and associated to the game design process component of musical instrument. The framework has been implemented using three case studies of musical instrument (saron, kendhang, and angklung). Each components of the framework are mapped to the new case studies which produce three software game applications. Each application has been evaluated by 20 users. The result shows that the framework has been able to effectively and efficiently help game developer to create musical instrument game.

Neural network accelerators are widely deployed in application systems for computer vision, speech recognition, and machine translation. Due to ubiquitous deployment of these systems, a strong incentive rises for adversaries to attack such artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Trojan is one of the most important attack models in hardware security domain. Hardware Trojans are malicious modifications to original ICs inserted by adversaries, which lead the system to malfunction after being triggered. The globalization of the semiconductor gives a chance for the adversary to conduct the hardware Trojan attacks.Previous works design Neural Network (NN) Trojans with access to the model, toolchain, and hardware platform. However, the threat model is impractical which hinders their real adoption. In this work, we propose a memory Trojan methodology without the help of toolchain manipulation and model parameter information. We first leverage the memory access patterns to identify the input image data. Then we propose a Trojan triggering method based on the dedicated input image other than the circuit events, which has better controllability. The triggering mechanism works well even with environment noise and preprocessing towards the original images. In the end, we implement and verify the effectiveness of accuracy degradation attack.

While spatial feature extraction from images has been extensively explored, research on extracting spatio-temporal features from event streams is still emerging. A unique aspect of event streams is that the same network architecture can be used for recognizing static objects and motions. However, it remains unclear what features are most effective in providing a good abstraction for different scenarios. In this study, we assess the quality of features in a spiking HMAX architecture by evaluating classification performance before and after each layer. We demonstrate that classical edge features, reminiscent of the V1 area of the visual cortex, combined with fixational eye movements possess strong abstraction capabilities. Our approach outperforms previously reported F1 scores on the N-Caltech101 dataset, using a similar architecture without a STDP learning layer. However, when observing motions in a static DVS from the DvsGesture dataset, the same edge features are found to be ineffective in abstraction. In addition, our results suggest that liquid state machines show promise as a computational model for the classification of DVS data with temporal dynamics. This paper is a significant contribution to advancing our understanding of biological vision and its potential applications.

This paper presents a new method for haze removal in RGB images by utilizing near infrared images and a dense stacked conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN). The deep network architecture incorporates the corresponding near infrared image to enhance the learning process of image characteristics. A triplet layer is used to enable independent learning of each channel of the visible spectrum image, facilitating the removal of haze from each color channel separately. The method employs a multiple loss function scheme that balances the learning between colors and image structures, resulting in effectively haze-free images. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach compared to a state of the art method.

The problem of finding the vertex correspondence between two noisy graphs with different number of vertices where the smaller graph is still large has many applications in social networks, neuroscience, and computer vision. We propose a solution to this problem via a graph matching matched filter: centering and padding the smaller adjacency matrix and applying graph matching methods to align it to the larger network. The centering and padding schemes can be incorporated into any algorithm that matches using adjacency matrices. Under a statistical model for correlated pairs of graphs, which yields a noisy copy of the small graph within the larger graph, the resulting optimization problem can be guaranteed to recover the true vertex correspondence between the networks. However, there are currently no efficient algorithms for solving this problem. To illustrate the possibilities and challenges of such problems, we use an algorithm that can exploit a partially known correspondence and show via varied simulations and applications to Drosophila and human connectomes that this approach can achieve good performance.

The regression testing method called Visual Regression Testing checks whether application screens display correctly without any presentation failures. This method uses image comparison tools that detect differences in screen elements, e.g. the disappearance of or change in the position of a button, by comparing images of the correct screen and the target screen by using computer vision techniques. It can detect differences in all the screens of an application automatically, but the tester needs to confirm all the differences detected in the screens. On the other hand, the application screen is often composed of areas such as the header, footer, navigation and content areas. Since the header, footer and navigation are displayed at fixed positions on a screen and commonly exist on many screens, if a difference is detected in them, the same difference will be detected in many other screens. As a result, we need labor to repeat the same confirmation for screens containing the same differences. Here, we propose a method to reduce the labor in making such confirmations by analyzing all the screen comparison results to identify the same differences so that the tester only has to confirm one screen comparison result as a representative. We confirmed the effectiveness of our method on real application screens and confirmed that it reduces the number of differences that the tester needs to confirm by about 60%.

Recommendation systems are an integral part of daily internet use, and GAN-based models have been recently proposed to enhance their performance. However, these models can be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, resulting in mode collapse. To address this issue, a new framework named Collaborative Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) has been proposed, which uses Variational Auto-encoder (VAE) as the generator and performs adversarial training in the continuous embedding space. The CGAN framework has two advantages: it uses the auto-encoder as a generator to capture the subtle latent factors underlying user-item interactions and improve model robustness through adversarial training in continuous space. Our experiments conducted on two real-world benchmark recommendation datasets demonstrate that the CGAN outperforms the state-of-the-art GAN-based models.

Melanoma skin cancer is a growing concern in today's society. Early detection is critical in increasing the chances of a successful outcome for the patient. Unfortunately, it can be difficult to distinguish melanoma from non-melanoma skin cancer accurately. Recent advancements in the classification of skin lesions using deep learning have been proposed. In this paper, we propose an improved skin lesion detection and classification strategy utilizing a convolutional neural network. Unlike traditional methods, this approach uses only the textural information of the lesion as input and not the entire image. Textural lesion is obtained through the projection of the segmented object and texture components using multi-scale decomposition. Experimental results prove that our proposed approach is superior in accuracy compared to previous literature in this field.

Aiming at the weight degeneracy phenomena in fundamental particle filter algorithm, the particle filtering algorithm improving the important samples based on generalized regression neural network (GRNN) was presented. This algorithm optimizes the samples from importance density function by GRNN. The samples of particle filter are selected as the neural network input and the observed values as the neural network target vector. The smooth factors are optimized to approach the target vector through multiple trainings, and the samples and the corresponding surrounding adjusted values are regarded as the input of the neural network after training. The best optimized values are used to replace the sample indicated by the output vector indicator of neural network. The samples are adjusted by GRNN so as to be closer to the posterior probability density. The simulation results show that the performance of particle filtering algorithm based on generalized regression neural network is better than that of basic particle filtering algorithm in terms of effective particle number and mean square error parameter. Good results have been achieved in improving the filtering precision. It is proved that the generalized regression neural network is available and effective in particle filtering algorithm.

This work develops robust diffusion recursive least-squares algorithms to mitigate the performance degradation often experienced in networks of agents in the presence of impulsive noise. The first algorithm minimizes an exponentially weighted least-squares cost function subject to a time-dependent constraint on the squared norm of the intermediate update at each node. A recursive strategy for computing the constraint is proposed using side information from the neighboring nodes to further improve the robustness. We also analyze the mean-square convergence behavior of the proposed algorithm. The second proposed algorithm is a modification of the first one based on the dichotomous coordinate descent iterations. It has a performance similar to that of the former, however, its complexity is significantly lower especially when input regressors of agents have a shift structure and it is well suited to practical implementation. Simulations show the superiority of the proposed algorithms over previously reported techniques in various impulsive noise scenarios.

Fused helical and spiral (FHS) coils have been developed as a means of improving the efficiency of wireless power transfer. To achieve this goal, both neural network and generic algorithms have been utilized to optimize the structure and parameters of FHS coils with variable pitches. FHS coils are uniquely designed to balance the coupling coefficient and the quality factor to achieve optimal performance.

A simulation conducted on a proposed 3.25mm FHS coil structure with three layers of 15 turns demonstrates the effectiveness of the design. The pitches used for each layer are 0.075mm, 0.225mm, and 0.3mm respectively. The condensed magnetic field distribution of the FHS coils results in a significant improvement of power transmission efficiency of up to 24% as compared to traditional single turn coils at a distance of 20mm.

Overall, the utilization of FHS coils and the incorporation of neural network and generic algorithms in their optimization presents a promising approach to achieving enhanced wireless power transfer efficiency.

Specialized hardware for deep learning utilizing analog memory devices has the potential to surpass conventional GPUs in terms of performance. This hardware relies on non-volatile-memory (NVM) devices arranged in arrays to carry out matrix operations necessary for deep learning in parallel and in constant time. Various implementations in the literature employ different memory element materials, such as phase-change-memory (PCM), resistive-random-access-memory (RRAM), electrochemical-random-access-memory (ECRAM), and ferroelectric devices. Although current efforts are primarily focused on demonstrating functionality, concerns about the reliability margins of this emerging technology are increasing. This paper provides a brief description of the operation and device requirements before concentrating on possible reliability issues related to variability, stability and drift, retention, and durability.

Measurement-based black box behavioral models are widely used nowadays. To handle nonlinear effects efficiently, such models often rely on approximation techniques. Polyharmonic distortion (PHD) modeling emerged as a viable approach for describing a nonlinear mapping. Typical PHD-based models, such as the well-known X-parameter model, are gained from linearization while operating on a certain large signal (LS) operational point. This limits the accuracy, especially for hard nonlinearities. However, quadratic terms can be added, which result in the quadratic PHD (QPHD) model. This enables highly accurate models for devices in strongly nonlinear operation, even in highly mismatched environments. In this paper, the accuracy of such models is investigated by predicting typical nonlinear measures, such as load-pull contours and intermodulation distortion, to assess the model accuracy for both static and dynamic stimulus. Furthermore, the LS matching problem is solved for both the X-parameter and the QPHD model. This allows to predict the optimum matching analytically, without performing load-pull analysis. To verify the accuracy of the model, the results are presented by comparing the model prediction with verification measurements for a commercially available GaN HEMT.

This paper presents an innovative surface velocity measurement system for fluids, which utilizes a multiple channel radar module with a center frequency of 77 GHz. The system is mounted above the stream and utilizes a frequency-modulated continuous-wave approach to measure the distance between the target and the radar module, the angle of arrival of the radio frequency signal, and the target velocity. This allows for the identification and separation of unwanted reflections from stationary or moving scatterers from the target of interest. The system has been successfully demonstrated through measurements taken from a channelized stream.

Mobile devices, along with wearable sensors, allow patients to access healthcare services from anywhere at any time. The longstanding constraints of computational capability and storage space on mobile devices can be alleviated by outsourcing computation- or data-intensive tasks to remote cloud centers. Thus, mobile cloud computing (MCC) has been recognized as a promising approach to provide pervasive healthcare services to people in their daily life. As the development and adoption of MCC techniques in healthcare, new optimization strategies have been explored and studied to help mobile cloud healthcare services to be deployed in a more effective and efficient manner. In this survey, we demonstrate how MCC techniques have been extensively deployed in various healthcare applications and, specifically, describe the general architecture and design considerations one should take into account while designing an MCC for healthcare scenarios. Given a large number of factors that may affect the performance of the MCC and even result in catastrophic consequences in healthcare, this paper presents the state-of-the-art optimization methods on the MCC for meeting the diverse priorities and achieving the optimal tradeoff among multiple objectives. Finally, the security and privacy issues of the MCC in healthcare are also discussed.

This paper presents the method that recognizes the road boundary situation from a single image and detects a driving lane based on the recognition result. Driving lane detection is important for lateral motion control of the vehicle and it usually realized based on lane mark detection. However, there are some roads where lane marks such as white lines are not drawn. Also, when the road is covered with snow, lane marks cannot be seen. In these cases, it's necessary to detect the boundary line between the roadside object and the road surfaces. Since traffic lanes are divided by various roadside objects, such as curbs, grass, walls and so on, it's difficult to detect all kinds of road boundary including lane marks by a single algorithm. Therefore, we propose the method which changes the driving lane detection method according to the road boundary situation. At first, the situation of the road boundary is identified as some classes, such as white line, curb, grass and so on, by the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Then, based on this result, the lane mark or the boundary between the road surface and the roadside object is detected as the lane boundary. When a clear lane mark is drawn on a road, this situation is identified as a class of "White line" and a lane mark is detected as a lane boundary. On the other hand, when a lane mark is not present, this situation is identified as the other class and the boundary of the roadside object corresponding to the identified class is detected as the lane boundary. Experimental results using the KITTI dataset and our own dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed method. In addition, the result of the proposed method is compared with the boundary of the road area extracted by some semantic segmentation method.

State space search is a technique used in the field of computer science, specifically artificial intelligence (AI), where a series of progressive designs or conditions of an event are studied in order to find an objective state that has a desired property. While this approach has a wide range of applications, including motion planning and heuristic use with design information, AND/OR charts, among others, the main objective of this paper is to apply the Multi-Heuristic Planner to a 3D environment. This particular framework is built on the belief that multiple searches, each with different inadmissible heuristics, can guide an object towards its desired goal in such a way that completion is ensured, while sub-optimality bounds are preserved.

The ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting technology has recently been regarded as a potential solution for powering the wireless sensor networks (WSNs). However, the ultra-low power density of ambient RF energy is the main impediment to its further application. In this paper, we propose a novel energy efficient cooperative communication scheme (EECCS), which combines energy beamforming communication and ambient backscatter communication, to overcome the energy problem of WSNs powered by ambient RF energy harvesting. Moreover, to further reduce the energy consumption of nodes, we present an optimal resource allocation problem for EECCS. It can be formulated as a signomial geometric programming (SGP), which is nonconvex and NP-hard. We develop a Sequential Convex Approximation (SCA) algorithm for finding a solution of this SGP problem, which transforms the SGP problem into a sequence of geometric programming (GP) problems that are convex. The simulation results indicate that the EECCS can improve the energy efficiency of the ambient RF powered WSNs and maximize the total amount of data received by the sink.

This paper introduces a novel C-band Hybrid Semiconductor Integrated Circuit (HySIC) rectifier that employs a Gallium Nitride (GaN) Shottky barrier diode and silicon (Si) matching circuit to facilitate RF energy harvesting. The main objective of the HySIC rectifier is to provide power to drive wireless sensor network systems in spacecraft applications. The development of this small-size, low-cost, and highly functional rectifier was made possible by the combination of GaN and Si materials, which exhibit high resistivity to cosmic rays and excellent integration technology, respectively. 

To fabricate the HySIC rectifier, the GaN diode was subjected to rigorous testing, and the measurement results were used to guide the design and production of the rectifier. The final size of the rectifier was 3.9 mm x 8.1 mm, and it was observed to have a maximum conversion efficiency of 21.7% in the C-band. 

In summary, the successful development of the HySIC rectifier with GaN Shottky barrier diode and Si matching circuit represents a significant milestone towards the realization of efficient RF energy harvesting for wireless sensor network systems in spacecraft. This technology has the potential to significantly reduce the cost and complexity of space missions while also extending the operational capabilities of spacecraft.

In this paper, we consider the problem of building descriptive three-dimensional (3-D) maps from sparse and noisy range sensor data. We expand our previously proposed method leveraging Bayesian kernel inference for prediction of occupancy in locations not directly observed by a range sensor. In this paper, we show that our kernel inference approach generalizes previous “counting sensor model” approaches from discrete occupancy grids to continuous maps. Our approach enables prediction about occupancy in regions unobserved by the range sensor based on local measurements, and smoothly transitions to a prior in regions lacking sufficient data for reliable inference. Furthermore, we demonstrate quantitatively using simulated data that the mapping performance of our method can be improved by considering rays as continuous observations, rather than sampling discrete free-space point observations along rays. Though the maps produced by our method are in principle continuous, discretizing space affords us several computational advantages, including the ability to apply recursive Bayesian updates, that allow us to perform inference very efficiently, even on large datasets. To demonstrate this advantage, we present experimental results applying this method to large-scale lidar data collected with a ground robot, showing real-time performance. Other field robotics applications, including underwater 3-D mapping with sonar, are explored qualitatively.

In this study, we examine the effectiveness of histogram-based features- the asynchronous amplitude histogram (AAH) and the IQ histogram (IQH)- in monitoring optical signal performance in coherent optical systems. Our research utilizes a dimensionality reduction technique, t-distribution stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE), and investigates the conditions under which optical channel impairments can be monitored. We found that under certain conditions, the histogram-based features may not be able to distinguish between high and low impairment effects, rendering them ineffective for certain cases. Our extensive simulations indicate that both AAH and IQH can be used to monitor all types of single impairments except for phase noise in the case of AAH. Additionally, under multiple impairments, it is challenging to monitor optical signal-to-noise ratio and chromatic dispersion values, especially in the case of concurrent presence of more than two impairments. The study's validity is confirmed by the quantitative measure of estimation results obtained using linear support vector machine (SVM) regression, which matches the separability investigation using t-SNE to a great extent.

An advanced method for intelligent diagnosis of rotary equipment has been proposed, which utilizes multi-sensor data-fusion and an improved deep convolutional neural network (CNN) models. The LeNet-5 based CNN has been improved with the addition of bottleneck layers, which enhances the features of the samples while maintaining their size. A new approach has been introduced for transforming multi-sensor vibration signals into color images using the RGB color space, which improves the feature refinement and amplifies the differences between various types of fault signals. The network is evaluated using t-SNE for visual clustering in the final stage of network learning. The proposed method has been validated by diagnosing the wind power test rigs and industrial fan system with a prediction accuracy of 99.89% and 99.77%, respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been compared with other baseline approaches such as deep belief network and support vector machine (SVM) for efficiency. The results suggest that the proposed intelligent diagnosis method based on multi-sensor data-fusion and CNN offers higher prediction accuracy and better visualization clustering effects.

It is known that in the simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) problem when a robot's orientation is known, an estimation of the history of its poses can be formulated as a standard linear least squares problem. In this letter, we exploit this property of SLAM to develop a robust pose-graph SLAM framework that uses absolute orientation sensing. Our contribution are as follows: 1) we show that absolute orientation can be estimated using local structural cues; and 2) we develop a method to incorporate absolute orientation measurements in both the front and back-end of pose-graph SLAM. We also demonstrate our approach through extensive simulations and a physical real-world demonstration along with comparisons against existing state-of-the-art solvers that do not use absolute orientation.

Disasters are a frequent occurrence in Indonesia due to geographical factors like tectonic plate movements which can cause earthquakes. Earthquakes have a far-reaching impact in a short period, making them unpredictable and posing significant dangers to human lives. Therefore, it is crucial to locate victims quickly and comprehensively after a disaster. In this paper, we propose a victims detection framework starting from the acquisition of images using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and processing them through a convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect victims robustly in post-disaster scenarios.

The victim detection framework involves acquiring images of the affected area using UAVs and transmitting them to a victim detector dedicated ground station server. The server processes the images using a CNN to identify the possibility of victims in the area. To test our framework in real-time, we developed a simulation system mimicking a real environment. Additionally, we developed a transmission protocol for effectively transmitting data between the robot and the server.

Unlike human detection processes, our proposed framework requires additional pre-processing stages to increase the variation in the dataset to improve victim detection accuracy. We use an embedded system to capture images and sensor data such as location and time using the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS).

In conclusion, our proposed victims' detection framework can help locate victims and streamline the search process after disasters. By leveraging technology like UAVs, CNNs, and GNSS, we can increase effectiveness and speed in detecting victims, ultimately saving more lives.

Natural and man-made disasters pose an ever-present threat to our community and society. Effective information and communication platform are important for disaster response. However, under disaster scenarios, network infrastructure, such as power grid, cellular tower and backbone networks can be damaged. In addition, the communication channels often become congested by exceptionally high levels of data traffic, as people impacted by the disaster are trying to contact with their family and friends and seeking for help; disaster responders are working to deploy rescue resources, and lots of citizens are broadcasting the disaster by uploading pictures or videos. In this paper, we propose an emergency information platform that is suitable for a challenged environment where the traditional communication paradigms either completely fail or poorly perform. We utilize the vast deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) and citizens in the community to bring benefits in terms of data network resilience in face of disaster. In particular, we propose a software-defined communication network that combines IoT technology, Fog computing, Cloud computing, peer-to-peer computing and delay-tolerant network together to enable an effective emergency-response information platform. It integrates the power of community, and citizen with IoT devices and existing partially damaged communication platform to address critical disaster communication problems.

With advancements in cloud manufacturing technology, the Manufacturing Service Ecosystem (MSE) has emerged as a complex cyber-social system. The community of manufacturers (social layer) is driven by the service strategy (cyber layer), but the initial conditions of the manufacturing community also affect the performance of the service strategy. In order to ensure the desired evolution of the MSE, it is essential to establish a feedback mechanism between heterogeneous networks. However, analyzing and controlling the possible evolution directions of the MSE has become a significant challenge.

To address this challenge, this paper proposes a research framework based on parallel system theory to study the evolution and control of the MSE. The framework involves constructing the corresponding digital system of MSE from the perspective of supply and demand matching. Furthermore, specific computational experiments are performed to determine the effect of different service strategies (cyber layer) and initial conditions (social layer) on the evolution of MSE. The experiment results are compared with real data, confirming the reliability of the proposed approach.

The research framework presented in this paper offers a new method for analyzing the complexity of the MSE. By clarifying the feedback mechanism between heterogeneous networks, the evolution of the MSE can be effectively controlled, promoting its growth in the intended direction.

An increasing number of organizations choose distributed green data centers (DGDCs) and use their infrastructure resources to deploy and manage multiple applications that flexibly provide services to users around the world in a cost-effective way. The dramatic growth of tasks makes it highly challenging to maximize the total profit of a DGDC provider in a market, where the revenue, price of power grid, solar radiation, wind speed, the maximum amount of energy, on-site air density, and the number of servers in DGDCs all vary with geographical sites. Different from existing studies, this paper designs a profit-sensitive spatial scheduling (PS3) approach to maximize the total profit of a DGDC provider by smartly scheduling all tasks of multiple applications to meet their response time constraints. PS3 can well utilize such spatial diversity of the above factors. In each time slot, the profit maximization for the DGDC provider is formulated as a constrained nonlinear program and solved by the proposed genetic-simulated-annealing-based particle swarm optimization. Real-life trace-driven simulation experiments demonstrate that PS3 realizes higher total profit and throughput than two typical task scheduling methods. Note to Practitioners-This paper investigates the profit maximization problem for a DGDC provider, while the average response time of all arriving tasks of each application is within their corresponding constraint. Existing task scheduling approaches fail to jointly consider the spatial variations in many factors, including the revenue, price of power grid, solar radiation, wind speed, the maximum amount of energy, on-site air density, and the number of servers in DGDCs. Consequently, they cannot schedule all tasks of multiple applications within their response time constraints in a profit-sensitive way. In this paper, a profit-sensitive spatial scheduling (PS3) method that tackles the drawbacks of previous approaches is presented. It is achieved by adopting a proposed genetic-simulated-annealing-based particle swarm optimization algorithm that solves a constrained nonlinear program. Simulation experiments prove that compared with two typical scheduling approaches, it increases the total profit and throughput. It can be readily realized and incorporated into real-life industrial DGDCs. The future work should improve the proposed method by analyzing the indeterminacy in green energy and the uncertainty in tasks.

The relational database service in cloud usually achieves energy efficiency by using virtualization technology, in which it consolidates multiple independent database systems into a single physical machine while enforcing the hardware-level isolation among them. However, the disk I/O performance is inevitably hurt due to the resource contention on the shared device. We propose VMSQL, a novel disk I/O model for the virtualized relational database management system (RDBMS). VMSQL has two innovations over the original disk model of virtualized database systems. First, VMSQL enforces the synchronous operation in guest operating system to handle with the transaction commitment. Due to its simplicity, a portion of CPU cycles is decoupled from I/O buffer management and then used to serve the upcoming requests, thereby improving their response times. Second, in host system, VMSQL asynchronizes the storage path of transactions which are committed from the different co-located guest databases. An obvious advantage of this procedure is that systems can apply host-level improvements into the disk I/O performance of virtualized RDBMS, relieving the random I/O and enhancing the throughput of whole system. We implement a prototype of this Sync-Async model in QEMU-KVM hypervisor, in which the InnoDB engine is deployed in the guest operating system. Extensive experiments are conducted to verify its advantages and the results are positive without any loss of ACID-compliance. In the meanwhile, VMSQL incurs moderate overhead at the hypervisor layer.

This paper introduces a novel method to assess the social activity maintained by psychiatric patients using information and communication technologies. In particular, we model the daily usage patterns of phone calls and social and communication apps using point processes. We propose a novel nonhomogeneous Poisson process model with periodic (circadian) intensity function using a truncated Fourier series expansion, which is inferred using a trust-region algorithm. We also extend the model using a mixture of periodic intensity functions to cope with the different daily patterns of a person. The analysis of the usage of phone calls and social and communication apps of a cohort of 259 patients reveals common patterns shared among patients with relatively high homogeneity and differences among patient pathologies.

Hand gesture recognition is a prominent field in the domain of computer vision, which offers enhanced and convenient human-computer interaction. The proficiency of hand gesture recognition is highly reliant on the representation of hand gestures. In this article, we propose a novel approach for measuring the similarities between hand gestures, which can be exploited for hand gesture recognition. Our approach utilizes the depth maps of hand gestures, which are captured via Kinect sensors. This approach enables the segmentation of 3D hand shapes without the influence of the background clutter. 

To extract the patterns of the significant 3D shape features, we propose a new descriptor termed as 3D Shape Context for 3D hand gesture representation. The descriptor is used to gather Shape Context information from every 3D point in multiple scales, since both local and global shape distributions are critical for recognition. The collective description of all the 3D points constructs the representation of the hand gesture, and dynamic time warping algorithm is utilized for exploring hand gesture recognition. 

We conducted extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets to verify the efficacy of our proposed method. The experimental results demonstrate that our method is robust to noise, articulated variations, and rigid transformations. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, our method exceeds in terms of accuracy and efficiency. 

Overall, our proposed method offers an innovative approach for hand gesture recognition that can facilitate more natural and intuitive human-computer interaction.

This paper presents nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) for nonlinear systems and applies it to the inverted pendulum. A key distinction between optimal control and NMPC is that optimal control aims to minimize the cost function over a finite horizon and applies a control input to the system, while NMPC employs state feedback and updates the control input at each time step. At each sampling time, the control design of NMPC is formulated as a two-point boundary-value (TPBV) problem. When calculating the optimal control law, only the first control input is applied to the controlled system.

To solve the TPBV problem, we employ an iterative steepest descent algorithm. Numerical results show a comparison between optimal control and NMPC applied to the inverted pendulum.

We present a denotational semantics for a simple concurrent language based on Milner's CCS extended with multiparty synchronous interactions. We show that our denotational model is weakly abstract with respect to a corresponding operational semantics. The denotational semantics is designed with metric spaces and continuation semantics for concurrency. The significance of the results presented in this paper is given also by the flexibility provided by the continuations technique.

Robotic navigation and automatic geocoding of businesses require artificial agents to rapidly and accurately recognize words in natural images. To tackle this challenge, we developed a deep learning method for recognizing words from different languages in captured images with high accuracy and with fewer captured samples. Our experiments yielded three main findings. 
Firstly, we directly fed images of words as inputs to the neural network, omitting segmentation and post-processing steps to avoid compound errors, and found this method to be successful for our samples. 
Secondly, we were able to train machine learning models to recognize words using purely synthetic training samples by applying feature extractions to both training and testing datasets before passing them through deep networks. This achievement enables us to train neural networks inexpensively on synthetic data and transfer knowledge to recognize words in real data. 
Lastly, we conducted experiments to compare model performance using Canny edge detection and Chu's 3D thinning algorithm as preprocessing methods and found that Canny edge detection performed better in the majority of cases.

With the advancement of smarter technologies in cellular networks, substantial portions of the bands used for lower versions have remained unoccupied. To maximize the use of these white spaces in existing cellular networks, this work proposes a new paradigm of cognitive radio. The nodes of a self-organized opportunistic ad hoc network are utilized as secondary users (SUs) to access the unused spectrum. SUs are free to move around and coordinate with neighboring SUs to gather reliable information on the channels of the primary network for cognitive use of the licensed spectrum. By employing distributed techniques of collaboration among SUs for channel allocation, the system eliminates the need for any centralized control, improving channel utilization and throughput. 

Moreover, to enhance the spectrum latency, the reinforcement learning technique is applied for better channel estimation. Simulation studies validate that the proposed approaches considerably improve call drop/block rates and enhance Quality of Service (QoS) compared to existing methods. In terms of overhead, the additional message costs of the proposed techniques are negligible.

The output tracking problem for a class of nonlinear systems presented in Nonlinear Block Controllable (NBC) form is addressed. Both matched and unmatched perturbations are considered. First, the Block Control iterative feedback linearization technique combined with a perturbation estimation are employed to design a sliding manifold. With the perturbation estimation, the effect of unmatched perturbation is mitigated. Then, a discrete-time sliding mode controller is synthesized such that the system state is driven toward a vicinity of the designed sliding manifold and stays there for all sampled time instants, avoiding chattering and reducing the matched perturbation effect. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is confirmed by simulation.

Gene order evolution of unichromosomal genomes, for example mitochondrial genomes, has been modelled mostly by four major types of genome rearrangements: inversions, transpositions, inverse transpositions, and tandem duplication random losses. Generalizing models that include all those rearrangements while admitting computational tractability are rare. In this paper, we study such a rearrangement model, namely the inverse tandem duplication random loss (iTDRL) model, where an iTDRL duplicates and inverts a continuous segment of a gene order followed by the random loss of one of the redundant copies of each gene. The iTDRL rearrangement has currently been proposed by several authors suggesting it to be a possible mechanisms of mitochondrial gene order evolution. We initiate the algorithmic study of this new model of genome rearrangement by proving that a shortest rearrangement scenario that transforms one given gene order into another given gene order can be obtained in quasilinear time. Furthermore, we show that the length of such a scenario, i.e., the minimum number of iTDRLs in the transformation, can be computed in linear time.

Image translation is a type of problem that focuses on learning how to map an input image from one domain to an output image in another domain. This technique has been used in various applications, including unsupervised training, data augmentation, and domain adaptation.

However, the lack of paired training data can make image translation a difficult problem to solve. To address this issue, we propose a straightforward image translation model that includes a single generator with a self-regularization term and an adversarial term. This approach constrains the problem by assuming that the translated image must look similar to the original image while appearing to have come from the new domain.

We also noticed that existing image translation techniques tend to introduce unwanted changes or artifacts into the input, which can impact the output's quality. To address this problem, we propose a solution that adds an attention module to predict an attention map. This module is designed to attend to specific parts of the input image while leaving other areas unaltered. Therefore, it avoids undesired artifacts or changes in the output image.

Our extensive experiments and evaluations demonstrate that our model outperforms existing image translation methods while being simpler. Therefore, this technique can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of image translation in various applications.

Recently, counterfeiting of semiconductors has become an increasing concern, leading to a need for countermeasures such as Physical Unclonable Function (PUF). Among the PUF techniques, ring oscillator (RO) PUFs have gained popularity. However, Genetic Programming (GP) based attacks have been proposed to compromise the tamper resistance of RO PUFs. These attacks only utilize basic genetic strategies, and a more accurate evaluation of tamper resistance for RO PUFs is required. To address this issue, this study proposes an advanced attack that uses dynamic adaptive mutation and is based on GP, ensuring improved accuracy for evaluating the tamper resistance of RO PUFs.

The demand for indoor location-based services is on the rise, and as a result, the received signal strength fingerprinting-based localization algorithm has gained attention due to its accuracy and low hardware requirements. However, achieving accurate location discovery under the sparse reference points condition remains challenging. This paper proposes a solution to this problem with three contributions. First, the Voronoi diagram is utilized to regionalize the positioning area and create a distributed signal propagation description, which reduces the influence of environmental interference. Second, a region-based location search model is established to achieve initial position estimation and provide a motion model for subsequent optimization of location estimation to track local motion accurately. Finally, the regularized particle filtering algorithm with map-correction is employed to minimize the cumulative error caused by environmental noise and local optimum problems. To confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, an indoor wireless experiment system is designed, and experiment results show improved positioning accuracy by 28.2% compared to the fingerprinting-based localization algorithm when the RPs density is reduced to 0.2/ (0.5m*0.5m).

The initialization is one of the less reliable pieces of Visual-Inertial SLAM (VI-SLAM) and Odometry (VI-O). The estimation of the initial state (camera poses, IMU states and landmark positions) from the first data readings lacks the accuracy and robustness of other parts of the pipeline, and most algorithms have high failure rates and/or initialization delays up to tens of seconds. Such initialization is critical for AR systems, as the failures and delays of the current approaches can ruin the user experience or mandate impractical guided calibration. In this paper we address the state initialization problem using a monocular-inertial sensor setup, the most common in AR platforms. Our contributions are 1) a general linear formulation to obtain an initialization seed, and 2) a non-linear optimization scheme, including gravity, to refine the seed. Our experimental results, in a public dataset, show that our approach improves the accuracy and robustness of current VI state initialization schemes.

The lack of communication between local authorities, first aid responders, and the population present in a natural disaster area is a critical issue that can jeopardize relief efforts aimed at saving human lives. During natural disasters such as earthquakes and tsunamis, the telecommunication network infrastructure in the affected area may be damaged or inoperable, severely compromising the efficiency of first aid operations. 

This paper proposes a device-to-device (D2D)-based framework that can facilitate communication from a disaster area towards a functional area, using basic victim device information such as positions and battery level. The framework, which is utilized by a base station located in a functional area, organizes users in the disaster area into clusters and selects a gateway for each cluster. It also evaluates the optimal transmission power for each gateway to maximize energy efficiency and create a multi-hop path from the disaster area to a relay node, minimizing end-to-end delay. 

Simulation results carried out indicate that our proposed approach outperforms random policy assignment and static policies assignment, both in power allocation and routing path creations. This proposed framework enhances communication between local authorities, first aid responders, and disaster victims, thereby increasing the efficiency of relief operations aimed at saving human lives.

This paper demonstrates a possible application of the Moving Path Following (MPF) motion control approach applied to the marine environment. Specifically, the problem of target estimation and tracking using Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is considered, wherein the robotic vehicle is equipped with a ranging sensor in order to localize a possibly moving target. Such a problem bears a strong resemblance to the single beacon navigation problem, in which the AUV is expected to execute state and input trajectories that renders the target states observable. To this end, control laws are proposed for an AUV to follow a geometric path, that is stationary with respect to the moving target, leading to the MPF problem. The geometric path is chosen such that the target states are observable. An extended Kalman filter is utilized to estimate the target position and velocity using range-only measurements. The efficacy of the MPF approach is illustrated through a source localization and tracking scenario in simulations.

Event detection is a crucial function for decision makers to stay informed about real-world events. Social media platforms like Twitter play a significant role in our daily lives and have emerged as a valuable source of information for political and social events. However, event detection from Arabic tweets has not received much attention from researchers. In this study, we employed the Python Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) library to construct two classifiers for filtering and detecting extracted events from Arabic tweets. 

The first classifier utilizes a two-pass approach to filter out irrelevant tweets. The first pass identifies hashtags that are commonly associated with event-related tweets, while the second pass analyzes the content of the tweets using a shallow analysis. The second classifier analyzes the text extracted from the tweets and detects events of interest.

To highlight the effectiveness of our approach, we present the tragic events of the Jordan flash floods near the Dead Sea as a case study. Our model successfully filtered all the collected tweets and identified those that described the incidents in the impacted region. By analyzing the data, we gained important insights and lessons for future prevention and mitigation efforts.

Our proposed solution can be generalized and adapted to other event detection problems, providing valuable information to support decision making in various domains.

Although significant progress has been made in deep face recognition, concerns have arisen around racial and gender bias in these models, which has raised questions about their suitability for deployment in sensitive scenarios. In this study, the demographic imbalance of popular public face datasets was quantified for the first time, in terms of identity, gender, and ethnicity. Additionally, a new validation set called DemogPairs was publicly released, featuring 10.8K facial images and 58.3M identity verification pairs, distributed according to demographically-balanced folds of Asian, Black, and White females and males. Using DemogPairs, experiments were carried out to analyze the cross-demographic behavior of state-of-the-art deep face recognition models (SphereFace, FaceNet, and ResNet50). The experimental results showed that the studied models suffered from a structured and damaging demographic bias. This study highlights the need for novel testing protocols to validate the generalization capabilities of face recognition models appropriately.

Accurate and automated segmentation of organs is crucial for computer-aided analysis in medical diagnostic and treatment planning. While state-of-the-art methods have achieved impressive results with larger organs like liver and kidneys, smaller organs such as the pancreas, gallbladder, and adrenal glands are more challenging, especially with limited training data. This paper introduces an automatic approach for small organ segmentation with limited training data using two discrete steps of localization and segmentation.

In the localization step, a region of interest (ROI) is extracted after registering images to a common template. A graph-based groupwise image registration method is proposed to build the template, which minimizes the potential bias and avoids getting a fuzzy template. During the segmentation stage, a novel knowledge-aided convolutional neural network is proposed to achieve better segmentation results. This network combines both deep learning and traditional methods, thus achieving more accurate segmentation compared to individual methods.

Experimental results using the ISBI 2015 VISCERAL challenge dataset show that the proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, traditional forest-based approaches, and multiatlas approaches in small organ segmentation. This research presents an important contribution towards improving computer-aided medical analysis involving small organs with limited training data.

Improving the development and utilization of renewable energy is a critical goal in China's green industrial revolution. To accomplish this task, measuring energy efficiency and determining the factors that influence it are vital issues. This paper applies feature recognition to determine the key factors that affect energy efficiency. Utilizing a dataset of 24 provinces and cities in China, data mining methods are used to derive knowledge. In the process, three problems are addressed: (1) selecting the optimal subset of features that affect energy efficiency, (2) evaluating energy efficiency based on the optimal feature subset, and (3) predicting China's energy efficiency using seven good-fitted classification models with accuracy rates above 90%. Combining the results of feature selection and energy efficiency prediction, a strategy and policy to improve energy efficiency in China is suggested. It is recommended that each province implement green energy policies and institutions that focus on energy efficiency to improve their energy consumption structures. Additionally, it is important to coordinate the development of traditional and renewable energy.

Based on the background of DC normal education project in the Jinji Lake core area of Suzhou Industrial Park, this paper discusses the key technologies in the practice of multi-terminal DC power distribution technology engineering. Firstly, the basic situation of Suzhou four-terminal DC project was outlined, and the key electrical equipment and its selection principle were analyzed, including the converter valves, bridge arm reactors, link transformers, and DC monitoring and protection systems. Secondly, based on the RTLAB real-time simulation platform, the simulation model of Suzhou four-terminal DC distribution system was built. Finally, based on the RTLAB simulation model, single-ended converter startup, four-terminal stable operation, active power step and reactive power step were simulated. The simulation results show that the four-terminal DC grid model has good steady state performance and active power and reactive power step response performance. It can provide reference for the future DC distribution network construction.

In this paper, we present a false alarm reduction algorithm for Ventricular Tachycardia (VT) arrhythmias in intensive care unit (ICU) using multivariate statistical process control (MSPC) and frequency analysis of electrocardiogram (ECG) signal. First, we decompose the ECG signal into three different frequency bands. The ECG beats are detected, and VT beats are labeled. In the next step, several features consist of time domain features, bispectrum features, and Poincaré plot features are extracted from ECG Signal The extracted feature vector of each ECG beat is monitored using MSPC for detecting anomalies. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using the Ventricular Tachycardia cases of 2015 Physionet challenge database. This dataset consists of 2 ECG channel, arterial blood pressure (ABP) and/or photoplethysmograph (PPG) signal, and an alarm annotation for each record. The obtained sensitivity and specificity were 86.5%, and 80.7% respectively. We have also investigated the advantage of using ABP signal in improving the results of false alarm reduction. For this purpose, some biological features are extracted from ABP and used as an extra feature vector. Results show that using ABP signal can improve the performance of the algorithm.

One of the main challenges in tunnel construction is predicting the geological conditions before excavation to ensure the safety of the construction process. This paper proposes a data-driven framework for real-time interpreting the operating data of tunnel boring machines (TBMs) without interrupting tunneling operations, and eventually automate the tunneling operation. 

To exhaustively explore the inherent characteristics of TBM operating data, the framework converts the indexes of the original data from discontinuous operating time to continuous operating displacement. After screening outliers, features are augmented by using the first-order and the second-order difference information. 

Developing a desired geological-type predictor raises two main concerns. Firstly, since multiple geological types could exist in one tunnel section, the predictor should have multiple outputs. Secondly, since the geological types are specified by the values of 7 kinds of physical-mechanical indexes of geological types, this geological characteristic should also be encoded into the predictor's structure. 

A feed-forward multiple-output artificial neural network (ANN) with two hidden layers is designed as the predictor, where the second hidden layer has 7 nodes corresponding to the 7 kinds of physical-mechanical indexes. The experimental results show that the feature augmentation (FA) method improves the prediction performance. The ANN predictor has the best performance on the test set when the second hidden layer has 7 nodes. The proposed ANN predictor outperforms many widely-used learning models, e.g., XGboost, random forest (RF), and support vector regression (SVR). The predictor is capable of accurately predicting the geological types of stratum.

The exhaustion of the capacity of conventional optical systems based on standard single-mode fibers (SSMF) requires new solutions cope with the exponential traffic increase. In this scenario, transmission by few-mode fibers (FMFs) appears as a strong candidate. These systems require adaptive digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms with multiple inputs and multiple outputs (MIMO) at the receiver in order to recover the signals multiplexed in the various spatial and polarization modes. However, proper functioning of these equalizers requires the pre-compensation of chromatic dispersion (CD) in the receiver using static filters. Since the DSP algorithms in mode-multiplexed systems have a slow convergence, the typical scanning algorithms become difficult to apply. In this work, we investigate the applicability of an algorithm based on the auto-correlation of the signal power waveform to estimate the CD in FMF systems. The results indicate an algorithm vulnerability with the increase of the inter-mode crosstalk level.

Finite mixture models are widely applied in various domains of applications. They assist to analyze datasets, achieve better insight into the nature of data, discover latent patterns and provide critical knowledge that we are looking for. The main focus in past works was on Gaussian statistical models, however there are several applications involving asymmetric and non-Gaussian data. Parameter estimation is one of the essential and fundamental challenges of statistical researches. Some deterministic approaches such as expectation maximization (EM) have been mainly considered as effective techniques to deal with this issue. In this article, we introduce a bivariate Beta distribution with three parameters as our main parent distribution which could be applied in skin detection and image segmentation. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated by experimental results that concern both artificial and real datasets.

Conversion of existing image and video content to High Dynamic Range (HDR) using inverse Tone Mapping Operators (iTMOs) is expected to enable the HDR market and open new market opportunities for studios and content owners. In this paper, we propose a high contrast video iTMO that addresses shortcomings of existing approaches, yielding HDR video quality worth the expectations of the emerging HDR technology. Our approach is content adaptive and is able to convert SDR videos to HDR videos of any target dynamic range. Our approach follows the Human Visual System (HVS) characteristic of being more sensitive to luminance changes in dark areas than bright and normal ones, mapping each of these areas accordingly. Our subjective evaluations demonstrate that our proposed method on average outperforms existing iTMOs in terms of overall HDR visual quality.

This paper presents an investigation into the performance of a single-phase inverter connected to the grid for optimal photovoltaic transfer. The study employs sliding-mode variable structure systems and a fuzzy logic control method optimized through particle swarm algorithm (PSO) techniques, along with a boost converter for extracting Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). The effectiveness of the proposed control strategies is verified through simulation using Matlab/Simulink software under different environmental and operating conditions, thus demonstrating the satisfactory performance of the system.

Receding Horizon Control (RHC) is a very effective control methodology which has been employed in an extensive range of industrial applications. However, most of the stability results involve terminal costs or constraints which are sometimes not computationally desirable. In this work, it is shown that the smoothness of the value function is sufficient to ensure stability for control affine systems under RHC laws with no terminal cost or constraint. In order to find the infimum for all stabilizing horizons, an ODE problem based on the linearized system is developed that provides the set of stabilizing and destabilizing horizons. It is shown that the infimum of stabilizing horizons can be estimated without the need to solve the nonlinear optimal control problem, and that subject to certain conditions the exact infimum can be obtained. Simulations are provided to illustrate the application of these methods to some nonlinear systems.

Direction-based methods have become a popular choice for palmprint recognition due to their impressive results. However, there has been a lack of research analyzing the discrepancies among different direction-based models and determining the most significant direction feature extraction for palmprints. In this study, we aim to establish a connection between the discriminability of direction features and the direction feature extraction model. We propose a new model, the exponential and Gaussian fusion model (EGM), which captures the discriminative power of various directions. This model offers crucial insights into picking the optimal direction feature selection of palmprints. Furthermore, we introduce the local discriminant direction binary pattern (LDDBP) to represent the direction features of a palmprint fully. LDDBP-based descriptors can be formed by utilizing the most discriminant directions determined by the EGM for palmprint recognition. The LDDBP model performs better than other state-of-the-art direction-based models on four widespread palmprint databases, as shown by our extensive experimental results.

Soccer video event identification has been an interesting task in research community during past few decades. Numerous machine learning techniques and C2D (Convolution 2-dimensional) have been used for this problem, but C3D has not been implemented for this task. By taking advantage from C3D (Convolution 3-dimensional), to completely exploit spatio-temporal relation, deep convolution network is developed to highlight distinct video events in proposed research work. Initially, we detect soccer video event marks by pixel differencing and edge change ratio. After this semantic features of segmented frames are extracted followed by CNN to map soccer event categories: Corner, Shoot, Goal Attempt, Penalty Kick. Because no effective and suitable dataset is available, we categorized soccer videos into four classes and developed soccer videos dataset for training CNN network. Evaluation results on soccer match clips generated results with high efficiency.

The task of underwater target tracking is one of the most important challenges in recent upsurge of smart aquaculture, especially in the application of AI-driven cage culture. However, tracking often requires short computational time and draws little attention from researchers in the field of deep learning. A convolutional network tracker (CNT) was proposed [1], which uses 2D features of local structure and internal geometric layout information between the target candidates in adjacent frames to address the tracking tasks without pre-training. In [14], an improved version of CNT (called Fast-CNT) was proposed for performing underwater multi-target tracking. This paper further proposes a 3D version of CNT (called 3D-CNT) characterized by extracting spatiotemporal features between successive frames to make the target (e.g. fish) template more robust in tracking. Experimental results show that with these temporal features, 3D-CNT outperforms the Fast-CNT in tracking moving fish.

Steganography, the practice of concealing messages in plain sight, is a highly sought-after skill in covert communication. In order to achieve high undetectability, minimal distortion embedding is a popular framework for adaptive steganography. Distortion function plays a crucial role in this framework, and a novel distortion is proposed for audio steganography in this paper. The proposed distortion takes into account the fragility of low amplitude audio samples, and it is inversely proportional to the amplitude. To resist strong steganalysis, the derivative filter is utilized to acquire the residual of audio, which is important in defining the distortion. Experimental results show that the proposed distortion outperforms state-of-the-art methods in defending against strong steganalytic methods. The authors also proposed non-additive extensions of the proposed method, which take into account mutual impact caused by embedding modification. The results of the extension experiments show that in most cases, the proposed non-additive extensions achieve higher levels of security than the original methods.

The aim of our research was to elaborate the current concept of the IoT based on the scientific papers up to now and to draw up the potential legal and security risks, which may affect the users or the state. We categorized the challenges of the IoT usage. The main problems in the aspect of data protection, are traceability and confidentiality issues.

In this paper, we develop computationally efficient and theoretically justified tools for analyzing high dimensional brain signals. Our approach is to extract the optimal lower dimensional representations for each brain region and then characterize and estimate connectivity between regions through these factors. This approach is motivated by our observation that electroencephalograms (EEGs) from many channels within each region exhibit a high degree of multicollinearity and synchrony thereby suggesting that it would be sensible to extract summary factors for each region. Here, the summary factors are the encodings that lead to the lowest reconstruction error. We focus on two special cases of linear auto encoder and decoder. The first characterizes the factors as instantaneous linear mixing of the observed signals. In the second approach, the factors are convolutions of the observed signals (which is more general than the first). These methods were compared through simulations under different conditions and the results provide insights on advantages and limitations of each. Finally, we performed exploratory analysis of resting state EEG data. The spectral properties of the factors were estimated and connectivity between regions via the factors using coherence measures were computed. We implemented these methods in a Matlab toolbox XHiDiTS (https://goo.gl/uXc8ei). The toolbox was utilized to investigate consistency of these factors across all epochs during the entire resting-state period.

In this paper, we explore resource management for radio access network slicing from user access control and wireless bandwidth allocation perspectives. Our aim is to ensure users’ quality of service (QoS), and we propose two admission control (AC) policies that can select admissible users. These policies take into account optimizing the QoS and the number of serving users, respectively. To further optimize bandwidth utilization for selected admissible users, we investigate the slice association and bandwidth allocation (SABA) problem. We propose both network-centric and user equipment (UE) centric SABA policies. Our numerical results demonstrate that our proposed AC and SABA policies significantly outperform traditional policies in terms of wireless bandwidth utilization and the number of admissible users across typical scenarios.

Controlling industrial processes that have multiple input and single manipulated variables can be a daunting task for automatic models. This is especially true for processes related to gas extraction or transport. Therefore, the research presented in this article focuses on developing a control algorithm based on artificial neural networks to identify an industrial process using historical records and knowledge from the operation itself. The output of the identification stage is then used to feed a classic PID controller to perform control actions, thereby creating a hybrid controller. 

To achieve this, an actuator or final control element is modeled, which estimates its space-state dynamic equation. With the estimated model, a local control loop is created to control the main process or manipulated variable. To test the proposed control algorithm, the process of gas transport in a copper smelter plant was chosen. The necessary data and scenarios were obtained from this plant for testing the control algorithm.

The application of this control strategy attempts to provide a solution to problems inherent in manual control, such as multiple key variables coexisting in a system, mechanical stress in equipment due to manual actions, etc. The computer simulation made with real process data shows that the proposed control signals improve the transient periods of the final actuators, and these technologies can be implemented in both an existing plant hardware/software or in a conventional control system. 

In summary, the research presented in this article demonstrates that the use of artificial neural networks can lead to improved control of complex industrial processes with multiple input and single manipulated variables. This can help reduce the need for manual control, thereby minimizing mechanical stress and improving the overall efficiency of industrial processes.

Systems Analysis Modeling is considered to be the foundation for Information and Communication Technology (ICT) students, and is included in nearly all ICT and computer science degrees. However, novice system analysts find modelling and systems thinking quite challenging to learn and master. This results in frustration and a significant amount of time spent teaching the fundamentals. The purpose of this paper is to discuss the fundamental problems faced by learners in learning Systems Analysis modeling. A systematic literature review was conducted to propose a framework based on the key problems that novice learners experience. The proposed framework presents a sequence of activities designed to facilitate an understanding of requirements, solutions, and incremental modeling, aimed at improving motivation and learning. An example of incorporating visualization and gaming elements into a Systems Analysis classroom is provided to demonstrate how the framework could be used. This paper offers a means to guide future teaching activities and provides a greater understanding of the approach to teaching modeling within the computer science classroom.

Location information is an essential factor in wireless sensor networks, but the accuracy of existing algorithms for positioning nodes in 3D scenarios is limited. This paper proposes a new method called N2-3DDV-Hop, which improves positioning accuracy by using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II with 3D distance-vector hop. The limitations of the traditional single-objective positioning model are analyzed, and a multi-objective model is presented using the NSGA-II algorithm. The relationship between the average hop distance, the number of sensor nodes, and the theoretical average distance is also discussed. To evaluate its performance, the N2-3DDV-Hop method is compared with other current algorithms using three different complex network topologies. The simulation results show that the N2-3DDV-Hop method offers the best overall positioning performance and greater robustness than the 3DDV-Hop algorithm.

In this paper, we propose a new computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system for early detection of prostate cancer from diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI). Our system starts by defining a region of interest (ROI) that includes the prostate across the different slices of the input DWI volume. We then calculate, normalize and refine the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) of the defined ROI. Finally, we achieve classification of prostate into either benign or malignant using a two-stage classification system. 

In the first stage, we use seven convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to determine initial classification probabilities for each case. Then, we use a Support Vector Machine (SVM) with Guassian kernel that is fed with these probabilities to determine the ultimate diagnosis. The proposed system is novel in that it is able to detect prostate cancer with minimal prior processing (e.g., rough definition of the prostate region). 

We evaluated the developed system using DWI datasets collected at seven different b-values from 40 patients (20 benign and 20 malignant). The acquisition of these DWI datasets was performed using two different scanners with different magnetic field strengths (1.5 Tesla and 3 Tesla). The resulting area under curve (AUC) after the second stage of classification was 0.99, indicating a high performance of our system without segmentation, similar to that of up-to-date systems.

To meet the growing demand for mobile traffic, mobile operators are deploying denser cellular access networks which can be costly in terms of energy supply. Therefore, renewable energy (RE) sources are being utilized to power base stations (BSs) in order to make them more self-sufficient and reduce energy bills. However, sizing an RE generation system can be a critical task and current methods available in literature are time-consuming or computationally complex. 

This paper proposes a simple yet effective analytical method to find feasible combinations of photovoltaic (PV) panels and battery sizes suitable to power a BS and decrease the storage depletion probability below a target threshold. The method is based on the location dependent mean value and variance of RE production, which highlights the importance of RE production variance in determining optimal sizing. For locations with higher variance, larger PV panels are required, sometimes almost doubling the size needed for locations with low variance. However, only locations with higher variance benefit from increasing the battery size and relaxing the constraint on energy self-sufficiency. This can reduce required PV panel capacity and lower capital expenditures. 

Overall, this analytical approach provides a simple and efficient way to determine optimal sizing of RE generation systems for BSs, reducing costs and increasing energy efficiency in mobile networks.
