The RR Interval feature that has been extracted was then analyzed using KUBIOS to obtain the value of HRVi (Heart Rate Variability Triangular Index) in time domains. The results show that the average HRVi value after being induced by video stimuli is 14.87. There is a significant difference between HRVi value before and after the stimulation process. Immediate increase of HRVi can lead to a fatal heart attack. The result showed us that in seven minute, HRVi value can immediately increase after experiencing Sad Emotion induced by Sad Video Stimuli.

One issue with computer-based histopathology image analysis is the large size of the raw image, making it computationally expensive to input into a deep learning model. However, resizing the image to low resolution may result in information loss. To address this issue, a novel deep hybrid attention approach to breast cancer classification is presented in this paper. The approach adaptively selects coarse regions from the raw image by a hard visual attention algorithm, and then uses a soft attention mechanism to investigate abnormal parts for each selected region. A recurrent network is built to classify each image region and predict the location of the next region to investigate. As the region selection process is non-differentiable, the whole network is optimized through a reinforcement approach to learn an optimal policy to classify the regions. This 'Look, Investigate and Classify' approach significantly reduces computational resources without sacrificing performance, achieving around 96% classification accuracy while only processing 15% of the original image pixels. Evaluation on a public breast cancer histopathology database demonstrates the superiority of this approach compared to state-of-the-art deep learning techniques.

The utilization of Software Defined Networking (SDN) in vehicular networks has gained significant attention in recent years. SDN's flexibility and programmability offer promising solutions for addressing the challenges faced by Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs), namely Quality of Service (QoS) and scalability, which are essential characteristics of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). The dynamicity and density of vehicular networks result in fast topological changes, making SDN an appropriate solution for configuring the network by decoupling the control plane and data plane. However, it has been criticized for not offering scalability and reducing overall network QoS when using a single controller. As a result, recent works have shown that using multiple controllers is becoming the norm to accommodate larger networks. This paper surveys the proposed SDN-based architectures for vehicular networks, where the impact of the control plane, centralized or distributed, and the QoS improvements are evaluated and analyzed to determine the efficacy of each proposal in addressing the challenges faced by IoV and meeting the requirements of various applications.

The statistical delay of a path is traditionally modeled as a Gaussian random variable assuming that the path is always sensitized by a test pattern. Its sensitization in various circuit instances varies among its test patterns and the pattern induced delay is non-Gaussian. It is modeled using probability mass functions. The defect coverage is improved by test pattern selection using machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate accuracy in defect coverage when comparing to existing methods.

Individuals with cochlear implants (CIs) experience more difficulty understanding speech in reverberant environments than normal hearing listeners. As a result, recent research has targeted mitigating the effects of late reverberant signal reflections in CIs by using a machine learning approach to detect and delete affected segments in the CI stimulus pattern. Previous work has trained electrode-specific classification models to mitigate late reverberant signal reflections based on features extracted from only the acoustic activity within the electrode of interest. Since adjacent CI electrodes tend to be activated concurrently during speech, we hypothesized that incorporating additional information from the other electrode channels, termed cross-channel information, as features could improve classification performance. Cross-channel information extracted in real-world conditions will likely contain errors that will impact classification performance. To simulate extracting cross-channel information in realistic conditions, we developed a graphical model based on the Ising model to systematically introduce errors to specific types of cross-channel information. The Ising-like model allows us to add errors while maintaining the important geometric information contained in cross-channel information, which is due to the spectro-temporal structure of speech. Results suggest the potential utility of leveraging cross-channel information to improve the performance of the reverberation mitigation algorithm from the baseline channel-based features, even when the cross-channel information contains errors.

By renting cloud resources on a pay-as-you-go basis, scientific workflows that are data-intensive can prove to be costly, not just in terms of the time taken for execution, but also in terms of money due to the large amounts of data transfers required. Delays in these transfers can severely compromise workflow execution time, leading to prolonged resource rentals and ultimately exceeding budgets. To mitigate this issue, a new approach is proposed whereby some communication may be traded for computation during the scheduling production of workflows. This will involve duplicating computation of certain tasks to reduce the communication load between dependent tasks. The Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time (HEFT) algorithm and the Lookahead variant of HEFT are leveraged for this purpose, and the approach is evaluated using simulations and synthetic data from four real-world scientific workflow applications. The results suggest that task duplication can effectively reduce data transfer size, leading to shorter rental durations of resources and minimising network traffic in the cloud.

Deploying complex student projects in a realistic production environment can pose a significant challenge for university computing centers. While using public or private clouds is an option, it does not allow students to focus solely on project deployment and requires them to handle system administration tasks as well. To address this issue, a proposed platform as a service solution must meet three essential requirements: scalability, ease of use, user isolation, and security.

This work is a continuation of a larger research work which advocates that Distance Education (DE) through audio-only learning mode can be developed into a full fledge audio-MOOC. Audio MOOC framework is an innovative framework which enables learning through mere phone calls. It has been conceived to digitally include low literate population in the education process by opening up access to learning materials to the unreached and the have-nots usually hindered by barriers such as language, literacy, culture, connectivity and distance which existing MOOCs have failed to address. This work demonstrates how our proposed framework is used to connect to a remote island lost in the middle of the Indian Ocean with limited maritime and air access but which since some few years back can be connected via basic phones through voice calls. Agalega is an ideal test case scenario for our research since it characterizes remoteness, limited connectivity, semi-literate population with limited access to education which our research aims at addressing. A group of 50 Fishermen was identified from both the Agalega islands. The course was of 9 days duration from 15 to 23 September 2017. The system was conducted live over the telephony network making use of our GSM gateway. The specificity of the system was that our GSM gateway resided in Mauritius connected to a cloud server, while the course was delivered to people of Agalega 1100 Km far from Mauritius over the sea. Nevertheless, our system performed as expected and proved to be a success.

The IoT is experiencing massive growth in the industrial sector. This growth requires the development of innovative security concepts to keep up with the changing requirements of industrial IoT systems and applications. One important area of such M2M communication, where appropriate security measures need to be developed, is the authentication between devices. This paper proposes context-awareness as a method to enhance the authentication process in the industrial IoT. First, the problems of industrial IoT authentication are analyzed and the consequential requirements are formulated. Then it is shown, how context-awareness can help to overcome those problems. The advantages, which context-aware authentication brings, are afterwards demonstrated with concrete use cases.

Clustering also called cluster analysis is the task of data objects grouping where group objects are similar. Simultaneously, they should be different from other groups objects. Such groups are termed as Clusters. We are study in this paper several clustering algorithms applied in E-learning systems. Our objective lies in performing a deep analysis of clustering data mining techniques both theoretically and experimentally and to do a comparative study in order to distinguish which technique is more suitable to identify e-learners profile and also to evaluate better student performance in engineering education. A good clustering method is able to yield high quality clusters. The algorithms under investigation are: Canopy algorithm, Cobweb algorithm, EM algorithm, FarthestFirst algorithm, FilteredClusterer algorithm, MakeDensityBasedClusterer algorithm. The performance of clustering the six algorithms is compared through the use of clustering tool WEKA (version 3.7.12) as an open source tool.

A stylus is a popular instrument for interacting with touch-screen devices. It is especially useful when creating digital illustrations or handwriting. However, most styluses lack the ability to detect writing pressure and altitude, which are important factors in the expression of drawing and writing. Even digitizer styluses, like the Apple pencil, are limited in this regard due to the specifications of the touch panel. 

To address this issue, researchers have proposed a pen-grip shaped device that can estimate writing pressure and altitude from the force of the fingertip. The device consists of a pen-grip part and 3 axis force sensors embedded in a position related to the stylus' state. 

Results from the study showed that the proposed method can accurately estimate writing pressure in many cases, although it may struggle with low or drastically changed pressure. However, the estimated altitude showed low accuracy. 

Overall, the pen-grip shaped device could potentially improve the stylus' ability to detect writing pressure and altitude.

This paper presents an innovative low-power and low-energy 8T dual-port SRAM for real-time image processing, particularly suitable for deep-learning processors. The proposed SRAM utilizes a novel MSB-based inversion logic, which eliminates the need for an additional flag bit, resulting in a significant reduction of the area overhead. Compared to the 8-bit conventional majority logic, the proposed SRAM only incurs an area overhead of 0.6% for the MSB-based inversion logic. 

The proposed technique offers significant energy savings, as demonstrated in a 28-nm 64-kb FD-SOI SRAM, where 14.76% of total energy is saved when a set of images are read out. When image processing in the VGG-F convolutional neural network is considered, a saving factor of 17.31% is achieved, with a read operation energy of 304.81 fJ/cycle. 

Overall, the presented dual-port SRAM with MSB-based inversion logic shows promising results, offering a low-power and low-energy solution for real-time image processing in deep-learning processors.

Traffic noises, particularly the sound of vehicle horns, have a significant impact on the daily lives of individuals, and researchers have conducted numerous studies on the detection and localization of traffic sounds. This study presents a novel approach to locate vehicle horn sounds utilizing an optimized SRP-PHAT technique. Analysis of vehicle horn sounds and the identification of frequency-domain characteristics that facilitate detection of the sound using a time-frequency transformation (VHSR-TFT) was conducted. To overcome the high computational time associated with SRP-PHAT, the study used a stochastic region contraction method to boost real-time performance. The simulation and experimental results showed that the proposed method improved the accuracy and efficiency of sound detection compared to existing methods.

The HEVC standard introduced new tools to improve the encoding efficiency of video coding. However, those tools result in a high complexity that hampers the design of fast and energy-efficient encoders. In this work, we call into question the impact of the Integer Motion Estimation (IME) to the overall HEVC coding efficiency. We analyze how the encoder changes its behavior to handle extreme conditions where IME may not be performed for all the symmetric partitions. The analysis of the tradeoff between complexity and coding efficiency reveals an average of 67.16% IME complexity reduction at the expense of 4.63% BD-Rate.

This paper aims to compare the performance of two different methods for predicting the future values of a vehicle's slip angle - conventional adaptive finite impulse response filters and feed forward multi-layer neural networks. The study evaluates the results based on the number of inputs and prediction horizon, considering prediction error and the required number of algorithmic operations.

Currently, many deep neural networks are utilized for image recognition. However, most of them rely on real-valued operations and representations. A complex operation algorithm has been proposed, and in this paper, we applied the VGG model to the complex domain. We demonstrated that the complex-valued network offers advantages in terms of the depth and width of networks by conducting calculations. Specifically, the complex-valued network is deeper and wider than the real-valued network when possessing the same parameters. We conducted experiments to test the complex-valued VGG network and real-valued network on image recognition. The results indicate that the complex-valued VGG network performs better than the traditional real-valued VGG network in terms of stability and convergence speed.

We are proud to present an innovative approach to STEM education that combines machine learning, gamification, and social context, all based in Thailand. Our emphasis is on empowering students to learn in a fun and creative way, and we have accomplished this through a game-based agricultural AI challenge that focuses on the Four P’s of Creative Learning - Projects, Passion, Play, and Peers. 

Our goal is to inspire students to connect emerging technological solutions, such as AI, to real-world struggles, while creating an educational environment that is both engaging and playful. Our approach has demonstrated that machine learning is a powerful tool for interdisciplinary learning at the middle school level.

Though face recognition using traditional (hard) biometrics has attracted massive research interest and received extensive studies, it still confronts degrading variability challenges and notably achieves lower performance compared with other biometric recognition forms like fingerprint and iris. Recently, a number of research studies have been interested in enhancing face recognition performance by all means of supplementary facial biometric traits or other biometric modalities. Thus, soft biometrics have been emerged as a new promising modality of biometrics and highlighted as likely viable and fusible traits for augmenting traditional/hard biometrics. This is due to the expected advantages of soft biometrics over the traditional biometric traits, such as the high collectability and invariance properties. Other than fusing different kinds of traditional traits to augment face recognition, adding soft biometrics to augment various traditional facial traits has yet gained little research attention. Hence, in this research, unlike the majority of existing work, we investigate the viability of global soft face biometrics in supplementing traditional (hard) biometrics and the efficacy of concurrently using absolute and relative descriptions as soft biometrics. We conduct a new soft biometric-based fusion scheme in feature-level for augmenting a traditional Gabor-based face identification/verification in different potential forensic scenarios, considering performance variability evaluation and comparison with the baseline performance of Gabor features in isolation.

The number of containers is usually far greater than the number of virtual machines in data center. In order to avoid the energy waste caused by the frequent migration of container after initial deployment, an efficient container initial deployment strategy is particularly important. Therefore, this paper studies a many-to-one stable matching algorithm and proposes a container placement strategy MLSM. We start at an initial hosting solution for containers to reduce their migration times by using a stable matching algorithm. This algorithm uses the similarity methods as the matching preference strategy for containers and virtual machines. The virtual machine preference list is sorted by the resource utilization rate. The simulation results show that the algorithm can reduce the energy consumption by an average of 12.8% compared with using FirstFit algorithm.

Forecasting fine-grained network traffic is crucial for many network management and optimization tasks such as traffic engineering, anomaly detection, network accounting, network analytics, load balancing, and traffic matrix estimation. However, building models that are able to predict a wide-variety of network traffic types is not a trivial task due to a) the diversity of network traffic, and b) the computational challenges in processing large datasets to train the prediction models. In this paper, we present a network traffic prediction framework that uses real network traces from a Tier-1 ISP to train a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network and generate predictions at short time scales (≤ 30 seconds). In order to reduce the number of models needed to capture the very diverse dynamics of the various traffic sources, we develop a feature-based clustering framework that acts as a preprocessing step in order to group similar time-series together and train a single model for each group. Our extensive experimental evaluation study shows that LSTMs can indeed be used to predict network traffic with low prediction errors.

The potential of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) heights from TanDEM-X for estimating vegetation canopy height and aboveground biomass (AGB) has been widely acknowledged. However, the penetration of X-band through the canopy affects these estimations, resulting in biased canopy height and AGB retrieval, which cannot be directly compared to other data sources. The aim of this letter was to address this issue by applying a penetration depth model to correct for height biases in TanDEM-X InSAR heights. The corrected estimates of canopy height were then utilized to obtain AGB estimates using regression models. The uncorrected InSAR heights of the forest canopy display a bias due to signal penetration and differ significantly from light detection and ranging (LiDAR) canopy height estimates. By applying the penetration depth correction, unbiased forest canopy height estimates were obtained, and AGB regression models were developed that could be compared between InSAR and LiDAR. These findings suggest that TanDEM-X InSAR and LiDAR technologies can be used in combination to estimate AGB in complex tropical forests, benefiting from the synergistic use of these fundamentally different observation concepts.

Researchers have extensively investigated accurate classification of images using few-shot samples. However, two major drawbacks plague the existing methods. Firstly, the images are often used independently. Secondly, class imbalance is not taken into account, which results in a decrease in classification accuracy with the increase in classes. In order to address these issues, we present a novel visual classification method that utilizes image pairs with binary transformation (IPBT). This method involves bundling one image with each training image to generate an image pair by concatenating the representations of the two images along with their similarity. The class consistency of the two images in a pair is used to divide the image pairs into binary groups. One group comprises image pairs of the same class, while the other consists of image pairs of different classes. We trained classifiers to distinguish between the binary groups. In order to classify a testing image, we first bundle it with all the training images and then use the learned binary classifier to predict the results. The image pair with the highest response is selected to determine the class of the testing image. We conducted few-shot visual classification experiments on three public image datasets, and the results revealed the effectiveness of the proposed IPBT method.

In the past few decades, numerous scholars have conducted research on the stability and Hopf bifurcation problem of integer-order delayed neural networks. However, there is a lack of knowledge about the stability and Hopf bifurcation for fractional-order delayed neural networks. This paper aims to analyze the stability and existence of Hopf bifurcation for fractional-order bidirectional associative memory (BAM) neural networks with four delays.

By choosing the sum of two different delays as a bifurcation parameter, we establish a set of sufficient criteria to ensure the stability and the existence of Hopf bifurcation for the fractional-order BAM neural networks with four delays. It is evident that the delay has a crucial impact on the stability and Hopf bifurcation of these networks. We present an example to test the theoretical findings and demonstrate their rationality.

The results derived in this paper are new and have significant implications for optimizing neural networks and improving human life.

Inchworm locomotion is comprised of a simple anchor-slip gait which has inspired a wealth of mobile robots spanning rigid, soft, composite, and foldable mechanisms. Here, we expand upon that work by introducing centimeter-scale, inexpensive, simple, and soft robots capable of forward and backward motion, as well as tight turns. The robots are based on partially antagonistic fluid elastomer actuators; using a low fidelity model and experimental verification, we reason about actuator geometry. We introduce a simple two-step manufacturing process, and test actuator longevity and payload capacity. To enable stand-alone operation, we design a lightweight, low volume electro-mechanical backpack, capable of driving up to 3 actuators. We then show how differential friction can be used to enable forward and turning motion in a single actuator, and how three actuators can be combined to additionally enable backwards motion and on-axis turns. Due to the use of miniature pumps, inflation and corresponding motion is slow. However, the robot cost, durability, and ability to maneuver in confined spaces may be beneficial in applications such as duct mapping and maintenance.

The linear consensus protocol is an iterative distributed algorithm that possesses asymptotic convergence guarantees. This paper presents an algorithm that is capable of detecting convergence to consensus within a specified error tolerance in a distributed manner for agents that are running linear consensus iterations. The distributed stopping criterion overcomes the limitation of time-varying bounded delays that occur between information transmission and reception among agents. To achieve this, the algorithm relies on determining the maximum and minimum values in a distributive manner.

In addition, this paper includes the development of an algorithm for average consensus. This algorithm also utilizes a distributive stopping criterion based on maximum and minimum consensus. Unlike prior work, centralized coordination is not needed to determine how each agent should weight its neighbor's values. The previous assumption of double stochasticity is relaxed to only column stochasticity. Through simulations and comparison with previous work in the literature, the effectiveness of both algorithms is demonstrated.

To validate the applicability and utility of the proposed algorithms, we demonstrate their use on an experimental test bed of Raspberry-Pi agents communicating wirelessly.

In the past few years, the Subjectivity and Sentiment Analysis (SSA) has garnered a lot of attention, and many unsuccessful attempts were made for developing an SSA model for the morphologically-rich languages like Arabic. In this study, we aimed to fill the gap by designing a new manual and auto-annotated corpus of the Sudanese-Dialect Arabic (SDA) along with a novel polarity lexicon. The corpus is a collection of political tweets, which were annotated by Twitter on a sentence-level. We have also described some automated, online SSA-tagging tools, which could explore all annotated data. Furthermore, we have investigated the effect of various pre-processing techniques on the Sudanese SSA process. Here, we presented a novel SSA technique for the Sudanese dialect, which displayed a good subjectivity classification result and showed an 83.5% accuracy for the Decision Tree performance.

This paper presents a novel framework for indoor subarea localization through acoustic sensing using an ordinary smartphone. The proposed approach addresses the subarea localization problem in scenarios where there are similar space physical structures by constructing a multidimensional fingerprint of each environmental background audio in a room using the auditory scene analysis method. The room-level fingerprint is then extracted by the acoustic background spectrum method, and the subarea-level fingerprints are clustered using Pearson correlation coefficient technology. By combining the offline stage long short-term memory recurrent neuron network and online stage least variance algorithm, effective indoor subarea localization is achieved. The localization results are presented in both text form and a privacy-protected color sound pattern built by chroma DCT-reduced log pitch. This framework was evaluated with real-world audios from 96 hours of environment background audios from 14 different rooms, demonstrating that the room-level localization accuracy was higher than 90% and subarea-level accuracy could be up to 97.64%. Overall, these results support the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving accurate subarea localization even in complex small rooms.

A new nonparametric Bayesian-based motion planning algorithm for autonomous plume source term estimation (STE) and source seeking (SS) is presented in this paper. The algorithm is designed for mobile robots equipped with gas concentration sensors. Specifically, robots coordinate and utilize a Gaussian-plume likelihood model in a Bayesian-based STE process, then they simultaneously search for and navigate toward the source through model based, bioinspired SS methods such as biased-random-walk and surge-casting. Compared with the state-of-the-art Bayesian- and sensor-based STE/SS motion planners, the strategy described takes advantage of coordination between multiple robots and the estimated plume model for faster and more robust SS, rather than rely on direct or filtered sensor measurements. A set of Monte Carlo simulation studies are conducted to compare the performance between the uncoordinated and coordinated algorithms for different robot team sizes and starting conditions. Additionally, the algorithms are validated experimentally through a laboratory-safe, realistic humid-air plume that behaves similar to a gas plume, to test STE and SS using mobile ground robots equipped with humidity sensors. Simulation and experimental results show consistently that the algorithm involving coordination outperforms traditional bioinspired SS algorithms and it is approximately twice as fast as the uncoordinated case. Finally, the plume source is distorted to study the algorithm's limitations and impact on STE and SS, where results show that even for distorted plumes, useful source localization information can be obtained.

The polarization millimeter wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system has been deployed in next-generation wireless communication since it can provide a high-data stream and high space efficiency simultaneously. Polarization channel parameter estimation for polarized mmWave massive MIMO systems is extremely important for directional beamforming with data transmissions. In this paper, the base station (BS) equipped with a large polarization-sensitive array is considered in massive MIMO systems. The polarization channel consists of direction-of-arrival (DOA) and polarization parameters that are estimated from the coexistence of circular and non-circular signals. Based on the unconjugated covariance matrix, the initialized polarization channel estimation is achieved by multiple signal classification (MUSIC). Then, the high-accuracy polarization channel estimation for general non-circular rate signals is performed by reconstructing the corresponding noise matrix. The high-accuracy polarization channel estimation for circular signals is obtained based on covariance matrix differencing. Moreover, the dimension of parameter search is reduced based on the partial derivative of the spectrum function with respect to the non-circular phase. The high-accuracy polarization channel estimation for the maximum non-circular rate signal is finally achieved based on the initialized parameter estimation of the polarization channel. The proposed algorithm estimates different kinds of signals separately. The effect of different kinds of signals is reduced significantly, which means that the resolution probability of different kinds of signals can be dramatically improved. Numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm, especially in small angular distances.

Sensors drift is one of the most critical challenges while designing an Electronic Nose System (ENS). The discrimination and quantification of gases in the presence of drift is challenging and requires either (i) system recalibration, (ii) domain transformations or (iii) data from target domain. This paper proposes a heuristic optimization technique integrated with a pattern recognition model to estimate the concentration of different industrial gases in the presence of small experimental drift. The proposed method is validated against an experimental data acquired with an array of 16 screen-protected gas sensors. Samples from 6 volatile compounds; ethylene, ethanol, ammonia, acetone, acetaldehyde and toluene are tested to validate the proposed solution. Besides giving accurate performance in terms of concentration estimation the proposed solution does not require system recalibration, domain transformations or target domain data and meanwhile it also reduces the computational complexity of the system.

Use of mobile health (mHealth) systems has increased with the advancement and proliferation of mobile computing and related technologies. It has improved efficiency and effectiveness of healthcare services. Non-invasive pain level detection from facial images is one of the promising mHealth applications. Effective pain treatment requires regular and continuous pain assessment. Most of the pain research tools are study or disease specific while some are pain (lumbar pain, cancer pain, etc.) and patient group specific (neonatal, adult, woman, etc.). This results in recurrent but potentially avoidable costs such as time, money, and workforce to develop similar services or software research tools for each research study. In this study, we have proposed, designed, and implemented a customizable personalized pain study platform that offers real-time data collection, research participant management, role-based access control, research data anonymization etc. It is also used to investigate pain level detection accuracy using evidence-based continuous learning from the facial expression data, collected from Bangladesh, Nepal and USA, which yielded about 71% classification accuracy.

Many wearable devices employ the sensors for physiological signals (e.g., electrocardiogram or ECG) to continuously monitor personal health (e.g., cardiac monitoring). Considering private medical data storage, secure access to such wearable devices becomes a crucial necessity. Exploiting the ECG sensors present on wearable devices, we investigate the possibility of using ECG as the individually unique source for device authentication. In particular, we propose to use ECG features toward both cardiac monitoring and neural-networkbased biometric authentication. For such complex functionalities to be seamlessly integrated in wearable devices, an accurate algorithm must be implemented with ultralow power and a small form factor. In this paper, a smart ECG processor is presented for ECG-based authentication as well as cardiac monitoring. Data-driven Lasso regression and low-precision techniques are developed to compress neural networks for feature extraction by 24.4×. The 65-nm testchip consumes 1.06 μW at 0.55 V for real-time ECG authentication. For authentication, equal error rates of 1.70%/2.18%/2.48% (best/average/worst) are achieved on the in-house 645-subject database. For cardiac monitoring, 93.13% arrhythmia detection sensitivity and 89.78% specificity are achieved for 42 subjects in the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database.

In recent years, deep reinforcement learning methods have achieved impressive performance in many different fields, including playing games, robotics, and dialogue systems. However, there are still a lot of restrictions here, one of which is the demand for massive amounts of sampled data. In this paper, a hierarchical meta-learning method based on the actor-critic algorithm is proposed for sample efficient learning. This method provides the transferable knowledge that can efficiently train an actor on a new task with a few trials. Specifically, a global basic critic, meta critic, and task specified network are shared within a distribution of tasks and are capable of criticizing any actor trying to solve any specified task. The hierarchical framework is applied to a critic network in the actor-critic algorithm for distilling meta-knowledge above the task level and addressing distinct tasks. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple classic control tasks with reinforcement learning algorithms, including the start-of-the-art meta-learning methods. The experimental results statistically demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance and attains better results with more depth of meta critic network.

The Hausdorff Distance (HD) is a widely-used measurement in evaluating the effectiveness of medical image segmentation methods. However, current segmentation methods do not directly aim to minimize the HD. In this study, we introduce new loss functions to train convolutional neural network (CNN)-based segmentation methods with the objective of directly reducing HD. We suggest three methods to estimate HD from CNN-produced segmentation probability maps. The first method utilizes the segmentation boundary’s distance transform. The second method involves performing morphological erosion on the difference between the real and estimated segmentation maps. The third method uses circular/spherical convolution kernels with various radii on the segmentation probability maps. Based on the three HD estimation methods, we propose three loss functions for training to decrease HD. We employ these loss functions to train CNNs for segmentation of the liver, prostate, and pancreas in magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, and computed tomography images, and compare their results to commonly-used loss functions. Our findings demonstrate that applying the proposed loss functions can reduce HD by approximately 18-45% without compromising the performance of other segmentation criteria such as the Dice similarity coefficient. Overall, the suggested loss functions can facilitate the training of medical image segmentation methods by minimizing significant segmentation errors.

Early detection and prediction of cardiac anomalies plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Electrocardiography (ECG) is widely used by doctors as it provides critical information on heart activity. However, ECG classification remains a challenging task due to the complexities of the data and the reliability of manual data collection methods.

IoT technologies have facilitated the development of wearable devices for ECG monitoring. However, the automatic data collected from these devices present even more challenging issues for ECG classification. In this paper, we propose a novel solution for ECG signal classification using Deep Learning techniques. Our solution combines Auto Encoder and Long-Short Term Memory models to handle data collected from intelligent IoT devices such as Shimmer and VitalSigns Holter. 

Our approach leverages the power of auto-encoders to obtain a compact representation of the ECG signal. The compressed data is then passed through the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) model to capture the temporal dependencies and classify the ECG signals accurately. The proposed model significantly outperformed existing state-of-the-art approaches for ECG classification.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Deep Learning model effectively classifies ECG signals from IoT devices. The accurate classification of ECG signals based on IoT devices will help doctors diagnose cardiac anomalies early and provide timely treatment to patients. Furthermore, our proposed model can be extended to handle other medical data collected from IoT devices to improve healthcare outcomes. Thus, our proposed solution has immense potential in revolutionizing healthcare systems.

With the integration of electronic products and advancements in electronic industrial technology, the assembly density of printed circuit boards (PCBs) has significantly increased, resulting in smaller spacing between wires and solder joints. However, the diverse working environments of electronic products, such as high temperature, high relative humidity, and environmental contamination, pose a significant risk for electrochemical migration (ECM) of high-density PCBs. It is crucial to establish a life model that correlates the time to failure (TTF) of ECM with environmental factors like temperature, relative humidity, and bias voltage in the circuits. 

This paper proposes two methods to establish an ECM life model on PCBs and compare their efficacy. The first model is based on failure physics, while the other employs machine learning. To determine the unknown coefficients in the failure physics model and train the machine learning model, TTF data was obtained through accelerated experiments under temperature humidity bias conditions. Finally, the two models were evaluated based on a test dataset. 

The study found that the machine learning model established by random forest regression algorithm had better life prediction performance than the failure physics model. Therefore, the study confirms that machine learning can be applied to model ECM failure under complex environmental conditions.

Recent technological advancements have resulted in an overwhelming amount of medical data from various sources. However, this data is often poorly annotated, noisy, and unstructured, making it difficult to establish actionable insights for clinical applications. While Electronic Health Records (EHR) contain a plethora of patient information, such as clinical notes, charted events, medications, and laboratory test results, traditional machine learning and statistical methods have not been sufficient in providing insights that can aid physicians in treating patients. This is largely due to the need for expert opinion assisted features before building a benchmark task model. 

With the emergence of deep learning methods, there is an opportunity to use this technology to save lives. The purpose of this study is to explore the possible use cases of deep learning with EHR and offer an intuitive explanation for its application. health informatics professionals can utilize deep learning algorithms to approach each clinical task effectively. By highlighting technical intuitions and blueprints, this study examines how deep learning can be used to provide better insights into EHR data that can be used to improve clinical decision-making.

Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks are a special type of Ad-Hoc network that supports communication between highly mobile vehicles and stationary Roadside Units or base stations. As the demand for more bandwidth increases with the introduction of autonomous vehicles and Multi-Media entertainment, the network size must scale to accommodate the demand. However, when deploying any additional networking resources, energy consumption should be taken into account. Existing works target routing as a means to reduce the energy consumed in end-to-end communications, but little work has been directed towards energy-aware infrastructure planning. In this work, we present a spatio-temporal clustering approach that models the connection time for potential Roadside Unit deployment sites. Our techniques leverage crowdsourced data, which is collected at the vehicle, and accurately represents the trends of users in the network. Modeling the connection time of deployment sites allows for transmission power to be adjusted based on traffic flow. We also present a technique to model the signal strength in deployment sites, thus identifying areas with sufficient coverage and selecting sites with weak connectivity from existing networking infrastructure. Combined this information allows infrastructure to be deployed in a manner that matches the real-time traffic and operate with an optimal transmission power.

Collective activity recognition is an advanced field of computer vision that aims to identify what activities a group of people are doing. Unlike individual actions, collective activity recognition requires an intricate consideration of complex interactions amongst multiple individuals. Unfortunately, previous approaches have been hampered by extensive annotations such as precise labeling of individual actions, pairwise interactions, and poses. These annotations can be challenging to obtain in practice. Furthermore, many of these approaches treat human detection as a disjoint task, ignoring the relation between the two tasks and subsequently making it difficult to remove extraneous persons from the activity. In this paper, we propose a rapid weakly supervised deep learning architecture for collective activity recognition. We suggest making actor detection and collective activity recognition work together in an end-to-end framework, sharing convolutional layers between them. This joint learning helps to reinforce the two tasks' effectiveness and enable the filtering out of outliers that are not involved in the activity. Our proposed weakly supervised learning includes a latent embedding scheme that explores interactive relationships between people and groups to reduce the need for pairwise relation and individual action labels. The experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches on three separate datasets. Our joint modeling enables collective activity recognition at the unprecedented speed of 22.65 frames per second, making this approach more deployable for real-time applications.

This paper proposes a logic-based control algorithm for Variable Speed Limits (VSLs) in order to reduce or avoid traffic jams created at bottlenecks. The proposed controller estimates, for each controller time step, the number of vehicles that have to be held back or released by the VSLs in order to maximize the outflow of the bottleneck (avoiding the capacity drop). Afterward, based on the estimated number of vehicles, the VSLs are increased or decreased sequentially. The proposed controller uses a feed-forward structure that allows to anticipate the future evolution of the bottleneck density in order to avoid or reduce traffic breakdowns. As a result, although the implementation of the controller is quite easy with an almost instantaneous computation time, the performance of the controller is effective in reducing Total Time Spent (TTS). The proposed controller is tested, using the macroscopic traffic flow model METANET, for 10 scenarios and the results are compared with the ones obtained with the Mainstream Traffic Flow Control (MTFC) algorithm, and with the optimal solution. The simulations show that the proposed controller is able to approach the optimal behavior and that its behavior is quite robust (especially comparing with MTFC) in cases where different demands are considered.

Solving optimization problems in multi-agent networks where each agent possesses only partial knowledge of the problem has become increasingly significant. In this study, we focus on minimizing the sum of n convex functions, given that each function is only known by one agent. We demonstrate that the generalized distributed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) shows Q-linear convergence to the solution of the aforementioned optimization problem if the overall objective function is strongly convex, but the functions that each agent knows are allowed to be only convex.

The Q-linear convergence ensures that tracking statements can be established, which cannot be made if only R-linear convergence is guaranteed. In scenarios where the objective functions undergo variation in time, which is at the same scale as the algorithm is updated, R-linear convergence is often insufficient. Additionally, we establish the equivalence amid the generalized distributed ADMM and proximal exact first-order algorithm (P-EXTRA) for a sub-set of mixing matrices. 

This equivalence offers a better understanding of P-EXTRA's convergence when overshooting to enhance convergence.

In the field of process mining, a lot of information about what happened inside the information system has been exploited and has yielded significant results. However, information related to the relationship between performers and performers is only utilized and evaluated in certain aspects. In this paper, we propose an algorithm to classify the temporal work transference from workflow enactment event log. This result may be used to reduce system memory, increase the computation speed. Furthermore, it can be used as one of the factors to evaluate the performer, active role of resources in the information system.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of the reliability, average reliability, availability, maintainability, and supportability (RARAMS) of enterprise services, and their relationship to the demands placed upon them. To achieve this, we introduce a dynamic simulation model that is capable of simulating a closed system, complete with negative feedback and time delay. 

The closed system is formed by the effect of the average reliability on demand, and the negative feedback arises from the inverse relationship between service time and service reliability. We employ a system dynamics simulation approach to run the model, generating dynamic behavior profiles for both the RAMS of enterprise services and the demands placed upon them. 

Our model provides a powerful tool for predicting the performance characteristics of enterprise services, enabling organizations to better tailor their service offerings to meet the demands of the market. Moreover, our model is capable of being adapted to reflect changing market conditions, ensuring that organizations are equipped to respond quickly and effectively to changing circumstances. Overall, our results suggest that the careful management of reliability, availability, maintainability, and supportability is essential to the successful operation of any enterprise service.

Magnetic Resonance Image (MRI) is a medical technique commonly used by radiologists to visualize organ structures in humans without surgery, MRI provides a wealth of information about human soft tissue, which helps to diagnose brain tumors. Classifying normal and abnormal MRI images helps in early detection of brain tumors. Usually classifies MRI images using T2-weighted MRI images. However, to achieve perfect accuracy, sensitivity and specificity is very difficult. Fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) image is superior to T2-weighted image for detecting MS brain lesions. This study aims to classify FLAIR MRI images of the brain by classifying abnormal and normal MRI images based on statistical texture analysis, 44 abnormal datasets of BRATS 2017 training data and 4 normal datasets from Patient Contributed Image Repository (PCIR). At the beginning of the step, pre-processing of the image is followed by the histogram equalization method to extract the feature with statistical texture analysis by calculating the mean, variance, deviation, skewness, kurtosis, energy, entropy and smoothness. Finally, a multinomial logistic regression model with a ridge estimator is used to classify abnormal and normal MRI images and evaluated by k-fold validation. The results obtained from the proposed method of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity reached 100%. This shows the method used to do a good classification in this case.

Classic DC power flow and Generalized Generation Distribution Factors (GGDF) are utilized to model transmission network constraints in a DC optimal power flow (OPF) scenario. The former is praised for its straightforwardness, precision, and stability, while the latter is celebrated for its capacity to convey transmission power flows as a function of power generation with fewer equality constraints. This research study compares the efficacy and efficacy of both methods by analyzing their performance on a PJM 5-bus system and an IEEE 57-bus system, incorporating transmission losses, using various commercial optimization solvers.

Fast and energy efficient data collection is the most important function of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) which governs the performance of WSNs. Time division multiple access (TDMA) is an effective data collection strategy in which node only schedules the active slot to save energy when transmitting data. However, many previous studies are designed for static traffic pattern such that each node to generate one data packet in a data collection cycle. Moreover, all nodes in the network use the same transmission radius r, so that the network data collection has a larger delay, a lower lifetime, and energy utilization rate. In view of the shortcomings of previous research, this paper proposes a reducing delay and maximizing lifetime (RDML) data collection strategy for WSNs with dynamic traffic patterns. The main innovation point of our work is the data transmission radius is no longer unified as r, while some nodes with energy surplus use a data transmission radius of mr(m > 1). The following network performance can be achieved by adopting the RDML scheme. First, because the nodes in the near sink mr radius area can send data directly to sink, the amount of data carried by hotspots nodes in the original strategy is greatly reduced, and the lifetime is improved. Second, since some nodes can go mr distance to the sink in data transmission, thus accelerating the data routing and reducing the time needed for data collection. Finally, since the remaining energy of nodes is fully utilized to increase the radius of data transmission, the energy utilization rate can be effectively improved. Through the theoretical analysis and experimental results, the RDML scheme can reduce the maximum delay of data collection by 22.32% and improve lifetime as well as the energy utilization rate by 0.86%-84.40%, and 23.33%-88.00%, respectively, compared with previous strategies.

The primary objective of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) is to enable communication between human brains and external devices, such as computers, by utilizing EEG signals. This study focuses on the classification of P300 signals using the transfer learning approach. The basic learning algorithms used were Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Support Vector Machines (SVMs). The CNN-FT model was built using Fine-tuning (FT) with CNN as the learning algorithm, and the SVM-TL model was constructed using the Tradaboost algorithm, a novel transfer learning framework, with SVM as the learning algorithm. Both models were tested and compared against the Data set II of BCI Competition III. The analysis revealed that the CNN-FT model outperformed the CNN model, and the SVM-TL model outperformed the SVM model.

In this article, we introduce an innovative and durable approach to quantized matrix completion. Our approach includes proposing a rank minimization problem with constraints induced by quantization bounds. We then form an unconstrained optimization problem by regularizing the rank function with Huber loss. This approach uses Huber loss to control the violation from quantization bounds, as it is both differentiable and less sensitive to outliers than quadratic loss. Furthermore, we use a smooth rank approximation to endorse lower rank on the genuine data matrix, leading to an unconstrained optimization problem with a differentiable objective function, which can be optimized using gradient descent techniques. 

Our approach has several significant contributions. Firstly, we provide novel and robust theoretical analyses of the problem model and convergence of our algorithm to the global solution. Secondly, our method does not require projections or initial rank estimation, unlike the state-of-the-art. Finally, in the Numerical Experiments section, we illustrate the superior performance of our proposed method in learning accuracy and computational complexity compared to those of the state-of-the-art literature methods.

In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the use of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) for various applications such as security surveillance, building health monitoring, habitation monitoring, healthcare, and disaster management. However, the primary constraint with WSNs is the limited energy of the sensor nodes, which are often deployed in harsh environmental conditions where changing or replenishing batteries is difficult. Therefore, sustaining a long life for WSNs is a significant challenge. 

To address this challenge, hierarchical routing protocols have been proposed as an energy-efficient solution for routing data in WSNs. These protocols often gather sensor nodes into non-overlapping clusters, with cluster heads performing data aggregation and routing data to a sink. This paper provides a taxonomy of hierarchical routing protocols and envisions a hybrid hierarchical routing protocol that integrates characteristics of intelligent routing protocols. 

Overall, hierarchical routing protocols offer a promising solution for extending the life of WSNs by conserving energy and reducing data loss. By incorporating the advantages of intelligent routing protocols, the proposed hybrid protocol has the potential to further enhance the performance and efficiency of WSNs in various applications.

Accident and emergencies are unpredictable. In case of accidents, human intervention causes time delay and it can result in many problems, even human life loss. In this regard, IoT offers a lot of benefits. The main purpose of IoT based disaster management system is to provide aid in an emergency system with minimum delay. Cloud computing plays a vital role in IoT. It provides storage, management, and processing of a large amount of data. As a large amount of data is processed on the cloud, the overall processing time increase due to transferring and processing delay. Here, Fog Computing comes into play as it provides processing at the edge of the network. it provides many advantages such as reduced latency, mobility, geographical distribution, real-time interactions etc. the purpose of this paper is to exploit the advantages of fog computing to develop a fog-based accident detection and emergency response system, which employs Android device sensors to detect an accident emergency, accident location and create an action plan to handle the emergency timely. We evaluated our approach with the help of iFogSim which is an open source toolkit for simulating fog technologies along with IoT and cloud. The results achieved after simulation are promising and illustrate that fog provides superior results in comparison to the cloud.

The human face facial complexity and the face changes make the face recognition system a challenging task to design and difficult to implement. The correlation between the training images which has a high impact on the accuracy of the face recognition system never considered by researchers. In this paper, we presented an enhanced framework to improve the face recognition using the classical conventional Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). A key contribution of this work is based on obtaining a robust training dataset called the T-Set using the correlation between all the images in the training dataset not based on the image density which adds a distinct layer between the dataset. We used the PCA descriptor for features extraction and dimension reduction to show that there is a promising enhancement even with using traditional algorithms. We combined five distance methods (Correlation, Euclidean, Canberra, Manhattan, and Mahalanobis) to obtain the T-Set using the square-root of the sum of the squares to achieve higher accuracy. We added a strength factor to each of the distance methods, and we achieved higher face recognition accuracy than the current approach. Our experimental results on YALE and ORL datasets demonstrate that the approach we proposed improved the accuracy of face recognition system with respect to the existing methods.

In this article, it is demonstrated that heterogeneity and noise in big data can increase the generalization error in traditional learning approaches used for deep neural networks (deep NNs). To counter this, the article suggests a direct error-driven learning (EDL) scheme that overcomes the issue of vanishing gradients. The concept of a neighborhood is introduced to reduce the impact of heterogeneity and data noise, and an approximation of generalization error is obtained. An overall error, consisting of learning and the approximate generalization errors, is defined to obtain a novel NN weight-tuning law through a layer-wise performance measure. Additional constraints are added to the layer-wise performance measure to guide and enhance learning in the presence of noisy dimensions. The proposed direct EDL scheme effectively addresses the issues of heterogeneity and noise, while reducing vanishing gradients and noisy dimensions. A comprehensive simulation study is presented, which shows that the proposed method mitigates the vanishing gradient problem and improves generalization error by 6%.

The model of reactive power optimization including interval uncertainty (RPOIU) is used to make a voltage control strategy for ensuring the interval state variables (including load voltages and reactive power generation) of the power grid within their safe operating limits, under interval active power generation and power load demand input data. To solve the RPOIU model, this paper defined security limits, and then switches the RPOIU model to two deterministic reactive power optimization models, whose constraints bound limits are the security limits. By solving the deterministic models through the interior point method, a voltage control strategy is obtained as the solution of the RPOIU model. The results obtained by the proposed method are compared with the linear approximation method, which is a previously proposed effective method for solving the RPOIU model, and simulation results and analysis demonstrate the advantages, effectiveness, and good applicability of the proposed method.

Ever since humans attained the cognitive capability, his covet of disseminating own knowledge has walked side by side. The quest of having suitable ways to disperse his or her inbound awareness, or information, into others' inner-space lead to several methods, starting from the combination of vocal and hand gestures to full-fledged spoken and orthographic languages. The purpose of any of these methods is the same, which is to create a replication of information from one's cognizance to others' inner domain; the whole process being described by a single word commonly known as `communications'. Today, the word `communications' is not just limited to humans and rather has trespassed to machine's domain that we know as machine-to-machine communications (M2M). However, as long ago as we have our historical evidence, there were only three modes of communications we are able to use that are, strictly auditory, strictly visual, and the combination of both, and we are not able to use other modes of human capabilities for communicating information. Besides some exceptional mentioning in our mythologies, one of them being Mahabharata, an ancient Hindu religious epic, in which, use of five primary senses namely, visual (or seeing), auditory (or hearing), olfactory (or smelling), gustatory (or tasting), and tactile (or touching) is explicitly mentioned for describing a subject (object in question) and transferring the holistic information to another person distance apart. It was very recent when an idea of Human Bond Communications (HBC) was put on the floor, which has a similar concept of using all five senses to transmit and recreate holistic information using the sensing and communication techniques.This article presents a technical framework to realize the complex HBC environment so that the idea of a holistic recreation of a subject can be seen as an achievable possibility and long thirst of a shift from mythology to reality is quenchable. From this framework, using the additional three senses other than visual and auditory, we expect to have a system that can have more meaning to the information for its closeness to the reality.

Glycol ethers are organic solvents commonly used in various industries and household products, including paints, cleaning agents and cosmetics. Recent studies have focused on investigating the subtle neurotoxic effects of early-life exposure to these solvents on children's neuropsychological performance. Through the use of neuroimaging, researchers can examine brain function and identify any changes in cerebral connections caused by these neurotoxicants. This study specifically examined the effects of prenatal low-level exposure to different glycol ethers on brain development in children aged between 10 and 12 years old. Previous studies have suggested cognitive disabilities in attention, inhibition and working memory; therefore, the researchers proposed a structural connectivity analysis using graph theory in the regions connected to these functions. The study results suggest that there may be a link between prenatal glycol ether exposure and impairments in attention, inhibition and working memory, particularly with respect to ethoxyacetic acid, ethoxyethoxyacetic acid and 2-butoxyacetic acid.

Objective: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) imaging has been recently implemented with deep learning techniques. However, there are certain challenges to address, such as the inability to recover sharp or cornered targets with the traditional circular inclusion training data. This paper introduces an iterative-based inversion method and a convolutional neural network (CNN) based inversion method to recover challenging inclusions such as triangular, rectangular, or lung shapes. The CNN-based method uses random circle or ellipse training data. 

Methods: The paper proposes a bases-expansion subspace optimization method (BE-SOM) as an iterative method with induced contrast current (ICC) concept and total variation regularization. Additionally, the theory behind BE-SOM and the introduced physical concepts prompt the proposal of a dominant-current deep learning algorithm for EIT imaging, where the dominant parts of the ICC generate multi-channel inputs for the CNN.

Results: The proposed methods underwent testing with numerical and experimental data, with consideration for realistic phantoms such as pneumothorax and pleural effusion pathologies. The results showed significant improvements in reconstructing targets with sharp corners or edges. The proposed methods showed capabilities of stable, fast and high-quality EIT imaging, with great potential for clinical applications.

Conclusions and Significance: The proposed methods provide a solution to existing limitations in traditional EIT imaging techniques. The iterative-based inversion method and CNN-based inversion method proved promising in overcoming the challenge of recovering sharp or cornered targets, which indicates their potential for clinical use in creating quantitative EIT images.

The Wearable Instantaneous Ball Speed Estimator (WIBASE) is a prototype system developed to measure the speed of a cricketer's bowling during training. This equipment is vital for coaches as it helps them assess the performance of fast bowlers and their ability to bowl consistently. WIBASE comprises two primary hardware components- a computer and a wrist-worn electronic board with a 3-dimensional (3D) acceleration sensor.

The system tracks the three-axis acceleration generated by the arm's movement during the delivery of the ball and stores the data. Data from three different sensors- accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer- is processed by a Digital Motion Processor (DMP) on the board in a Sensor Fusion process before being sent to the computer via Bluetooth. A Python script on the computer receives the filtered acceleration, consisting of both static and dynamic acceleration. Numerical integration using the Trapezoidal method is used to derive the speed of the bowler, and the data is logged into a file while displaying the speed on the computer. 

The WIBASE has undergone three sets of experiments, and test results indicate that the equipment can effectively track 3D acceleration, derive the bowler's speed, and log all data into a file in real-time. The WIBASE is a reliable, accessible, and affordable solution to measure the speed of a cricketer's bowling during training.

Computer processing power has grown exponentially over the past decades. At the same time the sophistication of sensors has increased, providing more numerous and accurate data points for control. Based on these trends it would seem that expert systems would be more capable and more in demand than ever. However, many plants and companies have struggled to maximize the benefits of expert control systems. Expert control has been shown to provide increased operational efficiency with lower emission levels and reduced costs. However, these targets can be elusive if the expert system is not properly understood and the prerequisites for success not followed. This paper explores some of the issues that inhibit expert control system operation. The paper provides some guidelines for optimizing existing expert control systems and provides prerequisites for companies considering the installation of expert control systems.

This brief provides analytical results on the impact of additive weight/bias noise on the performance of a Boltzmann machine (BM) where the output of the unit belongs to the set {-1, 1} as opposed to {0, 1}. When such noise is present, it is observed that the state distribution remains a Boltzmann distribution but with an increased temperature factor. Consequently, a gradient ascent learning algorithm is proposed, and a corresponding learning procedure is developed. The learning process is then compared with the learning procedure employed for training a BM with noise. It is found that both methods are identical, and therefore, the learning algorithm for noise-free BMs is applicable as an online learning algorithm for an analog circuit-implemented BM, irrespective of the variances of the additive weight noise and bias noise.

Image registration plays a crucial role in numerous technical researches. It reduces deviations in sequential images and facilitates the analysis of information variation in a specific area. This study proposes a procedure for creating a fixed image using facial IR thermography data. The method involves a visual saliency map through a detected image and a cluster algorithm. A comparison between affinity parameters is made using Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Simulated Annealing Algorithm. Two control parameters are considered: time allocation for each alignment calculation and the use of parallel computing toolbox. The optimum method is chosen using objective function values based on control parameters. The Taguchi experiment verifies the optimal internal parameter, validating the procedure's efficiency. Overlapping images before and after alignment and image quality measurements validate the difference in images. Results indicate that the alignment procedure in this study accurately aligns human faces, aiding data statistics and analysis of temperature area interdependence.

The Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) plays a crucial role in ensuring and enhancing the quality of education at all levels. It strives to provide inclusive and participative intercultural education to all, and effective planning of resources such as physical infrastructure, technology, and teaching staff is a priority in their educational policy. In line with this, MINEDUC has implemented the National Student Census application across all educational institutions- fiscal, fiscomisional, private, and municipal. 

The student census system collects and stores information on all educational institutions. This case study will analyze the existing processes and identify areas where COBIT 5.0 can be integrated to improve the quality of response information. By doing so, MINEDUC can make effective use of resources, enhance the quality of education, and achieve its institutional objectives.

This study presents a design method for a time-varying control Lyapunov function (CLF) for nonlinear systems defined on manifolds. The authors introduce a definition of a time-varying CLF defined on manifolds, which extends the conventional CLF defined on Euclidean space. They also propose a time-varying CLF design method by extending the minimum projection method. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through an application to the dynamical obstacle avoidance control problem. The study shows that an analytic global controller can be designed for the dynamical obstacle avoidance of a mobile robot.

In the aftermath of large-scale disasters, communication and infrastructure are often severely damaged, making it difficult for rescue and relief teams to exchange vital information with control stations. To tackle this issue, several network architectures have been proposed, which utilize wireless devices and deployable towers to set up a temporary communication network. However, these architectures often fail to consider the limited availability of network resources due to budgetary constraints. 

To address this problem, we propose a novel network architecture specifically designed for resource-constrained post-disaster scenarios. Our aim is to allocate the limited network resources in a rational manner so that each shelter point is served by at least one network resource and the end-to-end network latency is minimized. To achieve this, we formulate the resource allocation problem as a non-linear programming optimization problem and propose a sub-optimal heuristic for solving it. 

Our experiments conducted on the real map of Durgapur, India, showed that our planned architecture outperforms an unplanned architecture in terms of both delivery probability and end-to-end network latency. Our work highlights the importance of considering resource-constraints in post-disaster relief efforts and provides a practical solution for setting up a communication network in such scenarios.

This paper is based on genetic algorithm to solve the target assignment problem in the course of target reconnaissance. In order to increase the efficiency and improve the local search ability of the genetic algorithm, a hybrid algorithm of genetic algorithm and hill-climbing algorithm is adopted in this paper. And population catastrophe is also used to improve the performance of hybrid algorithm. The simulation results show that the improved algorithm has faster solution speed, better optimization capability, and can solve target assignment problem effectively.

With the growing consumer credit market, credit scoring has become increasingly important in auto financial companies. However, current modeling techniques that exclude rejected applicants and an imbalanced distribution of accepted examples lead to suboptimal predictive performance. This paper proposes a new credit scoring framework that leverages imbalanced-learning-based reject inference. 

Firstly, an imbalanced learning approach is utilized to upsample the accepted applicant data using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique. Next, reject inference is conducted for rejected applicants based on graph-based semi-supervised learning using the label propagation algorithm. Afterwards, tree-based ensemble learning models are used as base classifiers to train the combined training data. Finally, an evaluation experiment on data from a Chinese auto loan company is conducted to assess the proposed framework. 

The results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms comparative models, providing a promising solution for credit scoring in the auto financing industry.

Sparse representation plays a crucial role in numerous applications, including image denoising and face recognition. Researchers have proposed the use of sparse representation based on regularization, which not only exhibits excellent computational efficiency but also offers a straightforward solution. In this article, we introduce a novel method for sparse representation that utilizes both regularization and Tikhonov regularization. Our face recognition implementation consists of two phases: firstly, we utilize sparse representation-based representation to select the top M suspected classes for each test sample. Secondly, we use our proposed sparse representation method to train the M suspected classes, followed by testing our method with test samples. Our experimental results demonstrate that the new algorithm shows better performance in image classification than existing methods.

With the younger generation's affinity for video games, many teachers now want to incorporate serious games in their classes. However, gamifying their training modules can pose a challenge for these educators. To address this, a light and dual gamification approach is suggested in this article. This approach allows teachers to gradually experiment with game-based teaching tools within their own modules. The approach involves aggregating different resources and implementing a suitable gamification process to monitor progress. By adopting this method, teachers can effectively incorporate gaming elements into their teaching methods.

Electrical energy has become the most vital resource in our modern world. However, its access to all parts of the world especially rural areas has not been accomplished. At the same time, rapid exhaustion of fossil fuels, GHG emissions have posed a threat to energy generation. Thus, there is great need to not only find alternate means of energy generation, but also to make it available to all parts of the world. Solar energy is a potential energy source capable of completely resolving our energy demands, but still remains the most underutilized energy resource. In this paper, a standalone solar PV system is developed for a village school as a part of project and awareness initiative for solar energy. The system is designed and simulated using PVsyst 6.7 software. To enhance the system efficiency, maximum power must be extracted. To obtain this, Maximum power point (MPP) tracker is designed, and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK. For more enhancement in extraction of solar power, a prototype model for dual axis tracker with self-cleaning feature is designed and simulated on PROTEUS 8 software.

This paper presents a method for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm with variable step size in order to prevent steady state oscillations. This will avoid the impact of partial shading conditions in the efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems. To optimize power output of the solar panels a DC-DC boost converter is used. Special emphasis is put on software development and implementation in the TMS320F28027 microcontroller in Texas Instruments Code Composer Studio.

Determination of model order is an important task in many problems such as sinusoidal parameter estimation. In this paper we consider the data matrix corresponding to the given sequence and introduce the Ratio of Cumulative Sums (RCS) of eigenvalues. We then exploit the structure of RCS to obtain a performance that is comparable to the Cumulative Sums based method of Shah and Tufts (ST). However the advantage is that we do not require knowledge of the noise level; moreover, our method is computationally cheaper. RCS can also be used in conjunction with existing methods to improve performance: we showcase improved results for Cheng and Hua's least-squares (LS) method when RCS information is used. When there are three closely spaced sinusoids, our method outperforms both the ST and LS methods.

Mobile cloud computing systems, or simply mobile clouds, have attracted tremendous attention because they allow mobile devices with limited computational resources to offload complex computations. However, due to the channel uncertainty and the complexity of a computation task, mobile computation offloading may suffer from poor outage performance that the offloaded task cannot be completed within the desired delay constraint. Thus, how to efficiently identify and overcome the outage bottleneck, which could be used to optimize resource allocation schemes and improve the system performance effectively is an open problem. In this paper, we shall develop a unified framework that minimizes the overall outage probability in various mobile computation offloading scenarios.
