Based on the hierarchical structure of multi-layered RWN, we proposed a multi-channel utilization scheme for local data delivery in robot clusters. The joint design of local data sharing via robot clustering and multi-channel utilization increases the available wireless resources for accommodating of the increasing number of service robots. Quantitative analysis results illustrate that the proposed channel separation-and-sharing system increases significantly the capability of robot accommodation and improve the channel availability. Furthermore, the preliminary experiment results confirm the functionality of the proposed system.

In the field of multi-robots, various research works have addressed the problem of coordination and task division between robots. Coordination in a multi-robot system is necessary when they collaborate to perform a given task or simultaneously share the same resources. The coordination aims to ensure that each robot in the multi-robot system (MRS) performs its tasks safely. As well as a good method of distribution and assignment of tasks must be effective, reliable and well-defined. In this work, we will present a conceptual architecture, that ensures coordination between the entire team of heterogeneous robots and then a new strategy based on artificial intelligence algorithms to assign tasks for a heterogeneous MRS in the optimal way.

Scene classification and semantic segmentation are two fundamental fields of research in computer vision that play an integral role in numerous applications like automatic driving and human-computer interaction. The primary goal of scene classification is to analyze the background and target object in an image and classify it into a specific scene category utilizing the image classification technique. On the other hand, semantic segmentation aims to classify each pixel in an image and assign a label to it, identifying the position and semantic information of the scene unit.

This paper's primary objective is to train the semantic segmentation neural network using various scenarios to obtain models with a similar number of scene categories. This ensures that the models can process the input images adequately. During the testing phase, we segmented the semantic segmentation dataset into three categories based on the scene classification algorithm. We then trained the semantic segmentation neural network in three different scenarios and obtained three corresponding models.

To test the models' performance, we selected the segmentation models obtained and applied them to other pictures. The results of the scene-aware semantic segmentation were significantly better than semantic segmentation without considering categories. Our study makes a significant contribution to the improvement of semantic segmentation by including category information in model training. This approach can result in more precise models, ensuring better picture analysis in the future.

Kinship verification from facial features remains a challenging task, despite attracting increasing attention in recent years. Previous methods have struggled to accurately predict kinship based solely on facial appearance, while early attempts at utilizing deep convolutional neural networks have been held back by limited training data. To overcome this obstacle, our proposed approach combines color features with extreme learning machines (ELM), allowing us to better handle smaller training sets while enhancing the predictive power of our model. We tested our methodology on three popular kinship databases, KinFaceW-I, KinFaceW-II, and TSKinFace, achieving results that compare favorably to some of the best-performing techniques currently in use, including those based on deep learning.

The presence of IoT networks in our daily lives has led to increasing research to improve its reliability and stability, particularly for mission critical systems such as health-related IoT networks. One major bottleneck in these networks is the Gateways (GW), which handle all traffic flowing from sensors to the backend cloud. These GWs are a single point of failure, disrupting critical applications.

To address this issue, we propose an optimized automated workload migration mechanism that allows closely ad-hoc mobile GWs to enhance the reliability and efficiency of mission critical IoT networks. The system uses mobile devices as temporary GWs for nearby IoT networks, improving reliability and efficiency.

The proposed system also includes a multi-objective GW selection mechanism to choose the best GW for each IoT network, ensuring high performance and reducing power consumption. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in minimizing IoT network power consumption and expanding the network's lifetime.

Overall, this approach provides a practical and efficient solution to enhance the reliability and efficiency of mission critical IoT networks, improving their ability to handle critical applications.

Memory-augmented neural networks (MANNs) are designed for question-answering tasks. It is difficult to run a MANN effectively on accelerators designed for other neural networks (NNs), in particular on mobile devices, because MANNs require recurrent data paths and various types of operations related to external memory access. We implement an accelerator for MANNs on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) based on a data flow architecture. Inference times are also reduced by inference thresholding, which is a data-based maximum inner-product search specialized for natural language tasks. Measurements on the bAbI data show that the energy efficiency of the accelerator (FLOPS/kJ) was higher than that of an NVIDIA TITAN V GPU by a factor of about 125, increasing to 140 with inference thresholding.

Current interaction methods for VR/AR headsets need hand-held devices/joysticks, head-mounted cameras or external sensors to detect hand and body movements in order to generate actionable commands. It is not feasible for the people with motor or movement disabilities. In the meanwhile, the current assistive technologies need complicated, cumbersome, and expensive equipment, which are not user-friendly, not portable, and still require certain motor control capabilities from the user. Our approach aims to bridge this gap by developing a compact, non-obtrusive and ergonomic wearable device, to measure physiological signals associated with human eye/facial gestures, and therefore generate simple and intuitive commands to interact with the VR/AR headset. Our innovation uses machine learning and non-invasive biosensors attached on top of the ears (temple positions) to identify eye movements and facial expressions. Through proper design of Human-Machine interactions, we have come up with several engaging human-game multimodal interaction methods by simply moving user's eyes and doing facial expressions. It allows people with motor impairment have a fun time to play VR games with other people, totally "hand-free".

Binary matrix completion (BMC) has become increasingly important in machine learning as it is often used to recover a binary matrix from partial information. This is particularly relevant in cases where only a subset of positive elements can be observed. While convex regularization-based methods are popular, recent applications of nonconvex surrogates in standard matrix completion have demonstrated superior empirical performance. To address this, we propose a novel BMC model that utilizes nonconvex regularizers and provide a guarantee for successful model recovery. Additionally, we improve the proximal algorithm with acceleration strategies to solve the resultant nonconvex optimization problem. Our algorithm guarantees a convergence rate on the order of 1/T, where T is the number of iterations. Through extensive experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world data sets, we demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms other competing methods.

Applications of wireless sensor networks span from the agricultural field to the battlefield and from smart city to smart city health care. There are certain applications where millions of sensor nodes or motes are deployed to sense the environmental parameters. However, in certain applications like health care and smart city applications, few hundreds of nodes can solve the purpose. Routing in energy-constrained networks like WSN is a challenging task. Parameters like consumed energy, congestion and signal to noise ratio etc. are considered to find a routing path in WSN. The Survival Path Routing (SPR) protocol is an earlier version of the work proposed here. The said protocol fails to provide a better result when the number of nodes in the network is increased. Thus a Scalable Survival Path Routing (SSPR) protocol is proposed where the method of clustering is applied to meet the efficiency of a scalable network. Weights of the nodes are computed to choose the cluster heads among them. It is observed that the proposed protocol SSPR outperforms SPR and Directed Diffusion protocol in terms of packet delivery ratio, end to end delay and throughput.

This paper demonstrates how different machine learning techniques performed on a recent, partially labeled dataset (based on the Locked Shields 2017 exercise) and which features were deemed important. Moreover, a cybersecurity expert analyzed the results and validated that the models were able to classify the known intrusions as malicious and that they discovered new attacks. In a set of 500 detected anomalies, 50 previously unknown intrusions were found. Given that such observations are uncommon, this indicates how well an unlabeled dataset can be used to construct and to evaluate a network intrusion detection system.

In recent times, many network operators have started offering content delivery network (CDN) services that utilize traffic engineering techniques such as base station (BS) association, along with content delivery, to reduce network operating costs and improve the quality of service (QoS) for end-users. In this paper, we focus on the BS association and file caching problem while taking into account the spatial diversity of file popularity and the separation between file caching and BS association decisions. Our objective is to minimize file delivery latency and operating power consumption in cellular networks by controlling the tradeoff between these two objectives with a single parameter.

We propose a design that solves the short time-scale BS association problem using convex optimization techniques, conditioned on the file caching solution. However, the long time-scale file caching problem, which considers the varying BS association decisions taken at the short time-scale, is challenging to solve. To tackle this, we prove and leverage the submodularity of the underlying objective function to develop a greedy content caching algorithm that provides a constant approximation ratio of the optimal objective value.

Our simulation results, utilizing real-world datasets, demonstrate that our proposed algorithms outperform file caching and BS association algorithms that do not consider the spatial diversity of file popularity, in terms of power consumption and delay performance in the geographically heterogeneous file popularity scenario.

Selecting the number of assents to obtain the maximized expected return under the possible lowest risk is the main concern of portfolio optimization problems. Optimization algorithms -multi/many-objective- are evaluated to find the desired/possible level of investment. Converging to the best possible asset set and -if possible- distribution of the many possible solution sets for an efficient frontier is expected as the result of the multi/many-objective optimization algorithms. Obtaining an accurate and well-distributed set of solutions is the main motivation. Hence, in this paper, two initialization approaches are proposed for multi/many-objective optimization algorithms to obtain a better convergence and distribution solution set for the portfolio optimization problem. The initial population set is composed of the assets with the largest income and binary combinations of the assets where their sum returns the maximum income. These proposed approaches are integrated with eight different optimization algorithms and the performance of the algorithms is compared with respect to the convergence and diversity metrics.

The semi-formal verification method, in which the functionality is formally specified and the checking is undertaken through the formal model-based simulation, has been a promising choice for the functional verification of hardware designs. The existing methods derive the formal model from design implementation. This causes poor scalability and practicality. A more feasible solution is to derive the formal model directly from the specification. In this paper, we propose a specification-based semi-formal method for functional verification. The proposed semi-formal method uses a stage transition graph (STG) model to formally describe the function points in the specification. Meanwhile, we propose an automatic test pattern generation (ATPG) method to generate the test vectors based on the STG model. The proposed STG-based ATPG method can reach possible corner cases and ensure exhaustive exploration of functionality for both control-dominated designs and data-dominated designs. Moreover, we develop an STG-based tool for automatic verification. Our experiments show that our method can automatically verify the functional correctness from the specification while achieving similar code coverage as implementation-based semi-formal approaches.

The variant of recurrent neural networks (RNN) such as long short-term memory (LSTM) is successful in sequence modelling such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) framework. However the decoded sequence is prune to have false substitutions, insertions and deletions. We exploit the spectral flatness measure (SFM) computed on the magnitude linear prediction (LP) spectrum to detect two broad manners of articulation namely sonorants and obstruents. In this paper, we modify the posteriors generated at the output layer of LSTM according to the manner of articulation detection. The modified posteriors are given to the conventional decoding graph to minimize the false substitutions and insertions. The proposed method decreased the phone error rate (PER) by nearly 0.7 % and 0.3 % when evaluated on core TIMIT test corpus as compared to the conventional decoding involved in the deep neural networks (DNN) and the state of the art LSTM respectively.

This paper deals with the description of a newly practiced method of teaching in EI. CESI, a French engineering school. This method called "The Active Project-Based Learning" (APBL) belongs to an emergent trend of innovative and active learning methods. The APBL approach has as a goal to eliminate the drawbacks of the classical education methods, which are often based on an almost unidirectional teacher speech, an unbalance in the amounts of information exchange and interaction between the transmitter (the teacher) and the receiver (the learner). Moreover, clearly, the great quantity of knowledge flow, the inactivity of the learner, a certain monotony of the teacher speech and finally the abstract character of some scientific fields are critical factors of risk and failure of the conventional method. This is more and more true face to a new generation growing in a digital environment where media and digital tools are preponderant. Consequently, the "old" conventional method has reached its limitation. In opposition to the conventional method, the APBL puts the student in the center of the learning mechanism. The learning is based rather on a flexible and dynamic interaction between the teacher and the student. he teacher ensures a role of coaching and accompanying the learner to reach the preplanned pedagogical goal with an easier and a faster way on a hand and with a greater chance of success on the other hand. The student can trust more and more in his capacities and can manage better, organize and customize his own learning process. Organizing studies by project will increase the student autonomy and will set up a similar context of professional work of an engineer in a company. Finally, elementary steps of the project are defined to ensure a continual improvement process, by following the PDCA process (P-Plan, D-Do, Check, A-Act), a widely used management method in industry. These are the great outlines of the APBL method, its expected results and impacts on the quality and efficiency of learning.

This paper deals with a class of inertial quaternion-valued high-order Hopfield neural networks with state-dependent delays. Without decomposing the considered neural networks into real-valued systems, based on a continuation theorem of coincidence degree theory and the Wirtinger inequality, the existence of anti-periodic solutions of the networks is established. By constructing a suitable Lyapunov function, the global exponential stability of anti-periodic solutions of the networks is obtained. Finally, a numerical example is given to show the feasibility of our results.

Current approaches to brain-machine interface (BMI) rehabilitation often concentrate on a particular aspect of neural activity. However, auxiliary signals, which are obtained from independent measurements of neural activity and recorded simultaneously, may be useful in measuring and monitoring a patient's mental state and performance. In this study, we have found that event-related potentials can be reliably detected in stroke survivors with chronic paralysis undergoing BMI intervention. The mean evoked response remains consistent over multiple sessions but differs among individuals. An apparent negativity and positivity complex develops, and its characteristics can be monitored across subjects and sessions.

The concept of Security Aware Routing is not widely adopted in current networks. However, the new IoT-centric core networks give possibilities to re-open that field of research. We consider routing to be an addition to existing network security methods, especially in IoT domain. Security-aware routing incorporates the security and safety metrics to the traditional set of metrics (bandwidth, network delay, hop count, path cost, load etc.). The paper shows a new approach in which, based on the Software Defined Networks (SDN) we estimate trust relationships between nodes and flows and use them to create SDN paths, based on the Cognitive Packet Network (CPN) principle. The Random Neural Networks (RNN) supported with cognitive packets are used for making routing decisions. The proposed solution was designed and is being implemented within the SerIoT project to demonstrate secure networks for the Internet of Things (IoT).

Accurately modeling and predicting wireless channel quality variations is essential for a number of networking applications such as scheduling and improved video streaming over 4G LTE networks and bit rate adaptation for improved performance in WiFi networks. In this paper, we propose an encoder-decoder based sequence-to-sequence deep learning model that is capable of predicting future wireless signal strength variations based on past signal strength data. We consider two different versions of the deep learning model; the first and second versions use LSTM and GRU as their basic cell structure, respectively. In contrast to prior work that is primarily focused on designing models for particular network settings, the deep learning model is highly adaptable and can predict future channel conditions for different networks, sampling rates, mobility patterns, and communication standards. We compare the performance (i.e., the root mean squared error of future predictions) of our model with respect to two baselines-i) auto-regression(1), and ii) linear regression for multiple networks and communication standards. In particular, we consider 4G LTE, WiFi, an industrial network operating in the 5.8 GHz range, Zigbee, and WiMAX networks operating under varying levels of user mobility and observe that the deep learning model provides significantly superior performance. Finally, we provide detailed discussion on key design decisions including insights into hyper-parameter tuning of the model.

Based on expert system, fuzzy logic, neural network and grinding theory, an intelligent control system for grinding process was proposed. The system is constructed by grinding parameter decision support system (DSS), size prediction control system (SPCS) and roughness prediction control system (RPCS) The initial grinding parameters are decided by the grinding parameter decision support system (DSS) based on neural network. Size prediction control system (SPCS) is constructed by fuzzy control subsystem, deformation control subsystem and size prediction subsystem. The first and the second derivative of the actual amount removed from the workpiece are added into the network input, which can greatly improve the size prediction accuracy. The roughness prediction control system (RPCS) is made from surface roughness prediction subsystem and fuzzy neural network controller, which can adapt grinding parameters in process to decrease the surface roughness of machined parts when the roughness is not meeting requirements. The experiment of the external cylindrical grinding was implemented. The results showed that this intelligent control system was feasible, and could significantly increase the grinding quality.

Motor imagery electroencephalogram (EEG) is a brain signal induced by subjective consciousness that has been studied in the field of sports rehabilitation. It has been found to promote the recovery of damaged nerves and the reconstruction of motor pathways. To this end, a human-brain cooperative control strategy for a pneumatic muscle-driven ankle rehabilitation robot based on motor imagery EEG has been proposed in this paper. The robots provide assisted rehabilitation training for patients with impaired neural transmission who have movement intentions. 

A brain network algorithm was used to select the optimal channels for the motor imagery signal. The common spatial pattern (CSP) method was applied with the time-frequency analysis method local characteristic-scale decomposition (LCD) to extract time-frequency information. The classification was processed by a spectral regression discriminant analysis (SRDA) classifier. Two rehabilitation training modes were designed: synchronous and asynchronous rehabilitation training. 

Experimental results have proven that a brain intention driven human-robot cooperative control method is effective for completing ankle rehabilitation training tasks. This strategy has significant implications for the field of sports rehabilitation, as it provides a non-invasive solution to promote nerve recovery and reconstruct motor nerve pathways.

The recently proposed posit number system is more accurate and can provide a wider dynamic range than the conventional IEEE754-2008 floating-point numbers. Its nonuniform data representation makes it suitable in deep learning applications. Posit adder and posit multiplier have been well developed recently in the literature. However, the use of posit in fused arithmetic unit has not been investigated yet. In order to facilitate the use of posit number format in deep learning applications, in this paper, an efficient architecture of posit multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit is proposed. Unlike IEEE754-2008 where four standard binary number formats are presented, the posit format is more flexible where the total bitwidth and exponent bitwidth can be any number. Therefore, in this proposed design, bitwidths of all datapath are parameterized and a posit MAC unit generator written in C language is proposed. The proposed generator can generate Verilog HDL code of posit MAC unit for any given total bitwidth and exponent bitwidth. The code generated by the generator is a combinational design, however a 5-stage pipeline strategy is also presented and analyzed in this paper. The worst case delay, area, and power consumption of the generated MAC unit under STM-28nm library with different bitwidth choices are provided and analyzed.

Recently, the use of reinforcement-learning algorithms has been proposed to create value and policy functions, and their effectiveness has been demonstrated using Go, Chess, and Shogi. In previous studies, the policy function was trained to predict the search probabilities of each move output by Monte Carlo tree search; thus, a number of simulations were required to obtain the search probabilities. We propose a reinforcement-learning algorithm with game of self-play to create value and policy functions such that the policy function is trained directly from the game results without the search probabilities. In this study, we use Hex, a board game developed by Piet Hein, to evaluate the proposed method. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed learning algorithm in terms of the policy function accuracy, and play a tournament with the proposed computer Hex algorithm DeepEZO and 2017 world-champion programs. The tournament results demonstrate that DeepEZO outperforms all programs. DeepEZO achieved a winning percentage of 79.3% against the world-champion program MoHex2.0 under the same search conditions on 13 × 13 board. We also show that the highly accurate policy functions can be created by training the policy functions to increase the number of moves to be searched in the loser position.

The article explores fundamental image contrasting algorithms and noise compensation approaches, alongside a methodology for estimating image quality based on an integral quality indicator. Furthermore, it delves into various means of calculating noise value within images. The findings from assessing the effectiveness of contrast algorithms (including numerical estimations) and the most notable image filtering techniques are detailed. An automated image enhancement algorithm, derived from a mobile synthetic vision system, is explained, which employs a contrasting algorithm selection module and an integral quality indicator. Additionally, a space-time filter, applied through a pyramidal version of the Lucas-Kanade optical flow algorithm, is proposed.

As genome sequencing continues to become more cost-effective and affordable, more raw and aligned genomic files are expected to be generated in future years. In addition, due to the increase in the throughput of sequencing machines, the size of these files is significantly growing. In particular, aligned files (e.g., SAM/BAM) are used for further processing of the data, and hence efficient representation of these files is a pressing need. In this work we present AliCo, a new compression method tailored to the aligned data represented in the SAM format. We demonstrate through simulations on existing datasets that AliCo outperforms in compression ratio, on average, the state-of-the-art compressors for SAM files, achieving more than 85% reduction in size when operating in its lossless mode. AliCo also supports a variety of modes for lossy compression of the quality scores, including for the first time the recently proposed lossy compressor CALQ, which uses information from the aligned reads to adjust the level of quantization for each location of the genome (achieving more than 10× compression gains in high-coverage datasets). AliCo also supports optional compression of the reference sequence used for compression, hence guaranteeing exact reconstruction of the compressed data. Finally, AliCo allows to stream the data as it is being compressed, as well as to decompress the data as it is being received, potentially providing significant time savings. AliCo can be accessed at: https://github.com/iochoa/alico.

Surface-hardened steels, commonly used in industrial components such as cam and gears, require accurate surface-hardness (SH) prediction for quality assessment. In this paper, an intelligent approach for automatic SH prediction model establishment is proposed. The approach consists of three key steps. Firstly, hysteresis loops (HLs) are measured from surface-hardened steel rods with different SHs using a sensor. Next, a binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) feature selection is applied to automatically select an optimal feature subset from the measured HLs signal. Finally, a single-layer feedforward neural network (FNN) model is utilized to establish a relationship between the selected features and SH. Through experimentation, the intelligent method demonstrated the automatic establishment of SH prediction models. Moreover, the optimal feature subset-based single-layer FNN model was able to accurately predict SHs in surface-hardened steel rods with a prediction error of only 0.298%. Results indicate that the intelligent approach can be integrated into an industrial robot to predict SH in surface-hardened steel rods.

A prediction method based on Elman neural network is proposed to achieve dynamic ankle moment decoding from surface electromyography (sEMG). The method uses smoothed filtering normalized sEMG signal, thigh angle, and shank angle as input variables, and the ankle moment obtained by the Newton-Euler inverse dynamics method as the expected output of the network. A network prediction model based on Elman training algorithm is established, which is employed to carry out a dynamic prediction experiment of ankle moment during normal walking. The results show that the Elman neural network forecasting method utilizing surface electromyography signal and thigh/shank angle as input variables is effective, with an average correlation of 0.979 and an average normalized root mean square error of 0.116. The method's accuracy and validity are confirmed, making it useful as an interface for the control research of lower extremity exoskeleton robots.

A sketch is useful as a communication tool. By expressing ideas using sketches, we can explain the information we want to convey to others in an easy-to-understand way. In general, learning sketches is done by experienced teacher feedback. If we can do this approach with technology, we can expect to provide sketch education opportunities to many people. In our system, utilizing the fact that cube sketch can be evaluated by perspective, we recognize and evaluate the sketch of the learner's cube and educate sketch acquisition by feeding back the mistake. The developed system is evaluated by testing whether the handwritten cube can be recognized and whether we can point out the mistakes of the learner's cube correctly.

Unknown input estimation have a major importance in real-time monitoring, diagnosis and fault-tolerance control. Consequently, this paper concentrates on state estimation for nonlinear system where a part of its inputs is unknown. In particular, the problem is oriented towards an experiential application for laboratory three tank system affected by actuator faults. Our objective is to perform the fault detection (FE) by the synthesis and the implementation of the unknown input observer (UIO). Simulation and experimental results confirm the performance of the suggested observer.

Proximity identification is widely used in various applications to provide users with convenience and efficiency. However, these applications are vulnerable to different attacks, including skimming, eavesdropping, and relay attacks. To address these concerns, modern mobile devices come equipped with sophisticated sensors and receivers that collect and compare information retrieved from the environment. In this paper, we propose multiple physical security features accessible via smart devices, namely RSSI, round-trip time, GPS coordinates, and Wi-Fi access point lists, to identify two devices' close proximity. These security features efficiently offer proof of physical proximity. We evaluate each physical security feature individually through real-life experiments to demonstrate their efficacy in identifying environment characteristics. We then evaluate the performance of each security feature using the Wilcoxon test, which shows that the proposed security features are effective in identifying physical proximity and can be combined for greater accuracy.

Fifth Generation (5G) Cloud-Radio Access Networks (C-RANs) are set to utilize both optical and Millimeter Wave (mmWave) technology to meet the ever-increasing demands for data traffic. In order to achieve an efficient Medium Transparent-Medium Access Control (MT-MAC) protocol that meets the strict requirements of 5G services, a new converged Fiber-Wireless (FiWi) system will be needed. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an MT-MAC protocol for mmWave Analog Radio-over-Fiber (A-RoF) C-RANs. Our protocol employs gated service, which grants users transmission windows equal to the number of bytes contained in their buffer. 

In addition to our proposal, we also provide an analytical model for the mean packet delay. This model has been verified by simulations under various fiber length values, network load conditions, and optical capacity values. The results of these simulations confirm not only the accuracy of our proposed model, but also the adaptability of the proposed MT-MAC protocol to meet the sub-ms delay challenge of latency-critical 5G network requirements. 

Overall, our proposed MT-MAC protocol for mmWave A-RoF C-RANs provides a reliable and efficient solution for managing the high data traffic demand of 5G networks.

In this paper, we present a critical analysis of the current Network Function Virtualization (NFV) model and highlight the challenges that system integrators may face while implementing 5G networks. Fundamentally, NFV leverages cloud computing principles in the domain of networking and telecommunications. It promises a flexible and programmable infrastructure that can support a multitude of services while eliminating the risks of a single vendor lock-in. This is achieved by transitioning the core functionalities from dedicated hardware, such as packet processors or DSPs, to virtualized environments that operate on general-purpose CPU cores.

Previous research has suggested that muscle synergies are the fundamental units used by the central nervous system to generate movements. In this study, we aimed to investigate the construction of reaching movements across different directions and distances by adjusting the recruitment of a few muscle synergies. We recorded electromyographic signals from nine upper limb muscles during reaching movements across six directions and three distances in the horizontal plane. We utilized a non-negative matrix factorization algorithm to extract muscle synergies. Our findings indicated that for each of the eleven participants, three muscle synergies could account for a substantial proportion (88.85±1.68%) of variations in EMG signals across all conditions. 

By examining the activation of synergies in each direction and distance, we discovered that two of the synergies only activated in specific directions. Furthermore, positive correlations existed between their degrees of activation and distance in these directions. Meanwhile, the remaining synergy was nearly activated to the same extent in all directions and distances. Overall, our results suggest that a variety of reaching movements can be controlled by flexibly manipulating the activation of several muscle synergies.

The encoding process in the HEVC standard is much more complex than previous standards due to the heavy involvement of motion estimation which contributes significantly to the complexity. To reduce complexity, the new Test Zone (TZ) search is utilized as a fast search algorithm but it results in a high rate of off-chip memory access leading to high power consumption. However, the current process of finding the best starting search point in TZ search algorithm does not effectively reduce memory access in hardware encoders. To address this issue, a new fast motion estimation algorithm is proposed that estimates a single starting search point and adaptively reduces search range based on information from coded neighboring blocks. Experimental results indicate that this algorithm can reduce the required memory access for ME by approximately 78% and reduce integer ME time by approximately 70%, while achieving only a 1.1% Bjontegaard Delta (BD) Rate.

In recent times, machine learning algorithms have demonstrated their ability to learn complex hierarchical patterns in data while also providing superior generalization. This paper focuses on the learning of intricate fuzzy patterns through the use of a Mamdani Fuzzy Network (MFN) which employs the Mamdani fuzzy inference system. The MFN has an input layer, hidden layers, and an output layer, with each layer utilizing the Mamdani fuzzy inference system as its fundamental building block. The Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) optimization algorithm is used to train the MFN where all parameters in the architecture are identified according to the training data. This methodology is tested on air compressor vibration data that contains 1200 samples with 5 characteristics. The 5 characteristics are passed to the MFN to learn abstract fuzzy representations in the form of multiple distinct fuzzy rule bases with linguistic IF-THEN rules consisting of premise and consequent parts as linguistic labels. The proposed methodology's effectiveness is verified by testing the vibration data sets collected from the air compressor, which are recorded from the most sensitive positions of the compressor under various health conditions.

Optical wireless communications (OWC) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are two burgeoning technologies that are poised to become ubiquitous in the near future. In this paper, we propose an innovative concept that explores the application of OWC in the context of real-time location-based services for IoT. Specifically, we demonstrate how OWC systems, such as visible light communications (VLC), can leverage light-emitting diodes (LEDs) as data transmission nodes that already exist in most consumer electronics.

While existing studies on indoor OWC positioning typically assume that the location of backbone communication network-connected LEDs is provided to the user equipment (UE), we present a scenario where no a priori knowledge of the LED and UE locations is available, and the UE utilizes a single photodetector to measure the received optical intensity. We leverage these measurements to extract distances between the UE and LEDs, which we then use to establish geometric relationships to locate the LEDs. Once we have successfully located the LEDs, we can effectively track the UE using an extended Kalman filter. In addition, we introduce the use of measurements obtained by other members of the OWC-IoT network to further enhance the joint source LED localization and UE tracking process.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the root mean square error of the LED localization can be significantly decreased to just 10 centimeters, which in turn leads to a UE tracking accuracy better than 20 centimeters utilizing our proposed method. Overall, our study highlights the potential of OWC in aiding location-based services for IoT, and opens up exciting avenues for future research in this area.

In this paper, we investigate the outage performance of the proposed relay-user selection (RUS) scheme for amplify-and-forward full-duplex multi-relay multi-user network, where the direct link between the source node and the user node is used to convey information. Meanwhile, each relay node is energy-constrained and the simultaneous wireless information and power transfer technology is employed to harvest energy. A power splitter is equipped in each relay node to split the received signal into energy harvesting part and signal processing part. The closed-form and a simple asymptotic expression for outage probability is provided. Moreover, the optimal power splitting factor of each relay node is calculated to minimize the outage probability of the system. Finally, the numerical simulations are provided to validate the analysis.

This article assesses the current state of development of Intelligent Agents. It begins by providing a detailed explanation of the characteristics that differentiate an agent from regular software code. Additionally, this article investigates the essential components required for Intelligent Agents to achieve success, while simultaneously highlighting the primary challenges they face. To illustrate the goals and objectives of various agent types, a few real-world examples are provided.

This paper is concerned with the model predictive control (MPC) for Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems under the event-triggered mechanism. First, in order to make a rational and effective utilization of the communication resources, the event-triggered mechanism is employed in the network from the controller to the actuator. Second, a “min-max” optimization is put forward to dealing with the MPC problem for systems in the context of T-S fuzzy nonlinearities, and an online auxiliary optimization problem is constructed to obtain sub-optimal feedback gains. Third, by fully taking the influence of the event-triggered mechanism and the T-S fuzzy nonlinearities into consideration, some sufficient conditions are provided to guarantee the input-to-state stability (ISS) for the underlying system. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the robust MPC-based controller for the closed-loop system under the event-triggered mechanism.

In this letter, we consider the problem of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with one-bit quantized array measurements. With analysis, it is shown that, under mild conditions the one-bit covariance matrix can be approximated by the sum of a scaled unquantized covariance matrix and a scaled identity matrix. Although the scaling parameters are unknown because of the extreme quantization, they do not affect the subspace-based DOA estimators. Specifically, the signal and noise subspaces can be straightforwardly determined through the eigendecomposition of the one-bit covariance matrix, without pre-processing such as unquantized covariance matrix reconstruction. With so-obtained subspaces, the most classical multiple signal classification (MUSIC) technique can be applied to determine the signal DOAs. The resulting method is thus termed as one-bit MUSIC. Thanks to the simplicity of this method, it can be very easily implemented in practical applications, whereas the DOA estimation performance is comparable to the case with unquantized covariance matrix reconstruction, as demonstrated by various simulations.

In this research, we illustrate the utilization of Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (Kernel ELM) to classify P300 waves in EEG brain signals. Our aim is to investigate the subject's responses to an oddball paradigm and to propose a selection criteria to enhance the accuracy of classification. We collected and analyzed EEG signals from both healthy subjects and those who suffered a stroke. Our findings demonstrated that with target by block evaluation, we could achieve 100% classification accuracy and an average bitrate of 18.38 bits per minute. These results surpass the performance of various other machine learning algorithms that we compared.

Underwater sensor networks (UWSNs) are vulnerable to jamming attacks due to the narrow frequency bandwidth and the fast fading channels. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based antijamming relay scheme for UWSNs that enables an underwater relay to decide whether to leave the heavily jammed location and choose the relay power based on the state that consists of the bit error rate of the previous transmission, the previous relay power, the current transmit power of the sensor, and the jamming power measured by the relay node. We also propose a deep-RL-based relay scheme to further improve the relay performance for the node that supports deep learning computation. We discuss the computational complexity of the deep-RL-based relay scheme and provide the relay performance bound regarding the bit error rate, energy consumption, and utility of the relay node. Experiments taken in a nonanechoic pool with underwater transducers against smart jamming attacks verify the analysis results. According to the experimental results, the proposed relay scheme can improve the relay performance compared with the benchmark underwater relay schemes.

Process mining is a novel technique that uses event logs stored in information systems to automatically create business process models. This technique enables a comprehensive understanding of the real behavior of processes, facilitating the identification of bottlenecks for improvement. Despite numerous process discovery algorithms being proposed, there remain complexities in some control-flow constructs that challenge accurate identification of models based on event logs. These include short loops, invisible tasks, and non-free choice constructs, which cannot be captured by a single algorithm in a restricted time. In this paper, we present a framework that identifies these complex control-flow constructs from event logs, allowing the selection of an appropriate process model notation or process discovery algorithm for the given event log. The framework has been implemented in ProM, and the results indicate accurate identification of the constructs.

The classic midpoint method for triangulation is extremely fast, but usually labelled as inaccurate. We investigate the cost function that the midpoint method tries to minimize, and the result shows that the midpoint method is prone to underestimate the accuracy of the measurement acquired relatively far from the three-dimensional (3-D) point. Accordingly, the cost function used in this letter is enhanced by assigning a weight to each measurement, which is inversely proportional to the distance between the 3-D point and the corresponding camera center. After analyzing the gradient of the modified cost function, we propose to do minimization by applying fixed-point iterations to find the roots of the gradient. Thus, the proposed method is called the iteratively reweighted midpoint method. In addition, a theoretical study is presented to reveal that the proposed method is an approximation to the Newton's method near the optimal point and, hence, inherits the quadratic convergence rate. Finally, the comparisons of the experimental results on both synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that the proposed method is more efficient than the state-of-the-art while achieves the same level of accuracy.

To efficiently develop and interoperate smart city applications, smart city IoT platforms must handle various types of sensor devices, networking and computing resources, and different domain applications. To address this challenge, the authors proposed the "Fed4IoT" project, a federation of IoT and cloud infrastructures that provides scalable and interoperable smart city applications. The project's two key technologies are IoT device virtualization and context-information sharing. This paper focuses on the IoT device virtualization, which enables efficient utilization of networking and computing resources by applying micro-service sharing and dynamic resource scaling. To evaluate the performance of the proposed virtualization, the authors implemented three microservices for object detection, garbage detection, and road damage detection, and dynamically allocated computing resources to optimize performance using Docker and Kubernetes. The evaluations showed that the proposed IoT device virtualization can efficiently utilize computing resources while reducing networking resources.

This paper proposes a novel low-complexity training symbol for OFDM signals in burst mode which serves the purpose of both time and frequency synchronization. The proposed training symbol utilizes a set of special codes that possess the lowest peak-to-average power ratio as compared to other codes with ±1 mapping. Additionally, these codes exhibit high auto-correlation functions, which are utilized to design an algorithm for time and frequency synchronization of the OFDM signals. The algorithm employs an integer frequency-error estimation technique and has been shown to outperform other algorithms suggested in the literature. Notably, the proposed algorithm is efficient in handling Raleigh mobile channels and adverse Doppler shifts. Overall, the proposed method represents a significant contribution to the field of OFDM signal synchronization, offering a low-complexity and effective solution.

Providing seamless connectivity to mobile users on-board railway vehicles is quickly gaining ground as part of the society in motion. Today, the main challenge for academia and industry coping with service quality improvements for smartphone users stems from a few tens of decibels vehicle penetration loss impacting mobile communication frequencies. To deal with this, we demonstrate two designs such as frequency selective surface- and amplify-and-forward repeater-aided railway vehicles. In this paper, we use the rank-based nonparametric inferential approach to assess the service quality improvements of various smartphone placements' on-board railway vehicles. As part of the presented framework, we demonstrate the problem of characterizing vehicle penetration loss along particular railway tracks. All in all, the proposed framework is evaluated on inter-city and regional trains as well as over two heavy-traffic railway environments in Austria. The smartphone users placed next to frequency selective surface structures as well as in the proximity of an amplify-and-forward repeater are shown to gain in coverage the most.

The power load of residential communities is characterized by wild fluctuations, complex influence factors, and difficult forecasting. To address this issue, a short-term load forecasting method based on gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural networks was proposed. The method utilizes least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso) and partial correlation analysis to analyze the impact of temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind speed on load. Results showed that average temperature has the greatest impact on load change among various factors, leading to the addition of average temperature as an input variable in the load forecasting model based on GRU network. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed method is faster than long short-term memory (LSTM) networks and traditional recurrent neural networks (RNN) while retaining similar accuracy, thus proving to be a highly effective residential community short-term load forecasting method.

A sophisticated and efficient network slicing architecture is required to support the orchestration of network slices across multiple administrative domains. This multi-domain architecture must be independent of the underlying virtualization and network infrastructure technologies. Its objective is to enhance the traditional orchestration, management, and control capabilities through models and constructs to form a well-coordinated composition of network slices.

To ensure that networking and compute/storage resources can be combined seamlessly, this article proposes a management and orchestration architecture that leverages Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) components in addition to the basic 3GPP network slice management. The proposed architecture is divided into four major strata:

1. Multi-domain Service Conductor Stratum: This stratum coordinates and manages the service requests received from different administrative domains.

2. Domain-specific Fully-Fledged Orchestration Stratum: This stratum is responsible for orchestrating and managing network slices within a specific administrative domain.

3. Sub-Domain MANO and Connectivity Stratum: This stratum is responsible for managing network slices within small administrative domains.

4. Logical Multi-domain Slice Instance Stratum: This stratum is responsible for creating and managing federated network slices that span multiple administrative domains.

Each of these strata is described in detail, providing the necessary operational specifics for instantiating and managing the resulting federated network slices. By incorporating SDN and NFV components alongside traditional network slice management, this architecture enhances the overall efficiency and coordination of network slicing across multiple administrative domains.

Lip reading, the ability to recognize text information from the movement of a speaker's mouth, is a difficult and challenging task. Recently, the end-to-end model that maps a variable-length sequence of video frames to text performs poorly in real life situation where people unintentionally move the lips instead of speaking. The goal of this work is to improve the performance of lip reading task in real life. The model proposed in this article consists of two networks that are visual to audio feature network and audio feature to text network. Our experiments showed that the model proposed in this article can achieve 92.76% accuracy in lip reading task on the dataset that the unintentional lips movement was added.

The estimation of the fundamental matrix using the RANSAC algorithm can be challenging when the outlier ratio is high due to issues related to computational inefficiency and low accuracy. However, an optimized approach based on modifications to the RANSAC algorithm has been introduced in this article. The proposed technique makes use of an isolation forest algorithm to detect outliers in putative SIFT correspondences based on the consistency of features in location, scale, and orientation. The detection of these outliers eliminates several obvious correspondences, effectively improving the inlier ratio. Ultimately, the fundamental matrix estimation is performed using the optimized set, leading to impressive results, as demonstrated through multiple experiments. It was observed that this method resulted in a remarkable increase in speed and accuracy compared to the RANSAC algorithm.

Recently, significant attention has been given by the semiconductor industry to the benefits of Three-dimensional integrated circuits (3-D ICs), which provide a high degree of integration and high bandwidth. However, these chips have through-silicon vias (TSVs) that vertically connect multiple dies, and faulty TSVs could fail, leading to a reduced yield. While previous methods for repairing TSVs have been proposed, they cannot handle certain failure patterns, such as clustered TSV faults that commonly occur. Additionally, the number of redundant TSVs is typically determined by the number of signal TSVs, leading to wasteful redundancies. The proposed method replaces defective TSVs with redundant TSVs by utilizing the architecture of a cube that can replace any face with another. Hence, both signal and redundant TSVs are positioned on the face of the cube, allowing for the replacement of faulted TSVs with redundant ones. The experimental results of this new method indicate that it guarantees 100% coverage with any number of signal and redundant TSVs.

Auscultation of heart sounds is usually used as an important way to identify symptoms of heart disease. In this case the experts need to concentrate on diagnosing heart sound abnormalities in humans. Finding various characteristics to classify heart sounds according to the group is a very important part. This research was made to improve the results based on previous research which still had an accuracy rate of 92%. Heart collection obtained from the Michigan Sound Heart Database. Data used only on the apex. The Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) method is used to extract heart sound features, while for classification from the results of heart sound extraction using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method. Based on the results of this study, the accuracy reaches 100%.

We propose a novel optimization control strategy that integrates model-based optimization and square-wave extremum seeking control to optimize the efficiency of permanent-magnet synchronous machines using direct torque control (PMSM-DTC). Ordinary efficiency-optimization methods tend to require a precise mathematical model of the PMSM for estimating the optimal stator flux. Model-based optimization can rapidly shift the optimal parameters when operating conditions change. However, deviation in the stator flux estimation will occur if variation of the internal parameters is considered. The strategy proposed in this paper allows rapid switching of optimal parameters, and uses square-wave extremum seeking control to offset the deviation in the stator flux estimation quickly. The latter control scheme, ensures that the system always runs near the optimal point.

This paper describes a real-time voltage sag monitoring system based on S-Transform analysis. The system extracts and analyzes real-time signal features using LabVIEW software, with a data acquisition module for voltage measurement used to capture voltage sag events generated by Three Phase Chroma Programming AC Source. The S-transform algorithm is utilized to identify significant features of voltage sag for accurate detection. The efficacy of this technique is compared and validated against theoretical types of voltage sag events in terms of magnitude and phase angle jump. The results demonstrate that the S-transform algorithm is superior in providing an accurate analysis for monitoring voltage sag activity.

Due to the space inconsistency between benchmark image and segmentation result in many existing semantic segmentation algorithms for abdominal CT images, an improved model based on the basic framework of DeepLab-v3 is proposed, and Pix2pix network is introduced as the generation adversarial model. Our proposed model realizes the segmentation framework combining deep feature with multi-scale semantic feature. In order to improve the generalization ability and training accuracy of the model, this paper proposes a combination of the traditional multi-classification cross-entropy loss function with the content loss function of generator output and the adversarial loss function of discriminator output. A large number of qualitative and quantitative experimental results show that the performance of our proposed semantic segmentation algorithm is better than the existing algorithms, and can improve the segmentation efficiency while ensuring the space consistency of the semantics segmentation for abdominal CT images.

Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and physical layer network coding (PNC) are both techniques that offer high spectral efficiencies. When used in conjunction in a parallel relay channel, they have the potential to greatly enhance spectral efficiency. However, simultaneous parallel communication can result in additional interference that may limit the overall capacity gain. 

This paper explores the potential throughput enhancement achieved through the use of NOMA in PNC coded parallel relay channels, as compared to conventional PNC coded parallel relay channels where the two communications occur in distinct time-slots. Our analysis shows that joint NOMA and PNC in parallel relay channels achieves considerable throughput enhancement.

In multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems that employ pilot-symbol aided channel estimation, the pilot-to-data power ratio (PDPR) has a large impact on the system performance. In this paper, we consider the problem of setting the PDPR in multi-cell MU-MIMO systems in the presence of channel estimation errors, intercell interference and pilot contamination. To analyze and address this problem, we first develop a model of the multi-cell MU-MIMO system and derive a closed-form expression for the mean squared error of the uplink received data symbols. Building on this result, we then propose two decentralized PDPR-setting algorithms based on game theoretic approaches that are applicable in multi-cell systems. We find that both algorithms converge to a Nash equilibrium and provide performance improvements over systems that do not properly set the PDPR, while they maintain different levels of fairness.

We present an algorithm designed to identify the nonlinear dynamics of a specific type of micropositioning systems. These systems are modeled as Hammerstein systems, which comprise a generalized Prandtl-Ishlinskii (GPI) hysteresis nonlinearity and a linear dynamic system arranged in a cascade. Moreover, the GPI nonlinearity, the linear dynamic system, and the intermediate signal between them are assumed to be unidentified. 

The algorithm consists of three main steps. Firstly, the linear dynamic plant is identified using the input and output measurements from the Hammerstein system. Subsequently, the unknown intermediate signal is reconstructed by employing the output and the identified model of the linear system. Finally, the GPI nonlinearity is estimated by using the input and the reconstructed intermediate signal. 

This algorithm will provide a valuable tool for characterizing the nonlinear dynamics of smart micropositioning systems. It has the potential to enhance the performance of these systems and improve their accuracy, which can positively impact fields that rely on micropositioning, such as robotics and precision manufacturing.

Fog computing extends cloud computing paradigms to the edge of the network, enabling a new generation of applications and services. This paper mainly elaborates the related background and characteristics of fog computing, discusses the concept and hierarchical structure of fog computing services, compares the advantages of cloud computing and fog computing, analyzes the existing techniques and applications of fog computing, and analyzes possible security issues in fog computing and solutions to some of the security issues.

The frequency-domain Kalman filter (FKF) has been utilized in many audio signal processing applications due to its fast convergence speed and robustness. However, the performance of the FKF in under-modeling situations has not been investigated. This letter presents an analysis of the steady-state behavior of the commonly used diagonalized FKF and reveals that it suffers from a biased solution in under-modeling scenarios. An effective improvement of the FKF is proposed, having the benefits of the guaranteed optimal steady-state behavior at the cost of a very limited increase of computational burden. The convergence behavior of the proposed algorithm is also analyzed. Computer simulations are conducted to validate the improved performance of the proposed method.

This paper proposes a novel framework to encode time series data into two-dimensional (2-D) images, and aggregate the images into one single image to solve multiple time series classification problem. In this research, Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF) and Gramian Angular Difference Field (GADF) were applied to encode time series into images. The proposed image aggregation method which appends multiple images into a single image is suggested. After transformation and aggregation, the 2-D images passed through a convolutional neural network (CNN), which is outstanding in solving computer vision problems, for classification. An open wafer dataset was used to validate the proposed method. The preliminary results of the experiments find that encoding time series data into images and aggregating the images by the appending method are helpful on increasing classification accuracy. The statistical test also showed that the proposed image appending is “order-free” on the sequences of 2-D images.

Named entity recognition is a fundamental task in biomedical text mining. Compared to other methods of named entity recognition, the ones relying on domain relevance measurements require smaller training corpora and entity samples, making them suitable for recognizing narrow-domain entities that are part of a small semantic class. However, obtaining high-quality target corpus sets has proved to be a significant challenge. In this paper, a biomedicine named entity recognition approach that integrates domain contextual relevance measurement and active learning is proposed. 

To begin with, density-based clustering and semantic distance measurement are used to identify representative and informative contexts. These are then used to create a target corpus set through an active learning approach. Next, candidate entities' domain contextual relevance is calculated using Domain discrimination degree and domain dependence function to recognize target entities. The results of experiments show that this approach can considerably reduce training time and enhance entity recognition accuracy.

Electronic health record (EHR) systems have become increasingly popular in developed countries as a means of replacing traditional paper-based health record keeping. However, in developing countries such as Pakistan, the adoption of these systems has been limited by socioeconomic and technological factors. Despite some healthcare providers implementing their own EHRs, there is currently no central electronic repository for patients' health data at the government level. 

To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cloud-based architecture for implementing an EHR system in Pakistani hospitals. By utilizing this architecture, patients will benefit from improved care, diagnostics, and disease presentation, as well as the availability of their electronic health information on a 24/7 basis. Additionally, the cost of maintaining paper-based records will be reduced. 

Implementing an EHR system in this way will not only enable doctors and hospitals to exchange patients' information with each other more easily, but it will also establish a national electronic health data repository. This repository can subsequently be used for a range of purposes, including predictive diagnostics and personalized medicine. 

Overall, the adoption of an EHR system in Pakistani hospitals through a cloud-based architecture will have significant benefits for healthcare providers and patients alike. This proposal represents an important step forward in improving the quality of healthcare in Pakistan, despite socioeconomic and technological constraints.

Prominent closed frequent itemsets (CFIs) are the set of highly frequent closed itemsets whose support is considerably larger than remaining closed itemsets in the given transactional dataset. The support value between the prominent CFIs and remaining closed itemsets make the optimum minimum support threshold as it segregates frequent and infrequent item-sets. However, finding an optimum minimum support threshold for mining prominent CFIs is not known prior especially when the data arriving as a stream. Also, using a static minimum support threshold for mining CFIs from the data stream may lead to missing of some itemsets due to concept drift and lossy counting. In this paper, the authors propose to use dynamic and adaptive minimum support threshold for mining prominent CFIs in the landmark streaming setting. This work is first of its kind and closely relate to Top-K CFI mining techniques. The novelty is in using Jenks natural break technique to dynamically find an optimum minimum support threshold for a landmark window and adaptation to the concept drift through delayed insertion. The proposed method has experimented on some well-known real and synthetic datasets demonstrating its suitability for mining prominent CFIs in transactional data streams.

Reverse referral strategy, i.e. transferring patients from the upper-level hospital (ULH) to the lower-level hospital (LLH) in the same Hospital Alliance, has been proposed to deal with the problem of inappropriate use of medical resource in health care systems. Despite these actions have brought some positive effects, the problem of making optimal decisions for the cooperating hospitals to enforce the reverse referral strategy at an operational level and how the cooperated hospitals will react to each other remains unclear. In this study, we consider a Hospital Alliance comprising an ULH and a LLH with reverse referral. We study how these cooperating hospitals can compromise with each other when both adopt a threshold control policy. The Pareto front and corresponding optimal control policies are obtained through multi-fidelity optimization.

In this paper, the passivity problem is investigated for neural networks of neutral type with Markovian jumping parameters and time-varying delay. By applying novel Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, using reciprocal convex combination method and improved free-matrix-based integral inequality, the delay-dependent criterion for the passivity of the addressed neural networks is established in terms of linear matrix inequalities(LMIs), which can be checked numerically using the effective LMI toolbox in MATLAB. An example with simulations is given to show the effectiveness and less conservatism of the proposed criterion.

Numerous experiments have demonstrated that there are analogous gestures in visual-based gesture recognition. To address this issue, a new algorithm based on Convolution neural network has been proposed in this paper. The testing of the model has led to the establishment of a confusion matrix. Furthermore, based on the relationship between each gesture and its predicted outcome, a misjudgment probability matrix has been developed. With the aid of this matrix, incorrect identification of gestures by the Convolution neural network model has been rectified. The implementation of this algorithm has increased the recognition rate of similar gestures from 5% to 12%. This paper's innovation lies in its secondary error correction of the Convolution neural network structure's incorrect gestures.

This paper introduces a new algorithm for satellite image time series change detection. This algorithm is based on image subtraction analysis and does not directly work on raw images, but on their encoded feature representation version. The encoding is realized with neural network autoencoder. The change detection method is totally unsupervised and does not need any labeled data.

Traffic Signal control optimization is a key element is future smart cities. We present, in this paper, an optimized agent, based on Reinforcement Learning, with Double Deep Q-Learning. Since intersections influence each other, cooperation between agents will be key in our study. For state representation, we use real-time data, that can be collected by a smart camera, as vehicle position and speed. The rewards function will consider the waiting time of drivers, which has the advantage of better representing the case of congestions in large agglomerations. In our network, we will use Convolutional Layers to extract features that will help our model to learn the best actions to take, in every state. This model will be used to solve convergence and oscillation problems that commonly appears in multi-agent context with Neuronal Networks. A future article will present the details of the implementation and the results obtained and will make a comparison between our model and other state-of-art solutions used in the Traffic Signal Control.

In the DV -HOP algorithm of the wireless sensor network, an inaccurate estimation of the minimum hop count and the average hop distance produces a positioning error. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved DV-HOP algorithm. The algorithm reevaluates the average hop distance of the anchor node and corrects the minimum hop count of the node to be located and the anchor node, which reduces the above error. First, the average hop distance of the anchor node closest to the positioned node is reassessed according to the error. Then, the minimum hop count is obtained by the average hop distance of the revaluation, and the correction coefficient of the ratio of the minimum hop count to the actual minimum hop count is obtained, and the minimum hop count of the node to be positioned is corrected by the correction coefficient. Finally, the distance between the node to be located and the anchor node is calculated, and the position of the node to be positioned is calculated by the least squares method. Simulation results show that the improved dv-hop algorithm can reduce the node positioning error and improve the positioning accuracy.

Machine-type communications (MTC) is a technology that is rapidly growing and has revolutionized the development of the Internet of Things (IoT) by providing ubiquitous connectivity and services. Providing such hyper-connectivity is a primary challenge in the cellular-based MTC due to the large number of connection requests. Congestion control mechanisms such as Extended Access Barring (EAB) have been proposed by the 3GPP to overcome this issue. In this paper, we analyze the limitations of EAB's current specification and propose two enhanced EAB schemes to improve key performance indicators.

The first enhanced EAB scheme proposed is the combined use of EAB and access class barring, which improves the success access probability even in heavily congested scenarios. The second enhanced EAB scheme proposes the introduction of a congestion avoidance backoff after the barring status of a User Equipment (UE) is switched to unbarred, which reduces the number of required preamble retransmissions, thereby resulting in energy savings. Our proposed solutions have been extensively simulated, and the results show significant improvement in key performance indicators such as shortened access delay.

Furthermore, we present an accurate congestion estimation method that solely relies on the information available at the base station. This method permits a realistic and effective implementation of the EAB, allowing cellular networks to provide the necessary hyper-connectivity required for MTC. The proposed enhanced EAB schemes and congestion estimation method together provide a robust solution for handling the large number of connection requests, thereby ensuring the successful deployment of MTC in the IoT ecosystem.

In distributed software-defined networks (SDN), multiple physical SDN controllers, each managing a network domain, are implemented to balance centralized control, scalability and reliability requirements. In such networking paradigm, controllers synchronize with each other to maintain a logically centralized network view. Despite various proposals of distributed SDN controller architectures, most existing works only assume that such logically centralized network view can be achieved with some synchronization designs, but the question of how exactly controllers should synchronize with each other to maximize the benefits of synchronization under the eventual consistency assumptions is largely overlooked. To this end, we formulate the controller synchronization problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and apply reinforcement learning techniques combined with deep neural network to train a smart controller synchronization policy, which we call the Deep-Q (DQ) Scheduler. Evaluation results show that DQ Scheduler outperforms the anti-entropy algorithm implemented in the ONOS controller by up to 95.2% for inter-domain routing tasks.

We propose a strategy for resource allocation and clustering in a Femtocell-based cognitive radio heterogeneous network (CR-HetNet) to facilitate handover of both primary and secondary users. Two approaches have been considered- resource allocation-clustering (RC) and joint clustering-resource allocation (JCR). RC allocates resources to Femtocells first and then performs clustering while JCR performs clustering and resource allocation simultaneously. Our numerical results suggest that the utility function of primary and secondary users increases with the number of clusters. However, the number of horizontal handovers reduces within the cluster while it increases between the clusters. Moreover, it reduces energy efficiency and maximum achievable throughput in each cluster. Therefore, a tradeoff exists between the utility function and maximum throughput that can be managed by choosing an appropriate number of clusters and resource allocation. Finally, simulation results and numerical analyses show that this strategy can reduce the handover execution time by 25% compared to the conventional approach of no clustering in a network consisting of 10 Femtocells.

Improving the accuracy of speed predictions for urban roads is essential for traffic monitoring and route planning, and can help alleviate traffic congestion. Existing studies have mainly focused on using convolutional neural networks to capture the spatial proximity among different road segments. However, the real cause of traffic congestion lies in the connectivity of these road segments, making it difficult to improve prediction accuracy. Luckily, graph neural networks (GNNs) can model the connectivity of road segments as a graph, embedding the properties of road segments and connections as nodes and edges. This paper proposes a SeqGNN model that combines the advantages of both sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) models and GNNs. Traffic conditions on road networks are modeled as a sequence of graphs, and the SeqGNN model represents both inputs and outputs as graph sequences. Experimental results using real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach and its superiority compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents a simulation model developed using Arena 14.0 (Rockwell Automation) to manage the transport system of copper deposits. It starts with a review of existing methods that have been used to study the transport system in mining enterprises. The paper then goes on to describe the simulation model of dump trucks moving along pendulum routes in the copper mine. Additionally, alternative methods for arranging the overburden transportation from the mining area are analyzed.

The study applies systematic calculation methods blended with elements of discrete mathematics, in conjunction with discrete event simulation modeling using Arena 14.0 (Rockwell Automation). A computer-based experiment was performed to determine the optimal transportation method for copper ore from the mining area to the ore processing plant. The results of this experiment produced detailed statistics that described the main parameters of the transport system's performance, such as the volume of mine rock being transported, transport utilization rate, downtime percentage, and average number of dump truck haul cycles.

The developed simulation model allows for real-time study of the complex system and the optimization of the number and characteristics of transport. This enables the efficient management of the transport system, ensuring the smooth and efficient transportation of copper from the mining area to the ore processing plant.

This paper develops an approach for household appliance identification and classification of household activities of daily living (ADLs) using residential smart meter data. The process of household appliance identification, i.e., decomposing a mains electricity measurement into each of its constituent individual appliances, is a very challenging classification problem.
