Recent advances have made deep learning a dominant approach for classification in fields, such as image processing and speech recognition. This paper presents a deep learning approach based on multilayer, feedforward neural networks that can identify common household electrical appliances from a typical household smart meter measurement. The performance of this approach is tested and validated using publicly available smart meter data sets. The identified appliances are then mapped to household activities, or ADLs. The resulting ADL classifier can provide insights into the behavior of the household occupants, which has a number of applications in the energy domain and in other fields.

Teeth are important organs in vertebrates. The accurate classification of teeth is beneficial for dentists to diagnose. In this manuscript, we put forward a novel teeth classification algorithm combined principle component analysis and extreme learning machine. Principle component analysis was used to extract features from the teeth images and extreme learning machine served as the classifier. Experimental results suggested that our method is effective in identification of four categories of teeth.

We address the problem of selecting optimal sensors in large-scale dynamical systems by using a suitable convex surrogate for complexity to overcome the combinatorial aspect of the problem. This leads to a non-convex optimization problem that can be solved using a sparsity-promoting framework to select sensors that degrade performance gracefully relative to the optimal Kalman filter that uses all available sensors. The problem can be cast as a semidefinite program using a standard change of variables. To address scalability, we propose a customized proximal gradient method that scales better than standard SDP solvers for large-scale problems. Although proximal Newton method is challenging due to structural features, we investigate alternative second-order extensions using the forward-backward quasi-Newton method.

The railway axlebox is a crucial component of rolling stock, playing a vital role in bearing its weight and minimising friction with the rotating axle. Failure of the axlebox can lead to disastrous consequences, including derailment. Hence, its maintenance is an essential aspect of ensuring safe and efficient train operation. 

This article presents a methodology for creating a standard Health Index that combines expert criteria with recorded vibration data to provide a flexible and granular diagnostic. The proposed approach utilises an auto-encoder neural network to accommodate two approaches: a principal component-based approach and an anomaly detection scheme at the vibration signal level. 

The analysis demonstrates that the former approach results in a smoother and more uncertain index, while the latter provides a sharper and more sensitive index. Both approaches offer unique diagnostic designs to better ensure timely and appropriate maintenance.

Overall, this methodology provides a critical tool for incorporating various expert knowledge and actual vibration data to create a standardised Health Index. By doing so, we hope to increase the safety and efficiency of rolling stock maintenance and operation.

Recommender systems play a crucial role in suggesting new items to users based on their preferences. With the vast amount of information available on the web such as reviews, ratings, and feedback on items, it becomes essential to extract meaningful information from this unstructured data to comprehend user choices. Two common techniques employed for making recommendations are collaborative filtering and content-based filtering. However, in Big Data Systems, where the data volume is extensive, a technique that combines both these approaches can prove to be more efficient.

To address this, a hybrid recommendation technique has been proposed in this paper that combines collaborative and content-based filtering techniques to suggest items that a user is most likely to prefer. The system also uses an item ranking and classification technique to further refine the recommendations. To take user preferences from social media into account, a social media opinion mining technique has also been added to comprehend users' tastes from their social media posts.

A prototype system has been implemented and evaluated based on the proposed hybrid recommendation technique. The results suggest that the combination of collaborative and content-based filtering techniques with social media opinion mining can improve the accuracy of recommendations, especially for users with diverse interests. Overall, the hybrid recommendation technique proposed in this paper can help achieve more personalized and accurate recommendations in Big Data Systems.

Distribution transformers often face issues such as overloading and internal hydration that can cause overheating, deformation, short-circuits, and suffocation of windings. To address these problems, an efficient and reliable Internet of Things (IoT) based Thermal Monitoring and Protection System (TMPS) for DT under residential loading is proposed. 

The proposed system is comprised of a Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and a monitoring station. The RTU consists of diverse feedback control protection systems and wireless communication modules. Temperature and humidity sensing units (THSU) and Current Sensing Units (CSU) installed in the oil immersed windings of DT constantly collect data and send it to ThingSpeak server for real-time monitoring, analysis, and control.

Furthermore, the IoT based TMPS system sends an alert in the form of emails and buzzers to the operator in case of protection failure. The results show that the proposed system has effectively resolved the overloading and internal hydration issue of DT while optimizing costs and reducing human interaction.

We have developed a novel method called QuickCent for estimating network centrality measures. Inspired by fast and frugal heuristics, which model human quantitative estimation processes, our approach is simple and efficient. Specifically, we estimate the harmonic index, a measure based on shortest-path distances, which is infeasible to compute on large networks. We evaluated QuickCent against known machine learning algorithms using synthetic data and found that it achieved robust estimates and low-error variance even with a small training set. Moreover, QuickCent's accuracy and time cost were comparable to more complex methods. Our initial results suggest that incorporating simple heuristics and biologically inspired computational methods may be a promising direction for research in network measure estimation.

Achieving a proper time-frequency (TF) resolution is the key to extract information from seismic data using TF algorithms and characterize reservoir properties using decomposed frequency components. The generalized S-transform (GST) is one of the most widely used TF algorithms. However, it is difficult to choose an optimized parameter set for the whole seismic data set. In this paper, we propose to set the parameters of the GST adaptively using the instantaneous frequency (IF) of seismic traces. Our workflow begins with building a relationship between the parameter set of the GST and IF using a synthetic wedge model. We use the IF as an indicator for the time thickness of each trace in the wedge model. We then compute the TF spectrum of each trace using the GST with different parameter sets and compare the similarity between the computed TF spectrum and theory TF spectrum. The parameter set with the largest similarity is regarded as the best parameter set for each trace in the wedge model. In this manner, we build a relationship between the parameter set and IF value. We can finally choose the optimum parameter set for the GST according to the IF values of seismic traces. We name the proposed workflow as the self-adaptive GST (SAGST). To demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed SAGST, we apply it to synthetic seismic traces and field data. Both synthetic and real data examples illustrate that the SAGST can obtain a TF representation with a high TF resolution.

This paper presents the design, 3-D printing, construction, and testing of a cutting-edge prototype smart wheelchair that employs the Emotive EPOC headset to assist blind and paralyzed individuals who lack control over certain bodily functions. The device utilizes deep learning techniques to identify four different movements based on recorded EEG signals. The four movements recognized by the device include turning left, turning right, advancing forward, and stopping. The device was tested using data from 10 volunteers which demonstrated a success rate of 70% from the row EEG. More impressively, the Fourier Transform of frequency bins that corresponded to the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma waves was able to achieve a remarkable 96% success rate.

These days, based on the recent development in IoT technologies, a large number of innovative healthcare applications should be created. Health Internet of Things (HIoT) is a novel technology that used to connect many diver's medical sensors to IoT devices. The HIoT facilitates remote data collection and monitoring in healthcare fields. This paper is a review study that addresses the impact of HIoT on healthcare applications. In this regards, we investigated the most important technologies used in HIoT and describe the main strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of HIoT-based applications. Based on the results, the potential strengths and opportunities of the HIoT technology is very different and widespread; however, it has some significant weaknesses and threats including complexity of handling a huge number of heterogeneous objects, achieving scalability, reliability, efficiency, availability, security, and interoperability with IoT systems across healthcare applications.

In this paper, Bayesian based aggregation of decision trees in an ensemble (decision forest) is investigated. The focus is laid on multi-class classification with number of samples significantly skewed toward one of the classes. The algorithm leverages out-of-bag datasets to estimate prediction errors of individual trees, which are then used in accordance with the Bayes rule to refine the decision of the ensemble. The algorithm takes prevalence of individual classes into account and does not require setting of any additional parameters related to class weights or decision-score thresholds. Evaluation is based on publicly available datasets as well as on an proprietary dataset comprising network traffic telemetry from hundreds of enterprise networks with over a million of users overall. The aim is to increase the detection capabilities of an operating malware detection system. While we were able to keep precision of the system higher than 94%, that is only 6 out of 100 detections shown to the network administrator are false alarms, we were able to achieve increase of approximately 7% in the number of detections. The algorithm effectively handles large amounts of data, and can be used in conjunction with most of the state-of-the-art algorithms used to train decision forests.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of internet-connected devices that are capable of gathering and exchanging information through embedded sensors. These devices can be anything such as objects, animals or people, and each entity is given a unique identifier which allows for information to be transferred without the need for human-to-computer or human-to-human interaction. While the benefits of the IoT are numerous, security threats are also increasing.

To address this issue, this research project aims to implement an access control policy on each node of the IoT by utilizing context awareness. This approach monitors the context and behavior of IoT nodes in the network and determines the rate of data transfer among them. Nodes that do not follow the policy based on the context are not given access to network resources under this access control framework.

This work utilizes ontology to simplify the node recognition process. The ontology describes the node's identity, network performance, and data transmission procedures. By using this framework, IoT devices can be identified and managed more effectively, making the system more secure and efficient.

In routing protocol (RPL), a child node exclusively makes the decision in selecting a parent based on the Rank value. In this paper, we make the parent selection mechanism, a mutual decision between the potential parent node and the child node, which significantly improves the network throughput under a heavy and highly dynamic load. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our parent selection mechanism, we used it to balance the load to avoid congestion by preventing the child node from using the congested parent node. The proposed parent selection mechanism is implemented as an add-on feature in RPL and hence is called enhanced RPL (EN-RPL). Furthermore, we introduce a new objective function for efficient routing (OF-ER) that is based on the newly defined composite efficient routing (CER) metric. CER metric takes important metrics, namely, the link quality, queue utilization, lifetime of node, delay, and number of bottleneck nodes, into account for optimal parent selection. The simulation results demonstrate that EN-RPL lowers the packet loss by up to 37% and reduces energy consumption by up to 46.5% compared with the standard RPL. The evaluation results of OF-ER outperform the state-of-the-art load balancing-based OF with respect to the network stability, reliability, and energy efficiency.

Measuring textual semantic similarity has been a subject of intense discussion in NLP and AI for many years. A new area of research has emerged that applies semantic similarity measures within Twitter. However, the development of these measures for the semantic analysis of tweets imposes fundamental challenges. The sparsity, ambiguity, and informality present in social media are hampering the performance of traditional textual similarity measures as "tweets", have special syntactic and semantic characteristics. This paper reviews and evaluates the performance of topological, statistical, and hybrid similarity measures, in the context of Twitter analysis. Furthermore, the performance of each measure is compared against a naïve keyword-based similarity computation method to assess the significance of semantic computation in capturing the meaning in tweets. An experiment is designed and conducted to evaluate the different measures through examining various metrics, including correlation, error rates, and statistical tests on a benchmark dataset. The potential weaknesses of semantic similarity measures in relation to Twitter applications of textual similarity assessment and the research contributions are discussed. This research highlights challenges and potential improvement areas for the semantic similarity of tweets, a resource for researchers and practitioners.

Sensory data forwarding from on-road smart vehicles to the road side units is challenging mainly due to the highly dynamic nature of the vehicular network. Road safety and traffic related applications demand reliable and fast delivery of these data packets from vehicles to the nearest RSU. We propose a novel forwarding strategy based on vehicle rating that ensures the selected next-hop forwarder would deliver the data packets with high throughput and low delay with consistency. From theoretical analysis we found that the performance can further be enhanced by dynamically tuning the parameters of vehicle rating. Extensive simulation proved significant performance benefits (up to 1.5 times better delivery ratio and 55% less delay in the best case scenario) for the proposed RDDF protocol than that of the best among existing schemes. Most importantly, unlike others, it does not require any prior topology information for taking the routing decision.

The importance of software testing in enterprise system development is growing more and more from cost reduction, quality improvement and time-to-market of their enterprise services. Especially in recent years, companies with the spread of API economy trend has been faced with the need to publish their services via public API-Gateway as Restful-API services. Simultaneously, there is a need for software testing for a part of migrated function from a legacy monolithic architecture to microservice one. In this situation, we have a concern how far range implementation is influenced by getting rid of migrated function's implementation, new function as microservice and isolated data on cloud container. Despite existing several test case extraction methodologies, these are not enough to reveal rage of influence in this case. Therefore, we propose a new test case extraction methodology for a part of system modification and system transition like migrating to microservices from a monolithic system. Our approach focuses on the interaction between function and data to extract test cases from only influenced ranges. On that account, we leverage improved "Impact Data All Used" method as "Code-Based - Impact Data All used." Moreover, we apply graph mining techniques to extracted test cases for reducing the number of test cases efficiently. As a result of this study, by exhaustively searching CRUD operations in source codes level, clarified that it is possible to extract dependencies between functions and data as test cases which are not able to be detected by previous study's IDAU method. Moreover, we suggest the possibility of a test case reduction model by Bonachich Power Centrality and Link-Community analysis.

Virtual Machines (VMs) offer great flexibility, reusability, and portability for managing applications in physical resources of a Cloud data center or a mobile cloud. However, VMs may need to migrate from one data center to another or from one cloudlet to another in vehicular cloud scenarios. This poses a challenge for establishing a VM migration policy, as it has to deal with unique challenges of vehicular networks while meeting the demands of services to avoid impacting their performance.

To address this challenge, this paper proposes a decision policy based on multiple attributes to migrate VMs in vehicular cloud scenarios. This policy allows for quick decision-making on whether a VM migration is necessary and to which cloudlet it should be migrated. Simulation results show that the proposed policy reduces the amount of VM migration in the network by 2%, decreases the blockages of migration requests by 3%, and reduces inference time by approximately 5 ms.

Many real-world problems are modeled as multi-agent problems, which are often partially observable. However, the nonstationary nature of the environment from the perspective of each agent poses a challenge for combining experience replay with IQL. While DDRQN has been proposed as a solution to partially observable RL problems, it still faces limitations such as the inability to enable memory replay. In this article, we present a method based on importance sampling to address these drawbacks of DDRQN. Our results on the SC2LE environment demonstrate a significant improvement in performance compared to the original DDRQN method.

We investigated the mean shift (MS)-type algorithms for estimating modes of probability density functions (PDFs) and analyzed their properties. Our approach considered these algorithms as gradient ascent on estimated PDFs with adaptive step sizes. We established rigorous convergence of mode estimate sequences generated by the MS-type algorithms when an analytic kernel function is used. Our analysis on the MS function revealed novel properties of mode estimate sequences and corresponding density estimate sequences. Notably, we found that the density estimate monotonically increases between two consecutive mode estimates in the MS-type algorithm using a Gaussian kernel. This finding implies that, in the one-dimensional case, the mode estimate sequence converges monotonically to the stationary point nearest to an initial point without jumping over any stationary point.

Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) use 5G network access technologies to fulfill the requirements of their services. In this environment, Drone to Infrastructure (D2I) communication is supported, while each drone could use both Disaster Management (DM) and non-Disaster Management (nDM) services. Efficient network selection algorithms are required to satisfy the constraints of the used services, since the presence of DM services affects the importance of nDM services in situations where a natural disaster occurs. This paper proposes a network selection algorithm which is called Dynamic Trapezoidal Fuzzy Topsis with Adaptive Criteria Weights (DTFT-ACW). DTFT-ACW accomplishes the ranking of the candidate networks considering the importance of each service, as well as the weights of the corresponding selection criteria, as they are obtained with respect to the severity level of a natural disaster occurred. Interval-Valued Trapezoidal Fuzzy Numbers (IVTFN) are used for the criteria evaluation. Experimental results show that the suggested method outperforms existing algorithms by satisfying the constraints of DM services when a disaster becomes severe. Furthermore, DTFT-ACW eliminates the computational complexity of the network selection by considering past decisions.

Nowadays, advertisements are becoming increasingly personalized. Internet data mining algorithms are often used to collect information about users' activities, analyze it, and offer the most relevant contextual advertisement. However, when it comes to displaying ads in public places, finding the right information to show to a group of viewers can be much more challenging. This is due to privacy restrictions and a lack of algorithms capable of finding mutual interests for a group of users. In this article, we propose an approach to addressing these issues through the analysis of multiple visual viewers' characteristics.

Electromyographic (EMG) signals are utilized to analyze the neuromuscular disorders. Machine learning algorithms have been employed as a decision support system to detect neuromuscular disorders. EMG signals contain noise from different sources, such as electrical and electronic instruments and movement artifacts. In this paper, the multiscale principal component analysis (MSPCA) has been used to remove the impulsive noise from the EMG signals. Then, the dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DT-CWT) is utilized for feature extraction, and the rotation forest ensemble classifier is employed for the recognition of EMG signals. In addition, the performance of several classifiers with rotation forest has been studied. An efficient combination of DT-CWT and rotation forest achieved good performance, using tenfold cross validation regarding the total classification accuracy. Results are promising and showed that the rotation forest achieved an accuracy of 99.7% with clinical EMG signals using support vector machine and 96.6% with simulated EMG signals using the artificial neural network (ANN).

Overall Internet Protocol (IP) traffic is expected to grow to 396 Exabyte per month by 2022, as a result of the demands of new applications such as Cloud, Internet of Things (IoT) and the expected arrival of fifth generation mobile networks (5G). In particular, mobile networks contribute most to this predicted increase in traffic and have a heavy burden on technological developments. Most of this traffic will be local with a significant burden on the access network and the metropolitan and less to the backbone network. Thus, focusing on the corresponding traffic, produced by 5G applications running in the core network, the need for data analysis and performance estimation becomes essential, in order to enhance the Validation and Verification (V&V) of different Network Services (NS) across heterogeneous platforms. In this paper, we are focusing on the analysis of the monitoring data, that are produced by the running Network Services (NSs), over a Software Defined Network (SDN). Furthermore, we propose an approach where the test developers would benefit from all the essentials in order to understand the service's behavior, and optimize the V&V tests, prior to the production.

In this paper, we explore methods of generating accurate, real-time household energy usage predictions and the practical use cases for this prediction data. The ability to perform real-time prediction and the usefulness of such predictions are recent developments as connected smart energy devices become increasingly prevalent. These devices not only gather relevant data to learn historic trends, but can also improve overall grid functionality through direct device responsiveness. Machine learning has not yet been widely explored as an approach for this type of non-aggregated prediction, but we demonstrate its effectiveness as a tool even for this highly noisy data relative to other baseline and statistical approaches, and how all these approaches can complement each other. These predictions are crucial for enabling smart grid systems to effectively communicate their needs to the grid, and for the grid to appropriately prepare for future demand.

In this letter, we propose a novel lightweight network HiNet: hybrid inherited feature learning network and its variants: HiNet -ReLU, HiNet -Concat, Large Scale HiNet, 2 stack HiNet and 4 stack HiNet for facial expression recognition. In HiNet, we introduce the hybrid feature (HyFeat) block that follows a two - level hybrid structure to capture the local contextual information of expressive regions. In level -1, HyFeat block uses two different scaled conv filters to preserve the domain knowledge features for expressive regions. Similarly, level -2 captures the enriched features through refine edge variation of the receptive fields by employing another two filters. Thus, HyFeat block allows network to perpetuate prominent features of facial expressions and enhances the discriminability of the HiNet. Moreover, performance of the proposed HiNet is evaluated by conducting person dependent (PD) and person independent (PI) experiments on four datasets: CK+, MUG, AFEW and OULU respectively. Experimental results on CK+ dataset prove the adequacy of the proposed HiNet over its variants in terms of accuracy and computational complexity. Furthermore, the proposed HiNet uses approximately 5 /16, 1/138, 1/144 and 1/31 times less parameters as compared to the MobileNet, VGG -16, VGG - 19 and ResNet, respectively. The experimental and computational complexity analysis demonstrate the significant performance improvement of the proposed method over the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of recognition rate.

Despite the rapid development of computer networks, congestion control continues to be a pressing issue due to the unprecedented increase in traffic. Active queue management (AQM) is an effective approach to congestion control as it helps to reduce congestion by discarding packets in router buffers even before congestion occurs. 

This paper focuses on predictive congestion control with the implementation of long short-term memory (LSTM) as the most popular recurrent neural network. The aim is to ensure efficient compensation for the delay in TCP networks. The TCP dynamic system is identified to account for the impact of network latency. Results indicate that the proposed control scheme using LSTM reduces network latency and stabilizes the router queue length more effectively than other well-known AQM algorithms.

Edge computing surpasses the restrictions set by cloud computing and brings information technology to a new level. By performing computations near sensors, edge computing has the potential to tackle challenges present in bandwidth and delay-sensitive applications. Despite the availability of many smart video surveillance approaches based on machine learning (ML) algorithms, the efficient migration of these smart algorithms to edge remains a challenge.

To address this challenge, we propose an intelligent Surveillance as an Edge Network Service (iSENSE) that explores the feasibility of moving ML to the edge by testing two commonly used human-object detection schemes. We also introduce a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (L-CNN) that utilizes depth-wise separable convolution to improve computational execution. We further improve edge performance by proposing a hybrid lightweight tracking algorithm, Kerman (Kernelized Kalman filter), which is designed for human-object tracking and utilizes a decision tree-based hybrid Kernelized Correlation Filter algorithm.

We have implemented both Kerman and L-CNN algorithms on edge by utilizing different types of single board computers. The proposed iSENSE system was validated using real-world campus surveillance video and open image sets. The results of our experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can track human objects in real-time with good accuracy while working with limited resources on edge devices.

In the field of natural language processing, word sense disambiguation is a crucial technique. Traditional machine learning-based methods for word sense disambiguation are not very accurate and require manual text feature extraction. On the other hand, deep learning-based methods have not been widely applied to cases where there are many ambiguous meanings. This paper proposes a deep Chinese word sense disambiguation method based on sequence to sequence models. The model takes a word context sequence as input and outputs a word meaning sequence, making it applicable to all word meaning ambiguity cases. The proposed method is evaluated using the SemEval-2007 Task #5 dataset and compared with seven other methods. The results show that the proposed method improves disambiguation accuracy by 11.48% compared to the method with the highest accuracy among the seven methods.

With the current significant penetration of mobile devices (i.e. smartphones and tablets) and the tremendous increase in the number of the corresponding mobile applications, they have become an indispensable part of our lives. Nowadays, there is a significant growth in the number of sensitive applications such as personal health applications, personal financial applications, home monitoring applications, etc. In addition, with the significant growth of Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, smartphones and the corresponding applications are widely considered as the Internet gateways for these devices. Mobile devices mostly use wireless LANs (WLANs) (i.e., WiFi networks) as the prominent network interface to the Internet. However, due to the broadcast nature of WiFi links, wireless traffics are exposed to any eavesdropping adversary within the WLAN. Despite WiFi encryption, studies show that application usage information could be inferred from the encrypted wireless traffic. The leakage of this sensitive information is very serious issue that will significantly impact users' privacy and security. In addressing this privacy concern, we design and develop a lightweight programmable privacy framework, called PrivacyGuard. PrivacyGuard is inspired by the vision of pushing the Software Defined Network (SDN)-like paradigm all the way to wireless network edge, is designed to support of adopting privacy preserving policies to protect the wireless communication of the sensitive applications. In this paper, we demonstrate and evaluate a prototype of PrivacyGuard framework on Android devices showing the flexibility and efficiency of the framework.

Hyperspectral remote sensing imagery provides valuable and rich information to distinguish the characteristics of materials. However, this advantage of hyperspectral imagery often encounters the problem of a limited amount of training samples, which is caused by the difficulty of manually labeling. Fortunately, the spatial distribution of surface objects can be integrated with the spectral signature to improve the discriminative ability. In this paper, a 3-D Gaussian-Gabor feature extraction and selection framework has been proposed for hyperspectral image classification. First, a bank of 3-D Gaussian-Gabor filters are convolved with the concatenated data of both extended multi-attribute profile (EMAP) features and raw hyperspectral data. Second, an improved fast density peak clustering (IFDPC) method is introduced to select the most representative features from each extracted 3-D Gaussian-Gabor feature cube. Finally, the retained features are combined together to accomplish the classification task. The proposed method is thus named as GG-IFDPC. Three real hyperspectral imagery data sets have been utilized, and the experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed GG-IFDPC approach over the compared ones.

Recently, the Massive Internet of Things (IoT) and Web of Things (WoT) are remarkable research fields aiming to facilitate the connectivity, accessibility, and control of the Things by Web standards and technologies for large-scale deployment. In such context, the end-user is capable of simply creating, mashing-up, and presenting the multiple Things to gain high-level information. However, current research approaches much more pay attention to describe a single Thing. The modeling and building the application for the compound objects consisting of groups of Things namely "Asset" are still limited due to the lack of description and seamless integration mechanism. Moreover, the traditional IoT Device Description Language directly installed on device is highly restricted in Massive IoT scenario because of stringent requirements for power consumption and operation cost. In this paper, we introduce the WoT based Asset Description (WoT-AD), a descriptive language for the Asset aiming to mitigate such limitations. WoT-AD explicitly describes a group of Things as homogeneous object to enable mash-up, self-discovery, and simply access their resources, entities, and services. We also provide a lightweight framework that fully integrates with WoT-AD to enable WoT for Massive IoT scenario. Such integration not only effectively models the Asset but also simplifies the development of mash-up application to different-skilled users. Finally, we evaluate the performance of our proposal to demonstrate its effectiveness and scalability in real use-case.

Usually Small Hydro Power Plants are frequently constituted of fixed speed drives. With the development power electronics converter, an autonomous variable speed drives i.e. Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) came into the fashion. Small Hydro Power Plant (SHPP) allied with doubly fed induction generator as an alternative source of energy plays a foremost part for changing the face of an emerging country in the terms of the energy crisis, environment protection, and economic development. The foremost objective of this paper is to represent a newly improved control strategy using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in grid-connected doubly fed induction generator associated with the small hydropower plant. The SHPP system embraces the back to back voltage source converter. The suggested control scheme controls both sides of converter i.e. converter of rotor side and grid side and sustains the power factor at unity level in the grid side for abbreviating the loss as well as controlling the effective reactive and real power flow in the rotor side. Optimum reactive and real power flow from the rotor side to grid side occurs at variable speeds with the assistance of DFIG. Here ANN controller improves the transient response of DFIG and makes the system more apposite for real-time applications. The stability of the system is constant under diverse load conditions and it is investigated with the help of the model, and simulations result. A 2 MW DFIG linked with 2 MW SHPP model is simulated in SIMULINK for Time domain applications.

Quantum data structures, methods, algorithms and software applications for parallel solution of combinatorial problems, including design and test, on classical computers by using extra memory are proposed. Quantum models and methods for design and test of specific logic functionalities are developed based on the use of vector qubit data structures and memory-driven architectures for parallel computing algorithms, in order to significantly improve the performance of testing and deductive simulation of digital systems-on-chips. A new quantum method of test generation for single stuck-at faults of logic functions through taking Boolean derivatives with respect to their qubit coverages is proposed. The quantum method of deductive simulation of stuck-at faults of logical functions through the synthesis of matrices of Boolean derivatives with respect to their qubit coverage has been developed. The performance of methods for test synthesis and their analysis has no analogues in algorithmic performance.

This paper focuses on developing a scoring system for figure skating sports videos. The proposed approach involves a deep architecture comprising of two components, namely Self-Attentive LSTM and Multi-scale Convolutional Skip LSTM. These components can effectively learn both local and global sequential information in each video. In addition, the authors introduce the FisV dataset - a large-scale figure skating sports video dataset comprising of 500 videos with an average length of 2 minutes and 50 seconds. Each video is annotated by two scores provided by nine different referees: Total Element Score(TES) and Total Program Component Score (PCS). The proposed model is validated on FisV and MIT-skate datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the model in scoring the figure skating videos. The codes and datasets are available for download at https://github.com/loadder/MS_LSTM.git.

This study focuses on resource allocation for a sustainable cooperative network. The network comprises several IoT nodes that run on RF energy, a relay that utilizes renewable energy supplies, and a destination. The relay receives data from IoT nodes and transmits it to the destination while also charging the IoT nodes. The aim is to maximize throughput while accounting for transmit power limits, stochastic energy harvesting, and channel conditions. The problem is solved by analyzing the time allocation for cooperative communications with EH, considering the data and energy dependency of the two hop transmissions. Closed-form solutions for optimal power and time allocation in a symmetric link network are derived. Extensive simulations validate the analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

In this paper, we present a synthesis of a current mode second order band pass filter that is composed of current conveyor circuits. To achieve this, we utilized a nature-inspired algorithm called Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize the sizing of CMOS positive second-generation Current Conveyors (CCII+). By utilizing GA, we were able to obtain the optimal physical dimensions of the constituent PMOS and NMOS transistors of the CCII+, which enabled the circuit to deliver superior performance. 

The optimized CCII+ configuration was utilized as a building block for constructing the current mode second order band pass filter. In this paper, we conducted a comparative analysis of the performances achieved by GA and other Meta-heuristics found in literature. We relied on PSPICE simulation to validate the results and performances obtained from the experiments. 

Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the design and synthesis of a current mode second order band pass filter. Our approach demonstrates the usefulness of nature-inspired algorithms in optimizing circuit designs and achieving superior performance.

The recognition of emotions from textual data is a rapidly growing field of research. It allows for the analysis of an additional dimension of textual data, which is extremely valuable for understanding human behavior. Emotions are expressed through facial expressions, speech, and written content, making social media and microblogging platforms a rich source of data for identifying emotions. However, recognizing emotions from text is a complex task.

To address this challenge, we propose a technique that utilizes word lexicons, emoticons, negations, and intensity modifiers. Our approach follows Ekman's emotion model, and word lexicons are generated using WordNet from a set of manually collected seed words. Emoticons are collected from Twitter, while negations and intensity modifiers are sourced from the literature. We have designed several heuristic rules to support our keyword spotting technique.

Our experiments using data obtained from Twitter show high precision and recall for all emotional classes. Our proposed technique offers a new way of identifying emotions from textual data, which can be used for a wide range of applications, including sentiment analysis, opinion mining, and customer feedback analysis. It has the potential to significantly advance the field and improve our understanding of human emotions.

With the growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), massively connected devices are exposed to cyber-attacks and are becoming active as bots. To protect IoT devices efficiently from increasing threats, in addition to honeypot-based approaches, we need to gain more complete understanding of IoT botnets and potential victims including purposes of attacks and events which they are participating in. In this paper, we propose a two-step subspace clustering method to cluster botnets and clarify their types (functionalities). For each target host, the proposed method separates features into several subspaces and generates a sub-label in each subspace to represent partial characteristic (e.g., low-size flows or high TCP-SYN rate). Major combinations of sub-labels presents different partial characteristic, and the proposed method classify bots and interprets the whole behaviors for each bot group. In the evaluation, we reveal the scale and variety of botnets in the wild through two real-world datasets.

Involving consumers as influencers of the video game development process is the main feature of Steam's early access model. This has led to the exponential increase in the popularity of Steam's early access games. Steam being the most widespread digital distribution platform for video games on computers is part of the reason for the success of the early access model. Another part is the abundance of possibilities for game developers to communicate with end users and vice versa. The model is considered a success by the game development community as numerous games using Steam's early access as their distribution platform have gained a large user base (game owners) and high sales, even though, on principle early access games are not complete and are offered for sale in alpha and beta stages with no guarantees on release date or development schedule. Hence, the success of such a model cannot just be measured with owner and sale numbers. This paper aims to explore the interconnection between employing Steam's early access model and the satisfaction of consumers.

This paper presents a rapid algorithm for training adaptive hinging hyperplanes (AHH), a widely used and efficient continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) model comprising a linear combination of basis functions. The original AHH approach generates new basis functions incrementally by traversing all existing basis functions in each dimension with pre-specified knots, while integrating a backward process that removes redundant basis functions, preventing over-fitting. In this work, we accelerate the procedure for generating new basis functions and replace the backward deletion with Lasso regularization. Lasso regularization is more resilient, requires less computation, and effectively prevents over-fitting. Additionally, we discuss the selection of the splitting knots based on training data. Numerical experiments establish that our proposed algorithm significantly enhances the efficiency of the existing AHH algorithm, with even higher accuracy and better robustness in the given benchmark problems.

The paper addresses the discrete-time distributed Kalman filtering over a sensor network to generate system fault residuals. The problem of interest are distributed sensor data consensus filtering for systems whose dynamics, as well as the control objectives, are not decoupled. Limited to linear systems and fixed network connectivity, the state observability and fault detectability is analyzed to guarantee stability of the distributed filters and responsibility of fault residuals. The performance of fault residuals generated within distributed Kalman filtering algorithms are demonstrated in the numerical example.

ICT technology is widely applied to various industries including agriculture. In the agricultural sector, most of the devices and greenhouses still use very old serial communication technologies. Nowadays, many ICT technologies such as ZigBee, Bluetooth and the Internet are spreading but still not interoperable. A set of standards is under development in Korea to ensure interoperability between different vendors. In particular, core interoperability can be provided by standardizing the LCP protocol independent of the underlying network infrastructure. In this paper, we designed service control protocol based on LCP protocol and implemented it using Python. We have deployed the implementation to Raspberry PI with actual physical devices.

Short-term traffic flow prediction is one of the most important issues in the field of intelligent transportation systems. It plays an important role in traffic information service and traffic guidance. However, complex traffic systems are highly nonlinear and stochastic, making short-term traffic flow prediction a challenging issue. Although long short-term memory (LSTM) has a good performance in traffic flow prediction, the impact of temporal features on prediction has not been exploited by existing studies. In this paper, a temporal information enhancing LSTM (T-LSTM) is proposed to predict traffic flow of a single road section. In view of the similar characteristics of traffic flow at the same time each day, the model can improve prediction accuracy by capturing the intrinsic correlation between traffic flow and temporal information. The experimental results demonstrate that our method can effectively improve the prediction performance and obtain higher accuracy compared with other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we propose a novel missing data processing technique based on T-LSTM. According to the experimental results, this technique can well restore the characteristics of original data and improve the accuracy of traffic flow prediction.

In this study, we compare topicalization in Mandarin Chinese with previous studies on topicalization in English and Romance languages. Our findings suggest that the topicalization asymmetry observed between arguments and circumstantial adjuncts versus manner adjuncts does not necessarily indicate an argument-adjunct asymmetry in topicalization. Instead, this asymmetry can be better explained in terms of the movement-merger distinction, which supports the hypothesis put forward by Liliane Haegeman's recent work.

This paper introduces a novel approach, perturb-max, for performing high-dimensional statistical inference in graphical models. Perturb-max operates by injecting randomness into maximum a-posteriori (MAP) predictors through the use of random perturbations, followed by optimization. While generating high-dimensional random variables can be computationally expensive, low-dimensional perturbations can be sampled as efficiently as MAP optimization. This paper demonstrates that the expected value of perturb-max inference with low dimensional perturbations can be utilized sequentially to generate unbiased samples from the Gibbs distribution. Additionally, the expected value of maximal perturbations provides a natural bound on the entropy of such perturb-max models. Using a measure concentration result, this paper shows that the deviation of sampled perturb-max values from their expected values decays exponentially with the number of samples, allowing for effective approximation of expectations.

The fused lasso signal approximator (FLSA) is an important optimization problem that has extensive applications in signal processing and biomedical engineering. However, this optimization problem is challenging to solve since it is both nonsmooth and nonseparable, making existing numerical solutions time- and memory-inefficient, while also implicating the use of several auxiliary variables to handle the nondifferentiable penalty.

To address these challenges, this paper proposes a compact neural network as a solution to the FLSA. This neural network has a one-layer structure with the number of neurons proportionate to the dimension of the given signal, thanks to the utilization of consecutive projections. Furthermore, the proposed neural network is stable in the Lyapunov sense, and is guaranteed to converge globally to the optimal solution of the FLSA.

Through experiments on several applications from signal processing and biomedical engineering, the results confirm the reasonable performance of the proposed neural network. This approach offers a promising means to solve the FLSA, with its improved efficiency and effectiveness in handling the nonsmooth and nonseparable aspects of the problem.

The number of component classifiers chosen for an ensemble greatly impacts the prediction ability. In this paper, we use a geometric framework for a priori determining the ensemble size, which is applicable to most of the existing batch and online ensemble classifiers. There are only a limited number of studies on the ensemble size examining majority voting (MV) and weighted MV (WMV). Almost all of them are designed for batch-mode, hardly addressing online environments. Big data dimensions and resource limitations, in terms of time and memory, make the determination of ensemble size crucial, especially for online environments. For the MV aggregation rule, our framework proves that the more strong components we add to the ensemble, the more accurate predictions we can achieve. For the WMV aggregation rule, our framework proves the existence of an ideal number of components, which is equal to the number of class labels, with the premise that components are completely independent of each other and strong enough. While giving the exact definition for a strong and independent classifier in the context of an ensemble is a challenging task, our proposed geometric framework provides a theoretical explanation of diversity and its impact on the accuracy of predictions. We conduct a series of experimental evaluations to show the practical value of our theorems and existing challenges.

In this paper, state-of-the-art power electronics and energy management solutions utilized in low-power (less than 5 mW), low-voltage (less than 3 V) energy harvesting powered wireless sensors for Internet of things related applications are detailed. All aspects of an energy harvesting powered sensor system are examined, including the challenges of low-power energy harvesting sources, energy management circuits including power converters and energy storage elements, as well as the impact of wireless sensor pulsed power profiles. In particular, this paper focuses on existing voltage step-up energy management techniques, including the issues of cold-start and maximum power point tracking, as well as energy storage which is necessary for wireless sensor operation. Both academic and commercially available energy harvesting powered systems are examined to provide a comprehensive analysis of existing solutions. Issues that are limiting the current system performance are identified to help define future developments needed to enable efficient and effective energy harvesting powered wireless sensor operation.

The combination of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) with frequency division duplex (FDD) mode holds great promise for increasing system capacity and link robustness for fifth generation (5G) wireless cellular systems. However, accurate downlink channel state information (CSI) feedback can be challenging due to the large number of base station (BS) antennas found in massive MIMO systems. To address this issue, researchers have turned to the combination of deep learning (DL) and superimposed coding (SC) for CSI feedback. In this method, downlink CSI is spread and then superimposed on uplink user data sequences (UL-US) toward the BS. To recover the downlink CSI and UL-US, researchers propose a multi-task neural network (NN) architecture at the BS. This system also utilizes a subnet-by-subnet approach for network training to facilitate parameter tuning and expedite convergence rate. Results show that this DL-SC approach improves estimation of downlink CSI with similar or better UL-US detection under varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and power proportional coefficient (PPC) conditions compared to a standalone SC-based CSI scheme.

In order to maintain high-quality service traffic transmission within a communication network, it is essential to ensure that quality indicators remain within their allowable ranges. One crucial indicator is the traffic transmission rate defined in the user traffic profile configuration. By continuously monitoring the actual user traffic profile against the specified configuration, it is possible to uphold the quality of traffic transmission by keeping the quality indicators within the predetermined range.

The limitless potential of the Internet of Things (IoT) has captured the interest of both public and private sectors. In this age of technological advancement, companies are constantly seeking new ways to incorporate IoT applications in order to meet customers' demands and gain a competitive edge. The automotive industry is particularly interested in developing IoT technologies to improve the safety of their vehicles.

One possible application of IoT technology in the automotive industry involves equipping cars with sensors and other technology that can detect accidents and quickly alert emergency personnel. Currently, in the event of an accident, someone must actively call 911 or other emergency services to seek help. This process can delay the arrival of first responders, potentially putting lives at risk. However, with the implementation of IoT technology, an automatic notification can be sent to emergency personnel as soon as an accident occurs.

The system works by utilizing sensors such as accelerometers and GPS to detect the location and severity of an accident. This information is then sent to the cloud, where it is analyzed and an alert message is sent to whoever is subscribed to that car. This could include the police, ambulance, friends, or family. The ambulance is able to quickly locate the scene of the accident using the GPS coordinates provided, enabling them to arrive on the scene as quickly as possible.

In addition to improving the speed and accuracy of emergency response, implementing IoT technology in the automotive industry can also help manufacturers meet customer demand for cutting-edge products. By prioritizing safety features, companies can gain a competitive advantage and maximize profits.

Overall, IoT technology has the potential to revolutionize the automotive industry, improving the safety of vehicles and streamlining emergency response in the event of an accident. By investing in these technologies, companies can position themselves as industry leaders, while also providing invaluable benefits to their customers.

The aim of this study is to provide developers of cloud infrastructure for corporate information systems with an effective solution to streamline their information security processes. The paper analyzed various types of clouds and their associated information security risks, along with different models of providing cloud services. The architecture of cloud systems was also examined in detail. The study introduced a comprehensive model of a secure information system that takes into account the identified information risks. To enhance the model, the study also recommended incorporating templates that classify and outline the characteristics of information risks. The study introduced an undirected graph with cloud structure that can be used to accurately evaluate the information risks linked to corporate information systems with cloud services using the model developed.

We propose a solution for Electric Vehicles (EVs) energy management in smart cities, where a deep learning approach is used to enhance the energy consumption of electric vehicles by trajectory and delay predictions. Two Recurrent Neural Networks are adapted and trained on 60 days of urban traffic. The trained networks show precise prediction of trajectory and delay, even for long prediction intervals. An algorithm is designed and applied on well known energy models for traction and air conditioning. We show how it can prevent from a battery exhaustion. Experimental results combining both RNN and energy models demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed solution in terms of route trajectory and delay prediction, enhancing the energy management.

Recently, the popularity of 3D Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) designs has increased owing to their superior performance at oblique incidence angles compared to planar designs. While discrete nature-inspired evolutionary optimization algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) have successfully designed planar FSS, they are unsuitable for the 3D FSS design problem since they generate non-contiguous structures that are challenging to manufacture. The Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) technique is an alternative that generates contiguous segments, but traditional ACO methods may lead to a PEC unit cell by forcing meanders to continue until they are trapped. This paper proposes a Multi-Objective Lazy Ant Colony Optimization (MOLACO) algorithm for the FSS design problem. The innovative use of lazy ants allows exploration of solutions that were previously inaccessible using conventional ACO implementations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MOLACO algorithm is well-equipped to handle the complexities of 3D FSS design.

This paper proposes a prediction study of transformer oil density using multi-frequency ultrasound, genetic algorithm GA, and backpropagation neural network BPNN. The study uses 110 sets of transformer oil samples from the China southern power grid to establish a prediction model based on the BPNN algorithm. The model takes the 242-dimensional multi-frequency ultrasonic data of the oil sample as input and the density as output. The number of hidden layer neurons was adjusted, and the GA algorithm was introduced to optimize the network parameters. The results show that the GA-BPNN model outperforms the traditional standard BPNN model in predicting the density of transformer oil, with much closer output values and smaller errors. This study establishes a solid foundation for testing other parameters of transformer oil using multi-frequency ultrasound technology.

Vehicular Adhoc Networks (VANET) is a technology that is the backbone of the Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), offering a wide range of safety and comfort applications. Vehicles with their powerful computation and storage capacities have the potential to produce services and realize the Vehicular Clouds (VC) concept. However, their services are published in a shared repository within the fixed Roadside Units (RSU), making it hard to request or publish a service if the requesting vehicle is not within the range of the RSU. 

To address this issue, we propose an efficient vehicular cloud architecture that uses public buses as mobile cloud repositories, also known as brokers, to store existing services. The known path and coverage of all city areas make public buses the most suitable place to store services. Our proposal is implemented over a trust-based routing protocol that selects the most connected and trusted path to deliver requests and provide services. 

The simulation results demonstrate that our proposal can achieve high success ratios (> 90%) using a reduced number of mobile brokers in the network. We believe that our proposal has the potential to enhance the reliability and efficiency of VANET-based services, making them more accessible to a wider range of users.

Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has potential applications for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but lengthy fNIRS measurements can be uncomfortable for participants, leading to a lack of sufficient data for classification model training and decreased accuracy of fNIRS-BCIs. To address this issue, a data-augmentation method using generative adversarial networks (GANs) was proposed and evaluated using fNIRS simulation data. The results showed that the proposed method could generate artificial fNIRS data based on cerebral blood flow (CBF), although the generated data contained an extra noise component. Training a deep neural network (DNN) using the augmented data resulted in a doubling of classification accuracy, indicating that the proposed data-augmentation method is useful for improving BCI performance.

The issue of deep learning attacks launched by adversaries has gained immense attention recently, especially with the growing use of edge computing devices that connect with the central cloud. Protecting neural network models and private data from these attacks has become a vital topic of discussion. This paper examines two collaborative edge-cloud deep learning scenarios. In the first scenario, deep learning models are trained on the cloud and deployed on terminal deep learning accelerators for delay-sensitive tasks. In the second scenario, edge-collected data is transferred to the cloud for computationally-intensive tasks. However, both scenarios leave the pre-trained neural network models and private data vulnerable to attack if transmitted and processed unencrypted. 

To address this security vulnerability, the paper introduces a lightweight protection scheme against model-oriented and data-oriented attacks. This scheme employs Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and Processing-in-memory (PIM) technology to confine model execution only to specific edge devices and prevent unauthorized access of private data. Experiments on state-of-the-art deep learning networks demonstrate that this method secures edge deep learning models and user-data with only a negligible performance overhead.

Fault detection of nonlinear processes using Kernel Principal Component Analysis(KPCA) method has recently prompt a lot of interest due to its industrial practical importance. However, this method cannot be applied for data sets with a large amount of samples. To overcome this deficiency, this paper proposes a reduced KPCA method based on K-means clustering. This method aims to find a reduced data set among the training data in the input space and uses this reduced data set to built the reduced KPCA model in the feature space. The relevance of the proposed method is illustrated on an air quality monitoring network. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new method when compared to the classical KPCA technique.

In this paper, we present a recent survey on the advancements made in parallel join algorithms using the popular MapReduce framework on the distributed file system Hadoop. We briefly introduce the MapReduce and Hadoop frameworks and discuss the general steps to install, configure, and use Hadoop. 

Next, we classify parallel join algorithms into categories and review the primary works of improvement from the beginning to the present in chronological order. We organize these works into a user-friendly table and analyze them in terms of their advantages and disadvantages. This survey provides researchers with a comprehensive and chronological overview of the enhancements made to parallel join algorithms using MapReduce on Hadoop. 

By consolidating these works in one place, this survey will make it simpler for researchers to study the improvements made to parallel join algorithms and to come up with novel approaches to further enhance them.

Network densification is becoming an overwhelming phenomenon in many emerging wireless communication paradigms. Although network densification may promote system metrics like the throughputs, the quality-of-service (QoS) issue needs to be carefully investigated. Commonly, the QoS-aware power management is tightly restricted by the complicated patterns of interferences among multiple active communication devices. Conventional approaches in optimizing the QoS-aware power management problem may either fail to convergence or the overall power rate is unsatisfactory. In this paper, we make an effort to solve the QoS-aware power management problem with the aid of the deep learning (DL) methodology. Recently DL has shone light on wide variety of research fields, such as image processing and natural language processing. It is our intensive interest in exploring the role that DL plays to solve the QoS-aware power management problem. In the presented extensive experimental analysis work, we show that the DL-based method can well match the solution generated by a conventional optimization procedure. It is impressed that the convergence of DL is quite fast. Moreover, the DL-based approach demonstrates the better performance when the conventional method enters the infeasible region.

Mobile cloud computing technology enables users to cooperate with each other so that their mobile devices' resources can be integrated together to afford complicated application, such as machine auto-translation and image processing, which can always be represented as Directed Acyclic Graphs. On mobile clouds, due to the social relationships of mobile devices' owners, networks on mobile clouds are always complex and consist of multiple sub-networks intersecting at several joint devices. In these complex networks, joint devices can communicate with all devices of their related multiple sub-networks, whereas the other devices can only contact devices in the same sub-network. In this paper, we study the workflow task scheduling problem in the aforementioned complex networks on mobile clouds, and formulate it as Integer Programming problem that is generally NP-Hard. Due to the constraint of each device's power capacity, the dependence among tasks in a workflow and the network complexity, it is too difficult to achieve feasible scheduling solutions for the considered problem. To solve this problem, we propose an Improved Round-Robin scheduling algorithm (IRR) and an Improved Greedy scheduling algorithm (IG) with the consideration of workflow tasks' features. Experimental results show that our proposed IRR and IG guarantee to achieve feasible solutions, whereas the General Round-Robin scheduling algorithm (GRR) does with the probability of 2.3%. Moreover, experimental results also indicate that IG outperforms IRR.

This paper presents an innovative approach to modeling the walk pattern of powered exoskeletons using a complex-valued neural network. The research team has been developing a powered exoskeleton to support workers in nuclear power plants during hazardous situations, with the aim of reducing the physical strain experienced by workers wearing heavy radiation suits. While conventional reactive power assist control based on EMG sensors has been considered, it was found to be unreliable when the workers sweated due to the high temperature and humidity in the suit. As a result, feed-forward control based on motion recognition was developed to help the worker's motion. However, previous studies using a simple k-nearest neighbor algorithm lacked the desired smoothness in the estimated trajectory and were not designed for online learning. 

Therefore, this paper introduces a complex-valued neural network to model the walk motion of powered exoskeletons, demonstrating its ability to achieve fast and stable learning. Experiments showed the validity of this approach in modeling the walk motion of powered exoskeletons, providing a potential solution to support workers' physical movement in hazardous environments.

Adjustable speed drives (ASDs) are widely used due to their efficiency and flexibility. However, they also generate harmonics that can adversely affect the power quality of distribution networks. These harmonics lead to power losses in the grid and thus, different mitigation strategies using active front end have been proposed. Although effective, these strategies are expensive and conventional front ends like diode rectifiers are still preferred in many industries. This paper proposes a new approach to eliminate grid harmonics using a three-phase diode rectifier with a controlled DC link current or boost converter. The simulation results show that this strategy can selectively eliminate specific harmonics from the grid. This new approach offers a cost-effective alternative to address the power quality concerns posed by ASDs.

The significant role of nitrogen element in plants growth resulting in increased usage of nitrogen fertilizer in the agriculture field. With the aim to avoid improper use of nitrogen fertilization on plants and to assist local farmers in improving plants monitoring, this paper presents an economical and non-destructive method in determining nitrogen status of Napier grass using digital image processing approach. Three authentic techniques of image segmentation Otsu, K-means clustering, and watershed transformation were applied and compared to recognize the most accurate method for segmenting leaf pixel from its background. Otsu was discovered as the most efficient technique with less time-processing. Out of 36 features extracted from the segmented image, kurtosis, skewness and standard deviation of the blue color image were the most related features in classifying nitrogen status of the images. Classifiers like KNN, decision tree, and linear discriminant were used to classify the leaves image and nitrogen status accordingly. The accuracy of 100% was recorded in classifying the leaves image using decision tree and KNN classifier.

This study investigates how different input text representations impact the performance of a Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network Language Model (LSTM RNNLM). LSTM RNNLM struggles to capture long-range context information due to vanishing gradients during training. Word embedding vectors capture similarity and semantic context information, while additional context can be captured by socio-situational setting information, topics, named entities, and parts-of-speech tags. Using a character LSTM RNNLM as a control, experiments reveal that adding socio-situational information results in a 0.1% reduction in perplexity, while swapping character embeddings with word2vec embeddings yields a reduction of 2.77%. However, adding socio-situational information to a word embedded model results in a 5.79% perplexity increase compared to the word2vec only model. Similar trends are observed when other context information is added, with the largest increase in perplexity obtained when word embeddings and topics are applied, resulting in a perplexity increase of 7.55%. This increase is due to the addition of more data, resulting in a larger and sparser input that takes longer to train and captures less useful information. A better method for text representation would be to add the vectors together instead of concatenating them, reducing input size while still capturing necessary semantic information.

Operational Support System (OSS) is a critical program used for monitoring and controlling services in telecommunication and computer networks. Its primary function is to manage the overall operation of the network, including its performance, availability, and minimizing downtime. In this paper, we explore the various use cases of implementing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in OSS/BSS (Business Support System) network, the system architecture model, and how AI can help in improving network performance and overall profitability.

The implementation of AI in OSS/BSS Network is essential since it improves network availability and provides real-time data insights, which help in proactive network management. The AI algorithms can analyze network data and identify network faults, performance issues, and configuration changes that can adversely affect the network. Once identified, the system can take action and address the problem before it affects users' experience. Additionally, OSS/BSS can use FCAPS (Fault, Configuration, Account, Performance, and Security) framework to manage the network's performance and security.

The system architecture model used in implementing AI in OSS/BSS Network involves four stages. The first phase involves data collection, where the network data is gathered and fed into the AI system. The second stage involves data pre-processing, where the data is cleaned and normalized to standardize data formats. The third step is data analysis, where AI algorithms analyze the data to identify patterns, trends, and insights. Finally, the fourth stage is the action stage, where the system takes proactive measures to improve network performance.

The use cases of implementing AI in OSS/BSS Network are diverse, and they include network optimization, anomaly detection, root cause analysis, prediction and forecasting, automatic fault identification, and resolution. For instance, AI can help in identifying anomalies within the network by analyzing historical data and identifying unusual data patterns that indicate faulty devices or possible attacks. The system can then take necessary action to prevent or minimize the impact of the anomaly.

In conclusion, the implementation of AI in OSS/BSS Network is essential in ensuring optimal network performance, availability, and reducing downtime. The use cases discussed above show how AI can help in improving network performance, detecting anomalies, and taking proactive measures to prevent problems that may affect users' experience. Furthermore, incorporating FCAPS framework helps in ensuring that the network's performance and security are managed comprehensively.

In this paper, our objective is to tackle the issue of temporal segmentation in videos. Due to the presence of multiple continuous actions in real-world videos, many researchers divide them into various fixed-length video clips. However, since a single frame's traits cannot wholly describe human motion over a period, it could lead to the inclusion of frames from various adjacent actions in a clip, which adversely impacts action segmentation and recognition. To address this, we present a novel unsupervised technique that is based on the directions of velocity to break down videos into a set of clips with variable lengths. Our experiments, conducted on the IXMAS dataset, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

This study outlines a system designed for automatic landing of a small fixed-wing UAV on a Fast Patrol Boat. The proposed approach employs a ground-based camera system installed on the ship, which enables reduced size, weight, and power requirements for the UAV. The vision system tracks the UAV and calculates the control commands, which are sent to the UAV via radio. This approach allows the use of standard UAVs with commercial autopilots. The system uses a Particle Filter (PF) structure to estimate the trajectory of the UAV based on captured images. The translational motion is filtered using an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), while the rotational motion is filtered through an Unscented Bingham Filter (UBiF). This filtering structure is similar to the Unscented Particle Filter (UPF). The tracking error obtained is in accordance with the requirements for automatic landing.

The analysis of Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal is very cumbersome due to its non-stationary nature. ECG signal is the combination of P-wave, QRS-wave and T-wave. R-peaks detection is very important for classifying heart diseases in QRS-wave. R-peaks detection is not easy task due to the involvement of various types of noises and large length of data sets. In this work, discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is considered for preprocessing step. Hilbert transform has been used for spectral estimation for the step of extracting features. Finally, principal component analysis (PCA) is adopted for reducing feature vectors. R-peaks have been detected from reduced features on the basis of calculating the variance of principal components (PCs). The detection sensitivity (SE), positive predictivity (PP), F-measure (F-m) and mean squared error(MSE) are estimated for evaluating the performance of the proposed technique. It gave 99.88% SE, 99.88% PP, 99.88 % F-m, and 0.0766 MSE.

This paper presents a fast and efficient equivalent model for the prediction of the installed radiation pattern of patch antenna. The accurate prediction of radiation pattern on different platforms demands significant CPU time and memory cost. Nonetheless, the proposed model can save both these resources by reproducing a similar radiation pattern as that of the patch antenna. A code is formulated, which uses Green function derivation to determine the electric field of a magnetic dipole. The radiation pattern for near-field and far-field is computed and validated using a commercial software tool (FEKO). Based on the radiation mechanism, an equivalent model is constructed with only two design parameters, i.e., spacing distance between the dipoles in x- and y-directions. The height of the dipole is kept constant above the ground plane. This reduces CPU time and memory cost and makes the model more computationally efficient. After the optimization with FEKO, the installed radiation pattern is computed, and simulation results show that the proposed model can predict the installed radiation pattern of patch antenna mounted on a platform. The proposed model does not require detailed geometry and material information of the patch antenna.

The exoskeleton robot in the rapid development requires physical relation interpretation about scene understanding to fulfill effective interaction. Although traditional scene understanding provides good performance of object recognition and semantic segmentation, it tells us little about physical relation interpretation. Meanwhile, there are few methods to demonstrate the contextual relations among objects in the scene. While some of them artificially define prior constrains and solve the equation by minimizing the objective function, others aim at perceiving the stability of 3D blocks to classify the support relation to several classes. In this paper, a novel approach is proposed which can automatically get the prior knowledge based on deep learning and Conditional Random Fields(CRF) to infer support relationship. In addition, unlike all of previous methods applying the post-processing step after segmenting or recognizing objects, our method is based on end-to-end deep network which could be trained by back-propagation algorithm.
