The support relationship can be directly obtained as the output from a RGB picture input through our approach, where no other intermediate steps are needed. We show the effectiveness of the proposed method on the NYU-Depth V2 dataset in which we manually re-annotate 1449 images.

A genetic-based synthesis approach for different types of rectangular microstrip antenna elements with mutually specified coupling coefficients has been proposed. To achieve this, the continuous parameter genetic algorithm (CPGA) was employed for the synthesis process. Three examples of the synthesized antenna elements are provided, including the rectangular microstrip antenna (RMSA), rectangular ring microstrip antenna (RRMSA) with a smaller slot dimension, and the RMSA with a pair of offset slots (RMSAPOS).

Chatbots are intelligent conversational systems that enable seamless communication between businesses and customers. One of the primary advantages of deploying a chatbot in any industry is that it can operate as a personal assistant, assisting customers with their queries, and concerns. A chatbot must provide an experience that is comparable to interacting with a human personnel.

The objective of this research is to assess the effectiveness and naturalness of chatbot applications in customer service. The naturalness of a chatbot has been compared to that of a human personal assistant to evaluate its performance. The study was conducted using two expert users and cognitive walkthrough method. 

The experiment findings indicate that a human-machine chatbot can offer interactions that are comparable to those of human personnel. However, in some minor cases, human-human communication outperformed machine-based interactions. 

In conclusion, chatbots have emerged as a valuable tool in the business landscape providing an interactive interface for seamless communication between businesses and customers. While their performance may not be at par with that of human personnel, chatbots are a cost-effective and valuable alternative. It is necessary to continue evaluating chatbot naturalness and efficiency to optimize their performance and provide a superior experience to customers.

IoT today invented for creating, editing and sharing information and data. Some sources predict the number of tens and hundreds billion connected devices for the year 2020-2025. One of the most popular standard machine-to-machine application layer protocols to interconnect the things and applications to the Internet of Things is Message Queuing Telemetry Transport protocol. Quality of service (QoS) deal with network performance elements like latency, error rate and uptime. MQTT provides three levels of QoS. Usage time of IoT devices is constrained by its most critical resource - battery. This paper deals with the estimation of energy consumption in transferring data using lightweight MQTT protocol over it different QoS levels. For experiments, we implemented client-server architecture and employ MQTT publish/subscribe protocol to transfer data between nodes.

This paper aims to propose a new optimal hierarchical clustering approach to 3D mobile light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds. The hierarchical clustering is performed on unorganized point clouds based on a proximity matrix that consists of a distance term and a direction term. In the dissimilarity calculation of two clusters, a pair of points from each of two clusters is selected, respectively, and Euclidean distances between the points are employed to define the distance term. The direction term is obtained by the differences of normal vectors at chosen points. The main contribution is that the cluster combination in the hierarchical clustering is optimized by a point-based graph model. The cluster combination is formulated as a problem of matching, optimized by finding the minimum-cost perfect matching in a bipartite graph. The results show that the proposed hierarchical clustering method succeeds in segmenting object from point clouds without any human-computer interaction and outperforms the state-of-the-art segmentation approaches in terms of completeness and correctness.

This chapter tackles the issue of fair resource allocation in wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) for both types of energy storage strategies. For the purpose of analytical tractability, it considers only the additional power consumed by the circuitry and assumes linear radio frequency (RF)‐to‐direct power conversion. The chapter proposes policies for optimal power allocation at the base station (BS) and optimal time sharing among the energy harvesting units (EHUs), such that the resource sharing is proportionally fair. The proposed policies satisfy a constraint for an average power consumption at the BS, which necessitates imposing silence at the BS in the extremely poor channel conditions, and therefore facilitates high energy efficiency of the WPCN. The proposed power and time allocations for fairness‐aware WPCNs are provided in closed forms.

Material degradation detection and diagnosis is a challenging task that presently relies on manual inspection, leading to inaccurate classification and diagnosis. This paper proposes a computer-assisted detection method for material failure using a deep learning approach. The method involves training a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model combined with image processing techniques to classify a real-world turbine tube degradation image dataset. An adaptive histogram equalization technique is used during the training process. The proposed approach demonstrates superior predictive classification accuracy, with a rate of up to 99.99% compared to shallow machine learning algorithms, such as linear SVM. The study also evaluates the performance of deep CNN models with and without the aforementioned image processing technique. This study presents a novel application of constructing a deep-structure neural network model for material degradation diagnosis that is not available in the current literature.

Medical image analysis is currently undergoing a major transformation thanks to the emergence of deep learning technology. Its potential has sparked significant interest within the Medical Imaging Community, culminating in a specialized conference on "Medical Imaging with Deep Learning" in 2018. In this paper, we survey recent developments in this field and offer a critical review of the key aspects involved. The literature is organized according to pattern recognition tasks, and further subcategorized based on human anatomy. This paper offers an accessible introduction to core deep learning concepts for those unfamiliar with the technology. We provide a unique perspective on the advances of deep learning in medical imaging from a computer vision/machine learning perspective. Our analysis identifies the lack of appropriately annotated large-scale data sets as a key challenge in this research direction. Drawing on insights from related research fields such as computer vision, pattern recognition, and machine learning, we offer promising directions for the Medical Imaging Community to harness the full potential of deep learning in the future.

In order to address the issue of teachers being unable to monitor students' e-learning progress and assess their e-learning outcomes during MOOC teaching, we propose capturing student-learning images through a computer camera and utilizing the "Three Angles Synthesis" to determine if the student is actively watching the teaching video online. The proposed approach involves several steps: 

First, we use the Average Feature Point method to locate the center of the iris and calculate the iris deflection angle, as well as the distance between the iris center and the eye center. Second, we utilize the face key point detector in Dlib to identify the key feature points of the face, including the eyes, nose, and mouth, to determine the face rotation angle. Third, we extract the student's target body using the Maximum Connected Domain Moment Characteristic method and calculate the body tilt angle. Finally, we evaluate whether the three angles meet the predetermined conditions to determine whether the student is watching the teaching video online.

This approach allows teachers to effectively monitor students' learning progress during MOOC teaching, and assess the effectiveness of e-learning. The proposed approach is applicable to various e-learning scenarios and provides an effective solution to the monitoring of student learning progress in MOOCs.

User-generated content on social media platforms plays a significant role in shaping and spreading popular topics. However, the increase in online rumors among regular user-generated content has led to the spread of fake news in social networks, causing panic among people. Existing research on rumor detection, such as detection mechanisms based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) or Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), have encountered limitations in feature extraction, which needs improvement in terms of contextual feature extraction. 

This study proposes a dynamic slide-window based text feature scoring and extraction mechanism that facilitates accurate semantic structure representation. Moreover, an effective rumor detection scheme is designed by incorporating the proposed feature scoring and extraction with CNN. The experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed feature scoring and extraction mechanism can extract the important text features by considering their roles in online texts and the relations of these features. Thus, the detection scheme can distinguish rumors from regular messages more accurately.

In single image super-resolution problems, recent feedforward deep learning architectures have been using residual connections to preserve and transfer local features through the next layer. However, the simple concatenation method used in a simple residual skip connection does not take into account the varying usefulness of features. To address this issue, we present an extended architecture or baby neural network that takes the previous layer's learned features as input and outputs a multiplication factor that gives importance to specific features, thus improving the accuracy of training for the current layer's features. Our proposed model has demonstrated superior performance over existing methods.

Digital signal modulation recognition has significant applications in military and civilian scenarios. It can aid in identifying targets and aiding in better management of military and non-cooperation communication scenarios. While deep learning is widely used for classification accuracy, it has not yet been considered for deployment in edge equipment with storage and compute limitations. This paper proposes utilizing neural network pruning techniques to reduce convolution parameters and floating point operations per second (FLOPs) – which will enable the deployment of signal classification convolution neural networks (CNN) in edge equipment. The paper sets the Average Percentage of Zeros (APoZ) criterion for convolution layers, resulting in a light CNN convolution layer that can use just 1.5%~5% parameters and 33%~35% time without significant loss in accuracy when compared to the original CNN.

Super-resolution convolutional neural network (SRCNN) is a deep learning method that reconstructs high-resolution image from low-resolution image. In this paper, we propose to change the ReLU which is the activation function of existing SRCNN, as modified and bilateral ReLU. This modification gives increased number of active nodes and results in improved image quality.

Retrieving contextual information from on-board sensors is a crucial aspect of Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios. However, the battery capacity and physical size of smart devices can limit the on-board sensors that can be utilized, thereby restricting the potential of applications for multi-agent IoT systems. To address this issue, we propose a novel scheme that builds a context neighborhood among nearby devices through infrastructure-less collaboration. A context neighborhood refers to an ad hoc collection of sensing devices that collaborate to sense physical attributes of their environment, allowing all devices to leverage the information collected without requiring every device to sense every context attribute directly.

Our approach involves a distributed algorithm that adjusts a device's sensing and sharing strategy based on the heterogeneity of resources in its proximity. We demonstrate our approach using off-the-shelf IoT sensor kits, showcasing the self-stabilization feature of our prototype system to demonstrate the higher-layer applications' benefits. 

In conclusion, our approach enables IoT devices to collaborate and share context information, thereby expanding the capabilities of the system without requiring additional sensors. The approach's dynamic adaptation strategy ensures optimal resource utilization, which further enhances the system's efficiency.

In this paper, we propose a power minimization problem for heterogeneous cloud radio access networks (H-CRANs). The proposed system takes into account the computing delay constraints and uses M/M/k queues to model the edge device coexisting with the small base station (SBS) to provide computing capabilities alongside the central cloud. The SBS sleeping is governed by the availability of resources provided by the macro base station (MBS), which accommodates offloaded users from sleeping SBSs. However, switching off lightly loaded SBSs can pose significant burdens on cloud servers. Our proposed sleeping scheme allows SBSs serving more computing tasks to remain active to fulfill task completion deadlines requested by mobile users and keep the cloud response time within a predefined limit. 

Our proposed scheme aims to save power by undertaking a centralized selection of active and sleeping SBSs while considering the delay constraints of both cloud and mobile devices. We consider two systems: a disjoint cloud-edge system and a shared computing system. For the disjoint system, where computing services can be provided by either the cloud or the edge device, we aim to minimize the number of active SBSs. The problem is formulated as a 0-1 knapsack problem, with SBS utilization considered as the weight and the ratio of computing tasks to all incoming tasks considered as the value of that SBS. SBSs processing fewer computing tasks are given higher values, resulting in a higher chance to sleep compared to others. The problem is solved using dynamic programming.

For the shared computing system, active SBSs (edge devices) contribute to the total computing capability. Here, we use an exhaustive search approach to achieve the optimal power saving. We also proved that the shared computing system performs better in terms of response time compared to the disjoint system depending on the number of active SBSs.

The prevalence of sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (SAHS) has been steadily rising, with a rate of up to 14% in 2016. This disease can pose a serious threat to human sleep safety, making it vital to detect and pre-alert individuals who may be at risk. To address this need, a new method for diagnosing SAHS has been developed that utilizes respiratory signals.

In this method, nonlinear characteristics such as fractal dimension and sample entropy are introduced based on time-domain characteristics, including variance and clinical zero passing numbers, as well as frequency-domain characteristics such as wavelet coefficients and wavelet energy. These characteristics are used to create a 6-dimension feature vector that is input into the support vector machine (SVM), back propagation neural network (BPNN), and improved back propagation neural network (IBPNN) based on morphology.

The proposed method was validated using eight data sets, which consisted of 3840 samples of the Physionet Apnea Database. The experimental results showed that classification accuracy of SVM and BPNN were 71.2% and 84.5% respectively. The IBPNN based on morphology improved the classification results by 85% and increased accuracy by 7.3%.

Overall, this study shows that the feature vector and IBPNN based on morphology can effectively detect SAHS, providing an efficient and convenient method for diagnosing this disease. As the prevalence of SAHS continues to rise, this method has the potential to help address this growing public health issue.

Internet of Things (IoT) has evolved for building smart environments in a distributed system, where the data produced by IoT devices are transmitted through Edge computing devices to streamline the flow of traffic from IoT devices to a distributed network. In such a scenario, the attacker introduces many attacks to the edge before forwarding them to distributed servers. This necessitates intrusion detection systems for such environments to mitigate security attacks. This paper has projected a basis for characterization of intrusive behaviors in a distributed system based on the functional link neural nets response weighted-average and teaching-learning metaheuristic with elitism on weight-space. The proposed technique makes use of teaching-learning metaheuristic optimization to obtain suitable parameters for the functional link neural net. Furthermore, the processing of duplicate parameters is successfully avoided by using mutation operation. In addition to this, in this paper the proposed method is found to be more efficient in terms of computational burden.

Although deep learning algorithms for diagnosing pathology have shown similar results to those of human experts across a variety of tasks, they require vast amounts of accurately annotated data for training. However, generating such data sets is time-consuming and not feasible for certain tasks, meaning that many medical data sets have limited images, making them insufficient for training. In this study, we demonstrate that few-shot learning techniques can effectively transfer knowledge from a well-defined source domain focused on Colon tissue to a more generic domain composed of Colon, Lung, and Breast tissue, using only a few training images. Our results demonstrate that our few-shot learning approach achieved a balanced accuracy (BAC) of 90% with just 60 training images, even for Lung and Breast tissues that were not included in the training set. This outperforms the fine-tuned transfer learning approach, which achieved a BAC of 73% with 60 images and required 600 images to achieve a BAC of 81%.

In recent years, there has been a significant rise in global energy consumption, which threatens to deplete future energy resources. Given this, it is crucial to explore sustainable energy management options and develop efficient means of energy use at a residential scale. With this in mind, our proposed energy management policy is based on three types of loads: continuous load, intermittent load, and phantom load. We have identified these loads through data collection devices and smart plugs, and in this paper, we outline an approach to classifying and recognizing these loads using machine learning systems like k-NN. Furthermore, we compare our approach with other classifiers in order to identify the most effective means of load recognition.

Optical Character Recognition (OCR) of Arabic text from manuscript images is considered to be extremely challenging due to the semi-cursive nature of Arabic script. Algorithms and image processing methods often struggle to decipher the intricacies of the script. To address this issue, we propose a method for exploring and researching the content of Arabic manuscript images. This method involves characterizing segmented handwritten words using a set of points of interest to identify and study the manuscripts. Each segmented word is described by key features and compared to query words.

Compared to other methods, the results of this approach are highly encouraging, particularly in relation to the consistency of the handwriting style used in the text. Overall, this method offers a promising solution for researchers seeking to deepen their understanding of Arabic manuscripts.

Advancements in sensor design and the convergence of computing, cognition, and communications have opened up a world of possibilities for incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) techniques into assistive technology for the elderly. By combining wearable body sensors with the sensors and processing capabilities of smartphones, researchers have conducted experiments to test various AI algorithms for detecting critical events such as accidental falls, prolonged stationary states, and wandering away from home for those living independently.

The studies revealed impressive results, utilizing AI models such as threshold, artificial neural networks (ANN), support vector machines (SVM), and k-nearest neighbors algorithm (kNN) to identify falls and other events accurately. The AI models were versatile enough to distinguish clearly between fall and non-fall events, and wrist-based sensors proved to be the most effective.

To implement these detection models into a smartwatch and smartphone application, researchers proposed a system architecture that could alert caregivers in the event of an accident or wandering incident. Additionally, data fusion, including video images, is also a consideration for improving the accuracy of detection.

Overall, these advancements in AI-assisted assistive technology have the potential to improve the quality of life of the elderly, providing a means for them to live independently while still maintaining a sense of security for caregivers or family members.

This paper presents a co-design methodology for integrated circuit (IC) packaging that aims to reduce jitter induced by power supply noise in a 28 Gbps high-speed serial link with a 10-layer flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) substrate using TSMC 28nm technology. The proposed methodology focuses on enhancing the power distributed networks (PDNs) during the layout design phase to reduce the parasitic inductance of the power supply and isolate cross-power domains. By implementing these enhancements, the supply noise-induced jitter is reduced by 800% at the output eye-diagram of the 28 Gbps high-speed serial link, compared to the design without PDN enhancements. Notably, the proposed methodology achieves this significant reduction in jitter without increasing package manufacturing costs.

Multimedia researchers have utilized crowdsourced geo-referenced image collections to gain a better understanding of both a location and the subject of an image. The aim of this research is to develop a framework that uses ground-level images to perform fine-grain land use mapping at a city scale. This research presents a novel approach to the geographic knowledge discovery problem, which directly uses ground-level images to map 45 different land-use classes for the city of San Francisco. An end-to-end trained convolutional neural network contains two streams: one for objects recognition and the other for scene recognition. The framework also comprises multiple tactics aimed at overcoming the noisiness of user-generated data, including search-based training set augmentation and online adaptive training. Quantitative analysis and geovisualization demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework, achieving over 29% recall at the individual land parcel level. This research presents a significant contribution towards addressing the challenging 45-way land use classification problem, especially considering the noisiness of the image data.

This paper outlines an algorithm-hardware co-design that supports camera-based autonomous flight in small drones. The authors acknowledge that nonvolatile memory (NVM)-based embedded systems have large write-latency and write-energy, making them unsuitable for real-time reinforcement learning (RL). The proposed solution involves conducting transfer learning (TL) on meta-environments and RL on the last few layers of a deep convolutional network. The NVM stores the meta-model from TL, while on-die SRAM stores the weights of the last few layers. As a result, all real-time updates via RL are performed on the SRAM arrays, creating a practical platform with comparable performance to end-to-end RL at 83.4% lower energy per image frame.

Skin lesion segmentation is a fundamental step in computer aided diagnosis (CAD) for automated melanoma diagnosis. While fully convolutional networks (FCNs) have shown success in general image segmentation, the lack of large labelled medical image datasets has contributed to current FCN models relying on specific cost functions and post-processing techniques to improve segmentation accuracy. In this paper, we propose the use of generative adversarial networks (GANs), which can produce consistent and realistic image features using deep neural networks and adversarial learning concepts. By incorporating a stacked adversarial learning architecture, the proposed method improves skin lesion feature learning in a class-specific manner. Our results demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing skin lesion segmentation methods on the ISIC 2017 dataset. Furthermore, adding the outputs of our method to existing FCN training data increases overall feature diversity.

A new non-contact heartbeat detection method has been proposed in this paper using non-negative matrix factorization (NMF)-based blind source separation (BSS), which improves the accuracy of heartbeat extraction by incorporating the stochastic gradient approach. In traditional methods, the decomposition of signal by singular spectrum analysis (SSA) is often affected by interfering signals from respiration and body motion, resulting in inaccurate extraction of heartbeat component. The proposed BSS approach considers the motion noise as one of the sources and decomposes the spectrogram originating from radar signal twice by NMF to learn the basis spectra based on spectral correlation. This method achieved relatively stable separation in various scenarios and showed improved accuracy and robustness in heart rate (HR) measurement against subjects' sitting still or typewriting. The method exploits the spectral sparsity of the heartbeat component and suppresses residual noises after signal decomposition, allowing for high-resolution heartbeat spectrum reconstruction by Doppler radar signal.

Most existing state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms discover sophisticated representations in huge datasets using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that mainly adopt backpropagation (BP) algorithm as the backbone for training the face recognition problems. However, since decades ago, BP has been debated for causing trivial issues such as iterative gradient-descent operation, slow convergence rate, local minima, intensive human intervention, exhaustive computation, time-consuming, and so on. On the other hand, a competitive machine learning algorithm called extreme learning machine (ELM) emerged with extreme fast implementation and simple in theory has overcome the challenges faced by BP. The ELM advocates the convergence of machine learning and biological learning for pervasive learning and intelligence and has been extensively researched in widespread applications. Nonetheless, till date, none of the work of ELM has proved its competency in tackling face verification problem. Hence, in this paper, we are going to probe for the first time the feasibility of ELM-based network in handling the face verification task. We devise and propose a novel and distinguished hybrid local receptive field-based extreme learning machine with DeepID (hereinafter denoted as H-ELM-LRF-DeepID), to discriminate face pairs. The experimental results on the YouTube face database, labeled faces in the wild (LFW), and CelebFaces datasets have shed light upon the feasibility and usefulness of the H-ELM-LRF-DeepID in the face verification task.

With the increasing availability of acquisition and display devices for Light Field (LF) content in the consumer market, the popularity of this new immersive media is rapidly growing. However, this also raises the urgent question of how to effectively compress LF images to ensure their efficient transmission and storage. To address this issue, we propose a convolutional neural networks (CNN)-based LF image coding scheme that incorporates Rate Distortion Optimization (RDO) and post-processing steps.

At the encoder side, our scheme rearranges the views into sparse and dropped sets. The former is compressed using a standard encoder and transmitted, while the latter is either linearly approximated or synthesized by a CNN block based on the RDO process. At the decoder side, the dropped views are reconstructed using either linear approximation or CNN synthesis and then passed through a post-processing block based on superpixel to pixel-matching to further improve visual quality.

Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme outperforms state-of-the-art LF image compression solutions by -30% in terms of BD-BR and 0.62 dB in BD-PSNR, while providing views with high visual quality. Our CNN-based approach effectively addresses the issue of LF image compression, ensuring efficient transmission and storage while maintaining high-quality images.

Deep learning-based methods have been proven to be effective in classifying hyperspectral images, especially through the use of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). However, previous methods relied on manually selecting input cuboids, which can lead to suboptimal results. To address this issue, this letter explores the use of a spatial transformation network (STN) to optimize the input for CNN-based HSI classification. By applying translation, rotation, and scaling to the original input, the resulting input is better suited for the following CNN. Additionally, to mitigate overfitting in CNN-based HSI classification, a new regularization technique called DropBlock is introduced, which has been shown to outperform the popular dropout technique. Experimental results on the Salinas and Kennedy Space Center datasets demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods utilizing deep CNNs.

The prospects of achieving a trillion connected internet of things (IoT) devices by 2020 has created the urgency for effective intrusion detection systems (IDS) for these devices. Although it has been argued that the most effective technique used in such systems is anomaly detection, there exist no mechanisms to determine their performance in real-life deployment. In this paper, we report the results of applying asymptotic analysis to evaluate the performance of an anomaly detection algorithm which is designed using logic reasoning through fuzzy logic methodologies. In order to achieve this, the IDS was included as part of intrusion detection software for ZigBee Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). In particular, the solution is targeted to address the ZigBee protocol's vulnerability to flood attacks during node discovery and association to the network. The intrusion detection software is hosted external to the WSNs in pursue of a light solution mindful of resource preservation in sensor nodes.

Wireless energy transfer (WET) is a promising solution for powering energy-efficient devices. Our proposed strategies involve using multiple antennas at a power station to wirelessly charge a large set of single-antenna devices without relying on channel state information (CSI). We have successfully attained the distribution and main statistics of the harvested energy under Rician fading channels with sensitivity and saturation energy-harvesting impairments. 

Our study found that switching antenna strategy, where a single antenna transmits at a time, provides the most predictable energy source and is suitable for sensor nodes with highly sensitive EH hardware operating under non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions. Other WET schemes perform similarly or better in terms of the average harvested energy. 

Transmitting simultaneously with equal power in all antennas is the most beneficial as line-of-sight (LOS) conditions increase. Spatial correlation is not beneficial unless the power station transmits through all antennas simultaneously, creating a tradeoff between the average and variance of the harvested energy. 

Finally, the number of devices has a significant effect on the performance gap between CSI-free and CSI-based strategies. As the number of devices increases, the performance gap decreases rapidly. Overall, our study presents effective and efficient strategies for wireless energy transfer.

In this paper, we present a new channel estimation technique specifically designed for frequency-division duplex (FDD) based massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. In these systems, cascaded precoding is used to reduce the dimensionality of the physical channels, so that traditional channel estimation techniques can be applied over a lower-dimensional effective channel. However, because of the lack of a priori knowledge of the downlink channels, these traditional techniques often fail to achieve the minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) performance required for optimal performance.

To address this challenge, we propose a limited feedforward strategy for downlink channel estimation based on the parametric model. This model represents the frequency response of the channel using path delays and corresponding complex amplitudes. Specifically, we first estimate and quantize the path delays of uplink channels at the base station, and then feed them forward to the user equipment (UE) via a dedicated feedforward link. The UE can then use this information to obtain a good approximation of the downlink channel, assuming reciprocity between downlink and uplink path delays.

Our analysis and simulation results demonstrate that our limited feedforward method can achieve near-MMSE performance, making it a promising approach for improving FDD-based massive MIMO systems.

In the machine learning community, data augmentation techniques have been widely used to make deep neural networks invariant to object transition. However, less attention has been paid to data augmentation in traditional classification methods. In this paper, we take a closer look at traditional classification methods and introduce a new data augmentation technique based on the concept of image transformation. Starting with a few existing examples, we add noise and generate new data points to reduce sparseness in a given feature space. Then, we generate images corresponding to the new data points, although this is usually an ill-posed problem. Herein, the novelty is in constructing an image transformation tree and generating new data from a small number of instances. This allows us to reduce sparseness in the feature space and build more robust classifiers. We evaluate our method on the Caltech-101 dataset to verify its potential. In the context of the situation where the amount of training data is limited, we demonstrate that the support vector machine-based classifiers trained with an augmented dataset using our method outperform classifiers trained with the original dataset in most cases.

Sparse representation of structured signals requires modelling strategies that maintain specific signal properties, in addition to preserving original information content and achieving simpler signal representation. Therefore, the major design challenge is to introduce adequate problem formulations and offer solutions that will efficiently lead to desired representations. In this context, sparse representation of covariance and precision matrices, which appear as feature descriptors or mixture model parameters, respectively, will be in the main focus of this paper.

As a multimedia security mechanism, CAPTCHAs serve as a completely automated public Turing test to differentiate between computers and humans. Despite several efforts to crack CAPTCHA, it still remains a challenging problem for real-life solutions. In this demonstration, we present a text-based CAPTCHA cracking mechanism, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs). To tackle the small sample problem, we propose combining conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (cDCGAN) and CNNs, which has resulted in a significant accuracy improvement. Additionally, multiple models with low Pearson correlation coefficients are selected for majority voting ensemble, which further enhances the system's accuracy. The experimental results have shown remarkable progress in the accuracy of the system, thus providing a new method for cracking CAPTCHAs.

In real-time applications, a fast and robust visual tracker should generally have the following important properties: 1) feature representation of an object that is not only efficient but also has a good discriminative capability and 2) appearance modeling which can quickly adapt to the variations of foreground and backgrounds. However, most of the existing tracking algorithms cannot achieve satisfactory performance in both of the two aspects. To address this issue, in this paper, we advocate a novel and efficient visual tracker by exploiting the excellent feature learning and classification capabilities of an emerging learning technique, that is, extreme learning machine (ELM). The contributions of the proposed work are as follows: 1) motivated by the simplicity and learning ability of the ELM autoencoder (ELM-AE), an ELM-AE-based feature extraction model is presented, and this model can provide a compact and discriminative representation of the inputs efficiently and 2) due to the fast learning speed of an ELM classifier, an ELM-based appearance model is developed for feature classification, and is able to rapidly distinguish the object of interest from its surroundings. In addition, in order to cope with the visual changes of the target and its backgrounds, the online sequential ELM is used to incrementally update the appearance model. Plenty of experiments on challenging image sequences demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed tracker.

In this study, we sought to investigate whether a virtual avatar with non-human likeness, capable of expressing basic emotions, could increase user engagement and interest in a virtual reality (VR) environment. While VR environments offer realistic renderings, we posited that not all virtual characters need to closely resemble humans. Simple, non-human characters, such as cartoons, can also have a strong impact on users' affinity towards games. 

Therefore, our aim was to examine if interactions with a cartoon-like character that can express common emotions could influence users' behavior and engagement with the character. Specifically, we sought to determine if adding emotions to virtual characters would increase user interest. To address these questions, we conducted a study using a human-like cartoon character in a VR environment that responded to users' input with simple, basic human emotions. 

Our findings indicate that displaying emotional traits or responses can benefit a cartoon-like character when interacting with humans in a VR environment. With these results, we conclude that adding emotion expression to non-human virtual characters can effectively improve user engagement and interest.

This letter presents a novel hand-eye calibration technique that utilizes reprojection error minimization. In contrast to conventional hand-eye calibration methods, the proposed approach directly captures images of the calibration pattern and does not necessitate explicit estimation of the camera's pose for each input image. The proposed technique is formulated as a pose graph optimization problem, ensuring efficient and robust estimation, while also allowing for easy adaptation to various projection models. By changing the projection model, it can accommodate different camera models, such as X-ray cameras with a source-detector projection model. Through simulations, the proposed method demonstrated excellent estimation accuracy and proved to be effective for hand-eye calibration with a source-detector camera model. The experimental results with real robots confirmed that the proposed approach is viable in real-world scenarios and enhances the quality of tasks that require precise hand-eye estimation, such as three-dimensional reconstruction.

A highly efficient memristor-based activation circuit for memristive neuromorphic systems has been developed, which utilizes only two memristors and a comparator. This circuit approximates the ReLU activation function for the first time, which significantly reduces the time and computational costs associated with training in neuromorphic systems due to its simplicity and effectiveness in deep neural networks. Furthermore, this activation circuit has been used to simulate a multilayer neural network along with traditional memristor crossbar arrays. The results demonstrate that the proposed circuit is capable of training effectively, while reducing the time and area required in memristor crossbar based neural networks.

Event-based online social platforms, such as Meetup and Plancast, have experienced increased popularity and rapid growth in recent years. In EBSN setup, selecting suitable venues for hosting events, which can attract a great turnout, is a key challenge. In this paper, we present a deep learning based venue recommendation system DeepVenue which provides context driven venue recommendations for the Meetup event-hosts to host their events. The crux of the proposed model relies on the notion of similarity between multiple Meetup entities such as events, venues, groups, etc. We develop deep learning techniques to compute a compact descriptor for each entity, such that two entities (say, venues) can be compared numerically. Notably, to mitigate the scarcity of venue related information in Meetup, we leverage on the cross domain knowledge transfer from popular LBSN service Yelp to extract rich venue related content. For hosting an event, the proposed DeepVenue model computes a success score for each candidate venue and ranks those venues according to the scores and finally recommend the top k venues. Our rigorous evaluation on the Meetup data collected for the city of Chicago shows that DeepVenue significantly outperforms the baselines algorithms. Precisely, for 84 percent of events, the correct hosting venue appears in the top 5 of the DeepVenue recommended list.

The studies performed by the authors show that when using the model of generalized syntagmas, it is possible to implement the PMT process using a shorter and simpler technological scheme. This technological scheme can be reduced to two stages: 1) the stage of formation of several search syntagmas characterizing the semantic content of the source text sentences (on the base of results of morphological and simplified syntactic analysis); 2) the stage of searching for semantic information in the reference dictionaries of translations of global and local constructions of sentences, having which it will be possible to automatically form translated sentences of text on their basis. A comparison of the effectiveness of phraseological machine translation using the method of generalized syntagmas and without using it was made.

In this paper, we present a framework that focuses on mitigating multi-vector anomalies that are detected in common enterprise networks. Our approach involves distributing access control rules in a non-proprietary and distributed manner that utilizes the potential of all the devices in the attack path. The devices are categorized into separate defense stages, and operators express their preferences for specific attack types. Our mechanism automatically assigns generic mitigation rules to each of the defense stages. Then, device-specific access control rules are generated and distributed seamlessly to the corresponding defense stages of the network substrate through commonly used protocols.

To model the rule assignment to defense stages, we propose a mitigation schema that treats the problem as a Generalized Assignment Problem. The generic mitigation rules act as items that are assigned to bins, which are the defense stages considered based on capacity constraints and reward values that align with operator policies. To enable the integer programming formulation to be reasonable in execution, our approach includes reducing the GAP input size by organizing rules into groups and aggregating malicious IP sources into prefixes.

Our proposed approach was tested in a proof of concept prototype, where it was used to mitigate realistic multi-vector attack scenarios. The results show that our mechanism successfully detects and mitigates multiple types of attacks in enterprise networks.

The measurement of software trustworthiness is a widely-discussed topic in the industry. As software component technology dominates the software development field, it is imperative to determine the trustworthy degree of software components accurately and efficiently. However, this is no small challenge for component-based software development. Obtaining the level of trustworthiness required for software components necessitates numerous successful cases from multiple users. 

In this paper, we propose an innovative updating model for software component trustworthiness. Initially, we compute the trustworthy degree of the software component based on users' feedback. Then we determine the weight of updating based on the number of users. Finally, we cluster different companies using the Euler distance method. 

In conclusion, we demonstrate that this method is reasonable and effective by presenting a case study.

This study aims to explore the application of brainwave-controlled light changes, Unity visual images, sound effects, and virtual reality immersive training in educational fields for concentration training. It has been found that using brainwaves to control interactive game applications can be an effective way to improve students' concentration and learning outcomes. In the study, participants were exposed to different game effects which were controlled by the brainwave controller that outputted alpha (α) and beta (ß) waves. The study found that interesting training can effectively enhance the concentration level of students. Not only does it create an immersive learning environment, but it also increases students' interest and motivation towards concentration training. Thus, the results of this study suggest that integrating brainwave-controlled game applications can help students to improve their concentration levels, leading to better academic performance.

Base on the fourth-order cumulants, a direction finding algorithm for noncircular sources under unknown mutual coupling is proposed. Utilizing the symmetric Toeplitz structure of the mutual coupling matrix and the noncircularity of the sources, a closed form solution for the DOA estimation is obtained by constructing a series of cumulant matrices. According to the simulation results, the proposed algorithm is effective in the presence of unknown mutual coupling. Moreover, it enjoys better estimation performance via utilizing the noncircularity of the sources.

In this study, we have developed and demonstrated two variable stiffness soft elastomeric actuators, each consisting of two symmetrical pneumatic chambers and an inextensible layer embedded in the middle. The inextensible layer limits elongation and instead generates an isometric expansion, resulting in bending of the structure when a pressure is applied to each chamber. The proposed actuators are called Antagonistic Pneumatic Actuators (APA Pneunet and APA FRA) and demonstrate antagonistic behavior due to their symmetric assembly of two chambers. 

The APA actuators have enhanced properties, including bi-directional motion and a higher capacity for withstanding external loads. When equal pressure is applied, the actuators increase their stiffening behavior. The stiffness of the structure can be changed by varying the applied pressure on either chamber. In terms of actuation force displacement, both the APA Pneunet and FRA actuators have demonstrated good performance, providing stiffness and actuation at the same time. 

In axial position, the APA Pneunet and FRA actuators have shown 19.93N and 29.6N in passive mode and 23.53N and 44.87N in active mode (maximum pressure 1.0 bar), respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of the APA actuators for creating a wide range of soft robotic applications that require variable compliance and stiffness.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has become a powerful platform for connecting objects to the internet and allowing for machine-to-machine communication using standardized network protocols. As IoT continues to grow, with billions of devices already connected and the number expected to reach trillions in the coming years, various industries are adopting IoT for advanced solutions in military, agriculture, healthcare, robotics, nanotechnology, and more. 

This research paper proposes a new concept for robotics, called the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT), which combines various technologies such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and IoT. The paper also examines the architecture necessary for designing multi-role robotic systems for IoRT, including the technologies behind IoRT, its applications, and existing robotic systems based on humanoid, mobile, flying, and swarm technology. 

Overall, this paper lays a strong foundation for researchers to envision the concept of IoRT and encourages them to think creatively in designing and implementing IoRT-based robotic systems into real-world applications.

With the technologies for machine learning and big data handling new opportunities for classification and prediction tasks have arisen. On the other hand the technology of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) has become indispensable in aviation in the last ten years. Putting these items together paves the way for new applications for real-time radar surveillance systems. That applies to both the civil environment and the world of military systems. This paper describes the complete processing chain to prepare ADS-B data for machine learning and training, which finally leads to applications that can be applied to real-time systems.

Digital evidence is an essential part of cyber-forensics and legal proceedings. However, with the increasing volume of digital content, the work of forensic examiners is becoming more challenging. In this study, machine learning, particularly deep learning, was used to detect hidden watermarks in various types of files. The approach used in this study was different from current steganographic and cryptographic methods. The researchers used a black box approach to detect patterns of candidate file locations for hidden data. 

Deep Neural Networks (DNN) were employed to predict hidden watermarks using the Deep Learning 4 Java (DL4J) implementation and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) algorithms as implemented in Weka. The MLP models were evaluated by varying the number of neurons and hidden layers, while the DL4J models were evaluated by varying the number of dense layers and nodes. 

The MLP models predicted hidden watermarks in DOCX and PPTX files with predictive accuracies ranging from 47.5% to 100%. For JPEG singleton models, predictive accuracies ranged from 35% to 65%. HYBRID3 models had predictive accuracies ranging from 42.5% to 95%, while HYBRID_OOXML had predictive accuracies ranging from 47.5% to 100%. On the other hand, JPEG_DOCX had predictive accuracies ranging from 47.5% to 97.5%, while JPEG_PPTX had predictive accuracies ranging from 40% to 85%. 

Deep learning models also provided significant improvements in predicting hidden watermarks in PPTX files using DL4J models. HYBRID3 DL4J models predicted hidden watermarks in DOCX files with predictive accuracies of 100%. In PPTX files, the predictive accuracies ranged from 55% to 82%, while in JPEG files, the predictive accuracies ranged from 50% to 52.5%. 

Overall, this study shows the potential of machine learning, particularly deep learning, in detecting hidden watermarks in various types of files. The results of this study can be useful in cyber-forensics and legal proceedings.

Indoor localization has become a hot topic in recent years because of its wide applications. Map matching is a popular method used to improve the localization accuracy without adding hardware. However, the existing map matching methods are usually computationally expensive, leading to the unsuitability of running on resource-limited devices such as smartphones. In this paper, we present an efficient map matching system for indoor localization, called HTrack, which uses a hidden Markov model, considering the user's heading and spatial information. By considering user's heading information, we significantly reduce the number of candidate states for each step, and hence improve the computational efficiency. The experimental results show that the HTrack outperforms the state-of-the-art methods (more than 25% localization accuracy improvement), and consumes about five times less energy than the state-of-the-art methods.

With the significant increase in integration of renewable energy generation into the electric grid, market-based transactive exchanges between energy producers and prosumers will become more common. Transactive energy systems (TESs) employ economic and control mechanisms to dynamically balance the demand and supply across the electrical grid. Emerging transactive control mechanism depends on a large number of distributed edge-computing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices making autonomous/semi-autonomous decisions on energy production, and demand response. However, the electric grid cyber assets and the IoT devices are increasingly vulnerable to attack. TES will likely have similar vulnerabilities and cyber attacks especially with financial interest motives of stakeholders, which could affect the operation of the power grid. Therefore, new analytical methods are needed to continuously monitor these systems operations and detect malicious activity. In this research work, various components of transactive energy systems are modeled and simulated in detail. Various cyber attack models are developed based on threats identified in TES. A deep learning approach called deep stacked autoencoder (SAE) is utilized to detect possible anomalies in the market and physical system measurements. The proposed unsupervised technique is validated for satisfactory performance to detect anomalies and trigger a further investigation for root cause analysis using end-to-end TES testbed and use case.

Generating SQL queries from natural language has been a challenging problem for a long time. To answer a question about a database table, it is necessary to model complex interactions between table columns and the question. Recently, there has been a surge of interest in this area, driven by the advancements in deep learning techniques. In this paper, we propose a sketch-based approach to address the problem. We decompose the model into three sub-modules based on the structure of SQL queries and design specific deep neural networks for each of them. To enhance the result, we use bidirectional attention mechanisms and character-level embedding with CNNs. Our experimental evaluations indicate that our model outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods in the WikiSQL dataset.

Danger Theory stipulates a powerful defensive mechanism underpinning the human immune system, which is a sophisticated classification metaphor, namely, Dendritic Cell Algorithm (DCA) which has been demonstrated in many real-life applications. In this paper, the DC-inspired metaphor is adopted in the domain of the behavioural detection for field operation training. This signal-based classification algorithm empowers with a robust learning capability and self-organizing control mechanism, whereby the "danger signals" correspond to the safety and procedural related activities, are being differentiated from the information which are captured in immersive virtual environments including the Training of Ramp Operations in Virtual Environment (TROVE) and Detective Boulevard supported by the imseCAVE virtual reality system. As such, the performance of the trainees can be assessed and enumerated by the DCA autonomously, that can improve the quality of assessment made by the trainers or coaches. In a benchmark study, the operational training of aircraft door handling is considered, in particular to study the behaviours in operational procedures and safety concerns. According to the experimental results, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) outperformed DCA in the given domain with respect to the performance of classification accuracy and run time.

In this paper, a low-energy rate 1/2 successive cancellation (SC) decoder hardware architecture is proposed for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Arikan's SC decoder and different optimized versions of it are implemented in ASIC flow. Hardware optimizations are applied to the conventional SC architecture, including the removal of frozen bits driving blocks, resource sharing between f and g blocks and the removal of log-likelihood magnitude computation in the last stage. Synthesis results show that these optimizations provide 38.7% saving in energy/bit consumption, 83% saving in area and 68.0% increase in throughput for 64-bit conventional SC decoder and up to 79.5% in 1024-bit implementation. The synthesis results are compared with the literature, and the results show that the proposed 64-bit SC architecture gives less energy/bit consumption and area. Moreover, linearly scaled 1024-bit synthesis results predict a middle-ground performance of the proposed architecture compared to the literature, hence suggesting the proposed structure to IoT applications, especially small packet size applications.

The growing interest in machine learning among business leaders and decision makers demands that researchers explore its use within business organisations. One of the major issues facing business leaders within companies is the loss of talented employees. This research studies employee attrition using machine learning models. Using a synthetic data created by IBM Watson, three main experiments were conducted to predict employee attrition. The first experiment involved training the original class-imbalanced dataset with the following machine learning models: support vector machine (SVM) with several kernel functions, random forest and K-nearest neighbour (KNN). The second experiment focused on using adaptive synthetic (ADASYN) approach to overcome class imbalance, then retraining on the new dataset using the abovementioned machine learning models. The third experiment involved using manual undersampling of the data to balance between classes. As a result, training an ADASYN-balanced dataset with KNN (K = 3) achieved the highest performance, with 0.93 F1-score. Finally, by using feature selection and random forest, F1-score of 0.909 was achieved using 12 features out of a total of 29 features.

Classification is a crucial aspect of Brain-Computer Interface issues where the main objective is to identify an individual's intent from various options, typically individuals with physical or verbal disabilities. Our research involved recording MEG signals from a subject while they viewed 5 different types of video clips, and our task was to process the MEG signals for each experiment to determine the type of movie from the 5 options. To solve this multiclass classification problem, we utilized a range of approaches and eventually formulated a novel algorithm that could be applied to any multiclass issue. 

Our algorithm uses a decision tree approach where the classes are divided into two groups at each node. But, we have defined a criterion to find the optimal partitioning using the training data results of only (n/2) classifications between each set of classes. This makes the algorithm polynomial and ensures that it can be applied to any multiclass problem easily. In terms of accuracy, our algorithm had the best accuracy (61.4%) compared to other routine methods. Therefore, this algorithm could be a robust tool to solve any multiclass classification problem.

Hierarchical heavy hitters (HHH) identification is a crucial process in network monitoring, as it enables various utilities such as anomaly detection, DDoS mitigation, and traffic analysis. However, with the increasing use of jumbo frames, attackers can overload the system with fewer packets and easily bypass detection by packet counting techniques. 

In this paper, we propose an efficient algorithm for HHH detection based on their traffic volume. Our algorithm asymptotically improves on the runtime of previous works, making it a more effective solution. We implemented our algorithm in Open vSwitch (OVS) and found it to have only a 4-6% overhead, compared to the 42% throughput reduction experienced by the current state-of-the-art.

By identifying HHH more efficiently, we can better detect and prevent network attacks, safeguarding the integrity and security of our networks.

Feature-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms with additional semantics can have better feature matching and tracking accuracies than the original SLAM algorithms. Therefore, this paper shows how to improve feature-based SLAM by only matching features from objects of the same semantic class. The basic idea is to use a deep neural network, YOLO (you only look once [1]), to classify objects and to associate features with the objects in whose bounding box they appear, thus giving features the semantic label of these objects. During feature matching of the SLAM algorithms, only features with the same semantic label are matched (e.g. books with books, bottles with bottles etc.), eliminating matches of similar features on different classes of objects. Experiments of classical ORB-SLAM2 with YOLO have been performed on an embedded PC. Additionally, ORB-SLAM2 with different versions of YOLO has also been tested on a powerful desktop GPU as well as on an Nvidia Jetson TX2 board. The experimental results show that using the semantic information given by object recognition methods reduces wrong feature matches in tracking and decreases the tracking lost cases.

The research work on camera placement has traditionally focused on maximizing coverage or minimizing installation costs for video surveillance systems. However, typical placement schemes do not account for divergences in coverage demands, leading to increased system costs and reduced efficiency. In this paper, we propose an inverse modeling taxonomy to address the camera placement problem. Through the use of Risk Maps, we prioritize security sensitive zones prior to coverage optimization, enhancing the reliability of our proposed placement scheme. Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, and we validate our scheme in a constraint environment.

This paper proposes an Automated E-R Diagram Generation (AGER) System that can generate E-R Diagram from a given text in Natural Language given as input. Natural language texts are used to perform the information extraction by parsing the syntax of the sentences and semantically analyzing their content. The AGER System parses an input text in natural language, semantically analyzes it and internally uses some domain specific database and POS tagging to detect Entity and Relations from the given passage and builds a graph that represents the E-R Diagram. The E-R Diagram can be traversed to generate Data Definition Language to create the actual relations in any RDBMS system. The abstract nature of entity relationship diagram makes it difficult for database designers to directly create E-R Diagram from the natural language text input statement which is used to create the physical model of the database. In the requirement analysis phase of any software design, often Databases designers need to have elaborate discussions with the client on the use cases of the databases and at the end of the work they come up with a neat E-R Diagram which shall be used in subsequent phases to physically realize the relations and implement them. The AGER system proposed here is aimed to assist database designers to create E-R Diagram directly from Client’s requirements in natural language.

Accident prevention is a critical concern at construction sites where trucks, cranes and work vehicles are in operation. To ensure worker safety and mitigate risks of collisions, high-precision surveillance cameras with 4K resolution are being used as IoT terminals in these environments. Our research involves transmitting photographic images from construction equipment with 4K cameras fitted at the work site to a database via 5G wireless networks. Using AI, the interactions and movements of workers are assessed in the database, allowing us to implement a system that prevents crashes by informing truck and crane drivers of potential risks and notifying automatic driving vehicles of the situation.

However, as more vehicles equipped with 4K cameras transmit images simultaneously over the 5G uplink, there is a risk of uplink traffic congestion. To address this issue, we have developed a system that evaluates the basic characteristics of 5G, where transmission of 4K images from trucks or cranes moving at low speeds is prioritized based on moving speed and distance to the 5G terminal connecting the base station and IoT device.

We have also conducted evaluations of the system's performance in error-prone environments that impact AI's ability to accurately identify and judge the surrounding environment in degraded video quality. By analyzing the relationship between system errors and video quality degradation, we can improve the reliability of the system's error management and ensure that workers are in safe environments at all times.

Product lifecycle management (PLM) is an engineering management approach that assists organizations in managing product-related technical data throughout its lifecycle. Having the right product data is crucial for effective business functioning in organizations. PLM systems are recent and upcoming tools in the manufacturing industry, and cloud technology is taking it from organizational boundaries to a global level through the Internet. However, there are various challenges that manufacturing firms face during cloud PLM adoption.

The aim of this paper is to empirically investigate the critical challenges manufacturing firms face while adopting cloud PLM. There is limited academic research in the cloud PLM domain. This paper results in the three most significant challenges, which are “Data security on clouds,” “Lack of trust on services,” and “Lack of customization.” These challenges not only assist managers in manufacturing firms in planning to migrate to the cloud but also aid technical cloud providers in enhancing their cloud services and systems appropriately to improve the compatibility of cloud PLM in firms.

This paper uniquely identifies the essential challenges for cloud PLM adoption in large manufacturing firms, which will undoubtedly bring robust insight to the industry. It is crucial to address these challenges to ensure successful cloud PLM adoption, which will result in efficient product lifecycle management in the manufacturing industry.

There is a continual increase in the number of real-world Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. However, single IoT devices are not yet able to fully exploit the capabilities of Artificial Intelligence due to computation complexity and energy consumption being constraining requirements for their development and implementation. This paper presents an experimental study that observes the time of execution, overheating, Central Processing Unit (CPU) load and power consumption of an embedded system alone and one with an external low-power Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). The latter is able to run pre-trained neural networks for object detection. A series of experiments is conducted on neural networks with different depth and input size to report on their potential for AI applications on IoT devices. The experimental results demonstrate a high potential for AI on IoT devices.

The health status of distribution equipment and networks is not considered directly in existing distribution network planning methods. In order to effectively consider the health status and deal with the risk associated with load and renewable generation uncertainties, this paper presents a new optimal expansion planning approach for distribution network (EPADN) incorporating equipment's health index (HI) and non-network solutions (NNSs). HI and relevant risk are used to help develop the optimal equipment replacement strategy and temporary NNSs are considered as promising options for handling the uncertainties of load growth, reliability requirements of power supply and output of distributed energy resources (DERs) at a lower cost than network alternatives. An EPADN model using network solutions (NSs) and NNSs is proposed. The planning objectives of the proposed model are safety, reliability, economy, and `greenness' that are also the meaning of distribution network HI. A method integrating an improved niche genetic algorithm (INGA) and a spanning tree algorithm (STA) is fitted to solve the model presented here for real sized networks with a manageable computational cost. Simulation results of an actual 22-node distribution network in China, illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Shrinking of device dimensions has undoubtedly enabled the very large scale integration of transistors on electronic chips. However, it has also brought to surface time-zero and time-dependent variation phenomena that degrade system's performance and threaten functional operation. Hence, the need to capture and describe these mechanisms, as well as effectively model their impact is crucial. To this extent, we follow existing models and propose a complete framework that evaluates failure probability of electronic components. To assess our framework, a case-study of packet-switched Network on Chip (NoC) routers is presented, studying the failure probability of its SRAM buffers.

In this paper, we introduce a deep-learning-based framework to solve electromagnetic inverse scattering problems. This framework builds on and extends the capabilities of existing physics-based inversion algorithms. These algorithms, such as the contrast source inversion, subspace-optimization method, and their variants face a problem of getting trapped in false local minima when recovering objects with high permittivity. We propose a novel convolutional neural network architecture, termed the contrast source network, that learns the noise space components of the radiation operator. Together with the signal space components directly estimated from the data, we iteratively refine the solution and show convergence to the correct solution in cases where traditional techniques fail without any significant increase in computational time. We also propose a novel multiresolution strategy that helps in producing high resolution solutions without any significant increase in computational costs. Through extensive numerical experiments, we demonstrate the ability to recover high permittivity objects that include homogeneous, heterogeneous, and lossy scatterers.

The Multi User-Multiple Input Multiple Output (MU-MIMO) technique offers big advantages over traditional MIMO solutions. Nevertheless, Nonlinearity of High Power Amplifier (HPA) presents a crucial role in the performance of MU-MIMO systems.This paper investigates the performance of Massive MIMO system in the presence of nonlinear HPA over Rayleigh fading channel. Different receivers and algorithms are used in order to illustrate this fact, such as LS, MMSE, ZF and AMP, are evaluated and mutually compared. Specifically, we assess the effect of the nonlinear distortion on the BER. Numerical results are provided and show the impacts of several system parameters, such as type of receivers, number of antennas, number of users and values of IBO, on system performance.

We propose an end-to-end architecture for joint 2D and 3D human pose estimation in natural images. Key to our approach is the generation and scoring of a number of pose proposals per image, which allows us to predict 2D and 3D poses of multiple people simultaneously. Hence, our approach does not require an approximate localization of the humans for initialization. Our Localization-Classification-Regression architecture, named LCR-Net, contains 3 main components: 1) the pose proposal generator that suggests candidate poses at different locations in the image; 2) a classifier that scores the different pose proposals; and 3) a regressor that refines pose proposals both in 2D and 3D. All three stages share the convolutional feature layers and are trained jointly. The final pose estimation is obtained by integrating over neighboring pose hypotheses, which is shown to improve over a standard non maximum suppression algorithm. Our method recovers full-body 2D and 3D poses, hallucinating plausible body parts when the persons are partially occluded or truncated by the image boundary. Our approach significantly outperforms the state of the art in 3D pose estimation on Human3.6M, a controlled environment. Moreover, it shows promising results on real images for both single and multi-person subsets of the MPII 2D pose benchmark and demonstrates satisfying 3D pose results even for multiperson images.

Vehicle mobile Internet of Things uses sensor technology, mobile Internet technology, and intelligent computing technology to effectively monitor and provide comprehensive services for vehicle operation status. It is an important part of building a smart city, making urban transportation more efficient, environmentally friendly, intelligent, and safety. In the vehicle mobile Internet of Things, when in-vehicle sensors are in communication with each other, they are often affected by factors, such as network mobility, transmission range, and signal interference. Therefore, in order to ensure the continuity of communication between nodes and improve the quality of network communication, this paper proposes a vehicle mobile Internet of Things coverage enhancement algorithm (PANM). First, we derive the probabilistic analysis model of communication duration by analyzing the functional relationship of vehicle initial velocity, acceleration, spacing distance, and communication duration. Then, under the premise of ensuring the communication duration, in order to improve the coverage of the vehicle mobile Internet of Things, the network overlap ratio is introduced in the probability analysis model. Finally, we improve the network coverage performance of omnidirectional radiation and fan-shaped radiation communication models of vehicle mobile Internet of Things by limiting the overlap ratio threshold. The experimental simulation results indicate that the PANM algorithm can reduce the packet loss rate of the vehicle network and have a shorter communication delay.

The coordination of directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) is essential in ensuring the safe protection of power systems by coordinating primary and backup protection systems. However, the optimization model for this problem is non-linear and highly constrained. In this paper, we propose a hybridized version of the Whale optimization algorithm (WOA) called HWOA for the optimal coordination of DOCRs.

The proposed algorithm combines WOA with simulated annealing (SA) to improve the best solution found after each iteration and enhance the exploitation by searching for the most promising regions located by the WOA algorithm. This leads to a globally optimal solution. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we applied it to five test systems, including the IEEE 3-bus, 8-bus, 9-bus, 15-bus, and 30-bus test systems.

Comparing the results obtained using the proposed HWOA with those obtained using traditional WOA and several up-to-date algorithms, we found that the proposed algorithm effectively minimizes the relay operating time for the optimal coordination of the DOCRs. Therefore, the hybridized version of the WOA algorithm provides an efficient approach for solving the non-linear and highly constrained optimization model for the coordination of DOCRs.

The merger of actors and sensors in a wireless network has evolved those opportunities that we can't think before some years. This merger has captured the interest of researchers from around the globe. In the last decade, wireless networks have become much stronger, reliable and secure but as the technology evolves, it carries their own problems. Researchers are targeting different problem according to their own interest like power consumption, network security, link failure etc., so we are also working on link failure detection that can be caused by power breakage, network delay or traffic overload. This model detects the link failure in the network through Link Failure Detection Algorithm (LFDA) and provide recovery mechanism against failure using cluster-based approach. Our purposed model detects network link failure accuratly and precisely solve the problem by creating alternative virtual route for data packets. Our technique can detect current failures also it can detect weaker links, those might be the cause for future failures. Most of the literature have their proof of correctness as simulation but no technique is there which is formally verified, therefore we have presented our idea including its formal verification and validation with the help of formal methods tool box and its formal specification language like (VDM-SL).

Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) channels are unique due to the dynamic environment and low elevation of antennas at both ends of the link. The behavior and reliability of the communication link depends on the severity and dynamics of both line-of-sight and multipath components (MPCs) blockage. Blockage becomes more critical with increasing carrier frequency, and signal penetration through objects diminishes. In this study, we measured V2V channels in four frequency bands (6.75, 30, 60, and 73 GHz) in urban and highway scenarios to characterize the effects of vehicle blockage. Our analysis shows that blocking vehicle size and position strongly influence blockage loss and angular/delay spread. Frequency dependence is limited, with slight increases in blockage loss and reduction in scattered MPCs as frequency increases. Our results suggest that V2V communication in high frequencies, even in the case of blockage by other vehicles, is possible.

For the acceptance of spectral measurement technology for quality assurance and inspection in the industrial sector, the acquisition and processing of spectral images must be adapted to the production cycle. When processing spectral images, variations of the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) are often used as preprocessing steps, for example for segmentation, spectral decomposition or data compression. To speed up this time-consuming algorithm, hardware and software cores were implemented on a system-on-a-programmable-chip (SoPC).
