To enhance service provisioning architectures in NFV-based transport optical networks, we suggest a reallocation-based provisioning mechanism. This approach can decrease experiencing blocking up to three orders of magnitude.

To measure the ability of a machine to understand professional-level scientific articles, we construct a scientific question answering task called PaperQA. The PaperQA task is based on more than 80 000 “fill-in-the-blank” type questions on articles from reputed scientific journals such as Nature and Science. We perform fine-grained linguistic analysis and evaluation to compare PaperQA and other conventional question and answering (QA) tasks on general literature (e.g., books, news articles, and Wikipedia texts). The results indicate that the PaperQA task is the most difficult QA task for both humans (lay people) and machines (deep-learning models). Moreover, humans generally outperform machines in conventional QA tasks, but we found that advanced deep-learning models outperform humans by 3%-13% on average in the PaperQA task. The PaperQA dataset used in this paper is publicly available at http://dmis.korea.ac.kr/downloads?id=PaperQA.

The visual data gathered from widespread visual sensors situated across cities are of immense value and are vital in improving the efficiency and development of smart cities. This paper outlines the essential building blocks of a comprehensive visual data management and analytical infrastructure that serves as the backbone of the economical visual system in the city brain. The aim is to facilitate the efficient utilization of the visual signal in the era of artificial intelligence.

The paper begins by discussing the smart visual sensing in the context of economical communication and service in a heterogeneous network. The paper details the need for compact visual feature and deep learning model representations. Subsequently, the utilities of the infrastructure are demonstrated through two intelligent applications at the back-end, including vehicle re-identification and person re-identification. 

The paper also addresses the standardizations surrounding compact feature and deep neural network representations, which are crucial components of this infrastructure and greatly aid the construction of the visual system in the city brain. Finally, the paper envisions how the potential challenges relating to economical visual communications for smart cities can be addressed pragmatically within this unified infrastructure.

This paper studies underdetermined direction of arrival (DOA) estimation accuracy by sum and difference composite co-array. We have studied to further enhance the DOF by combining the concepts of the sum co-array and the difference co-array, which is called “sum and difference composite coarray”, and evaluated its beamforming performance. We aim at investigating if the sum and difference composite co-array also works well for underdetermined DOA estimation problems. Performance of the proposed array configuration is evaluated through computer simulation of DOA estimation.

To solve the problems of the data reliability for NAND flash storages, a variable-node-based belief-propagation with message pre-processing (VNBP-MP) decoding algorithm for binary low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is proposed. The major feature is that, by making use of the characteristics of the NAND flash channel, the proposed algorithm performs the message pre-processing (MP) scheme to effectively prevent the propagation of unreliable messages and speed up the propagation of reliable messages. To further speed up the decoding convergence, the treatment for oscillating variable nodes (VNs) is considered after the MP scheme being employed. Simulation results show that the proposed VNBP-MP algorithm has a noticeable improvement in convergence speed without compromising the error-correction performance, compared with the existing algorithms.

Fingerprint Indexing is a technique that can be used to filter databases for samples that are most similar to a query fingerprint. This approach uses fixed-length feature vectors and is insensitive to the number of minutiae. As a result, comparison can be done quickly. The first approach, Deep Convolutional Neural Networks are used to generate fixed-length index vectors from minutia neighbourhoods. This approach is also insensitive to minutiae sorting. Fingerprint image data is not required. The use of standardized ISO/IEC minutia templates enables deployment in legacy systems as well. Therefore, this approach is known as Deep ISO Minutiae Indexing (DIMI). Index vectors can be as short as 16 float values per sample. DIMI was evaluated at the independent benchmark framework FVCongoing. In the incremental search scenario, DIMI achieves an average penetration ratio of 0.747% for test FIDX-50K and 0.723% for test FIDX-10K respectively. These are the best results reported so far.

This paper reviews the development and application architecture of an expert system to assist the Mauritian population with queries they may have about labor or employment law. The expert system makes use of Machine Learning, Speech Recognition/Synthesis and Natural Language Processing techniques to converse with users through a web interface. The expert system also takes advantage of a large knowledge base, that allows the system to teach itself employment law principles. The knowledge base is created from "Understanding Employment Law and Remuneration Orders in Mauritius", written by Ved Prakash Torul [1], which is a simplified version of the Employment Relations Act and the Employment Rights Act. The book explains employment law in common language, to help the public understand their constitutional rights. The expert system allows users to communicate and express their employment issues, so that they are aware of their next course of action, either they are an employer, employee, or a union. The paper also reviews the evaluation period, which consisted of a preliminary testing period. Through the evaluation, it was concluded that the expert system was able to respond to individual responses with a Precision of 66% and Recall of 85%. While the Expert System is able to converse with users on certain topics on Employment Law, further evaluation would need to be conducted. Additionally, the knowledge base will need to be updated over time.

This work presents the development of a Network-on-Chip environment based on multiagent systems. This simulator aims to provide high level of abstraction to quickly simulate, compare and choose routing algorithms. The simulator calculates routers occupancy rate, number of messages that passed through each router and the number of messages lost. As a case study, the XY and West-First routing algorithms were modeled and analyzed. Simulation results indicated a better use of spare routers by the West-First algorithm when compared to the XY algorithm.

Event-based social networks (EBSNs) are becoming increasingly important as they provide a perfect platform for offline social events to be conveniently organized online. EBSNs offer the benefits of both online social networks and offline social communities, allowing users to interact face-to-face in organized events. Despite previous research showing that member and structural features play an essential role in group popularity in EBSNs, the interplay between member roles and their contribution to group popularity is still not clear. 

In this study, we analyzed a real-world dataset from Meetup, a well-known EBSN platform, and proposed a deep-neural-network-based method to forecast the popularity of new Meetup groups. Our method incorporates group-level features specific to EBSNs, such as event time and location of groups, as well as internal structural features, such as the inferred member roles and social substructures among group members. 

Our findings demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces the normalized root-mean-squared error of predicting group popularity (measured in RSVPs) by up to 12% compared to existing state-of-the-art models. Moreover, our method identifies patterns in member and structural characteristics that are highly predictive of a group's future success. 

Overall, our study provides new insights into the strategies that make a group successful in EBSNs.

Radar technology for at home health-care has many advantages such as safety, reliability, privacy-preserving, and contact-less sensing nature. Detecting falls using radar has recently gained attention in smart health care. In this paper, CapsFall, a new method for fall detection using an ultra-wideband radar that leverages the recent deep learning advances is proposed. To this end, a radar time series is derived from the radar back-scattered matrix and its time-frequency representation is obtained and used as input to the capsule network for automatic feature learning. In contrast to other existing methods, the proposed CapsFall method relies on multi-level feature learning from radar time-frequency representations. In particular, the proposed method utilizes a capsule network for automating feature learning and enhancing model discriminability. The experiments are conducted using a set of radar signals collected from ten subjects when performing various activities in a room environment. The performance of the proposed CapsFall method is evaluated in terms of classification metrics and compared with those of the other existing methods based on convolutional neural network, multi-layer perceptron, decision tree, and support vector machine. The results show that the proposed CapsFall method outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity values.

Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is considered to be one of the best candidates for future networks due to its ability to serve multiple users using the same resource block. Although early studies have focused on transmission reliability and energy efficiency, recent works are considering cooperation among the nodes. The cooperative NOMA techniques allow the user with a better channel (near user) to act as a relay between the source and the user experiencing poor channel (far user). This paper considers the link security aspect of energy harvesting cooperative NOMA users. In particular, the near user applies the decode-and-forward (DF) protocol for relaying the message of the source node to the far user in the presence of an eavesdropper. Moreover, we consider that all the devices use power-splitting architecture for energy harvesting and information decoding. We derive the analytical expression of intercept probability. Next, we employ deep learning based optimization to find the optimal power allocation factor. The results show the robustness and superiority of deep learning optimization over conventional iterative search algorithm.

In this article, the author delves into the structure of engineering activity, shedding light on the challenges faced during its formation in higher education institutions. A significant aspect highlighted by the author is the necessity for educational departments in leading higher education institutions located in St. Petersburg to adopt efficient practices that will assist in training graduates for independent work. The article also addresses the issue of professional orientation for school children, emphasizing the importance of extracurricular activities in general secondary schools as a means of providing them with insights into choosing engineering professions.

Consider a convex set from which we have removed a number of disjoint convex sets, called obstacles, and a convex function whose minimum is the goal of the agent. We propose a local and stochastic approximation of the gradient of a Rimon-Koditschek navigation function, where the attractive potential is the convex function that the agent is minimizing. Our approach guarantees convergence to the desired location while avoiding the obstacles with probability one, provided that the estimate available to the agent is unbiased. This holds true under the same geometrical conditions as in the deterministic case. The conditions state that the ratio between the maximum and minimum eigenvalue of the Hessian of the objective function is not too large, and that the obstacles are not too flat or too close to the desired destination. We show that even if the estimate available to the agent is biased, convergence to a point arbitrarily close to the goal is achieved with probability one, provided that certain assumptions on the bias are met. These assumptions are motivated by the study of the estimate of the gradient of a Rimon-Koditschek navigation function for sensor models that fit circles around the obstacles. Finally, we demonstrate the practical value of our theoretical results through numerical examples.

Recognizing a submerged body in turbid water poses a significant challenge, as limited light conditions and water turbidity prohibit clear image quality. Additionally, conventional feature-based approaches may be limited due to the diverse form and intensive noise level in the target object image. To address this issue, we propose an automated submerged body classification system which utilizes multibeam sonar technology. To train our system, we utilize Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based models such as AlexNet and GoogLeNet. We tested our system using two sets of underwater sonar image data from a submerged body of a dummy, which included varying levels of water clarity and noise such as clear water in an indoor pool and turbid water in the ocean.

A statistical language model is essentially a probability distribution that assigns probabilities to sequences of words. This model is widely used in various computing tasks such as speech recognition, machine translation, handwriting recognition, and information retrieval. Traditionally, n-gram models have been used for language modeling, but recently, neural language models have emerged as a more accurate means of approximating the probability of a sentence using neural networks and word embeddings.

One key advantage of neural language models is their ability to be applied to other NLP tasks where limited training data is available. In this talk, we demonstrate this by introducing the use of a Vietnamese neural language model that has been trained on a large corpus of social media data. By applying this model to tasks such as entity recognition, spam detection, and topic modeling, we have achieved improved performance compared to other existing approaches using deep learning and typical word embedding techniques.

Overall, the emergence of neural language models offers significant promise for improving the accuracy and efficiency of NLP tasks in a variety of applications.

In large-scale cellular internet-of-things (IoT) networks, bursty traffic can lead to network overload, despite periodic and sporadic traffic being able to be managed effectively. This paper presents a generalized random access (RA) control mechanism that considers the entire RA process and the available resources at each step to handle bursty traffic in cellular IoT networks. The proposed mechanism includes an estimation method for the backlog of nodes and a computation method for access class barring (ACB) factors. Extensive computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed RA control mechanism outperforms the conventional RA control mechanism, which only focuses on controlling preamble transmissions at the first step of the RA process. Specifically, the proposed mechanism showed enhanced performance in terms of the total service time, average access delay, and energy efficiency.

This paper proposes a novel two-archive evolutionary algorithm called TwoArchM, which takes into account both convergence and diversity for many-objective optimization problems. The main idea of the proposed algorithm is to use two separate archives to balance the trade-off between convergence and diversity, while employing a multi-search strategy to improve both aspects. The algorithm adopts two updated strategies to maintain diversity and enhance convergence, respectively, and uses a search strategy to balance exploration and exploitation. The search strategy selects convergent solutions from offspring and two archives as parents to improve the convergence, while the other strategy aims to balance exploration and exploitation. The experimental results on the CEC2018 many-objective benchmark functions with up to 15 objectives demonstrate the competitiveness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm when compared to several state-of-the-art algorithms.

This paper presents a novel method for image classification using the encoding of a set of covariance matrices. This is done through the use of Fisher vectors adapted to the log-Euclidean metric, resulting in log-Euclidean Fisher vectors (LE FV). Furthermore, this approach is extended to encompass full local Gaussian descriptors, which consist of a set of local mean vectors and local covariance matrices. Local Gaussian models are transformed into zero-mean Gaussian models with augmented covariance matrices for improved accuracy. 

Both handcrafted and deep learning features are utilized in these approaches. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed LE FV, this method is applied in a remote sensing application on the UC Merced dataset, which involves the classification of land cover images. To test the potential of the proposed method, a sensitivity analysis is carried out. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in accurately classifying images.

Increasing the number of photovoltaic (PV) parks, along with wind farms and other renewable energy sources, represents a promising solution to reducing carbon emissions, which are believed to contribute significantly to climate change. However, PV cells are vulnerable to the effects of various weather events due to their open-space installation - this can lead to a decrease in efficiency and performance over time. In this study, we propose a monitoring system for PV panels that utilizes machine learning techniques to identify potential operation issues. Our model is developed and validated using data collected from both the control system of the PV panels and weather data sourced from the Internet.

Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) refers to inferring semantic labels based on the content of the remote sensing scenes. Recently, most works take the pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) as the feature extractor to build a scene representation for RSSC. The activations in different layers of CNN (named intermediate features) contain different spatial and semantic information. Recent works demonstrate that aggregating intermediate features into a scene representation can significantly improve the classification accuracy for RSSC. However, the intermediate features are aggregated by some unsupervised feature encoding methods (e.g., Bag-of-Visual-Words). Little attention has been paid to explore the information of semantic labels for the feature aggregation. In this paper, in order to explore the semantic label information, an end-to-end feature aggregation CNN (FACNN) is proposed to learn a scene representation for RSSC. In FACNN, a supervised convolutional features' encoding module and a progressive aggregation strategy are proposed to leverage the semantic label information to aggregate the intermediate features. The FACNN integrates the feature learning, feature aggregation, and classifier into a unified end-to-end framework for joint training. In FACNN, the scene representation is learned by considering the information of semantic labels, which can result in better performance for RSSC. Extensive experiments on AID, UC-Merged, and WHU-RS19 databases demonstrate that FACNN performs better than several state-of-the-art methods.

This study aimed to determine the rail voltage for a 1500 V DC-fed rail system by utilizing three different techniques: the adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), support vector machines (SVM), and artificial neural networks (ANN). The distance on the line was calculated based on the operating parameters using the ANFIS, SVM, and ANN. These three methods were described and compared. 

The electrification system for rail systems is designed based on operating data and design parameters. When forming the electrification system, the maximum rail voltage needs to be provided within the limits of the touch voltage limits during operation. The highest value of rail voltage that occurs on the line is determined by the line's characteristic properties. This value needs to be kept within certain limits to ensure the continuity of operation. 

To simulate both one-way and two-way supply conditions, data were collected and analyzed. Overall, this study demonstrates that ANFIS, SVM, and ANN can be effective techniques for determining rail voltage in 1500 V DC-fed rail systems.

We suggest utilizing a silicon photonics (SiP) solution to alleviate signal-signal beat interference (SSBI) and salvage a fraction of the downlink carrier for uplink use in a passive optical network. The direct detection Kramers-Kronig (KK) receiver can handle advanced modulation formats while overcoming SSBI, but requires a significant carrier to signal ratio (>6 dB) and high oversampling (4×). Our optical SSBI solution surpasses KK in terms of performance, while requiring only standard sampling and low (3 dB) carrier to signal power ratio. The SiP-based receiver is optimized for the downlink in passive optical networks, where carriers must be conserved for reuse in the uplink. Our SiP solution filters the incoming signal, suppresses SSBI, and redirects a portion of the carrier for the uplink. We experimentally prove SSBI suppression using cost-effective and power-efficient SiP, rather than relying on bulky, discrete components for significant Q-factor improvement. We study the optimum frequency offset between the carrier and the microring resonator center frequency, as well as robustness to frequency drift and the effects of imperfect filtering, and quantify these factors.

Anonymous Voice over IP (VoIP) communication is a valuable tool that enables freedom of speech. To ensure both quality of service (QoS) and anonymity, connecting mixes by padded links is a promising approach. However, building suitable overlay topologies for establishing padded links is challenging. The existing approaches are either not scalable due to using full meshes or impractical because of the computational complexity of the algorithms used to create optimal reduced topologies. This limits their deployment as volunteer-based networks like Tor. 

In this paper, we propose and investigate various heuristic strategies for reduced topology construction and path selection with low computational complexity. We assess the effectiveness of our approach using latency and bandwidth estimates from the Tor network. Our results show that we can achieve appropriate performance and anonymity metrics for VoIP. Moreover, the achieved features are similar to those of a recently proposed approach that computes optimal topologies for small networks.

In this paper, an optimum broadband Conformal Strongly Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) is designed which provides simultaneously high efficient power transfer and high data-rate communication through the same link. This wireless power transfer system is able to achieve 20 MHz bandwidth at the operating frequency of 115 MHz maintaining over 80% power transfer efficiency. The integrated planar broadband strongly coupled magnetic resonant system is able to deliver 30% of the given power to a 50 Ω load. Utilizing the large bandwidth, a high data rate digital communication through the same link is achieved, using backscattering modulation. The data transfer is accomplished with 6 Mbps data-rate and 30% overall system efficiency.

The small-signal model of the incremental optical encoder introduced in this paper provides an insight on the impact of this sensor in the dynamics of the motion control loop of a motor drive. The model is derived and validated for the most commonly employed speed estimation methods: the pulse count and the elapsed time methods. Using the model, the reduction of the phase margin due to the encoder phase lag can be quantified at an early design stage. This model facilitates the design of control techniques to compensate for the phase margin reduction due to the associated feedback delays.

Image registration is a critical process in computer vision that enables the alignment of images depicting the same scene taken from different perspectives or at different times. This process involves the use of area-based or feature-based image matching techniques. Feature-based image registration, in particular, is concerned with identifying relevant features in the input images and attaching descriptors to them. The matching of these visual descriptions is an essential task in image registration, and it is currently accomplished through Exhaustive Search or the Nearest Neighbor Search.

Traditionally, the k-d tree representation has been used for nearest neighbor search. However, this process can also be performed using combinatorial optimization algorithms such as Simulated Annealing, which is known to be a computationally intensive technique. To address this issue, this work proposes a novel method that streamlines the image feature matching process by using a faster version of Simulated Annealing called Threshold Accepting.

Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms several existing methods in terms of producing better results in a minimal number of iterations. This approach would undoubtedly improve the efficiency and accuracy of image registration and lay the groundwork for more advanced applications in computer science and computer vision.

The noise effect during training and inference for deep artificial neural network hardware acceleration is analyzed in this paper. The noise effect is extremely important when designing hardware for machine learning due to non-ideal devices and circuits. We found that both forward propagation noise and weight update noise can have detrimental effect on the inference, but may not necessarily harm the training result. Pipelining approach supporting redundant runs for each input image is proposed to address the forward propagation noise, and an additional approach of using parallel memory weight cells to represent one synaptic weight is proposed to address the weight update noise. By using these approaches, MNIST classification accuracy on a deep neural network can be improved close to the ideal accuracy when no noise is present.

A significant amount of research has been conducted on adapting 3GPP Long Term Evolution (LTE) and LTE-Advanced (LTE-A) random access to be more efficient for machine-to-machine (M2M) devices because of the huge number of such devices that may reside in each LTE/LTE-A cell. However, there are other attributes of M2M applications that can be used as the basis of independent efficiency improvements. One characteristic which has been overlooked thus far is the spatial and temporal correlations that often exist in the activity of neighboring M2M devices belonging to the same M2M application. In this paper, we illustrate how these correlations can be exploited by coordinating the preambles to be used by neighboring M2M devices to reduce the number of collisions during LTE-A random access, particularly in wireless sensor network (WSN) type applications. The technique is referred to as proximity coordinated random access (PCRA). Through simulation of an example local preamble coordination algorithm that can be executed autonomously by randomly deployed devices of the same M2M application, we demonstrate an increase in the efficiency of the random access process.

Face analysis data often have an imbalanced class distribution, with a few majority classes containing most of the data and scarce instances in minority classes. Current deep learning methods address this issue by using classic strategies such as class re-sampling or cost-sensitive training. In this study, we conducted extensive experiments to validate the effectiveness of these classic approaches for representation learning on class-imbalanced data. We also demonstrated that deep representation can be improved by enforcing a deep network to maintain inter-cluster margins within and between classes, resulting in more balanced class boundaries locally. The approach, called Cluster-based Large Margin Local Embedding (CLMLE), was deployed with angular margins on a hypersphere manifold and combined with a simple k-nearest cluster algorithm, resulting in significant improvements in accuracy for face recognition and attribute prediction tasks that exhibit imbalanced class distribution.

Most existing algorithms for depth estimation from single monocular images need large quantities of metric ground-truth depths for supervised learning. We show that relative depth can be an informative cue for metric depth estimation and can be easily obtained from vast stereo videos. Acquiring metric depths from stereo videos are sometimes impracticable due to the absence of camera parameters. In this paper, we propose to improve the performance of metric depth estimation with relative depths collected from stereo movie videos using existing stereo matching algorithm. We introduce a new “relative depth in stereo” (RDIS) dataset densely labeled with relative depths. We first pretrain a ResNet model on our RDIS dataset. Then, we finetune the model on RGB-D datasets with metric ground-truth depths. During our finetuning, we formulate depth estimation as a classification task. This re-formulation scheme enables us to obtain the confidence of a depth prediction in the form of probability distribution. With this confidence, we propose an information gain loss to make use of the predictions that are close to ground-truth. We evaluate our approach on both indoor and outdoor benchmark RGB-D datasets and achieve the state-of-the-art performance.

This chapter delves into the fundamental characteristics of network elements, aimed at providing an understanding of their functionality without immersing too much into their specific architecture or technology. Optical and electrical network resources are the two broad categories under which the network elements in an optical network are classified. The chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the optical fiber, laser transmitter, p-type, intrinsic and n-type, and avalanche photodiode receivers, and optical amplifiers, highlighting their attributes and functionalities as they relate to communication networks. 

Moreover, basic optical components that constitute different network modules are discussed in detail. The various types of multiplexers and de-multiplexers, as well as different kinds of wavelength routers, are exhaustively explained. Additionally, the chapter focuses on the broad range of large port switching fabrics and describes the wavelength converters, followed by an overview of function blocks that includes the network access terminal, reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexers, and optical cross-connects.

Online anonymity is considered as one of the great gifts of the Internet, but it also brings dangers to society, such as cybercrime, online sexual abuse and bullying, and love scams. Many people are fond of chatting online to make new friends, but how can they be sure that the person sitting behind the other computer is really the person they claim to be? By studying stylometry and keystroke dynamics features from chat data, it is feasible to reveal the actual gender of an online user. In this paper, we examined stylometry and keystroke dynamics features from chat data, and proposed a Random Forest based gender prediction approach by analyzing these features. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a data acquisition was conducted to capture the keystroke dynamics and text information when participants were chatting remotely via Skype. All participants were invited to chat freely on any topic they prefered in order to get to know each other. Based on our experimental result, the proposed approach achieved 72% prediction accuracy by analyzing on this free-text data captured only in 15 minutes.

Adding the feature of business process event prediction to information systems increases its productivity in the long run, enhances the quality of the taken decisions, and eliminates inconsistencies. Inspired by the previous works of employing deep learning approaches to predicting the next process event based on files of logged events, we propose the use of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) to address the same problem. In the proposed approach we used a five-layer 1D CNN method to predict the next process event based on the previous instances. This paper compared the proposed approach with other approaches that used recurrent neural networks (RNN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks, and others on eight datasets. The proposed approach outperformed all the previous studies of the state-of-the-art in this domain on all the provided datasets.

Probabilistic Occupancy Map (POM) is a method to estimate a location of multiple people, given images taken by multiple cameras from different angles set at a head level. It is useful even in the case of significant occlusion and can derive a location of people without an appearance model and prerequisite knowledge about the number of people in a detection space. However, the computation time of POM increases according to the area of detection space and number of cameras, which limits its performance. In this paper, we report performance enhancement of POM by applying OpenMP and GPGPU. As a result of evaluating test videos with different area size and cameras, we confirm that OpenMP implementation marks 1.8 to 2.7 times speedup compared to single CPU core implementation for all videos, whereas GPU implementation provides speedup in case of large grid size by a maximum of 7.6 times.

This work proposes a sensor fault isolation scheme for co-existence of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) current sensor and non-sensor imbalance faults. The proposed method examines DC link battery current residuals to determine the location of machine current sensor and non-sensor imbalance faults. Power conservation evaluation, phase current signals estimation and sensor information recovery are performed in the proposed method to derive DC link battery current residuals which reflect different features of various fault scenarios for fault isolation. The proposed scheme is capable of isolating complicated fault scenario of a machine current sensor fault and a non-sensor imbalance fault co-existence, which is a challenging issue in PMSM and is not well addressed in existing literature. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is confirmed by simulation results in MATLAB for a PMSM under both phase current sensor fault and non-sensor phase imbalance fault.

We present an adaptive observer that is capable of accurately estimating the state and parameters of linear time-varying systems, even when the state matrix depends on unknown parameters. Initially, we assume that the state matrix is affine in these parameters. Our proposed observer is capable of generating state and parameter estimates, which exponentially converge to the plant state and the true parameter, respectively. This is ensured by the persistence of excitation condition, which must hold, and when the unknown parameters are situated in a neighborhood of known nominal values. It is important to note that prior knowledge of the unknown parameters is required, but not of the state itself.

Additionally, we have modified the adaptive observer and its convergence analysis to be applicable to systems whose state matrix is smooth in the unknown parameters, instead of being affine. In this case, convergence is approximate, and no longer exponential. We provide an example as an illustration of these results, for which we investigate the required distance between the unknown parameters and their nominal values numerically.

Overall, our proposed adaptive observer provides a robust solution for accurately estimating the state and parameters of linear time-varying systems, even when the state matrix depends on unknown parameters. Furthermore, our modification of the observer to handle systems with smooth state matrices ensures that our observer is widely applicable to a range of real-world situations.

Selecting the appropriate specialization is a fundamental factor in achieving success both academically and professionally. Students' performance improves when the area of specialization matches their interests and abilities. Previous studies on the influential factors affecting specialization selection mainly utilized statistical analysis, but none employed machine learning techniques to aid in decision making. This research aims to identify the crucial local factors that impact specialization selection in Palestine and build a classification model that can predict suitable specializations for high school students.

The research employed a filter approach Correlation-based Feature Selection (CFS) and factor analysis approach Principle Component Analysis (PCA) to identify the five primary influential factors affecting specialization selection in Palestine. A special questionnaire was designed to collect data on these factors, including previous knowledge and student experiences. The collected data served as input to the classification model built using PART.

The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 77.4% for the training group and 73.7% for the testing group. It adopted 49 rules, which served as a map guiding high school students through the process of selecting the appropriate specialization. By considering the identified influential factors, the model aids students in making informed decisions that match their interests and skills.

In conclusion, the proposed model provides a valuable tool for high school students in Palestine seeking to choose a suitable specialization. It utilizes machine learning techniques to identify the critical factors affecting specialization selection in Palestine and builds a classification model that predicts the most suitable specialization for students based on the identified rules. This model has high accuracy and can serve as a guide for students seeking to achieve academic and professional success.

The growth of Internet usage changed the way of human communication, therefore also changing how malicious activity are conducted in the virtual world. Network security is still an issue that is treated by firewalls, Web Applications Filters and proxies in corporate networks, but there is a lack of solutions for personal networks monitoring that require no access to infrastructure, i.e. clients of one Internet Service Provider (ISP). In this paper we present a solution that addresses these issues and we focus on testing its performance on an typical WPA2 personal network scenario.

This paper presents a computational simulation of a low power, non-volatile memory cell utilizing inorganic molecular metal oxide clusters, known as polyoxometalates (POMs). The storage media is embedded in the gate dielectric of a Fully Depleted Silicon On Insulator (FDSOI) device. Using a multi-physics simulation framework, we evaluated the variability in the programming window of the molecular based flash cell, specifically focusing on threshold voltage variability caused by random dopant fluctuations and random special fluctuations of the molecules in the floating gate of the flash-cell. Our study can be applied not only to POM-based flash cells but also to flash cells based on alternative molecules used as a storage media.

Sweep coverage is a critical issue in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), where mobile sensor nodes move around to collect sensing data from Points of Interest (POIs) at a low cost. With remote sensing capabilities, mobile sensor nodes do not have to reach POI locations to gather sensing data. One of the essential considerations in sweep coverage planning is the sweep radius, which is the maximum distance between a mobile sensor node and POI that allows for sensing. Another critical factor is the energy limitation faced by mobile sensor nodes, which are typically battery-powered with a limited lifetime. Thus, they periodically return to the base station to replenish their energy to continue their coverage. 

This paper formulates the sweep coverage problem based on sweep radius and energy limitation as (t, T, R)-SCBR. Two algorithms, a centralized approach (CPS) and a distributed approach (DPP), are proposed to address the (t, T, R)-SCBR problem. Through extensive simulations, it is found that both proposed algorithms significantly outperform prior schemes in solving the sweep coverage problem.

"Source ID Mix" is a dangerous type of cyber attack that manipulates the source information of synchrophasor data, resulting in the breakdown of wide-area measurement systems applications. To combat this sophisticated threat, we have developed a method that utilizes the spatio-temporal characteristics of the data to authenticate source information. Our approach can detect three types of spoofing attacks and overcomes practical difficulties in applying the method in real-time with limited measurement data. Through experimentation with actual synchrophasor measurements, we have confirmed the effectiveness of our approach in detecting complex data spoofing and enhancing cyber security in power systems."

With the rapid development of the Internet, more and more users expressed their views on the Internet. Therefore, the big data of texts are generated on the Internet. In the era of big data, mining the sentiment tendencies contained in massive texts on the Internet through natural language processing technology has become an important way of public opinion supervision. In this paper, the sensitive information topics-based sentiment analysis method for big data is proposed. This method integrates topic semantic information into text representation through a neural network model. The attention mechanism is introduced into the neural network, and context-aware vector is introduced to calculate the weight of each word. In addition, in order to make the model more adaptable, the method of sentiment dictionary tagging is used to obtain the training data. The experimental results show that the proposed model can effectively improve the accuracy of sentiment analysis results.

Improving the communication abilities of people suffering from speech disorders or hearing impairments and who are struggling to learn sign or spoken language can improve their quality of life. However, methods to assist such people are not varied, and those that consider the degree of physical disability usually fail to attend particular needs. Thus, it is necessary to provide various communication methods according to the characteristics of each physical disability. In this paper, we devise a customized hand sign recognition system according to the degree of physical disability, and propose a method to select a customized set of signs comprising specific hand motions that an individual can effortlessly perform. We consider the optimal set as that providing high reliability and efficiency to realize smooth communication and apply information theory towards their selection. That is, we consider hand sign recognition from myoelectric potentials elicited by finger movement as a communication channel. Then, the optimal hand sign set is determined considering the set with the maximum channel capacity, as it reflects the most reliable and efficient combination. Finally, experimental results obtained from three subjects verify that the proposed method can determine the optimal set of hand signs according to each subject and that increasing the available hand signs or choosing hand signs with high recognition rate do not necessarily contribute to the optimal set.

Recent technological advancements are focused on developing smart systems to improve people's lifestyles, with machine learning algorithms and artificial intelligence becoming essential tools used in the establishment of modern smart systems worldwide. Automatic face detection solutions have been devised for various applications, including security, energy efficiency, and attendance solutions. The Viola-Jones face classification framework has proven to be a remarkable and robust approach for this purpose. In this context, an FPGA-based embedded realization of the Viola Jones algorithm has been achieved, with the circuit synthesized on the Cyclone IV FPGA family. The utilization of FPGA pins is discussed, and the prototype functionality is successfully tested, with results presented.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is in the midst of defining and developing the future space and ground architecture for the coming decades to return science and exploration discovery data back to investigators on Earth. Optimizing the data return from these missions requires planning, design, standards, and operations coordinated from formulation and development throughout the mission. The use of automation enhanced by cognition and machine learning are potential methods for optimizing data return, reducing costs of operations, and helping manage the complexity of the automated systems. In this article, we discuss the potential role of machine learning in the linkto- link aspect of the communication systems. An experiment using NASA's Space Communication and Navigation Testbed onboard the International Space Station and the ground station located at NASA John H. Glenn Research Center demonstrates for the first time the benefits and challenges of applying machine learning to space links in the actual flight environment. The experiment used machine learning decisions to configure a space link from the ISS-based testbed to the ground station to achieve multiple objectives related to data throughput, bandwidth, and power. Aspects of the specific neural-network-based reinforcement learning algorithm formation and on-orbit testing are discussed.

Collaborative filtering (CF) is vulnerable under shilling attack, which misleads recommendation of CF by injecting well-crafted profiles to a targeted system. Although a number of supervised learning based shilling attack detection methods are proposed, their features mainly measure rating values and items of a profile individually, but ignore the relation between items. This study aims to enhance the robustness of CF against shilling attack by considering the rated item correlation. Real users rate items based on their preferences, but rated items are randomly selected for malicious users profiles in most shilling attack. Therefore, the rated item correlation of real and malicious profiles is different. Three features are proposed to capture the information from different intervals of the distribution of rated item correlation in terms of Cosine Association (CA). A benchmark dataset, MovieLens 100K, is used to evaluate the proposed features. The discrimination ability of the proposed features is also illustrated. The experimental results suggest that the proposed features have significant contribution on shilling attack detection.

This article presents an innovative solution to address the motion camouflage challenge for point-mass robots. By utilizing a Lyapunov-based control approach, we tackle a particular scenario in which there exists one shadowee and one shadower in a predefined workspace. Our solution leverages control inputs developed for the shadower and the shadowee in a manner that ensures that the shadower continually follows the camouflage constraint line. The camouflage constraint line is defined as the line that links the shadowee's current position with a fixed focal point. This approach enables the shadower to appear stationary to the shadowee and efficiently capture the shadowee without expending excessive energy. 

Lyapunov's direct method guarantees convergence of the two robots to a neighborhood of a pre-defined target. This control scheme is validated through computer simulations, demonstrating the effectiveness of our control inputs and the Lyapunov-based control approach.

Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks (IWSNs) have emerged as flexible and cost-efficient alternatives to traditional wired networks in various monitoring and control applications within the industrial domain. One of the key features of IWSNs is their low delay, which is crucial for many delay-sensitive applications where data is only valid for a short interval of time. However, delays can lead to performance drops or system outages, resulting in significant economic losses. 

To address this issue, we propose a decentralized optimization algorithm to minimize the end-to-end (E2E) delay of multi-hop IWSNs. The optimization problem is formulated by considering the objective function as the network delay, with the constraint being the stability criteria based on the total arrival rate and the total service rate. This objective function is shown to be strictly convex for the entire network. 

Next, we propose a Decentralized Primal-Dual (DeP-D) algorithm based on the sub-gradient method to solve the formulated optimization problem. The performance of the proposed DeP-D algorithm is evaluated through simulations and compared with the popular WirelessHART network. The results show that the proposed DeP-D algorithm can achieve at least a 40% reduction in the average E2E delay. 

In conclusion, our proposed decentralized optimization algorithm shows promising results in minimizing the E2E delay of multi-hop IWSNs. This can lead to improved performance, reduced downtime, and ultimately, significant cost savings for industrial applications that rely on IWSNs.

Welcome to the inaugural "Tech Travel" column, a regular feature in upcoming editions of IEEE Potentials. As a PhD student in bioengineering, my primary affiliation is with Instituto Superior Técnico in Lisbon, Portugal. However, for the latter half of my four-year academic journey, I found myself in Boston, Massachusetts - a city that holds a deep passion for sports. This is evident in the way its inhabitants sport their favorite team's apparel with pride everywhere they go.

A proposed method for detecting extended texture objects on multi-channel images has been developed. This method utilizes a set of bit images for multi-digit digital image representation and approximates it through the use of three-dimensional Markov chains with two states. The method works by utilizing the transition probabilities and brightness characteristics averaged within a sliding window as textural features. To efficiently detect texture objects, the computation is performed using the bit planes of the most informative digits of the digital image. Texture object detection is accomplished through analysis of the texture feature histogram and pixel brightness. Simulations conducted on this method proved its effectiveness in detecting texture objects.

In engineering education, there is often a heavy focus on imparting content knowledge to students, with less attention paid to the technology and pedagogy used. However, our paper presents an innovative e-learning system that addresses this issue by enabling students to provide real-time feedback during lectures. By gaining a better understanding of students' needs, lecturers can more effectively adjust their teaching methods to promote effective learning.

Alongside exploring the relevance of our system in pedagogy, we also present a complete system prototype that contributes to technology, pedagogy, and content knowledge. By incorporating the latest technological advancements and best practices in teaching, our system promises to provide a holistic and comprehensive learning experience for engineering students.

This paper presents an investigation into the application of adaptive fuzzy tracking control for high-order nonlinear time-delay systems with full-state constraints and input saturation. The proposed approach eliminates the need for frequently used growth assumptions for unknown system nonlinearities by utilizing fuzzy approximation techniques. High-order barrier Lyapunov functions are employed to ensure that full-state constraints are not violated. In addition, the auxiliary subsystem and Nussbaum gain technique are used to analyze the effect of input saturation. Furthermore, the adverse effects of unknown time-delay are compensated for by the construction of appropriate Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals.

The feasibility conditions for the existence of proposed control are formulated as novel sufficient conditions. It is rigorously established that all the closed-loop signals are bounded in the semi-global sense, while error signals converge to small bounded compact sets. Full-state constraints and input saturation are not violated, and the arguments of unknown nonlinearities are constrained within a compact set, on which fuzzy approximation is valid. Finally, the theoretical results obtained are confirmed by two simulation examples.

Frequency-modulated differential chaos shift keying ultrawideband (FM-DCSK UWB) system has attracted more and more attention in recent years because of its low-complexity and low-power advantages. Nevertheless, its system performance is severely degraded in the presence of narrowband interference (NBI), which further limits its practical applications. In this paper, an enhanced energy-based detector (EED) is proposed for the FM-DCSK UWB system to tackle this problem. Compared with the conventional energy detector (ED), the proposed EED significantly enhances the anti-NBI capability while maintaining the low-power and low-complexity feature. As a further insight, the analytical bit-error-rate (BER) expression of the proposed EED-based FM-DCSK UWB system is derived over additive white Gaussian noise as well as IEEE 802.15.4a multipath fading channels. Moreover, simulation results are carried out to demonstrate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the merit of the proposed EED. It is illustrated that the proposed EED achieves better performance than the conventional ED in various transmission scenarios. Thanks to the above-mentioned advantages, the proposed EED-based FM-DCSK UWB system appears to be an excellent candidate for low-power and low-complexity tactile Internet-of-Things applications, e.g., wireless sensor networks and wireless body area networks.

Wireless sensor network is useful for human that attract more scientists although they are still limited and limited energy is a weakness of wireless sensor that make getting information is interrupted. To improve energy consumption in WSN, in this paper we show a routing algorithm combined of LEACH_C and Dijkstra algorithm. A mobile sink move from Base Station (BS) to the Cluster Head (CHs) to get data, the direction of mobile sink is decided by Dijkstra algorithm. An efficient is saving energy and expand alive time of the sensor network.

This study aims to identify the effectiveness of entrepreneurship training programs on forming an entrepreneurial attitude and spirit in university students. Descriptive qualitative research will be used as research method. Data collection is done through semi-structured interviews. Characteristics of entrepreneurship training programs are generally viewed from four dimensions, namely training design, presentation methods, content and curriculum, and services provided after training. Entrepreneurship training programs have a positive impact on forming an entrepreneurial attitude in the form of mindset, ability and entrepreneurial status. Entrepreneurship training programs also play a role in shaping the intentions of entrepreneurship in the form of desire among the participants of the training program to start and grow the business and see other visible business opportunities.

In medieval Arabic, no symbols are used to express mathematical problems and solutions. Instead, specific Arabic terms are used to describe mathematical processes. Nevertheless, a close examination of the text styles and how information is encoded into natural language phrases reveals that the notations contain no ambiguity, which makes it possible to formulate the problem and solve it. In this paper, we explore the idea of automatically generating modern symbolic mathematical equations from natural language medieval Arabic Algebra texts. We will describe a simple machine translation system using Rule-based Machine Translation (MT) with Dictionary Approach in order to translate medieval verbal equation to a modern equation. We construct a new dataset from scratch to facilitate our study, as there is no previously published similar dataset. Our system was able to achieve correct translation results for cubic equations with 100% accuracy, and quartic, quintic equations with 96.66% and 94.01%, respectively.

Decentralized algorithms for multi-agent networks have garnered substantial research interest, with stochastic gradient descent and its variations being popularly used for developing such algorithms. In this paper, we explore a stochastic gradient descent algorithm that randomly selects each node to carry out the update. We overcome the strenuous computational and communication requirements of the synchronous framework by proposing an asynchronous variant that allows updates to be carried out using delayed gradients.

To assess the performance of our algorithm, we develop non-asymptotic optimality bounds as a function of the number of iterations and for various diminishing step-size rules. These bounds reveal that the effect of asynchrony on the algorithm convergence rate is minimal. To illustrate our theoretical findings, we solve a distributed estimation problem over a large network.

In conclusion, we provide a performance comparison of our proposed algorithm against the classical cyclic incremental algorithm. Our work demonstrates how asynchronous variants of stochastic gradient descent are effective in overcoming the limitations of synchronous frameworks and achieving optimal convergence rates in multi-agent networks.

Industrial communication systems represent one of the most important innovations of the last decades in the context of factory and process automation systems. They are networks specifically designed to cope with the tight requirements of these challenging application fields such as real time, determinism, and reliability. Moreover, industrial networks are often deployed in environments characterized by strong electromagnetic interference, mechanical stress, critical temperature, and humidity. Over the last three decades, different classes of industrial networks have been developed according to changing requirements and available communication and information technologies. In this paper, we first provide an account of the state of the art, reviewing classical fieldbuses, real-time Ethernet networks, and industrial wireless networks, along with their most relevant features, applications, and performance figures. We introduce the complex standardization framework and analyze the market status and assumptions for future development. In the second part, we address the future perspectives focusing on new technologies, standards, and fields of application. In particular, we consider the time-sensitive networking (TSN) family of standards, Industrial Internet-of-Things (IIoT) systems, high-performance wireless LANs, industrial applications of cellular networks, and Ethernet networks for automotive communication.

In LTE/LTE-A networks, femtocells are used to improve service coverage in indoor environments. Cognitive radio allows femtocell users to share the available spectrum with primary macrocell users. However, some issues arise because of the coexistence between femtocells and macrocells. These issues include but not limited to mitigating interference and fair distribution of network resources. In this paper, we use NSGA II to solve a multi-objective optimization problem that maximizes resource utilization while minimizing interference and guaranteeing fairness among users in a femtocell LTE/LTE-A network. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme improves the multi-objective function score by 8% and enhances the overall performance of the network.

In an intelligent parking lot, the robot must accurately position the vehicle's wheels during automatic parking. However, conventional image processing algorithms are unsuitable for this application due to their sensitivity to environmental noise. To overcome this challenge, researchers have developed a new method that employs Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for robust and optimal performance. Specifically, this paper proposes a technique for positioning vehicle wheels from point cloud data using an RNN model. The experimental results demonstrate that the bidirectional RNN offers significantly higher prediction accuracy than the unidirectional RNN. Furthermore, it was found that both BiLSTM and BiGRU approaches deliver comparably effective results in a small-scale training set, but BiGRU offers faster training speeds and can thus be applied in wheel detection systems.

The article presents the results of the study of open educational resources in mathematical disciplines. The purpose of the article is to summarize the experience of teaching mathematical courses based on quantitative analysis of the corresponding open educational resources and determination of ways of using such resources in the conditions of Ukrainian universities. The definition of open educational resources and their specific features are specified, in particular, support of different formats for presentation of materials, their publication under conditions of an open license, provision of free access, the possibility of modification of materials by other users. The analysis of the number of open educational resources Coursera, Edx, Udemy, and INTUIT has revealed that the bulk of mathematical courses in relation to others is not large, which suggests a reduction in young people's interest in purely mathematical disciplines. At the same time, it was noted that the presence of such resources on the site of the university contributes to the formation of its positive image within the country and the world. The own experience of studying mathematical online courses on Analytical Geometry, Linear Algebra, Geometry and Mathematical Philosophy is described.

In this paper, a novel adaptive fuzzy tracking control strategy is developed for nonlinear time-varying delayed systems with full state constraints. State constraints and time delays are normally found in various real-life plants, which are two important factors for degrading system performance significantly. In the framework of adaptive control, the effects of state constraints and time-varying delays are removed simultaneously. The integral Barrier Lyapunov functionals (IBLFs) are applied to achieve full-state-constraint satisfactions and remove the need of the transformed error constraints in previous BLFs. The unknown time-varying delays are completely compensated by introducing the separation technique and Lyapunov–Krasovskii functionals (LKFs). The unknown functions existing in systems are approximated by employing fuzzy logic systems (FLSs). With the help of less-adjustable parameters, only one parameter is needed to be adjusted online in each step of control design. The novel strategy can guarantee that a satisfactory tracking performance is achieved and the signals existing in the closed-loop system are bounded. Finally, by presenting simulation results, the efficiency of the proposed approach is revealed.

Cyber-physical systems (CPS) are smart systems that include engineered, interacting networks of physical and cyber components. CPS are concerned with the collaborative and interactive activities between cyber and physical components through sensing and actuation. The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 1451, a family of smart transducer interface standards, defines a set of open, common, network- independent communication interfaces for smart transducers (sensors or actuators) to achieve sensor data interoperability between cyber and physical components of CPS. The IEEE 1516 high-level architecture (HLA) is a standard for the modeling and simulation of distributed, heterogeneous processes. CPS experimentation often requires the integration of different domain-specific simulation tools into a common platform using a method called co-simulation. In order to facilitate a wide range of CPS simulations and experiments, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has developed a universal CPS environment for federation (UCEF), which is a toolset for designing and implementing federated, collaborative, and interactive experiments for CPS using HLA.This paper introduces an IEEE 1451 smart sensor digital twin federation, which has been developed using UCEF. The digital twin is a digital simulator or digital replica of a real IEEE 1451 smart sensor. The digital twin emulates both desired, non-linear behaviors and failure modes to simulate a real sensor in the field. This federation consists of three federates: an IEEE 1451 smart sensor digital twin federate (DTF), an IEEE 1451 digital twin tester federate (DTTF), and a federation experiment manager. In this federation, the DTTF can communicate with the DTF via HLA interactions that represent IEEE P1451.1 request and response messages. One federated experiment using three instances of IEEE 1451 digital twins is described in detail and the experimental results are provided in this paper. This federation provides a foundation for CPS research and experiments in the NIST CPS testbed.

In this work, we explore techniques for analyzing and enhancing the performance of joint radar-communication waveform design with low probability of intercept (LPI) characteristics. The approach we adopt involves encoding data onto the scale parameter of a Weibull distribution, while the shape parameter is only known to authorized receivers. We subsequently generate random sequences from the distribution, which we use as amplitude weights for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) sub-carriers. 

Considering a scenario where an unauthorized interceptor aims to reconstruct the data by performing a maximum likelihood estimation of both distribution parameters, we demonstrate the limited effectiveness of this operation in the presence of additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). In particular, we show that the likelihood function of the distribution becomes less sensitive to the shape of the distribution as the noise level increases. 

Furthermore, we analyze a Monte Carlo-based method for improving two radar characteristics of the radar-com signals generated using our approach. Finally, we propose and evaluate a method of penalizing the interceptor by varying the shape parameter of the Weibull distribution over time. 

In summary, this study contributes to the development of approaches to designing waveforms with robust LPI characteristics, which could prove valuable in various military and civilian applications.

Sentiment analysis is a growing field of social analytics that involves analyzing the feelings, emotions, likes, dislikes, and opinions of users on the web. This can be done through textual data, as well as images and videos that are shared or uploaded through social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook.

Although much research has been done on sentiment analysis of textual data, there has been limited focus on analyzing the sentiment of image data. However, the concept of Adjective Noun Pairs (ANPs) has been discovered as a useful tool for detecting the emotions or sentiments conveyed by web images.

The challenge with image sentiment analysis is predicting or identifying the sentiments of unlabelled images. Deep learning techniques have been used to overcome this challenge, as deep learning models are effective at learning image behavior or polarity. Neural Network (NN) models have performed well in areas such as image recognition, image prediction, image sentiment analysis, and image classification.

Some of the noteworthy models of deep learning in image sentiment analysis include Deep Neural Network (DNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Region-based CNN (R-CNN), and Fast R-CNN. Each of these models has strengths and limitations in different applications.

Overall, image sentiment analysis is a rising field that presents challenges and opportunities for future research. Deep learning techniques have shown promise in this area and are likely to play a significant role in the development of new models and approaches for image sentiment analysis.

Intelligent systems offer numerous benefits in various aspects of human life, and sentiment analysis (SA) is one of them. SA is a mathematical approach that enables machines to analyze the opinion polarity of statements or documents, and it is commonly used to observe public opinion on an issue. SA is extensively used in e-commerce to analyze the trend of customer statements regarding a product based on their reviews. By utilizing SA, e-commerce business owners can gauge the level of acceptance towards their products. 

In this study, we evaluated the effectiveness of the artificial neural network (ANN) algorithm in conducting SA of electronic product reviews. The ANN was designed with one input layer, one hidden layer consisting of 10 neurons, and one output layer consisting of two neurons. Our experimental results indicated that the ANN had a reasonably high accuracy and precision while conducting SA towards electronic product reviews, achieving 70.80% and 71.07% respectively.

Therefore, the ANN algorithm is highly feasible for application in intelligent systems tasked with assisting e-commerce business owners in conducting SA of customer feedback.

We propose a new approach for quadrilateral surface remeshing that can be applied to the method of moments (MoM). The motivation for high-quality quadrilateral meshes is to achieve accurate and efficient integration and singularity extraction. In this study, we present results for simple surfaces that demonstrate the effectiveness of our method compared to a commonly used quadrilateral remeshing algorithm. 

Our approach is based on a higher-order quadrilateral mesh, which enables us to achieve a higher accuracy than traditional linear meshes. This is particularly useful for MoM, as it requires an accurate representation of the underlying geometry to ensure accurate results. In our approach, we start by generating a coarse mesh and then apply a local refinement scheme to improve the quality of the mesh. 

To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, we compared it to the quadtree algorithm, which is a commonly used quadrilateral remeshing algorithm. We tested both methods on a simple surface and found that our approach produced a higher quality mesh with fewer singularities, resulting in more accurate integration results. 

In conclusion, our higher order quadrilateral surface remeshing approach is a promising method for MoM applications, as it enables accurate and efficient integration and singularity extraction. The results of our study demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and its potential to be applied to more complex surfaces.

We summarize of significant functions of the systems from previous works which are considered as automatic plant watering systems. As an example of an enhancement of the existing automatic plant watering systems, we design and implement a prototype of our proposed system based on these functions. Then we provide some discussions of the proposed system and its results. The system can demonstrate the enhancement of automatic plant watering systems and how the Internet of Things and cloud computing can benefit automatic plant watering systems. Thus the enhanced system can be useful in agricultural applications with plain design and implementation. The enhanced system can be guidelines for individuals who want to build their own automatic plant watering systems to grow plants, especially for food by themselves.

The design and optimization process for enhancement in the performance of MEMS Unimorph Piezoelectric energy harvester based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Grey Wolf optimization (GWO) is studied. The analytical equations of Unimorph Piezoelectric Energy harvester have been derived, to determine the amount of voltage and power harvested from the piezoelectric cantilever. These analytical equations are used as the fitness function of GA and GWO. Both of the algorithms are a design optimization technique for optimization problems to enhance power and output voltage, harvested from the unimorph piezoelectric energy harvester. This is achieved by using GA and GWO, to optimize the parameters of the piezoelectric cantilever, in which the fitness function, is taken as the power and voltage derived by analytical equations, and the techniques are compared with each other. Furthermore, the effects of mechanical and electrical properties (natural frequency, stress, load impedance and harvester efficiency) are analyzed. Finally, with the results obtained, un-optimized results are compared with the optimized results (GA and GWO) and the optimized results are proved to be efficient in all aspects, which have significantly improved the efficiency of the piezoelectric energy harvester from 24.9% to 58.9%. Finally, a comparison is made within the optimization techniques and GWO has proved to be more efficient than GA and this performance of MEMS piezoelectric energy harvester is simulated using the MATLAB software.

For an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM), parameters mismatching would affect the performance and reduce the output efficiency.In this paper, a variable parameter Maximum Torque Per Ampere(MTP A)control method based on online parameters identification was proposed. Firstly, an adaptive linear neural network algorithm is used to identify the motor parameters, and then the MTPA control is modified by combining the identified parameters. The results show that the proposed strategy has a nice adaptation to parameters mismatching, along with an improved output efficiency which is beneficial to magnetic recording motor.

A novel methodology for designing thinned arrays with controlled pattern features is presented. The optimization of the binary weighting coefficients of the array elements is carried out through a multi-step procedure. In a first stage, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to determine the binary sequence whose autocorrelation function is closest to a target one. Then, the thinned array is constructed from one of its cyclic sequences which optimizes a given figure of merit. A preliminary numerical example is illustrated in order to show the potentialities of the proposed approach.

A novel method for long-term forecasting of wind speed distribution has been developed using a neural network trained through a phase space reconstruction method. The approach tracks the evolution of the wind speed distribution function parameters in a dynamic system and applies neural network training and forecasting features to learn the nonlinear model between historical data and next observation. Prior to implementing the proposed approach, different estimators were applied and compared to fit the annual distribution of wind speeds at the targeted sites. Overall, the proposed method exhibits excellent performance and holds promising potential in enhancing wind energy yield.

This letter proposes a pioneering method for detecting pilot spoofing attacks using an auxiliary node as a trusted user. The auxiliary node participates in the uplink training process and assists in detecting pilot spoofing in multiple-input single-output systems. A three-phase uplink training method is designed that ensures a malicious user can be reliably detected. Unlike existing methods, which involve two-stage uplink–downlink training, our method relies solely on the uplink training stage. Additionally, our approach detects spoofing attacks without altering pilot signals, which is beyond the capacity of existing methods. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach substantially improves the detection probability.

This article studies the consensus problem for a class of general second-order multi-agent systems with communication delay. The Lyapounov-Krasovskii functional with integral terms is constructed. Based on the Lyapounov-Krasovskii functional, the sufficient exponential consensus conditions for a class of general second-order multi-agent systems with communication delay are obtained. The effectiveness of the derived consensus conditions is illustrated by numerical example.

Today, the Internet of Things (IoT) is used for convenience in everyday life in many areas. Owing to the fact that the data collected from the IoT are generated in large quantities, cloud computing is inevitably used to store and analyze the data. However, cloud storage is not owned by the user, so it is unreliable. Verifying the integrity of data collected in an IoT environment and stored in a cloud has two problems: a large amount of data needs to be verified, and the data verification should be done directly on the IoT device. Many methods for data integrity verification use trusted third parties and devices that provide sufficient resources. However, it is difficult to directly apply existing research to the IoT devices that have limited resources. This paper proposes a secure cloud storage service for an IoT environment that is based on a provable data possession model and uses Bloom filters. The experimental results showed that the proposed method saves time and has no significant differences in the verification rate with existing methods, even though the Bloom filter causes false positives. Therefore, the proposed service can effectively process a large amount of data generated in an IoT environment.

The problem of removing unwanted reflections from a single image is considered ill-posed because it is difficult to define an exact physical model for it. Previous approaches have used multiple images or manually created features, but these methods are limited in terms of generality and realism. In this study, we propose a conditional Generative Adversarial Networks based deep neural network structure that can generate realistic images and solve the problem using a simple objective function. We use gradient information to maintain both low and high frequency details in our formulation. This approach does not require any physical prior knowledge and works well on single images. Our experimental results show that our algorithm performs favorably compared to existing methods from a human perceptual perspective.

Aircraft are becoming increasingly connected to other systems and networks, which introduces attack vectors and poses a threat to their operational effectiveness.
