The fuzzy logic is used because it has the potential to deal effectively with high nonlinear systems and imprecise data. The use of a type of Controller makes the system modular and increases its adaptability. It presents the design and implementation of a 6 degrees of freedom control system for a quadrocopter. Further, the work can be focused upon the detailed study of each motion and the real world communication of the quad rotor with the environment.

The identification of persons through earprint and voice print is one of the basic biometric matters. The context of use is situated in smart homes. The main issue is the lack of databases containing voice records and ear images from the same persons collected with a smart phone. In this paper, we propose a new database for the persons identification through ear and voice print in degraded conditions. The database contains 111 subjects with more than 12 samples for each one. The new database is collected in degraded conditions, the ear images have different occlusion as scarf, hair, glasses, earrings while the voice records are collected with different types of noise in the background as music, cars, street, conversation. Interested researchers could contact the author to acquire the database.

Ultrasound (US) beam can be focused at multiple locations to increase the lateral resolution of the resulting images. However, this improvement in resolution comes at the expense of a loss in frame rate, which is essential in many applications such as imaging moving anatomy. Herein, we propose a novel method based on Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) for achieving multi-focus line-per-line US image without a reduction in the frame rate. Results on simulated phantoms as well as real phantom experiments show that the proposed deep learning framework is able to substantially improve the resolution without sacrificing the frame rate.

The paper presents a soft computing based neural network model for analyzing the parameters of an ellipsoidal fractal microstrip antenna (EFM Antenna) for wide band applications. The radiating patch is designed using the Sierpinski Gasket fractal concept with the second degree of iterations. Design parameters such as minor and major axis of ellipse, height of substrate, number of iterations, resonant frequencies, and bandwidth are collected to predict efficient values for designing the proposed antenna. An artificial neural network model using multilayer perceptron algorithm is trained, tested and validated with 75 data sets and 25 sets respectively. The soft computing model is found to be in close agreement with simulated results. Moreover, the minor and major axis of ellipse for the second iteration of fractals indicate the wide band and multiband operation of the antenna in Ku (12-18 GHz) and K (18-27 GHz) band applications.

India is a country in which agriculture plays a wide role with around 70% of its population is dependent on agriculture good in direct or indirect way. The agricultural sector contributes about 14% to GDP of India. As the population is increasing, demand for crops is also increasing day by day. About all suicides in India farmer suicide accounts for 11.2%. There are many reasons given for farmer suicides like inadequate monsoon rainfall, interest rate is high, certain government policies are not in welfare, mental health issues, personal and family problems. It is also noticed that even the states are responsible for manipulating certain statistics. this research work uses data mining clustering technique to group attributes that results in low crop production. Case studies are conducted to map and co-relate the low crop production, monsoon factors along with farmer suicidal data. The states are affected most is identified and further analysed.

In the current age of computation, quantum computing has emerged as a potential solution for solving complex problems faster than classical methods. However, there are various challenges associated with implementing quantum circuits, and one such limitation is the nearest neighbor criterion. This criterion dictates that qubits that interact with each other must be placed in adjacent positions. In this study, we introduce a linear qubit placement technique that rearranges the position of qubits and enhances the nearest neighbor-based design by inserting SWAPs.

To accurately insert these SWAP gates, we incorporate a look-ahead strategy that evaluates the impact of the other gates and determines the appropriate position for the SWAPs. We test our methodology on a wide range of benchmarks and compare the results to existing works. Our findings demonstrate that our proposed technique outperforms the previous approaches and leads to significant reductions in SWAP overhead.

Overall, by introducing the linear qubit placement technique and utilizing the look-ahead strategy, we can overcome one of the biggest challenges of quantum circuit implementation and improve the efficiency of quantum computing.

The field of gait analysis has seen recent advancements in techniques for identifying individuals based on their unique gait patterns. In Japan, an appearance-based method utilizing Gait Energy Images (GEIs) has been successfully utilized for forensic purposes, assuming the ideal conditions of an identical view angle, clothing, resolution, frame rate, and stable walking. However, when these conditions are not met, identification accuracy is compromised, rendering analysis impossible.

To address these limitations, we propose a novel human identification method that combines the strengths of both appearance-based and model-based methods to compare dynamic features. We semi-automatically extract feature points and local shape features from silhouette sequences and calculate the matching probability of two footages by comparing the dynamics of these extracted features.

Our results indicate that the GEI-based method is better suited for frontal views, low resolution, and multi-view angle comparisons, whereas our proposed method excels in identifying individuals in lateral views, low frame-rate conditions, and when clothing variation is a factor. Therefore, while the GEI-based method characterizes "figure" information, our proposed method is superior for characterizing "dynamic" information of human gait.

In conclusion, our proposed method represents an important development in gait analysis, providing a more versatile approach for identifying individuals regardless of challenging conditions.

This paper describes a context/model-based tour planning service that combines previous tourist activity with a recommender system for generating personalized attraction recommendations. The system utilizes the SCoR collaborative filtering algorithm to calculate synthetic coordinates between users in order to provide tailored suggestions. Unlike traditional collaborative filtering algorithms, SCoR is model-based and can easily incorporate new training information without the need for a full retraining process. The developed prototype is optimized for Android smartphones and has been tested for St. Petersburg city. The attraction database includes information on location, description, media, and ratings, leveraging OpenStreeMaps, Wikipedia, and Google Place.

In this article, we introduce a concurrent parameter estimation method that is designed for multiple periodic signals. The method presented here is intended for use with Doppler sensors and is straightforward yet highly effective. Through extensive computer simulations, we demonstrate the impressive performance of this technique.

The main advantage of our approach is that it allows for the simultaneous estimation of several important parameters, including the number of targets, their periods, directions, and fundamental waveforms. This offers significant advantages over traditional methods, which often require multiple techniques to estimate different parameters.

Furthermore, our simulations demonstrate that our method is highly effective in situations where the number of targets exceeds the degree of freedom of receiver antennas. This is a significant advantage, as it enables us to accurately estimate parameters in more complex scenarios.

Another key benefit of our method is that it is highly robust against coherence among incoming signals. This means that our technique is highly effective even in situations where there is a complex overlap of signals.

Overall, our proposed concurrent parameter estimation method offers significant advantages over traditional methods and is highly effective in a range of different applications.

This paper proposes a new system for controlling secondary voltage and frequency in islanded AC microgrids. The controller has several notable features, including the ability to track frequency and voltage magnitude references in a finite time and insensitivity to changes in the communication network and plug-and-play operations. Furthermore, the controller is effective regardless of the nature of the distributed generators and loads. The distributed nature of the controller eliminates the need for a complex communication network required for traditional centralized control systems and increases the microgrid's reliability by removing the dependence on a single centralized controller. The paper also presents a new distributed sliding-mode technique for designing the proposed control system. Finally, a case study demonstrates the robustness of the distributed controller in terms of voltage and frequency reference tracking, communication network changes, and plug-and-play operations.

We present a computation framework that enables collaborative inference of a distributed deep learning model across devices in a computing hierarchy. Specifically, in the context of IoT applications, this hierarchy comprises end devices, gateways, and server(s), and inference can be executed adaptively across one or multiple tiers. Unlike previous work, our proposed framework allows trained models to run on the distributed system, thereby enabling co-design of the model and the system. We highlight the importance of measuring not only model accuracy, but also the delivered performance of the model on the actual systems, as different computing platforms can impact the inference time of end devices. This measured performance can inform the design of the model and system in subsequent design cycles. We illustrate the framework by building a surveillance system for detecting objects as a case study. Through experimentation in a two-tier computing hierarchy, we validate the advantages of adaptive inference computation, assess system capacity under given workloads, and examine the effect of model parameter settings on system capacity. We argue that the ability to evaluate performance expedites the design of distributed deep learning models and systems.

Assessing memory in daily life can be extremely beneficial in detecting and monitoring symptoms of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's. In order to address one such symptom, disorientation, which can lead to domestic accidents, researchers have turned to the Internet of Things (IoT). The use of IoT allows for the collection of big data in real-time by processing information both on the edge and in the cloud, with the aim of avoiding communication overload.

To set up such a system, prototypes must be created and sensors must be chosen and implemented. However, a cost-effective alternative is to use realistic 3D simulations of scenarios in order to evaluate different algorithms for assessing memory. By tracking a person's movement within a simulated house and evaluating their level of disorientation, the algorithms can be evaluated and compared.

The contribution of this paper is a case study that allows researchers to design scenarios that include the daily activities of individuals, the types of sensors to be deployed, and the disorientation detection algorithms. This method provides a valuable way to assess memory in daily life and has the potential to aid in early detection and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases.

Conventional fault models define their faulty behavior at the IO ports of standard cells with simple rules of fault activation and fault propagation. However, there still exist some defects inside a cell (intra-cell) or between two cells (dual-cell) that cannot be effectively detected by the test patterns of conventional fault models and hence become a source of DPPM. In order to further increase the defect coverage, many research works have been conducted to study the fault models resulting from different types of intra-cell and dual-cell defects, by SPICE-simulating each targeted defect with its equivalent circuit-level defect model. However, it was considered computationally infeasible to simulate every possible defective scenario for a cell library and obtain a complete set of cell-level fault models. In this paper, we present a new dual-cell-aware (DCA) framework based on examining the layout of two adjacent cells (i.e., a dual cell) to identify potential defects, where time-consuming RC extraction can be avoided and the runtime for SPICE simulation can be reduced. Experimental results and silicon data on a SoC product show that the proposed DCA framework can not only save runtime significantly but also maintain the promising efficacy of DCA tests for the objective of lowering DPPM.

A novel method for word-dependent speaker recognition is proposed in this paper. The method utilizes unique temporal statistical techniques on Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) coefficients for recognizing the speaker based on specific words from a dataset. To demonstrate the proposed algorithm, digits ranging from zero to nine are used in the dataset of words.

Wavelet analysis is considered due to DWT's ability to analyze time-frequency multi-resolution for quasi-stationary speech signals. The speech signal of a word from the dataset is decomposed using Symlet 7 wavelet as the mother wavelet, and a 1D feature vector is extracted from the approximate coefficients of DWT. Temporal-statistical methods are used to construct unique features for each word in the dataset.

Compared to methods like LPC, LPCC, MFCC, and Power Spectral Analysis (FFT), the proposed method gives a better-robust feature for speaker recognition. The article also presents the details of the methodology followed by the results obtained and discussion.

Overall, the proposed word-dependent speaker recognition method that utilizes DWT coefficients with unique temporal statistical techniques shows improved robustness compared to existing methods.

This demonstration showcase a minimalist hand gesture recognition technology using single Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). With the state of the art recognition architecture (DRONA) running at the backend, the system is capable of learning more than 50 hand gestures in real time with very low misclassification error.

Recognizing different WaDang patterns is crucial for the digital protection of cultural relics. However, this recognition process is challenging due to various factors, such as different background patterns, rotations, and scales. To address this, we have developed an algorithm that combines hand-crafted and deep features using multiple instance learning. This method divides the features of instances into two parts and computes their similarity through multiple kernel learning. Our experiments on WaDang images, as well as MUSK and COREL datasets, have shown that this algorithm is effective and performs comparably to other state-of-the-art algorithms.

Early detection of a patient's disease can be a critical factor in saving their life. The disease status of a patient is considered Protected Health Information (PHI), and identifying it manually in structured datasets can be too expensive, time-consuming, and error-prone. To overcome this drawback, it is necessary to implement automated identification systems for PHI such as disease status. In this study, we present a novel approach based on deep neural models for automatic identification of disease status from free text clinical records. We evaluated the proposed models on two datasets from i2b2 Challenge tasks and found promising results, demonstrating the potential benefits of our scheme.

Banded linear systems arise in many communication scenarios, e.g., those involving inter-carrier interference and inter-symbol interference. Motivated by recent advances in deep learning, we propose to design a high-accuracy low-complexity signal detector for banded linear systems based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We develop a novel CNN-based detector by utilizing the banded structure of the channel matrix. Specifically, the proposed CNN-based detector consists of three modules: the input preprocessing module; the CNN module; and the output postprocessing module. With such an architecture, the proposed CNN-based detector is adaptive to different system sizes, and can overcome the curse of dimensionality, which is a ubiquitous challenge in deep learning. Through extensive numerical experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed CNN-based detector outperforms conventional deep neural networks and existing model-based detectors in both accuracy and computational time. Moreover, we show that the CNN is flexible for systems with large sizes or wide bands. We also show that the proposed CNN-based detector can be easily extended to near-banded systems such as doubly selective orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems and 2-D magnetic recording (TDMR) systems, in which the channel matrices do not have a strictly banded structure.

Breastfeeding is one of the best interventions that can bring down child mortality considerably. It could prevent nearly half of all diarrhea episodes and one-third of respiratory infections. It could also improve the IQ of child. Despite of such enormous benefits, compliance to breastfeeding is abysmally low in not only developing countries but also developed countries. There are many misconceptions about breastfeeding that prevent mothers from complying with optimal breastfeeding practices. These misconceptions arise out of incomplete information or outdated traditional practices. To address these concerns, collaborative work was undertaken by MBPC, BPNI Maharashtra, Department of Community Medicine-Seth G.S. Medical College & KEM Hospital (Mumbai) and TATA Consultancy Services (TCS).These collaborative efforts have resulted in development of “ShishuPoshan”, mobile based application for the mothers. This application addresses almost all the queries that a lactating mother may have in a simple yet lucid and comprehensive way. In this case-study paper we will discuss about our learnings, experiences, journey in developing the ShishuPoshan application and various other aspects like the collaborative effort, the best practices followed, the lessons learnt, application beneficiaries, its impact and the way forward. We feel that these learnings would be useful for anybody wanting to develop application in healthcare domain for masses and achieve a scaled impact on needy people.

The purpose of the investigation presented in this paper is to obtain the optimal restructure of radial distribution system under the impact of contingencies, with and without the scope of distributed generation. Firstly, solution to occurrence of contingency is proposed by finding out the best switching sequence of a specified number of tie lines and sectionalizes with an objective to improve the continuity of power flow in radial system. Secondly genetic algorithm (GA) has been used to find the optimal location and size of embedded distribution generation (DG), to improve voltage profile and to reduce losses for given load demand. The outcome of the proposed study is illustrated through simulations of loaded 69-bus radial distribution system. The obtained results suggest that the investment is distribution generation is attractive when reconfiguration is used to minimize load curtailment.

Geospatial information has become increasingly complex and vast in scale, requiring innovative and intuitive visualization tools to uncover valuable insights. In contrast to traditional methods of visual analysis, modern geospatial visualization technologies are capable of handling vast amounts of complex data. This paper takes a closer look at the technologies and applications of geospatial information visualization. Additionally, it explores some of the challenges inherent to geospatial visualization, and offers insights into future directions for the field.

The synthesis of frequency-scanned monopulse radiation patterns using an array of two leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) is demonstrated. The LWA array must be designed with appropriate shifted frequency-dispersion responses to fulfill the desired monopulse-scanning specification over the required bandwidth and number of channels. This is demonstrated using two manufactured LWAs in half-width microstrip technology, designed to scan in the band from 2.39 to 2.65 GHz covering a field of view (FoV) from -80° to +80° and using three frequency channels. Also, this paper addresses the procedure to estimate the direction of arrival (DoA) of an incoming beacon RF signal composed by prescribed tones distributed in the scanning band. This type of multicarrier beacon signals can be produced in wireless systems which allow for frequency-hopping operation. It is demonstrated that the proposed monopulse DoA-estimation technique combines good angular resolution and wide FoV using a simple passive antenna structure.

Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is a statistical approach to topic modeling that has been widely used in software engineering. However, a major challenge with LDA is that its probabilistic distributions for topics and documents are difficult to comprehend. To address this issue, we introduce VisioTM, a platform that utilizes visualizations to represent software systems based on LDA. VisioTM provides several visualizations for words, topics, and documents, making it easier for users to understand the basic elements of LDA. This paper discusses the key features and functions of VisioTM, which is a language-independent tool for visualizing software systems.

Advancement in trends provokes new ideas in our mind. We often desire intelligent robots that can solve our daily routine tasks. This paper successfully outlines the ways and methodologies that can be used to develop a robot that can monitor the growth of plants in the absence of human beings. As humans need proper food and nutrients to keep us energetic and working, similarly plants require proper nutrients in order live longer. The proposed method consists of a mobile robot integrated with a novel algorithm (implementing the concepts of Computer Vision) to segment out the plants from the image in the best possible way. This algorithm is much more robust to lightning conditions as compared to other available algorithms. The application of this research might not only improve the conditions of plants and trees but can also result in the overall improvement of our surroundings and atmosphere.

Brain signals were started to use in deception detection process from last few years. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals can reveal many important features of our thought which make it as a better tool for deception detection. A number of experiments were done in terms of visual stimuli based EEG signals. The purpose of this paper is to improvise the existing methods in the classification of familiar and unfamiliar faces which can be used as a basic model in deception detection. In this paper, we proposed a deep learning based classification of EEG signals for the given visual stimuli. In this experiment, the subjects were shown by familiar and unfamiliar faces. After processing using Independent Component Analysis (ICA), the signal was fed to an autoencoder for classification. By training the model properly we got a mean accuracy of 82.21% which is far better than the models using conventional machine learning methods. Our model achieved the state of the art results for classification of familiar and unfamiliar EEG signals.

This paper investigates the convergence and divergence on the acquisition of English vowels from a typological perspective. The focus is on the acoustic features of monophthongs produced by non-Mandarin learners from TJ and ZB dialectal areas. Comparing the vowels produced by learners and AM English speakers, the research explores the degree of phonetic transfer of dialects and Mandarin to English. Target samples of ten monophthongs and three similar vowels (i, u, and a) are selected. Results indicate that for ZB learners, i and a are more affected by Mandarin, u is more similar to dialect. For TJ learners, a and i are closer to dialect, u is more affected by Mandarin. The Speech Learning Model (SLM) is employed to explain the analysis results.

Dynamic zero-sum games have been extensively studied in the field of mathematical game theory, and this paper focuses on developing a sufficient condition for solving such games. Additionally, the paper provides insights into various reinforcement learning strategies that can be used to solve dynamic games with uncertainty, where the game matrices and transition probabilities between states are not known. 

One of the novel algorithms presented in the paper is the use of heterogeneous games of learning automata (HEGLA) in which automata play zero-sum games and identical pay-off games simultaneously. This algorithm is proposed as a possible approach to learning the solution Markov equilibrium policies when they are assumed to satisfy the sufficient conditions for existence. 

Other algorithms based on model-based and model-free reinforcement learning are also discussed in the paper. Simulation studies have been conducted to complement the theoretical and algorithmic discussions presented. 

Overall, this paper provides valuable insights and approaches to solving dynamic zero-sum games in the presence of uncertainty. The use of HEGLA, as well as other reinforcement learning strategies, is explored to address these complex decision-making problems.

ID card recognition is an application scenario in image recognition. As an important identity certificate for citizens, ID card identification and information management has also become a hot issue of concern. Chinese ID card images recognition mainly faces the following problems: Firstly, the shadow grid lines and the noise interference caused by the camera hardware conditions and illumination, together with the useful information in the picture, cause a huge problem of extracting useful information in the ID card. Secondly, the way to extract the foreground part in a complex context is also important for recognition. In response to these problems, this paper proposes an ID card region location method based on face detection and national emblem detection. This method can locate the foreground target area of the ID card in a complex context. In addition, the method of rotation correction of ID card region based on Hough transform is proposed, which can correct the tilt target within the range of tilt angle less than 45 degrees. In the text localization stage, the morphological method of the image is used to locate the text area. The deep convolutional neural network is then used to implement character segmentation and recognition. The recognition process proposed in this paper achieves a better recognition effect, and the recognition of Chinese and digital characters reaches 99.7% recognition rate, and can cope with the rotation tilt and the image containing the background.

Heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) and multi-access mobile edge computing (MA-MEC) are considered as the key technologies that support the development of smart cities. The widespread adoption of IoT is transforming our world into an Internet of Everything era, and the MA-MEC technology provides support to the resource-limited and computation-sensitive services and applications through computation offloading and distributed content delivery/caching. However, the deployment of cloud computing capability within the radio access network could pose serious security threats due to existing technologies and networks, as well as the MA-MEC-based IoT itself.

In this paper, we investigate security solutions from physical layer perspectives to address the possible security threats. Physical layer security technologies can achieve perfect secrecy, exhibit low-computational complexity, require minimal resource consumption, and possess adaptability to channel changes. Our research focuses on secure wiretap coding, resource allocation, signal processing, and multi-node cooperation. Additionally, physical layer key generation and authentication are also examined to combat emerging security challenges. In conclusion, we propose some future research directions to pave the way for further development in this area.

Mitotic detection and cell counting are key diagnostic factors in the detection and grading of cancers. This paper presents a method for automating the cell-mask generation process, which can be used for mitotic detection. The first stage of our approach involves using the Mask R-CNN network to classify cells with high recall and low precision whilst simultaneously generating masks for each cell. In the second stage, we utilize a combination of hand-crafted features and deep convolutional neural networks trained on ImageNet to classify cell candidates as either mitotic or non-mitotic. Our approach demonstrates improved performance over fully-supervised segmentation methods, as well as methods using a combination of hand-crafted and learned deep features. Notably, our method is able to transfer masks learned from the small ICPR 2012 dataset to the ICPR 2014 dataset, which does not provide cell mask annotations.

We propose a top-down approach for formation control of heterogeneous multiagent systems, based on the method of eigenstructure assignment. Given the problem of achieving scalable formations on the plane, our approach globally computes a state feedback control that assigns desired closed-loop eigenvalues/eigenvectors. We characterize the relation between the eigenvalues/eigenvectors and the resulting interagent communication topology, and design special (sparse) topologies such that the synthesized control may be implemented locally by the individual agents. Moreover, we present a hierarchical synthesis procedure that significantly improves computational efficiency. Finally, we extend the proposed approach to achieve fixed-size formation and circular motion, and illustrate these results by simulation examples.

In recent years, 3-D object retrieval has become a popular research topic, particularly in the area of view-based approaches due to their flexibility in data representation and impressive performance. However, one issue that remains is how to learn features that are both discriminative across classes and compactly distributed within each class. This paper proposes a new way to learn a view-pooling feature using a triplet network and introduces a new loss, the cube loss, which samples triplets equal to the cube of samples in a batch. With this new loss function, both hard-negative and hard-positive pairs can be effectively investigated. The experimental results on the ModelNet benchmark show that this method outperforms currently used approaches.

With the advancement of natural language processing techniques, robots are being built to interact in natural languages, in order to facilitate a more human like experience for its users. This study focuses on building a human-robot interaction system for a document delivering robotic assistant that is capable of following instructions and answering questions related to the domain of an office environment. The semantic analysis carried out in this closed domain intelligent system employs a hybrid approach comprised of both rule based and machine learning based techniques, while addressing the problem of limited domain related training data. Speech inputs obtained through speech recognition libraries are sent through several layers of classifiers in order to extract keywords that maps the input to the intended meaning of the user. Response templates backed by a knowledge base is used to generate the appropriate responses, which will then be converted into speech form. Apart from the rules utilized, machine learning based approaches SVM, KNN, Naïve Bayes and Decision Trees are evaluated in this research for the semantic analysis classifications. The results of this hybrid approach show a significant level of accuracy and provides a solution to the shortage of domain related training data that limits the ability to use neural network based techniques.

The work presented in this paper focuses on Quadrirotor UAV navigation control. Adynamic model of the Quadrirotor UAV is described followed by a control approach design based on conventional PID and PID optimized by Genetic Algorithm (GA) technique applied to the vertical position (z) control. Controller parameters optimization is based on a fitness function time weight square error (ITA). To approve our approach we have used different values of GA parameters in different simulations in matlab-simulink environment. The simulation obtained results illustrate the efficiency of our control design and open the perspectives for future works.

In this study, we explore the speed and accuracy of various neural network architectures, paired with alternate feature extractors, to improve object detection efficiency. Three architectures and three extractors were utilized to create various model combinations, and the resulting mean average precision (mAP) metric was used to evaluate accuracy. We used the COCO data-set to extract sample images, and implemented the work on the TensorFlow library. Through this process, we aimed to identify the fastest and most accurate architecture for object detection.

This paper proposes a novel gradient descent least squares regression (GDLSR)-based neural network (NN) structure for the control of grid-integrated solar photovoltaic (PV) system with improved power quality. Here, a single-layer neuron structure is used for the extraction of fundamental component (FC) from the load current. During FC extraction, GDLSR-based NN structure attenuates harmonic components, noise, dc offsets, bias, notches and distortions from the nonlinear current, which improves the power quality under normal as well as under abnormal grid conditions. This single-layer GDLSR-based NN structure has a very simple architecture, which decreases the computational burden and algorithm complexity. Therefore, it is easy in implementation. In this work, the GDLSR-based control technique is tested on a single-phase single-stage grid-integrated PV topology with the nonlinear loads. The prime objective of the GDLSR-based NN structure is to provide reactive power compensation, power factor correction, harmonics filtering and mitigation of other power quality issues. Moreover, when solar irradiation is zero, the dc-link capacitor and voltage-source converter act as a distribution static compensator, which enhances the utilization factor of the system. The proposed system is modeled, and its performances are verified experimentally on a developed prototype in different grid disturbances as well as solar insolation variation conditions, which performances have satisfied the motive of the proposed technique as well as the IEEE-519 standard.

This paper introduces a real-time application of a data-mining method aimed at conducting indirect contingency screening for power systems. The method involves the rapid identification of hazardous, recurring power-system operating conditions. This study employs the Slovenian power-system model for first-swing stability issues as a demonstration of the method, which is divided into several segments. 

The first segment involves the creation of a database that contains a set of pre-fault operating conditions characterized by a measurement matrix, and critical clearing times corresponding to several contingencies. The measurement matrix is subjected to principal component analysis, which decomposes it into dense clusters of points represented in a coordinate system defined by the principal components. Monitoring real-time steady-state conditions is facilitated through the identification of the shortest Euclidean distance metric in the coordinate system, which enables global screening.

Next, a second-stage (local) screening is applied to adaptively account for the fluctuating sensitivity of contingencies to variations in pre-fault operating conditions. This screening approach provides an accurate indication of each contingency impact rapidly as long as a similar operating state exists within the database. When a similar operating state is not available in the database, the case is thoroughly investigated and added to the database as a new entry. Therefore, this method is applicable to a wide spectrum of dynamic problems as long as problem-relevant sets of input data are available.

New On-Board systems using Big Data volume. For Big Data transmission it is useful WDM technology. Upon transition to new generation telecommunication networks it is important to have management and supervision for all network levels. It is very important to know future monitoring system characters. In this article we use imitation modeling for WDM parameters monitoring and IP over WDM signal transferring.

Neural network decoding algorithms are recently introduced by Nachmani et al. to decode high-density parity-check (HDPC) codes. In contrast with iterative decoding algorithms such as sum-product or min-sum algorithms in which the weight of each edge is set to 1, in the neural network decoding algorithms, the weight of every edge depends on its impact in the transmitted codeword. In this paper, we provide a novel feed-forward neural network lattice decoding algorithm suitable to decode lattices constructed based on Construction A, whose underlying codes have HDPC matrices. We first establish the concept of feed-forward neural network for HDPC codes and improve their decoding algorithms compared to Nachmani et al. We then apply our proposed decoder for a Construction A lattice with HDPC underlying code, for which the well-known iterative decoding algorithms show poor performances. The main advantage of our proposed algorithm is that instead of assigning and training weights for all edges, which turns out to be time-consuming especially for high-density parity-check matrices, we concentrate on edges which are present in most of 4-cycles and removing them gives a girth -6 Tanner graph. This approach, by slight modifications using updated LLRs instead of initial ones, simultaneously accelerates the training process and improves the error performance of our proposed decoding algorithm.

This paper presents the modeling and simulation of a spherical autonomous underwater vehicle. The robot was developed under the European Union H2020 innovation action UNEXMIN for the exploration of underground flooded mines, and is a small spherical robot with thrusters and an internal pendulum for pitch control. A model of the vehicle is presented, initially without the pendulum, then an extended formulation is derived accounting for a multibody dynamic description of the system. Experimental identification results for the determination of drag parameters are presented as well. A Modelica based simulator is developed for dynamic simulation of the vehicle, and is integrated with the Matlab/Simulink environment. The simulator is then validated based on preliminary experimental results.

The concept of the Internet of Things (IoT) is to establish widespread, cost-effective, and low data rate connectivity among people, machines, and objects. To make this vision possible, wireless communication technology is essential. However, incorporating this technology on a large scale may require certain considerations, such as battery-free and long-range communication.

To address this challenge, we have proposed a modulator utilizing Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) modulation that can backscatter various chirps. This approach provides high sensitivity for achieving long range communications. Moreover, our design demonstrates the ability to reflect backscatter Long Range (LoRa) preamble symbols with a Spreading Factor (SF) of 7 and 125 kHz bandwidth, enabling the reuse of the already developed LoRa receivers.

In conclusion, our proposal for a CSS modulator provides an optimal solution for embedding wireless communication technology on a large scale while ensuring long-range and battery-free communication.

this paper is presenting artificial neural network based pulse width modulation switching analysis for the three-phase dual two level inverters system with isolated two dc voltage sources. Some applications require power and torque variation, which takes time to improve the overall efficiency and reliability of the system. For such applications, an enhanced switching sequence analysis has presented. This scheme has improved quality of the output voltage and reduces THD in the line voltage. The performance analysis using ANN of this scheme has validated by simulation results.

Down syndrome (DS), the most common form of aneuploidy caused by the presence of part or all of a third copy of chromosome 21, is typically diagnosed through prenatal screening. However, traditional screening methods can be both socially and financially costly. To address these issues, we propose a noninvasive and accurate diagnosis procedure for DS through the use of machine learning. Although machine learning has received considerable attention in predictive analytics for medical problems, few applications have been reported for DS due to the difficulty of dealing with highly imbalanced and feature-correlated screening data. Our cascaded machine learning framework for DS prediction addresses these challenges through three complementary stages: 1) pre-judgment with isolation forest technique, 2) model ensemble by voting strategy, and 3) final judgment using logistic regression approach. Our experimental results show that this framework, when evaluated with different evaluation parameters, outperforms some machine learning methods in predicting DS based on maternal serum screening data set. The suggested combination of input features for DS screening is the group of alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, unconjugated estriol, and maternal age. Furthermore, our method holds the potential to generate accurate predictions for imbalanced and feature-correlated data, providing a novel and effective approach for analyzing certain diseases.

Cognitive Wireless Sensor Networks have become an integral part of the Internet of Things and are envisioned to be utilized by a wide range of services. While equipping the sensor nodes with cognitive radios would allow for the different spectrum bands to be utilized efficiently, most of the developed channel allocation schemes assume the data transmissions to be restricted to a single spectrum band at any given time. In an effort to further enhance the network's performance, we propose an allocation scheme that allow for the nodes to simultaneously utilize the multiple spectrum bands. In this paper, we extend our previous results and present a model for analyzing the performance of the nodes that employ our proposed multiple spectrum band allocation scheme. This model can also be applied for determining the optimal scheduling of transmissions across the various spectrum bands.

Reporting using query scripts often involves a lengthy process, which can cause delays in providing strategic decisions for a company. Furthermore, constantly updating and changing SQL queries to match the requirements of decision makers can be an inefficient process. 

To combat these issues, this paper proposes implementing data warehouse technology to create a faster way to generate reports based on specific requirements. This approach eliminates the need to customize SQL queries and instead reads the necessary data only. 

Using the Kimball methodology, data can be reported in various forms, allowing decision makers to make informed decisions within the eProcurement System.

Fingerprint Indexing allows filtering databases for samples most similar to a query fingerprint. Fixed-length feature vectors invariant to the count of minutiae allow fast comparison. This is the first approach, which uses Deep Convolutional Neural Networks to generate fixed-length index vectors from minutia neighbourhoods. It is also invariant to any sorting of minutiae with respect to their vicinity. No fingerprint image data is required. Usage of only standardized ISO/IEC minutia templates allows even to deploy to legacy systems. Our approach is therefore called Deep ISO Minutiae Indexing (DIMI). Index vectors can be as short as 16 float values per sample. DIMI was evaluated at the independent benchmark framework FVCongoing. In the incremental search scenario, DIMI achieves an average penetration ratio of 0.747% for test FIDX-50K and 0.723% for test FIDX-10K respectively. These are the best results reported so far.

Despite the emergence of many soft-bodied robotic systems, model-based feedback control for soft robots has remained an open challenge. This is largely due to the intrinsic difficulties in designing controllers for systems with infinite dimensions. This work extends our previously proposed formulation for the dynamics of a soft robot from two to three dimensions. The formulation connects the soft robot's dynamic behavior to a rigid-bodied robot with parallel elastic actuation. The matching between the two systems is exact under the hypothesis of Piecewise Constant Curvature. Based on this connection, we introduce a control architecture with the aim of achieving accurate curvature and bending control. This controller accounts for the natural softness of the system moving in three dimensions, and for the dynamic forces acting on the system. The controller is validated in a realistic simulation, together with a kinematic inversion algorithm. The paper also introduces a soft robot capable of three-dimensional motion, that we use to experimentally validate our control strategy.

A smart Internet of Things (IoT) system called the sEmoD has been developed to provide a scientific analysis of mental health crises. This system uses wearable technology called the Cyber-Human System (CHS) with a low-power Bluetooth communication module to collect data from Body Area Sensors (BAS) using a smartphone. The sEmoD IoT device is capable of collecting physiological data over an extended period of time so that experimentation and validation can be conducted with different test scenarios, including happy, depressed, stressed, and calm states of being. Signal processing and machine learning techniques are used for sensor data analytics to detect a potential personalized mental health crisis. This system can distinguish between different emotional crisis events with high accuracy of around 80%.

The media access control (MAC) layer of the vehicular ad-hoc network (VANET) is designed 3 to provide fast and reliable vehicles to vehicles (V2V) or vehicles to infrastructures (V2I) access. With the development of autonomous driving and intelligent transportation, many sensor information in large-scale vehicles require efficient and reliable transmission with V2V and V2I technologies. In recent years, the demand for various services in VANETs is growing rapidly, which poses great challenges to the design of the MAC protocol. An adaptive scheme for channel frame structure can enhance channel access flexibility to cope with the changing network topologies in vehicular environments. In this paper, we adopt an adaptive frame scheme on the control channel and the service channels, which mainly improves two aspects of channel access performance: improved time slot utilization of the broadcasting period as much as possible while ensuring the vehicle can access the control channel quickly; and increasing the throughput of the service channels without generating excessive overhead. Analysis and simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed mechanism.

Bitcoin is a decentralized digital currency system that utilizes blockchain technology to record all transactions on a public ledger. However, the pseudoanonymous nature of the Bitcoin network and the fact that its nodes are controlled by independent entities make it challenging to conduct network analysis. To address this issue, a fully controlled testing environment is necessary. In this regard, Kriptosare.gen, a dockerized and automatized Bitcoin testbed, has been developed to deploy custom Bitcoin networks on a full scale. The testbed is designed to run multiple experiments with different network configurations using a single machine. To investigate the relationship between network parameters and resource usage, a cost analysis was performed, and experimental data was generated to quantify the computational resources required for running various types of simulations. The results indicate that the testbed can be configured similarly to a real Bitcoin system, thus facilitating more comprehensive analysis and testing of the network.

Nowadays, metabolic diseases pose significant health challenges to individuals in various communities, incurring high costs for governments and healthcare systems. Critical issues such as continuous patient monitoring, gathering real-world data, and preventive education may impose implementation-related difficulties and demands for substantial financial resources. Despite the recent technological advancements that include feature-rich smartphones, location-based technologies, Internet of Things, and wearables, most efforts still rely on traditional, relatively inefficient approaches.

To address this gap and integrate metabolic disease research and patient care tasks, we present a system- Metabolic Syndrome Control and Caring (MetaSyCar). Our proposed system offers a comprehensive and multifaceted monitoring framework to track patients' behaviors, conditions, and health indices. Additionally, MetaSyCar's interactivity provides expert interventions and supervisory considerations to enhance the overall health management process.

This paper illustrates the foundations, conceptual architecture, and workflow of MetaSyCar. With the aid of the proposed system, we hope for a more efficient, cost-effective, and informed approach towards metabolic disease management.
